### S1.165 — Keyed indexes maintained by events

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: index
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.1 (phx-store), "Keyed indexes", written, with the instance inventory below.
**Depends on**: S1.159 (members named by slot of a generation-checked table); S1.164 (weighted instances keep their
members' weights in a sum-tree); S1.162 (lists are derived, rebuilt at load by the `Rebuild` pass; the round-trip
harness).
**Goal**: one kernel serves every "who is at this key" question a rule enumerates — owners at a zone, parties by zone
and
kind, searchers by region, holders by instrument — as a declared instance a system names in data: key function,
membership predicate, mode. It is kept by the events that change a key, read in O(k) for a key's k members, compacted
lazily and rebuilt at load in slot order; no index is rebuilt per call or per day.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/index.rs` | `Index`: key directory, member runs in 64 B blocks, lazy, weighted and count modes |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/index_decl.rs` | `IndexDecl { name, member_table, key_of, predicate, mode }` read at assembly |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/index_tests.rs` | unit tests over hand-built member columns |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/index.rs` | the `-F` driver: every instance of the inventory at its members at the design point; a flood day's owner draws |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.units] draw_ns` kept; `[fin.index]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.1 "Keyed indexes" and its inventory |

**Design**:
- **Key directory**: dense `Column<u32>` of list heads where the key space is dense (zones, (zone, kind), (instance,
  skill)); a sorted column of (key u64, head u32) searched by binary search where sparse. A key directory is sized from
  the declared key space, never from members.
- **Lazy mode** (unweighted sets): a key's members are u32 member slots in a block list (K-04 `BlockPool`: 16 entries in
  a 64 B block, three-quarters full, 5.33 B an entry). `insert(key, m)` appends O(1). A member whose key changes or that
  leaves is not searched for: its owning base calls `left(old_key)`, which counts one dead entry for that list. A walk
  `members(key)` reads the entries, keeps those whose member currently satisfies the instance's key and predicate (read
  from the member's own columns), sorts them by slot and drops duplicates: list order is never read, so a reused slot's
  new occupant is a member exactly when its own state says so, and a member that left and returned is counted once. No
  entry carries a generation and no member row carries a back-pointer. Every walk returns the entries it dropped as
  dead or duplicate, so each instance's dead share is counted per list and reported (K-15) against `[fin.index]
  dead_share`; each declaration states that its walks dedupe by slot.
- **Compaction**: a walk rewrites its list as the sorted, unique, valid entries it found; a list whose dead count passes
  its live count is compacted at the close by its owning base's apply (O(list)); the audit's rolling sweep (S1.171)
  compacts the lists it passes, so a list never walked is compacted within one audit cycle.
- **Weighted mode**: members in a sum-tree per key (S1.164); the member's position is a field of the member's own row
  (a declared `pos` column of the owning base, e.g. a stall's); `update(key, pos, w)`; removal = weight 0 and the
  position returned to the key's free list; a draw is `find` on a uniform below the key's total.
- **Count mode**: key → i64 count maintained on the same events, `#[maintained(writer = …)]` (S1.128), recounted by the
  audit from members' columns (N1, R4).
- **Declaration**: an instance is data in its owning system's `declare` (`IndexDecl`): the member table, the key
  function over declared columns, the predicate, the mode. An instance is declared only where a rule enumerates the
  members of a key; a set a party's own chain gives (a person's contracts, S1.257) is never indexed; a rare-day need
  over a whole store is a declared sweep (S1.171), not an instance; a need another instance answers reuses it.
- **Parallel**: inserts and `left` come from applies partitioned by key range (S1.170), so each list has one writer in a
  stage; walks are reads (`&self`) from any worker.
- **Save/load**: `#[saved(skip, rebuild = rebuild_from_members)]`: every list rebuilt at load from the member columns in
  slot order (S1.162); counters recounted.
- **The finished world's instances** (each declared by the step named; members at the design point; 5.33 B a lazy
  entry):

| Instance (declaring step) | Key | Mode | Members | Ledger line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| owners of physical units (S1.271; read by S1.274, S1.253, S1.294, S4.134, S5.113) | zone | lazy | ≈ 2.6 M at 1 000 zones | 12 |
| rows by holder (S1.271) | holder | lazy | ≈ 0.6 M | 11 |
| holders by instrument (S1.280) | instrument | lazy | ≈ 3.4 M | 11 |
| named units by tile (S1.284; read by S1.190, S8.200) | tile | lazy | ≈ 1.4 M | 12 |
| offers by poster (S1.296) | poster | lazy | ≈ 2.2 M | 17 |
| stalls (S1.301) | (good, zone): ≈ 250 k keys at 1 000 zones | weighted | ≈ 1.7 M | 17 |
| vacancy runs (S1.304) | (labour instance, skill) | lazy | ≈ 0.2 M | 17 |
| parties by zone and kind (S1.404; read by S1.221 frames, S1.224 electorates, S1.293, S1.294, S4.134, S5.155, S6.122) | (zone, kind) | lazy, with counts | ≈ 3.35 M | 16 |
| searchers by region (S1.304) | region | lazy | ≈ 0.2 M | 16 |
| messages by addressee (S1.237) | addressee | lazy | ≈ 0.5 M | 16 |
| queue memberships by claimant (S1.323) | claimant | lazy | ≤ 0.3 M | 16 |
| registered pairs by series (S1.336) | series | lazy | ≈ 0.1 M | 16 |
| loans awaiting workout (S2.101) | lender | lazy | ≈ 10 k | 16 |
| the bureau's subject index (S2.109) | subject | lazy | ≈ 0.3 M | 16 |
| firms in a procedure, `FRM.in_procedure` (S2.123) | firm | lazy | ≈ 3 k | 16 |
| shares by syndicate (S3.140) | syndicate | lazy | ≈ 50 k | 16 |
| registrations by instrument (S3.148) | instrument | lazy | ≈ 50 k | 16 |
| agencies by issuer (S3.207) | issuer | lazy | ≈ 20 k | 16 |
| pots pending by (trust, fund) (S4.142, S4.148) | (trust, fund) | lazy | ≤ 1.0 M on a payday | 16 |
| foreign-currency holders by currency (S5.165) | currency | lazy | ≈ 0.2 M | 16 |
| imitation pools (S6.109) | (product, region) | weighted | ≈ 0.15 M | 16 |
| singles (S6.122) | (region, age class) | weighted (8 B an entry with its weight's position) | ≈ 1.7 M | 16 |
| employment by (zone, industry) (S2.174) | (zone, industry) | count only | 0 entries | 16 |

  Not instances: S2.211's consumers by (region, priority class) (a declared sweep of the supply rows on a shed day,
  S1.171); S6.125's persons by region (a declared sweep of the persons' kind store); persons by zone for injury victims
  (S4.134 draws a household from parties by zone and kind, then a person in it).
- Replaces: indexes rebuilt per call (`stalls` ×5 a day, `Standing::new` ×2, `post`'s map of every vacancy,
  `keep_vacancies`, `searching` in `core_labour.rs`), the scan of every firm for a struck tile
  (`core_weather.rs`)
  — adopted by their bases' migrations.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: 115 k firms ending in a day: 115 k `left` calls, O(1) each; their entries read dead at the next walk —
  `ended_member_not_read`.
- E10: a slot reused by a party with the same key is read once — `reused_slot_read_once`; with another key, not read —
  `reused_slot_other_key_not_read`.
- E6: rebuilt at load equals incremental — `rebuild_equals_incremental` (through `roundtrip`).
- E2: an empty key reads nothing; a weighted key of total 0 draws `Missing` — `empty_key_draws_missing`.
- E9: dead entries bounded by live entries plus one audit cycle's changes — `compaction_bounds_dead`.
- E7: walks sort by slot, so the order handed to a rule never depends on insertion order — `walk_order_is_slot_order`.

**Extension points**: S1.167 (a ring's optional subject index is a lazy keyed index); S1.196 (declared index instances
maintained on writes); S1.222 (the parties-by-zone-and-kind index instance the frames read); S1.224 (electorates filter

events); S1.253 (owner instances for holding levies); S1.271 (K-06: the rows-by-holder instance, the index hooks);
S1.274 (K-06: the owners-by-zone instance); S1.280 (K-06: holders by instrument); S1.284 (K-06: the by-tile instance);

memberships by claimant); S1.336 (keyed index: registered pairs by series); S1.343 (keyed index memberships removed);

### S1.166 — Epoch flags and change sets

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.1 (phx-store), "Epoch flags", written.
**Depends on**: S1.160 (the touched sets' summary words and the iteration's output live in day buffers).
**Goal**: every store can say what the day changed — which rows, which parties — without a daily clearing pass: a row
is marked by writing today's day into a stamp or a bit under a word stamped with today, and "touched today" is read by
iterating set words only. The audit, per-day caches and perishable capacities read it.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/epoch.rs` | `DayStamps` (u32 a row), `EpochBits` (a bit a row, a day word per 64 rows, a summary bit per word) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/epoch_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/epoch.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[day.*] touched` parties over the party slots of `[store]`) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.epoch]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.1 "Epoch flags" |

**Design**:
- **`EpochBits`**: per 64 rows a `u64` of bits and a `u32` day; `mark(slot, today)`: if the word's day ≠ today, zero the
  bits and write today first (the lazy clear), then set the bit. A summary level (a bit per word, a day per 64 words)
  makes "the words touched today" an iteration over set summary bits. Iteration yields slots in slot order. 1.03 bits a
  row + summary.
- **`DayStamps`**: a `Column<u32>` for stores whose readers need a row's last day (a per-day cache's stamp, S1.211; a
  perishable capacity's day of use, S1.324; `last_change` for deposit accrual, S1.240): "stamp == today" is the test; no
  reset pass ever runs.
- **Writers**: marks are made where the fact is written, inside applies partitioned by target range (S1.170); a range is
  a
  multiple of 64 rows (every store's `RANGE_SHIFT` ≥ 6), so a word has one writer and no atomics are needed.
- **Change sets per store**: each base declares which of its columns the daily audit recounts and which parties'
  identities
  it must recheck; it marks them on write. The audit (S1.353) iterates the day's set and reads rows, never a
  writer's maintained aggregate (N1, R4).
- **Save/load**: not saved; a load starts a clean day (the save is taken at a close, after the audit read the day's set)
  (E6). Stamps that are state (a deposit's last change) are the owning base's saved columns, not this kernel's.
- Replaces: `Core::touched: BTreeSet<u32>` (`phx-world/src/core.rs`) and daily clears — adopted by the audit's
  migration (S1.354); the audit's full passes over every contract and firm (`core_audit.rs`,
  `core_accounts.rs`).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a payday touches most parties: iteration degrades to a dense sweep of words, still O(rows/64) and in slot order —
  `dense_day_iterates_every_word_once`.
- E6: nothing saved; the first day after a load starts empty — `load_starts_clean`.
- E7: marks from range-partitioned applies; iteration in slot order — `iteration_same_for_any_workers`.
- E11: day zero marks the opening's writes; the opening's audit (GEN.7) reads them —
  `opening_marks_read_by_first_audit`.
- E14: two marks of one row the same day are one mark — `double_mark_is_one`.

**Extension points**: S1.188 (a segment's load is stamped by day, so no reset pass runs); S1.197 (epoch stamps, K-07);
S1.219 (the day's touched parties, K-07); S1.273 (K-07: units touched today); S1.324 (epoch bitsets: a use touched
today); S1.330 (change sets: the parties touched today); S1.331 (change sets: the day's touched owned parties); S1.342
(change sets: proceeds arriving mark the estate); S1.353 (change sets: what the day changed); S4.172 (the day's change
set of holdings).
**Unit tests**: `mark_then_iterate`, `lazy_clear_on_new_day`, `double_mark_is_one`,
`dense_day_iterates_every_word_once`,
`iteration_same_for_any_workers`, `stamp_is_today_test`, `load_starts_clean`, `opening_marks_read_by_first_audit`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: `perf/design.toml [day.*] touched` parties over the party slots of `[store]`; marks ≈ 3 a touched party.
- Access: marks at writes; one iteration a day per change set at 10c.
- Unit targets: mark ≤ 0.8 VM ns (the word in the writer's cache line); iteration ≤ 0.4 VM ns a set bit.
- `ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (named slot: the audit's touched bitmaps, inside the 11 MB tallies lane,
  S1.161)`;
  `DayStamps` are 4 B a row in their owners' lines.
- Ratchets: `[fin.epoch]` (added) `mark_ns` 0.8, `iter_ns_per_set` 0.4; the audit's per-party identity is S1.353's
  `[fin.audit] ident_ns`.
**Guards**: PC-96 (S1.121) refuses a daily clearing loop over a store.
**Not allowed**: a daily reset pass; an ordered set of touched slots; atomics on marks; the audit reading a maintained
aggregate as evidence.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `EpochBits`, `DayStamps` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117, declared in `phx-store`) implemented for its stores; its traversals count rows visited into `ExecCounters::visited`, in the
  `phx-exec` traversal that runs them (only `phx-exec` shares a counter across workers).
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F epoch` at the design point within `[fin.epoch]`.
- [ ] §7.1 "Epoch flags" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.167 — Horizon rings

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.1 (phx-store), "Horizon rings", written.
**Depends on**: S1.160 (a ring's day's appends staged per chunk in day buffers before they join in chunk order); S1.165
(a ring's optional subject index is a lazy keyed index); S1.162 (the subject index rebuilt at load; the round-trip
harness).
**Goal**: every kept history — marks and volumes, events, filed statements, weather, credit records, volatility windows,
life records — is an append-only dated ring with its own declared horizon, pruned by whole chunks, never by a pass over
rows; its growth a year is its rows a day times its horizon, and nothing it holds outlives the horizon.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/ring.rs` | `HorizonRing<T: Pod>`: dated chunks, `append`, `range(from, to)`, `prune`, optional subject index |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/ring_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | the `-F` driver's ring part (`[store] events`, `filed_statements` at a full horizon) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.records] append_ns` kept; `[fin.ring]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.1 "Horizon rings" |

**Design**:
- Carries SET.13 (done at S0.20): its `#[clause]` carrier is added on `HorizonRing::prune`; the save's writer
  (`phx-world/src/save/mod.rs`) keeps its own.
- **Rows**: (day u32, payload `T: Pod`) in chunks of a declared row count (a chunk holds consecutive days' rows; a chunk
  is never split across a day boundary unless one day overflows it). A chunk header keeps its first and last day and its
  first row's ordinal. Rows are addressed by a monotone ordinal (u64); the live ordinals are [base, next).
- **`append(day, rows)`**: rows of one day, in the order the caller's stage fixes (chunk order of its traversal, E7); a
  day earlier than the last appended is a violation (TIME.9, TIME.10).
- **`range(from, to)`**: the chunks whose days intersect, found by binary search on the headers, O(log chunks + rows).
- **`prune(today)`**: drops every leading chunk whose last day is before today − horizon; its pages return to the ring's
  free chunk list (reused by later appends, never unmapped). Amortised ≤ 2 ns a row; no row is visited.
- **Horizon**: each ring kind declares its horizon as a RESOLUTION primitive (SET.13, SET.17, N8.5) with its POLICY
  floor where a keeper must follow one (BNK.21 credit records, HH.21, DRV.10 volatility windows, STA.5 revisions): the
  ring's horizon on a day is the larger of the RESOLUTION value and the floor its owner sets (`set_floor(day, days)`),
  which the owner reads from the POLICY in force (a dated schedule, S1.179). A floor that rises mid-run stops pruning
  from its effective day; rows already pruned stay pruned.
  Assembly refuses a RESOLUTION horizon below a floor in force at the opening.
- **Subject index** (declared per kind): a lazy keyed index (S1.165) from a subject (a party, an instrument, a series)
  to
  row ordinals; an entry below `base` is dead by construction; walks sort by ordinal.
- **Ended subjects**: a row naming a party keeps the party's `PartyRef`; a reader resolves it through the directory's
  tombstones (S1.194), which are kept at least as long as the longest horizon of any ring that can name a party
  (SET.13, PTY.10) — the ring declares which kinds it names so the directory reads that horizon.
- **Save/load**: the live chunks and their headers are saved (SET.12: the histories are state); the subject index is
  rebuilt from the rows in ordinal order (`#[saved(skip, rebuild = …)]`).
- **Growth report** (E9): per ring kind rows a day × horizon, reported by `StoreStats` (S1.117) each simulated year; a
  ring
  whose rows exceed its declared rows a day × horizon × 1.25 is a finding for the run's report.
- Replaces (in their bases' migrations): `Core::deaths`, `Taxes::sample`, `Outlooks::responses`, `Weather::shocks`,
  `CoreStats::published`, `Series::annual.insert(0, …)`, the fixed 2²⁴-row `EventStore` (`consts.rs`).

**Edge cases**:
- E9: two years of appends leave exactly the horizon's chunks — `rows_bounded_by_horizon`.
- E11: day zero: empty but for the opening's single latest values (GEN.5), appended at day zero —
  `day_zero_holds_opening_values`.
- E10: a row naming a party that ended reads as ended on its date through the directory's tombstones (S1.194's
  `pruned_past_horizon_reads_ended_beyond_horizon`); a subject's entries past the prune point are dead —
  `subject_index_skips_pruned`.
- E6: saved and loaded, the subject index equals one rebuilt — `rebuild_equals_incremental`.
- E5: a catastrophe day's thousands of events are one day's appends — `large_day_spans_chunks`.
- E9: a floor rising mid-run lengthens the horizon from its day — `floor_raises_horizon_from_its_day`.

**Extension points**: S1.192 (the weather's history is a horizon ring); S1.212 (K-08's per-kind horizons); S1.213 (K-08
dated chunks, per-kind horizons); S1.215 (K-08 rings with per-kind horizons); S1.219 (K-08 rings); S1.326 (horizon
rings); S1.336 (the horizon ring: yearly means); S1.340 (horizon ring: volatility windows); S1.353 (horizon ring:
findings kept for their horizon); S1.358 (the horizon ring); S4.108 (K-08: a risk factor's daily changes within the
lookback horizon).
**Unit tests**: `append_then_range`, `append_earlier_day_refused`, `prune_drops_whole_chunks`,
`rows_bounded_by_horizon`,
`floor_raises_horizon_from_its_day`, `day_zero_holds_opening_values`, `subject_index_skips_pruned`,
`large_day_spans_chunks`, `rebuild_equals_incremental`.
**Live checks**: none (N2's growth reads the rings' `StoreStats` at the gates).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: the rings' users' rows at a full horizon (`perf/design.toml [store] events`, `filed_statements`, marks by
  instrument; `[day.*] life_records` appended a day, resident only as index and buffers, S1.223).
- Access: appends at their stage; prune at 10d over chunk headers; ranges when read.
- Unit targets: append ≤ 3.8 VM ns a row (k 1.3); prune ≤ 1.5 VM ns a row amortised.
- Bytes: a chunk header 24 B a chunk; rows in their users' lines (line 18 records, line 19 weather), not stated here.
- Ratchets: `[fin.records] append_ns` 3.8; `[fin.ring]` (added) `prune_ns_per_row` 1.5, `range_ns_per_row` 1.
**Guards**: PC-100 (S1.125) refuses an unbounded `Vec` of dated rows in saved state (a history outside a ring).
**Not allowed**: a history without a declared horizon; a prune that visits rows; a horizon shorter than its POLICY
floor;
a history kept in an ordered map.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `HorizonRing` and its tests; the SET.13 carrier added; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117, declared in `phx-store`) implemented for its stores; its traversals count rows visited into `ExecCounters::visited`, in the
  `phx-exec` traversal that runs them (only `phx-exec` shares a counter across workers).
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` (the ring's part) at the design point within `[fin.records] append_ns` and
  `[fin.ring]`.
- [ ] §7.1 "Horizon rings" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.168 — The interner with reference counts

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.1 (phx-store), "The interner", written.
**Depends on**: S1.159 (interned ids are generation-checked slots, reused first in, first out after the close); S1.162
(the hash index rebuilt at load; the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every value many rows share — a contract's terms shape, a way set, a market key, a route key, an instrument
family's terms — is stored once and named by a 32-bit id found in O(1) from the value's bytes; each id counts the rows
that hold it and retires at zero; each interner declares whether a retired id's slot is reused after the close behind
its generation, or never.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/intern.rs` | `Interner`: value arena, hash index, refcounts, `intern`, `get`, `hold`, `release`, `close_day` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-store/src/intern_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/terms.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[store] terms` distinct values; `[day.*] interns`) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.terms]` kept |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.1 "The interner" |

**Design**:
- **Values**: variable-length byte strings (a terms shape's canonical encoding, S1.263) in a chunk arena (K-04), each
  addressed by (offset, length) in a 24 B row per id: offset u32, length u32, refcount u32, hash u64, generation u8,
  flags.
- **Index**: open addressing with linear probing, 16 B slots (hash u64, id u32, pad), kept at ≤ two-thirds load (24 B an
  entry); the hash is `Sip128` under the store's fixed key over the value's bytes
  (PC-13: no other hasher, no random seed), so the table's content depends on the values alone. The table is only
  probed, never iterated: its order is never read (CHN.6). Capacity from K-24 (S1.113) at the design point × two years;
  no
  resize inside a day.
- **`intern(bytes) -> InternId`**: hash, probe, compare bytes on a hash match; a hit returns the id and holds it
  (refcount
  + 1); a miss appends the value, takes a slot from the FIFO ring (S1.159) and inserts it. **`get(id) -> &[u8]`**: one
  row read (1 ns). **`hold`/`release`** adjust the count; a release to zero marks the id retiring: its slot and its
  arena
  bytes are released at the close, its index slot tombstoned; the arena is compacted when its dead bytes pass an eighth
  (K-04's rule).
- **Ids**: `InternId` = slot 24 bits + generation 8 bits. Each interner declares its reuse at construction, as data
  (`Reuse::AfterClose` or `Reuse::Never`):
  - `AfterClose` (terms shapes, market and route keys): a counted holder (a contract row's terms word) holds a live id
    by construction, so its reference is never stale; a retired slot is reused behind its generation because no stored
    value outside the counted references holds such an id — records and histories keep the values they need (SET.16),
    never a terms id; the generation lets any uncounted reader in a day (an intent) detect a stale id. A slot is never
    reused within the day it retired (S1.159).
  - `Never` (way sets and discovered ways, instrument families' term sets): ids that records name (a patent's way, an
    instrument's terms) are permanent; a retired id keeps its 24 B row, marked retired, and releases its value's bytes.
    The rows grow only by what is ever interned (ways discovered, instrument families created), reported by
    `StoreStats` (E9).
- **Parallel**: interns come from applies partitioned by owner range; each range's new values are staged in a day buffer
  and inserted at the stage's end in (range, emission) order, so ids depend only on the order of the day's work (E7).
- **Save/load**: values, rows, refcounts and the FIFO ring are saved; the hash index is rebuilt at load by hashing every
  live value in id order (`#[saved(skip, rebuild = rebuild_index)]`, ≈ 0.8 M × ≈ 100 ns = 80 ms).
- Replaces (in their bases' migrations): `sys-tec`'s compile-time `WaySets.index: BTreeMap`, the families' per-day new
  schedules (`core_open.rs` via `core_taxes.rs`, `core_credit.rs`, `core_central.rs`,
  `core_bills.rs`, `core_labour.rs`) — S1.263 interns the shapes.

**Edge cases**:
- E8: ids past 2²⁴ live, or a generation wrap of a slot, stop the run — `slot_capacity_stops`, `generation_wrap_stops`.
- E6: saved and loaded, every value found by `intern` returns its old id — `rebuild_index_finds_every_value`.
- E7: ids issued in (range, emission) order for any worker count — `ids_same_for_any_workers`.
- E9: under `AfterClose` churn does not grow the store: retired slots and bytes reused — `churn_keeps_size`.
- E10: a retired id is not reused within its day — `retired_not_reused_within_day`; under `Never`, not reused at all and
  still read as retired — `never_reuse_keeps_retired_row`.
- E14: two ranges interning the same new value the same day receive one id — `same_value_one_id`.

**Extension points**: S1.183 (instrument families' and classes' keys interned); S1.187 (route keys interned); S1.241
(the `Facility` slot's terms id is an interned handle); S1.257 (the interner, which holds terms ids); S1.259 (the
interner, whose terms name a book or a party); S1.263 (the interner); S1.279 (K-09: ids retired without reuse); S6.102
(the interner: ids issued at runtime with reference counts and a flags byte per row); S6.103 (interned sets with
counts).
**Unit tests**: `intern_twice_same_id`, `release_to_zero_retires_at_close`, `retired_not_reused_within_day`,
`get_is_one_read`, `same_value_one_id`, `ids_same_for_any_workers`, `churn_keeps_size`,
`rebuild_index_finds_every_value`, `slot_capacity_stops`, `generation_wrap_stops`, `never_reuse_keeps_retired_row`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: `perf/design.toml [store] terms` distinct values (loans, policies, tenancies, employment, derivatives and the
  rest); `[day.*] interns` a day, most of them hits.
- Access: event-driven (a contract opened or its terms changed by its parties).
- Unit targets: intern ≤ 46 VM ns (k 1.3, miss budget ≤ 0.3); get 1 ns.
- Unit bytes: ≈ 48 B an interned id (a 24 B row + a 16 B index slot at two-thirds load + ≈ 2 B of value), measured at
  0.8 M ids.
- `ledger line 10 (terms): +0 B (named slot: the terms' bytes are S1.263's)`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.terms] intern_ns` 46, `bytes_per_id` 48; the terms' `mb` is S1.263's.
**Guards**: PC-13 (no other hasher) holds; PC-99 refuses a `String` key per intern.
**Not allowed**: an ordered map of values; an `AfterClose` id stored in a record or history; a slot reused within its
day; a `Never` id reused; the index iterated.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `Interner` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117, declared in `phx-store`) implemented for its stores; its traversals count rows visited into `ExecCounters::visited`, in the
  `phx-exec` traversal that runs them (only `phx-exec` shares a counter across workers).
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F terms` at the design point within `[fin.terms]`.
- [ ] §7.1 "The interner" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.169 — Chunk plans and bounded spin

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.2 (phx-exec), "Chunk plans", written; §6.3 (traversals) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.117 (per-thread CPU, barriers and spin counters per span); S1.152 and S1.153 (settlement, the flows,
wheel takes, hiring's search and hazards passed the world's pool: the callers this kernel's API serves); S1.162 (the
rebuild pass's large rebuilds, which move onto `for_chunks` here).
**Goal**: every traversal of the day is one dispatch over chunks whose bounds depend only on rows and declared costs,
run inline when small, with results written into the caller's buffers by chunk index; there is no task per item, idle
workers spin at most 20 µs, and barriers and spin are counted. Results are bit-identical for one to eight workers.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/plan.rs` | `ChunkPlan`: bounds from rows and cost per row; `INLINE_BELOW` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/pool.rs` | one job per worker taking chunk indices from a shared cursor; bounded spin; `for_each`/`map` per item removed from the public API |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/traverse.rs` | `for_chunks`, `for_agenda` over a `ChunkPlan`, results into a `DayBuf` by chunk |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/consts.rs` | `SPIN_ROUNDS` replaced by `SPIN_US` 20 and the calibrated rounds; `POOL_MAX_WORKERS` 8 |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/plan_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/pool.rs` | the `-F` driver (every base's dispatches on B, NB, H) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.pool]` kept |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.2 "Chunk plans" |

**Design**:
- The families' dues, which S1.152 makes in turn into one chunk each (no traversal ran a closure per family), are
  made on the pool through `for_chunks`, each family its own chunk as before.
- The day's flows are cut by the plan's cost, not only by their makers: S1.152 left the day's stages' flows in one
  chunk, so grouping ran on one core and settlement gained nothing from the pool (1 000 000 persons, one day: the
  settle span 1 251 ms on the pool against 1 112 ms on one worker, `settle.group` 0.98 busy cores). The plan splits
  that chunk where its cost is, keeping the made order (grouping is stable, S1.152), so the outcome is unchanged.
- The day's hazard bookings are followed on the pool through `for_chunks`, chunked by slot range, each chunk
  following with its own buffers into `(slot, process, Followed)` and the booking, event, sampled rates and outcomes
  applied after in (slot, process) order: `run_hazards` already follows every due booking before applying any outcome,
  and S1.153 took its wheels on the pool, but no traversal yet ran the follow per chunk. Its tests
  `follow_same_for_any_chunking` and `apply_order_is_slot_then_process` are this step's.
- **`ChunkPlan::new(rows, cost_per_row_ns, rows_per_chunk_of_table)`**: chunk bounds snap to the table's chunks (so
  arena writes stay chunk-local) and close once a chunk's declared cost reaches the target (`CHUNK_COST`, 50–200 µs);
  the plan has at least 4 × `POOL_MAX_WORKERS` chunks when the rows allow, so balance holds for any worker count while
  the bounds never depend on it. The agenda's units (`agenda_units`) are a `ChunkPlan` over the agenda's rows.
- **Inline**: a plan whose total declared cost is below `INLINE_BELOW` (100 µs) runs on the calling thread over the same
  chunks in order, so the result is the same as on the pool.
- **Dispatch**: one broadcast per plan; each worker takes chunk indices from an atomic cursor and writes its result at
  the
  chunk's index of the caller's `DayBuf` (or into `DayBufs` by (chunk, handler)); the join is in chunk order. No
  `Vec` is allocated per dispatch; no job per item (today's `Pool::for_each` spawns one rayon job per item, 768 k a day
  for `make`, `pool.rs`).
- **Bounded spin**: after a dispatch, idle workers spin for at most `SPIN_US` (20 µs), the rounds calibrated once at
  pool
  start from the probe's core rate (`probe.rs`), then park; spin rounds and parks are counted (`spin_ns_per_day`). Today
  `SPIN_ROUNDS` 16 384 after every dispatch.
- **Rebuilds**: S1.162's large rebuilds (links, wheel, agenda, terms index) move from `Pool` onto `for_chunks` over a
  `ChunkPlan` of each store's slots, joined in chunk order.
- **Barriers**: each stage-table slot marked with a barrier ends with one (S1.185); the day's barriers are counted and
  held
  at ≤ 40 (B), 20 (NB), 48 (H).
- **Nested dispatch** is refused (a dispatch from inside a chunk is a violation); per-worker scratch is a `DayBuf` per
  worker reused every dispatch.
- **Only here**: `phx-exec` is the only crate that uses rayon or atomics (PC-04); world crates reach the pool only
  through `for_chunks`, `for_agenda`, `apply_by_range` (S1.170) and sweeps (S1.171) (PC-97, S1.122).

**Edge cases**:
- E7: 1, 2, 3 and 8 workers give bit-identical results — `plan_results_same_for_1_to_8_workers`.
- E5: a payday's plan is built from the day's real rows (`[day.h] dues`) — `plan_from_heavy_rows`.
- E7: a plan below `INLINE_BELOW` runs inline with the same result — `inline_equals_pooled`.
- E8: a violation inside a chunk reaches the caller — `a_violation_in_a_worker_stops_the_caller` (kept).
- E8: a nested dispatch is refused — `nested_dispatch_refused`.

**Extension points**: S1.157 (the stale comments, one of which the hazards followed on the pool makes true); S1.170 (one dispatch per pass over a chunk plan); S1.171 (a sweep is a chunk plan over its slice);
S1.225 (chunk plans and the pool for takes); S1.248 (chunk plans); S1.306 (chunk plans for meeting jobs); S1.321 (chunk
plans for the searchers' draws).
**Unit tests**: `bounds_independent_of_workers`, `bounds_snap_to_table_chunks`, `at_least_four_chunks_per_max_worker`,
`inline_equals_pooled`, `plan_results_same_for_1_to_8_workers`, `plan_from_heavy_rows`, `nested_dispatch_refused`,
`spin_is_bounded`.
**Live checks**: none (the world's busy cores are read by the bench's ratchet, S1.132).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: ≤ 40 (B) / 20 (NB) / 48 (H) barriers a day (`[day.*] barriers`); ≈ 2–4 dispatches a slot.
- Access: every traversal.
- Unit targets: dispatch ≤ 5 µs VM; spin ≤ 20 µs a dispatch.
- its share of fin.fixed.barriers: 90 / 45 / 110 core-ms (B / NB / H) — the whole line: barriers, serial tails and spin
  are the core's own.
- `ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (named slot: per-worker scratch in the tallies and pool lane, S1.161)`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.pool]` `dispatch_us` 5, `barriers_b` 40, `barriers_nb` 20, `barriers_h` 48, `spin_us` 20,
  `busy_hundredths` 270 (only rises).
**Guards**: PC-97 (S1.122) refuses `Pool::map`/`for_each` and literal `None` pools in world crates; PC-04 keeps rayon in
`phx-exec`.
**Not allowed**: a task per item; chunk bounds from the worker count; unbounded spin; a nested dispatch; an allocation
per dispatch.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `ChunkPlan`, the cursor dispatch, bounded spin and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for its stores; its traversals report rows visited through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F pool` at the design point within `[fin.pool]`.
- [ ] The settle span above one busy core and below its one-worker time at 1 000 000 persons over one day (the
  5 000 000-person day needs about 18 GB, beyond the bench machine's 15 GB), the criterion S1.152 could not meet.
- [ ] §7.2 "Chunk plans" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.170 — Partitioned apply with its sweep hooks

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.2 (phx-exec), "Partitioned apply", written; §3.1 (the layering rule for hooks, S1.101's) and §6.4
followed.
**Depends on**: S1.160 (per-worker range flush buffers and the partitioned items are day buffers); S1.161 (their lives
and the dues' wave lane in the day plan); S1.169 (one dispatch
per pass over a chunk plan).
**Goal**: every per-item effect on party state — a due's two sides, a sale's payee credit, an intent's target — is
scattered by target range into per-worker buffers and applied by one job per range sweeping its shard with the range's
columns in cache, in a declared order within the shard, so writes need no locks and the result is the same for any
worker count. A base kept inside another base's sweep (lines, levies, book folds) is reached through the sweep's hook
parameter, never by a lower crate naming a higher one.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/apply.rs` | `apply_by_range::<H: SweepHooks>(items, shift, key, hooks, f)`: scatter, flush, per-range sweep |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/hooks.rs` | `SweepHooks` (a tuple of `RangeHook`s, monomorphised, no `dyn`), `RangeHook::{open_range, item, close_range}` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/radix.rs` | the scatter reused, flush units of 256 B per range per worker |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/apply_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/apply.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[day.h] dues`' two sides; `[day.*] retail` payee credits) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.apply]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.2 "Partitioned apply" |

**Design**:
- **Ranges**: `range = target >> RANGE_SHIFT`, the shift declared per store from its count at the design point so a
  range
  is an L2's share (accounts: shift 12 → 4 096 accounts ≈ 80 KB a range, ⌈`[store] accounts` ÷ 4 096⌉ ranges); the
  dense index's high bits never collapse the ranges (a store of any size gets ⌈count ÷ 2^shift⌉ ranges). S1.161 sizes
  the flush buffers from this count.
- **Flush units and shards**: a flush unit is 256 B (16 items, four cache lines, enough to write-combine), so the flush
  buffers are ⌈count ÷ 2^shift⌉ × 256 B per worker; a range's shard is a list of flush units in a `DayBuf` whose life is
  its apply slot (S1.161). A producer that already writes its items by target range (a meeting's sale items, S1.306)
  or its intents (S1.348) hands its buffer as the shards and adds none.
- **Scatter**: the producing traversal (a chunk of the dues' stream, a meeting's sales) writes each item (16 B: target
  u32, amount i64, tag u32) into its worker's flush buffer for the item's target range; a full flush unit is copied to
  the range's shard, tagged with its producer's (chunk, sequence).
- **Waves**: an apply whose items at H exceed its shards' lane in the day plan is run in waves: the producing chunks are
  cut, in chunk order, into runs whose items fill the lane, and each run is scattered and swept before the next. The
  dues at 2b are the one such apply at the design point: ≈ 45 M sides at H against a lane of ≈ 144 MB (the day's
  maximum less what else lives at 2b) give 5 waves; B and NB take one. A wave's sweep reads each range's columns in
  address order, so the extra waves cost bandwidth (≈ 0.2 GB a wave), not a miss per item; the order within a target
  is still producing chunk, then emission, since waves follow chunk order.
- **Sweep**: one job per range (grouped into a `ChunkPlan` by the ranges' item counts) reads its shard's items in
  (producing chunk, emission) order — a declared order, never arrival order — and calls `f(&mut range_columns, item,
  &mut hooks)`. The range's columns are disjoint `&mut` views (`Column::chunks_mut`), so no two jobs write one word.
- **Hooks**: `SweepHooks` is a generic tuple of `RangeHook`s the sweep takes as a type parameter (monomorphised, no
  `dyn`); each hook gets `open_range(range)`, `item(&Item)` and `close_range()` with the mutable view of its own base's
  columns for that range. It is declared here, the lowest crate that runs a sweep; the concrete hooks — account lines
  (S1.328), equity folds (S1.330), carrying values (S1.332), levies, book folds — are implemented in their own crates
  and composed by `phx-world`'s routing at each stage slot, so `phx-ledger` or `phx-market` never name `phx-acct`. The
  rule is S1.101's §3.1 ("a base maintained inside another base's sweep is reached through the sweep's hook parameter").
- **Order within a target**: two effects on one party the same day meet in one shard in producing-chunk order, then
  emission order; a rule that needs another order sorts by a declared key within the shard (payment order, SET.6).
- **Two-sided items** (a due's payer and payee): scattered twice, once by each side's range.
- **No materialised batch**: items live in the shards until the sweep, then the shards are cleared (PC-27 kept).
- Replaces: serial per-item applies (`deliver_sales`, booking, tax accrual in `phx-world`) — adopted by S1.240–S1.250,
  S1.253, S1.309 and the intents' apply (S1.348).

**Edge cases**:
- E7: the same bytes for 1–8 workers — `apply_same_for_any_workers`.
- E14: two items on one target keep producing-chunk then emission order — `shard_order_is_declared`.
- E5: a quarter-end payday's sides flush without growth after warm-up — `second_heavy_day_maps_no_page` (S1.160) and
  `flush_units_preserve_items`; items beyond the lane run in waves with the same result as one pass —
  `waves_equal_one_pass`.
- E8: a target beyond the range's columns stops — `target_outside_columns_stops`.
- E10: an item for a party that ended today still applies (SET.7: settled against its estate), its slot live until the
  close — `ended_today_still_applies`.
- The ranges of a dense index are balanced for any store size — `ranges_balanced_for_dense_index`.
- A hook sees exactly its range's items, once — `hook_sees_each_item_once`.

**Extension points**: S1.191 (extractions applied by deposit range); S1.212 (partitioned sort of a day's items by key);
S1.221 (partitioned apply of the chunks); S1.245 (apply by range and its `SweepHooks` parameter); S1.248 (apply by
range); S1.263 (the dues' apply and its waves); S1.267 (apply by range and its `SweepHooks`); S1.285 (the sweep's hook
parameter the depreciation posts through); S1.296 (apply partitioned by target range at 5d); S1.298 (partition by
participant range); S1.306 (sale items scattered by seller range); S1.309 (apply by seller range and the sweep's hooks);
S1.328 (partitioned apply and its `SweepHooks` parameter: posts reach a party in its range's shard through a hook);
S1.330 (the sweeps' hook parameter); S1.332 (the sweeps' hook parameter); S1.338 (the sweeps' hook parameter); S1.341
(the sweeps' hook parameter); S1.345 (Claims and the priority waterfall (K-98)); S1.348 (partitioned apply at 5d).
**Unit tests**: `apply_same_for_any_workers`, `shard_order_is_declared`, `two_sided_items_reach_both`,
`flush_units_preserve_items`, `waves_equal_one_pass`, `target_outside_columns_stops`, `ended_today_still_applies`,
`ranges_balanced_for_dense_index`, `hook_sees_each_item_once`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: `[day.*] dues` × 2 sides, `[day.*] retail` payee credits and `[day.*] applies`, by day type.
- Access: every apply slot (2b, 5d, 6b, 6d, 7a–7c).
- Unit targets: scatter + sweep of a 16 B item with a trivial add ≤ 3.8 VM ns (k 1.3, miss budget ≤ 0.02), inside its
  users' units (`fin.dues.item_ns`, `fin.retail.apply_ns`); a hook call inlined.
- Waves at H: ⌈dues sides × 16 B ÷ the 2b lane⌉ ≈ 5; each adds one sweep of the touched ranges' columns.
- `ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (named slot: the flush buffers ≤ 4.8 MB, the decided flows' shards and the
  dues' wave lane, in S1.161's table)`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.apply]` (added) `item_ns` 3.8, `buffer_mb` 4.8, `waves_h` 5.
**Guards**: PC-97 (S1.122) refuses a per-item `&mut` apply outside `apply_by_range`; PC-01 (S1.112) refuses a lower
crate naming a higher one, the hooks being the way through; PC-27 kept.
**Not allowed**: a per-item serial apply; locks or atomics on party columns; an order within a shard read from arrival;
a materialised batch kept past its sweep; a `dyn` hook; a lower crate calling a higher crate's API.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `apply_by_range`, `SweepHooks` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117): none (no store); sweeps report items through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F apply` at the design point within `[fin.apply]`.
- [ ] §7.2 "Partitioned apply" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.171 — Declared sweeps and rolling cursors

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.2 (phx-exec), "Declared sweeps", written; §6.3 (traversals: the full-sweep list) and §6.6 followed.
**Depends on**: S1.121 (PC-96: a whole-table traversal only through a kernel traversal or a declared sweep); S1.169 (a
sweep is a chunk plan over its slice).
**Goal**: the few passes a clause needs over a whole store — the audit's rolling slice, a surprise's wake pass, a bank's
depositors on its failure, daily variation margin, funds' values, campaign intentions — are declared with their store,
cycle or reason, run as chunked traversals over a saved cursor's slice, and counted in the sweep ledger that the
bench ratchets; nothing else visits every row.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/foundation/phx-macros/src/sweep.rs` | `#[sweep(store = …, cycle = k)]` or `#[sweep(store = …, reason = "…")]` registration |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/sweep.rs` | `Cursor { store, next_slot }`, `slice(today)`, `SweepLedger` (rows visited per kind per slot per day) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-exec/src/sweep_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/settle.rs` | the `-F` driver's sweep part (a `pending` sweep of `[store] accounts`; the rolling thirtieth) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.settle] sweep_ns_per_account` kept; `[fin.sweep]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.2 "Declared sweeps" |

**Design**:
- **Registration**: a sweep is a declaration (`SweepDecl { store, slot, kind: Rolling { cycle } | OnReason { reason }
  }`)
  a base or a system's `declare` makes; the attribute marks the function that runs it, so PC-96 accepts its traversal.
  `cycle` is a RESOLUTION primitive where the spec makes it one (the full audit's cycle, N8.6, E 41) or the declared
  period of the clause (DRV.4's daily margin: cycle 1 over margin accounts only).
- **Rolling cursor**: `Cursor { store, next_slot: u32, cycle_start_day }` saved (SET.15: a restored world continues the
  cycle exactly); each day's slice is ⌈high_water ÷ cycle⌉ slots from `next_slot`, wrapping; a store that grows
  lengthens only its slice (E9). The slice runs as a `ChunkPlan` on the pool.
- **Reason sweeps** run on the days their reason occurs (a bank failing, a surprise's wake day, an election campaign's
  intention day), over the declared columns only (a `pending` column, an account's bank column).
- **Sweep ledger**: rows visited per (store kind, stage slot, day), from every traversal (agenda, index, apply) and
  every
  sweep; the bench compares it against the day's agenda plus the declared sweeps (S1.132's ratchet), so an undeclared
  full pass is visible.
- Replaces (as declared sweeps, in their bases' migrations): the audit's full passes (`core_audit.rs`), the
  `pending` settlement pass, `deposits_of` (a bank's depositors found by one sweep of the account columns on its
  failure,
  S2.199), `count` over households (`core.rs`).

**Edge cases**:
- E6: a cursor saved and loaded continues the cycle at the same slot — `cursor_survives_save`.
- E9: a store growing over two years lengthens the slice, never skips rows — `every_row_once_per_cycle_with_growth`.
- E5: a wake day's sweep over every hot record runs its slice as one chunk plan — `reason_sweep_runs_only_on_its_days`
  and S1.196's `-F` wake scan (`fin.parties.wake_scan_ns`).
- E7: slices as chunk plans — `sweep_same_for_any_workers`.
- E9: an undeclared full pass is counted in the ledger above the agenda — `ledger_counts_every_traversal`.

**Extension points**: S1.240 (the declared sweep finding a bank's depositors); S1.248 (the sweep as a declared sweep);
S1.251 (the 9a declared sweep); S1.259 (declared sweeps); S1.267 (declared sweeps); S1.270 (the period-close sweep of
collector cells); S1.331 (declared sweeps and rolling cursors: the rolling full recount); S1.340 (declared sweeps: the
one daily-for-all variation margin pass); S1.341 (declared sweeps: valuation by rows for shapes that keep no cells);
S1.353 (declared sweeps and rolling cursors: the full audit's cycle); S2.111 (K-14 the statements sweep); S2.176 (K-14 a
declared sweep); S2.186 (K-14: the large-exposure sweep on reporting dates); S2.195 (K-14: the declared sweep of K-47's
bank column on a surprise day); S2.199 (K-14: the sweep of K-47's bank column for the failed bank's accounts); S2.211
(K-14: the declared sweep of the supply rows' region column on a shedding day); S3.184 (the declared value sweep over
funds' positions); S4.107 (K-14: the VM pass a declared sweep); S4.119 (K-14: the declared sweep that finds the entity's
contracts on an event day); S4.146 (the year-end walk as a declared sweep); S4.152 (the declared sweep); S4.157 (a
declared sweep of the family's ends column); S4.161 (the sweep's registration); S5.137 (K-14 declared sweeps); S6.112 (a
rolling cursor over a declared cycle); S6.125 (a declared sweep of a kind store by slot range on a rolling cursor);
S6.129 (a declared sweep of a frame by slot range); S7.101 (a declared sweep over a window).
**Unit tests**: `every_row_once_per_cycle`, `every_row_once_per_cycle_with_growth`, `cursor_survives_save`,
`sweep_same_for_any_workers`, `reason_sweep_runs_only_on_its_days`, `ledger_counts_every_traversal`.
**Live checks**: none (the ledger's ratchet is the bench's, S1.132).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: the `pending` sweep over `[store] accounts` a business day; the rolling thirtieth of every audited store a
  day;
  wake scans over the hot records on a wake day.
- Access: declared days only.
- Unit targets: `pending` sweep 0.4 VM ns an account (sequential, k 1.3); rolling slice rows at their reader's cost;
  ledger counting fused.
- Bytes: a cursor 16 B a declared sweep (line 16, < 1 KB in all).
- Ratchets: `[fin.settle] sweep_ns_per_account` 0.4; `[fin.sweep]` (added) `ledger_undeclared_rows` 0.
**Guards**: PC-96 (S1.121) accepts a whole-table traversal only inside a `#[sweep]` function or a kernel traversal; the
sweep ledger's ratchet (S1.132).
**Not allowed**: an undeclared pass over a whole store; a sweep whose cursor is not saved; a slice sized by the worker
count; a daily pass over every party where no clause demands one.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The attribute, cursors, the ledger and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for its stores; its traversals report rows visited through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F settle` (the sweep's part) at the design point within `[fin.settle] sweep_ns_per_account` and
      `[fin.sweep]`.
- [ ] §7.2 "Declared sweeps" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.172 — Apportionment with a named residue

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.2 (Foundation: `phx-num`), "Apportionment", written.
**Depends on**: none (a pure function in `phx-num`; callers hand it the slice that receives the shares).
**Goal**: every split of a whole amount among claimants — an estate's rank, a dividend or coupon among holders, a
household payment drawn from its members, a joint holding's co-owners, a syndicate's shares, a batch failure's losses —
goes through one exact function: largest remainder, ties by a declared order or by lot keys the caller drew, and any
rounding residue landing on a named party, so the shares always sum to the total.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/src/apportion.rs` | `apportion(total, weights, rule, out)`, `Residue`, `Ties` |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/src/apportion_tests.rs` | unit tests over hand-built weights |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/apportion.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[store] estates`' claims; a dividend over 10⁵ holders) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.apportion]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §3.2 "Apportionment" |

**Design**:
- Carries MON.16 (done at S0.15): its `#[clause]` carrier is added on `apportion` (`round.rs`, `money.rs`,
  `price.rs`, `rate.rs` keep theirs).
- `apportion(total: i64, weights: &[u64], rule: Residue, out: &mut [i64])`: W = Σ wᵢ (checked `u64`; overflow stops,
  E8); each share floor(total·wᵢ / W) in `i128`, then:
  - `Residue::LargestRemainder { ties: Ties }`: the r = total − Σ floors units go one each to the r largest remainders;
    remainders compared exactly as `i128` numerators; ties broken by `Ties::Order` (the claimants' declared order, lower
    index first) or `Ties::Keys(&[u64])` (lot keys the caller drew from its named stream, CHN.3, CHN.6); the r largest
  are
    found by a deterministic selection over the total order (remainder, tie key) in O(n), then written.
  - `Residue::To(index)`: every share rounds by the governing convention (`Round`, MON.16) and the whole residue lands
    on the claimant at `index` (the payer, the payee with the largest share, or a named party the caller places in the
    list — `RoundingLanding` of today's §6.4).
- A negative total (a loss shared) apportions |total| and negates, so a loss's residue lands by the same rule.
- **No claimants**: `weights` empty or W = 0 is not a split: the caller's rule names the destination of the whole
  (POP.9,
  L3: the heirless destination; E3, E13); the function refuses it (`violation!`, clause MON.16) rather than inventing
  one.
- Pure: no allocation (the caller's `out`), no stream (tie keys handed in), no floating point; the same inputs give the
  same shares on any worker.
- Replaces (in their users' migrations): `vec![1; owners.len()]` shares and hand pro-rata in `estates_pay`
  (`core_day.rs`), `core_default::shares`, `apportion_amount`; `split_total` stays for the two-way split.

**Edge cases**:
- E3/E13: no claimant, or all weights zero — `empty_split_refused`; the caller's destination rule is S1.345's.
- E8: Σ weights past `u64` or a share past `i64` stops — `weights_overflow_stops`.
- E14: equal remainders fall by the declared order or the drawn keys, never by position in memory — `ties_by_keys`.
- Exactness: Σ out = total for every rule — `shares_sum_to_total` (exhaustive over small totals and weight sets).

**Extension points**: S1.190 (a split parcel's cost apportioned with a named residue); S1.274 (the uniform split over
undrawn tiles by largest remainder); S1.268 (apportionment with a named residue); S1.281 (K-16: apportionment with a named residue); S1.312 (apportionment with a named residue); S1.345
(apportionment with a named residue: every pro-rata payout); S1.406 (apportion with a named residue); S2.135 (K-16
apportionment); S3.133 (K-16: shares of a syndicate); S3.139 (K-16: cash in lieu); S3.140 (K-16: pro-rata cuts); S3.150
(apportionment); S3.158 (apportionment among members); S4.111 (K-16: apportionment with a named residue); S4.139 (K-16:
a person's limit apportioned across its policies); S4.148 (apportionment with a named residue); S5.153 (K-16 apportion);
S6.124 (apportionment with the residue to a named side).
**Unit tests**: `shares_sum_to_total`, `largest_remainder_matches_hand_example`, `ties_by_order`, `ties_by_keys`,
`residue_to_named_index`, `negative_total_mirrors`, `empty_split_refused`, `weights_overflow_stops`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: estates' claims distributed a day, dividends over holder rows on record days, households' payments split to
  their persons in the spend chain — each counted by its user (S1.345, S1.280, S1.406).
- Access: event-driven; a pure function its callers run.
- Unit targets: ≤ 7.7 VM ns a share for n ≤ 64, O(n) for large n; inside its users' units (`fin.waterfall.claim_ns`).
- Bytes: none of its own.
- Ratchets: `[fin.apportion]` (added) `share_ns` 7.7.
**Guards**: PC-06 (no numeric literals) and the `Missing` rules hold; PC-99 refuses a `Vec` of shares built per call.
**Not allowed**: equal shares where weights differ; a residue dropped or left with no holder (Law 2's "a residual with
no
holder is a defect"); a tie broken by memory order; a floating-point share.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `apportion` and its tests; the MON.16 carrier added; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117): none (a pure function); its callers report the shares through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F apportion` at the design point within `[fin.apportion]`.
- [ ] §3.2 "Apportionment" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.173 — The four money viewpoints

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: NUM.2 STATE
**Architecture**: §3.2 (Foundation: `phx-num`), "Whose money", written.
**Depends on**: none.
**Goal**: a figure in money says whose money it is by its type: the owner's home currency, a currency named beside it,
the reporting numéraire, or another named party's money are four types that never mix; the only way from one to another
is an exchange at a stated price or a declared conversion, so a signature that takes one refuses the others at compile
time.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/src/money.rs` | `HomeMoney`, `NamedMoney`, `NumeraireMoney`, `PartyMoney<P>` over `Money`; `Reported<M>` folded into `NumeraireMoney` |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/src/exchange.rs` | `exchange(from, at: Quote, round) -> to`, `Quote` (a price of one currency in another, with its date and source) |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/tests/compile_fail/viewpoint_*.rs` | a viewpoint passed or added where another is asked does not compile |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/src/money_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §3.2 "Whose money" |

**Design**:
- `Money { amt: i64, ccy: Ccy }` stays the column form (its own arithmetic refuses two currencies, NUM.5, and overflow).
  The four viewpoints wrap it, `#[repr(transparent)]`, with no `From`, no `Deref`, no arithmetic across viewpoints:
  - `HomeMoney`: a party's figure in its home currency (PTY.6), what its books are kept in (ACC).
  - `NamedMoney`: a figure in a currency named beside it (a foreign deposit, a foreign-currency loan, FX.1, MON.2).
  - `NumeraireMoney`: the reporting numéraire's figure, built only by exchange at a declared rate the observer reads
    (N3's cross-country measures; never written into the world, Law 17).
  - `PartyMoney<P>`: another named party's money (a subsidiary's figure in its parent's money, a counterparty's
    exposure in its own currency), `P` the owner's typed reference (supplied by `phx-id` at S1.174 through a marker
    trait `phx-num` declares).
- `exchange(from: NamedMoney, at: Quote, round: Round) -> HomeMoney` (and the other directed pairs a clause names): the
  amount × the quote's price through `value_of`'s checked `i128`, rounded once by the governing convention (MON.16); a
  `Quote` is built only from a print a market formed (Law 3, K-86) or a declared conversion (a recipe's content per
  unit,
  NUM.5), and carries its date (Law 8). A quote of the wrong pair is a violation (NUM.5).
- Missing is missing: a figure with no quote is `Missing<NumeraireMoney>`, never a zero.
- Why it completes NUM.2: every signature that reports, consolidates or converts money takes one of these types
  (statements are `HomeMoney`, the observer's cross-country totals `NumeraireMoney`), and the compile-fail tests show
  the four cannot be confused.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a party whose home currency has no quote on a day: its numéraire figure is `Missing` — `no_quote_is_missing`.
- E8: an exchange's product past `i64` stops — `exchange_overflow_stops`.
- Adding `HomeMoney` to `NamedMoney` does not compile — compile-fail `viewpoint_add`; passing one for another does not
  compile — compile-fail `viewpoint_arg`.

**Extension points**: S5.179 (K-16 viewpoints).
**Unit tests**: `exchange_rounds_once`, `quote_of_wrong_pair_refused`, `no_quote_is_missing`, `exchange_overflow_stops`;
compile-fail `viewpoint_add`, `viewpoint_arg`, `viewpoint_from`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**: none (types, `repr(transparent)`: no cost at run time, no bytes); no `-F` measure.
**Guards**: the compile-fail tests; PC-15 snapshots `phx-num`'s public API.
**Not allowed**: an implicit conversion between viewpoints; a converted balance stored as money (Appendix B #1); a
numéraire figure written into the world.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The four types, `exchange`, `Quote` and their tests (compile-fail included); the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` reads the budget at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §3.2 "Whose money" written; NUM.2's row in §13; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.174 — Typed references and the contract link's widths

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.2 (Foundation: `phx-id`), "Identities and their widths", written.
**Depends on**: S1.159 (typed references are `GenRef`/`ShortRef` of their tables).
**Goal**: every reference the finished world keeps has its own type and its width fixed for the design point and two
years' growth: a contract's link is family 8 bits + slot 24 bits in one word, each table's reference is its own type,
and a width overflowed stops the run.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/foundation/phx-id/src/ids.rs` | `ContractLink` (family 8 + slot 24), `ContractRef` (link + 8-bit generation), `HoldingRef`, `OfferRef`, `MessageRef`, `ProcessRef`, `EstateRef`; `InstrumentId` kept |
| `crates/foundation/phx-id/src/consts.rs` | `FAMILY_BITS` 8, `FAMILY_SLOT_BITS` 24, `HOLDINGS_FAMILY` 255 |
| `crates/foundation/phx-id/src/ids_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/foundation/phx-id/tests/compile_fail/*.rs` | one table's reference refused where another's is asked |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §3.2 "Identities and their widths" |

**Design**:
- **Contracts**: `ContractLink(u32)`: family 8 bits (≤ 255 families; code 255 reserved for holdings, S1.271) + slot 24
  bits (16.7 M rows a family; the largest, policies, `[store.contracts] "INS.policy"`), the word a person chain's link and a
  wheel entry hold — 0 B added to either. `ContractRef { link, gen: u8 }`, the 8-bit generation under S1.159's
  reference-life rule. The family count is asserted against the catalogue at assembly (`family_capacity`, S1.180; the
  codes, S1.181).
- **Tables' references**: `HoldingRef`, `OfferRef`, `MessageRef`, `ProcessRef`, `EstateRef` are `repr(transparent)` over
  (slot u32, generation u32), each its own type (no `From` between them); `phx-store` implements `Pod` for them
  (`pod.rs`) and `GenRef<T>` converts only to its own table's type.
- **Parties**: `PartyKey` (kind 5 + slot 27) for what lives within a day or moves with its party, `PartyRef` (kind,
  24-bit generation, slot) for what outlives a day (unchanged); `PartyId` offsets as `u32` in columns. The kinds census
  (≤ 31 kinds + NATURE) is S1.180's assembly refusal.
- **Instruments**: `InstrumentId(u32)`, never reused (unchanged).
- The unit id's width is S1.175's (`phx-num`); the flows' 15-bit denomination placeholder is S1.184's.

**Edge cases**:
- E8: a slot of 2²⁴ in a family link stops — `family_slot_width_stops`; a family code past 255 stops —
  `family_code_width_stops`.
- E10: a `ContractRef` whose generation differs resolves to none — `contract_ref_generation_checked`.
- Typed references are not interchangeable — compile-fail `holding_ref_as_offer_ref`.

**Extension points**: S1.181 (the 8-bit family code, 255 reserved for holdings); S1.194 (`PartyKey` 5 + 27 bits, the
kinds census ≤ 31 with NATURE); S1.207 (`PartyKey` usable as payer and payee); S1.277 (typed refs: `OfferRef`, `ProcessRef`).
**Unit tests**: `contract_link_packs_family_and_slot`, `family_slot_width_stops`, `family_code_width_stops`,
`contract_ref_generation_checked`; compile-fail `holding_ref_as_offer_ref`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**: none (types; 0 B added: the link stays one u32). No `-F` measure; the widths are held by the logic-level
tests against `perf/design.toml [store.contracts]`.
**Guards**: PC-14 (no default identity) holds; the compile-fail test; PC-100 (S1.125) refuses a literal shift as a
capacity.
**Not allowed**: an untyped `u32` edge id in any new structure; a width chosen for today's world; a silent wrap.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The references, the link's widths and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` reads the budget at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §3.2 "Identities and their widths" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.175 — 24-bit unit ids

**Kind**: data

**Goal**: a unit id — a good at a zone, a capital class at a zone, an instrument, a special unit — is 24 bits in a
`u32`,
room for the finished world's ids with two years' growth; every column form that carries a unit is re-laid without
padding; an id past 2²⁴ stops the run.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/foundation/phx-num/src/qty.rs` | `UnitId(u32)` with `UNIT_ID_BITS` 24 (`qty.rs`, `u16` today); `Qty`/`QtyRaw` re-laid |

**Budget**: none (types; a column that stores a unit id grows by 2 B only where it held a `u16`, stated by its owner).
No
`-F` measure.

**Not allowed**: a unit id width chosen for today's world; a silent wrap.

### S1.176 — Stream families in the key, slot ordinals in the counter

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.2 (Foundation: `phx-rand`'s addressing) updated.
**Depends on**: S1.102 (the day's stage table as documented: the slots whose ordinals address draws).
**Goal**: a stream's key carries its family — the world's, the observer's, or the player's advice — so two families
never share a key, and a draw's counter addresses the stage-table slot it is drawn in rather than one of the retired 46
sub-steps; a draw still depends only on its address.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/foundation/phx-rand/src/key.rs` | `StreamFamily` (world, observer, advice) and the family word in the key's derivation |
| `crates/foundation/phx-rand/src/draws.rs` | the counter's ordinal is a `SlotOrdinal(u8)` |
| `crates/foundation/phx-rand/src/key_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/streams.rs` | the `-F` driver (Philox blocks and x4 batches) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.kept] draw_ns` retired; `[fin.streams]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §3.2 `phx-rand`'s addressing |

**Design**:
- Carries CHN.6 (done at S0.10): its `#[clause]` carrier is added on the counter's addressing
  (`phx-rand/src/draws.rs`
  and `philox.rs` keep theirs).
- **Families**: a stream's key is `philox([fnv_lo, fnv_hi, seed_lo, seed_hi] ⊕ family word, fixed key)`, so a world and
  an observer stream of the same name never share a key; adding a stream of any family changes no other's draws
  (CHN.1).
- **Ordinals**: the counter's word 3 is `(slot ordinal << 24) | block`; `SlotOrdinal(u8)` is the stage-table slot's
  (1a … 10e, 8a–8f, the save), fixed by the documented table (S1.102) and owned by the stage table from S1.185. Adding a
  slot appends an ordinal; ordinals are never renumbered (a renumbering changes every draw, a new world).
- **Opening phases** keep their own ordinals beyond the day's (`OpeningPhase`, unchanged).
- **Batches**: `Draws::x4` over `philox_x4` (unchanged).
- The draws change once, when the day runner moves the world's callers to slot ordinals (S1.186): the committed world is
  re-opened from the same seed; a save of the old build is refused (E 36, E 44).
- Retires the `-F` baseline's `[fin.kept] draw_ns` (S1.119), replaced by `[fin.streams]`.

**Edge cases**:
- E7: a draw depends on (family, stream, subject, day, slot, block) only — `draw_depends_on_address_only`.
- CHN.1: adding a stream changes no other's draws — `adding_stream_changes_no_other`.
- REP.16: a world and an observer stream of one name never share a key — `families_never_share_a_key`.
- E6: streams have no position to save (counter-based) — `no_stream_state_saved`.
- E8: a slot ordinal past 255 stops — `slot_ordinal_width_stops`.

**Extension points**: S1.177 (the family word in the key and the slot ordinals); S1.185 (slot ordinals address the
draws); S1.222 (named world streams); S1.235 (named streams keyed by subject and day); S1.298 (the lot's stream);
S1.315 (the day's arrival order drawn on a named stream); S1.323 (the lots' streams); S1.358 (observer streams: the
panels' samples); S1.480 (observer streams: the family bit); S6.131 (observer streams apart from the world's); S8.102
(K-18: streams).
**Unit tests**: `families_never_share_a_key`, `draw_depends_on_address_only`, `adding_stream_changes_no_other`,
`no_stream_state_saved`, `slot_ordinal_width_stops`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: every draw of the day (hazards, tastes of `[day.*] retail` choices, lots), counted by their users.
- Unit targets: a Philox block 8 VM ns (k 1.0), an x4 batch 12 VM ns.
- Bytes: none.
- Ratchets: `[fin.streams]` (added) `block_ns` 8, `x4_ns` 12; `[fin.kept] draw_ns` retired.
**Guards**: PC-13 (no other random crate) and PC-19 (draws only from the run's streams) hold.
**Not allowed**: a stream key without its family; an ordinal from the retired sub-step list; a draw addressed by
processing order.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Families in the key, slot ordinals and their tests; the carrier added; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117): none (no store); draws counted per stream by the counters.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F streams` at the design point within `[fin.streams]`.
- [ ] §3.2 addressing updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.177 — Stream declarations by family, and the families' draw types

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core), "Streams", written.
**Depends on**: S1.176 (the family word in the key and the slot ordinals).
**Goal**: every declared stream names its family, and each family's code holds its own type of draws — `WorldStreams`
for the world, `ObserverDraws` for `phx-obs`, `AdviceDraws` for the player's advice and the player's draw — so a world
rule cannot be handed an observer's draws and an observer cannot open a world stream; the world's draws address the
stage table's slots.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/streams.rs` | `StreamDecl { family }`; `WorldStreams::open` refuses a non-world declaration; `ObserverDraws` (`streams.rs`) refuses a world one; `AdviceDraws` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/slots.rs` | the slots' ordinals of the documented table (taken over by the stage table at S1.185) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/streams_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/tests/compile_fail/observer_draws_in_world.rs` | a world rule handed observer draws does not compile |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.3 "Streams" |

**Design**:
- Carries REP.16 (done at S0.28): its `#[clause]` carrier is added on `StreamDecl::family` (`phx-core/src/streams.rs`
  keeps its CHN carriers).
- **Declarations**: `StreamDecl` carries its family; assembly refuses two declarations of one name in two families.
  `Streams::open_at(decl, subject, day, slot)` takes a `SlotOrdinal` from `slots.rs`; today's `open(…, SubStep)` stays
  for the world's current callers until the day runner moves them to slots (S1.186), which retires it.
- **Types**: the world's code holds only `WorldStreams`; `phx-obs` holds `ObserverDraws`; the player's advice panel and
  the player's draw (which household the player takes, OBS.4, CHN.3) hold `AdviceDraws` — separate types, so "observe
  with a world stream, or act on the observer's" (REP.16) is refused at compile time.
- `-F` streams `fin.<base>` are world-family streams of `phx-fin`'s own names.

**Edge cases**:
- REP.16: a world rule handed observer draws does not compile — compile-fail `observer_draws_in_world`; an observer
  opening a world stream is refused — `observer_refuses_world_stream` (kept `NotObserver`).
- E8: one name declared in two families is refused at assembly — `same_name_two_families_refused`.
- E7: a draw at a slot depends on its address only, the same for any worker count — `world_draws_by_slot`.

**Extension points**: S1.186 (the stream families' `open_at`, to which the world's callers move); S1.235 (the hazard
streams declared by family, with their draw types); S1.358 (stream families and their draw types: the panel draw).
**Unit tests**: `observer_refuses_world_stream`, `same_name_two_families_refused`, `world_draws_by_slot`; compile-fail
`observer_draws_in_world`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**: none (types and declarations; a draw's cost is S1.176's `[fin.streams]`). No `-F` measure of its own.
**Guards**: PC-19 (draws only from the run's streams) extended: world crates may not name `ObserverDraws` or
`AdviceDraws`.
**Not allowed**: a stream shared between families; a world rule holding observer draws; an ordinal from the retired
sub-step list.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Families on declarations, the three draw types and their tests; the carrier added; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F streams` within `[fin.streams]` (S1.176's measure, unchanged: the draw types add no work)
  and the bench at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §7.3 "Streams" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.178 — The calendar's day facts

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core), "Calendar and day facts", written.
**Depends on**: none.
**Goal**: each country's facts about a day — its civil date, whether it is a business day, the period ends it closes,
the dates a business-day convention rolls onto it — are computed once at the day's open and read from a cache by every
rule, so no day path converts a date or tests a business day per call.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/calendar/facts.rs` | `DayFacts` per country, `Calendar::open_day(day) -> &[DayFacts]` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/calendar/mod.rs` | `date(day)` and `is_business(country, day)` kept for the opening and assembly; day paths read `DayFacts` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/calendar/facts_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/calendar.rs` | the `-F` driver (3 countries × 730 days) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.kept] civil_ns` retired; `[fin.calendar]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.3 "Calendar and day facts" |

**Design**:
- `DayFacts { date: Date, weekday, business: bool, month_end, quarter_end, year_end: bool (civil), period indices
  (month u32, quarter u32, year i32 since the epoch), rolled: [RolledRange; CONVENTIONS] }` per country (≈ 64 B), built
  at stage 1a by `open_day` from the country's business-day bitset and rules (unchanged, `calendar/mod.rs`):
  `rolled[c]` is the range of calendar days a convention c (Following, ModifiedFollowing, Preceding, …) moves onto
  today — after a closed weekend, Saturday to Monday under Following — so the wheel takes those dates' buckets together
  (K-42) and a payday stacked on Monday is visible as such (E5).
- A party's fiscal calendar (RAT.8's own fiscal year, filing day) is not here: it is the party's own dated schedule
  (K-43, K-55), placed by `Calendar::plus` (TIME.3, PC-17).
- `Calendar::plus` stays the one way to add a period (PC-17); `DayFacts` never advances a date.
- Per-day values of dated policies in force are cached beside the facts by S1.179.
- Save/load: not saved (derived from the calendar's rules and the day); rebuilt by `open_day` on the first day after a
  load.
- Retires the `-F` baseline's `[fin.kept] civil_ns` (S1.119); readers of `civil_from_days` per call on day paths
  (`Calendar::date`, the `(day + slot) % days` date tests of `core_deposits.rs` and `core_freight.rs`)
  switch to `DayFacts` or to agenda dates (K-43) in their migrations.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: three closed days rolled onto a Monday: `rolled` spans Saturday–Monday — `following_rolls_weekend_onto_monday`.
- E13: a day that is a business day in one country only: facts per country — `business_in_one_country`.
- E11: day zero's facts are the day before the first (GEN.13) — `day_zero_facts`.
- E6: rebuilt after a load equal to the facts before — `facts_rebuilt_equal`.
- E5: a modified-following month end rolls back, not into the next month — `modified_following_month_end`.

**Extension points**: S1.197 (the calendar's day facts for a window's open and close days); S1.227 (the day's facts:
business days); S1.242 (day facts and day counts); S1.250 (per-country business-day facts); S1.263 (day facts, day
counts and conventions); S3.114 (K-19: maintenance periods).
**Unit tests**: `following_rolls_weekend_onto_monday`, `modified_following_month_end`, `business_in_one_country`,
`period_indices_match_plus`, `day_zero_facts`, `facts_rebuilt_equal`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: the countries of `perf/design.toml [store]` a day; reads by every dated rule.
- Unit targets: `open_day` ≤ 1 µs a country a day; reads cached in L1.
- its share of fin.fixed.open: ≈ 0.003 / 0.003 / 0.003 core-ms (B / NB / H) — the core's own open.
- Bytes: ≈ 64 B a country (line 1, the process).
- Ratchets: `[fin.calendar]` (added) `open_us` 1; `[fin.kept] civil_ns` retired.
**Guards**: PC-17 (days placed only by the calendar) extended: `civil_from_days` and `Calendar::date` refused in
day-path
modules (the S1.120 path list).
**Not allowed**: a civil conversion per call on a day path; a second clock (TIME.11); a date placed by counting days
(TIME.12).
**Done when**:
- [ ] `DayFacts`, `open_day` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117): none (derived, per day); `open_day` counted in its span.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F calendar` at the design point within `[fin.calendar]`.
- [ ] §7.3 "Calendar and day facts" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
