### S1.179 — Dated policy schedules and rule handles

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core), "The register: handles and policy schedules", written; §4.6 (policy values) restated.
**Depends on**: S1.146 (day paths read the register by handles bound at assembly); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every POLICY primitive its owner may change during the run — a tax rate, a policy rate, a haircut, a capital
rule, an appropriation — is a dated schedule of (effective day, value, owner, announced day), saved with the world and
read "in force on day d" from a per-day cache; a party reads what was announced by the day it decides; rules take
their schedules through handles bound once.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/policy.rs` | `PolicySchedule<T>` replacing `PolicyValue<T>` (`policy.rs`): owner a party, entries sorted by effective day, `announce`, `in_force(day)`, `announced_by(day)`, `segments(from, to)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/register/mod.rs` | `PolicyH<T>` handles bound at assembly; the per-day cache of values in force |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/policy_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/policy.rs` | the `-F` driver (10 k schedules) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.policy]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.3 "The register: handles and policy schedules"; §4.6 |

**Design**:
- Carries (done at S0.09): NUM.3 — its `#[clause]` carrier added on `PolicySchedule` (the register's other declarations keep
  theirs).
- **`PolicySchedule<T: Pod>`**: the opening value from the register (its primitive must be POLICY with an owner, NUM.3)
  and the dated changes, a sorted `Vec`-free column of `Entry { effective: Day, announced: Day, owner: PartyRef,
  value: T }` per schedule in one arena; `announce(owner, announced, effective, value)` refuses a writer other than the
  primitive's owner (Law 16), an effective day before the next business day of the owner's country after `announced`
  (TIME.7), and an owner that has ended without a successor (Law 13: an abolished owner's schedules pass to its
  successor
  by the book move, S1.267).
- **Reads**: `in_force(day)` = the last entry with `effective ≤ day` (binary search); `announced_by(day)` = the entries
  a
  party could know on `day` (announced ≤ day), with their effective days, for VAL.6's announcement heuristic (Law 12);
  `segments(from, to)` yields each (from, to, value) a period spans, so a law changed mid-period splits it (a tax rate
  inside a filing year).
- **Per-day cache**: at 1a, after the day facts (S1.178), each schedule whose next effective day is today advances its
  cursor; rules read the value in force through `PolicyH<T>` (an index), 1 ns. Schedules are kept in a K-43-style list
  by
  next effective day, so 1a touches only the schedules that change today.
- **Rule handles** (C-26): a rule that reads a policy takes its `PolicyH`, bound at assembly by name once; no name is
  read
  on a day path (PC-98).
- **Save/load**: every schedule's entries are state (SET.12: the run's dated changes are saved); the cache is rebuilt at
  load from the entries (`#[saved(skip, rebuild = …)]`).

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a POLICY primitive absent from the register is refused at assembly, never read as 0 — `absent_policy_refused`.
- E5: a law changed mid-period splits the period — `segments_split_at_effective_day`.
- E14: an announcement effective the same stage it is made is refused — `effective_too_soon_refused`; by a non-owner —
  `non_owner_refused`.
- E10: an owner ending passes its schedules to its successor — `owner_succession_moves_schedule`.
- E6: saved and loaded, `in_force` equal on every day — `schedule_roundtrip`.
- E11: day zero reads the opening value — `day_zero_reads_opening`.

**Extension points**: S1.253 (dated policy schedules: rates and bands in force); S1.319 (dated policy schedules); S1.338
(dated policy schedules: a limit's amount in force); S1.345 (dated policy schedules: the country's insolvency law's
class order in force); S1.423 (dated policy schedules: the appropriation); S1.435 (dated policy schedules: bands and
rates in force); S2.132 (K-20 the law as a dated POLICY schedule); S2.137 (K-20 register); S2.179 (K-20: rule handles;
the central bank's facility rates in force); S2.180 (K-20: haircuts and facility rates in force); S2.186 (K-20: the
supervisor's requirements and weights as dated POLICY); S2.189 (K-20: rule handles); S2.201 (K-20: each change a dated
POLICY value with its announcement and effective day); S2.212 (K-20: energy policy as dated POLICY); S3.105 (K-20:
announced policy changes by effective day); S3.111 (K-20: the dated policy schedule, announced and effective); S3.112
(K-20); S3.116 (K-20: the regime as a dated schedule owned by the parliament); S3.120 (K-20: announced rates); S3.145
(the exchange's rules as dated POLICY schedules); S4.103 (K-20: dated POLICY schedules with owners); S4.125 (K-20: the
solvency and reserving rules as dated POLICY with owners); S4.144 (dated POLICY schedules with an owner); S5.101 (K-20
`PolicySchedule<T>` with owner, announced and effective day; rule handles taking their schedule); S5.116 (K-20: dated
schedules with their announced and effective days); S5.135 (K-20); S5.174 (K-20); S6.101 (dated policy schedules: patent
law's life and fees are POLICY with an owner); S6.114 (dated policy schedules: education and family law are POLICY with
an owner); S6.129 (dated policy schedules); S6.138 (the register); S8.101 (K-20: register handles).
**Unit tests**: `in_force_is_last_effective`, `announced_by_hides_future_announcements`,
`segments_split_at_effective_day`, `effective_too_soon_refused`, `non_owner_refused`, `owner_succession_moves_schedule`,
`absent_policy_refused`, `schedule_roundtrip`, `day_zero_reads_opening`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: ≈ 10 k schedules at the design point (policies × countries × owners); changes a few a day at most.
- Access: 1a advances only the schedules due; reads by handle.
- Unit targets: handle read 1 ns; the day's resolution ≤ 1 ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.open: ≤ 1 / 1 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H) — the core's own open.
- `ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.4 MB resident (≈ 10 k schedules, ≈ 40 B an entry)`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.policy]` (added) `resolve_ms` 1, `read_ns` 1.
**Guards**: PC-98 (S1.123) refuses a register read by name on a day path; PC-91 (no tuning) unchanged.
**Not allowed**: a POLICY value changed by anyone but its owner; a value read as in force before its effective day; a
default for an absent policy; a per-day scan of every schedule.

### S1.180 — The kind catalogue

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: MKT.21 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core), "The kind catalogue", written; §5.3 (schema compilation) and §5.4 (assembly refusals)
restated.
**Depends on**: S1.141 (kinds' features declared: owners (and so an equity account), money class, statistical class,
player kind, holding money); S1.143 (`DEM.heirless_to`, the one declaration of the heirless destination, validated
against the kinds here); S1.145 (families and kinds bound to handles at assembly, `Bound`, the jobs families declared in `families::JOBS`).
**Goal**: everything that differs between kinds of thing — legal forms, party kinds and their attributes, contract
families, reasons, account lines, markets, hazards, decision kinds, products, grades, ways, capital kinds — is declared
data compiled once at assembly into dense tables of typed handles, with a refusal for every inconsistency; no mechanism
reads a name, and adding a kind, a family, a product or a market is a declaration.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/mod.rs` | `Catalogue`: compiled tables, handles `KindH`, `FamilyH`, `ReasonH`, `LineH`, `MarketH`, `HazardH`, `DecisionH`, `ProductH`, `GradeH`, `WayH`, `CapitalH` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/forms.rs` | legal forms (`kinds.rs`'s `LegalForm` compiled): may hold, separate party, limited liability, deposit taking, endings, offices, owners, features (`has_owners`, `issues_currency`, `holds_money`) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/kinds.rs` | party kinds: attribute schemas (typed hot/cold column declarations for K-32), `sector`, `place` (site, region or country), statistical and money class |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/families.rs` | contract families from `FamilyDecl { name, reason, kinds, jobs, debt }`: sides' kinds, listed sides, row layout, cold columns, schedule program, default definition, statement period |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/reasons.rs` | reasons: lines posted to, tax base, BoP category, payment order, levy set, an optional refusal gate (a predicate handle over the instruction and POLICY data); account lines |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/markets.rs` | markets: form, operator, meeting days, settlement convention, participants, tick sizes and price points (REP.34), each valuer's published method |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/refusals.rs` | every inconsistency refused at assembly, by item and system |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/catalogue_tests.rs` | unit tests over hand-built declaration sets |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/catalogue.rs` | the `-F` driver (the finished world's catalogue compiled) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.catalogue]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.3 "The kind catalogue"; §5.3, §5.4 |

**Design**:
- **Inputs**: each system's `declare` (the `System` trait, `system.rs`) and the register's data files; the declarations
  S1.141, S1.142 and S1.145 added are compiled here: each `declare_kind!` with its `sector` and `place` (site, region or
  country word);
  the legal-form feature `has_owners` (PTY.4: who its owners are), which is also exactly when a party keeps an equity
  account (ACC.4: every party that has owners keeps one; the central bank and state-owned firms have owners, the
  treasury and agencies do not) — one feature, no separate equity flag;
  `STA.sectors`, `STA.money_classes`, `OBS.player_kind`, `DEM.heirless_to`; each family as a `FamilyDecl { name, reason,
  kinds, jobs, debt }`, `jobs` from S1.145's `families::JOBS` and `debt` every other, replacing its `Bound` of kind and
  family handles.
- **Compilation**: every declared name is interned once into a dense handle (u16 or u8 per table); every cross-reference
  (a family's side kinds, a reason's lines, a market's participants' kinds, a decision's office in its taker's form, a
  hazard's subject kind, a way's inputs by product and grade, a capital chain's classes) is resolved to handles; tables
  are `Pod` columns indexed by handle (≈ 10 MB for the finished world). No name is kept on a day path: a mechanism
  holds only handles (PC-98).
- **Markets (MKT.21)**: each market's form (posted price, call, network call, book, dealer, bilateral, administered,
  search, queue — the forms S1.312–S1.325 implement), its operator (a party kind whose POLICY it is), its meeting days
  (a
  calendar rule), its settlement convention (T+n, SET.17), its participants (kinds and the admission rule), its tick
  size
  and price points (POLICY of the trade, REP.34), and each valuer's published method (POLICY of the valuer, read by
  S1.326 and S1.335). These are declared data with their owners, the register holding every number (NUM.3).
- **Reasons' refusal gates**: a reason may name a predicate over (payer, payee, their countries, currency, amount) and
  declared POLICY data; it is compiled to a predicate handle here and evaluated at emission by S1.245; a reason without
  one costs a handle test.
- **Widths**: families are coded in 8 bits with code 255 reserved for holdings (S1.174), so `family_capacity` is 255
  families and dated-reason kinds together, each family's slots below 2²⁴; party kinds are 5 bits, 31 kinds and NATURE.
  S1.181 inventories the finished world's codes against these.
- **Refusals** (all reported at once, by item and system): a name declared twice; a reference to an undeclared name; a
  family whose side kinds may not hold it under their legal forms; a reason posting to an undeclared line or of no
  payment order; a market whose participants' forms may not trade it; a decision taken in an office its form does not
  declare (MND.20); a hazard acting on an undeclared kind; a way reading a product of no declared grade; a legal form
  with
  no ending that issues no currency (PTY.13, `kinds.rs`'s validation kept); more families and dated-reason kinds than
  `family_capacity`, a family declared with more slots than 2²⁴, or more than 31 party kinds.
- **Save/load**: not saved; the build supplies it (a save names the catalogue's hash in its manifest, and a load with
  another is refused, E 36).
- Replaces: kind and family names compared in mechanisms (`"firm" || "bank"` `core_accounts.rs`, `"treasury"`,
  `"agency"`, `starts_with("LAB.")` `core_labour.rs`, 60+ `names.iter().position`), the hard-coded kinds table
  (`phx-world/src/consts.rs`) — their users move in S1.182 and the base migrations.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a kind with no family, a product with no grade, a market with no participant: each is either refused (a reference
  with no target) or declared data meaning none — `market_without_participants_refused`.
- E8: the 256th family code (255 being holdings') and the 32nd kind stop at assembly — `family_capacity_refused`,
  `kind_census_refused`.
- E12: a number a declaration needs absent from the register is refused, never 0 — `absent_primitive_refused`.
- A decision whose office its form lacks refused — `decision_office_refused`.
- A reason's refusal gate is compiled to a handle and a reason without one reads none — `reason_gate_compiled`.
- The same declarations in any registration order compile to the same handles — `handles_independent_of_order`.

**Extension points**: S1.181 (`family_capacity` and the refusal that reads it); S1.182 (the compiled catalogue and its
handles); S1.183 (products, grades, capital kinds and chains, special units declared); S1.196 (K-21 compiles each kind's
declared attributes to handles); S1.204 (ways' declared data); S1.209 (each legal form declares its offices, each
decision kind its office); S1.215 (record kinds, series keys and publishers declared); S1.225 (families and dated-reason
kinds declared, with `family_capacity`); S1.227 (each kind's declared reasons); S1.240 (products and money-holder
classes as declared data); S1.243 (reasons and money-holder classes); S1.245 (reasons with payment order, source kind
and lines); S1.246 (reasons with their gates as declared data); S1.250 (currency systems and their members as declared
data); S1.253 (reasons with their levy sets and collector roles); S1.254 (reasons, with the tallies each feeds); S1.255
(payment order as K-21 data per (payer kind, reason)); S1.257 (families declared with their columns and side modes);
S1.273 (K-21: ways, their inputs and yields; source kinds); S1.276 (K-21: each reason's declared gains tally; a legal
form's permitted cost flows); S1.279 (K-21: instrument families and their declared term sets, legal forms whose parties
issue equity); S1.281 (K-21: each family's events, amount rules and cessation outcomes); S1.284 (K-21: unit kinds and
their declared columns); S1.285 (K-21: capital chains — each class's efficiency and value as declared fixed-point
shares, leaving rates over age and use, the failed band); S1.287 (K-21: process kinds and their declared columns);
S1.296 (markets as declared kinds: form, meeting days, participants, lapse rules); S1.297 (each trade's declared points
and each market's tick grid, MKT.21); S1.302 (declared scopes of the market kinds); S1.326 (markets' forms and mark
rules); S1.328 (the kind catalogue: each kind's lines declared as data); S1.335 (the kind catalogue: valuers' methods
declared as data, MKT.21); S1.348 (the kind catalogue: decision kinds and concerns compiled to handles); S1.357 (the
kind catalogue: price points declared per market); S2.126 (legal forms declare limited liability); S2.177 (K-21: deposit
products per holder class, reasons and lines); S2.192 (K-21: the authority kinds and their offices); S2.193 (K-21: the
insurer kind; the uninsured-depositor claim class); S2.200 (K-21: the bank legal form with its minimum capital); S2.202
(K-21: the plant, storage and line kinds, the system operator's kind, the power products); S2.213 (K-21: the union kind
with its leader's office); S3.101 (K-21: market declarations); S3.123 (K-21: reasons' payment order); S3.127 (K-21: the
publisher's method as a declared valuer); S3.129 (K-21: families); S3.145 (families, market declarations, legal forms);
S3.163 (the dealer legal form declared); S3.182 (legal forms and kinds as data); S4.101 (K-21: the family, its side

S4.160 (kinds, families, reasons); S5.101 (K-21: a reason's tax base and levy set as declared data); S5.127 (K-21: the

pair market's settlement convention); S5.180 (K-21 refusal predicates on reasons); S5.185 (K-21: reasons declare their

**Unit tests**: `handles_independent_of_order`, `every_reference_resolved`,
`market_declares_form_days_convention_participants`,
`market_without_participants_refused`, `decision_office_refused`, `family_capacity_refused`, `kind_census_refused`,

**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:

### S1.181 — The family codes of the finished world

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core), "The kind catalogue", its table of family codes written.
**Depends on**: S1.180 (`family_capacity` and the refusal that reads it); S1.174 (the 8-bit family code, 255 reserved
for
holdings).
**Goal**: every contract family and every dated-reason family the finished world declares has a fixed 8-bit code in one
data file, the codes never reused, and their count asserted against `family_capacity` at assembly, so the width chosen
at S1.174 is shown to hold the finished world with room to grow, not today's.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/shared/families.toml` | one row per family: code u8, name, kind (contract or dated reason), declaring step, status (declared, planned, retired) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/families.rs` | the codes read from the file; a declared family's code must be its row's |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/catalogue/catalogue_tests.rs` | the inventory's tests |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.3 "The kind catalogue": the table of family codes |

**Design**:
- **Codes are data**: a family's code is its row in `families.toml`, fixed when the row is written and kept when the
  family retires (a save names codes, so a code is a permanent identifier: code 9 stays reserved after its family moves
  to instruments); a planned row reserves its code before its step is built, so no later step renumbers one.
- **The inventory**: contract families first, in the order their steps are built (S1.257 lists their rows and bytes and
  restates no code); then the wheel's other families (S1.225: dated commitments, process kinds, offer books, messages
  and declared dated reasons), each named by its declaring step, which gives it its handle. The agenda files party keys,
  not family codes (S1.227), and takes none.

### S1.182 — Kinds, families and capacities read from the catalogue

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core) and §3.6 (assembly) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.180 (the compiled catalogue and its handles).
**Goal**: the world's kinds, their places and the families' names come from the catalogue: the hard-coded kinds table
and its places in `phx-world` are deleted, the opening builds each kind's store from its declaration and capacity, and
every user holds handles.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/consts.rs` | `kinds` module (`consts.rs`: `KINDS`, `CENTRAL_BANK` … `AGENCY`) deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_open.rs` | `Core::empty` (`core_open.rs`) builds each kind's store from `Catalogue::kinds()` with its declared stride and its capacity (K-24); `HOLDS_MONEY` (`core_open.rs`) read as the form's `holds_money` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_*.rs` | each `KINDS[...]`/`kinds::FIRM`-style index and family name replaced by `KindH`/`FamilyH` |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-98.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- Users move by function: `Core::empty` and every opening module (`core_open.rs`, `core_firms.rs`, `core_jobs.rs`) take
  their kinds from the catalogue in its declared order; the day modules (`core_goods.rs`, `core_labour.rs`,
  `core_day.rs`, `core_central.rs`, `core_default.rs`, `core_stats.rs`, `core_agencies.rs`) hold `KindH` and `FamilyH`
  bound at assembly (S1.145's `Bound`) instead of positions in `KINDS` and names; the families' names
  (`consts::families`) become `FamilyH`s, the save still writing each family under its declared name (§11).
- Capacities: every kind's slot capacity is K-24's (S1.113) for the kind, never `KIND_ROWS`/`AGENT_ROWS`.
- The world's behaviour is unchanged: the same kinds in the same order open the same world.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-98.toml` (kind and family names on day paths); the file's count falls by them.

**Edge cases**:
- E6: a save writes each kind and family by its declared name; a load binds them to the build's handles and refuses an
  undeclared name (§11) — kept test `unknown_name_refused_at_load`.
- E13: a kind the catalogue declares with no party at the opening has an empty store — `empty_kind_empty_store`.

**Extension points**: S1.186 (kinds and families on handles, so routing needs no name); S1.407 (kinds and families read
from the catalogue).
**Unit tests**: `stores_built_from_catalogue_order`, `empty_kind_empty_store`, `unknown_name_refused_at_load` (kept).
**Live checks**: the Stage 0–1 live checks, unchanged, read on the bench's run.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: the kinds' stores, built once at the opening from their declarations and capacities (≤ 1 ms more on the
  opening's span).
- No day line changes; `ledger line 3 (directory): +0 B (named slot: the same stores, now built from declarations)`.
- Ratchets: none added; the bench's spans unchanged within noise (a measure of code, never read as the world's).
**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-98.toml` falls by this step's sites.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a kind or family index written as a literal.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `consts::kinds` deleted; every user on handles; the fast checks pass; `exceptions/PC-98.toml` lowered.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` reads the budget at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken; its spans unchanged within
  noise.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.183 — The units registry

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: REP.24 PROCESS *(part: capital classes carry an age class)*
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core), "The units registry", written.
**Depends on**: S1.168 (instrument families' and classes' keys interned); S1.175 (24-bit `UnitId`); S1.180 (products,
grades, capital kinds and chains, special units declared); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every unit a holding, flow, offer or print can be denominated in — a good (a product's grade at a zone), a
capital class at a zone, an instrument, a special unit (accrued pension, kWh of a region), a deposit's right — has one
24-bit id issued at run time from the catalogue's keys, a 16 B row saying what it is, and its grade's content per unit;
ids are resolved into party records when they change and never looked up on a day path.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/units/mod.rs` | `Units`: rows by `UnitId`, `issue(key) -> UnitId`, `row(id)`, `retire(id)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/units/keys.rs` | `UnitKey`: `Good { product, grade, zone }`, `Capital { class, zone }`, `Instrument { id }`, `Special { kind, place }`, `Right { deposit }`; the key → id index per unit kind |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/units/grades.rs` | grades' content per unit (GDS.1, GDS.13, E 45): `content(grade) -> (content unit, per unit)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/units/units_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/units.rs` | the `-F` driver's registry part (`perf/design.toml [store] unit_ids` issued) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.units] ids_mb`, `issue_ns` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.3 "The units registry" |

**Design**:
- Carries GDS.1 and CAP.1 (both done at earlier steps): their `#[clause]` carriers move from `phx-core/src/goods.rs`
  and `phx-core/src/units.rs` to the registry.
- **Row** (16 B, `Pod`): kind u8 (good, capital, instrument, special, right — declared unit kinds of the catalogue), key
  u32 (product and grade, capital class, instrument id, special kind, deposit), zone u16 (or none), price exponent u8,
  storable/perishable u8, spoilage class u8, retired day u32 (or none), pad. A capital class is (kind, size band,
  quality band, condition band, **age class**) as the catalogue's chains declare (REP.24, CAP.1); its service date and
  remaining life are carried by its age class.
- **Grades' content** (the owner's answer, GDS.1, GDS.13, E 45): each grade declares its content per unit (the metal in
  a
  tonne of ore, the heat in a tonne of coal) in a content unit, a TECHNOLOGY primitive of GDS; the registry exposes it
  by
  `GradeH`, so a way that states a graded input in content reads the units it needs of a grade as content ÷ content per
  unit (the mechanism step moving the ways' reads to content is S1.439). A good's unit row names its grade; content is
  never stored per holding.
- **Index**: per unit kind a key → id table: dense offset tables where the kind declares its key space dense (goods:
  product × grade × zone; capital: class × zone), sorted runs of (key, id) where sparse (instruments, special units,
  rights), searched by binary search. Lookups happen only when a party's units change (a firm's inputs chosen, a class
  issued); the resolved ids live in the party's record (R1).
- **Issue**: `issue(key)` returns the key's id or appends a row (≤ 200 ns); ids never reused (a record or print naming
  a unit reads it after it retired). Goods and capital classes are issued the first time something names them and are
  not retired (their count is bounded by the declared keys); an instrument's unit retires with its instrument (K-64); a
  special unit when its issuer declares; a right with its deposit's end.
- **Land**: land is counted by (zone, land class) like dwellings; land owned apart is a parcel's row (S1.190), read as a
  holding of place kind parcel (S1.271), not a registry id per parcel or cell.
- **Parallel**: issues come from applies in range order and assembly; ids depend on the order of issue only (E7).
- **Save/load**: rows saved; the key indexes rebuilt at load eagerly (`#[saved(skip, rebuild = …)]`, S1.162), unlike
  today's lazy `UnitIds::plain` (`goods.rs`).
- Replaces: `UnitIds`/`GoodIds` (`phx-core/src/goods.rs`, within 2¹⁵), `plant_kind_of_unit` linear — their users
  move in S1.184.

**Edge cases**:
- E8: the 2²⁴th id stops the run — `issue_past_capacity_stops`.
- E13: a zone with no goods of a product issues none; an absent key reads `Missing`, never id 0 —
  `absent_key_is_missing`.
- E6: rebuilt index equals the incremental one — `index_rebuild_equals`.
- E7: ids in issue order for any worker count — `ids_same_for_any_workers`.
- A grade's content per unit is read for the grade's goods at every zone — `content_by_grade`.

**Extension points**: S1.184 (the registry); S1.274 (a class at a zone is a registry unit); S1.191 (each deposit's
resource at its grade and zone is a registry unit, and its extraction right a registry unit of kind `right`); S1.271
(K-22: 24-bit `UnitId`s, each unit's kind, grade, zone and content per unit); S1.279 (K-22: an instrument's unit id);
S1.299 (24-bit unit ids: a good at a zone is a stall's group); S1.438 (the units registry, which holds each grade's
content per unit); S2.139 (K-22 classes with condition and age classes); S2.202 (K-22: power as a special unit, MWh per
(region, day, block)); S4.142 (special non-money units).
**Unit tests**: `issue_twice_same_id`, `absent_key_is_missing`, `issue_past_capacity_stops`, `content_by_grade`,
`age_class_in_capital_key`, `ids_same_for_any_workers`, `index_rebuild_equals`, `retired_row_still_reads`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: `perf/design.toml [store] unit_ids` (≈ 110 k at `[resolution] zones` 1 000: ≈ 60 product-grades and ≈ 50
  capital classes a zone, with instruments, special units and rights; 220 k at 2 000); a few thousand
  issues a day at most after the opening.
- Access: on change only; never on a day path.
- Unit targets: issue ≤ 200 VM ns; a row read 1 VM ns.
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +3 MB resident (≈ 110 k × 16 B rows + ≈ 1.2 MB key indexes)`; 6 at 2 000
  zones.
- Ratchets: `[fin.units]` (added) `ids_mb` 3 (6 at 2 000 zones), `issue_ns` 200.
**Guards**: PC-92 extended by S1.120 refuses `UnitIds::find`/`unit` on day paths; the rule then names `Units::issue`.
**Not allowed**: a unit looked up on a day path; a unit id reused; content stored per holding; a default id for a
missing
unit.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `Units`, keys, grades' content and their tests; the carriers moved; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for the registry; issues report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F units` (the registry's part) at the design point within `[fin.units] ids_mb`, `issue_ns`.
- [ ] §7.3 "The units registry" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.184 — Goods and capital classes issued by the registry

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.183 (the registry).
**Goal**: goods, plant and freight name their units through the registry; each party's unit ids are resolved into its
record when they change; `UnitIds` and `GoodIds` are deleted and no unit is found on a day path.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/goods.rs` | `UnitIds`, `GoodIds` (`goods.rs`) deleted |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/units.rs` | `issue_chain` issues a kind's classes through `Units::issue` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | each firm's own and input unit ids resolved into its record at the opening and when its way or zone changes |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_plant.rs` | plant classes by registry id; `plant_kind_of_unit`, `plant_kind` (`core_plant.rs`) linear searches deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | shipments' leaving and arriving goods by registry id |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/flows.rs` | `Denom(u16)` (`flows.rs`) kept at 15 bits as the named placeholder, refusing a wider id |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- Users move by function: the opening issues every good and class the opening names (`core_firms`, `core_plant`,
  `core_goods`); a firm's record keeps its own product's and its inputs' ids (the firm's hot words, K-32's layout at
  S1.196 takes them over), written when its way or zone changes; `move_goods`, `receive`, `deliver` and the meetings
  read those ids; freight's shipment names its leaving and arriving goods by id; plant's capacity reads classes by id.
- `find` / `unit` (`goods.rs`) disappear from day code: the 9.1 % of the day's CPU spent in unit lookups and
  `memcmp` goes.
- Behaviour unchanged: the same goods and classes, the same ids' order at the opening.
- **Placeholder** (retired by S1.245): the flows' `Denom(u16)` keeps its 15 bits while units are 24; a flow naming an id
  of 2¹⁵ or more stops at emission with `capacity_exceeded!`, the placeholder naming S1.245, whose 24-bit `Denom`
  retires it. At the design point the flows name fewer than 2¹⁵ ids until the registry issues past it.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (the `UnitIds::find`/`unit` day-path sites); the file's count falls.

**Edge cases**:
- E6: after a load the registry's index is eager; the first day's reads find every id (no fallback search) —
  `first_day_after_load_finds_ids`.
- E8: a flow naming an id of 2¹⁵ or more stops at the placeholder `Denom` until S1.245 —
  `denom_placeholder_width_stops`.

**Extension points**: S1.272 (units resolved into records, so no `UnitIds::find` on a path); S1.439 (goods issued by the
registry); S5.177 (goods keyed by grade and place).
**Unit tests**: `firm_record_holds_resolved_ids`, `chain_issued_through_registry`, `first_day_after_load_finds_ids`,
`denom_placeholder_width_stops`.
**Live checks**: LC-1 goods and capital checks unchanged on the bench's run (GDS.10's identity read by the audit).
**Budget**:
- Day cost: the unit lookups and their `memcmp` (9.1 % of the day's CPU on the bench today, in the `goods` and `freight`
  spans) go; the spans fall by them (a measure of code, never read as the world's).
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +0 B (named slot: the registry's rows, S1.183's figure)`.
- Ratchets: none added.
**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-92.toml` falls by this step's sites.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a unit found by search on a day path.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `UnitIds`/`GoodIds` deleted; users on the registry; the fast checks pass; `exceptions/PC-92.toml` lowered.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` reads the budget at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken; the lookup share gone from its
  spans.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.185 — The stage table

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §6.1–§6.3 (the day) restated from the table; §7.3 (phx-core), "The stage table", written.
**Depends on**: S1.102 (the day's stage table documented); S1.176 (slot ordinals address the draws).
**Goal**: the day's order is data: TIME.6's ten stages as slots, each with its business-only flag, its inclusion on
non-business days (TIME.8), what runs there (a base kernel or a system's rule set), its read tags and whether a barrier
follows, in three modes — ordinary, day zero, settling; a slot that reads a later stage's writes is refused at assembly.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/stages.rs` | `StageTable`: slots 1a … 10e and save, `SlotDecl`, modes; `SlotOrdinal` owned here from S1.176's `slots.rs` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/stages_check.rs` | the read-tag check: every declared read of a slot names a writer at an earlier slot today or a previous day |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/stages_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/stages.rs` | the `-F` driver (a day walked in each mode with empty slots: the runner's own cost) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.stages]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §6.1–§6.3; §7.3 "The stage table" |

**Design**:
- Carries TIME.6, TIME.8 and TIME.10 (done at earlier steps): the carrier at `phx-core/src/substep.rs` moves to the
  stage table and its read tags here; those in `phx-world/src/day.rs` move with the runner at S1.186.
- **Slots** (S1.102's table): 1a, 1b; 2a–2f; 3a, 3b; **4a, 4b, 4c**; 5a–5d; 6a–6d; 7a–7c; **8a–8f**
  (orders posted, the linked call, its settlement, administered facilities, their settlement, a shortfall's end); 9a–9d;
  10a–10e; save. Each `SlotDecl { ordinal, stage, business_only, on_non_business: bool (TIME.8's list), runs: Kernel(k)
  |
  Rules(set), reads: [Tag], writes: [Tag], barrier_after, pool: Chunked | Apply | Serial }`.
- **Stage 4's trips** (GEO.20, the owner's answer): 4b places every trip of the day — each adds its legs' loads to the
  segments it crosses (K-26's use, S1.187) — and 4c reads each trip's time and cost at the loads all the day's trips put
  on its legs; a trip never reads the load of trips placed before it. 4a keeps production kinks, wear, processes
  arriving, jobs starting and ending. Until travel (S2.172) no rule declares a trip, and 4b–4c run nothing.
- **Read tags** (TIME.10): a tag is (store or column group, as-of): "today, written at slot ≤ k" or "yesterday's close";
  stage 5 reads yesterday's prints and publications, stage 9 today's; `stages_check` refuses at assembly a slot whose
  read
  names a writer at a later slot of the same day (TIME.6's Done when), and a slot that writes what an earlier slot of
  the
  day declared it reads as today's.
- **Modes**: *day zero* runs stage 5 only (GEN.13: the opening's first decisions from the snapshot); *settling* runs the
  ordinary table for the declared settling length (GEN.6); *ordinary*. Non-business days run the slots TIME.8 lists; a
  business-only slot whose countries are all closed is skipped (E13).
- **Barriers**: ≤ 40 on B, 20 on NB, 48 on H (the table's `barrier_after` flags counted per day type at assembly).
- The table holds no state; the runner that walks it is `phx-world::day` (S1.186), which also deletes the 46 old
  sub-steps (`substep.rs`) once their users are on the table; they stay beside the table until then.
- **Save/load**: not saved (build data); a save names the table's hash in its manifest (a load with another refused).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: an H day runs every slot with its heavy volumes; the table itself is the same — `h_day_runs_every_business_slot`.
- E11: day zero runs stage 5 only, reading the snapshot — `day_zero_runs_stage_five_only`.
- E13: a slot whose countries are all closed is skipped — `closed_countries_skip_business_slots`.
- A slot reading a later slot's write refused — `later_read_refused`.
- Stage 8's six slots run in order on a business day only — `stage_eight_slots_business_only`.
- 4b's loads complete before 4c reads any — `trips_read_all_loads`.

**Extension points**: S1.186 (the stage table); S1.188 (stage 4's slots 4b and 4c); S1.491 (the stage table's day-zero
mode: stage 5 only); S2.172 (K-23: stage 4 split into 4a, 4b, 4c); S3.101 (K-23: stage 8's slots); S6.140 (the stage
table).
**Unit tests**: `slots_in_time6_order`, `non_business_runs_time8_list`, `later_read_refused`,
`day_zero_runs_stage_five_only`,
`closed_countries_skip_business_slots`, `stage_eight_slots_business_only`, `trips_read_all_loads`,
`barrier_counts_within_budget`, `h_day_runs_every_business_slot`.
**Live checks**: none (the runner's own at S1.186).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: ≈ 45 slots; ≤ 40 / 20 / 48 barriers a day (B / NB / H).
- Unit targets: the runner's own walk of the table (routing, empty slots, spans) ≤ 2 ms a day.
- its share of fin.fixed.barriers: 2 / 2 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- `ledger line 1 (process baseline): +0 B (named slot: the table, < 100 KB of build data)`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.stages]` (added) `runner_us` 2 000.
**Guards**: PC-21 re-aimed: the code names only the table's slots (`SlotOrdinal`s), never the retired sub-steps.
**Not allowed**: an order of the day written in code; a slot reading a later stage; a business-only slot on a closed
day;
a trip reading only the trips placed before it.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `StageTable`, the read-tag check, modes and their tests; the carriers moved; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117): none (build data); the runner's spans report rows visited per slot through
  `ExecCounters::visited` (S1.186).
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F stages` at the design point within `[fin.stages]`.
- [ ] §6.1–§6.3 and §7.3 "The stage table" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.186 — The day runner walks the stage table

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §6.1 (the day) and §7.18 (the day runner and saves) written.
**Depends on**: S1.185 (the stage table); S1.182 (kinds and families on handles, so routing needs no name); S1.177
(the stream families' `open_at`, to which the world's callers move).
**Goal**: `phx-world::day` walks the stage table: for each slot that runs today it routes the slot's base kernel or rule
set, in the table's order, with its barrier; the hand-sequenced day, the per-day clone of the regions and the systems'
states found by string and downcast each day are gone.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day.rs` | `core_day` (`day.rs`) replaced by `run_day(table, mode)`: slot by slot, each routed to its handler |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_day.rs` | the day's wrappers `gather`, `after_settle`, `after_settlement` and `keep_books` dissolved: each call inside them becomes its own route in its slot (7a, 7c, 7c, 10c), and the wrappers are deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/route.rs` | the routing table: slot → the call into today's `core_*` code (which later mechanism steps replace by `sys-*` rules) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/world.rs` | systems' own states bound once at assembly by `SystemCode` handle (no per-day `find` + `downcast_ref`, `day.rs`) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/substep.rs` | the 46 old sub-steps and `SUB_STEPS` deleted, their users now on the table |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/substeps.rs` | PC-21 reads the table's slots |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-98.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- Carries TIME.6, TIME.8 and TIME.10 (done at earlier steps): the carriers at `phx-world/src/day.rs` move to
  `run_day` and its routes.
- `run_day(day, mode)`: open the day (K-19's facts, K-20's values in force), then for each slot of the table that runs
  today (business-only slots only for countries with a business day; NB slots per TIME.8) call its route, time its span
  with items (K-15), and place the barrier the slot declares; the day's record keeps a span per slot.
- Today's calls move into slots, unchanged in what they do: weather → 3a; `measure_rates` → 10d; `run_hazards` → 3b;
  `labour_day` → 5b–5d (its parts by slot as they are today, split later by the labour steps); `goods_day` →
  4a/5b/6a–6b; `ship` → 4a and
  6a; `run_day` of settlement → 7a–7c; `audit` → 10c; `stats_day` → 9d; publications → 10a; `player_day` → 1b. Their
  order is the order `day.rs` runs today, which the table admits (a finding otherwise: a call that reads a later
  stage's write moves to the slot that reads yesterday's).
- The world's stream callers move from `open(…, SubStep)` to `open_at` with their slot's ordinal (S1.177), which
  retires the old form; the draws change once, here (S1.176).
- The year's first day's refresh of windows (`day.rs`) becomes a declared 5a rule reading K-19's `year_end`.
- `self.regions.clone()` per day (`day.rs`) goes: routes take `&regions`; `retail_weights` read by name each day
  (`day.rs`) is bound once at assembly (S1.146's handle).
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-98.toml` (states found by name each day) and `exceptions/PC-99.toml` (the
  per-day clone).

**Edge cases**:
- E11: day zero walks stage 5 only (S1.185's mode) — `day_zero_routes_stage_five`.
- E13: a day closed in every country runs only the NB slots — `nb_day_runs_nb_slots`.
- E5: a heavy day runs the same slots with more work, its barriers within 48 — `heavy_day_routes_same_slots`.

**Extension points**: S1.401 (the runner routes stage 3b).
**Unit tests**: `routes_cover_every_running_slot`, `day_zero_routes_stage_five`, `nb_day_runs_nb_slots`,
`heavy_day_routes_same_slots`.
**Live checks**: every Stage 0–1 live check, unchanged, read on the bench's run.
**Budget**:
- Day cost: the runner within S1.185's share of `fin.fixed.barriers` (≤ 2 ms); the per-day clone of the regions and the
  systems' states found by name go; the bench's spans, now one per slot, otherwise unchanged (a measure of code, never
  read as the world's).
- No ledger line changes (the per-day clone of the regions was a transient allocation).
- Ratchets: none added.
**Guards**: PC-21 re-aimed at the table's slots; `exceptions/PC-98.toml`, `PC-99.toml` lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an order of calls outside the table; a system state found by name on a day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `run_day` over the table; `day.rs`'s hand sequence, the old sub-steps' users and the per-day lookups deleted; the
      fast checks pass; the exceptions lowered.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` reads the budget at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken; every live check that passed
  before passes.
- [ ] §6.1 and §7.18 written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.187 — Networks and routes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.4 (phx-geo), "Networks and routes", written.
**Depends on**: S1.168 (route keys interned); S1.162 (routes rebuilt at load by the `Rebuild` pass).
**Goal**: the network is a table of segments with their capacity a day, condition, closure and owner's unit; routes
between places are flat arrays of segment ids found in O(1) by (mode, origin, destination) and recomputed only for a
region whose segment closes or opens.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/network.rs` | `Segments` (32 B rows) replacing `Network { segments: Vec<Segment> }`; modes as declared data (the `ROAD`/`RAIL`/`SEA` consts, `network.rs`, retired) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/routes.rs` | `Routes`: dense (mode, origin, destination) → path in an arena; `route`, `recompute(region)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/network_tests.rs` | unit tests over hand-built networks |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/routes.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[store] segments`; a struck region's recompute) |
| `perf/design.toml` | `[store] segments` (added) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.routes]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.4 "Networks and routes" |

**Design**:
- **Segment row** (32 B, `Pod`): from zone u16, to zone u16 (or a cell's end, S1.190), mode u8 (a declared mode handle),
  condition class u8, flags u16 (closed), length m u32, free-flow time s u32, capacity a day u32 (in the mode's declared
  unit: tonnes, vehicles, MW for a line), closed-until day u32 (or none), named unit u32 (the segment as owned capital,
  S1.284: its owner is its unit's holder, one writer; GEO.4), pad.
- **Routes**: per mode, a dense table over (origin, destination) at **region** resolution (25 × 25: freight, crossings)
  and, for the regions a travel rule declares, at **zone** resolution within a region (≈ 40 × 40 at `[resolution] zones`
  1 000); an entry is (offset u32, length u16, metres u32, free-flow s u32) into a path arena of segment
  ids (u32). `route(mode, o, d)` is two reads; a pair with no path is `Missing` (E2). Paths are Dijkstra over the open
  segments (the opening's generation, `network.rs`, kept), recomputed at 3a for a region one of whose segments closed
  or reopened (a catastrophe's closure, FRT.7, GEO.8), over that region's segments only.
- **Use**: a segment's use on a day is S1.188's; this step keeps no load.
- **Change hook**: a segment opened or removed calls the hooks declared on `Segments` in the same apply (S1.190's
  per-tile segment index), so what is derived from the segments' lines is never stale.
- **Save/load**: segments and their closures are saved (state: condition, closures, owners' units); routes are rebuilt
  at load from the open segments (`#[saved(skip, rebuild = …)]`, S1.162).
- Replaces (S1.189): `core_freight.rs`'s `lengths` and `routes` maps (`core_freight.rs`), route clones
  (`core_freight.rs`), `network.rs`'s `BTreeMap` route lengths.
**Edge cases**:
- E1: a region struck: its segments closed for days, its routes recomputed without them; a shipment whose route has
  none waits or is stranded by its rule — `closure_recomputes_region_routes`.
- E2: no route between two places reads `Missing`; the carriage meeting fails visibly (MKT.10) — `no_route_is_missing`.
- E6: routes rebuilt at load equal the saved world's — `routes_rebuild_equals`.
- E7: a recompute's paths do not depend on the worker count — `recompute_same_for_any_workers`.

**Extension points**: S1.188 (segments, capacities and routes); S1.189 (the route table); S1.190 (K-28's per-tile
segment index, fed at a segment's opening and removal through the segments' change hook); S1.284 (K-26: the path a line
or road follows); S1.314 (lines as segments with capacity); S2.160 (K-26 segments with capacity and condition); S2.172
(K-26 routes, segment capacity, daily use by epoch); S2.202 (K-26: power lines as network segments with capacity);
S5.131 (K-26); S5.175 (K-26); S6.134 (the map: segments along their cells, their capacity, condition and closure).
**Unit tests**: `route_is_shortest_open_path`, `no_route_is_missing`, `closure_recomputes_region_routes`,
`recompute_same_for_any_workers`, `routes_rebuild_equals`, `change_hook_called_on_open_and_remove`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**:
- Volumes: `perf/design.toml [store] segments` (≤ 0.5 M at `[resolution] zones` 1 000, ≈ 1 M at 2 000); routes 3
  modes × 625 region pairs + ≤ 25 regions × 1 600 zone pairs × 2 modes at 1 000 zones (6 400 at 2 000).
- Access: route reads at decisions and meetings; 3a recomputes the struck regions' routes only.
- Unit targets: a route read 2 VM ns; a region's recompute ≤ 10 ms.
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +19 MB resident (≤ 0.5 M segments × 32 B = 16 MB + routes' tables and arena ≈ 3
  MB)`; ≈ 42 at 2 000 zones (32 + 10).
- Ratchets: `[fin.routes]` (added) `route_ns` 2, `recompute_ms` 10, `mb` 19 (42 at 2 000 zones).
**Guards**: PC-23 (places belong to phx-geo) holds.
**Not allowed**: a route found by search on a day path; a route map keyed by a tuple; a route recomputed outside its
region's closure or reopening.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `Segments`, `Routes` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for segments and routes; recomputes report rows through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F routes` at the design point within `[fin.routes]`.
- [ ] §7.4 "Networks and routes" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.188 — The day's use of the network as pair flows

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: GEO.20 PROCESS *(part: the day's use of each segment as the fixed point of the day's trips; the trips and
their choices are S2.172's)*
**Architecture**: §7.4 (phx-geo), "The day's use", written.
**Depends on**: S1.187 (segments, capacities and routes); S1.166 (a segment's load is stamped by day, so no reset pass
runs); S1.164 (the lot's draws over crossing pairs); S1.185 (stage 4's slots 4b and 4c).
**Goal**: each segment's use today is the exact sum of every trip placed on it that day, counted as flows per (origin
zone, destination zone, mode) rather than per trip, and each trip's time is read at the loads all the day's trips put
on its legs; the kernel's cost follows the active pairs, not the trips.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/use_.rs` | `SegmentUse`: day-stamped loads; `add_flows`, `time_at(pair)`, `admit` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/use_tests.rs` | unit tests over hand-built networks and flows |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/routes.rs` | the `-F` driver's use part (the active pairs of a working day at `[resolution] zones`) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.day_use]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.4 "The day's use" |

**Design**:
- **Flows, not trips**: at 4b the travel rules (S2.172) hand the day's trips as counts per (origin zone, destination
  zone, mode), summed by the rules' own shards in integers; a pair's flow adds itself to each segment of its route
  (S1.187) as one item through the partitioned apply by segment range (S1.170); each range sums into the segment's
  day-stamped load (a stamp ≠ today reads as zero load: no reset pass, S1.166).
- **Times at the full load** (GEO.20): only when every pair's flow is summed does 4c read each pair's time: Σ over its
  route's legs of the leg's time at its load against its capacity by the mode's declared congestion function (a
  TECHNOLOGY primitive of GEO, e.g. free-flow time × (1 + a·(load/capacity)ᵇ), its numbers from the register). Every
  trip of a pair reads the pair's time, so every trip reads the load all of the day's trips put on its legs, never only
  those placed before it; sums are integers, so the result is the same for any order and worker count.
- **Capacity** (GEO.13): after the sums, the segments whose load passed their capacity are taken in segment-id order;
  each admits its capacity across the pairs crossing it by one multivariate hypergeometric draw over their
  still-admitted
  flows, on the lot stream the travel rule names (REP.22); a pair's refused trips leave its other legs' loads before a
  later segment is read, and return to their rule, which decides what they do. A segment's settled use never exceeds
  its capacity; the audit recounts it (GEO.13).
- **Freight's use**: the carriage meeting books its shipments' tonnes as flows of its (origin, destination, mode) on
  the same loads (S1.189).
- **Save/load**: nothing saved (a save is at a close; loads are the day's).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a working day's trips as ≈ 40 k active pairs in one apply — `pair_flows_sum_exactly`.
- E7: loads summed as integers by range; times read after all sums — `use_same_for_any_workers`, `trips_read_all_loads`.
- E13: a day with no trips reads zero loads by stamp — `stale_stamp_reads_zero`.
- GEO.13: a segment's load past capacity admits by lot up to capacity, the refused leaving the pair's other legs —
  `over_capacity_admits_by_lot`.

**Extension points**: S1.189 (the day's use, on which carriage books its flows); S1.314 (the day's use of lines and
segments); S2.172 (the day's use: trips as counts per (origin zone, destination zone, mode), maintained by job and home
events); S6.134 (the map: a segment's use today, read by its stamp).
**Unit tests**: `pair_flows_sum_exactly`, `trips_read_all_loads`, `use_same_for_any_workers`, `stale_stamp_reads_zero`,
`over_capacity_admits_by_lot`, `congestion_time_rises_with_load`.
**Live checks**: none (LC-2's travel checks arrive with S2.172).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: ≈ 40 k active (origin zone, destination zone, mode) pairs on a working day at `[resolution] zones` 1 000
  (≈ 100 k at 2 000), ≈ 10 legs a route (≈ 0.4 M load items); carriage bookings ≈ 0.1 M a business day.
- Access: 4b/4c on days with trips.
- Unit targets: a load item scattered and summed ≤ 2.3 VM ns; a pair's time ≤ 10 VM ns a leg; ≈ 1 core-ms a working
  day at the count above (≈ 2.5 at 2 000 zones), S2.172 stating the share of `fin.fixed.day_use` it calls.
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +4 MB resident (≤ 0.5 M segments × 8 B load and stamp)`; 8 at 2 000 zones; the
  pair flows are a day buffer at 4b–4c (≤ 1 MB, below the day's maximum, S1.161).
- Ratchets: `[fin.day_use]` (added) `load_ns` 2.3, `pair_time_ns` 10.
**Guards**: PC-99 refuses a per-meeting segment array.
**Not allowed**: a load per trip; a trip reading only the loads placed before it; loads reset by a pass; a segment's use
past its capacity settled.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `SegmentUse` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for the loads; 4b/4c report items through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F routes` (the use part) at the design point within `[fin.day_use]`.
- [ ] §7.4 "The day's use" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.189 — Freight's routes onto the route table

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.4 (phx-geo) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.187 (the route table); S1.188 (the day's use, on which carriage books its flows).
**Goal**: freight reads its routes and books its segments' use through the route table: the route maps, per-meeting
segment arrays and route clones in `core_freight.rs` are deleted, and the carriage kernel reads `Routes` and
`SegmentUse`.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | `Freight::lengths`, `Freight::routes` (built at assembly), the consignment's cloned segments, the per-meeting tonnes, `route` deleted |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/carriage.rs` | the carriage meeting reads `Routes::route` and books loads on `SegmentUse` (capacity per segment per day) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- Users move by function: `weigh` (`core_freight.rs`) reads a route's metres from `Routes`; `meet_carriage` takes
  each
  consignment's route by (mode, origin region, destination region) and books its tonnes on each segment through
  `SegmentUse` as a flow of its (origin, destination, mode) on the day-stamped loads (S1.188), a full segment refusing
  the rest as today (FRT.9, GEO.13); departures and arrivals
  unchanged.
- `Freight::modes` (`BTreeMap<PartyKey, u16>`) is the carriers' mode, a firm column that moves with K-32
  (S1.196–S1.198), not here.
- Behaviour unchanged: the same routes (Dijkstra over the same segments) and the same capacities.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (the two `BTreeMap`s) and `exceptions/PC-99.toml` (the clones and the
  per-meeting `Vec`).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a pair with no route: the consignment fails visibly, as today — `no_route_consignment_fails`.
- E1: a closed segment's routes recomputed at 3a; the day's carriage reads the new routes —
  `carriage_reads_recomputed_routes`.

**Extension points**: S1.466 (freight routes onto the route table); S8.132 (K-26 routes).
**Unit tests**: `carriage_books_route_loads`, `no_route_consignment_fails`, `carriage_reads_recomputed_routes`.
**Live checks**: the Stage 1 FRT live checks, unchanged, read on the bench's run.
**Budget**:
- Day cost: the `freight` span falls by its map lookups and route clones (a measure of code, never read as the world's);
  carriage's bookings are its share of `fin.fixed.real`, stated with freight's mechanism (S1.466).
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +0 B (named slot: freight's route maps go; routes are S1.187's figure)`.
- Ratchets: none added.
**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-92.toml` and `PC-99.toml` lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a route cloned per consignment.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The maps, arrays and clones deleted; freight on the route table; the fast checks pass; the exceptions lowered.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` reads the budget at the committed resolution; no ratchet broken; the Stage 1 freight checks pass.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.190 — Cells and the ground things stand on

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: GEO.19 STATE; GEO.5 STATE *(part: land held apart as parcels, their owner and cost; the holding at S1.271)*
**Architecture**: §7.4 (phx-geo), "Cells", written.
**Depends on**: S1.162 (the tile directory rebuilt at load; the round-trip harness); S1.187 (K-26 segments, whose
lines the per-tile segment index lists); S1.172 (a split parcel's cost apportioned with a named residue).
**Goal**: every tile is divided into 100 m cells whose identity, coordinates, surface and terrain are arithmetic on the
tile's; land held apart from its tile is stored as parcels, one row per rectangle of cells; a path's cells are computed
from its segment's line through a per-tile segment index; a building's cell is its named unit's site. No row is kept
per cell, so empty land, land under buildings and the ground under a road cost nothing.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/cells.rs` | `CellId` (tile × cells a tile + index, u32), cell arithmetic; `Parcels`: per-tile sorted runs of rectangles held apart; `SegmentIndex`: per-tile segment lists; `parcel_at`, `held`, `crossing`, `cells_of` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/cells_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/cells.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[store] parcels` inserted, split and looked up; `segment_tiles` built; crossings read) |
| `data/shared/GEO.toml` | `GEO.cell_m` = 100 (RESOLUTION the owner fixed, E 29; no valve) declared |
| `perf/design.toml` | `[resolution] cell_m`; `[store] parcels`, `segment_tiles`; `[bytes] parcel` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.cells]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.4 "Cells" |

**Design**:
- **The cell size** is the owner's (GEO.18, GEO.19, E 29; §12): `GEO.cell_m` 100 in the register, fixed like the 10 km
  grid and no RESOLUTION valve (N8.5); the design point's `[resolution] cell_m` reads it.
- **Arithmetic**: cells a tile = (tile side ÷ `cell_m`)² = 10 000 ≤ 2¹⁶; `CellId(u32)` = tile × cells a tile + index,
  tiles × cells a tile < 2³² checked at assembly; a cell's row and column in its tile are index ÷ and mod the side's
  cells, its coordinates its tile's origin plus its offset, its surface and terrain its tile's — computed, never stored
  (GEO.14: no second map). Distance between cells is the closed surface's (GEO.2), from the coordinates.
- **A building's cell is its site** (HSG.21): a named unit that stands on a cell — a building, a mine, a farm's plant —
  carries its `CellId` in its own row (S1.284); nothing is kept here for it. What stands on a cell or tile is read
  through S1.284's named units by tile.
- **Parcels** (GEO.5): land held apart — owned or leased apart from its tile — is one row per parcel, a rectangle of
  cells within one tile: a directory of the tiles × u32 (each tile's run offset in a chunk arena, K-04, with the run's
  tallest parcel u8), each run sorted by origin: cost i64 · owner u32 · origin cell index u16 · width u8 · height u8
  (≤ the side's 100 cells) · why held u16 (owned apart, leased apart: declared flags) = 18 B, 24 B aligned. Parcels in
  a tile never overlap. `parcel_at(cell)`: a binary search to the last origin row at or before the cell's, then back
  while origin row + the tallest height passes it, a rectangle test each (≤ 60 ns). The writer lays a holding of n
  cells as at most two rectangles in a tile (full rows of a width and one row of the rest); a part sold or leased
  apart is cut out by guillotine cuts, the part and at most three rectangles left, each its own row, the cost
  apportioned by cells with the named residue (S1.172).
- **Owned apart** (GEO.5): the parcel row is where land held apart lives; the holdings read it as a holding of place
  kind "parcel" (S1.271) and write its owner and cost only through their transfer, so the owner has one writer (Law 4).
  A lease is a land-lease contract on that holding (S2.139); the parcel stores no lessee. No named unit is kept for a
  parcel.
- **Paths** (GEO.19): a path's cells are not stored. Each K-26 segment's ends have coordinates (its zones' nodes or a
  cell's end, S1.187); the **segment index** — a directory of the tiles × u32 into a chunk arena of segment ids u32,
  each tile listing the segments whose line crosses it — is fed at a segment's opening and removal through K-26's
  change hook (S1.187's extension point; `index_segment`, `unindex_segment`) and rebuilt at load. `crossing(cell)` reads its tile's list and tests
  each segment's line against the cell (the line's supercover in integer arithmetic); `cells_of(segment)` walks the
  cells its line crosses.
- **Held** (GEO.19): `held(cell)` — a named unit's site, a parcel covering it or a segment crossing it — is a read of
  the three; no cell is held without one of them, and none is held by a row of its own.
- **Release**: a parcel row goes when its land is no longer held apart; a segment's entries go with it.
- **Save/load**: parcels saved (state); both directories and the segment index rebuilt (S1.162), the index from K-26's
  segments.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a tile with nothing held costs its two directory words — `empty_tile_costs_nothing`.
- E10: a building demolished: its site goes with its unit; a parcel no longer held apart released —
  `release_when_not_held_apart`.
- E6: parcels round-trip; the directories and the segment index rebuilt equal — `cells_roundtrip`,
  `segment_index_rebuilt_equal`.
- E8: a split keeps the parcel's cells and cost exactly, the residue named — `split_keeps_cells_and_cost`; tiles × cells
  a tile past u32 refused at assembly — `cell_id_fits_u32`.
- E9: parcels grow with land held apart and go with it; index entries with segments — `rows_bounded_by_holdings`.
- GEO.19: a parcel overlapping another or leaving its tile refused at the apply — `overlapping_parcel_refused`; a path's
  cells are its segment's line's — `path_cells_from_segment_line`.
- GEO.5: a parcel carries its owner and cost, written only by the holdings' transfer —
  `parcel_written_by_transfer_only`.

**Extension points**: S1.274 (recorded cells: a unit on one is not in the counted stock); S1.271 (K-28: a parcel, its owner and cost); S1.284 (K-28:
the cell a unit stands on); S1.287 (K-28: a process's own site cell); S2.139 (K-28 parcels leased apart); S2.140 (the
opening's parcels); S2.155 (K-28 parcels sold, leased and split); S2.169 (K-28 cells held only when something stands on
them); S2.175 (parcels as the land market's items); S2.203 (K-28: sites on cells); S6.134 (the map: sites, parcels and
paths' cells by tile).
**Unit tests**: `cell_arithmetic_from_tile`, `cell_id_fits_u32`, `parcel_lookup_in_sorted_run`,
`insert_keeps_run_sorted`, `overlapping_parcel_refused`, `split_keeps_cells_and_cost`, `path_cells_from_segment_line`,
`crossing_reads_tile_index`, `empty_tile_costs_nothing`, `release_when_not_held_apart`, `rows_bounded_by_holdings`,
`parcel_written_by_transfer_only`, `cells_roundtrip`, `segment_index_rebuilt_equal`.
**Live checks**: none (LC-2-52 — every unit in a building on its cell, every parcel with a reason — arrives with
S2.169).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: parcels ≤ 1.0 M (S2.140: the land holdings held apart, ≤ 0.3 M farms and land-using firms and ≈ 0.2 M
  leased shares, each at most two rectangles); the segment index ≈ 1.0 M entries (≤ 0.5 M segments at 1 000 zones ×
  ≈ 2 tiles, `[store] segment_tiles`); inserts, splits and releases with land sales and construction (a few thousand a
  day).
- Access: event-driven; parcel lookups at decisions that read a place (a builder's parcels, a sale, a strike's
  footprint); `crossing` and `cells_of` at a footprint's reach and the map (S6.134), never on a pass.
- Unit targets: a parcel lookup ≤ 60 VM ns; an insert or split ≤ 1 VM µs; `crossing(cell)` ≤ 150 VM ns (≈ 25
  segments a tile, a line test each); a segment's index update ≤ 1 VM µs. No share of its own on the day: its users'
  shares carry their reads.
- `ledger line 12 (physical units, cells, owner index): +37.7 MB resident (≤ 1.0 M parcels × 24 B at three-quarters
  fill = 32.0 MB; the segment index ≈ 1.0 M × 4 B at three-quarters fill = 5.3 MB and the two tile directories 0.4 MB,
  which follow the segments and tiles, not the persons)`; buildings and leases add no row, and paths none. saved: +24 MB
  (the parcels; the index and directories rebuilt).
- Ratchets: `[fin.cells]` (added) `lookup_ns` 60, `crossing_ns` 150, `mb` 38.
**Guards**: PC-23 (places belong to phx-geo) holds; GEO.14's "no second map": no cell geometry stored.
**Not allowed**: a dense cell grid; a row per cell; a path's cells stored; a cell's coordinates or terrain stored; a
lessee stored on a parcel; an owner written other than by the holdings' transfer; a row beside a building's site; a
named unit per parcel; overlapping parcels; a parcel held for no reason.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `CellId`, `Parcels`, `SegmentIndex`, `GEO.cell_m` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for parcels and the segment index; lookups report rows through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F cells` at the design point within `[fin.cells]`.
- [ ] §7.4 "Cells" written; GEO.19's row in §13; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.191 — The deposits register

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.4 (phx-geo), "Deposits", written (today's §7.8 "Deposits on the core" restated).
**Depends on**: S1.183 (each deposit's resource at its grade and zone is a registry unit, and its extraction right a
registry unit of kind `right`); S1.170 (extractions applied by deposit range); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every deposit is one 32 B row — tile, resource unit, grade, opening quantity (or unbounded), extracted to date
—
whose extracted total is written only by extraction transformations that name the deposit as their source; what remains
is a read; the right to extract is a registry unit a holder holds.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/deposits.rs` | `Deposits` register (rows by deposit id) beside the opening's draw (`deposits.rs`, kept); `extract_batch`, `remaining`, `grade_now` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/deposits_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/deposits.rs` | the `-F` driver (`[store] deposits`; a day's extractions) |
| `perf/design.toml` | `[store] deposits` (added, S1.437's count) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.deposits]` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.4 "Deposits" |

**Design**:
- **Row** (32 B, `Pod`): tile u32, resource unit u32 (registry: product, grade class, zone), right unit u32 (registry
  kind
  `right`, keyed by the deposit), grade i32 (fixed-point at issue, `Fixed<3>` narrowed), opening u64 (`MaybeU64`: absent
  = unbounded, never a large number standing for infinity), extracted u64 (maintained). No `remaining` column: remaining
  = opening − extracted, a read (Law 4).
- **`extract_batch(items: [(deposit, extractor, units)])`**: partitioned by deposit range (S1.170); each item is a
  transformation leg (SET.9, Law 5) with the deposit as its source: extracted += units, checked; an item beyond what
  remains is a contract violation at the site (GEO.12, GDS.12: no commodity extracted where there is no deposit) — the
  extraction rule asks within `remaining`, read before it decides. `extract_batch` writes `extracted` only; the caller
  (S1.293) receives the extractor's units through the holdings in the same apply.
- **Grade as worked** (GEO.9's "where its nature is that the richest part goes first, its grade falls with what has been
  taken"): `grade_now(deposit)` reads the resource's declared grade-by-share-extracted (a TECHNOLOGY primitive of GDS)
  at extracted ÷ opening; the unit the extraction yields is the grade class the tercile falls in (GDS's three grade
  classes, today's data). GEO.9's completion is S1.293, where extraction moves onto this register.
- **Rights**: the right to extract is the right unit, held through holdings (K-60) from S1.293; this step issues each
  deposit's right unit at the opening and holds its row.
- **Save/load**: rows saved (extracted is state; GEO.12's identity is audited against it: extracted + remaining =
  opening, with remaining a read — the audit recounts extracted from the day's transformation legs, N1).
- Replaces (at S1.293): `core_deposits.rs`'s `Deposits { holders, extracted, remaining, opening, resources, draws, days,
  held: BTreeMap, working: BTreeMap }`, `open_rights` O(deposits × firms), `take_from_deposits`'s
  cloned list, `audit_deposits` every deposit every day.

**Edge cases**:
- GEO.12: extracted + remaining = opening for every finite deposit — `identity_holds_after_batches`.
- GEO.9: a worked deposit's grade falls with its share extracted — `grade_falls_with_share_extracted`.
- E8: extraction past what remains stops at the site — `over_extraction_stops`.
- E13: an unbounded deposit never depletes and has no remaining figure; reading one is `Missing` —
  `unbounded_has_no_remaining`.
- E7: a batch by deposit range gives the same totals for any workers — `batch_same_for_any_workers`.
- E14: two extractors on one deposit the same day: both items in one shard in declared order —
  `two_extractors_one_deposit`.
- E6: rows round-trip — `deposits_roundtrip`.

**Extension points**: S1.293 (K-29: each deposit's opening, extracted and resource, its right unit); S1.437 (the
deposits register: per deposit its grade and opening size); S8.131 (K-29: deposits).
**Unit tests**: `identity_holds_after_batches`, `over_extraction_stops`, `unbounded_has_no_remaining`,
`grade_falls_with_share_extracted`, `batch_same_for_any_workers`, `two_extractors_one_deposit`, `deposits_roundtrip`.
**Live checks**: none here (GEO.12's audit and LC-1 extraction checks at S1.293).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: `perf/design.toml [store] deposits` (≈ 50 k); ≈ 100 k extractions a day at the design point.
- Access: event-driven (extractions in their makers' batches, S1.293 stating the share).
- Unit targets: an extraction ≤ 7.7 VM ns (10 phone-ns) fused into its batch.
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +1.6 MB resident (≈ 50 k × 32 B)`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.deposits]` (added) `extract_ns` 7.7, `row_bytes` 32.
**Guards**: PC-25 re-aimed here: `extracted` written only by `extract_batch`.
**Not allowed**: a remaining column beside extracted; extraction beyond a deposit; a daily pass over every deposit; an
unbounded deposit given a number.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `Deposits` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for the register; batches report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F deposits` at the design point within `[fin.deposits]`.
- [ ] §7.4 "Deposits" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.192 — Weather history and catastrophe footprints

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.4 (phx-geo), "Weather and catastrophes", written.
**Depends on**: S1.167 (the weather's history is a horizon ring); S1.160 (the day's footprint is a day buffer); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: each region's weather of each day is a row of a horizon ring, each day's catastrophe footprint — struck tiles
with their severities — is a day buffer the day's losses read, and the weather's latents are the one piece of weather
state kept.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/weather.rs` | `WeatherRing`: (day, region) rows of four values; latents as fixed-point state per region |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/catastrophe.rs` | the day's footprint into a `DayBuf<(TileId, severity)>` (`hazard_day`, `footprint` kept) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-geo/src/weather_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/weather.rs` | the `-F` driver (the regions × the ring's horizon; a strike day's footprint) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.weather]` (added); `[fin.geo] mb` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.4 "Weather and catastrophes" |

**Design**:
- **Weather rows** (20 B): day u32 (the ring's), region u16, wind, sunshine, temperature, rainfall as `i32` fixed-point
  in
  their declared units, pad; one row per region per day, appended at 3a from `region_day` (`weather.rs`, unchanged
  arithmetic) in region order. The ring's horizon is the weather's declared RESOLUTION horizon (SET.13), floored by the
  longest window a reader declares (crop yields over a season, GDS.9; energy demand).
- **Latents**: each region's AR(1) latent per variable is state (saved), held as `Fixed` (no float in a store, NUM.6);
  `next_latent` reads and writes it at 3a.
- **Footprints**: `hazard_day` (`catastrophe.rs`) writes each struck tile and its severity into the day's footprint
  buffer (a `DayBuf`, released at 10e). The losses at owners read it at 3a (S1.294, through the place index); the
  public event recording it is written by the event log's migration (S1.214), not here.
- **Reads**: a region's weather on a day or over a window is a ring range (`range(from, to)`, O(log chunks + rows)).
- **Save/load**: the ring's live chunks and the latents are saved; the footprint is not (a day buffer).
- Its users in `core_weather.rs` move at S1.193.

**Edge cases**:
- E9: two years of weather hold exactly the horizon's rows — `weather_bounded_by_horizon`.
- E11: day zero holds no weather; the first day's latents start from the declared stationary state —
  `first_day_from_stationary`.
- E1: a catastrophe over many tiles: one footprint buffer — `large_footprint_one_buffer`.
- E6: ring and latents round-trip; the next day's weather is the same — `weather_roundtrip_continues`.
- E7: regions drawn on their own streams keyed by (region, day) — `weather_same_for_any_workers`.

**Extension points**: S1.193 (the weather ring, the latents' state and the footprint buffer); S1.214 (the day's
catastrophe footprint); S1.294 (K-30: the day's footprint); S1.463 (weather per region per day in its ring: the
temperature and rain a crop's yield reads); S2.202 (K-30: the day's weather per region); S2.207 (K-30: degree-days per
region per day, with their running sum); S2.210 (K-30: the day's weather, stage 3a).
**Unit tests**: `one_row_per_region_per_day`, `weather_bounded_by_horizon`, `first_day_from_stationary`,
`large_footprint_one_buffer`, `weather_roundtrip_continues`, `weather_same_for_any_workers`.
**Live checks**: none (the weather's LC-1 checks read on the bench's run from S1.193).
**Budget**:
- Volumes: 25 regions a day; the ring holds the regions × its horizon (≈ 18 k rows at two years); footprints ≈ 200 tiles
  on a strike day.
- Access: 3a every day, business or not; reads at decisions and publications.
- Unit targets: ≤ 1 VM µs a region a day (draw and append); a footprint ≤ 1 VM µs a region.
- its share of fin.fixed.real: 0.03 / 0.03 / 0.03 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- `ledger line 19 (map and network): +0.4 MB resident (≈ 18 k rows × 20 B)`; the footprint is a day buffer at 3a (< 0.01
  MB, below the day's maximum, S1.161).
- Line 19's parts at the design point (`[resolution] zones` 1 000), each stated by its step: tiles 0.5 and zone
  distances 2 (8 at 2 000 zones), segments and routes 19 (S1.187), loads 4 (S1.188), the units registry 3 (S1.183),
  deposits 1.6 (S1.191), weather 0.4 — ≈ 30.5 MB (≈ 66.5 at 2 000), read together by `-F all` against `[fin.geo] mb`.
- Ratchets: `[fin.weather]` (added) `region_day_us` 1, `footprint_us` 1; `[fin.geo]` (added) `mb` 31 (67 at 2 000
  zones).
**Guards**: PC-100 (S1.125) refuses a saved unbounded `Vec` of dated rows (the old `Weather::shocks` form) once the
horizons are in.
**Not allowed**: weather kept without a horizon; a float in a store; a footprint's tiles found by scanning parties.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `WeatherRing`, the latents' state, the footprint buffer and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `StoreStats` (S1.117) implemented for the ring; 3a reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F weather` at the design point within `[fin.weather]`; `[fin.geo] mb` read by `-F all`.
- [ ] §7.4 "Weather and catastrophes" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
