#### Parties, records and what is due: phx-pop, phx-record, phx-agenda (S1.194–S1.239)

These steps build the bases that hold the world's parties, what it keeps of its past and what falls due: the party
directory with its tombstones and successors, every party kind's typed columns at their fixed byte maps and windowed
groups, persons as parties threaded through their households, offices, the per-day cache (`phx-pop`); the event log with
a stored tier, the records store, the day ledger, statistics accumulators and sample frames, life records on storage,
tallies (`phx-record`); the due wheel, the decision agenda, hazards drawn ahead, messages and notices, the trigger index
(`phx-agenda`). Each base is measured alone at the design point by `tools/bench.sh -F` before behaviour is put on it;
each migration step after a base deletes the `phx-world` structure it replaces.

Exit: every party kind is a directory slot with generation and typed columns at its byte map, with its reserve named;
every reference that outlives a day resolves to live, ended (day, successor) or ended beyond the horizon; nothing
visits a party except its agenda entry, a due, a hazard hit, a message, a trigger crossed or a flow; every history is
kept within its declared horizon, resident or on storage.

The byte maps (bytes a row at the design point; reserves are the bytes later steps' declared attributes take, allocated
in ARCHITECTURE §13's memory ledger):

| Record | Bytes | Groups | Reserve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Person | 66 | core 32 · banknotes 4 · tax year 16 · mind 13 · experience 1 | 15 bits of the packed word |
| Campaign window | person 1 · household 2 | windowed, inside a country's campaign only | none |
| Household | 174 | hot 128 · warm 46 | 16 B (hot 10, warm 6) |
| Firm | 520 | hot 192 · warm 184 · cold 112 · lists 32 | 39 B (hot 22, warm 9, cold 4, lists 4) |
| Institution | per kind (most ≤ 1 024; unions, authorities ≈ 3 KB) | per kind, declared | per kind |
| Office | 16 | one | none |

Placeholders introduced: none. Placeholders retired: none (the `[fin.kept] due_ns` baseline ratchet of S1.119 is
replaced by S1.225's `[fin.wheel]`).

### S1.194 — The party directory: generations, tombstones and successors

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.5 (phx-pop) "The directory"; follows §7.1 (generation references, S1.159).
**Depends on**: S1.159 (K-02's generation tables and FIFO slot reuse behind the close); S1.174 (`PartyKey` 5 + 27 bits,
the kinds census ≤ 31 with NATURE); S1.113 (capacities per kind, `perf/design.toml [store]`); S1.160 (day buffers for
the day's endings).
**Goal**: One directory in `phx-pop` owns every party kind's slots and generations: a party's lasting identity is its
reference (kind, slot, generation). A reference resolves in O(1) to its live slot, or through a tombstone to "ended,
on its day, with its estate or successor", or to "ended before the horizon". This step builds it beside today's
tables; S1.195 moves the world onto it.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/directory.rs` | `Directory`, `Tomb`, `Resolved`; begin, end, resolve, follow, the day's close |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/directory_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/lib.rs` | module |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/parties.rs` | -F driver: the directory at `[store] directory_slots`, `tombstones` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.5 "The directory" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.parties]` keys below; `[store] directory_slots = 11_000_000` (added) |

**Design**:
- Per kind (a K-21 kind handle): K-02's slot allocator and generation column (`u32` a slot, 24 bits used), a live
  bitmap and a maintained live count (REP.13's count, read by the day ledger, S1.219).
- `Tomb`, 16 B `#[derive(Pod)]`: `ended: u64` = packed reference (kind 5 | slot 27 | generation 24) and the high byte
  of the end day's offset; `successor: u64` = packed reference or `NONE`, and the low byte. The offset counts days from
  the run's first day: 16 bits, a declared run capacity of 65 535 days (K-24; beyond it `capacity_exceeded!`).
- Tombstones in two runs sorted by packed reference: `main` and `recent` (appended at 10e). When `recent` passes a
  sixteenth of `main`, one sequential merge at 10e joins them and drops every tombstone ended before today − horizon.
  The horizon is the longest declared horizon of any record kind that may name a party (K-08 kinds, K-37, K-40's kept
  records), read at assembly: derived, not a primitive.
- API, the only way in: `begin(kind, day) -> PartyRef` (slot from K-02, reused FIFO and never within the day it was
  released; generation + 1; count + 1; the caller's kind store writes the party's columns in full, S1.196);
  `end(party, day, successor: Missing<PartyRef>)` (a party not live stops the run, PTY.9; it reads as ended at once
  while the day's instructions naming it settle against its successor, SET.7; the tombstone goes to the chunk's day
  buffer; the slot is released at 10e); `set_successor(ended, successor)` (an estate's own ending names its heir, L3);
  `resolve(r) -> Resolved { Live(slot) | Ended { day, successor } | EndedBeyondHorizon }` (generation equal and live:
  one gather; otherwise a binary search of `recent`, then `main`; not found: ended beyond the horizon, SET.13; a
  generation above the slot's current one was never issued and stops the run, PTY.13); `follow(r)` (successors
  followed to a live party or to one ended with none, PTY.10; O(chain)).
- Parallel: endings written from any chunk (2f, 3b) into per-chunk buffers; 10e sorts them by packed reference (K-12)
  and merges, so the runs are the same for any worker count.
- Measurement: `StoreStats` (slots live, ever, bytes, tombstones, growth a simulated year); the 10e merge reports rows
  visited through `ExecCounters::visited`. Save: generations, bitmaps, free lists, one merged tombstone run and the
  counts are primary; nothing rebuilt.
- The `#[clause("PTY.1")]` carrier (done at S0.09) moves from `phx_store::Parties` to `Directory` at S1.195.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: 115 k endings in a day: per-chunk buffers and one 10e merge (`mass_endings_one_merge`).
- E6: every column primary; references resolve alike after load (`save_round_trip_resolves_alike`).
- E7: runs sorted by reference whatever the chunking (`endings_in_any_chunk_order_same_runs`).
- E8: a 2²⁴th generation or a run past 65 535 days stops the run (`generation_overflow_stops`).
- E9: tombstones grow to the horizon, then flat (`pruned_past_horizon_reads_ended_beyond_horizon`).
- E10: an ended reference resolves to its day and successor; a reused slot refuses the old generation
  (`stale_generation_refused`, `ended_resolves_to_day_and_successor`).
- E11: day zero holds no tombstone; opening parties begin at generation 0 (`opening_begins_at_generation_zero`).

**Extension points**: S1.195 (the world's kinds take slots and references from it); S1.196; S1.207 (kind stores and the
person kind begin and end through it); S1.213; S1.215; S1.217; S1.219; S1.237 (a sender resolved through its
tombstone); S1.267; S1.268; S1.342; S1.345; S1.404 (births, deaths, households formed and ended); S2.136; S3.196;
S5.152; S5.155; S6.120.

**Unit tests**: `stale_generation_refused`; `ended_resolves_to_day_and_successor`; `successor_chain_followed_to_live`;
`successor_chain_ends_at_distributed_estate`; `slot_not_reused_within_its_day`;
`pruned_past_horizon_reads_ended_beyond_horizon`; `recent_merge_keeps_order_and_prunes`; `generation_overflow_stops`;
`unissued_generation_stops`; `endings_in_any_chunk_order_same_runs`; `mass_endings_one_merge`;
`opening_begins_at_generation_zero`; `save_round_trip_resolves_alike`.

**Live checks**: none (the audit's Names family reads it, S1.354).

**Budget**: volumes: `[store] directory_slots` (11.0 M), `tombstones` (0.84 M); begins and ends ≈ 1.1 k a day (B, NB,
H), 115 k on a mass-failure day. Access: event-driven; resolve O(1) live, O(log n) ended. Units: resolve 2.3 ns VM
fused, begin or end ≤ 100 ns, tombstone lookup ≤ 60 ns. its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB
/ H) (≈ 1.1 k begins and ends at ≤ 100 ns, and the 10e merge amortised; persons end on every day). on
fin.calendar.mass_default (E1: ≥ 10 % of firms ending on one day): 12 core-ms; joins H and B′ (S1.345's table). Resident bytes: ARCHITECTURE
§13's ledger line "Directory", 57 MB (4 B a slot, 16 B a tombstone). Ratchets `[fin.parties]`: `directory_mb` 57,
`resolve_ns` 2.3, `begin_end_ns` 100, `tomb_lookup_ns` 60, `mass_end_core_ms` 12 (all added).

**Guards**: PC-100 (S1.125) refuses a map keyed by a bare slot or `PartyKey` in saved state; slot allocation is
`phx-pop`'s alone (PC-15 snapshot).

**Not allowed**: an identity → slot table; a reference count per record; a tombstone kept for ever; a slot reused
within its day; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate (S1.195's); a store, index, map or per-party pass
outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Directory` built in `phx-pop`; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks (`fmt`, `clippy`, tests, `phx-check`) pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F parties` within `directory_mb`, `resolve_ns`, `begin_end_ns`, `tomb_lookup_ns`,
  `mass_end_core_ms` at the design point.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.5 "The directory" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

**Status**: planned

**Architecture**: writes §7.5 "Kind stores"; follows §7.4 (the kind catalogue compiles attributes, S1.180).
**Depends on**: S1.180 (K-21 compiles each kind's declared attributes to handles); S1.159 (generation-checked

(capacities).
**Goal**: Every party kind's state is fixed-width column groups by slot — hot split from cold — at the byte maps below,
each attribute a compiled handle read and written in O(1) behind the generation check. A party with nothing reads
`Missing` for every absent value; a reused slot is written in full at `begin`. The zone of each site is an attribute,
from which its region and country are read (PTY.5). This step builds the stores in `phx-pop`; S1.198–S1.206 move
today's kinds onto them.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/kinds.rs` | `KindStore`: groups, `Attr<T>` handles, begin, end, index hooks |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/layout.rs` | the byte maps as declarations, reserves, `const` size checks |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/kinds_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/parties.rs` | -F driver: `[store] households`, `firms`, `institutions` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.5 "Kind stores", with the byte maps and each word's owning base |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.parties]` keys below |

**Design**:
- A kind declares (K-21) its groups and attributes. A group is one `Pod` row a slot of declared width in a column
  reserved at capacity (K-01), 64-byte aligned where the width is a multiple of 64. A handle `Attr<T>` holds (group,
  offset, width, integer type, absent sentinel); `get(&self, r, a) -> Missing<T>` and `set(&mut self, r, a, v)` check
  the generation (a stale reference stops the run, PTY.10). Stores hold integers only (PC-12): outlooks are `Fixed` i32.
- Absent values: an attribute that can be absent declares its sentinel (`i64::MIN`, `u32::MAX`, `u16::MAX`); `get`
  returns `Missing::Absent`; writing the sentinel as a value stops the run (NUM.8).
- Byte maps (words declared by the bases named; reserves are declared-attribute space, allocated in ARCHITECTURE §13):
  - **Household 174 B** — *hot 128* (two lines): attributes 12 (residence place u32, tagged: a zone, or a building —
    S1.284's named unit, its zone read through its site, K-66 — from which region and country are read; tenure 2 bits,
    credit stage 3 bits and stance 3 bits in one byte; preference type u16; flags u8; formed day u32) · persons head u32
    (S1.207) · chain head u32 (K-53) · positions 24 (recent income, debt service, buffer target, i64; REP.20) · own
    outlooks 16 (income growth, job loss: level and width, `Fixed` i32; public variables' outlooks are per method,
    VAL.23) · agenda 58 (base day u32 + 27 next-day slots u16, S1.227) · reserve 10 — *warm 46*: two owner-named unit
    slots 40, each (owner u32: a person or a participation group, K-58 · unit id u32 · count u32 · cost i64; K-60) ·
    reserve 6. Money, holdings, units and debts are the persons' or their groups' (PTY.3); the household reads their sum
    over its slots and its persons' K-60 rows, and a person leaving takes its units to K-60 rows (REP.26).
  - **Firm 520 B** — *hot 192*: own and four input unit ids 20 · own product's stall u32 (K-71) · own stock units and
    cost 16 · four input stocks 64 (K-60) · work in progress 8 (K-69) · the exact rate row 20 (output rate Q32.32 i64,
    anchor day u32, realised count i64; input-use rates are reads of it × the way's declared inputs a unit, K-68) · unit
    cost i64 and its day stamp u16 10 (K-35) · sales since review 16 · expected-sales trigger 8 · flags 4 · reserve 22
    — *warm 184*: agenda 52 (base + 24 slots) · sales outlook 12 · wage bill i64, staff hours 4 × u32, plant capacity
    i64 (K-54, K-67) · plant occupancy mask and flags u32, overflow run u32 (K-60) · own stock committed i64 (K-60) ·
    identity 21 (account u32, zone u16, legal form u8, flags u8, types: founding preferences, memory, stance u8 each,
    head's office u32, industry u16, founded day u32) · markup `Fixed` i32, productivity i32, last price review u16
    (S1.198) · equity i64, net assets i64 (K-88) · cumulative output per way 2 × u64 (K-68) · reserve 9 — *cold 112*:
    income-statement lines 10 × i64 (K-87) · tax accrued 2 × i64 (K-51) · trade-credit terms id u32 (K-55) · equity
    issued i64 (K-64) · reserve 4 — *list headers 32*: employer, invoice seller, invoice buyer (block u32, length u16,
    dead u16 each), holder-chain head u32 (K-53) · reserve 4. Beyond four inputs, plant classes or sites: K-60's rows.
  - **Institution**: per kind, declared groups, the record's width declared by its kind (most ≤ 1 024 B; unions and
    public authorities ≈ 3 KB), their slots declared per kind (S1.227).
  - Reserve allocations: firm 39 B (41 before S4.120's `carry` slot took 2 B of the warm reserve into the agenda) —
    S1.426 4, S1.441 1, S1.458 8 (`CAP.invest_stamp`), S1.461 4, S2.109 3, S2.123 3, S5.104 1, S6.103 4, S6.106 8,
    S8.104 2; 1 spare. Household 16 B — S2.109 3, S3.158 10, S6.124 2 (`DEM.divergence`); 1 spare. Person (S1.207): the
    1 B reserve is S8.197's `experience`; 15 word bits spare.
- A declaration that does not fit its group's reserve is refused at assembly (K-21), naming the kind, group and bytes;
  widening a group is a ratchet change stated in its step.
- `begin(r, init)` writes every group's row in full (declared openings or sentinels); `end(r)` leaves the row until
  the slot's next `begin`. Index instances (K-06) on a kind are maintained by `set` through the instance's hook.
- Parallel: reads by `&self` over agenda chunks; writes only to the chunk's own slots (§6.6's R3).
- Measurement: `StoreStats` a kind (rows live, ever, bytes a group, growth a year); traversals report rows visited
  through `ExecCounters::visited`. Save: groups raw (K-10); cache words (S1.211) saved absent; index instances rebuilt
  in slot order.
- Replaces `phx_core::store::KindStore` (`crates/kernel/phx-core/src/store.rs`, row-major `MaybeI64` words read
  through checked slicing); its kinds move at S1.198–S1.206, the last of which deletes it. The clause carriers of
  REP.20 (done at S1.12), REP.41 (S0.28), PTY.4 and PTY.6 (S0.09) move to `KindStore` with those migrations.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a party with nothing reads `Missing` (`absent_reads_missing`, `sentinel_write_stops`).
- E6: groups saved raw; index instances rebuilt equal (`save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`).
- E7: writes only to own chunk's slots (`chunk_writes_disjoint`).
- E8: a declaration beyond its group's reserve is refused (`overfull_group_refused`).
- E10: a stale reference is refused; `begin` on a reused slot overwrites every byte (`stale_reference_refused`,
  `reused_slot_written_in_full`).
- E13: a kind with no parties reads nothing (`empty_kind_reads_nothing`).
- E14: two writes to one attribute the same day are its one declared writer's (`one_writer_per_attribute`).

**Extension points**: S1.197 (windowed groups); S1.198; S1.199; S1.201; S1.205; S1.207 (persons head); S1.209; S1.211
(cache words); S1.219; S1.227 (agenda slots); S1.240; S1.244; S1.253 (tax accrued); S1.258; S1.261 (K-54 aggregates);
S1.271; S1.274; S1.279; S1.324; S1.328; S1.342; S1.350 (the wake scan reads the households' 12 B attributes); S1.404;
S1.407; S1.426; S1.441; S1.458; S1.461; S1.481; S2.109; S2.148; S2.179; S3.114; S3.158; S8.104; S4.102; S4.120 (the firm
agenda's `carry` slot); S4.142; S4.143; S5.104; S5.136; S6.103; S6.106; S6.120; S6.124; S6.131; S6.133.

**Unit tests**: `absent_reads_missing`; `sentinel_write_stops`; `stale_reference_refused`;
`reused_slot_written_in_full`; `overfull_group_refused`; `household_layout_is_174_bytes`; `firm_layout_is_520_bytes`;
`firm_hot_is_192_bytes`; `index_instance_follows_set`; `chunk_writes_disjoint`; `empty_kind_reads_nothing`;
`one_writer_per_attribute`; `save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**: volumes `[store] households`, `firms`, `institutions`; view gathers 1.6 M / 0.9 M / 1.6 M a day; the wake
scan 3.35 M hot records on a surprise day. Units: a household visit gathers its 128 B hot row (2 lines), a firm visit
hot and warm (≤ 6 lines); attribute get ≤ 1 ns after the gather; wake scan 3.8 ns VM a record. It adds no stage line of
its own (reads ride the decisions' units). ledger line 4 (households): +384.5 MB resident (2.21 M × 174 B). ledger line 5
(firms): +599 MB resident (1.152 M × 520 B). ledger line 6 (institutions): +18 MB resident (15 k × ≤ 1 024 B + 1 k
unions × 3 KB; the public authorities are among the 15 k). Ratchets `[fin.parties]`: `household_bytes` 174,
`household_hot_bytes` 128 (added), `firm_bytes` 520, `firm_hot_bytes` 192, `wake_scan_ns` 3.8, `faults_per_day` 0,
`attr_ns` 1 (added).

**Guards**: PC-12 (integers only); PC-92 as extended by S1.120; `const` size checks in `layout.rs` (compile level).

**Not allowed**: a map keyed by party; a `MaybeI64` word read by index; a float in a store; a default for an absent
attribute; a group widened without its ratchet; a per-kind branch; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate;
a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `phx-pop::KindStore` built with the byte maps and handles; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F parties` within `household_bytes`, `household_hot_bytes`, `firm_bytes`, `firm_hot_bytes`,
  `wake_scan_ns`, `attr_ns`, `faults_per_day`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.5 "Kind stores" written with the byte maps and reserves.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.197 — Windowed groups: columns that exist only within a dated window

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.5 "Windowed groups".
**Depends on**: S1.196 (kind groups and handles); S1.166 (epoch stamps, K-07); S1.178 (the calendar's day facts for a
window's open and close days).
**Goal**: A kind can declare a group that exists only inside a dated window — a campaign's voting intentions and vote
occasions — allocated in reserved address space when its window opens, committed only where written, read as
`Missing` outside the window, saved while open and released at its close. Nothing about a window costs a byte on the
days no window is open.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/windowed.rs` | `WindowedGroup`: declare, open, close, handles, save |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/windowed_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/parties.rs` | -F driver: all three countries' campaign windows open at once over their persons and households |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.5 "Windowed groups" |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.parties] windowed_mb` (added) |

**Design**:
- A kind declares (K-21) a windowed group: its attributes (as S1.196's handles), the dated schedule whose instances
  give each window's open and close days (a declared schedule, e.g. a country's campaign period), and the country or
  subject set it covers.
- `open(window)` (stage 1a of the open day): reserves the group's column in address space (K-01, pages committed on
  first write), stamps it with the window's epoch (K-07). `get` outside an open window, or on a slot the window does
  not cover, returns `Missing`; `set` there stops the run. `close(window)` (10e of the close day) decommits the pages.
- Parties are begun at the opening region by region, so a country's persons and households occupy mostly contiguous
  slot ranges and a country's window commits pages for them alone.
- Declared users: the person kind's campaign group (intention u8, S5.137) and the household kind's `vote` slot (the
  next occasion's day, u16, S1.227, S5.137), both on a country's campaign window. Nothing keeps two countries' campaigns
  apart, so all three may be open at once.
- Save: an open window's pages saved with its stamp; a closed one saves nothing. Measurement: `StoreStats` (windows
  open, bytes committed).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: an election day reads the window's column once (`read_inside_window`).
- E6: a save inside a window restores it open with its values (`save_inside_window_round_trip`).
- E8: a set outside the window stops the run (`set_outside_window_stops`).
- E9: a closed window holds no page (`close_decommits`).
- E10: a person ended during a window reads `Missing` through its generation (`ended_party_reads_missing`).
- E13: a country with no campaign has no window open (`no_window_no_bytes`).

**Extension points**: S1.227 (the household's windowed `vote` slot); S5.137; S5.140 (vote occasions in the campaign
window).

**Unit tests**: `read_inside_window`; `outside_window_reads_missing`; `set_outside_window_stops`; `close_decommits`;
`save_inside_window_round_trip`; `ended_party_reads_missing`; `no_window_no_bytes`.

**Live checks**: none until S5.137 (its first user).

**Budget**: volumes: one campaign window per country at a time, all three at once at the peak; persons 1 B, households
2 B inside it. Units: get and
set as S1.196's (≤ 1 ns after the gather); open and close ≤ 0.1 core-ms. It adds no stage line. ledger line 25
(windows): +12 MB resident at the peak, all three countries' campaigns open (7.5 M persons × 1 B + 2.21 M households ×
2 B), reserved once, faulted once a window. Ratchets `[fin.parties]`: `windowed_mb` 12 (added).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a windowed column allocated at the opening for the whole run; a window read as zero outside itself;
an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `WindowedGroup` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F parties` within `windowed_mb`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.5 "Windowed groups" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.198 — Firms' record words to typed columns

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.5 "Kind stores".
**Depends on**: S1.196 (the firm kind's groups and handles).
**Goal**: The firm kind's table moves onto `phx-pop`'s kind store, and a firm's product, region, site, productivity,
price, output, markup, expected sales, units sold, review day, sales width and units last seen are firm attributes read
through handles; the twelve record words, their constants and the per-call `goods_firm` assembly are gone.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core.rs` | the firm kind's table built on `phx_pop::KindStore` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/consts.rs` | `pub mod firm` record words deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `record_word`, `set_record_word` and `goods_firm` deleted; users read handles |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs`, `core_plant.rs`, `core_deposits.rs`, `core_freight.rs`, `core_outlooks.rs`, `core_firms.rs` | readers of firm words through handles |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/lib.rs` | the firm attributes declared (product as the own unit id, sales outlook, flags) |

**Design**:
- Mapping: `PRODUCT` → the own unit id (hot); `REGION` → zone (warm identity; region read from it); `SITE` → a typed
  `FRM.site` tile (u32, warm, in the 4 B of reserve S1.426 takes later) until S1.294 finds the plant's tile through the
  place index (K-27, REP.23) and deletes the column; `PRICE` → a typed posted-point column (hot, u32, the slot that
  becomes the own product's stall at S1.300, K-71); `OUTPUT` → the output rate (hot); `EXPECTED`, `SALES_WIDTH` → sales outlook (warm);
  `SOLD`, `SEEN_SOLD` → sales since review (hot). In the warm words S1.196 adds for them (9 B; the firm is 520 B):
  `MARKUP` → `FRM.markup` (`Fixed` i32, 4 B); `PRODUCTIVITY` → `FRM.productivity` (the drawn log factor, i32
  billionths, 4 B, in place of the productivity type byte: net 3 B); `REVIEWED` → `FRM.reviewed` (the last review's
  day offset, u16); the next review stays today's (the production schedule's day) until the firms' visits move
  onto the agenda (S1.228), where it is the `price` slot.
- Users move by function: `making`, `input_orders`, `review_prices`, `offer_point`, `own_use`, `attend`
  (`core_goods.rs`), `post_one` (`core_labour.rs`), extraction and shipping reviews, `unit_cost_of`: each gathers the
  firm's hot row once and reads handles.
- Every `MaybeI64` read with its two bounds checks (`core_goods.rs`) becomes one typed load; an absent word
  stays `Missing` (no `unwrap_or`).
- Bench line expected to fall: the record reads inside `goods.*` spans (price reviews 2.9 s, input orders 2.3 s,
  production 1.8 s at 5 M persons); `goods_firm`'s six checked reads a call disappear.

**Edge cases**: E3: a firm with no expected sales yet reads `Missing` and decides nothing, as today
(`firm_without_outlook_decides_nothing`). E6: the firm's groups round-trip (`save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`,
S1.196). E10: a firm ended and its slot reused reads the new firm's columns (`reused_slot_written_in_full`, S1.196).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: the pure rules' tests (`sys-frm`) take typed values; `firm_words_map_to_handles` (a declarations
fixture: every old word has one handle, none two); `firm_without_outlook_decides_nothing`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**: no base operation added; reads fall from six checked words a call to one row gather a visit, inside
`fin.decide.visit_ns` and `fin.decide.review_ns` (no ns added). ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute: markup,
productivity and last review are S1.196's 9 B).

**Guards**: removes its sites from `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-100.toml` (`unwrap_or` on firm words) and
`exceptions/PC-92.toml` (per-party record reads).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a firm word kept beside its handle.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Firm words, `record_word`, `set_record_word`, `goods_firm` deleted; users read handles.
- [ ] Fast checks pass; its sites removed from the exceptions files named in Guards.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows the goods spans' record reads gone (the spans' notes count row
  gathers, not words).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.201 — Banks onto the bank kind: lending records and loan books

**Architecture**: follows §7.5 "Kind stores".

### S1.207 — Persons as parties in their households

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: PTY.3 STATE *(part)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.5 "Persons".
**Depends on**: S1.196 (kind groups and handles); S1.194 (persons are a directory kind); S1.174 (`PartyKey` usable as
payer and payee).
**Goal**: Every person is a party of the person kind with its own reference, 66 B of columns and bit-field views that
allocate nothing; a household's persons are threaded through them, so moving a person between households is an
unlink, a link and one column write, and everything the person owns names the person (REP.26).

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/person_kind.rs` | the person kind: groups, household threading, moves |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/person_word.rs` | `PersonWord` bit fields and `PersonView` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/person_kind_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/parties.rs` | -F driver: `[store] persons` in `[store] households` (1–8 a household, mean 3.4) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.5 "Persons" with the byte map |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.parties]` keys below |

**Design**:
- The person kind's groups (66 B): *core 32* — packed word u64 · skills u32 (8 occupation families × 4 bits, POP.1) ·
  household u32 (the household's key) · next in household u32 · account u32 (K-47 slot; `Missing` = unbanked; a second
  account through K-47's side rows) · chain head u32 (K-53) · search start u16 (days from the run's first day, the
  directory's run capacity; `Missing`) · goal u16 (the adult's active goal: its row's offset in its slot-range block,
  named slot `goal`, K-102, S1.352) — *banknotes 4* (i32, K-47: written only by settlement's apply, S1.240) — *tax year
  16* (taxable income i64, withheld i64, K-52, S1.254) — *mind 13* (K-102, S1.352) — *experience 1* (i8 log experience
  factor, named slot `experience`, recomputed at the yearly step and at adversity writes, S8.197).
- The packed word, bits from 0: birth day 32 (the calendar's day serial, REP.25) · role 3 (head, partner, adult,
  child; declared) · sex 1 · health 2 · education stage 4 · education field 4 · in the labour force 1 · searching 1 ·
  life record kept 1 (held an office or founded a firm, OBS.10) · reserve 15. Widths are asserted by `const` checks.
- `PersonView` reads fields by shift and mask; `age_on(day)` reads the birth day through the calendar's day facts
  (K-19); nothing allocates. Setters write one field of the word.
- The household's list: household `persons head` → person `next` → …; its order is never read (a reader that needs an
  order sorts by role, then birth day). `members(h)` iterates the list (k ≤ the household's size).
- `move_person(p, to)`: unlink from the old list (O(k)), link at the new head, write `household`; accounts, holdings
  and contracts name the person, so nothing else moves (REP.26). A household left with no person is ended by its
  caller the same day (PTY.11, K-97).
- `begin_person(household, word, init)`: a directory `begin` of the person kind and its columns in full; `end_person`:
  unlinked, then the directory's `end` with the successor the ending names (K-97).
- Parallel: a household's persons are written only by the handler holding that household's chunk (3b outcomes by
  household range); each person belongs to one household (PTY.11), so writes are disjoint for any worker count.
  Persons are begun at the opening in household order, so a household's persons start adjacent.
- Index instances on the kind are declared by their users in S1.165's inventory (the searchers by the `searching` bit;
  electorates and sample frames reuse the parties-by-zone-and-kind instance, +0 MB).
- The campaign's intention lives in the person kind's windowed group (S1.197), 1 B inside a window only; the vote day
  is the household's windowed `vote` slot.
- Save: every group raw; household links are primary. Measurement: `StoreStats` (K-15); `members` walks report rows
  visited through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- Replaces `phx-pop/src/persons.rs` (two words a person in a chunk arena, found by the household's slot) and
  `person.rs` (`unpack` allocating a `Vec` a read); both stay until S1.208 moves their users and deletes them.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: mass deaths on a catastrophe day: each an unlink and an ending, household range on the pool
  (`many_deaths_one_household_range`).
- E3: an unbanked person reads `Missing` for its account (`unbanked_reads_missing`).
- E6: links round-trip; `members` gives the same set after load (`save_round_trip_lists`).
- E7: disjoint writes by household (`writes_disjoint_by_household`).
- E8: 8 occupation families × 4 bits; a skill level beyond 15 or a role beyond 7 stops the run (`field_overflow_stops`).
- E10: a person ended is unlinked the same day; its reference reads ended (`ended_person_unlinked`).
- E14: a birth and a death in one household the same day are two list edits in the processes' declared order (POP.3
  before POP.4), one writer (`birth_and_death_same_day_in_order`).

**Extension points**: S1.208 (users onto the kind); S1.209; S1.223 (the life-record flag); S1.224; S1.235 (hazards read
persons' own rates, which persons a hit reaches); S1.240; S1.243; S1.254 (accounts, banknotes, the tax-year pair);
S1.258; S1.271; S1.304; S1.352 (the mind's 13 B and the `goal` slot); S1.402; S1.404; S8.102 (characters drawn at
birth); S8.106; S8.121; S8.197 (the `experience` byte); S4.149; S4.152; S5.137 (the campaign group, windowed); S5.183;
S6.115 (labour state and employment history as reads); S6.116; S6.118 (education record in the word's 8 education bits);
S6.120; S6.133.

**Unit tests**: `word_fields_round_trip`; `field_overflow_stops`; `age_read_from_birth_day`;
`move_is_unlink_link_write`; `members_after_moves_is_the_set`; `unbanked_reads_missing`; `writes_disjoint_by_household`;
`person_layout_is_66_bytes`; `save_round_trip_lists`; `many_deaths_one_household_range`; `ended_person_unlinked`;
`birth_and_death_same_day_in_order`.

**Live checks**: none (REP.13's count is the audit's, S1.354).

**Budget**: volumes: `[store] persons` in `households`; view gathers 1.6 M / 0.9 M / 1.6 M a day; moves ≤ 10 k a day
(formation and separation, Stage 6); deaths and births ≈ 400 a day. Access: through the household's agenda entry,
hits and flows. Units: a person view ≤ 1 line (≤ 3 ns VM after the gather), a move ≤ 200 ns; views ride the
decisions' units (no ns added to `fin.decide`). ledger line 2 (persons): +495 MB resident (7.5 M × 66 B). Ratchets
`[fin.parties]`: `person_bytes` 66, `person_view_ns` 3 (added), `move_ns` 200 (added), `mb` 1 654 (lines 2–7 at
S1.194–S1.209's figures).

**Guards**: PC-12 (integers only); a `const` size assertion of 66 B; PC-34's scope (a person's links written by
`phx-pop` and the population's rules only) restated for the person kind.

**Not allowed**: a person held in its household's arena; an allocation to read a person; an attribute by name; a
household-level copy of what its persons own; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate (S1.208's); a store,
index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The person kind built with its byte map, threading and views; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F parties` within `person_bytes`, `person_view_ns`, `move_ns`, `mb`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.5 "Persons" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.208 — Persons onto the person kind

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.5 "Persons".
**Depends on**: S1.207 (the person kind); S1.199 (households' columns, which hold the persons head).
**Goal**: Every reader and writer of persons uses the person kind: no household arena of person words, no `unpack`
allocating a vector, no attribute found by name, no scan of a household to place a person, no yearly unpacking of
every household.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/persons.rs` | the arena-list `Persons` and `place_of` deleted |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/person.rs` | `pack`, `unpack`, `read` deleted |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/pop_process.rs` | `Person`/`Household` attributes by name → views |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_pop.rs` | outcomes, `person_left`, `end_household` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `seekers` (`unpack` a searcher a day) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_owners.rs` | `owners_pay` (`unpack` an owner a unit cost) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_outlooks.rs` | `refresh_windows` → reads of age classes from birth days when the decision runs |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_stats.rs` | `exposed`, `labour_force` read views (their monthly pass is K-39's to remove) |

**Design**:
- Users by function: `outcomes` changes persons in place through setters (no `attrs.clone()`, no fresh `Buffers`
  a household hit); `person_left` and `end_household` keep walking today's families until S1.260 puts them on the
  contract store, where they read the person's chain (K-53); `seekers` iterates the searchers' index instance; `owners_pay` reads the owner's view; the observer reads
  views.
- The person's identity is its reference (S1.195), so `Held { word, id }` disappears; a person's place in its
  household is not an index.
- `refresh_windows`' yearly unpack of every household: the outlook window of an age class is read from the person's
  birth day when its decision runs (VAL.23), so no yearly pass exists.
- Bench line expected to fall: labour postings and search (0.9 s at 5 M), the unit-cost chain's owner unpack (part
  of the 13 % unit cost), the allocator's share of the day (≈ 6 % malloc/free), hazards' outcomes (0.6 s).

**Edge cases**: E1: a catastrophe's deaths apply through views with no allocation (`outcomes_allocate_nothing`). E6:
persons round-trip (`save_round_trip_lists`, S1.207). E14: two outcomes on one household apply in process order
(`birth_and_death_same_day_in_order`, S1.207).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `sys-dem` outcome rules over views; `core_pop` pure helpers re-tested over views;
`outcomes_allocate_nothing` (a counting-allocator fixture over one household's outcomes).

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**: no base operation added; the person reads of labour, hazards and unit cost become one-line views inside
`fin.decide.search_ns`, `fin.hazards.hit_ns` and `fin.decide.review_ns` (no ns added). ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B
(core attribute).

**Guards**: removes its sites from `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-98.toml` (attributes by name),
`exceptions/PC-99.toml` (allocation per read) and `exceptions/PC-96.toml` (`refresh_windows`' pass over households).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a person copied out of its columns to be read.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Arena persons, `unpack`, attributes by name, `place_of` and `refresh_windows`' pass deleted; users read views.
- [ ] Fast checks pass; its sites removed from the exceptions files named in Guards.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows the labour and hazard spans' allocations at 0 and the yearly pass
  absent.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.209 — Offices and founding preferences

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: PTY.16 STATE *(part)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.5 "Offices".
**Depends on**: S1.207 (holders are persons); S1.196 (institutions' and firms' records hold their first office and
founding preferences); S1.180 (each legal form declares its offices, each decision kind its office).
**Goal**: Every office an institution decides through is a 16 B row naming its institution, its kind and its holder —
a person who owns and manages, or the appointment contract that names one — or `Missing` while it is being filled.
An institution's offices lie in one block found from its record; an office of a declared kind is found in O(1);
founding preferences are the institution's own columns, read while an office is empty.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/offices.rs` | `Offices`: rows, blocks per institution, fill, vacate, holder resolution |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/offices_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/parties.rs` | -F driver: 2.5 M offices (1.1 M owner-managed, 1.4 M appointed) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.5 "Offices" |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.parties]` keys below |

**Design**:
- Office row, 16 B: institution key u32 · office kind u16 (K-21 handle of its legal form's declared offices) · flags u16
  (filling, term-bound) · holder u32, tagged: person slot (owner-managed offices, which name no contract: the owner acts
  under ownership) or appointment `ContractRef` slot (an employment-kind row naming the person, K-53; holder and start
  read from it by the decision core, one writer) or `Missing` while filling · since u32 (owner-managed only; `Missing`
  for appointed, whose start is the contract's).
- Blocks: at a party's founding, its legal form's declared offices are allocated as one contiguous block (K-02 slot
  runs); the record holds the block's first row (the firm's `head's office` word). The office of kind k = first +
  the form's declared offset of k (O(1)); line heads, added as a firm enters a line, grow the block by one move of its
  rows (rare).
- API: `office(institution, kind) -> OfficeRef`; `holder(o) -> Holder { Owner(PartyRef) | Appointment(ContractRef) |
  Vacant }` (the tagged word decoded; the appointment row's person end is read by the decision core, K-100 at S1.348,
  which sits above `phx-contract`, so this base reads no higher crate); `fill_owned(o, person, day)`, `fill_appointed(o,
  contract)`, `vacate(o)` — written only by these, called by the ownership apply (K-60), the appointment's opening and
  ending (K-53) and the holder's death (K-97); `offices_of(person)` = its appointment rows in its chain plus the firms
  it owns and manages.
- Founding preferences (MND.16, FRM.1): a type index byte of the institution's record (a firm's warm identity) into
  its country's declared sets, drawn at founding; an institution without one stops the run (never a default).
- Decider resolution (MND.20) is K-100's (S1.348): player, else holder, else founding preferences; this base answers
  holder and founding preferences.
- Save: rows raw; blocks are primary. Measurement: `StoreStats`; `offices_of` walks report rows visited.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: an office never filled reads `Missing` and its decisions read founding preferences (`empty_office_reads_missing`).
- E10: a holder's death vacates every office it holds the same day (PTY.17): appointed through its chain, owned through
  its holdings (`death_vacates_all_offices`).
- E13: a legal form with no offices (a household) allocates no block (`no_offices_no_block`).
- E14: an appointment and a vacancy of one office on one day apply in the day's order of events, one writer
  (`fill_and_vacate_same_day_in_order`).

**Extension points**: S1.210 (today's holders and founding preferences onto it); S1.343; S1.348; S2.192 (supervisors'
heads, empty until the government forms); S3.111 (the central bank's committee); S3.156 (boards and chief executives
appointed by votes, K-41); S8.104 (founding preferences drawn as a character); S8.123; S8.124; S8.125; S4.102; S4.142
(clearing houses', schemes' trustees); S5.135; S5.136; S5.142; S5.144 (the parliament's and the government's offices,
party leaders, seats and ministers; PTY.16 completes there).

**Unit tests**: `office_of_kind_is_first_plus_offset`; `owner_holder_direct`; `appointed_holder_decodes_contract_ref`;
`no_offices_no_block`; `fill_and_vacate_same_day_in_order`; `empty_office_reads_missing`; `death_vacates_all_offices`;
`missing_founding_preferences_stops`; `line_head_grows_block`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**: volumes: `[store] offices`; holder reads with every decision taken in an office (≈ 0.6 M B, 0.2 M NB);
fills and vacancies ≈ 1 k a day. Units: holder read ≤ 3 ns (one gather), inside `fin.decide.handler_ns` (no ns added).
ledger line 7 (offices): +40 MB resident (2.5 M × 16 B). Ratchets `[fin.parties]`: `office_bytes` 16 (added),
`holder_ns` 3 (added).

**Guards**: offices written only through `fill_*` and `vacate` (PC-15 snapshot of the kernel API).

**Not allowed**: a map from (party, office) to holder; a default preference for a missing founding draw; an office
holder copied beside its appointment contract; a read of a higher crate (`phx-contract`); an edit of `phx-world` or an
older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Offices` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F parties` within `office_bytes`, `holder_ns`, `mb`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.5 "Offices" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

**Goal**: The decision core finds a decision's holder and an empty office's founding preferences through the offices

### S1.211 — The per-day party cache

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.5 "The per-day cache".
**Depends on**: S1.196 (the cache's words live in the party's record); S1.128 (`#[per_day]`, refused outside the
cache by PC-101); S1.161 (the day plan: the write-back buffer's life ends at its sub-stage's barrier).
**Goal**: A value that is a pure function of a party's state and today's prices, read several times a day, is computed
once a day on first use and kept in the party's own record with its day stamp: a firm's unit cost is computed at most
once a firm a day.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/cache.rs` | `DayCached<T>`, `get_or` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-pop/src/cache_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/parties.rs` | -F driver: 1.152 M firms' unit cost read 2–7 times each on 0.34 M reviews and 0.25 M visits |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.5 "The per-day cache" |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.parties] cache_hit_ns` (added) |

**Design**:
- `DayCached<T: Pod>`: (value T, stamp u16) in a declared group of the party's record (a firm's unit cost: i64 +
  u16 = 10 B in its hot row). The stamp is the day's offset from the run's first day (the directory's declared run
  capacity of 65 535 days); `u16::MAX` is "never".
- `get_or(&self, r, today, f) -> T` for readers holding `&self` in decide (5b, 5c): a hit reads the value; a miss
  computes `f` and returns it, recording (party slot u32, value) — 12 B for an i64 — into the chunk's write-back buffer
  (K-03). Each decide sub-stage's buffer is applied at that sub-stage's own barrier (the end of 5b, the end of 5c) by
  the chunks owning the slots, so decide stays `&self` (§6.6's R3), 5c's reviews hit what 5b computed, and nothing is
  live at 5d. Writing a cache word changes no outcome: it equals `f` recomputed. `get_or_mut` writes in place where the
  caller holds the party's row mutably.
- `#[per_day]` functions (the unit cost at today's prices, a fund's NAV, a netting set's IM) are callable only
  through `get_or` (PC-101); a day-stamped value never changes an outcome: it equals `f` recomputed.
- Save: cache words saved as "never" and excluded from the logical hash (their value is recomputed on first use).
- Measurement: the cache counts hits and misses per declared cache (`StoreStats` notes); `unit_cost_per_firm_day` is
  S1.132's world counter.

**Edge cases**: E6: a load starts every cache at "never" (`load_clears_stamps`). E7: write-back applied by the owning
chunk, the same value for any worker count (`write_back_applied_by_owner_chunk`). E11: day zero computes on first use
(`miss_computes_then_hits`). E14: two handlers the same day read one value (`second_read_hits`).

**Extension points**: S1.295; S1.348; S1.406; S2.174; S2.179; S3.184 (a fund's NAV, FND.5, on the fund kind's layout);
S8.122; S8.130; S4.108 (IM per netting set); S6.104.

**Unit tests**: `miss_computes_then_hits`; `stale_stamp_recomputes`; `second_read_hits`; `load_clears_stamps`;
`write_back_applied_by_owner_chunk`.

**Live checks**: none (`unit_cost_per_firm_day` ≤ 1 is S1.132's ratchet on the world's run).

**Budget**: volumes: firms' unit-cost reads ≈ 1.2 M a business day (reviews, visits, postings, own use); misses ≈
0.6 M B / 0.2 M NB / 0.6 M H (the firms deciding), ≤ 0.35 M in one sub-stage. Units: a hit ≤ 2 ns phone (1.5 VM) in
the hot row already gathered, inside `fin.decide.review_ns` and `fin.decide.visit_ns` (no ns added). ledger line 5
(firms): +0 B (core attribute: 10 B inside the hot 192). ledger line 21 (day buffers): +4 MB at 5c's end (≤ 0.35 M ×
12 B), none live at 5d. Ratchets: `fin.parties.cache_hit_ns` 1.5 (added); world counter `unit_cost_per_firm_day` ≤ 1.

**Guards**: PC-101 (S1.128) refuses a `#[per_day]` call outside `get_or`.

**Not allowed**: a cache outside the party's record; a cache that survives its day; a per-day value recomputed by a
second caller; a write-back live past its sub-stage's barrier; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store,
index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `DayCached` and `get_or` built; the firm's unit cost declared through it; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F parties` within `cache_hit_ns`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.5 "The per-day cache" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.212 — The stored log: immutable day segments on storage

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 (phx-record) "The stored log".
**Depends on**: S1.167 (K-08's per-kind horizons); S1.160 (the day's per-chunk buffers); S1.170 (partitioned sort of a
day's items by key); S1.113 (capacities, `[resolution]` horizons).
**Goal**: A history too large to keep resident — hazard occurrences and fails, life records — is written each day as
one immutable, content-addressed segment of encoded frames on storage, found through a small resident frame index,
merged in tiers when its kind asks, deleted past its horizon, and shared by every snapshot that lists it.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs` | the crate (L1.6), created by this step |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/stored.rs` | `StoredLog`: segments, frames, frame index, tiers, pruning, reads |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/stored_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: 100 k items a day for a horizon's days; reads |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "The stored log" |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.records]` keys below |

**Design**:
- A stored kind declares its key (an ordering over its items: (kind, first subject) for events, (person, day) for life
  records), its item encoding (delta-coded keys, zigzag varints), its frame size (4 KiB to 1 MiB) and its horizon.
- `flush(day, items)` at 10d: the day's items sorted by key (K-12) and encoded into frames of one immutable day
  segment, written behind the pool (write-behind; the day never waits on storage); the resident frame index keeps each
  frame's first key and offset (≈ 12 B a frame).
- `merge_slice(budget)`: a kind that asks for tiers (S1.223) merges standing segments day → week → month → quarter →
  year by a rolling job at 10d, a bounded input a day (K-14 cursor), dropping items past the horizon or marked dead.
- `find(key, from, to)`: in each standing segment, the frame index gives the one frame that may hold the key; frames
  are read and decoded on demand. `read_many(keys)`: frames deduplicated, sorted by offset, read in one storage round
  on the pool.
- Segments are content-addressed files; every full snapshot (K-104) lists the segments it holds and the two retained
  snapshots share them, so each save is complete and storage holds a segment once (E 22). A segment past every
  horizon of the kinds in it, and listed by no retained snapshot, is deleted.
- Measurement: `StoreStats` (segments, frames, resident index bytes, stored MB a simulated year); flush and merges
  report rows visited through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a heavy day's segment is written behind the pool (`flush_is_write_behind`).
- E6: segments listed by a snapshot load alike; the index is rebuilt from their frame headers
  (`index_rebuilt_from_headers`).
- E7: a day's segment is the same for any chunking (`flush_same_for_any_chunking`).
- E8: a frame past its declared size stops the run (`frame_overflow_stops`).
- E9: storage flat after the horizon (`segment_deleted_past_horizon`).
- E11: day zero writes no segment (`no_items_no_segment`).

**Extension points**: S1.213 (the event log's non-public tier); S1.223 (life records, tiered); S1.356 (snapshots list
and share segments). Further users, by their Depends on: S1.214.

**Unit tests**: `stored_segment_round_trip`; `flush_is_write_behind`; `flush_same_for_any_chunking`;
`index_rebuilt_from_headers`; `merge_keeps_order_and_drops_past_horizon`; `find_touches_one_frame_a_segment`;
`read_many_dedups_frames_one_round`; `frame_overflow_stops`; `segment_deleted_past_horizon`; `no_items_no_segment`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**: volumes: its kinds' items (events ≈ 100 k a day, S1.213; life records 1.6 M / 0.8 M / 1.6 M, S1.223).
Units: encode ≤ 3 ns VM an item; a frame read ≤ 50 µs with storage latency. Its flush shares are its kinds'
(S1.213, S1.223). ledger line 18 (records): +1 MB resident (frame indexes at the declared horizons). saved: segments on
storage, shared by the retained snapshots. Ratchets `[fin.records]`: `encode_ns` 3 (added), `index_mb` 1 (added).

**Guards**: `StoredLog` is written only through `flush` and `merge_slice` (PC-15).

**Not allowed**: a segment rewritten in place; a day waiting on storage; a segment kept past every horizon and every
retained snapshot; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the
core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `phx-record` created; `StoredLog` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `encode_ns`, `index_mb`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "The stored log" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.213 — The event log: public events resident, occurrences stored

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: OBS.3 STATE
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "The event log"; follows §7.1 (the horizon ring, S1.167).
**Depends on**: S1.212 (the stored tier); S1.167 (K-08 dated chunks, per-kind horizons); S1.194 (subjects are
references, resolved through tombstones); S1.160 (the day's per-chunk buffers).
**Goal**: Every event — a hazard occurrence, a fail, a default, a failed auction, an estate's distribution — is
recorded with its day, kind, size in its kind's unit and named subjects before any party reacts to it; the declared
rule of what becomes public (OBS.9) makes some public at the close, and those stay resident for their horizon and can
develop over days; the rest go to the stored tier. No fixed row cap exists. Today's `EventStore` stays until S1.214.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/events.rs` | `EventLog`: day buffers, the public ring, the rule's pass, reads |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/events_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: public events at `[resolution] horizon_events_days`; 100 k occurrences a day |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "The event log" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.records]` keys below; `[resolution] horizon_events_days = 365` |

**Design**:
- **Retires** the capacity table's `events_unpruned` store (S1.115: the log as it stands, every event of a gate's
  run resident): `EVENT_ROWS` reads the `events` store again, the design point's resident rows within the horizon.
- Declared event kinds (K-21): name, size unit (Law 8), clause, whether the kind may become public, and its horizon (a
  RESOLUTION primitive, owner the declaring system, floored by any POLICY its keeper follows, SET.13; listed in
  Appendix C in the same change).
- `record(day, kind, size, subjects, develops_from)` appends to the calling chunk's day buffer (16 B head + 8 B a
  subject). It is the occurrence's first write (CHN.4); the same day's readers (the audit, claims following a hazard,
  INS.8) read the day buffers.
- 10a: buffers joined in chunk order (ids the same for any worker count); the declared rule of what becomes public
  (OBS.9, a standing SHAPE) reads each event alone; public events move into the resident ring, the others to S1.212's
  stored tier at 10d, keyed (kind, first subject).
- Public ring: one K-08 chunk a day. Row 24 B `#[derive(Pod)]`: kind u16 · flags u8 (public, develops) · subject count
  u8 (255: more, counted in the arena) · size i64 · develops-from `EventId` u32 · first subject u64 (packed reference);
  further subjects in the chunk's arena, 8 B each. `EventId` is the running number of public events.
- Reads: `public(from, to, kind)` for deciders (VAL.5), stage-tagged (TIME.10: stage 5 reads earlier days);
  `today(kind)`; `develops(id)`; `naming(r, from, to)` for the observer (OBS.8) scans the ring and the stored frames
  that may hold r — outside the turn, building nothing the world reads (Law 17). No resident subject index exists; a
  day-path question about a subject is answered by state the asker keeps.
- Measurement: `StoreStats`; the 10a pass reports rows visited.
- Replaces `phx_core::EventStore` (`crates/kernel/phx-core/src/events.rs`: fixed 2²⁴ rows, `consts.rs`
  `EVENT_ROWS`; two `Vec`s allocated a `record`), removed with its users at S1.214.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: one catastrophe event with 20 k subjects is one row and 20 k arena words (`one_event_many_subjects`); a
  mass-failure day's 115 k defaults are appended on the pool (`many_events_one_day`).
- E5: a heavy day's buffers keep their size (`buffers_reused_after_heavy_day`).
- E6: ring and arena saved, stored segments listed; a load reads the same events (`save_round_trip_events`).
- E7: ids assigned in chunk order at 10a (`ids_same_for_any_chunking`).
- E9: the ring prunes whole chunks past the horizon (`ring_flat_after_horizon`).
- E10: an event naming a party that ended reads it as ended, on its day (`ended_subject_reads_ended`).
- E11: `develops_from` naming a later or unknown id stops the run (`develops_forward_stops`).

**Extension points**: S1.214 (today's users and weather's public events from the day's footprint); S1.235; S2.128;
S2.182; S2.185; S2.192; S2.195; S2.211; S3.102; S3.109; S3.121; S3.123; S3.135; S3.137; S3.186; S8.121; S8.122; S8.197;
S8.198; S8.199; S8.200; S4.101; S4.111; S4.112; S4.113; S4.129; S4.131; S4.132; S4.133; S4.135; S4.165; S4.166; S4.172;
S4.175; S4.179; S5.142; S5.154; S5.168; S6.105; S6.107; S6.125; S6.130; S6.133; S6.135 (events that develop, and the
news).

**Unit tests**: `record_before_reaction_readable_same_day`; `rule_marks_public_at_close`; `one_event_many_subjects`;
`many_events_one_day`; `buffers_reused_after_heavy_day`; `ids_same_for_any_chunking`; `develops_forward_stops`;
`ring_flat_after_horizon`; `ended_subject_reads_ended`; `save_round_trip_events`; `public_read_stage_tagged`.

**Live checks**: LC-0-41 (each hazard's hits counted as events of its kind the day it draws them) reads the log from
S1.214 on.

**Budget**: volumes: public events 2 k a day (B, NB, H), 0.73 M at `horizon_events_days`; occurrences and fails ≈ 100 k
a day stored. Units: append 3.8 ns VM. its share of fin.fixed.observer: 3 / 2 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the 10a pass
over ≈ 100 k / 70 k / 100 k events and their stored flush; hazards run on every day). ledger line 18 (records): +18.5 MB
resident (0.73 M × 24 B + subjects) at the declared 365-day horizon, forced by the owner's memory margin (§12; 37 MB
at 730 days). saved: ≈
300 MB a simulated year of stored segments. Ratchets `[fin.records]`: `append_ns` 3.8, `events_mb` 18.5 (added),
`stored_mb_per_year` 300 (added), `flush_core_ms` 3 (added).

**Guards**: the audit's engine (S1.353) reads events as handed values; the observer's `naming` is not reachable from a
world crate (PC-01).

**Not allowed**: a fixed row cap; an allocation a record; a resident subject index; a hazard occurrence kept only in
memory; an event written after a party reacted to it; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate (S1.214's); a
store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `EventLog` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `append_ns`, `events_mb`, `stored_mb_per_year`, `flush_core_ms`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "The event log" written; each event kind's horizon in the register and Appendix C.

### S1.214 — Hazard events, weather records and deaths onto the event log

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.6 "The event log".
**Depends on**: S1.213 (the event log); S1.212 (its stored tier); S1.192 (the day's catastrophe footprint); S1.193
(`core_weather`'s `struck` already on the footprint buffer, so its events move here).
**Goal**: Every event the world records today goes through the event log: hazard hits, weather's catastrophes, the
publication pass and deaths. The per-hit allocations, the fixed-capacity store and the growing list of deaths are gone.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/events.rs` | `EventStore` deleted; `EventKindDecl` stays as the kinds' declaration |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_pop.rs` | `record_event` (ids and details allocated a hit), `count_event`, `outcomes`' `deaths` pushes |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_weather.rs` | `weather_day`'s events recorded (after S1.193's move of `struck`) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day.rs` | the publication pass → the log's 10a pass |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core.rs` | `happened: EventStore`, `Core::deaths` deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/consts.rs` | `EVENT_ROWS` deleted |

**Design**:
- Users by function: a hazard hit records its occurrence through `EventLog::record` from the hit's chunk (no `Vec` a
  hit); a death is an event of the mortality kind with its person as subject (`Core::deaths` was a second record of the
  same fact, Law 4); weather's catastrophes: this step writes the public event from S1.192's footprint (a day buffer),
  one event with the struck tiles' owners as subjects; the publication rule runs in the log's 10a pass.
- `count_event`'s linear search over today's kinds → the kind's handle (K-21).
- Bench line expected to fall: hazards (0.6 s at 5 M) by the allocations removed; the capacity stop at 2²⁴ rows gone;
  `Core::deaths`' growth (≈ 50 k a year) gone.

**Edge cases**: E1: a catastrophe's thousands of subjects are one event (`one_event_many_subjects`, S1.213). E6:
events round-trip (`save_round_trip_events`, S1.213). E9: no list of deaths grows (`death_is_an_event_only`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `sys-dem` outcome tests read events from a log fixture; `day.rs`'s publication order test restated
on the 10a pass; `death_is_an_event_only`.

**Live checks**: LC-0-41 reads the log.

**Budget**: no base operation added; the hazards' per-hit allocations go (inside `fin.hazards.hit_ns`, no ns added).
ledger line 18 (records): +0 B (S1.213's ring).

**Guards**: removes its sites from `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-99.toml` (allocations a hit) and the literal
capacity from `exceptions/PC-100.toml`.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a second record of a death.

### S1.215 — The records store: series records by vintage, as published

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: GEN.5 STATE *(part: the opening's present values as series of one)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "The records store".
**Depends on**: S1.167 (K-08 rings with per-kind horizons); S1.194 (subjects and publishers are references); S1.180
(record kinds, series keys and publishers declared); S1.160 (the day's buffers).
**Goal**: Every record the world publishes or keeps for others — statistics with their vintages, indices, ratings,
reports, estimates, auction and election results, polls, policy decisions, patents — is a typed record with its
publisher, subject, series, reference period, value in its unit, publication day, vintage and audience, kept within
its horizon; "as published by day d" is answered in O(log n) and nothing is readable before its publication day.
Filed accounts (S1.216) and the credit bureau (S1.217) are its two encoded kinds.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/records.rs` | `Records`: record kinds, rings, as-published reads |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/records_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: 6 k series × 12 months × 3 vintages at `horizon_series_days` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "The records store" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.records]` keys below; `[resolution] horizon_series_days = 730` |

**Design**:
- Record kinds are declared (K-21): publisher kind, subject kind, series key type, value columns with units (Law 8),
  audience (public or the parties the law names), horizon (RESOLUTION, never shorter than a POLICY its keeper follows:
  BNK.21, HH.21, STA.5; SET.13).
- Series records: 16 B rows — series u32 · reference period u16 · vintage u8 · flags u8 · publication day offset u16 ·
  value i64 in the series' unit — in one ring a kind; a per-series run of (period, vintage) positions (derived,
  rebuilt at load) gives `as_published(series, period, day, stage) -> Missing<Value>`: the latest vintage published
  on or before the day, stage-tagged (TIME.10: stage 5 reads days before; stage 9 today's), O(log n). A record not yet
  published reads `Missing` (STA.4); a publication dated before its period's end stops the run.
- Small kinds (ratings, reports, estimates, auction results, patents): 16–32 B rows in their rings.
- GEN.5's present values: the opening writes each observed fact's single latest value as a record of vintage 0
  published on day zero, a series of one (E 38); nothing else stands in for a missing history.
- Writes at 9d by publishers (per publisher, pool); reads by deciders through `as_published`.
- The `#[clause("STA.4")]` carrier (done at S1.14) moves here with S1.218.
- Save: rings raw; per-series runs rebuilt at load. Measurement: `StoreStats` a kind; reads note rows visited.

**Edge cases**:
- E6: indexes rebuilt equal after load (`save_round_trip_as_published`).
- E9: every kind prunes at its horizon (`kind_flat_after_horizon`).
- E10: a record naming an ended party reads it as ended, on its date (`record_names_ended_party`).
- E11: day zero holds only GEN.5's series of one; a read before any record is `Missing`
  (`opening_present_value_is_vintage_zero`).
- E12: a series never published reads `Missing`, never 0 (`unpublished_reads_missing`).

**Extension points**: S1.216; S1.217 (encoded kinds); S1.218 (today's releases, auction history, the opening's present
values); S1.263; S1.265; S1.282; S1.333; S1.335; S1.336; S1.358 (the recorder reads published series); S1.407; S1.425;
S1.486; S2.161; S2.176; S2.182; S2.191; S2.195; S2.200; S2.215; S3.103; S3.111; S3.113; S3.118; S3.119; S3.126; S3.128;
S3.134; S3.141; S3.145; S3.155; S3.162; S3.203; S3.204; S3.207; S3.209; S3.211; S8.105; S8.126; S8.200; S4.110; S4.112;
S4.129; S4.146; S4.152; S4.159; S4.165; S4.171; S4.180; S4.182; S4.184; S5.121; S5.133; S5.138; S5.142; S5.158; S5.173;
S5.186; S6.105; S6.108; S6.129; S6.131; S6.132.

**Unit tests**: `as_published_latest_vintage_on_or_before`; `stage_five_reads_before_today`;
`unpublished_reads_missing`; `future_read_is_missing`; `record_names_ended_party`;
`opening_present_value_is_vintage_zero`; `kind_flat_after_horizon`; `save_round_trip_as_published`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-100 — no decision reads a record before its publication day (the read trace's stage and day
against each record's publication), from the first release.

**Budget**: volumes: ≈ 0.2 M series records at `horizon_series_days`; appends ≈ 3 k a day; as-published reads ≈ 0.5 M
a business day inside `fin.decide` units and `fin.fixed.outlooks` (≤ 100 ns each; no ns added to their units). Units:
append ≤ 3.8 ns VM; as-published ≤ 100 ns. ledger line 18 (records): +7 MB resident (series and small kinds at the
declared 730-day horizon; 3.5 MB at 365 days). Ratchets `[fin.records]`: `series_mb` 7 (added),
`published_ns` 100 (added).

**Guards**: the as-published read is the only read of a series record (PC-15 snapshot).

**Not allowed**: a latest-value field beside the records; a record readable before its day; an edit of `phx-world` or
an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every
day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Records` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `series_mb`, `published_ns`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "The records store" written; record kinds' horizons in the register.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.216 — Filed accounts encoded per block

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "Filed accounts".
**Depends on**: S1.215 (the records store's kinds, horizons and as-published reads).
**Goal**: Every statement a firm files (RAT.8) is kept, encoded per 1 024-row block, within its declared horizon, with
each filer's latest annual statement kept however old; a reader decodes one block to read one filer's statement as
published by day d.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/filings.rs` | `Filings`: append by filing day, block encoding, per-filer lookup, pruning |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/filings_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: `[store] filed_statements` at `horizon_filings_years` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "Filed accounts" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.records]` keys below; `[resolution] horizon_filings_years = 2` |

**Design**:
- A statement is (filer, period end, filed day, vintage, the ten lines). Rows are appended per filing day and packed
  per 1 024-row block: packed filer references delta-coded, lines zigzag and bit-packed per column at the block's
  widest — ≈ 48 B a statement. A block is decoded whole on read (≈ 2 µs). A restatement keeps both vintages (RAT.2).
- Per-filer lookup: a derived sorted index (filer → block, row) of the latest statement a filer has in each vintage,
  rebuilt at load; `latest(filer, day, stage)` answers as published, stage-tagged (TIME.10).
- Pruning at `horizon_filings_years` keeps each filer's latest annual statement however old, so a reader always finds
  one where one was filed; the rest of an expired block is dropped at its merge.
- Save: blocks raw; the per-filer index rebuilt. Measurement: `StoreStats`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a filing window's last days (≈ 30 k filings a day) append whole blocks (`filing_window_appends_blocks`).
- E6: blocks round-trip, the index rebuilt equal (`filings_block_round_trip`).
- E9: flat after the horizon, the latest annual statements kept (`latest_annual_kept_past_horizon`).
- E12: a firm that never filed reads `Missing` (`never_filed_reads_missing`).

**Extension points**: S1.218 (lenders' filed earnings); S1.333; S2.108 (filing decisions and the registry); S3.145;
S3.207; S4.102 (members' filed accounts); S4.105.

**Unit tests**: `filings_block_round_trip`; `restated_keeps_both_vintages`; `latest_as_published_stage_tagged`;
`latest_annual_kept_past_horizon`; `filing_window_appends_blocks`; `never_filed_reads_missing`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-100 applies.

**Budget**: volumes: 0.92 M statements at the two-year horizon (0.46 M at one year); appends ≈ 2.5 k a day, ≈ 30 k on a
filing window's last days. Units: append ≤ 50 ns a statement; a block decode ≤ 2 µs. Its callers (S2.108) carry the
shares, ≤ 2 core-ms on a filing window's last day. ledger line 18 (records): +44 MB resident (0.92 M × 48 B at the
declared two-year horizon; 22 MB at one year). Ratchets `[fin.records]`: `filings_mb` 44 (added),
`filing_bytes` 48 (added).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a statement stored unencoded; a filer's latest annual statement pruned; an edit of `phx-world` or an
older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Filings` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `filings_mb`, `filing_bytes`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "Filed accounts" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.217 — The credit bureau's records: sparse summaries and adverse events

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "The credit bureau's records".
**Depends on**: S1.215 (the records store's kinds and horizons); S1.194 (borrowers are references).
**Goal**: A credit bureau keeps, for each borrower with an adverse event within the law's retention, a compact summary,
and each adverse event in an encoded ring pruned at that retention; a lender reads a borrower's summary in O(log n).

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/bureau.rs` | `Bureau`: summaries, the adverse-event ring, reads |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/bureau_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: `[store] bureau_borrowers`, `bureau_events` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "The credit bureau's records" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.records] bureau_mb` (added); `[store] bureau_borrowers = 500_000`, `bureau_events = 700_000` (added) |

**Design**:
- Summary (BNK.21, HH.13), 12 B, for borrowers with an adverse event within the retention only: packed reference 8 B
  and worst stage 4 bits · months in arrears 8 · defaults 4 · last event day offset 16; a sorted column by reference,
  merged daily from the day's changes.
- Adverse events (arrears, default, write-off, collection: day offset, borrower, lender, kind, amount), ≈ 12 B encoded
  each, in a ring pruned at the bureau's retention, which is the law's POLICY (BNK.21), never shorter (SET.13).
- The borrower's own credit-record stage is its record's attribute (REP.41, S1.196), written by the bureau's rule; the
  summary is the bureau's own record of it.
- Save: column and ring raw. Measurement: `StoreStats`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day adds 100 k events and summaries in one merge (`mass_defaults_one_merge`).
- E6: round-trip (`bureau_round_trip`).
- E9: flat after the retention (`bureau_flat_after_retention`).
- E10: an ended borrower's summary reads it as ended until pruned (`ended_borrower_reads_ended`).
- E12: a borrower with no adverse event has no summary and reads `Missing` (`clean_borrower_reads_missing`).

**Extension points**: S2.109.

**Unit tests**: `bureau_summary_updates`; `mass_defaults_one_merge`; `bureau_round_trip`; `bureau_flat_after_retention`;
`ended_borrower_reads_ended`; `clean_borrower_reads_missing`.

**Live checks**: none until S2.109.

**Budget**: volumes: 0.5 M summaries, 0.7 M adverse events at BNK.21's floor; ≈ 300 events a day, 100 k on a
mass-default day. Units: a summary read ≤ 60 ns; an event append ≤ 50 ns (its callers, S2.109 and the lenders, carry the
shares). ledger line 18 (records): +14 MB resident (0.5 M × 12 B + 0.7 M × 12 B, at BNK.21's floor). Ratchets
`[fin.records]`: `bureau_mb` 14 (added).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a summary for a borrower with no adverse event; a retention shorter than the law's; an edit of
`phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every
party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Bureau` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `bureau_mb`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "The credit bureau's records" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

and maps that held them are gone.
