### S1.219 — The day ledger: the representation reported every day

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: REP.15 MEASURE
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "The day ledger".
**Depends on**: S1.167 (K-08 rings); S1.194 (live counts per kind); S1.196 (kinds' counts); S1.166 (the day's
touched parties, K-07).
**Goal**: Each system's day record is a declared fixed-width row per (day, country) in a ring within its horizon, and
the representation is reported every day per kind — size, parties, contracts, persons, parties touched, events per
party — from counters the bases maintain, never from a pass over the parties.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/daylog.rs` | `DayLedger`: declared day-record kinds, rows, the representation report |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/daylog_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: 20 day-record kinds × 3 countries × 365 days |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "The day ledger" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.records] daylog_mb`, `day_row_us` (added); `[resolution] horizon_day_ledger_days = 730` |

**Design**:
- A day-record kind is declared (K-21) by its system: columns of i64 counts and sums with their units, keyed by
  country; one row per (day, country) in a K-08 ring at the kind's horizon (RESOLUTION).
- The representation's report (REP.15), one declared kind written by the core at 10d, per party kind and country:
  parties live (the directory's counts, S1.194), contracts by family (K-53's counts), persons (the person kind's
  count), parties touched today (K-07's epoch count), events today and events per party (the event log's counts by
  kind), the representation's size (REP.40). Every number is a maintained counter read once; no party is visited.
- Writers: each system's day record is written at 10d from its own counters (K-39 accumulators, the day's buffers'
  totals); a row written twice for one (day, country) stops the run (one writer).
- Reads: the run report and N2's liveness reads (`phx-cli`), the recorder (S1.358); deciders do not read it (Law 12:
  it is not public information unless a publisher publishes it through K-37).
- Save: rows raw. Measurement: `StoreStats`.

**Edge cases**: E1: a mass-failure day is one row with large counts (`mass_day_one_row`). E6: rows round-trip
(`save_round_trip_rows`). E9: flat after the horizon (`ring_flat_after_horizon`). E11: day zero writes the opening's
report (`day_zero_report_written`). E13: a country with no party of a kind reports zero parties, a count and not a
missing value (`empty_kind_counts_zero`).

**Extension points**: S1.220 (today's per-day vectors); S1.221; S1.248; S1.358 (the recorder writes N2/N3 series from
it).

**Unit tests**: `report_reads_counters_not_parties` (a counters fixture); `row_written_twice_stops`;
`ring_flat_after_horizon`; `save_round_trip_rows`; `mass_day_one_row`; `day_zero_report_written`;
`empty_kind_counts_zero`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-101 — the representation's report exists for every day and country from day zero, and its
counts equal the directory's and families' counts at the close (REP.15; applicable from this step).

**Budget**: volumes: ≤ 20 kinds × 3 countries a day. Access: 10d, serial, small. Units: ≤ 1 µs a row. its share of
fin.fixed.observer: 0.1 / 0.1 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H). ledger line 18 (records): +2 MB resident (≤ 60 rows a day × ≤
32 B at the declared 730-day `horizon_day_ledger_days`; 1 MB at 365 days). Ratchets:
`fin.records.daylog_mb` 2 (added), `fin.records.day_row_us` 1 (added).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a count computed by visiting parties; a `Vec` of day records in a system's state; a store, index, map
or per-party pass outside the core bases; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a pass over every party every
day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `DayLedger` and the representation's report built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `daylog_mb`, `day_row_us`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "The day ledger" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |

**Guards**: removes its sites from `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-96.toml` (the household count, the fold) and
`exceptions/PC-92.toml` (per-day vectors in world state).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a `Vec` of days in a system's state.

### S1.221 — Statistics accumulators

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: STA.1 STATE *(part: the accumulators its statistics are computed from)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "Statistics accumulators".
**Depends on**: S1.219 (day records the accumulators close into); S1.160 (per-chunk stock deltas in day buffers);
S1.170 (partitioned apply of the chunks).
**Goal**: Every number a statistics agency computes from records is read from declared accumulators kept exact by
the events that change them — stocks moved at hires, deaths, births and age-class crossings, person-days exposed
accrued at each change; a month's close reads counters, never the population. Flow sums are K-52's tallies (S1.254);
samples are S1.222's.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/accum.rs` | `Accumulators`: declared keys and periods, chunk deltas, stock counters, exposure |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/accum_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/stats.rs` | -F driver: 20 k stock events a day from every chunk, a catastrophe day's 115 k; period closes |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "Statistics accumulators" |

**Design**:
- An accumulator is declared (K-21) by its system: key (country, region, industry, occupation, age class, sex, kind,
  category — each a declared handle), value (count or sum in a unit, i64), period (a calendar period, TIME.3) and its
  maintaining events. Cells are a dense array over the key's declared sizes (≈ 0.4 M cells, 8 B each).
- No flow tally is kept here: sales, dues and wages summed by key and period are K-52's tallies (S1.254), which reverse
  by place when a leg fails; a release reads them beside these cells. A declared accumulator whose maintaining event is
  a flow is refused at assembly, naming K-52.
- Stock counters: moved by the event that changes them — a hire or separation moves a labour-state count; a birth,
  death or migration a population count; an age-class crossing on its date (filed by its caller on the agenda) moves a
  person between classes. Exposure (person-days by class, for period life tables) accrues as
  `exposed += count × (day − last_change)` at each change of a class's count: O(1) an event, exact.
- Money stock by holder class: read from the ledger's maintained totals (S1.243), never recounted here.
- Period close: on a period's last day the period's cells close into the agency's release inputs and reset by stamp;
  releases (STA.1–STA.2) are `sys-sta`'s rules over them, published into the records store (S1.215) with lag and
  vintage. The `#[clause("STA.2")]` carrier (done at S1.14) moves to the release path with S1.256.
- Save: cells and stamps; chunk delta buffers are day buffers. Measurement: `StoreStats`; merges report rows visited.
- Replaces (users move at S1.256): `core_stats.rs` (`exposed`, `labour_force` over every household and person
  monthly), `employed_ids` (sorted), `money_stock` (over every account).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe's deaths move counts one event each, no pass (`death_moves_count_and_exposure`).
- E5: a catastrophe day's stock events merged by chunk; the close's merge sized by chunks, not by the day
  (`heavy_day_merge_bounded`).
- E7: chunk deltas merged in chunk order, integer sums (`merge_order_free`).
- E9: cells reset by period stamp (`period_close_resets_by_stamp`).
- E11: day zero's cells hold the opening's stocks counted once (`opening_counts_once`).
- E13: a country with no firm of an industry has a zero count, a count and not a missing value
  (`empty_cell_counts_zero`).

**Extension points**: S1.222 (samples); S1.256 (today's statistics passes onto accumulators); S1.304; S1.337; S1.358
(the recorder reads cells and day rows); S1.402; S1.453; S1.477; S1.478 (population and labour counts); S1.479; S1.480;
S2.128; S2.161; S2.174; S2.175; S2.176; S2.215; S8.122; S4.124; S4.159 (pension measures); S4.171; S4.180; S4.184;
S5.121 (tax receipts); S5.133; S5.137; S5.138; S5.142 (the election's counts); S5.158; S5.186; S6.105; S6.111; S6.115
(research, productivity, labour state); S6.118; S6.126; S6.129; S6.130; S6.134 (the map's sums by zone).

**Unit tests**: `flow_accumulator_refused`; `merge_order_free`; `death_moves_count_and_exposure`;
`age_crossing_moves_class`; `exposure_integral_exact`; `period_close_resets_by_stamp`; `heavy_day_merge_bounded`;
`opening_counts_once`; `empty_cell_counts_zero`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-102 — every published labour-force and population figure equals its accumulator's closed period
value, and no release passes over persons, from the first release.

**Budget**: volumes: stock events ≈ 20 k a day, 115 k on a catastrophe day (measured at these counts; their callers
carry them). Units: stock event ≤ 20 ns. its share of fin.fixed.stats: 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.5 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the
chunk deltas' merge; releases are `sys-sta`'s share, flow tallies S1.254's). ledger line 18 (records): +3.2 MB
resident (0.4 M cells × 8 B). Ratchets `[fin.stats]`: `stock_event_ns` 20, `merge_core_ms` 0.5 (added).

**Guards**: an accumulator's cells are written only by its declared maintaining events (`#[maintained(writer = …)]`,
PC-101); the audit never reads them as evidence.

**Not allowed**: a monthly pass over persons or accounts; a statistic computed at the close from anything but
accumulators, samples or records; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party
pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Accumulators` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F stats` within `stock_event_ns`, `merge_core_ms`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "Statistics accumulators" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.222 — Sample frames and saved samples

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "Sample frames".
**Depends on**: S1.165 (the parties-by-zone-and-kind index instance the frames read); S1.221 (the accumulators a
sample's records close into); S1.176 (named world streams).
**Goal**: A statistics agency's survey or a polling firm's poll reads the records of a sample drawn from a declared
frame on its own world stream (STA.2, CHN.3), sized by its survey design, kept as a panel of references until redrawn;
no frame is a new index and no observer draws from a world stream.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/frames.rs` | `SampleFrame`: a frame over an index instance, a draw, a saved sample |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/frames_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/stats.rs` | -F driver: 10 k-member samples drawn from a 3.35 M frame |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "Sample frames" |

**Design**:
- A frame is declared (K-21) as a filter over S1.165's parties-by-zone-and-kind instance (households of a region, firms
  of an industry through its kind's key, adults of a country); a sample is drawn from it on the agency's world stream
  (`STA.sample` keyed by the survey and period), sized by the survey design (STA.5, POLICY), and saved as a list of
  references — a panel kept until its design redraws it; the frame's members are read through the instance's runs.
- An observer's panels draw on observer streams (K-18), never on a world frame's stream (REP.16); this base serves the
  world's agencies only.
- A sampled party that ended reads as ended (S1.194) and is replaced by the design's rule.
- Save: samples saved as reference lists. Measurement: `StoreStats`; draws report members visited.

**Edge cases**:
- E6: samples round-trip (`sample_round_trip`).
- E7: a draw keyed by (stream, survey, period) is the same for any chunking (`draw_same_for_any_chunking`).
- E9: samples bounded by their design (`sample_bounded_by_design`).
- E10: a sampled party that ended is replaced by the design's rule (`ended_member_replaced`).
- E13: an empty frame yields an empty sample (`empty_frame_empty_sample`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `sample_drawn_on_agency_stream`; `sample_round_trip`; `draw_same_for_any_chunking`;
`sample_bounded_by_design`; `ended_member_replaced`; `empty_frame_empty_sample`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-102 applies (a release's rows visited equal its sample's size).

**Budget**: volumes: samples of 1–10 k members per survey a month, polls of 1–2 k. Units: a member drawn ≤ 50 ns (its
callers carry the shares). ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB (reuses the parties-by-zone-and-kind instance,
S1.165); samples ≤ 1 MB in line 18. Ratchets `[fin.stats]`: `draw_ns` 50 (added).

**Guards**: a frame's draw takes a world stream; PC-19 refuses an observer stream there.

**Not allowed**: an index instance of its own; a sample drawn on an observer stream for a world agency or the
reverse; a sample growing without its design; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or
per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

### S1.223 — Life records on storage within their horizon

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: OBS.10 PROCESS *(part: the record kept compactly within its horizon; its entries written at S8.199)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "Life records".
**Depends on**: S1.212 (`StoredLog`'s immutable segments and frame index); S1.207 (the person kind and its
life-record-kept bit).
**Goal**: Every person's life is recorded compactly as it happens — its events and the concern that tipped each of its
decisions — into write buffers flushed each day as a person-sorted segment on storage; segments are merged in tiers
by a bounded rolling job, entries past the life record's declared horizon (SET.13) are dropped, and a dead person's
record is dropped unless it held an office or founded a firm. Resident memory holds only the buffers and the frame
index; a person's record is read in a bounded number of frame reads.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/life.rs` | `LifeRecords`: the stored kind, append, death pruning, reads, prefetch |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/life_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/records.rs` | -F driver: 1.6 M / 0.8 M / 1.6 M appends a day over two years; reads |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "Life records" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.records]` keys below; `[resolution] horizon_life_records_days = 730` |

**Design**:
- Declared life-record kinds (K-21): birth, schooling, job taken and left, pay changed, partnered, child, home, firm
  founded, office taken and left, elected, illness, a decision's tipping concern (MND.15), death; each with its payload
  width (0, 2 or 12 B: a concern handle; a counterpart reference and an amount).
- `append(person, day, kind, payload)`: into the calling chunk's write buffer (K-03); 3.8 ns VM; nothing else touched.
- The kind on S1.212's stored log: key (person, day, kind); 4 KiB frames; tiers day → week → month → quarter → year
  by the log's `merge_slice` (≤ 4 MB of input a day), dropping entries past the horizon and the runs of dead persons
  whose kept bit (S1.207) is clear — a death entry closes a run; ≤ 20 segments stand within two years.
- Reads: `record_of(person, from, to)` reads ≤ 20 frames (≤ 1 ms with storage latency), outside the turn for the
  observer and the biography (OBS.11). In the turn a reader uses the one prefetch form: `prefetch(persons, into)`
  issued at a stage's apply — the frames every person needs deduplicated, sorted by offset and read as one storage
  round, decoded by the pool's chunks as they land (spread over the chunk plan) into `into`, a K-03 buffer the caller
  names: a day buffer released at 10e, or a held buffer the caller owns across days and releases (a campaign's daily
  slices). The reader reads `into` at memory speed at its decision.
- The horizon is the life record's RESOLUTION primitive (SET.13, owner OBS), `[resolution]
  horizon_life_records_days`, which this step sets (730 at the design point); its play value is the budget's (E 41).
- Save: segments shared by the snapshots that list them (S1.212); write buffers empty at a save; held prefetch buffers
  saved with their owners. Measurement: `StoreStats` (resident bytes, stored MB a simulated year).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe's deaths append death entries; their runs drop at the next merges (`dead_run_dropped_unless_kept`).
- E6: segments listed by the snapshot round-trip; buffers empty at a save (`save_between_days_round_trip`).
- E7: a day's segment is the same for any chunking (`flush_same_for_any_chunking`, S1.212).
- E9: storage flat after the horizon; resident bytes constant (`storage_flat_after_horizon`).
- E10: a person's slot reused after its death holds a new reference; its runs never mix (`reused_slot_runs_apart`).
- E11: day zero records nothing; the opening's persons start at their opening entries (`opening_entries_first`).

**Extension points**: S8.121; S8.124; S8.125; S8.199 (entries at their events, the reason recorded, the biography's
hand-off; OBS.10 completes there); S5.144 (a government's forming prefetches its shortlist).

**Unit tests**: `append_then_read_after_flush`; `merge_drops_past_horizon_and_dead`; `dead_run_dropped_unless_kept`;
`kept_record_survives_death`; `reused_slot_runs_apart`; `storage_flat_after_horizon`; `opening_entries_first`;
`read_touches_at_most_one_frame_a_segment`; `prefetch_one_round_spread_over_chunks`; `held_prefetch_survives_the_day`;
`save_between_days_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: none until S8.199.

**Budget**: volumes: appends 1.6 M / 0.8 M / 1.6 M a day (the design point's count; the appending steps carry them);
merges ≤ 4 MB input a day. Units: append 3.8 ns VM; a record read ≤ 20 frames; a prefetch ≤ 20 frames and ≤ 85 µs of
decode a record, as one storage round (its callers carry the shares: S5.144 ≈ 600 records spread over the days between
tally and formation). its share of fin.fixed.observer: 18 / 12 / 18 core-ms (B / NB / H) (flush 12 / 6 / 12 and the
tiers' merge 6 / 6 / 6). ledger line 18 (records): +7 MB resident (write buffers, frame index). saved: ≈ 250 MB a
simulated year of shared segments. Ratchets `[fin.records]`: `append_ns` 3.8, `life_record_bytes` 4,
`storage_mb_per_year` 250, `life_resident_mb` 7 (added), `life_flush_core_ms` 18 (added), `prefetch_record_us` 85
(added).

**Guards**: `LifeRecords` is written only through `append` (PC-15); no world crate reads `record_of` except through a
declared decision's budgeted read (PC-01 layering keeps the observer's reads above the world).

**Not allowed**: a resident index per person; a record without a horizon; a dead person's record kept without the kept
bit; a merge of a whole tier in one day; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or
per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `LifeRecords` built on `StoredLog`; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F records` within `append_ns`, `life_record_bytes`, `storage_mb_per_year`, `life_resident_mb`,
  `life_flush_core_ms`, `prefetch_record_us`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "Life records" written; the life record's horizon in the register and Appendix C.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.224 — Tallies and votes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.6 "Tallies".
**Depends on**: S1.165 (electorates filter its parties-by-zone-and-kind instance); S1.207 (adults are persons); S1.160
(per-shard tally buffers).
**Goal**: One kernel counts every vote in the world — elections, parliament votes, incorporation votes, shareholder
meetings, takeover acceptances, bondholder and exchange-offer votes — over an electorate fixed at its record date, each
voter's choice tallied as it is cast into per-shard (district, choice) sums with its weight, merged exactly; no ballot
is stored, and a recount reads the choices' own source.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/tally.rs` | `Electorate`, `Tally`: cast, merge, result |
| `crates/kernel/phx-record/src/tally_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/tallies.rs` | -F driver: 5.6 M adults in 3 countries' districts; 10⁵ holders on one meeting |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.6 "Tallies" |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.tallies]` (added) |

**Design**:
- `Electorate`: a filter over S1.165's parties-by-zone-and-kind instance (adults of a country or district, residents
  of a settlement; no instance of its own) or a holder list at a record date (K-65's holders of record), fixed when
  the vote is called; a voter who dies or sells
  after the record date is handled by the vote's rule (the kernel counts whom the electorate names).
- `cast(tally, district, choice, weight)`: a column add in the calling shard's (district, choice) cells (K-03), weight
  i64 (one a person; shares or face for holders); abstention is a choice. `close()` merges shards in shard order (K-13):
  exact integer sums, the same for any worker count.
- Results are handed to the vote's rule (a sys-* rule reads thresholds and allotment, POL.1, MNA.2, CRD.6), which
  publishes them as records (S1.215) and events (S1.212).
- No ballot is kept (Law 15: a vote is a decision, not a draw; the choice lives in its source — the campaign's
  windowed intention column, a holder's recorded decision); the audit recounts from that source (N1).
- Campaign intentions are the person kind's windowed group (S1.197), not part of this kernel; an election's counts may
  equally be read from K-39's intention counts (S1.221), which its step chooses.
- Measurement: `StoreStats` (cells); `close` reports rows merged.

**Edge cases**: E5: a large vote's casts run on the pool (`many_casts_on_pool`). E7: merge order-free
(`merge_same_for_any_sharding`). E8: a weight sum beyond i64 stops the run (`weight_overflow_stops`). E13: a district
with no voter reads zero votes (`empty_district_zero_votes`). E14: a voter casting twice in one vote stops the run,
checked by the electorate's cast bit (`double_cast_stops`).

**Extension points**: S2.124; S3.124 (an exchange offer's holdouts and collective action, TRS.5); S3.138 (holders' votes
on acceleration and waivers, CRD.6); S3.140 (syndicate lenders' votes); S3.150; S3.155 (shareholder meetings, EQY.5);
S8.124; S8.127; S4.176 (takeover acceptances and squeeze-out, MNA.2).

**Unit tests**: `cast_and_close_sum_exact`; `merge_same_for_any_sharding`; `double_cast_stops`; `weight_overflow_stops`;
`electorate_fixed_at_record_date`; `many_casts_on_pool`; `empty_district_zero_votes`.

**Live checks**: none until S3.124 (its first user).

**Budget**: volumes: measured at 5.6 M casts (the largest electorate); shareholder meetings ≤ 10⁵ holders each. Units:
≤ 5 ns a cast (its callers carry the shares on `fin.fixed.holder_rows`). ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB
(reuses the parties-by-zone-and-kind instance, S1.165; cells only, districts × choices × 8 B); ledger line 21 (day
buffers): cast bits ≤ 1 MB on a vote's day. Ratchets `[fin.tallies]`: `cast_ns` 5 (added).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a stored ballot; a drawn result; a tally over an electorate fixed after the vote; an index instance of
its own; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core
bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Electorate` and `Tally` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F tallies` within `cast_ns`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6 "Tallies" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.225 — The due wheel in phx-agenda with due-day runs

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.7 (phx-agenda) "The due wheel".
**Depends on**: S1.169 (chunk plans and the pool for takes); S1.160 (page-granular day buffers); S1.112 (the crate map's
`phx-agenda`, L1.7); S1.180 (families and dated-reason kinds declared, with `family_capacity`); S1.181 (the entry's
8-bit family codes, `data/shared/families.toml`: 0–77, 255 for holdings); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: Every dated row — a contract's next due, a commitment, a process's completion, a lapse, a message due, a
party's dated one-off reason — waits as a 4 B entry in the bucket of its day over a 128-day horizon, or in a far list
beyond it; a day's take gives each family's due rows slot-sorted in runs, taken on the pool, stale entries skipped by
their owner's own due. This step builds the wheel in `phx-agenda`; S1.226 moves today's users onto it.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs` | the crate (L1.7), created by this step |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/wheel.rs` | `DueWheel`: buckets, far list, file, take, refile at load |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/wheel_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/wheel.rs` | -F driver: `[store] wheel_rows` over `wheel_days` + `wheel_far`; takes at `[day.*] dues` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.7 "The due wheel" |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.wheel]` keys below |

**Design**:
- Entry 4 B: family 8 bits | slot 24 bits (a contract family, a commitment family, a process kind, an offer book, the
  messages, or a declared dated-reason family whose slot is a party's of one kind, e.g. a firm's statement-ready date).
  The kind catalogue asserts `family_capacity` (≤ 255 families; code 255 is holdings, K-60) and each family's rows
  < 2²⁴ (the largest at the design point, policies, 6.75 M); a row beyond stops the run (`capacity_exceeded!`).
- Buckets: a ring of 128 day buckets (`[store] wheel_days`); a bucket is a list of per-chunk page runs (K-03), so a
  filing from any chunk appends to its own run (3.1 ns VM) without a lock. The far list: 8 B entries (day u32 +
  entry), read every half horizon into the buckets now in reach.
- Take (1a): today's runs joined, split by family (counting sort on 8 bits), radix-sorted by slot within each family on
  the pool (K-11), duplicates removed: `today() -> &[FamilyRun]`, slot-sorted runs read in slot order by their takers.
- Lazy invalidation: the taker checks each entry against its owner's own due (the row's due column, or its terms'
  schedule for families that keep none — employment, pensions in payment, pension rights — filed from their terms,
  K-55) and skips a stale one; a closed row, or a slot reused by a row not due today, is skipped the same way.
- Dates: an entry is filed on its business day (TIME.3's convention applied by the filer), so the first business day
  after closed days holds their dues; a non-business day's bucket holds only what TIME.8 runs.
- Save: `#[saved(skip, rebuild = refile)]`: at load every owner refiles its rows from their own dues and terms (≈ 36 M
  × 3 ns ≈ 0.1 s); the far list likewise. Measurement: `StoreStats` (entries, bytes, heaviest bucket); takes report
  rows visited through `ExecCounters::visited`.
- Retires the placeholder ratchet `[fin.kept] due_ns` of S1.119, replaced by `[fin.wheel]`. The `#[clause("TIME.3")]`
  carrier (done at S0.08) moves to it with S1.226.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a month-end bucket of 22.5 M entries is taken on the pool (`month_end_take_on_pool`); a Monday after closed days
  takes their rolled dues (`closed_days_dues_on_next_business_day`).
- E6: rebuilt at load equal to the saved state's dues (`refile_after_load_equals`).
- E7: runs sorted by slot, the same for any worker count (`take_same_for_any_chunking`).
- E8: a family beyond 255 or a slot beyond 2²⁴ stops the run (`entry_width_refused`).
- E10: stale entries of closed rows or reused slots skipped (`stale_entry_skipped`).
- E11: day zero files the opening's rows; the first day takes them (`opening_rows_taken_first_day`).

**Extension points**: S1.226 (today's users); S1.227 (the agenda reuses its bucket ring); S1.237 (messages due);
S1.242; S1.251 (dated commitments); S1.257; S1.260; S1.281; S1.289 (production kinks); S1.290; S1.296 (offers'

### S1.227 — The decision agenda: one entry a party, a next day a reason

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.7 "The decision agenda".
**Depends on**: S1.225 (the day-bucket ring and far list it reuses); S1.196 (each kind's agenda group of next-day
slots); S1.197 (windowed slots); S1.180 (each kind's declared reasons); S1.178 (the day's facts: business days); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: A party is touched only on a day one of its reasons falls due or it is woken: each party has one entry at the
earliest of its reasons, and each reason's next day is a 2-byte slot in its own record. The day's take gives each due
party with the mask of its due reasons and its wakes, by kind, in slot order; refiling and waking are O(1) a reason.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/agenda.rs` | `Agenda`: slots, entries, take, refile, wake, the wake ring |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/agenda_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/agenda.rs` | -F driver: `[store] agenda_entries` parties, 27 / 24 slots; takes at `[day.*] entries` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.7 "The decision agenda" (the slot lists; replacing §7.3's agent-table agenda) |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.agenda]` keys below |

**Design**:
- Reasons are declared per kind (K-21): continuous decisions (a `DecisionSchedule`, read from `phx-core`, and the
  business-day rule), lumpy decisions' next reviews (K-101), hazards' next hits (K-44), kinks (K-68), dated needs.
- Slot lists (the finished world's): household 27 — spend, buffer, search, ages (its persons' birth-dated needs: school
  entry, enrolment's window, statutory ages, age-class crossings), filing · death, illness, disability, conception,
  dwelling_damage, vehicle_damage, harm, formation_meeting, housing_meeting · work, where_to_live, vehicle, borrow,
  bank_choice, supplier_choice, heuristic, found, portfolio (also a holder's answer to an offer), insure, retrain,
  separate, pension (the earliest of its members' own review days, which sit on their pension pot rows, S4.150); plus
  `vote` in the household's windowed campaign group (S1.197). Firm 24 — visit, pay_round, EQY.meeting · stock_out,
  wear, output_threshold · plant_failure, damage, harm, discovery, imitation · price, wage, investment, lines,
  extraction, shipping, bank_choice, supplier_choice, insure, innovate, finance, grant_terms, carry (the carry
  decision's review months out, S4.120). Institutions per kind (e.g. `accept`, `position`; a fund's `carry` in its own
  layout). A slot not yet activated reads "none".
- Record words: `base` u32 and one u16 a slot = day − base (`u16::MAX` none, `u16::MAX − 1` beyond the window). A
  hazard's or a review's day beyond base + 65 533 books a redraw at that edge (exact: daily chances are memoryless,
  REP.7); a dated reason beyond it is re-derived from its schedule or birth dates at a later refile.
- Entries: 4 B (party key) in the day's bucket of a ring like the wheel's, 8 B in the far list; an entry is live when
  the party is live and its `base` equals the bucket's day (lazy invalidation).
- Phases (TIME.5, CHN.3): a draw on `TIME.phase` keyed (party, schedule), recomputed when needed, never stored.
- Take (1a): today's bucket radix-sorted by key on the pool, duplicates removed; per party the mask of slots at delta 0
  and its wakes, merged by key; `DueParties` runs per kind in slot order for 3b, 4a, 5b, 5c through `for_agenda`. On a
  non-business day a business-only reason due moves to the next business day (K-19, TIME.8).
- Refile (at the stage's apply): each handled slot takes its owner's next day; `base` = the minimum; deltas rewritten;
  one entry filed. O(slots) in the party's own record.
- `wake(party, kind, day)` (apply phases only): a slotted kind sets its slot to min(slot, day) and files an entry; a
  woken-only kind (a need or a notice with no review of its own) puts (packed reference with generation, kind) in the
  wake ring's buffer for that day — at most seven days ahead. A lumpy kind with no slot on a party's kind books its
  next occasion ≤ 7 days ahead as a wake-ring entry and, beyond that, as a dated message to itself (S1.237) whose lapse
  is the review day.
- Save: slots and bases are saved columns; buckets, far list and wake ring are `#[saved(skip, rebuild = refile_all)]`
  (3.35 M × 3 ns). Measurement: `StoreStats`; takes and refiles report rows visited.
- The `#[clause("TIME.5", "REP.12")]` carriers (done at S0.08, S0.28) move to `Agenda`. The world's wheels and modulo
  scans move onto it at S1.228–S1.236.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a surprise waking every household: each redraw an O(1) slot write and one entry (`mass_wake_files_entries`).
- E6: rebuilt at load, the same take (`rebuild_takes_same`).
- E7: takes sorted by key (`take_same_for_any_chunking`).
- E8: slots beyond the group's bytes refused at assembly; a wake beyond seven days stops the run (`far_wake_refused`).
- E10: an ended party's entry skipped (`stale_entry_skipped`).
- E11: every party's slots filed once the opening is done, phases drawn then (`opening_files_every_party`).
- E14: two wakes of one kind the same day taken once (`double_wake_once`).

**Extension points**: S1.228; S1.229; S1.230; S1.231; S1.232; S1.233; S1.234; S1.235; S1.236 (schedules, pay
rounds, hazards onto it); S1.237; S1.239 (crossings wake); S1.265; S1.285; S1.289 (kinks); S1.290; S1.293; S1.328;
S1.330; S1.342; S1.348; S1.350; S2.101; S2.108; S2.120; S2.123 (the `finance` slot); S2.195; S3.105; S3.111; S3.119;
S3.145; S3.148; S3.155; S3.160; S3.205; S3.209; S3.212; S4.105; S4.107; S4.120 (the firm slot `carry`); S4.145; S4.146;
S4.150; S4.172; S4.174; S4.179; S5.109; S5.123; S5.137; S6.117.

**Unit tests**: `earliest_slot_is_entry`; `refile_rebases_deltas`; `beyond_window_books_redraw`;
`dated_reason_rederived_past_window`; `business_only_reason_moves_on_closed_day`; `wake_sets_min_and_files`;
`woken_only_kind_through_ring`; `double_wake_once`; `far_wake_refused`; `stale_entry_skipped`;
`take_same_for_any_chunking`; `rebuild_takes_same`; `opening_files_every_party`; `mass_wake_files_entries`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-104 — rows visited per kind per stage never exceed that day's due parties plus declared sweeps
(the sweep ledger, S1.117), from S1.228 on.

**Budget**: volumes: `[store] agenda_entries` (3.35 M); the day's take at 1a is the core's own: adds 1.6 M / 0.95 M /
1.6 M items to `fin.agenda.entry_ns`; refiles as many (`fin.agenda.file_ns`); wakes ≤ 3.35 M on a surprise day (their
callers carry them). Units: entry 2.3 ns VM, file 3.1 ns VM, wake ≤ 10 ns. ledger line 14 (wheel and agenda): +15 MB
resident (3.35 M × 4 B + far entries); slots are in the records (lines 4–6, +0 B). Ratchets `[fin.agenda]`: `entry_ns`
2.3, `file_ns` 3.1, `mb` 15, `wake_ns` 10 (added).

**Guards**: PC-96 (S1.121) refuses a whole-kind traversal outside `for_agenda` or a declared sweep; `wake` is not
reachable from a decide phase (`&self` handlers, R3).

**Not allowed**: a second entry a party; a wheel per reason; a stored phase; a `(day + slot) % days` test; an edit of
`phx-world` or an older kernel crate; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every
party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Agenda` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F agenda` within `entry_ns`, `file_ns`, `mb`, `wake_ns`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.7 "The decision agenda" written; §7.3's agenda retired.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.235 — Hazards drawn ahead on the agenda

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.7 "Hazards drawn ahead".
**Depends on**: S1.227 (hazards' next hits are agenda slots); S1.207 (the persons a hit may reach); S1.176 (named
streams keyed by subject and day); S1.177 (the hazard streams declared by family, with their draw types); S1.213
(every occurrence recorded before any party reacts).
**Goal**: Every declared hazard acts on its subjects by the draw scheme REP.7 declares: each subject's next hit of each
process is drawn ahead on its own stream and held as an agenda slot (or, for tiles, zones and regions, a small column);
it is drawn again when anything its rate reads changes or on the next day its rate may change; on a hit day the persons
it reaches are drawn, the occurrence is recorded, and the outcome follows on the pool. A subject nothing hits is not
visited. This step builds the kernel in `phx-agenda`; S1.236 moves today's hazards onto it.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/hazard.rs` | booking, following, redraw, subjects' columns |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/hazard_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/hazards.rs` | -F driver: 3.35 M subjects' next hits; 68 k hits, 75 k redraws a day |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.7 "Hazards drawn ahead" |

**Design**:
- A hazard process is declared (CHN.2, K-21): its subject (a party kind for its persons' or its own hazards; a holding
  class through its holder; a tile, zone or region), its rate as a rule over declared state (a TECHNOLOGY table),
  what an occurrence does (its outcome rule), its stream `<SYS>.<process>`, and the day its rate may next change
  (`changes_after`).
- Booking from day d (moved `any_hit`, `next_booking`): p = 1 − Π(1 − qᵢ) over the subject's persons (or its own q),
  computed as −expm1(Σ log1p(−qᵢ)); constant until c, the earliest day any rate may change; a geometric draw keyed
  (process, subject, d) gives a hit before c, else a redraw at c; p = 0 with no c books nothing. The day goes into the
  subject's slot (S1.227); tiles', zones' and regions' next hits into a u32 column a process over
  the declared subjects (≤ 1 MB).
- Hit (3b, pool by subject range over the day's due list): which persons it reaches, each by its own qᵢ conditioned on
  at least one (`binomials_joint_at_least_one`); the occurrence recorded (S1.212) first (CHN.4); the outcome rules run
  in the processes' declared order (POP.3 before POP.4) on the subject's own row; the processes whose rate inputs the
  outcome changed are rebooked from the next day, the others keep their days.
- Redraw: an outcome, a person joining or leaving, or a changed attribute rebooks the subject's processes that read
  it (declared reads), O(processes) at the apply; a redraw due at c draws from c.
- Hazards over counts (catastrophes, GEO.8): a tile's hit at 3a is handed to its outcome rule, which draws the owners
  from the zone's stock through the place index (K-27, REP.23) in `phx-world`'s routing (S1.294); this kernel reads no
  higher crate. Each owner's loss is its own occurrence subject.
- Draws are keyed by (stream, subject, day, index): the result is the same for any worker count (E7); the observer
  never draws from a world stream (REP.16).
- Save: next-hit days are the subjects' saved slots (E6). Measurement: `StoreStats` (subjects booked a process); the
  follow reports rows visited.
- The `#[clause("REP.7", "CHN.2", "CHN.4")]` carriers (done at S0.28, S0.10) move here with S1.236.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe on a tile hands one hit to its outcome rule (`tile_hit_handed_to_outcome`).
- E5: hits are drawn per subject, never bunched by the calendar (`hits_independent_of_calendar`).
- E6: next hits saved; a load follows the same hits (`save_round_trip_same_hits`).
- E7: keyed draws (`follow_same_for_any_chunking`).
- E8: a chance outside [0, 1] stops the run (`chance_outside_probability_stops`).
- E11: every subject booked once the opening is done (`opening_books_every_subject`).
- E14: two processes hitting one household the same day apply in declared order (`processes_in_declared_order`).

**Extension points**: S1.236 (today's hazards onto it); S1.294; S1.321; S1.401; S2.129 (plant failures by age, CAP.6);
S2.150; S2.202; S8.102 (characters drawn at birth); S8.105; S8.198; S4.125; S4.133; S4.134 (harm to third parties);
S5.128; S6.107 (discovery, a firm subject); S6.109 (imitation, a region subject); S6.122 (meetings drawn).

**Unit tests**: `any_hit_without_cancellation`; `hit_before_change_else_redraw`; `zero_chance_books_nothing`;
`persons_reached_at_least_one`; `occurrence_recorded_before_outcome`; `processes_in_declared_order`;
`changed_inputs_rebook_only_readers`; `follow_same_for_any_chunking`; `chance_outside_probability_stops`;
`tile_hit_handed_to_outcome`; `hits_independent_of_calendar`; `opening_books_every_subject`;
`region_subject_column`; `save_round_trip_same_hits`.

**Live checks**: LC-0-41 (each hazard's hits counted as events of its kind the day it draws them) and CHN.7's measure
read the log from S1.236 on.

**Budget**: measured at 68 k hits and 75 k redraws a day (B, NB, H) over 3.35 M parties and 40 k tiles; its callers
(S1.401, S1.402, S1.464, …) carry the counts on `fin.hazards.hit_ns` and `redraw_ns`. Units: hit 727 ns VM with a
synthetic outcome (one row write), redraw 73 ns VM; pool by subject range. ledger line 15 (hazards, streamed): +1 MB
resident (subjects' columns); party slots +0 B (named slots, S1.227). Ratchets `[fin.hazards]`: `hit_ns` 727,
`redraw_ns` 73.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a wheel a process; a subject visited without a due hit or redraw; an outcome drawn (CHN.5); an
occurrence recorded after its outcome; a read of a higher crate; an edit of `phx-world` or an older kernel crate
(S1.236's); a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Booking and following built in `phx-agenda`; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.

- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.7 "Hazards drawn ahead" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.237 — Messages and notices

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: REP.21 PROCESS *(part)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.7 "Messages and notices".
**Depends on**: S1.225 (a message falls due on the wheel); S1.227 (its due day wakes its addressee); S1.159
(`MessageRef` with generation); S1.165 (the per-addressee index instance); S1.194 (a sender resolved through its
tombstone).
**Goal**: Every notice, demand, call, protocol message and queued intent addressed to a party is a typed 24 B message
with its sender, addressee, kind, issue day, due day and payload; it waits on the wheel for its due day, wakes its
addressee there as an occasion (REP.21), lapses at stage 1 by its kind's rule, follows an ending party to its estate or
lapses, and is saved as a pending event.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/messages.rs` | `Messages`: rows, payload arenas, post, answer, lapse, re-address |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/messages_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/messages.rs` | -F driver: 0.5 M live; 300 k posts on a heavy day |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.7 "Messages and notices" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.messages]` (added); `[store] messages_live = 500_000` (added) |

**Design**:
- Message kinds are declared (K-21): payload type, the decision kind it wakes (the addressee's occasion), whether it
  awaits an answer, its lapse rule (what an unanswered message does at its due: the contract or rule that consumes it
  decides the consequence in that day's stages, TIME.7), and its ending rule (to the estate or successor, or lapse).
- Row, 20 B `#[derive(Pod)]`: addressee key u32 · sender key u32 · kind 12 bits and flags 4 (answered, lapsed) u16 ·
  the two parties' generations' low 8 bits u16 · issued and due days as u16 offsets from the run's first day (the
  directory's declared run capacity) · payload u32 — inline where the kind's payload is one reference (a
  `ContractRef`, an `OfferRef`), otherwise an index into the kind's typed payload arena (K-04, 12 B an amount-bearing
  payload). Rows in a K-02 slot table with generation (`MessageRef`); one index instance, by addressee (K-06). The
  due list is the wheel's entries (the messages' family, S1.225); no index by sender.
- `post(kind, from, to, due, payload)` (apply phases): a message issued in stage 9 due before the next business day
  stops the run (TIME.7); the row is filed on the wheel at its due day (the messages' family). ≤ 50 ns.
- Due (1a): the wheel's take hands today's messages; each wakes its addressee for its kind (S1.227), and the
  addressee's handler reads its messages through the addressee index at its occasion; `answer(m, payload)` marks it
  and, for a protocol, posts the reply.
- Lapse (1b): a due message unanswered past its due lapses by its kind's rule (≤ 10 ns); the player's queued intents
  (OBS.4) are messages to its household that lapse at stage 1 (TIME.8).
- Endings (2f): an addressee ended today has its messages found through the addressee index (O(k)) and re-addressed
  to its estate or successor or lapsed, by kind. A sender is resolved only when its message is used (an answer, a
  consequence): a key whose low generation bits no longer match is looked up in the directory's tombstones and
  followed to its successor (S1.194), or the message lapses by its kind's rule; 8 bits of generation are exact within
  256 reuses of a slot inside a message's life (days to weeks).
- Save: rows, payload arenas and flags saved (SET.12: pending events); the indexes and the wheel's entries rebuilt.
  Measurement: `StoreStats`; lapse and ending passes report rows visited.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a margin spiral's or a bank run's 300 k posts on a day, on the pool into per-chunk runs (`many_posts_one_day`).
- E5: TIME.7's next-business-day rule across closed days (`stage_nine_due_next_business_day`).
- E6: live messages round-trip; indexes rebuilt (`save_round_trip_messages`).
- E10: an ending party's messages re-addressed or lapsed the same day (`ending_readdresses_by_kind`).
- E14: two notices to one party the same day are two messages, one occasion for their decision kind
  (`two_messages_one_occasion`).

**Extension points**: S1.238 (today's notices, applications and offers); S1.265; S1.317; S1.321; S1.340; S1.343; S1.350;
S2.101; S2.104; S2.105; S2.114; S2.120; S2.124; S2.150; S2.153; S2.179; S2.183; S2.192; S2.193; S3.107; S3.114;
S3.117; S3.124; S3.133; S3.176; S3.195; S4.107; S4.108; S4.109; S4.111; S4.114; S4.133; S4.136; S4.139; S4.153; S4.158;
S4.181; S5.132; S5.153; S5.178; S6.122.

**Unit tests**: `post_files_on_due_day`; `stage_nine_due_next_business_day`; `due_wakes_addressee_kind`;
`unanswered_lapses_by_rule`; `ending_readdresses_by_kind`; `answer_posts_reply`; `many_posts_one_day`;
`save_round_trip_messages`; `two_messages_one_occasion`; `ended_sender_followed_or_lapses`.

**Live checks**: LC-1-105 — no message is answered or consumed before its due day's stage 1, and every stage-9 demand
is due no earlier than the next business day (TIME.7), from the first notice.

**Budget**: volumes: `[store] messages_live` (0.5 M; 0.1–0.5 M live); posts ≈ 50 k B, 300 k H; lapses as many.
Access: event-driven, due on the wheel. Units: post ≤ 50 ns, lapse ≤ 10 ns; a sender's tombstone lookup ≤ 60 ns, only
for an ended sender. its share of fin.fixed.open: 0.5 / 0.1 / 0.5 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the day's lapses at 1b; posts
and answers ride their callers' units). ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +15 MB resident (0.5 M × ≈ 30 B: a 20 B row,
5.3 B of the addressee index, ≈ 5 B of payload arena on average); the wheel's 4 B entries are line 14's. saved: +15 MB
(pending events, SET.12). Ratchets `[fin.messages]` (added): `post_ns` 50, `lapse_ns` 10, `mb` 15.

**Guards**: messages written only through `post`, `answer`, `lapse`, `readdress` (PC-15).

**Not allowed**: a notice kept as a world `Vec` or set; a demand paid in the stage it was issued; a message naming an
ended party after its day; a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; an edit of `phx-world` or an
older kernel crate; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `Messages` built; tests pass.
- [ ] Fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F messages` within `post_ns`, `lapse_ns`, `mb`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.7 "Messages and notices" written.
- [ ] Both reviews' findings fixed; status `done`, section removed.

### S1.239 — The trigger index

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: index
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.7 "The trigger index".
**Depends on**: S1.165 (sorted runs maintained by events); S1.227 (crossings wake through the agenda).
**Goal**: A party that wants to be woken when a watched series crosses a threshold — a price crossing its own trigger,
a stop, a mandate boundary, a covenant ratio, a conversion trigger, a reserve floor — registers it once; when the series
takes a new value, only the thresholds in the crossed interval are found, in O(log n + k), and their parties woken for
their decision kind. Nothing scans holders.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/triggers.rs` | `Triggers`: runs per (series, direction, decision kind), register, remove, cross |
| `crates/kernel/phx-agenda/src/triggers_tests.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/triggers.rs` | -F driver: `[store] thresholds`; a crash day crossing 300 k |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.7 "The trigger index" |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.triggers]` (added); `[store] thresholds = 600_000` (added) |

**Design**:
- A watched series is a declared handle: a mark (K-86), a rating or a published ratio (K-37), a reserve level, or a
  party position series — a value an owning rule writes and publishes to the index by calling `cross` (a fund's NAV at
  S3.184, a vehicle's tally at 7c, a scheme's funding level at a curve's publication, a bank's capital ratio). Per
  (series, direction up or down, decision kind): a sorted run of entries in 4 KiB blocks with the blocks' least
  thresholds indexed; entry 8 B — threshold u32 as a point on the series' declared tick grid (its price points or
  tick, a rating's grade, a ratio's basis points; a threshold beyond the grid's 2³² points stops the run), party key
  u32. Each registration's kind declares whether it is one-shot (a stop) or standing (a covenant).
- Endings: a party holding registrations carries a flag bit; its ending adds its key to the day's ended-registrants
  list, and a declared sweep (K-14) at the end of 2f, where parties with registrations end, removes their entries from
  every run (≤ 0.6 M entries × 1 ns, only on business days with such an ending, before 10e releases any slot), so no
  entry outlives its party and no reused slot is woken.
- `register(series, direction, kind, threshold, party)` (apply phases, 5d): O(log n) find, shift within a block, split
  at full; `remove` the same.
- `cross(series, from, to)` (when the series' writer publishes a new value: 6c marks, 9d publications): the entries
  in (from, to] of the matching direction's runs, found by two binary searches (the new value converted to the grid);
  each party woken for the run's decision kind (S1.227); one-shot entries removed. A party crossed on two series
  the same day is woken once a kind (E14).
- Stage order (TIME.10): crossings found at 6c or 9d wake parties for the next day's decisions (or the same day's
  later stages the kind declares), never an earlier stage of the same day.
- Save: runs saved; the block index rebuilt. Measurement: `StoreStats` (entries, blocks); crossings report entries
  visited.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a crash day moves every mark: only crossed ranges wake (`crash_wakes_only_crossed`).
- E6: runs round-trip (`save_round_trip_runs`).
- E7: crossings processed per series in threshold order (`same_wakes_any_chunking`).
- E8: a threshold beyond the tick grid's 2³² points stops the run (`threshold_width_refused`).
- E10: an ended party's entries removed by the 2f sweep the day it ends, before its slot is released
  (`ended_registrant_swept_same_day`).
- E14: two series crossing for one party: one wake a kind (`one_wake_a_kind`).

**Extension points**: S1.263; S1.338; S2.122 (net assets crossing zero wakes); S3.102; S3.109 (lenders' limits, doubted
names); S3.112 (collateral eligibility by rating); S3.119; S3.122; S3.137 (covenant thresholds, CRD.6); S3.139
(conversion triggers, CRD.7); S3.184; S3.212 (rating-bound holdings, RAT.4); S4.123 (funds' stops on the NAV series,
FND.4); S4.136; S4.138; S4.153; S4.155 (schemes' funding levels and trustees' thresholds); S4.161 (banks' capital ratio

#### phx-ledger and phx-contract (S1.240–S1.270)

These steps build the two crates through which money and every contract between named parties move. `phx-ledger`
holds the money accounts (K-47), the decided flows and the fused chains' entry points (K-48), settlement (K-49), dated
commitments (K-50), the levy engine (K-51) and the settlement tallies (K-52). `phx-contract` holds the one contract
store (K-53) with its side aggregates (K-54), the interned terms and the day's due plans (K-55), status and arrears
(K-56), books and bulk side moves (K-57), participations (K-58) and accruing statement contracts (K-59). Each base is
followed by the migration of today's users onto it; no base step edits `phx-world` or an older kernel.

The representation:
- **Nets live in `pending`.** A sale is its own payment. A dated item is streamed from the wheel straight into both
  parties' `pending`, with its levies and income line fused through the sweep's hooks (S1.170's `SweepHooks`). Only
  decided flows outside those chains are stored.
- **Contract rows carry only what their family declares.** A side is held in one of four modes: a party column on its
  holder's chain; a party column in the holder's block list; a party column found by a declared sweep; or through the
  terms, whose interned word names a book (K-57) whose owner is the party.
- **Every family of the finished world** is listed in S1.257 with its rows and bytes, under its 8-bit code from
  S1.181 (family 8 bits + slot 24 bits in the chain link and the wheel entry; code 255 is holdings, K-60): 43.2 M
  rows, 1 074.0 MB at the design point (`perf/design.toml` `[store.contracts]`).

**Exit**: the money and contract bases stand at the design point within their `[fin.ledger]`, `[fin.settle]`,
`[fin.dues]`, `[fin.commitments]`, `[fin.contracts]`, `[fin.contracts.*]`, `[fin.terms]`, `[fin.stats]` and
`[fin.waterfall]` ratchets. Today's account, flow, settlement, dated-family and tax structures in `phx-world` are
deleted (S1.244, S1.247, S1.249, S1.252, S1.255, S1.256, S1.260, S1.262, S1.264, S1.266, S1.270).

**Placeholders** (introduced → retired):

| Placeholder | Introduced | Retired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a flow's 15-bit unit denomination (an id beyond 2¹⁵ stops the run) | S1.174 | S1.245 |
| money totals folded by today's settlement apply, moved from `phx-core` into `phx-ledger` (naming S1.248) | S1.244 | S1.248 |
| `[fin.kept] flow_ns` and `flow_h_ns`, today's flows and settlement measured as kept kernels | S1.119 | S1.248 |
| floating and indexed resets read the last published value (naming IDX) | S1.263 | S3.203 |
| books with no world user until today's endings adopt them, measured by `-F` only (naming EST) | S1.267 | S1.344 |
| participations with no world user, measured by `-F` only (naming the opening's joint holdings) | S1.268 | S1.405 |

### S1.240 — Money accounts: one 20-byte row, no owner column, banknotes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: PTY.3 STATE *(part: a person's accounts are its own)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts"; follows §6.1 (stage 7a), §13.
**Depends on**: S1.159 (generation references for the records naming an account); S1.196 (kind records name their
account); S1.207 (the person's `account` and `notes` words); S1.171 (the declared sweep finding a bank's depositors);
S1.180 (products and money-holder classes as declared data); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every account is one 20-byte row — balance, `pending`, issuer and product, currency and flags — the deposit
contract between its holder and its issuer, with no owner column. A person's banknotes are a word of its record; a
firm's or institution's are an account at the central bank.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/accounts.rs` | `Accounts`, `AccountId`, `Product`, `Flags`; `open`, `close`, `add_pending`, `move_notes`, reads |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/accounts_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/ledger.rs` | `-F ledger` driver |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" | the section, written first |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.ledger]` | `row_bytes` 20, `mb` 148, `apply_ns` 7.7, `pending_ns` 3.1, `faults_per_day` 0 |
| `perf/design.toml` `[store]` | `accounts` (7.4 M), `account_products` 64 (added) |

**Design**:
- **The account is the contract.** It is the deposit (or the reserve, banknote or treasury account, MON.1) between the
  holder, named by its record, and the issuer, named by `bank`: one record (REG.14, REP.3), never a K-53 row. An
  overdraft, credit line or card is its facility term (S1.241): the negative balance within `limit` is MON.3's
  recorded loan.
- **Row** (SoA by `AccountId` u32): `balance` i64; `pending` i64 (the business day's net before 7a; closed days'
  commitments, SET.2, TIME.8); `bank` u16 (issuer 10 bits — banks, central banks, correspondents — and product 6
  bits); `currency` u8; `flags` u8 (five side-slot bits, S1.241; frozen; money-holder class 2 bits, K-21).
- **No owner column.** A person's `account` word, or a firm's or institution's record word, names the account;
  further accounts follow through a `Link` slot (S1.241). A bank's depositors are found by
  `#[sweep(accounts, reason = "depositors")]` over holder records, on the rare days a bank fails or is valued whole.
  Each account has one referrer, cleared in the apply that closes it; its slot is released at the close (K-02, SET.7).
- **Banknotes** (MON.4, MON.9, MON.14): a person's are its record's `notes` i32 (smallest units); a firm's or
  institution's are an account of product `notes` at the central bank. One writer, settlement's `move_notes` (any day,
  at the purchase, TIME.8). A person's notes passing 2³¹ − 1 switch to a notes account at that write — a
  representation switch, never a clamp. An unbanked person needs no account.
- **API** (the only writers): `open(holder_class, bank, product, currency)`; `close(id)` (balance and pending 0, else
  a violation); `add_pending(id, Δ)` (the chains' and batches' sweeps only); `commit_range` (S1.248 only);
  `move_notes`. Reads: `balance`, `pending`, `available` (balance + limit + min(pending, 0)), `bank`, `product`. No
  balance setter (Law 5).
- Carried (done at S0.15: MON.1, MON.2; at S1.12: MON.4): their `#[clause]` carriers move to these types.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (rows live, rows ever, bytes, growth a year); traversals report rows through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a bank failure rewrites ≈ 3 M `bank` words by range on the pool — `bank_rewrite_by_range`.
- E3: an unbanked person holds notes in its record only — `notes_only_holder`.
- E6: columns saved, hash equal — `accounts_roundtrip`.
- E8: i64 balances; a person's notes past 2³¹ − 1 switch at the write — `notes_promote_at_limit`; an issuer beyond
  10 bits or a product beyond 6 is refused at assembly — `account_code_capacity`.
- E10: an account closed with money is a violation — `close_nonzero_stops`.
- E13: a currency with no accounts in a country is an empty range — `empty_currency_range`.

**Extension points**: S1.241, S1.243, S1.245, S1.246, S1.250, S1.309, S1.343, S1.405, S1.407, S1.408, S2.117, S2.177,
S2.179, S2.181, S2.193, S2.195, S2.199, S2.200, S3.104, S3.113, S3.119, S3.158, S8.105, S4.102, S4.139, S5.136, S5.159.

**Unit tests**: `notes_only_holder`, `notes_promote_at_limit`, `accounts_roundtrip`, `bank_rewrite_by_range`,
`account_code_capacity`, `close_nonzero_stops`, `empty_currency_range`, `no_balance_setter` (compile-fail).

**Live checks**: none. The audit's Money family reads the columns (S1.353).

**Budget**:
- `fin.ledger.apply_ns` 7.7 VM (10 phone-ns) at 4.5 M / — / 11.0 M items (B′ 7.5 M); `fin.ledger.pending_ns` 3.1 VM
  (4 phone-ns: one i64 add into a range-partitioned `pending` column, no balance read) at — / 1.0 M / —. Miss budget
  ≤ 0.05 an apply.
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +148 MB resident (7.4 M × 20 B); saved: +148 MB.
- ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B (core attribute `notes`, S1.207).

**Guards**: PC-92's hot list gains `accounts.rs`; `balance` has no public setter (compile-fail test).

**Not allowed**: an owner column or per-account `Vec`; a balance written outside settlement's apply; an account per
household (E 46); a default bank.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; `fmt`, `clippy`, tests, `phx-check` pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F ledger` at the design point within `[fin.ledger]` (B, NB, H)
- [ ] §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" written
- [ ] both reviews (the builder's); status `done`; section removed

### S1.241 — Account side slots: facilities, held amounts, links and statements

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts".
**Depends on**: S1.240 (the account row and its slot bits); S1.168 (the `Facility` slot's terms id is an interned
handle); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: the few accounts that carry more than a balance — a facility, money held through a closed bank, a holder's
next account, a card statement, an interest accrual — keep 16-byte side slots in per-range runs, found in O(1) and
walked by 7a's sweep with a cursor; no column rides on every account.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/side.rs` | `SlotKind`, per-range runs, rank directory, `add_slot`, `drop_slot`, `set_limit`, `limit`, `drawn` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/side_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/ledger.rs` | 9.37 M slots filled by kind (`[store] side_rows`); random reads and cursor walks |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.ledger]` | `slot_read_ns` 20 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Slots**, each as wide as its payload in 4-byte words (an account's slots are the kinds its five flag bits name):

  | kind | payload | bytes |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `Facility` | `limit` i64, `terms` u32 (debit rate or margin, fee, committed, cancellable, charging dates, statement schedule) | 12 |
  | `Held` | i64 paid through a closed bank, held until the bank's fate is known | 8 |
  | `Link` | u32: the holder's next account | 4 |
  | `Statement` | a card statement's `amount` i64 and `due` u32 | 12 |
  | `Accrual` | `s` i128 (S1.242); one a sign-dependent or reference-margin rate needs two, a commitment fee one more | 16 |

- **Placement**: accounts in ranges of 4 096 (`CORE_RANGE_BITS`); each range's slots lie in account order. A slot's
  position is a u32 word prefix per 64 accounts plus, for each kind, its width × the popcount of that kind's flags
  among the preceding accounts (five popcounts): a random read is O(1); 7a's
  sweep walks a run with a cursor, O(1) an account. Adding a slot shifts its range's run (≤ 16 KiB; lumpy events
  only: a product change, a facility granted, a bank closing).
- **Facilities** (MON.3, BNK.18): `drawn = max(−balance, 0)` and `undrawn = limit − drawn` are reads, never stored.
  Draws and repayments are payments. `set_limit(account, limit)` is the lender's decision applied at 7c; a limit below
  `drawn` stops the run (BNK.18: only the undrawn part is cut). A payment below −limit fails (MON.3, MON.12).
- **Save**: slots saved; the rank directory rebuilt at load.
- Carried (done at S0.15): MON.3 — its facility carrier moves to `Facility`.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats`; cursor walks report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a bank failure adds `Held` slots in each range's run on the pool — `held_slots_by_range`.
- E6: slots saved, directory rebuilt, hash equal — `side_roundtrip`.
- E8: a range's run past its reserved pages grows in whole pages — `side_run_grows_by_page`.
- E14: two slot changes of one account the same day apply in declared order — `slot_changes_ordered`.

**Extension points**: S1.242, S1.243, S1.244, S1.251.

**Unit tests**: `side_rank_random_read`, `side_insert_shifts_run`, `payment_below_limit_fails`,
`limit_below_drawn_stops`, `held_slots_by_range`, `side_roundtrip`, `side_run_grows_by_page`, `slot_changes_ordered`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Slot reads inside `fin.ledger.apply_ns` (the cursor); a random read ≤ 20 VM-ns (`slot_read_ns`, added).
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +134.2 MB resident at the design point's 9.37 M slots (`[store] side_rows`):
  `Facility` 1.97 M × 12 B (S2.117: households' cards and overdrafts 1.52 M, firms' lines 0.45 M), `Accrual` 5.59 M × 16 B
  (the facilities' two for a reference-margin rate and the firms' commitment fee, 4.39 M; interest-bearing deposits
  1.2 M, S2.177), `Statement` 1.52 M × 12 B (cards), `Held` and `Link` 0.3 M × 8 B (a failed bank's held payments on
  E1's day), + 0.6 MB directory; saved: +134 MB. Slots sized by kind rather than 16 B each free 16.4 MB (150.6 at a
  uniform 16 B).

**Guards**: slot payloads are written only through `side.rs` (compile-level visibility).

**Not allowed**: a column on every account for a sparse attribute; a stored `drawn` or `undrawn`; a limit clamped to
drawn.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F ledger` within `[fin.ledger]` including `slot_read_ns`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.242 — Exact interest on accounts by Abel summation

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts".
**Depends on**: S1.241 (the `Accrual` slot); S1.178 (day facts and day counts); S1.225 (a crediting or charging date
per (bank, product) on the wheel).
**Goal**: interest on an account's daily balance is exact at any rate path. Each balance change adds one i128 product
to its accrual, a credit is one expression rounded once, and no account is visited for interest except on its
product's crediting or charging date, inside 7a's sweep.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/interest.rs` | cumulative indices J, `set_rate`, `accrue_change`, `credit_due` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/interest_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/ledger.rs` | 1.2 M interest-bearing accounts; a crediting date |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.ledger]` | `credit_ns` 5 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Indices**: J (i128, 10⁻¹² units) per (bank, product) or per (currency, day count) advances at the day's open by the
  rate in force × `DayFraction` (TIME.4). Rates are written only by `set_rate(bank, product, Rate, effective_day)`,
  the bank's decision (effective the next day, Law 14).
- **Accrual** (MON.16, REP.9): a change ΔB on day t does `s −= ΔB·J_open(t)` inside settlement's apply. The credit on
  day c is `div_round(B·J(c) + s, 10¹²)` by the product's convention; the remainder r stays: `s ← r − B′·J(c)`. No
  last-change day is stored; a mid-period rate change is exact without visiting accounts.
- Two slots serve sign-dependent rates (credit and debit interest) or a margin over a reference (the reference index
  and the day-fraction index); a commitment fee is one slot on `limit`.
- **Interest-bearing is data**: a product declared at rate 0 is not interest-bearing and its accounts carry no
  `Accrual` slot; S2.177 states the count from its data, inside S1.241's 9.37 M slots (`[store] side_rows`).
- **Crediting and charging**: on a (bank, product) date the day facts list it; 7a's sweep credits (payer the bank,
  payee the holder, reason `LED.interest`) or charges (payer the holder) each flagged account of that product. A charge
  beyond `limit` fails (MON.12) and its arrears are the account's.
- **Measurement**: crediting reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a quarter-end crediting date credits ≈ 1.2 M accounts inside the sweep — `crediting_heavy`.
- E8: |B|·J ≤ 10³³, far below i128's range — `accrual_bounds`.
- E11: day zero: J = 0, s = 0 — `day_zero_accrual`.
- E12: a product with no rate in force is refused at assembly — `rate_missing_refused`.
- E14: two changes the same day commute — `abel_changes_commute`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `abel_equals_daily_sum` (the credit equals Σ daily balance × rate, rounded once),
`credit_remainder_kept`, `abel_changes_commute`, `crediting_heavy`, `accrual_bounds`, `day_zero_accrual`,
`rate_missing_refused`, `charge_beyond_limit_fails`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 2 phone-ns to `fin.ledger.apply_ns` on ≈ 0.3 M / 0 / 0.5 M applies of interest-bearing accounts.
- on fin.calendar.crediting (each product's crediting and charging dates, mostly month- and quarter-ends): ≈ 1.2 M ×
  5 VM-ns ≈ 6 core-ms; joins H.
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +0 B (its `Accrual` slots are counted in S1.241's 1.5 M).

**Guards**: `s` is written only by `accrue_change` and `credit_due` (compile-level visibility).

**Not allowed**: a last-change day; a daily interest pass; a rate read by name; a default rate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F ledger -D B,H` within `[fin.ledger]` including `credit_ns`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.243 — Money totals maintained in the settlement sweep

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: MON.10 MEASURE
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts"; follows §7.17 (the audit's independence).
**Depends on**: S1.240 (accounts, holder class and product bits); S1.241 (facility limits for the undrawn totals);
S1.207 (the persons' `notes` words the recount reads); S1.180 (reasons and money-holder classes); S1.128
(`#[maintained]`).
**Goal**: the money stock of each currency is maintained as whole-unit integers folded in the settlement apply — by
issuer and holder class, a bank's deposits owed, reserves, notes out, facilities granted and drawn, and change by
source — while the audit keeps its own recount; no other pass over accounts exists.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/totals.rs` | `MoneyTotals`: range-local cells merged in range order; `fold` called by the apply |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/recount.rs` | per-range slice recount for the audit |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/totals_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/ledger.rs` | the recount measure |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.ledger]` | `recount_ns_per_row` 0.4 |

**Design**:
- **Fold**: the apply's range job calls `fold(range, Δ)` for each committed change into range cells (K-13), merged in
  range order: per (issuer, currency, holder class); per bank (deposits owed, Σ limit, Σ drawn, reserves); per
  (currency, reason) created or destroyed. Cells are `#[maintained(writer = "phx_ledger::totals::fold")]` i128. The
  caller is today's `phx-core` apply until S1.248 (S1.244's placeholder), then S1.248's sweep.
- **Source** (MON.6, MON.8): an item whose payer issues the payee's money creates it; one whose payee issues the
  payer's money destroys it; one between two banks' depositors moves reserves only (MON.5) — read from the two `bank`
  words in the same apply.
- **Reads**: `stock(currency)` (reserves, notes, deposits by holder class), `deposits_owed(bank)` (MON.7),
  `notes_out` (MON.9), `undrawn(bank)` (REG.10's facility commitments, a read), `change_by_source`. MON.10's release
  with its lag reads them through K-39 and K-37 (S1.256).
- **Independent recount** (N1, R4): `recount(range)` sums the columns (and the persons' `notes` by person range) into
  slice totals; the audit compares them with its own prior totals plus the day's Δ, never with `MoneyTotals`
  (PC-101). A non-business day recounts `pending` only.
- **Save**: saved; rebuilt from the columns after load and asserted equal.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats`; the recount reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a `bank` rewrite moves each balance between the banks' cells in the same pass — `rewrite_moves_totals`.
- E5, E7: an order-free integer fold for any workers — `fold_order_free`.
- E6: rebuild equals the saved totals — `totals_rebuild_equal`.
- E8: i128 cells — `totals_i128_capacity`.
- E13: an empty class sums over no rows, a count of nothing — `empty_class_total`.

**Extension points**: S1.244, S1.248, S1.256, S1.330, S1.429, S1.430, S1.476, S2.117, S2.179, S2.180, S3.114.

**Unit tests**: `fold_order_free`, `created_destroyed_by_issuer`, `rewrite_moves_totals`, `totals_rebuild_equal`,
`recount_independent`, `undrawn_is_read`, `totals_i128_capacity`, `empty_class_total`.

**Live checks**: none; the money release is the statistics agency's (S1.256).

**Budget**:
- The fold is inside `fin.ledger.apply_ns` (0 items of its own).

### S1.244 — Accounts and money passes moved onto the ledger

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts"–§7.8 "K-47 Money accounts".
**Depends on**: S1.243 (totals, fold and recount); S1.241 (facility and held slots); S1.196, S1.200 (kind records
name their account); S1.144 (the kind-name compares in `core_central.rs` are its sites).
**Goal**: today's accounts, one per party of a money-holding kind, move into K-47 (persons' own come at S1.405);
today's settlement apply moves, as it stands, from `phx-core` into `phx-ledger` — the lowest crate that may name
K-47 — where it writes K-47's columns and calls `MoneyTotals::fold`; the world-sized money passes are deleted.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/store.rs` | `Accounts`, `KindStore::book`/`money`, `books`, `deposits_of` deleted |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/settle.rs`, `settle_tests.rs` | moved to `phx-ledger` (`store.rs`'s last use of `Book`/`Books`/`Lines` goes with `KindStore::book`) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/settle.rs`, `settle_tests.rs` | today's apply as moved: `Book`/`Books` read and write K-47 columns and call `MoneyTotals::fold` (placeholder naming S1.248) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_day.rs` | `phx_core::settle` → `phx_ledger::settle` (also in `core_open.rs`, `core_central.rs`, `core_credit.rs`); `money_totals`, `money_breaks`' passes and its helper `finding`, `run_day`'s passes → `MoneyTotals` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_central.rs` | `fund_stage`, `bank_deposits`, `issuer_held` → `deposits_owed`, `stock` (the kind-name compares at 559, 593: removed at S1.144) |

  moves up into `phx-ledger` unchanged but for its account reads and writes, and S1.248 rewrites it in place.

- E10: an ended party's account closes after its estate's flows settle (SET.7) — `estate_account_closes_after`.
- E13: a kind with no accounts reads no rows — `no_account_kind_empty`.
