### S1.245 — Flow batches: 16-byte items, 24-bit denominations, link groups, the chains' entry points

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-48 Flow batches"; follows §6.1 (stages 2b, 6b, 6d, 7), §3.1 (sweep hooks).
**Depends on**: S1.160 (day buffers); S1.161 (the day plan: the batches' and chains' buffers declare their lives
there); S1.175 (24-bit unit ids; retires its 15-bit placeholder); S1.170 (apply by range and its `SweepHooks`
parameter); S1.180 (reasons with payment order, source kind and lines); S1.240 (`add_pending`).
**Goal**: every movement is a fused chain's item added straight into both `pending`s (a sale, a dated due), a decided
flow stored as a 16-byte item under a batch header, or a transformation naming its party and its source; every
instruction has a number, legs, a cause, trade and settlement dates and a link group.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/flows.rs` | `Denom`, `BatchHeader`, `Item`, `Batches` over `DayBufs`, `LinkGroups`, `Place`, commit mode |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/chains.rs` | `DueItems` (payer and payee scattered through S1.170's ranges), `ShardCredits`, `SpendSplit` (E 48), each generic over `H: SweepHooks` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/flows_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/settle.rs` | decided flows' driver |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-48 Flow batches" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.settle]` | `flow_ns` 19.2 |

**Design**:
- **Types**:

  | type | layout |
  | --- | --- |
  | `Denom` u32 | bit 31 money/units; low 24 bits the unit id (K-22) or the currency |
  | `BatchHeader` 32 B | `reason` u16, `denom` u32, `order` u8, `source_kind` u8, `link` u32, `trade_day` u32, `settle_day` u32, `first` u32, `count` u32, `sources` u32 (per-item source column or `NONE`) |
  | `Item` 16 B | payer PartyKey u32, payee PartyKey u32, amount i64 |
  | `Place` | (chain: sales, dues or decided; shard or buffer; index) |

- `order` is read from K-21's payment order of the payer's kind for the reason — PREFERENCE, or POLICY where a law sets
  it (REP.18, MON.5, TRS.10) — never stored per party.
- **Numbering** (SET.1): (day, handler, chunk, batch), from chunk plans (K-11), never from arrival.
- **Transformations** (SET.9, Law 5): the other side is `NATURE`, with the way, deposit, event or purchase in the source
  column.
- **Link groups** (SET.4): a group spans batches and denominations; `LinkGroups` counts failed legs and S1.248 fails a
  group whole.
- **Fused entry points**: `DueItems::push` scatters each due's payer and payee through S1.170's `apply_by_range` (its
  account ranges and flush units; at H its waves, each byte-identical to one pass); the range sweep adds into both
  `pending`s and calls its hooks (levies, lines, tallies), composed by `phx-world`'s route, so
  `phx-ledger` names no higher crate (S1.101 §3.1). `ShardCredits` serves K-74's seller-shard sweep; `SpendSplit`
  apportions (K-16) a household's day spend to its persons at 6b. Nothing is stored past its day buffer.
- **Commit mode** (TIME.8, SET.2): on a non-business day card payments and electricity trades stay in `pending`; notes
  move at once; a decided flow is a violation.
- **Refused at the site** (II.5, SET.11): an absent payer or payee; a same-party item; money and units mixed; a unit
  id ≥ 2²⁴.
- **Retires** S1.174's 15-bit `Denom(u16)` placeholder (`phx-core/src/flows.rs`, deleted by S1.247).
- Carried (done at S0.15: SET.1, SET.9; at S0.17: MON.5): their `#[clause]` carriers move to these types.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` for the batch buffers; rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E3, E13: a payee with no account in the currency fails at S1.248 (MON.5) — `no_account_fails_visibly` (S1.248).
- E5: buffers sized by H (0.6 M decided, 22.5 M streamed) and kept — `buffers_reuse_no_alloc`.
- E7: numbering identical for 1–8 workers — `numbering_worker_free`.
- E8: `Denom` holds 2²⁴ ids — `denom_24_bits`.
- E14: one payer's flows ordered by order, then lot (S1.248) — `order_then_lot` (S1.248).

**Extension points**: S1.246, S1.247, S1.248, S1.251, S1.253, S1.254, S1.281, S1.309, S1.406, S2.152, S2.199, S2.209,
S2.210, S3.106, S3.124, S4.101, S4.107, S4.108, S4.151, S4.163, S4.176, S5.161, S5.180, S6.128.

**Unit tests**: `denom_24_bits`, `money_and_units_refused`, `one_sided_refused`, `numbering_worker_free`,
`link_group_counts`, `due_items_scatter_by_range`, `commit_mode_refuses_decided`, `buffers_reuse_no_alloc`,
`hooks_called_per_item`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- `fin.settle.flow_ns` 19.2 VM (25 phone-ns) at 0.45 M / 0 / 0.6 M decided flows; dues scattered inside
  `fin.dues.item_ns`.
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +10 MB at H (0.6 M × 16 B), inside the 6a live set's figure only if decided flows are
  live then (they are written at 6d: +0 MB at 6a's peak).

**Guards**: `const` size checks on `Item` and `BatchHeader`; account mutators visible only to `chains.rs` and
`settle.rs` (R6).

**Not allowed**: a 24-byte flow or a per-sale flow object; a chain's items kept past the day; a payment order stored
per party; a 15-bit unit id; a `phx-ledger` call into a higher crate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F settle` within `flow_ns`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-48 Flow batches" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.246 — Card authorization and reason gates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-48 Flow batches".
**Depends on**: S1.245 (batches and the chains' entry points); S1.240 (`available`); S1.180 (reasons with their gates
as declared data).
**Goal**: a card payment is TIME.8's commitment made through authorization (Law 1): it is admitted only against the
payer's available funds, so an authorized payment never fails later for its payer's funds; a reason may declare a
refusal rule evaluated once at emission.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/authorize.rs` | `authorize(account, amount) -> Admit`, the authorized rank, `Gate` evaluation |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/authorize_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/settle.rs` | authorization and gates on the decided and retail items |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-48 Flow batches" | the section |

**Design**:
- **Retail and services**: the authorization is the household's want budgets, bounded by its persons' `available` in
  the spending view at 5d (S1.448) — no write to K-47. Retail items apply as they flush at 6b; an authorized debit
  ranks ahead of every other item of its payer (a declared payment order), so 7b never re-derives or fails it, and no
  retail item is kept for re-derivation.
- **Any other card debit** (a decided purchase, a closed day's service) calls `authorize` at emission: admitted if
  `amount ≤ available`, else refused there and the purchase fails visibly before delivery (MON.5).
- **Reason gates**: a reason may declare a refusal predicate — a pure function over (payer, payee, their countries,
  currency, amount) and declared POLICY data, bound at assembly — evaluated at emission and at a commitment's draw
  (S1.251). A refused instruction is a fail (SET.3) with the rule as its cause, never scaled. A reason without a gate
  costs one handle test.
- **Measurement**: refusals counted per reason (`ExecCounters`).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a card debit beyond the available funds is refused at emission — `card_beyond_available_refused`.
- E5: four closed days' card payments live only as authorized `pending` nets — `closed_days_authorized`.
- E14: an authorized retail debit and a later decided flow of one payer: the decided flow fails first —
  `authorized_ranks_first`.
- E12: a gate reading an absent POLICY value is refused at assembly — `gate_missing_policy_refused`.

**Extension points**: S1.247, S1.248, S1.251, S1.252.

**Unit tests**: `card_beyond_available_refused`, `closed_days_authorized`, `authorized_ranks_first`,
`gate_refuses_never_scales`, `gate_missing_policy_refused`, `ungated_reason_one_test`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 1 phone-ns to `fin.settle.flow_ns` at 0.45 M / 0 / 0.6 M items (the gate's handle test); 0 on the retail
  chain (the want budget is the authorization).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B.

**Guards**: `authorize` is the only admission of a card debit (compile-level visibility).

**Not allowed**: a reservation written into `pending` and released later; a refused instruction scaled down; a gate
branching on a kind's name.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F settle` within `flow_ns`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-48 Flow batches" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.248 — Settlement in `phx-ledger`: the `pending` sweep, short payers re-derived, outcome by place

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: SET.10 MEASURE
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-49 Settlement"; follows §6.1 (stage 7).
**Depends on**: S1.245 (batches, places, chains); S1.161 (the day plan: the outcome bitmap's and 7b scratch's lives);
S1.246 (authorized debits rank first); S1.244 (K-47, the only balances); S1.243 (`MoneyTotals::fold`); S1.170 (apply by
range); S1.171 (the sweep as a declared sweep); S1.169 (chunk plans); S1.219 (the day ledger publishing SET.10).
**Goal**: stage 7 settles each currency in one sweep of `pending` by account range; only the payers left short have
their items re-derived in payment order from the chains' sources, the unpayable suffix failing, ties by lot; the
greatest fixed point with the closing ring, bank shortfalls and link groups decides what settles, and an outcome
bitmap by place replaces every value-keyed failure map.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/settle.rs` | beside today's apply (moved here at S1.244; S1.249 deletes it): `settle_day(currencies)`, `sweep` (7a), `rederive`, fixed point, ring, bank shortfall (7b), `commit`, `Outcome`, `Values` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/settle_tests.rs` | new tests; today's (moved here at S1.244) go with today's apply at S1.249 |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/settle.rs` | shorts, sweep, fixed point on B, B′, H |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-49 Settlement" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.settle]` | `short_ns` 38.5, `sweep_ns_per_account` 0.4, `fixed_point_core_ms_h` 25 |

**Design**:
- **Per currency** (`settle_day`): each currency on its country's business day is swept and settled; on its closed day
  it is committed only. This is the per-currency loop of today's `pay_currencies` (moved by S1.249).
- **7a sweep** (one job per 4 096-account range): decided flows and commitments due (K-50) are added into `pending`
  first; accounts at a closed bank become `Held`; an account with `balance + pending ≥ −limit` commits, calling
  `MoneyTotals::fold` (retiring S1.244's placeholder) and the accrual (S1.242) in the same pass; otherwise it is
  marked in the day's short bitmap (K-07).
- **7b short payers**: authorized debits (S1.246) are never re-derived. One filtered pass on the pool over today's
  between-firm sale shards, wheel buckets and decided batches collects the short payers' items (≤ 7 M tests at
  0.3 ns); each payer's items are sorted by (order, lot), lots from stream `SET.lot` keyed (payer, day, place) (CHN.3,
  MON.5); the suffix beyond `balance + credits + limit` fails; each failure lowers its payee's credits and newly short
  payees join the worklist — the greatest fixed point, by rounds. Starting from "all settle", payers settled only by
  the same settlement's receipts (the ring) settle and are counted (SET.6).
- **Bank shortfall** (MON.5): a bank whose reserves and intraday credit cannot cover its customers' net has their legs
  removed (cause `Bank`) and the rest resettles. **Link groups**: any failed leg fails its group (SET.4).
- **Commit and reverse**: survivors move `pending → balance`; a failed item leaves both `pending`s; the hooks' postings
  (lines, tallies, levy accruals) are reversed through the same hooks from the outcome; a failed sale's delivery is
  reversed before the close (K-74's hook).
- **`Outcome`**: a bitmap by `Place` with the cause (`Payer`, `Bank`, `Link`, `NoAccount`, `Held`); failed dues reach
  K-56 at tomorrow's 2d.
- **`Values`** (SET.10): gross, net, ring count and value, fails by cause, per currency — written each business day to
  the day ledger's kind `settlement` (K-38).
- **SET.7**: an ending party's items settle against its estate's account (K-31's successor).
- **Retires** `[fin.kept] flow_ns` and `flow_h_ns` (S1.119; replaced by `[fin.settle]`, `[fin.ledger]`).
- Carried (done at S0.15): SET.4 — its carrier moves.
- **Measurement**: sweep and passes report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a failing bank's customers removed, then resettled; a cascade fails only necessary suffixes —
  `bank_short_removes_customers`, `cascade_rounds_minimal`.
- E5: B′ with 7.5 M applies and 60 k shorts; the closed days' authorized `pending` commits first —
  `bprime_pending_first`.
- E7: shorts, lots and rounds worker-free — `settle_worker_free`.
- E10: an ending payer settles against its estate — `ending_payer_estate`.
- E13: a payee without an account fails `NoAccount` — `no_account_fails_visibly`.
- E14: order, then lot — `order_then_lot`.

**Extension points**: S1.249, S1.250, S1.254, S1.265, S1.310, S1.328, S1.347, S1.406, S1.417, S1.427, S2.104, S2.107,
S2.110, S2.113, S2.117, S2.177, S2.185, S2.195, S2.199, S2.210, S3.101, S3.104, S3.106, S3.123, S3.147, S4.101, S4.107,
S4.114, S4.133, S4.151, S4.163, S4.176.

**Unit tests**: `ring_settles`, `cascade_rounds_minimal`, `order_then_lot`, `bank_short_removes_customers`,
`link_group_all_or_none`, `no_account_fails_visibly`, `held_through_closed_bank`, `failed_sale_reversed_before_close`,
`bprime_pending_first`, `ending_payer_estate`, `settle_worker_free`, `values_gross_net_ring`.

**Live checks**: none new; the audit's Flows family reads the outcome (S1.353).

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.fixed_point: 15 / 0 / 25 core-ms (B / NB / H).
- `fin.settle.sweep_ns_per_account` 0.4 VM over 7.4 M accounts (≈ 3 core-ms, B and H); `fin.settle.short_ns` 38.5 VM
  (50 phone-ns) at 20 k / 0 / 150 k items (B′ 60 k).
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +4 MB at H (short payers' items, written at 7b: +0 MB at 6a's peak).

**Guards**: PC-97 (the API takes `&Pool`); PC-25 re-aimed (only `settle.rs` writes `balance`).

**Not allowed**: a net buffer beside `pending`; failures matched by value; a map over every flow; a round count as the
loop's bound; settling on a non-business day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F settle,ledger -D B,BC,H` within `[fin.settle]`, `[fin.ledger]`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-49 Settlement" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_accounts.rs` | `account_flows`' map → the hooks' reversal by place |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_taxes.rs` | `accrue_taxes`' map and its clone → outcome by place (the rest moves at S1.270) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `deliver_sales`' map → the failed sale read by its place in `Outcome`; today's release of the delivery stays until S1.311 moves it onto K-74's reversal hook |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | `depart_shipments`' map → the freight item's place |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_credit.rs` | `lend_shortfalls`' map over every flow → each firm's `balance + pending` |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-97.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | this step's sites removed |

**Design**:
- Consumers read `Outcome::failed(place) -> Option<Cause>` for the places they emitted; a delivery, a freight release,
  a tax accrual or an income posting is reversed for that place only.
- A shortfall lender's rule reads each borrowing firm's projected net as `balance + pending` (K-47), one read a firm
  on its agenda; K-13's keyed reduce holds the per-bank sums.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (six ordered maps), `PC-97.toml` (`pool = None`) and `PC-99.toml`
  (the maps' allocations).

**Edge cases**:
- E14: two equal sales, one failed: the failed one's delivery is reversed and the other delivered, by place —
  `equal_sales_released_by_place`.
- E1: a mass-fail day reverses by place in the owners' range jobs — `mass_fail_reverses_by_range`.
- E7: settlement on the pool gives the same outcome for any workers — `routed_settle_worker_free`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `equal_sales_released_by_place`, `shortfall_reads_pending`, `mass_fail_reverses_by_range`,
`routed_settle_worker_free`.

**Live checks**: the goods identity (GDS.10) and the audit's Flows family hold as before.

**Budget**: removes ≈ 6 passes over every flow and ≈ 4.5 M map inserts a day; adds 0.

**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-97.toml`, `PC-99.toml` fall.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; matching a failure by amount.

**Done when**:
- [ ] maps deleted, consumers moved; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows `settle.fixed_point`, `goods.deliver`, `taxes.accrue` and
  `lend_shortfalls` reduced (a measure of code, never the world's)
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.250 — Linked legs across currencies and correspondent settlement

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: FX.4 PROCESS *(part: both currencies settle together)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-49 Settlement"; follows §7.8 "K-49 Settlement".
**Depends on**: S1.248 (`settle_day`, the fixed point and link groups); S1.240 (nostro accounts); S1.178 (per-country
business-day facts); S1.180 (currency systems and their members as declared data).
**Goal**: a group of legs in two currencies settles in both currencies' sweeps together or not at all, on a value
date that is a business day in both; a bank that is not a member of a currency's system settles its customers' legs
through its nostro at its declared correspondent. The first world user is S5.161; until then it is measured by `-F`.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/pvp.rs` | `JointDate`, cross-currency rounds inside `settle_day`, correspondent routing |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/pvp_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/settle.rs` | PvP driver |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-49 Settlement" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.settle]` | `pvp_ns` 30 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Value date**: `JointDate::next(day, [country_a, country_b])` is the first day on or after `day` that is a business
  day in both (K-19, TIME.3); a group whose legs name different settle days is refused (SET.4).
- **Rounds across currencies**: `settle_day` runs the currencies' 7b worklists together; a group with a failed leg in
  one currency is removed from the other's in the next round, until neither changes (monotone). No leg converts at the
  ledger (MON.13, NUM.5).
- **Correspondents** (FX.1, MON.13): membership per (bank, currency system) is declared data (the operator's POLICY);
  a non-member bank's net moves its nostro account at its correspondent, whose own net at the central bank includes
  it; a non-member without a nostro fails the leg (`NoNostro`); a correspondent that cannot cover removes its
  respondents' legs as a bank shortfall.
- **Conversion commitments** (K-50) drawn on their settle day enter as linked groups.
- **Measurement**: rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a day that is a business day in one country only is not a joint date — `joint_date_both_open`.
- E1: a correspondent's failure removes its respondents' legs — `correspondent_short_removes`.
- E3: no nostro gives `NoNostro`, visibly — `no_nostro_fails`.
- E7: cross-currency rounds are worker-free — `pvp_worker_free`.
- E14: two groups of one payer are ordered, then drawn by lot, per currency — `pvp_order_then_lot`.

**Extension points**: S5.159, S5.161.

**Unit tests**: `pvp_both_or_none`, `joint_date_both_open`, `no_nostro_fails`, `correspondent_short_removes`,
`no_conversion_at_ledger`, `pvp_worker_free`, `pvp_order_then_lot`.

**Live checks**: none until S5.161.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.fixed_point: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms until S5.161; then 4.5 / 0 / 4.5 core-ms (150 k groups ×
  30 VM-ns), stated by S5.161.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (nostros are accounts, S1.240).

**Guards**: `Item` carries one `Denom` (compile level).

**Not allowed**: a conversion at the ledger; a leg settled on a day closed in its currency; a default correspondent.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F settle` within `pvp_ns`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-49 Settlement" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.251 — Dated commitments on both books

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: REG.10 STATE
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-50 Dated commitments".
**Depends on**: S1.225 (the due wheel files a commitment by settle day); S1.245 (batches, which commitments enter on
their day); S1.246 (a draw passes its reason's gate); S1.171 (the 9a declared sweep); S1.241 (facility reads); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every commitment between trade date and settle date is one row, due on the wheel and read on both parties'
books — an unsettled trade (SET.2), a conversion or a forward, uncalled capital, a draw committed; undrawn credit
lines are K-47's facility reads (S1.243) and pending orders K-70's standing offers. REG.10 completes: every kind of
commitment it names is recorded on both books as what it is.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/commit.rs` | `Commitments` columns, `post`, `take_due`, `cancel`, the 9a fold |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/commit_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/commitments.rs` | `-F commitments` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-50 Dated commitments" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.commitments]` | `post_ns` 30, `take_ns` 10, `mb` 5.4 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Row**, 27 B (SoA): `payer`, `payee` PartyKey u32; `amount` i64 (money or units); `denom` u32 (Denom's 25 bits,
  the declared commitment kind 6 bits, "settles with the next row" 1 bit); `settle_day` u16 (days from the world's
  epoch); `source` u32 (the contract or instrument event a draw books into, or `NONE`); generation u8. A DvP or PvP
  pair is posted as adjacent rows with the link bit.
- **On the wheel**: `post` files the row under its commitment code (the 8-bit wheel code, S1.257) on `settle_day`;
  `take_due` at 1a hands today's rows to 7a as a batch with their link groups (SET.4), each draw passing its reason's
  gate. Unit commitments bind free units at `post` (K-63).
- **Both books** (REG.10): at 9a one declared sweep of the ≤ 0.2 M rows folds each party's commitments, both sides,
  into a K-03 day table for books, valuations and the audit; a rule earlier in the day reads the previous close
  (TIME.10). Card payments and electricity trades waiting across closed days stay in K-47's `pending`.
- **Cancel**: only the source's own event (a failed counterparty's close-out, SET.3) cancels a row.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats`; the take and the 9a sweep report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a quarter-end settle day takes up to 0.2 M rows in one bucket — `bucket_take_heavy`.
- E6: rows saved; wheel entries rebuilt from `settle_day` — `commit_roundtrip`.
- E8: `settle_day` u16 covers 179 years from the epoch; beyond stops — `settle_day_capacity`.
- E10: a party ending before settle: the row's side moves to its estate (K-97) — `commit_side_to_estate`.
- E11: day zero: the opening's unsettled trades posted with their dates — `opening_commitments_posted`.
- E14: two commitments of one pair the same day settle as their own groups — `same_day_commitments_apart`.

**Extension points**: S1.252, S1.277, S1.281, S2.131, S2.143, S2.152, S2.209, S3.121, S3.133, S3.135, S3.147, S3.166,
S3.185, S3.195, S8.110, S4.163, S4.172, S4.176, S5.162, S5.180.

**Unit tests**: `post_take_both_books`, `dvp_linked_on_take`, `units_bound_at_post`, `cancel_only_by_source`,
`commit_roundtrip`, `bucket_take_heavy`, `settle_day_capacity`, `commit_side_to_estate`, `opening_commitments_posted`,
`same_day_commitments_apart`.

**Live checks**: none. The audit's Ownership family reads commitments (S1.353).

**Budget**:
- adds 50 k / 0 / 0.2 M items to `fin.commitments.take_ns` (10 VM) and ≈ 0.1 M posts a day to
  `fin.commitments.post_ns` (30 VM) from S3.147 on.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the 9a fold).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +5.4 MB resident (0.2 M × 27 B).

**Guards**: a row without both parties is refused at `post` (SET.11).

**Not allowed**: a commitment kept as a flow; a `Vec<Flow>` of pending trades; undrawn limits copied into rows.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F commitments` within its ratchets
- [ ] §7.8 "K-50 Dated commitments" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.253 — The levy engine: declared levy sets fused at emission, accrued by collector

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: withheld at payroll, charged at the sale, owed by the collector until remitted)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-51 The levy engine"; follows §6.1 (stages 2b, 6b), §3.1 (sweep hooks).
**Depends on**: S1.245 (the chains' entry points and their hooks, where levies fuse); S1.180 (reasons with their levy
sets and collector roles); S1.179 (dated policy schedules: rates and bands in force); S1.196 (the collector's record
cells); S1.165 (owner instances for holding levies).
**Goal**: a levy is declared data on a reason — its base, schedule, rounding convention, collector role, payee and
follow-on — computed once per item where the item is emitted (the 2b dated-item stream, the 6b seller-shard sweep),
rounded once, and accrued in the collector's record as its liability to the payee until remitted (S1.270); a levy adds
no pass and no stored row per wage or sale.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/levy.rs` | `LevySet`, `Levy`, `apply_levies` (a sweep hook), accrual cells; today's `Withholding` becomes one `Levy` form |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/levy_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/dues.rs` | the dated-item stream with withholding sets |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-51 The levy engine" | the section (replaces §4.3's text) |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.dues]` | `levy_ns_extra` 0 (added) |

**Design**:
- **`Levy`** (declared per reason in K-21, compiled to handles): `base` (the leg's amount, or a year-to-date figure the
  remitter itself holds — a contract-keyed K-52 tally its declaring step adds with its bytes; never a person's own
  total, Law 12); `schedule` (bands or a rate through a `PolicySchedule` handle in force today, or a term of the
  contract); `rounding` (the law's convention, `div_round` once per item, MON.16, REP.9); `collector` (the leg's payer
  when withheld, its payee when charged); `payee` (a named party by declaration); `stream` (the collector's cell);
  `follow_on` (a declared reason or none).
- **Fused**: `apply_levies(item, set, view)` returns the amounts; the dated item's payee receives gross − withheld, a
  sale's buyer pays price + charged; each amount is added to the collector's cell in the range shard that already holds
  the collector (payer for withholding, seller for sales).
- **Collector cells**: a collector's record holds one i64 cell per collector it pays through, as the law declares (a
  firm's cold "tax accrued" 16 B: withheld income tax and taxes on products). Bases the law assesses together share a
  cell and the K-52 tally by base splits them (TAX.5); a stream to a collector with no cell accrues in the
  collector's open `tax_payables` row for (law, period), a further base in its run (S1.270). Cells are the liability
  until S1.270 closes them.
- **Holding levies** (property tax, S5.113): on the levy's dates the owners listed by the (zone, class) K-06 instance
  are raised as dated items (holder → payee) in 2b.
- **Follow-ons** (PEN.2, PEN.3): a levy with a follow-on writes (collector, payee, amount, source) into a K-03 buffer,
  read by the payee system's rule at 7c after the outcome (only settled levies follow on).
- **Refused at the site** (II.5): a withheld amount above the gross (TAX.2; today's silent skip at
  `core_day.rs`); a negative levy where the schedule states none; a levy with no payee.
- **Failure**: an item that fails reverses its accruals through the same hook, by place.
- **Measurement**: the owners' instance on holding-levy dates reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a quarter-end payday's 4.5 M wages × 2–4 levies, all fused — `payday_levies_fused`.
- E7: cells are integer sums in shard order — `levy_cells_order_free`.
- E10: a collector ending mid-period closes its cells into a payable against its estate — `collector_end_closes_cells`
  (S1.270).
- E12: a rate not in force is refused at assembly — `levy_missing_rate_refused`.
- E13: a country with no such tax has an empty set — `empty_levy_set`.
- E14: withholding above the gross stops the run — `withheld_above_gross_stops`.

**Extension points**: S1.270, S1.309, S1.435, S2.168, S2.213, S3.106, S4.146, S4.148, S5.101, S5.103, S5.105, S5.113,
S5.180.

**Unit tests**: `bands_rounded_once`, `withheld_above_gross_stops`, `sale_tax_charged_on_top`, `ytd_base_reads_tally`,
`empty_levy_set`, `payday_levies_fused`, `follow_on_only_settled`, `levy_missing_rate_refused`,
`failure_reverses_accrual`, `levy_cells_order_free`.

**Live checks**: none. The TAX.5 identity is the audit's (S1.270, S1.353).

**Budget**:
- adds 0 phone-ns to `fin.dues.item_ns` and `fin.retail.all_in_ns` (fused; `levy_ns_extra` 0) at 3.0 M / 0 / 22.5 M
  dated items and 10.05 M / 7.05 M / 10.05 M sales.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot "tax accrued", 16 B).

**Guards**: `apply_levies` takes one item, never a total (TAX.7, compile level).

**Not allowed**: an `Arising` row per wage or sale; a per-day levy pass; a tax computed on a total; a default rate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F dues -D B,H` within `item_ns` with levies fused
- [ ] §7.8 "K-51 The levy engine" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.254 — Settlement tallies by reason, fused in the sweeps

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.8 "K-52 Settlement tallies"; follows §7.6 (K-39's stock counters).
**Depends on**: S1.245 (the chains and batches where tallies fuse); S1.248 (the outcome by place a tally reverses on);
S1.180 (reasons, with the tallies each feeds); S1.207 (the person's tax-year pair); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every flow sum a rule or a statistic reads — a person's taxable income and withheld this tax year, an
agency's day payments by class, receipts by base, a (country, category) flow — is one declared tally added in the pass
that already touches the item, stamped by period and reversed by place when the item fails. It is the one flow-tally
kernel: K-39 (S1.221) keeps stock counters, exposure and samples and reads flow sums from here at its period close.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/tally.rs` | `TallyDecl`, `Tallies` cells, `add` (a sweep hook), `reverse`, `read(key, period)`, `day_cell` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/tally_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/flows.rs` | `-F flows`: tallies fused into the chains' shards |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.8 "K-52 Settlement tallies" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.flows]` | `tally_ns` 1.2 (added; K-39's `[fin.stats]` keeps stocks only) |

**Design**:
- **Why not K-39**: a flow tally must be reversed when its item fails at 7b (by the outcome's place) and must count
  only settled money; K-39's counters move on events that cannot fail (a hire, a death, a crossing) and sit below
  `phx-ledger` in the layer order. So flow tallies live here, and K-39's period close is handed these sums by the
  stage-10d route; `-F flows` and `fin.flows.tally_ns` measure this kernel alone.
- **Keys** (declared per tally with K-21 reason sets): person (the person record's pair: taxable income i64, withheld
  i64 this tax year); party (a declared cell in its record); (country, category) (dense per-currency arrays, shard
  copies merged in range order, K-13); (party, class) of the day (a day cell in K-03, cleared at 10e).
- **Period stamps**: a write finding an older stamp resets first; there is no daily reset pass; a read of another
  period is `Missing` (NUM.8).
- **Closed periods** (declared per tally, off by default): a tally declaring `keep_closed` moves its value into a
  closed cell at that reset (a cell not written since still holds t under its stamp), readable as period t − 1
  until the next close; +8 B a cell, stated by the declaring step. Without it a reader after the close takes its values at
  the close (a sample copies its members' cells into its K-39 frame).
- **Fused**: added in the 2b dues sweep, the 6b seller-shard sweep, 7a for decided flows, and the holdings apply for
  realised gains (S1.269 on K-62); reversed from S1.248's outcome by place.
- **Save**: person and party cells in their records; country arrays saved; day cells not saved.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` for the arrays; merges report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a heavy day adds 12 M tallies in the same sweeps — `tally_heavy_fused`.
- E6: stamps make a load mid-period continue exactly — `tally_roundtrip`.
- E7: shard merge in range order — `tally_merge_order_free`.
- E9: a new tax year resets by stamp; no growth — `stamp_resets_lazily`.
- E11: day zero: every cell at the opening period with 0, a count of nothing — `day_zero_tallies`.
- E12: reading a period not kept is `Missing` — `other_period_missing`; a `keep_closed` tally reads t − 1 exactly
  after the reset — `closed_period_kept`.

**Extension points**: S1.255, S1.256, S1.270, S1.276, S1.309, S1.334, S1.498, S2.177, S3.119, S3.128, S4.107, S4.128,
S4.129, S4.133, S4.135, S4.143, S4.148, S4.166, S5.103, S5.108, S5.121, S5.126, S5.133, S5.164, S5.165, S5.185, S6.105,
S6.115.

**Unit tests**: `tally_heavy_fused`, `tally_reversed_on_fail`, `stamp_resets_lazily`, `other_period_missing`, `closed_period_kept`,
`tally_merge_order_free`, `tally_roundtrip`, `day_zero_tallies`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 12 M / 8 M / 12 M items to `fin.flows.tally_ns` (1.2 VM), fused inside `fin.dues.item_ns` and
  `fin.retail.all_in_ns`.
- its share of fin.fixed.stats: 2.5 / 1.8 / 2.5 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the shard copies' merge in range order at the
  period close).
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +3.2 MB resident (0.4 M cells × 8 B); ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B (core
  attribute, the tax-year pair).

**Guards**: PC-99 (no allocation in `add`); PC-101 (the arrays are `#[maintained]`).

**Not allowed**: a pass over the day's flows; a `BTreeMap` accumulator; a daily reset pass; a flow sum kept in K-39.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F flows` within `[fin.flows]`
- [ ] §7.8 "K-52 Settlement tallies" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/declare.rs` | the treasury's and agencies' payment order per reason (TRS.10; POLICY, REP.18) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-96.toml`, `PC-98.toml` | this step's sites removed |

**Design**:
- **Wages settled**: a (country, reason) tally `wages_settled` (settled only), and a party-class tally for agencies.
- **Agency funding** (SOC.8, TRS.10): the agency's `day_cell(agency, wages | other)` at 7a's start gives its needs
  against its account's `balance + pending`; the treasury's funding items are decided flows added before the sweep.
- **Payment order**: each flow's `order` comes from K-21's order per (payer kind, reason); an agency's funding carries
  two reasons, `FUNDED_WAGES` and `FUNDED_OTHER`, each with its declared order (the `funded_wages` set is gone).
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (the `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet`), `PC-96.toml` (three flow passes) and
  `PC-98.toml` (`agencies.contains`/`treasuries.contains` per flow).

**Edge cases**:
- E14: an agency's wages and purchases the same day rank by declared order — `agency_order_declared`.
- E5: a payday's agency funding is read from the day cells — `funding_from_day_cells`.
- E13: a country with no agencies has no agency cells — `no_agency_no_cells`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `agency_order_declared`, `funding_from_day_cells`, `no_agency_no_cells`.

**Live checks**: the treasury's payment-order live check of S1.423 holds as before.

**Budget**: removes three passes over every flow (≈ 13.5 M items each on B); adds 0.

**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-96.toml`, `PC-98.toml` fall.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a payment order computed by kind name.

**Done when**:
- [ ] passes deleted; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows the flow passes of `settle.gather` gone (a measure of code,
  never the world's)
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.256 — The agency's statistics passes moved onto accumulators

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.6 (K-39), §7.8 "K-47 Money accounts", §7.8 "K-52 Settlement tallies".
**Depends on**: S1.221 (stock counters and sample frames); S1.243 (money totals); S1.254 (flow tallies).
**Goal**: the statistics agency's monthly passes over every household, person and account — `exposed`,
`labour_force`, `employed_ids`, `money_stock` — the rates' daily sample pass and `Taxes::sample` are deleted; month
closes read counters, money totals and tallies; `record_sale`'s kind lookup by name is gone.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_stats.rs` | `record_sale`'s lookup, `exposed`, `labour_force`, `employed_ids`, `money_stock` and the money class by kind name (420–428, 456–466) deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_rates.rs` | `measure_rates`' sample pass → a K-39 sample frame drawn on a world stream |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_day.rs` | `Taxes::sample` → a frame's tally |

**Design**:
- **Exposure and labour force** (STA.1, IDX.3): K-39 counters moved at the events that change them — a birth, a death,
  an age-class crossing on its date (K-43), a hire or separation.
- **Money stock** (MON.10): `stock(currency)` from S1.243, by money-holder class, never by kind name (Law 10).
- **Samples**: the rates sample and the tax sample are K-39 frames drawn once on stream `STA.sample`, saved as lists;
  their flow tallies are K-52's.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-96.toml` (four monthly passes, one daily) and `PC-98.toml` (kind-name lookups).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a month-end close reads counters in O(countries × classes) — `month_close_reads_counters`.
- E6: counters rebuilt from the population at load equal the saved ones — `counters_rebuild_equal`.
- E10: a sampled household ending leaves the frame (its generation fails) — `frame_drops_ended`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `month_close_reads_counters`, `exposure_by_crossing_dates`, `counters_rebuild_equal`,
`frame_drops_ended`.

**Live checks**: the statistics agency's release checks hold as before.

**Budget**: removes a monthly pass over 7.5 M persons and 2.2 M households, and a daily sample pass; adds 0.

**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-96.toml`, `PC-98.toml` fall.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a class by kind name.

### S1.257 — The contract store: declared families, compact rows, codes and runs

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: ACC.12 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-53 The contract store"; follows §13 (memory).
**Depends on**: S1.181 (every family's fixed 8-bit code); S1.159 (generation references); S1.168 (the interner,
which holds terms ids); S1.180 (families declared with their columns and side modes); S1.225 (the wheel, whose entries carry the family code); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every contract between named parties is one row of its declared family in a new crate `phx-contract`; a
family keeps only the columns it declares, and one `own_amount` is read by both sides' books. The store holds every
family of the finished plan, under its code from S1.181, in 1 074.0 MB at the design point.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/{lib,store,family,runs}.rs` | `Families`, `FamilyDecl`, `FamilyCode` (u8), `ContractRef`, `open`, `close`, typed column reads, run columns |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/store_tests.rs` | unit tests (with `phx-store/src/edges.rs`'s tests, moved at S1.260) |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | `-F contracts.<family>` driver |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.9 "K-53 The contract store" | the section and the family table, written first |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts]`, `[fin.contracts.<family>]` | restated below |
| `perf/design.toml` `[store.contracts]` | the rows of each family below |

**Design**:
- **The link and the code**: a row is found by `ContractRef` (family code u8 + slot 24 bits, row generation 8 bits in
  the terms word). The same 32-bit link is the chain link (S1.258) and the wheel entry (S1.225). The codes are
  S1.181's (fixed, never reused; 255 is holdings, K-60); the store refuses a family without one. A slot is < 2²⁴
  (16.7 M rows a family; the largest, `INS.policy` with `INS.annuity`, hold 6.25 M together).
- **Common columns**: `terms` u32 (terms id 24 + row generation 8); `own_due` u32 where the next due is the row's own;
  `own_amount` i64 where the amount is the contract's own (REP.3); declared extras (a start word, an arrears word,
  collateral as a `HoldingRef` u32). No per-side amount exists (REG.14, ACC.12). A family whose law fixes the amount
  reads it from the terms and declares no `own_amount`.
- **Run columns**: a family may declare a run of k i64 cells per row (k read from its terms), held in the family's
  run arena behind a u32 offset. A row with no run holds `NONE`; runs are released at the close.
- **Side modes** (declared per side; S1.258 builds Chain and List, S1.259 Column and Book): Chain 8 B, List 9.33 B,
  Column 4 B, Book 0 B.

  - The flat and individual benefit families split each scheme's claims by whether its law fixes the amount; the
    0.75 / 0.75 M split is the design point's, restated from S5.123's data at that step.

- E10: a stale `ContractRef` after close reads `None` — `stale_ref_none`.

### S1.258 — Chains and lazy block lists: the walked sides

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-53 The contract store" (walked sides).
**Depends on**: S1.257 (rows and the 32-bit link); S1.196, S1.207 (records holding chain heads and list headers).
**Goal**: a party finds its rows of a walked side through its own record — a chain of links for sides held by one
party of few rows, a lazy block list for firms' and institutions' sides with many — with no owner index.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/{chain,lists}.rs` | `Chain` (head in the record, link per row), `SideList` over K-04 `BlockList`, `rows_of(party, family)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/chain_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | walks and list compaction in `-F contracts` |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts]` | `list_entry_ns` 2.3, `dead_share` 0.5 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Chain** (8 B a side: party u32 + next link u32): the head is a record word per party kind (K-32); the link is
  S1.257's code + slot. Open pushes at the head; close unlinks in O(k), k the party's rows of all chained families,
  bounded by REP.31's declared counts.
- **List** (party u32 + 5.33 B): a lazy block list headed in the holder's record (8 entries of u32 per 48 B block).
  Close leaves the entry; a walk drops entries whose row generation changed, and a list whose dead share passes 0.5 is
  compacted in that walk. List order is never read.
- **`move_end(ref, side, party)`** on a walked side unlinks from the old holder and links to the new one.
- **Parallel**: links and lists are written in 7c's apply by the holder's range (K-12).
- **Save**: not saved; rebuilt at load in slot order (S1.162's rebuild hook).
- **Measurement**: walks report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: 115 k firms ending in a day re-point their rows through lists and chains on the pool — `mass_end_repoint`.
- E3: a party with no contracts has an empty chain — `empty_chain`.
- E6: rebuilt links and lists equal the saved rows' — `links_rebuilt_equal`.
- E9: a list with half its entries dead compacts in its next walk — `list_lazy_compaction`.
- E14: a hire and a layoff of one firm the same day commute — `hire_layoff_commute`.

**Extension points**: S1.260, S1.261, S1.267, S1.269.

**Unit tests**: `chain_unlink_k`, `mass_end_repoint`, `empty_chain`, `links_rebuilt_equal`, `list_lazy_compaction`,
`hire_layoff_commute`, `list_order_not_read`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 2.3 M / 0.1 M / 2.3 M items to `fin.contracts.list_entry_ns` (2.3 VM; walks and compaction).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (inside S1.257's row bytes).

**Guards**: PC-92 (no map by party); PC-99 (no allocation in a walk).

**Not allowed**: an owner index; reading list order; a chain on a side with millions of rows for one party.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F contracts` within `list_entry_ns` and `dead_share`
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.259 — Column sweeps and book sides

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-53 The contract store" (unwalked sides).
**Depends on**: S1.257 (rows); S1.171 (declared sweeps); S1.168 (the interner, whose terms name a book or a party).
**Goal**: a side no party walks each day holds only its party column, found by a declared sweep on the days it is
needed; a side whose one party faces millions of rows (insurer, scheme, supplier, lender, agency, treasury, school)
is named through the terms and costs no byte in the row.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/{column,book_side}.rs` | `ColumnSide` (the sweep's gather into a day buffer), `side_party(ref, side)` through the terms |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/side_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | column sweeps and book-side reads in `-F contracts` |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts]` | `column_sweep_ns` 1.0 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Column** (party u32): `#[sweep(contracts, family, side)]` reads the column once and gathers the rows of a day's
  flagged parties (a K-44 bitmap set by the day's visits and endings) into a K-03 buffer; ≤ 9 M × 1 ns a sweep.
- **Book** (0 B): the terms' interned word names a book (K-57) or a party; `side_party` resolves it through the day's
  terms array. A single row's `move_end` on a Book side re-interns its terms with the new party; a whole book moves in
  O(1) through K-57 (S1.267).
- **Users**: statements' payer and payee (S1.269, whose day sweep of the `pair` column is its own); bills until
  S1.282. A family whose side parties walk their rows most days declares Chain or List instead: a sweep's gather
  cannot live across stages without a day buffer larger than the list it replaces.
- **Measurement**: sweeps report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day gathers every ending party in the one sweep — `one_sweep_many_parties`.
- E3: a day with no flagged party skips the sweep — `no_flag_no_sweep`.
- E7: gathered rows in slot order for 1–8 workers — `column_gather_worker_free`.
- E10: a book side whose book closed resolves `None` — `closed_book_none`.

**Extension points**: S1.260, S1.267, S1.269.

**Goal**: today's ten dated families and their parallel vectors move into K-53 families — employment, public
employment, household loans, firm loans, benefits (flat and individual), pensions, the central bank's two facilities
and bills — and `DatedFamily`, `Family`, the 48-byte `Due` and `EdgeTable` are deleted. Tax collected moves at S1.270.

### S1.261 — Side aggregates maintained on row events

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-54 Side aggregates"; follows §7.17 (R4).
**Depends on**: S1.257 (row events: open, close, reprice, move); S1.258 (walked sides); S1.196 (record cells in the
party's record); S1.128 (`#[maintained]`).
**Goal**: every sum a rule reads over a party's contracts — a firm's wage bill and staff hours by class, a household's
debt service, a lender book's balance and collateral, an insurer's policies — is maintained exactly on the events that
change it, in the party's record, at ≤ 10 ns an event and read at 1 ns. Nothing walks a party's contracts to sum them
on a day path.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/aggregate.rs` | `AggDecl` (family, side, measure, cell), `on_open`, `on_close`, `on_reprice`, `on_move`, `rebuild` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/aggregate_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | aggregate updates on the row events |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.9 "K-54 Side aggregates" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts]` | `agg_update_ns` 10 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Declared measures** (K-21, per family side): `Count`, `SumOwn` (own amount), `SumTerm(field)` (wage, hours,
  premium), `SumTermByClass(field, class)` (hours by occupation class). Each writes one integer cell in the side
  party's record: a firm's wage bill i64 and staff hours × 4 classes (warm 32 B, with plant capacity, K-67); a
  household's debt service i64 in its positions; a book's Σ own amount, collateral Σ and count (K-57; BNK.11); an
  institution's declared cells (an insurer's policies, a scheme's rights, an agency's staff by (region, occupation)).
- **Events**: `open` adds, `close` subtracts, `reprice` (a pay round, a reset) adds new − old, `move` moves between
  parties or books. A `Book`-side aggregate lives in the book's record, so a book's move carries it with no per-row
  work. A payment that changes `own_amount` (principal repaid) updates `SumOwn` in the dated-item sweep's apply, where
  the row is in hand.
- All cells are `#[maintained(writer = "phx_contract::aggregate")]` integers; the audit recounts from rows on its
  rolling cycle, never from the cells (PC-101).
- **Headcount** (REP.41, LAB.13) is the employer list's live length, a read; by occupation it is a declared
  `SumTermByClass(one)` cell where a rule reads it.
- **Save**: cells are state in records; `rebuild` recomputes from rows after load and asserts equality (R4).
- **Measurement**: `rebuild` reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a book moved whole carries its cells in O(1) — `book_move_carries`.
- E6: rebuild equals the saved cells — `agg_rebuild_equal`.
- E8: cells are i64; an overflow stops the run at the site — `agg_overflow_stops`.
- E10: a side moved to an estate moves its contribution — `move_moves_contribution`.
- E14: a hire and a layoff of one firm the same day commute (integer Δs) — `hire_layoff_commute`.

**Extension points**: S1.262, S1.266, S1.267, S1.283, S1.285, S1.330, S1.338, S1.412, S1.415, S2.111, S4.105, S4.125,
S4.130, S6.107, S7.101.

**Unit tests**: `hire_layoff_commute`, `reprice_adds_delta`, `move_moves_contribution`, `book_move_carries`,
`headcount_is_list_length`, `agg_rebuild_equal`, `agg_overflow_stops`.

**Live checks**: none. The audit's Contracts family recounts on its cycle (S1.353).

**Budget**:
- adds 0.58 M / 30 k / 2.3 M items to `fin.contracts.agg_update_ns` (10 VM; the row events), and 0 / 0 / 1.5 M
  (principal repaid on loan dues, H) inside `fin.dues.item_ns`.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot "wage bill and hours", 32 B warm); ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (named
  slot "debt service").

**Guards**: PC-101 (`#[maintained]` never read by `phx-audit`).

**Not allowed**: a walk of a party's contracts to sum them on a day path; a floating sum; an aggregate with two
writers.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F contracts` within `agg_update_ns`
- [ ] §7.9 "K-54 Side aggregates" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.262 — Staff, wage bills, owed balances and collateral moved onto side aggregates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: LAB.13 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: follows §7.9 "K-54 Side aggregates".
**Depends on**: S1.261 (aggregates); S1.260 (families on K-53).
**Goal**: every walk of a party's contracts to sum them is deleted — `staff_of`, `staff_capacity`, `cost_at`'s wage
walk, `staff_means`, `owed_until`, `owed_on_loans` (every contract every day), the collateral sums over every firm
loan and the agencies' staff scans — and rules read maintained cells. `staff_capacity` is retired here; S1.295 moves
unit cost's callers and names this step. LAB.13 completes: headcount is the count of contracts, no wage is paid to
nobody, and no person holds more hours than the day.

| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `staff_means`, `staff_of` → cells and the employer list |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `cost_at`'s wage walk, `staff_capacity` → cells |

**Design**:
- **LAB.13**: headcount is the employer list's live length (a read; the audit recounts it from rows). A wage item is

- E10: a person's death closes its jobs; no wage is raised after — `wage_to_nobody_stops`.
- E14: a hire and a quit of one person the same day: the hours check sums after both — `hours_beyond_day_stops`.

### S1.263 — Terms, shapes and the day's due plans

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: BNK.2 STATE *(part: loan types and facilities declared)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-55 Terms, shapes and due plans" (replaces §4.4's algebra text).
**Depends on**: S1.257 (rows hold terms ids); S1.168 (the interner); S1.215 (the records store, read "as published by
day d"); S1.178 (day facts, day counts and conventions); S1.239 (the trigger index waking event legs); S1.170 (the
dues' apply and its waves); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: terms are interned once and shared (REP.3); each shape is a compiled program over a closed set of amount
forms; each terms id due today is resolved once at 1a into the day's terms array, which the dated-item stream reads;
schedules are shared per (country, period, anchor, convention). Loan types and facilities with their undrawn part and
commitment fee are declared data; the undrawn part's charge on capital and liquidity is built at S2.186.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/terms.rs` | `TermsRow`, `Shape`, `Schedules`, `DayTerms` (1a resolution), `intern`, `reintern` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/forms.rs` | the closed set of amount forms and their evaluators (written from `phx-ledger/src/{algebra,shape}.rs`, which S1.264 deletes) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/terms_tests.rs` | unit tests (algebra's, and new) |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/{terms,dues}.rs` | `-F terms`, `-F dues` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.9 "K-55 Terms, shapes and due plans" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.terms]`, `[fin.dues]` | `resolve_ns` 40 (added); `item_ns` 11.5, `miss_per_item` 0.08 a wave's item |

**Design**:
- **`TermsRow`** 24 B: `shape` u32; `schedule` u32; `book` PartyKey u32 (a `Book` side, or `NONE`); `param0` i64 (a
  rate, an amount, a limit); `params` u32 (arena offset of further i64 parameters). Currency, payment order, stay,
  seniority and flags are fields of the shape's header. The K-09 index adds a 12 B slot at 70 % load; a `plan_slot`
  u32 per terms links to today's array.
- **Amount forms** (closed; a new form is a change to this kernel): fixed; amortising (annuity, linear); bullet;
  balloon; grace; revolving (limit and drawn, with the commitment fee on undrawn); floating over a transacted
  reference with its fixing lag; indexed to a published series with its lag; step-up; payment in kind; conversion
  at a ratio; call, put and early termination; event-waiting legs (credit event, claim);
  `ValuedLoss{valuer, limit, deductible}` (K-91; INS.1); `WhileState{benefit per period, waiting, state}` (INS.1,
  SOC.3); career-average slices revalued (PEN.2); premium schedules; statement-period accrual (K-59).
- **Shapes** carry the leg structure with day count and convention, compiled once; terms share a shape and differ in
  parameters. **Schedules** are shared per (country, period, anchor, convention); the nth date comes by
  `Calendar::plus` in O(1) (TIME.3).
- **Seniority**: where a family declares a seniority term (senior or subordinated; a lien's rank for a secured claim,
  K-63) the class a creditor side ranks in is read from the row's terms; the family's own class applies only where the
  law ranks by creditor kind (wages, taxes, deposits).
- **Day terms** (1a): each row the wheel's take lists today has its terms id, on first sight today, resolved into
  `DayTerms` (fixed amounts, share of balance, accrual rate × day fraction, scale; the book's owner and account). The
  take buffer holds each entry's `DayTerms` index beside the row slot, so the 2b stream reads plan and row columns in
  slot order.
- **Published inputs**: floating and indexed legs read the fixing or series "as published by day d" (K-37, TIME.10).
  Until IDX's reference fixings exist a floating reset reads the last published value (the placeholder naming IDX,
  retired by S3.203). A leg waiting on a claim is woken through its K-46 trigger; a leg waiting on a credit event is
  found by S4.119's declared sweep of `DRV.contract`'s terms column on the credit-event day (0.675 M × 1 ns).
- **Re-interning** (REP.3): a restructuring (BNK.7), a pay round or a limit cut re-interns that row's terms (46 ns).
  A stay (FRM.15, HH.21) re-interns the debtor's rows with `stay` set; their plans yield no dues, so the take skips
  them. Confirmation re-interns them without the stay; liquidation converts them. 0 B on every family.
- **BNK.2's part**: loan types are declared families and shapes; a facility's undrawn part is `limit − drawn`, a read,
  with its commitment-fee leg.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (terms live, ever, bytes); resolution reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: 22.5 M items on H with ≤ 0.8 M distinct terms resolved once — `resolve_once_per_day`; the dues applied in
  S1.170's waves equal one pass — `waves_equal_one_pass` (S1.170).
- E6: terms and arena saved; the index and `plan_slot` rebuilt — `terms_roundtrip`.
- E8: 2²⁴ terms ids; the arena's offsets u32 — `terms_capacity`.
- E11: day zero: the opening's terms interned, balances on the steady path — `opening_terms_interned`.
- E12: a floating leg with no published value is `Missing`; the due is raised as a fail with that cause, never 0 —
  `unpublished_fixing_missing`.
- E13: a convention rolling onto a closed day stacks dues on the next business day — `rolled_due_stacks`.

**Extension points**: S1.264, S1.269, S1.279, S1.341, S1.407, S1.410, S1.416, S1.427, S1.434, S2.103, S2.105, S2.117,
S2.123, S2.124, S2.142, S2.168, S2.177, S2.182, S2.204, S2.207, S2.213, S3.101, S3.106, S3.118, S3.129, S3.140, S3.175,
S3.203, S3.217, S4.101, S4.115, S4.119, S4.125, S4.133, S4.142, S4.149, S4.154, S4.160, S4.176, S5.115, S5.123, S5.124,
S5.181, S6.110.

**Unit tests**: `annuity_rounded_once`, `balloon_grace`, `revolving_fee_on_undrawn`, `floating_reads_published_by_d`,
`valued_loss_limit_deductible`, `while_state_waiting`, `career_average_revalued`, `stay_yields_no_due`,
`seniority_read_from_terms`, `resolve_once_per_day`, `rolled_due_stacks`, `unpublished_fixing_missing`,
`terms_roundtrip`, `terms_capacity`, `opening_terms_interned`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 0.3 M / 15 k / 0.3 M items to `fin.terms.intern_ns` (46 VM; interns and re-interns).
- adds 0.2 M / 0 / 0.8 M items to `fin.terms.resolve_ns` (40 VM; the 1a resolution of distinct terms).
- `fin.dues.item_ns` 11.5 VM (15 phone-ns) all in at 3.0 M / 0 / 22.5 M items; `miss_per_item` 0.08 a wave's item.
- adds 1.4 phone-ns to fin.dues.item_ns at 0 / 0 / 22.5 M items (H's 4 extra waves re-reading ≈ 9.75 M × 8 B each,
  ≈ 31 core-ms).
- ledger line 10 (terms): +40 MB resident (0.8 M × 24 B rows 19.2 + index 13.7 + arena ≈ 4 + `plan_slot` 3.2).

**Guards**: PC-17 (`Calendar::plus` the one way to add a period); `forms.rs` is a closed `enum`.

**Not allowed**: a terms clone per call; a schedule per day or month; a rate read from a global; a missing fixing
read as 0.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F terms,dues -D B,H` within `[fin.terms]`, `[fin.dues]`

| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | arrears marks on the H day |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.9 "K-56 Status and arrears" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts]` | `mark_ns` 20 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Loans' arrears word** (u32): stage u8 (performing, arrears, impaired, workout, defaulted, closed; BNK.1), months
  in arrears u8, the lender's grade u8 (K-93), carrying basis 2 bits, 6 bits spare.
- **Own-due families** read arrears as `own_due < today ∧ own_amount > 0`; a statement's days late is
  `today − own_due`.
- **Marking** (2d, apply by contract range): each failed due of yesterday's outcome (by place, S1.248) marks the row's
  arrears word or leaves its own due past; the arrears are re-asked with the next due as the terms say. A grace expiry
  is filed on the agenda (K-43) at the stage's declared grace, and default follows at that entry (FRM.15, HH.13).
- **Transitions**: each stage change writes `(ContractRef, from u8, to u8, overdue i64, days_late u16)` into a K-03
  day buffer at 2d, read by the day's handlers (notices, workout wakes, bureau reports) and released at 10e.
- **Notices** (LAB.1, HSG.2, HH.13) are K-45 messages naming the contract, never a column. A stayed row (S1.263)
  raises no dues and does not advance.
- **Histories** (SET.16): on close, a row whose family declares a kept history copies it to K-37 (a bureau record;
  BNK.21, HH.21 horizons) before the slot frees.
- Carried (done at S0.15: SET.3, SET.16): their `#[clause]` carriers move to these types.
- **Measurement**: marking reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day marks 1.7 M rows into claims in range jobs — `mass_default_marks`.
- E5: a heavy day's 150 k fails marked ≤ 20 ns each — `mark_heavy`.
- E6: arrears words saved; the transitions buffer is not — `status_roundtrip`.
- E10: a closed row's history is copied before the slot frees — `history_before_free`.
- E14: two fails of one row on one day advance its stage once — `one_advance_a_day`.

**Extension points**: S1.266, S1.269, S1.339, S1.345, S1.416, S2.101, S2.109, S2.111, S2.114, S2.117, S2.123,
S2.168, S2.213, S3.106, S3.107, S3.123, S3.137, S3.207, S4.112, S4.113, S4.128, S4.176, S5.115.

**Unit tests**: `fail_marks_arrears`, `grace_on_agenda`, `own_due_past_is_arrears`, `one_advance_a_day`,
`transitions_buffer_released`, `history_before_free`, `stay_no_advance`, `mass_default_marks`, `mark_heavy`,
`status_roundtrip`.

**Live checks**: none. The audit reads status for the Contracts family (S1.353).

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.5 / 0 / 3.9 core-ms (B / NB / H) (20 k / 0 / 150 k marks at `mark_ns` 20 VM).
- on fin.calendar.mass_default: 45 core-ms (1.7 M marks); joins H.
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +4 MB at H (0.2 M × 20 B transitions).

**Guards**: PC-100 (no status map keyed by slot).

**Not allowed**: a `BTreeMap` of arrears; a daily scan for defaults; a status column on families that read arrears
from own due.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F contracts -D H` within `mark_ns`
- [ ] §7.9 "K-56 Status and arrears" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.266 — Arrears, grace, closes and default moved onto status

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.9 "K-56 Status and arrears".
**Depends on**: S1.265 (status and transitions); S1.261 (book cells); S1.249 (fails by place); S1.238 (notices on
messages; `noticed` left only for `staff_of`, deleted here).
**Goal**: `Insolvency::since` and its daily `retain`, `hold_arrears`' map rebuilt daily, `note_arrears`' linear family
search per failed flow, `end_defaulted`'s scan, `close_contract` and `end_settled` are deleted from `phx-world`.
Arrears are row status, grace is an agenda entry, default is taken at that entry, and a close writes off through the
row's own amount and status.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_default.rs` | `Insolvency.since`, `note_arrears`, `end_defaulted` → K-56 marks and grace entries |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_day.rs` | `hold_arrears` → K-56 at 2d; `close_contract` → the store's close with K-54's write-off; `end_settled` → an estate's last claim row closing |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `noticed` deleted: `staff_of` reads the employment rows' notice state through the contract's status (K-56) |
| `crates/systems/sys-{frm,bnk,hh}/src/declare.rs` | grace per family as declared data (FRM.15, HH.13) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-100.toml` | this step's sites removed |

**Design**:
- A failed due's place gives its row; 2d marks it (S1.265), and the grace expiry is filed on the debtor's agenda
  (K-43). At the entry the family's declared default rule runs; FRM.15's estate follows through K-97.
- **Close** (BNK.11): a row closed with own amount unpaid writes it off its creditor's book cell (K-54) and turns its
  arrears into a claim; no `written_off` or `arrears` vector remains.
- **Estates' end**: an estate ends at the transition that closes its last claim row with its accounts at zero, read
  from the transitions buffer; the ending kernel takes this over at S1.344.
- The generation-less slot keys of `insolvency.since` end with it: status lives in the row, and a reused slot starts
  clean.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (`since`, `hold_arrears`' map, `end_settled`'s sets) and
  `PC-100.toml` (slot-keyed state).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day files grace entries by range — `grace_entries_by_range`.
- E10: a reused slot that falls into arrears the same day starts from its own row's status —
  `reused_slot_clean_status`.
- E10: a row closed owing writes off exactly its own amount — `close_writes_off_own_amount`.
- E14: two fails of one row on one day advance once — `one_advance_a_day` (S1.265).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `grace_entry_defaults`, `reused_slot_clean_status`, `grace_entries_by_range`,
`close_writes_off_own_amount`, `estate_ends_at_last_claim`.

**Live checks**: FRM.15's default live checks and the audit's Contracts family hold as before.

**Budget**: removes a daily pass over `since` and a family search per failed flow; adds 0.

**Guards**: `exceptions/PC-92.toml` and `PC-100.toml` fall.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a scan for defaults.

**Done when**:
- [ ] moved and deleted; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows the arrears scans gone (a measure of code, never the world's)
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.267 — Books, bulk side moves and the rows of a book

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-57 Books"; follows §9 (endings).
**Depends on**: S1.257, S1.258, S1.259 (side modes); S1.194 (the party directory: a book is a party kind); S1.261
(aggregates carried in a book's record); S1.171 (declared sweeps); S1.170 (apply by range and its `SweepHooks`); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: a book is a declared party kind with no money and no decisions, owned by a party, named by a side through a
column or the terms. Moving a book changes its owner in O(1), so a bank's 3–4 M rows pass to an acquirer, a bridge or
an estate at once; any other party's rows are re-pointed through its lists, chains or a family's declared sweep, in
parallel. The rows of one book are found by one declared sweep of the family's terms column.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/book.rs` | `Book` records (owner PartyKey, aggregate cells), `move_book`, `move_end`, `repoint_party`, `rows_of_book` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/book_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | the re-pointing cursor and a mass-ending day in `-F contracts` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.9 "K-57 Books" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts]` | `move_row_ns` 15, `book_sweep_ns` 1.0, `repoint_day_core_ms` 1 (added) |

**Design**:
- **Book record** 32 B: owner PartyKey u32, the families it holds (declared), aggregate cells (K-54, 24 B). A book is a
  party kind (one `PartyKey` kind), so references to it are generation-checked (K-31).
- **Payments** name the owner, never the book (a book holds no money); 1a's `DayTerms` resolves book → owner →
  account once a day, and `side_party` resolves the same way.
- **`move_book(book, new_owner)`** is O(1); the aggregates move with it. It is written as the successor event of the
  ending or sale that decides it (PTY.9, L3).
- **`move_end(ref, side, party)`**: on a walked or Column side it re-links; on a Book side it re-interns that row's
  terms naming the buyer's book (one loan sold, BNK.10; one statement factored, TCR.3).
- **`repoint_party(party, successor)`**: on the ending day a row naming the ended party resolves through its
  successor (K-31), so its dues and claims already name the estate and the estate walks its predecessor's lists and
  chains; only book moves are made that day. From D+1 a rolling cursor (K-14) re-points the rows found through the
  ended parties' lists and chains, and Column sides by one declared sweep per family, on the pool by row range
  (≤ 15 ns a row); a day's endings share one cursor and one sweep per family. The cursor's apply is generic over
  S1.170's `SweepHooks`, so the ending's destination and the claims' classing (S1.345) are fused into it.
- **`rows_of_book(family, book)`**: `#[sweep(contracts, family, reason = "rows of a book")]` over the family's terms
  column (≤ 9 M × 1 ns), gathering the rows whose terms name the book into a K-03 buffer; on the occasions its users
  declare (a bank's securitisation, an insurer's D+1, a vehicle's determination, a resolution).
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` for book records; re-pointing and sweeps report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: the largest bank's ≈ 3.5 M rows in one book move O(1); 115 k firms' ≈ 1.7 M rows resolve through their
  successors on the day and are re-pointed by the cursor over the following days — `bank_book_o1`,
  `mass_repoint_batched`, `successor_until_repointed`.
- E3: a party with no rows re-points nothing — `repoint_nothing`.
- E6: book records saved; lists and chains rebuilt — `books_roundtrip`.
- E7: re-pointing and `rows_of_book` by row range are worker-free — `rows_of_book_worker_free`.
- E10: a book whose owner ended resolves through its successor (K-31) until moved — `book_owner_successor`.

**Extension points**: S1.343, S1.344, S1.345, S1.347, S2.107, S2.115, S2.199, S4.112, S4.114, S4.125, S4.127, S4.140, S4.160,
S4.161, S4.163, S4.164, S4.166, S4.167, S4.170, S4.176, S6.124.

**Unit tests**: `bank_book_o1`, `move_end_reinterns_book_side`, `payments_name_owner`, `mass_repoint_batched`,
`book_owner_successor`, `successor_until_repointed`, `repoint_nothing`, `books_roundtrip`, `rows_of_book_finds_all`, `rows_of_book_worker_free`.

**Live checks**: none until S1.344.

**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.mass_default: 1 core-ms (the day's book moves, O(1) each); joins H.
- spread after fin.calendar.mass_default over 5 days: 7 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.resolve (1.7 M rows re-pointed at
  `move_row_ns` 15 VM, ≈ 20 phone-ns, by the rolling cursor).
- adds 0 / 0 / 0 items by itself to `fin.contracts.book_sweep_ns` (1.0 VM); each user states its sweeps' days and rows.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +1.6 MB resident (50 k × 32 B).

**Guards**: a flow naming a book as payer or payee is refused (compile level: books have no `AccountId`); PC-96 (the
sweep is declared).

**Not allowed**: re-pointing a book's rows one by one; a per-ending sweep; a book that decides; a resident list of a
book's rows.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F contracts` within `move_row_ns`, `book_sweep_ns` and `repoint_day_core_ms`
- [ ] §7.9 "K-57 Books" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed

### S1.268 — Participations: sides held in shares

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: PTY.3 STATE *(part: a thing owned jointly is held in shares by its co-owners)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.9 "K-58 Participations".
**Depends on**: S1.257 (side modes); S1.172 (apportionment with a named residue); S1.194 (the directory: a group is a
party kind).
**Goal**: a side held jointly (a joint account, a loan taken together, a dwelling in shares, a household's division by
family law, a pool's members) names an interned participation group; its dues and payments are split among the
members by their shares at each due, by largest remainder with a named residue (MON.16). Each lender's share of a
syndicated loan is its own contract (BNK.3), never a group.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/group.rs` | `Group` rows, members arena, the intern index, `split_due`, `join`, `leave` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-contract/src/group_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/contracts.rs` | `-F contracts.participations` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7.9 "K-58 Participations" | the section |
| `perf/budget.toml` `[fin.contracts.participations]` | `split_ns` 15, `mb` 19 (added) |

**Design**:
- **`Group`**, interned: one group per distinct set of co-owners with their shares, shared by everything they hold
  together (a couple's joint account, mortgage and dwelling name one group). 16 B: member a u32, member b u32, weight
  a u16, weight b u16, refcount u24, residue rule 4 bits, count 4 bits; more than two members use an overflow run of
  (member u32, weight u16) in a K-04 arena. The intern index is a sorted column of (member a, group id), 8 B,
  searched only at a join. A group is a party kind, so any side, holding or account may name it; it is released at
  refcount 0 and its identity is never reused (PTY.13).
- **At each due**: a stream item with a group side becomes one item per member, `apportion(amount, shares, residue)`
  (K-16), rounded once; a member's own account pays or receives its part (E 48; PTY.3).
- **Joins and leaves** happen only by the members' own events (a marriage, a sale of a share, a death to the estate): a
  change to one holding's co-owners interns that holding's new group and moves its side (K-57 `move_end`); the other
  holdings keep theirs. A zero or overflowing weight is a violation.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats`; splits report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E3, E13: a group left with one member splits nothing; the residue goes to the named member (POP.9) —
  `one_member_group`.
- E8: shares over the whole stop the run — `shares_over_whole_stop`.
- E10: a member's death passes its share to its estate (K-97) — `member_death_to_estate`.
- E14: two dues of one group the same day split independently — `same_day_splits_independent`.

**Extension points**: S1.271, S1.405, S2.126, S2.135, S2.193, S5.108, S5.113, S6.124.

**Unit tests**: `split_largest_remainder`, `residue_named`, `one_member_group`, `member_death_to_estate`,
`shares_over_whole_stop`, `same_day_splits_independent`, `group_interned_once`.

**Live checks**: none until S1.405.

**Budget**:
- adds 20 phone-ns to fin.dues.item_ns at 0.1 M / 0 / 0.3 M items (the group items' split, `split_ns` 15 VM a member).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +19.2 MB resident (0.8 M × 24 B, group rows and index).
- ledger line 3 (directory): +3.2 MB resident (0.8 M × 4 B generations).

**Guards**: `apportion` is the only splitter (compile level: no hand pro rata).

**Not allowed**: a syndicated loan as a group; an average share; a split without a residue rule.

**Done when**:
- [ ] code and tests; fast checks pass
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F contracts` within the participations ratchets
- [ ] §7.9 "K-58 Participations" written
- [ ] both reviews; status `done`; section removed
