| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/src/named.rs` | per-kind slot tables; core and kind-declared columns; `standing(tile)`, `in_building(unit)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/tests/named.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/units.rs` | `named` measures |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.units]` `named_*` (added); `[store] named_units`, `buildings` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.10 "K-66 Named units" |

**Design**:

| Columns | Layout |
| --- | --- |
| Core (every named unit) | kind `KindH` u16 · condition u8 · age class u8 · owner `PartyKey` u32 · site u32 (a K-28 `CellId`, or a K-26 path, as the kind declares) · cost i64 (at cost, ACC.2) = 20 B |
| Kind-declared | SoA columns a kind declares in K-21, laid out per kind, never a union: a building's floors u8, position in its cell u8, floor area u16 (24 B a building in all); infrastructure's capacity u32, service day u32, maintenance state u8 (GEO.4); a plant's technology, efficiency, fuel, ramp limit, running cost (ENE.1) |

- A kind's table is a K-02 slot table with generations (`NamedRef`); a unit is created by its completion (a project,
  S1.287: CAP.5, HSG.8) or the opening, and ends by scrapping, destruction (GEO.8) or demolition.
- **Owner**: a named unit's holding is the unit itself (its owner column), carried at cost with its basis (K-89); a
  change of owner changes that column alone (GEO.15, CAP.12: the site never moves); an ending owner's units pass to its
  estate in the ending kernel's pass.
- **Reads**: `standing(tile)` — the named units standing on a tile, through a lazy by-tile K-06 instance (5.33 B an
  entry), filtered by cell at the walk; `in_building(unit)` — a building's composition, the holdings whose place is the
  building (S1.271's place key), read by walking the zone's owner index (S1.274) filtered by place — rare reads (a
  building's completion, demolition, the opening, a struck building), ≈ 13 µs each — never stored.
- **Remaining life** is a read from the kind's declared life, its service day or age class and its condition (CAP.1),
  never a stored second copy. **Condition** moves by use, age, damage and repair (S1.285, a hazard hit).
- **Capacity shared in a day** (GEO.4): a segment's or plant's use is K-26's per-epoch counter or the market's
  dispatch (K-77), read against this capacity; not stored here.
- **Saves**: tables saved; instances rebuilt in slot order. `StoreStats` per kind table; walks report rows visited
  through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**: E1 (a catastrophe on 200 tiles destroys what stands on them, found through `standing`, never a scan:
`standing_finds_struck_units`); E10 (a stale `NamedRef` refused: `stale_named_ref_refused`); E4 (an estate's
buildings held with no daily visit: `estate_building_no_visit`); E13 (a country with no plant of a technology has no
rows: `kind_without_rows`); E6 (`named_round_trip`); a sale of a building keeps its site (`owner_change_keeps_site`).

**Extension points**: S1.294 (strikes read `standing`); S2.160 (infrastructure owned privately); S2.169 (buildings on
held cells, their composition read); S2.202, S2.212 (power plants, storage, lines and investment in them); S8.200
(strategies read named units); S5.128, S5.131 (public services' and public capital's units); S6.134 (the map: units
by tile, their sites, owners and `in_building`).

**Unit tests**: the edge cases' tests, and `create_on_completion`, `remaining_life_is_read`, `kind_columns_per_kind`,
`building_composition_is_read`.
**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- ledger line 12 (physical units, cells, owner index): +38 MB resident (≈ 1.6 M buildings × 24 B, the count S2.171
  derives from recs2020's unit types by urban type plus firms' buildings), +9 MB (≈ 0.2 M other named units × ≈ 44 B),
  +9.6 MB (the by-tile instance, 1.8 M × 5.33 B); saved: +47 MB
- its share of fin.fixed.kinks: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 20 k changes a day ≤ 50 ns VM)
- on fin.calendar.catastrophe (a day a footprint strikes): 5 core-ms (≈ 3 k `in_building` reads × ≈ 13 µs, on the
  pool); joins H and B′ (an event, composed by S1.360)
- Ratchets `[fin.units]` (added): `named_ns` 50, `named_core_bytes` 20, `named_mb` 57.

**Guards**: named-unit columns written by `phx-hold` alone.
**Not allowed**: a union row for every kind; a stored remaining life; a building's composition stored; a scan of all
units to find a tile's; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Tables, core and kind columns, sites, `standing` and `in_building` with tests; fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F units` within the `named_*` keys.
- [ ] §7.10 "K-66 Named units" written; both reviews' findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.285 — Capital classes: wear and maintained capacity

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: CAP.6 PROCESS *(part: wear by age and use as class moves, charged once to income and to the unit;
failure completes at S2.129)*; CAP.9 INVARIANT *(part: plant capacity maintained; the output check
completes with production, S1.443)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.10 "K-67 Capital classes, wear and capacity".
**Depends on**: S1.271 (plant cells, household slots and their carry); S1.227 (K-43: a firm's period close among its
next days, until the close pass takes it); S1.180 (K-21: capital chains — each class's efficiency and value as
declared fixed-point shares, leaving rates over age and use, the failed band); S1.261 (K-54: the warm record's
maintained words); S1.170 (the sweep's hook parameter the depreciation posts through).
**Goal**: wear is a closed form of the plant's state at its last realisation, the days since and its use, realised —
units moved along their kind's classes, the value lost charged once to income and to the unit (CAP.6) — only at the
firm's period close and at a mechanism read, never by a walk; a failed band holds units that no longer work until
repaired or scrapped; a firm's plant capacity is read in closed form from the same state (CAP.9).

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/src/wear.rs` | chain moves over a period with carry and use; the value moved; legs with nature; the failed band |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/src/capacity.rs` | per kind efficient units; capacity = least over kinds; maintained on change |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/tests/{wear,capacity}.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/units.rs` | `wear_ns`, `capacity_read_ns`, `failed_cells` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.10 "K-67 Capital classes, wear and capacity" |

**Design**:
- **Chain** (K-21, from `CAP.condition_classes` and the kind's life): A classes; a class's leaving rate declared over
  age and use, r = r_age + r_use × u; over a period the hazard's integral is r_age·Δ + r_use·X with X = the period's
  output ÷ capacity, exact while capacity is constant, X handed in by the caller (the output since the period began is
  S1.289's rate-row count, reset at each close); efficiency and value per class as declared fixed-point shares (`Fixed`,
  PC-12). A kind with a failure hazard declares a **failed band**: efficiency 0, value its declared salvage share,
  outside A.
- **Realisation**: over the period since the last, from each class c the units the hazard takes, n_c × (1 −
  e^{−(r_age·Δ + r_use·X)}) — e^{−r_age·Δ} from a day-cached table per (kind, days), e^{−r_use·X} by a fixed-point
  polynomial once per kind a firm, ≈ 10 ns a cell — reckoned on the holdings before any moved, plus the cell's carry,
  floored; the remainder is the new carry (Law 7's continuous allowance, so a single dwelling ages on its expected
  schedule instead of rounding to nothing each period). Moved units carry cost × value[c+1] ÷ value[c] (half-even,
  once); the last class's leave the chain (retirement). A failure (a hazard hit, K-44) moves units to the failed band;
  a repair moves them back (both callers' decisions). Legs name nature and the chain as source (SET.9, CAP.8).
- **Depreciation** (CAP.6: one schedule to income and to the unit) is the cost lost, posted to the holder's income line
  through the sweep's hook parameter (S1.170), in the same apply; until S1.328 builds the lines it posts through today's
  `recognise` (placeholder naming S1.329, which retires it).
- **When**: at the firm's period close, fused into S1.328's per-firm close pass (each firm on its own fiscal calendar;
  until S1.328, the period end is a kink among its next days, placeholder naming S1.328); at any mechanism read of the
  plant (a sale, a hazard hit, a completion, an ending) first. A household member's units realise at their mechanism
  reads only. An observer's read computes without writing (Law 17).
- **Capacity** (CAP.1: the scarcest kind): per kind Σ_c units_c × efficiency_c over the way's plant a unit of output,
  the least over kinds; the warm record holds it at the last realisation (`#[maintained(writer =
  phx_hold::capacity)]`, rewritten on every plant change: realisation, failure, completion, loss, sale, pass), and a
  read applies each kind's decay factor for the days since in closed form (≈ 10 ns). A way needing no plant reads
  `Missing`, never infinity.
- `StoreStats` for carries and failed cells; realisations report cells visited through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**: E1 (a flood's losses re-maintain the struck firms' capacity only: `capacity_maintained_on_change`); E5
(a quarter-end close realises every firm closing that day in the close pass: `close_realises_in_one_pass`); the closed
form equals a daily walk (`lazy_condition_equals_daily_walk`, `use_integral_exact`); E6 (carry and capacity saved,
capacity rebuilt equal: `capacity_rebuilt_equal`); E11 (day zero: the opening's steady-path cells, capacity computed
once: `day_zero_capacity`); E12 (a way with no plant reads `Missing`: `no_plant_is_missing`); E14 (a completion and a
wear on one firm the same day, realise then apply: `completion_and_wear_same_day`).

**Extension points**: S1.286 (today's users moved); S1.289 (production reads capacity); S1.294 (capacity
re-maintained after losses); S1.295 (the capital charge's classes); S1.328 (the close pass realises wear); S1.330 (net
assets' depreciation deltas); S1.441, S1.442 (which way to run reads capacity, capacity's check); S1.457 (wear on its
kinks, with use); S1.484, S1.487 (the opening's plant, the dwelling kind); S2.116 (write-downs of plant); S2.129
(failures into the failed band); S2.202 (plants' condition).

**Unit tests**: the edge cases' tests, and `wear_moves_with_carry`, `single_unit_ages_on_schedule`,
`wear_faster_at_full_use`, `value_moved_half_even`, `last_class_retires`, `failure_into_failed_band`,
`capacity_least_over_kinds`.
**Live checks**: none (the Units family checks CAP.8 per owner and kind).

**Budget**:
- ledger line 24 (plant cells): +0.8 MB resident (≈ 0.1 M failed-band cells × 8 B: failures ≈ 3 k a day, live until
  repaired or scrapped); the cells themselves are S1.271's line (47 MB at A = 1, 90 at 2, 196 at 4); the step is
  parametric in A
- its share of fin.fixed.close_books: 0.6 / 0 / 116 core-ms (B / NB / H) at A = 2, the design point's (1.15 M firms ×
  5 cells × 2 × 10 ns at the quarter end; ≈ 5.5 k a business day on other fiscal calendars; half at A = 1)
- adds 10 phone-ns to fin.decide.visit_ns at 246 k / 30 k / 246 k items (capacity's closed form at the visit)
- its share of fin.fixed.kinks: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (no walk)
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot plant capacity, inside `[store] firm_bytes`)
- Ratchets `[fin.units]` (added): `wear_ns` 10, `capacity_read_ns` 10, `failed_cells` 100 000.

**Guards**: PC-96: no whole-kind traversal for wear; the capacity word `#[maintained]`.
**Not allowed**: a wear pass over every party; capacity recomputed per read; a float in a store; infinity for "no
limit"; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The closed form with carry and use, the failed band, capacity at read, the depreciation hook, with tests.
- [ ] Fast checks pass; `tools/bench.sh -F units` within `wear_ns`, `capacity_read_ns`, `failed_cells`.
- [ ] §7.10 "K-67 Capital classes, wear and capacity" written; both reviews' findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.287 — Processes in progress: shipments, projects, production in flight, spells

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: FRM.1 STATE *(part: work in progress at cost; completes at S3.156)*; CAP.5 PROCESS
*(part: a project over its lead time, in service only when complete; purchase in stages completes at S1.459)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.10 "K-69 Processes in progress".
**Depends on**: S1.271 (the owner's holdings the process draws from and delivers to); S1.277 (goods in transit
pledged to the carrier via the process); S1.160 (a day's arena page, K-03's page pool); S1.180 (K-21:
process kinds and their declared columns); S1.190 (K-28: a process's own site cell); S1.159 (K-02).
**Goal**: everything that takes time between start and completion — a shipment on a route, a construction project
paid in stages, production started and not yet finished, a spell of illness or training — is one row with its owner,
kind, subject, units and cost at start, its own site and its completion or arrival day on the wheel; the owner's work
in progress is read from its rows at cost.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/src/process.rs` | process rows, per-kind columns, open, complete, pass, cut |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/tests/process.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/processes.rs` | the `processes` driver |
| `perf/budget.toml`, `perf/design.toml` | `[fin.processes]` (added); `[store] processes`, read from the farm count S1.482 gives |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.10 "K-69 Processes in progress" |

**Design**:

| Record | Layout |
| --- | --- |
| Process row (every kind) | owner `PartyKey` u32 · kind `ProcessH` u16 · flags u16 · subject u32 (a way, a capital kind, a goods unit, a contract) · units i64 · cost at start i64 (WIP at cost) · completion day u32 = 32 B, in the arena page of its completion day |
| Kind-declared | shipments: carrier u32, vehicle u32 (a named unit or the class the room was sold from), arrival unit u32, promised day u32 (16 B); projects: site cell u32, stage-payment `ContractRef` u32 (8 B); production and spells: none |

- **Open** (`open_batch`): moves units and cost from the owner's holding into the row — production's starts still in
  flight when its rate changes (S1.289), their inputs consumed at start; a project's stage paid; a shipment's goods
  pledged to the carrier via the row (S1.277) — bump-allocating it in its completion day's arena page (the pages are
  the process's wheel: no K-42 entry). **Complete** at 4a on its day, reading the day's page in order and freeing it
  whole:
  delivers the finished units into the owner's holding (a shipment's arrival unit at the destination's zone; a
  project's plant into class 0 of its kind at its own site; a batch's output at its yield), each leg with nature and
  the process as source (SET.9), carrying the cost; a spell's end is a wake of its person (K-43).
- **Its own site**: a project keeps its site cell, so an owner ending mid-process passes the row to its estate at cost
  and completion reads the row, never the owner's record (so the run stopper S1.135 names cannot happen).
- **WIP** (FRM.1, CAP.2 "an asset of its owner at cost"): an owner's WIP is the sum of its rows' cost, maintained in the
  firm's hot record (8 B, `#[maintained]`), recounted by the audit from the rows.
- **Delays and losses** (FRT.7, FRT.8, GEO.8): a closure or breakdown moves the completion day (the row copied to its
  new day's page, never repriced); a `ProcessRef` keeps its generation, resolved only on a cancellation's path; cargo
  or work destroyed cuts the row's units at cost (a loss leg); a carrier's end leaves the goods the owner's, recovered
  through the estate (K-97 passes the row).
- **FRT.9**: one owner, one carrier, one vehicle a shipment; a vehicle's position (a named vehicle's site) changes at
  departure and arrival only, so it is never in two places — checked where written. FRT.3's `#[clause]` carriers move
  here (done at S1.07).
- **By owner**: a K-06 instance keyed by owner, declared only for kinds an owner's rule enumerates (a firm's projects,
  its shipments). Pages and rows saved; instances rebuilt. `StoreStats` for rows; completions report rows
  visited through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**: E1 (a region struck, its shipments delayed or cut, one row each: `cut_is_loss_at_cost`,
`delay_refiles`); E4 (an estate's project waits at cost, no visit: `estate_project_waits`); E5 (a month-end with many
completions in one wheel bucket: `many_completions_one_day`); E6 (`processes_round_trip`); completion in wheel order
(`arena_completion_order_equals_wheel_order`); E10 (owner ended mid-process: `estate_completes_project`); E14 (a
completion and a sale of its output the same day, complete at 4a and sell at 6: `complete_before_sale`); E9 (rows live
only between open and completion: `row_freed_on_completion`).

**Extension points**: S1.288 (today's shipments moved); S1.289 (starts in flight at a rate change); S1.292
(projects); S1.343 (the ending kernel passes rows); S1.466 (carriers' room and repositioning); S2.127 (goods aboard a
failed carrier); S2.172 (trips in transit); S2.212 (plants built as projects); S5.178 (goods under customs' lien in
transit); S6.115 (spells read into the employment history); S6.119 (retraining spells).

**Unit tests**: the edge cases' tests, and `open_moves_units_at_cost`, `complete_delivers_at_yield`,
`project_into_class_zero`, `wip_sum_matches_rows`.
**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- ledger line 13 (liens and processes): +40 MB resident (≈ 1.0 M rows × 32 B + shipments' 16 B + projects' 8 B;
  0.9–1.5 M with the farm count S1.482 gives: shipments ≤ 0.5 M, projects ≤ 0.1 M, spells ≈ 0.2 M, crops' starts in
  flight); saved: +40 MB
- its share of fin.fixed.kinks: 3 / 1.5 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (completions ≈ 0.1 M / 0.05 M / 0.1 M × 25 ns, a page
  read in order)
- its share of fin.fixed.real: 3 / 1.5 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (opens ≈ 0.1 M / 0.05 M / 0.1 M × 25 ns, bump-allocated)
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot WIP, 8 B inside `[store] firm_bytes`)
- Ratchets `[fin.processes]` (added): `open_ns` 25, `complete_ns` 25, `row_bytes` 32, `mb` 40.

**Guards**: process rows written by `phx-hold` alone.
**Not allowed**: a pass over every process; completion reading the owner's record for the site; a delay as a price
multiplier; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Rows, kinds, open, complete, delay, cut and pass with tests; carrier moved.
- [ ] Fast checks pass; `tools/bench.sh -F processes` within `[fin.processes]`.
- [ ] §7.10 "K-69 Processes in progress" written; both reviews' findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.289 — Standing rates realised lazily

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: FRM.4 DECISION *(part: the output decided is a start rate realised exactly; the decision itself is
S1.443's)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.10 "K-68 Standing rates and cumulative output".
**Depends on**: S1.271 (the own and input stocks the realisation writes); S1.273 (making groups); S1.276 (lot ages
for spoilage); S1.285 (capacity); S1.287 (starts in flight at a rate change become a process); S1.225 (K-42: kinks as
dated rows); S1.227 (K-43: kinks among the firm's next days, wakes).
**Goal**: production, input use and spoilage are standing rates realised exactly when something reads them — the
day's seller-good batch or a kink (an input running out at the current rate) — never by a daily pass; a visit reads
stock plus what the rate owes to the day as a pure value.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/src/rate.rs` | the rate row; realisation over [a, b]; derived input rates; `pending`; kinks |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/src/spoil.rs` | spoilage realised from lot ages (moves `goods::spoil`'s arithmetic) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-hold/tests/{rate,spoil}.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/batches.rs` | `prod_ns`; realisation fused into `batch_ns` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.10 "K-68 Standing rates and cumulative output" |

**Design**:

| Record | Layout (firm hot record) |
| --- | --- |
| Start rate | rate Q32.32 i64 (units started a day) · anchor day u32 · started count at the anchor i64 = 20 B |

- **Exact realisation** (R2): units started over [a, b] = ⌊r·(b − t₀)⌋ − ⌊r·(a − t₀)⌋ from the anchor t₀; a rate
  change re-anchors. The firm's period close realises production to the close day and resets the started count to 0, so
  the row counts starts since the period began (the output S1.285's wear reads; TEC.9's floor differences are taken
  within a period). **Inputs are reads**: an input's use = start rate × the way's input per unit in content ÷ the
  slot grade's content per unit (TEC.2; GDS.1), a rational rate realised by the same floor difference on the
  cumulative started count; no input rate is stored. **Output** = the start rate lagged by the way's lead time × its
  yield; starts still in flight when the rate changes are filed as a process (S1.287).
- **Where realised**: the seller-good batch at 6b (K-74) realises to today before its one stock move; a kink's day at
  4a. `pending(holder, good, day)` is the pure read of what the rate owes up to that day (to its stock-out kink if
  sooner): a visit's rule (5b) reads stock + pending and writes nothing (decide, then apply), and the meeting's cover
  counts it (S1.277). Each realisation writes one making group (S1.273, TEC.9) and its legs with nature (SET.9).
- **Kinks** (among the firm's next days, K-43): an input's stock-out day at the current rate (its stock ÷ its derived
  rate, the next whole day) and a grade's stock-out when the slot switches grade. At a stock-out the realisation stops
  what inputs cannot make — production without the input is impossible (GDS.12, TEC.9), not a bound — and the rate
  stands at what the stock allows until the firm's next decision.
- **Spoilage** (GDS.8): at each realisation, a holding of a perishable good loses what its declared yearly rate takes
  over the days each lot (or its mean day at weighted average) was held, floored with the lot's own remainder, as a
  leg to nature at the holding's cost; storage is a service bought apart. GDS.8's `#[clause]` carriers move here
  (done at S1.05).
- `StoreStats` for rate rows; realisations report rows visited through `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**: E14 (a sale and a production on one holding the same day, realise then apply:
`realise_before_apply`); E1 (a flood destroying input stock re-files the stock-out kink: `stockout_refiled_on_loss`);
E5 (NB days realise in the batches of markets that meet, TIME.8: `nb_realises_in_batches`); E6 (anchors and counts
saved, kinks rebuilt from them: `kinks_rebuilt_equal`); E8 (Q32.32 × days in i128 intermediates, i64 results, overflow
stops: `rate_overflow_stops`); E11 (day zero: the anchor at the opening: `anchor_at_opening`).

**Extension points**: S1.290 (cumulative output from realisations); S1.291 (production and spoilage moved); S1.293
(extraction as a rate); S1.301, S1.306, S1.309 (the stall book, the meeting's cover of `pending`, the batch
realising); S2.207, S2.211 (energy as an input, load shedding's lost output); S8.130 (a line head's production);
S6.104 (via S1.290).

**Unit tests**: the edge cases' tests, and `realise_exact_floor_difference`, `rate_change_reanchors`,
`input_rate_derived_rational`, `stockout_day_exact`, `pending_is_pure`, `spoil_by_lot_age`,
`visit_read_writes_nothing`.
**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.kinks: 6 / 1.5 / 6 core-ms (B / NB / H) (realisations beyond the batches 0.4 M / 0.1 M /
  0.4 M × 15 phone-ns, `fin.batches.prod_ns`)
- adds 0 phone-ns to fin.batches.batch_ns at 1.2 M / 0.9 M / 1.2 M items (realisation fused into the batch)
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot start rate, 20 B inside `[store] firm_bytes`)
- ≈ 40 k kinks a day on the agenda (line 14's entries).

**Guards**: the rate row has no public writer but the realisation and the rate change (compile level).
**Not allowed**: a daily production pass; a stored input rate; a clamp of output to capacity (production decided
within it is the rule's); an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Rate row, realisation, derived inputs, `pending`, spoilage and kinks with tests; carriers moved.
- [ ] Fast checks pass; `tools/bench.sh -F batches` within `prod_ns`, `batch_ns`.
- [ ] §7.10 "K-68 Standing rates and cumulative output" written; both reviews' findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

**Goal**: a firm's cumulative output on each way it runs is a position (FRM.23, REP.20) added to at every realisation;
the way's declared thresholds give the day each is crossed at the current rate, filed as a kink that wakes the firm.

**Status**: planned

**Depends on**: S1.191 (K-29: each deposit's opening, extracted and resource, its right unit); S1.271 (rights as

S1.165 (K-06: the parties-by-zone-and-kind instance for the opening's nearest-firm grant).
**Goal**: the right to extract is a holding of the deposit's right unit (GDS.3, GEO.6); extraction draws on the
holder's deposits as its rate is realised, depleting them exactly and never refilling; where the resource's nature
is that the richest part goes first, the grade of what is extracted falls with what has been taken (GEO.9); the maps,
the O(deposits × firms) opening and the daily audit pass are gone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_deposits.rs` | `Deposits { holders, held, working }` → K-29 and holdings; `open_rights` O(deposits × firms) → the nearest firm through the zone instance; `take_from_deposits` cloning its list → realisation against the holder's right holdings; `review_extraction` over every firm by `(day + slot) % days` → the extraction reason on K-43; `pass_rights` → the ending kernel; `audit_deposits` every deposit every day → the Units family over touched deposits |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/declare.rs` | each resource's nature (grade falls with depletion or not) and its grade bands by share extracted (TECHNOLOGY, GDS.13, GEO.6) |

- Extraction is the extractor's start rate (S1.289) whose input is the deposit's resource in content: each
  realisation takes from the holder's deposits in their declared order through K-29's `extract_batch` (which writes

  unit is the band's grade at the deposit's zone (a K-22 unit), so crossing a band is a kink that switches the output
  grade, and the richer early grade yields more in use by its content (GDS.1 as amended). A resource declared uniform
  keeps its grade.

re-maintained); S1.165 (K-06: the parties-by-zone-and-kind instance, filtered by a firm's site tile); S1.235 (K-44:
the catastrophe as a hazard occurrence); S1.198 (the interim site column it deletes).
**Goal**: a catastrophe on a tile destroys what stands there — firms' stocks and plant sited on it, persons' and
groups' dwellings and vehicles drawn from their zone's stock, named units standing on it — as real losses at their
owners whatever binds them (GEO.8, GDS.9), found through indexes, never by a scan of every firm.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_weather.rs` | `destroy`'s pass over every firm and its `BTreeMap` of struck tiles → the footprint's tiles through the indexes; `cost.unwrap_or(0)` after `move_goods` → the batch's cost or its refusal |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core.rs`, `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/lib.rs` | the interim `FRM.site` column (S1.198) deleted: a firm's site is the tile K-27 holds for its plant |

**Design**: at 3a, for each struck tile and its severity: (1) the firms of its zone (the parties-by-zone-and-kind
instance) whose site is the tile lose the severity's share of each holding and plant cell they hold there, of units
held, not only free; (2) counted units in the tile's zone: K-27 draws the units lost at the tile from the (zone,
class) stock and allocates them across holders by one multivariate hypergeometric draw on the stream

S1.284). All losses go into one `lose_batch` (their source the event, SET.9), which cuts bounds in declared order
(S1.277) and re-maintains the struck firms' capacity (S1.285); each owner's loss is posted at the units' cost through

since S1.198, is read here from K-27 (`draw_tile` on the firm's plant) and the column is deleted, freeing its 4 B.
**Edge cases**: E1 (a flood over 200 tiles: 0.2 M items in one batch, drawn per (zone, class), never per party:
`flood_one_batch`); E3 (a struck tile with nothing on it: `empty_tile_loses_nothing`); E7 (draws keyed by subject, any
worker count: `draws_workers_invariant`); E14 (a loss and a sale of the same holding, loss at 3a and sale at 6:

#### phx-market (S1.296–S1.327)

Every market form the specification names (MKT.3–MKT.8, and search and match for LAB.8, HSG.10, POP.7) is one kernel in
`phx-market`, over one store of standing offers and one store of prints, each designed for its last user (Stage 5's FX
and cross-border markets) and measured alone at the design point by `tools/bench.sh -F` before behaviour is put on it.
Local markets meet per region, and within a region every choice weighs distance at zone resolution (REP.24, GEO.3 as
restated, E 51): a stall stands in its good's zone, a buyer draws a zone from its own zone's distance-weighted
cumulative over its region's zones and a stall from that zone's sum-tree. A retail purchase costs 31 phone-ns all in,
because the sale is its own payment (an 8 B item in its seller-range shard, SET.13, MON.5, E 26), authorised at the till
by the buyer's wants within its `available`, and every per-seller effect (revenue, tax, tally, trigger, the payee's
`pending`, the income line, the day's batch of cost and delivery) is applied once per seller range. A posted-price
market's mark is its day's sales' mean weighted by units (MKT.12 as amended).

**Exit.** The kernels K-70–K-86 (K-75 and K-83 kept, K-75 changed at S1.306) at their `fin.*` ratchets; no pass over
every firm for stalls, cheapest prices, services' closing or marks; `book_sale`, `deliver_sales`, `traded`, `marks`,
`keep_vacancies`, `Standing::new`, `core_bills`' clearing, `apply_for_loan`'s hand-built rounds and `core_central`'s
request passes deleted; the markets' resident memory ≤ 100 MB at the design point (ARCHITECTURE §13's markets line) with
the perishable-capacity rows (≈ 9.4 MB) reported beside it.

### S1.296 — Standing offers and market instances

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes ARCHITECTURE §7.11 (phx-market), "Standing offers (K-70)"; follows §4 (the day's stage table).
**Depends on**: S1.159 (generation references), S1.160 (day buffers for the day's intents), S1.165 (keyed index
instances by poster), S1.170 (apply partitioned by target range at 5d), S1.180 (markets as declared kinds: form,
meeting days, participants, lapse rules), S1.225 (lapses on the due wheel), S1.277 (`Covered<Qty>` from free units).
**Goal**: every offer that stands — a posted price, a wage offer, a listing, a resting order, a two-way quote, a posted
rate — is one typed row of one store, keyed by its market instance, posted, repriced and withdrawn only at 5d and 6d
through a batch apply, and lapsing on the wheel.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/mod.rs` | `Offers`: the families, `post`, `withdraw`, `reprice`, `get`, the 5d/6d apply |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/families.rs` | vacancy, listing, standing order, two-way quote, posted rate rows (declared columns) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/instances.rs` | `Instances`: (market kind, subject) → `Instance` u32, interned on first naming |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/offers.rs` | -F driver `fin.offers` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.offers]` `mb` 10, `post_ns` 60 (added) |
| `perf/design.toml` | `[store]` `market_instances` 58_000, `posted_rates` 5_000; `[day.*]` `posts` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Standing offers (K-70)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carriers of REP.34 (done at S1.09) and MKT.1 (done at S0.18) move here.
- **Instances.** A market (MKT.1) is a declared kind (K-21: form, meeting days, settlement convention, participants,
  price points, lapse rule, admission) over a subject keyed as its thing is (Law 9): a good at a zone (`UnitId`), an
  instrument (`InstrumentId`), labour of an occupation family in a region, dwellings of a class in a zone, a route. An
  `Instance` u32 is interned on first naming (K-09 table of 8 B keys, saved; `[store] market_instances`). Prints and
  marks (S1.326) are kept per instance.
- **Points.** An offer's price on a posted form is a `PointWord` u32: the point's index 24 bits + the row's generation
  8 bits (the contracts' terms-word layout); the ladder that gives a point its price is S1.297's. A posted price is
  never averaged: rows hold points, never prices derived from them.
- **Families**: the stall family's good-major layout is S1.299's; the store's other families follow.
- **Other families**, SoA with only their declared columns: vacancy — employer u32, instance u32 (occupation family ×
  region), wage `PointWord` u32, jobs open u32, asks u32 (skill level, site zone), terms u32 (interned: hours, notice,
  severance, K-55), posted day u32 = 28 B × 200 k; standing order — poster u32, instance u32, price i64 (ticks,
  negative allowed, ENE.8), quantity i64 (a sell side `Covered<Qty>`, committed by K-63 at admission, S1.298), side and
  generation u32, next in its level u32 (S1.315) = 32 B × 200 k; two-way quote — dealer u32, instance u32, bid i64, ask
  i64, bid size i64, ask size i64 (`Covered<Qty>`) = 40 B × 50 k; listing — poster u32, instance u32, asked
  `PointWord` u32, unit u32 (a named unit or class row), terms u32, posted day u32 = 24 B × 45 k; posted rate (BFL.4,
  BNK.4) — poster u32, instance u32, `PointWord` u32 = 12 B × 5 k.
- **API** (the only way in): `post(family, row) -> OfferRef`, `reprice(OfferRef, Point)`, `resize(OfferRef, Qty)`,
  `withdraw(OfferRef)`, `get(OfferRef) -> Option<RowView>`; writes take the stage runner's `ApplyToken` (5d, 6d) and
  arrive as intents in (chunk, handler) buffers (K-03), applied by instance range (K-12) so one instance has one writer;
  reads are `&self`. Two intents on one offer the same day stop the run (one writer per fact).
- **Lapses.** Each family declares its lapse rule (never; a day; n business days; the day's close for day orders,
  which never become rows and live in the day's buffers). A lapse day is filed on K-42 under the family's 8-bit wheel
  family code; taken at 1b; an entry whose offer was withdrawn or reposted is skipped by generation.
- **Endings** (E10, K-97): a poster's stalls as S1.299 says; vacancies and standing orders through K-06 instances by
  poster (8 B an offer); listings, quotes and posted rates by one declared sweep of their poster column (≤ 0.1 M rows)
  on a day one of them ends.
- **Save/load**: rows, instances and lapse days saved; K-06 instances by poster rebuilt at
  load in slot order; the logical hash over the primary columns equal after a round trip.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` per family (rows live, rows ever, bytes, blocks); `ExecCounters::visited` on every apply
  and sweep.
- **Replaces**: the firm's PRICE word (`consts.rs`, a firm column after S1.198 — migration S1.300); the
  `vacancies`/`postings` vectors (`core_labour.rs` — S1.305).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: an instance with no offers is empty, not absent — `empty_instance_reads_empty`.
- E3: a poster with no free units posts no sell side: `Covered<Qty>` cannot be built — `sell_side_needs_cover`.
- E6: save and load mid-run — `round_trip_keeps_rows_and_rebuilds_instances` (a hand-built table).
- E7: apply by instance range — `apply_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E8: positions beyond `[store]`'s capacity are `capacity_exceeded!` — `positions_beyond_capacity_stop`.
- E10: a stale ref after withdrawal and reuse is refused — `stale_ref_refused`.
- E11: day-zero orders (GEN.13) are rows in the opening snapshot and stand into day one — `day_zero_rows_stand`.
- E14: two intents on one offer the same day stop the run — `second_intent_same_day_stops`.

**Extension points**: S1.297, S1.298, S1.299, S1.302, S1.304, S1.312, S1.315, S1.316, S1.317, S1.319, S1.326,
S1.342, S1.343, S1.466, S2.130, S2.133, S2.145, S2.153, S2.204, S2.205, S2.208, S3.101, S3.104, S3.107, S3.120, S3.165,
S3.175, S8.132, S4.105, S4.129, S5.162. A new family is a declaration of its columns and lapse rule, never a new store.
**Unit tests**: `point_word_packs_point_and_generation`, `stale_ref_refused`, `instance_interned_once`,
`lapse_filed_and_taken`, `second_intent_same_day_stops`, `apply_same_for_any_chunking`,
`positions_beyond_capacity_stop`, `day_zero_rows_stand`, `round_trip_keeps_rows_and_rebuilds_instances`,
`empty_instance_reads_empty`, `sell_side_needs_cover`.
**Live checks**: none (a base; its users' checks read it).
**Budget**: volumes `[store]` vacancies 200 k, standing orders 200 k, dealer quotes 50 k, listings 45 k, posted rates 5
k, market instances 58 k. Posts, reprices and withdrawals 0.2 M / 0.1 M / 0.2 M (B / NB / H) at ≤ 60 ns VM
(`fin.offers.post_ns` 60, added), each counted where it is emitted: adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.review_ns at 0.1 M /
50 k / 0.1 M items (inside the unit's 550); its share of fin.fixed.pay_rounds: 1.8 / 0 / 1.8 core-ms (B / NB / H) (30 k
vacancy posts); standing orders inside fin.fixed.securities' 150 ns an order (S1.298, S1.312, S1.315). Lapses 20 k a
day at the wheel's 2.3 ns. ledger line 17 (markets): +5.6 MB resident (200 k vacancies × 28 B), inside
`fin.vacancies.mb` 10 (S1.304); ledger line 17 (markets): +10 MB resident (standing orders 200 k × 32 B, quotes 50 k ×
40 B, listings 45 k × 24 B, posted rates, instances 58 k × 8 B; `fin.offers.mb` 10, added). Traversal: apply by instance
range on the pool. No allocation after the heaviest day (`fin.daybuf.allocs_per_day` 0).
**Guards**: row mutators take `ApplyToken` (compile level); `phx_market::offers` joins PC-92's hot list (S1.120).
**Not allowed**: a map keyed by poster; an offer written outside 5d/6d; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `Offers`, the families, instances and lapses, with the unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F offers` at the design point within `fin.offers.*`.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.11 "Standing offers (K-70)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.297 — Price points and ladders

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Price points (K-70)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (`PointWord`), S1.180 (each trade's declared points and each market's tick grid, MKT.21).
**Goal**: a point is an index into its trade's declared ladder of round and conventional prices (REP.34), resolved to
a price once per read by table; a ladder that cannot be held is refused at assembly.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/ladder.rs` | `Point`, `Ladder`, `Ladder::price(point)`, `Ladder::nearest(price)`, compile from K-21 |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/ladder_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/offers.rs` | the ladder reads in `fin.offers` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Price points (K-70)" |

**Design**:
- A **ladder** per trade (MKT.21: "tick sizes and price points (POLICY of the trade)"), compiled at assembly from K-21's
  declared points into a sorted `i64` table of prices a lot, in the market's currency's smallest units; a market with a
  tick grid (books, calls) has its grid as an arithmetic ladder (base and tick, no table).
- `Ladder::price(point) -> Price` is one table read; `nearest(price) -> Point` a binary search (a rule choosing its
  point from a computed price, FRM.5, LAB.4, BNK.4 — the choice among points stays the rule's).
- A ladder beyond 2²⁴ points, a point not ascending, or a ladder for a market of another currency is refused at
  assembly with its clause (REP.34, NUM.5).
- Ladders are declarations: never saved, rebuilt from the register at load.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (ladders, points).

**Edge cases**:
- E8: a ladder over 24 bits is refused — `ladder_over_24_bits_refused`.
- E12: a point beyond its ladder is a violation, never a default price — `point_beyond_ladder_stops`.
- E13: a currency with no ladder declared for a trade that posts there is refused at assembly —
  `missing_ladder_refused`.

**Extension points**: S1.300, S1.301.
**Unit tests**: `price_is_table_read`, `nearest_is_binary_search`, `ladder_over_24_bits_refused`,
`point_beyond_ladder_stops`, `missing_ladder_refused`, `tick_grid_arithmetic`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**: ledger line 17 (markets): +0.5 MB resident (≈ 250 trades' ladders × ≤ 250 points × 8 B, inside
`fin.offers.mb` 10); saved: +0 B (declarations, rebuilt at load). A read ≤ 1 ns, inside its caller's unit (no line of
its own).
**Guards**: `Point` constructible only from a `Ladder` (compile level).
**Not allowed**: a price stored beside a point; a ladder built at runtime.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The ladder and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F offers` within `fin.offers.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Price points (K-70)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.298 — The shared admission hook

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: DRV.6 PROCESS *(part: the admission of a participant's whole order set against declared limits; the
clearing member's re-margining limit is Stage 4's)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Admission (K-70)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (the families and their sell sides), S1.277 (commits of free units), S1.170 (partition by
participant range), S1.176 (the lot's stream).
**Goal**: one hook admits a participant's whole order set before any meeting matches: in an arrival order drawn by lot,
each order's need is taken from the participant's declared headroom, an order beyond it cut to whole lots or refused
visibly; every call, book, dealer market and administered facility uses it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/admit.rs` | `admit(participant, orders, headroom, lot) -> Admitted` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/admit_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/offers.rs` | the admission driver |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.call]` `admit_ns` 20 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Admission (K-70)" |

**Design**:
- At 5d, for market kinds that declare admission (calls, books, dealers, administered forms: S1.312, S1.315, S1.316,
  S1.319), the day's orders are partitioned by participant range (K-12); each participant's set is taken in an arrival
  order drawn by lot (stream `MKT.admission`, addressed by (participant, day)) (DRV.6, MKT.9, MKT.16, MKT.17).
- Each order carries its need in the kind's declared measure (margin, notional, cash), computed by its poster's rule at
  5b; headroom is handed in per participant as data (K-93's limits from S1.338 through the routing; a kind that declares
  no limit hands none) and carried from order to order; an order beyond it is cut to whole lots where the kind declares
  cutting, else refused.
- A sell side must carry a `Covered<Qty>`: K-63 commits free units at admission; released at withdrawal, lapse or the
  fill's delivery.
- Refusals are recorded per kind and participant (MKT.10), never dropped silently.
- **Measurement**: admitted, cut and refused per kind; `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a participant with no headroom has every order refused visibly — `no_headroom_all_refused`.
- E3: a sell order without free units is refused — `sell_side_needs_cover`.
- E7: arrival order by lot addressed by (participant, day) — `admission_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E14: two orders of one participant draw one headroom in lot order — `admission_in_lot_order_carries_headroom`.

**Extension points**: S1.312, S1.315, S1.316, S1.319, S3.165, S4.110, S5.180.
**Unit tests**: `admission_in_lot_order_carries_headroom`, `admission_cuts_whole_lots_or_refuses`,
`no_headroom_all_refused`, `sell_side_needs_cover`, `admission_same_for_any_chunking`.
**Live checks**: none (its users').
**Budget**: unit ≤ 20 ns VM an order (`fin.call.admit_ns` 20, added); design count 0.45 M / 0 / 0.6 M orders (B / NB
/ H). The users carry the shares (count × unit, inside fin.fixed.securities' 150 ns an order with S1.312's and S1.315's
units). ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (day buffers only).
**Guards**: a meeting kernel takes only `Admitted` orders (compile level).
**Not allowed**: an order met without admission where its kind declares it; a refusal dropped; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The hook and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F offers,call` within `fin.call.admit_ns`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Admission (K-70)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.299 — The stall family in good-major blocks

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Stalls (K-70)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (the offer store, `PointWord`, the apply), S1.183 (24-bit unit ids: a good at a zone is a
stall's group), S1.271 (the seller's holdings, read at its ending).
**Goal**: the 1.7 M posted prices of goods, services and carriage live in 8 B rows grouped in blocks owned by their
good, so a good's stalls are contiguous for the stall book, a stall's ref never moves, and no stall stores a quantity.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/stalls.rs` | the stall family: rows, blocks, block lists, `stalls_of(good)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/offers/stalls_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/stalls.rs` | the rows' fill and posts in `fin.stalls` |
| `perf/design.toml` | `[store]` `goods_with_stalls` 60_000 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Stalls (K-70)" |

**Design**:
- Rows live in **blocks of eight positions owned by one good** (`UnitId`: product, grade, zone), from a K-04 block
  pool. Per position: `seller` `PartyId` u32 · `point` `PointWord` u32 = **8 B**. Per block (SoA): `good` u32 · `rank`
  u16 (its place in the good's block list) · `live` u8 mask · `open` u8 mask = 8 B. Per good: its block list (K-04,
  u32 a block).
- A stall's ref is (position, generation). A freed position is reused first within its block; an emptied block returns
  to the pool; blocks never move, so a ref never changes.
- A stall stores **no quantity**: what it can serve on a day is read at the meeting from where the fact lives — the
  seller's free units (K-60, K-63, as a `Covered<Qty>`) with the production owed to the day (K-68), or a service's
  unused capacity (K-85) — so no pass refreshes it (Law 4, R2).
- A firm's own-product stall ref is 4 B in its hot record in place of a posted point (S1.196); a poster's other stalls
  are found through the goods it holds (K-60), each good's block run scanned for the poster — the path its ending takes
  (K-97).
- **Save/load**: rows, block headers and block lists saved.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (stalls, blocks, fill).

**Edge cases**:
- E8: positions beyond `[store]`'s capacity stop the run — `positions_beyond_capacity_stop` (S1.296).
- E9: blocks freed as goods lose their stalls; the pool's fill reported — `empty_block_returns_to_pool`.
- E10: a poster's stalls found and withdrawn at its ending — `ending_finds_stalls_through_goods`.
- E14: a withdrawal and a new post in one block the same day reuse the freed position —
  `freed_position_reused_in_block_first`.

**Extension points**: S1.300, S1.301.
**Unit tests**: `freed_position_reused_in_block_first`, `empty_block_returns_to_pool`, `ref_never_moves`,
`ending_finds_stalls_through_goods`.
**Live checks**: none (a base).
**Budget**: 1.7 M stalls; posts, reprices and withdrawals at S1.296's `fin.offers.post_ns` 60. At the design point's
declared settings (`perf/design.toml` `[store] zones` 1 000, the owner's): ledger line 17 (markets):
+17.4 MB resident (1.94 M positions × 8 B + 242 k blocks × 8 B; 19.6 MB at 2 000 zones), inside `fin.stalls.mb` 23 with
S1.301. saved: +17.4 MB.
**Guards**: `phx_market::offers::stalls` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a quantity column on a stall (a second copy of free units); a block that moves; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The family and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F stalls` within `fin.stalls.mb` and `fin.offers.post_ns`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Stalls (K-70)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.300 — Posted prices onto standing offers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "Standing offers (K-70)".
**Depends on**: S1.299 (the stall family), S1.297 (points priced by the ladder), S1.198 (the firm's price as a typed
column, which this step removes).
**Goal**: a firm's posted price is its stall's point, one fact in one place; the firm's record keeps the stall's ref;
the day-zero prices post as stalls (GEN.13).

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `goods_firm` reads the stall's point; `review_prices` emits a reprice intent |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `firm_record` and `price_expected` read the stall's point |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_lending.rs` | `open_credit` reads the stall's point |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_credit.rs` | `firm_loans` reads the stall's point |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | `carriage_offers`: carriers' posted price read from their stall |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_firms.rs` | `price_drafts`: the day-zero price posted as a stall |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/consts.rs` | `firm::PRICE` deleted |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-100.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- The firm's hot record's posted-point column (S1.198) becomes `own_stall: StallRef` (the same 4 B); every reader
  resolves the ref and reads the point, converting through the trade's ladder (`Ladder::price`). A firm with no stall
  (none posted, or withdrawn) reads `Missing` — its rule states its answer (VAL.10), never a zero price.
- `review_prices`' write becomes a reprice intent at 5b applied at 5d (K-70), so the price seen by 6a is today's and a
  reprice is O(1).
- Day zero: `core_firms`' opening price (the markup over its own cost at its nearest point) is posted as the firm's
  stall at its site's good; the opening snapshot carries the rows (GEN.13).
- Retires S1.278's placeholder (a stall's cover taken per meeting in `core_goods`, naming S1.300): a stall's sale is
  covered where it is made — the meeting reads the stall's capacity as a `Covered<Qty>` of the seller's free units by
  `cover_read` (K-63, a pure read that writes nothing) and the 6b batch delivers from it (S1.306, S1.309) — and a
  standing order's sell side is committed when K-70 admits it.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (the PRICE word reads through `record_word`) and `PC-100.toml`.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a firm with no stall reads `Missing` — `price_missing_without_stall` (logic level over the reader function).
- E10: a firm that ends: its stall is withdrawn by its ending (K-97 through the record's ref) — `stale_ref_refused`
  (S1.296).
- E11: day zero posts every opening firm's stall before day one's 5d — `day_zero_posts_stall`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `price_missing_without_stall`, `reprice_intent_applied_at_5d`, `day_zero_posts_stall`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-08 (prices' reads: every firm with sales has a posted point; none averaged) each day.
**Budget**: reprices 0.1 M / 50 k / 0.1 M; adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.review_ns at 0.1 M / 50 k / 0.1 M items (K-70's
apply, ≤ 46 of the unit's 550, is inside it); readers' cost unchanged (one resolve, 3 ns). Bench:
`tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows `goods.review` no higher and no `record_word(PRICE)` in the profile.
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses `firm::PRICE` (deleted constant).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a second copy of the posted point in the firm's record.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Readers moved, the word deleted, the tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; the ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench shows the span unchanged or lower; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.301 — The stall book: a sum-tree per good at its zone

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: index
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The stall book (K-71)"; follows §7.11 "Standing offers (K-70)".
**Depends on**: S1.299 (stall rows in good-major blocks), S1.297 (points and ladders), S1.164 (the sum-tree kernel),
S1.165 (keyed index instances), S1.271 (holdings: a stall's capacity is its seller's free units, `holding_of`), S1.289
(production owed to the day, `pending`); K-25 (zone distances, kept, no step); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: each good at its zone keeps its open stalls' logit weights in a sum-tree over its blocks, so a buyer's stall
draw, a sold-out close and a reprice are O(log n); each region's zones are weighed from any buyer zone by a declared
distance factor, so a market meets per region with distance at zone resolution (REP.24, GEO.3, E 51); the cheapest
open point per market instance is maintained, never recomputed over every firm.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/book/mod.rs` | `StallBook`: trees, `open`, `close`, `reprice`, `draw`, `cheapest` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/book/weights.rs` | `PriceWeights` per (ladder, price weight); `ZoneFactors` per (region, distance weight) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/book/tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/stalls.rs` | -F driver `fin.stalls` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.stalls]` `update_ns` 46, `close_ns` 15 (added), `mb` 23, `zero_weight` 0 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The stall book (K-71)" |

**Design**:
- **Weights.** A stall's weight is the logit's price term at its point, `(p/p₀)^(−α)`, α the market kind's declared
  price weight (a PREFERENCE of the buyers' kind, K-20) and p₀ the ladder's lowest price, held as u64 fixed point at
  2⁴⁴ (`PriceWeights`: one table per (ladder, α), a few KB, built at assembly and on α's dated change). A stall weighs
  its point's entry while its `open` bit is set, else nothing; no weight is stored per stall. Integer weights keep the
  maintained sums equal to a rebuild at load (E6); the 2⁻⁴⁴ resolution is the derived-arithmetic allowance of Law 7,
  and a weight that rounds to nothing is counted (`fin.stalls.zero_weight`), never floored.
- **Trees.** Per good (a product's grade at a zone): a K-05 Fenwick over its blocks in rank order, each leaf the sum of
  its block's open positions' weights (u64; a good-zone beyond 2²⁰ stalls at the top weight is `capacity_exceeded!`).
  Per block its least open point (u32); per good its least open point, recomputed over its blocks only when the least
  closes. `draw(good, u) -> StallRef`: `find` over the blocks (≈ 1–2 steps), then ≤ 8 positions scanned by the open
  mask and the weight table. Reprice, close and open: one leaf delta, O(log blocks).
- **Zones.** `ZoneFactors` per (region, the market kind's distance weight γ): a zones × zones table (40 × 40 at the
  declared 1 000 zones) of `e^(−γ·km)` as u32 at 2³² from K-25's distances; a pair with no path has no factor (out of
  reach). `cumulative(instance, buyer_zone, out)` writes the region's zones' `factor × tree total` running sums for a
  meeting's buyers standing in that zone. Rebuilt at load and on γ's dated change.
- **Closing and reopening.** A stall is opened at posting. A meeting closes a stall it sells out or finds empty (in its
  own instance's trees, 6a, `close_ns`). A sold-out stall had sales, so its (seller, good) batch at 6b (S1.309) reads
  its free units after delivery with tomorrow's owed production (`holding_of`, `pending(…, day + 1)`), or a service's
  renewing capacity (K-85, S1.324), and reopens it in the same apply when that is not nothing. A goods stall left
  closed has its reopening filed as a K-68 kink on the wheel at the first day its owed production reaches a whole
  unit; a service stall found empty for want of staff or plant reopens at its owner's next capacity event (K-54's or
  K-67's update, through the sweep's hook, S1.170). No pass looks at closed stalls.
- **Cheapest.** Per market instance its least open point over its region's goods, recomputed at 6d only for the
  instances whose goods' least changed that day (a dirty list); read at stage 5 as yesterday's close (TIME.10).
- **Writers.** A good's tree has one writer at a time: 5d's apply and 6d's apply by instance range, 6a's meeting job of
  its instance, 6b's batch by seller range touching only its own stalls' bits and leaves through the good's leaf delta
  (integer, order-free); so any number of workers gives the same trees (E7).
- **Save/load**: trees, least points and factor tables are `#[saved(skip, rebuild = …)]`, rebuilt in rank order from
  K-70's saved rows and open masks; the logical hash is over K-70's primary columns.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (goods with stalls, blocks, open stalls, bytes); `ExecCounters::visited` per apply;
  `meeting_work_per_sale` reads the tree steps and positions scanned.
- **Replaces** (users moved at S1.303): `stalls` rebuilt over every firm in each `meet_all` (`core_goods.rs`),
  `cheapest` over every firm every day, `Cheapest`'s `Vec<Vec<Option<f64>>>`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a good-zone with no open stall has total nothing and is never drawn — `empty_zone_never_drawn`.
- E5: a payday's sold-out wave closes 0.5 M stalls at one leaf delta each — `close_is_one_leaf_delta`.
- E6: rebuild equals the maintained sums — `rebuild_equals_maintained`.
- E7: trees written by one job per instance — `same_trees_for_any_chunking`.
- E8: sums beyond u64 at a good-zone stop the run — `sum_overflow_stops`.
- E10: a stall withdrawn at its seller's ending leaves its tree at once — `withdraw_leaves_tree`.
- E12: a weight rounding to nothing is counted, not floored — `tiny_weight_counted_not_floored`.

**Extension points**: S1.303, S1.306, S1.307, S1.309. A declared price weight per preference-type class (NUM.4) adds
one weight table per class, never a tree per buyer.
**Unit tests**: `weight_is_the_points_logit_term`, `draw_matches_weights`, `reprice_moves_one_leaf`,
`close_is_one_leaf_delta`, `empty_zone_never_drawn`, `cumulative_weighs_distance`, `no_path_no_factor`,
`cheapest_follows_closes`, `withdraw_leaves_tree`, `rebuild_equals_maintained`, `same_trees_for_any_chunking`,
`sum_overflow_stops`, `tiny_weight_counted_not_floored`.
**Live checks**: none (a base; S1.306's LC-1-160 reads it).
**Budget**: 1.7 M stalls over ≈ 60 k goods with stalls (`[store]` 250 products × 25 regions × 1 000 zones). Reprices
0.1 M / 50 k / 0.1 M at ≤ 46 ns VM (`fin.stalls.update_ns` 46): adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.review_ns at 0.1 M /
50 k / 0.1 M items (inside the review's 550). Closes 0.5 M a day at ≤ 15 ns (`fin.stalls.close_ns` 15, added): adds
0 phone-ns to fin.retail.all_in_ns at 6.75 M / 6.75 M / 6.75 M items (0.07 a sale × 15, inside the serve's share,
S1.306). Reopens ride the batch: adds 0 phone-ns to fin.batches.batch_ns (≤ 2 of its 35, S1.309). At the design
point's declared settings (`perf/design.toml` `[store] zones` 1 000, the owner's): ledger line 17
(markets): +5.3 MB resident (trees 242 k × 8 B, block least points 242 k × 4 B, goods' headers and index 1.1 MB, block
lists 1.0 MB, zone factors 0.3 MB); with S1.299's 17.4 MB, `fin.stalls.mb` 23 (22.7). At 2 000 zones: 8.0 + 19.6 =
27.6 MB. saved: +0 B (rebuilt).
**Guards**: `phx_market::book` joins PC-92's hot list; the tree's mutators take `ApplyToken` or the meeting's instance
token (compile level).
**Not allowed**: a per-stall stored weight or float sum; a pass over every stall or firm; a map by (product, place); a
rebuild of a tree per meeting or round; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `StallBook`, weights, factors and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F stalls` at the design point within `fin.stalls.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "The stall book (K-71)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.302 — Closed borders read as a declared scope

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The stall book (K-71)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (market kinds and instances), S1.180 (declared scopes of the market kinds).
**Goal**: the closure of searches at a country's border is a declared set of market kinds the kernels read as data,
so a later stage opening or closing a kind changes data only and no kernel read site is deleted then.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/reach.rs` | `Reach::new` reads the declared closed set per market kind; the one-number read of `XB.closed_borders` removed |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/reach_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/shared/XB.toml` | `XB.closed_borders` restated as the set of market kinds closed (SHAPE, `placeholder:XB`, declared by `phx-market`'s `MarketPrims`), every kind at the opening |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-98.toml` | the site this step removes |

**Design**:
- The defect: `reach.rs` reads one count primitive (`closed == 1` in `Reach`) for every search, so opening one kind
  (S5.163's currency markets) or all (S5.175) would need a kernel edit.
- The closure becomes a declared set of market kinds (K-21 data, SHAPE `placeholder:XB`); `Reach` is built per market
  kind from its membership; the stall book's zone factors (S1.301), the vacancy book's reach (S1.304) and search's
  reach (S1.321) read it through `Reach`. S5.163 narrows the set and S5.175 empties it as data; no kernel read site is
  deleted there.
- Removes its site from `exceptions/PC-98.toml` (a register read by name).

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a kind not in the set reaches across the border; one in it does not — `closed_set_read_per_kind`.
- E12: a market kind absent from the declaration is refused at assembly (never read as open) —
  `undeclared_kind_refused`.

**Extension points**: S5.163, S5.175 (the set narrowed, then emptied).
**Unit tests**: `closed_set_read_per_kind`, `undeclared_kind_refused`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**: assembly only; adds 0 phone-ns to any unit. Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` unchanged.
**Guards**: the ratchet file above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a kind branch on the closure.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The read and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet file lowered.
- [ ] The bench unchanged; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.303 — Stalls and the cheapest price onto the stall book

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The stall book (K-71)".
**Depends on**: S1.301 (the stall book), S1.300 (posted prices as stalls).
**Goal**: no pass over every firm builds a meeting's stalls or the cheapest prices; `meet_all`'s callers read the
book's goods for the products wanted today, and every reader of a cheapest price reads the book's.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `stalls`, `cheapest`, `Cheapest` and the `places` per product deleted; `meet_all` fed from K-71 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `cost_at` and input orders read `StallBook::cheapest` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | `carriage_offers` reads carriers' stalls from the book |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-96.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- `meet_all`'s five callers (`goods_day`'s households, state and investment, `buy_inputs`,
  `buy_services`) take the goods of each product wanted today from the book (the instances with a want bucket), so the stalls
  handed to today's `meet` are those of wanted goods only, O(their stalls), without the `BTreeSet` of wanted products
  or the `BTreeMap<u16, Vec<StallAt>>`; the meeting itself moves onto the trees at S1.306.
- Every reader of the cheapest price (unit cost, input orders, the shipper's gap) reads the instance's least open
  point through the ladder; an instance with no open stall reads `Missing`, and each reader states its answer
  (VAL.10).
- Carriers' posted carriage prices and room are read from their stalls (room from K-85 at S1.325; until then today's
  vehicle computation) instead of the daily table over every carrier.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (`BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet` in `stalls`), `PC-96.toml` (`firm_slots` in
  `stalls` and `cheapest`) and `PC-99.toml` (the per-call `Vec`s).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a product wanted where no stall is open: its want fails visibly (MKT.10) — `no_stall_unserved` (S1.306);
  LC-1-162.
- E12: no cheapest price reads `Missing`, never 0 — `cheapest_missing_reads_missing` (logic level, the reader).

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `cheapest_missing_reads_missing`, `wanted_goods_only`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-08 (prices' reads) each day.
**Budget**: removes 5 × ≈ 150 ms (`goods.stalls`) and the `cheapest` pass from the 5 M bench's day. Bench:
`tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows `goods.stalls` and `goods.cheapest` gone.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a per-meeting rebuild of stalls.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The functions deleted, their users moved, the tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench shows the spans gone; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.304 — The vacancy book and searchers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: index
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The vacancy book (K-72)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (vacancy rows), S1.165 (keyed index instances), S1.207 (persons: the searcher's flag and search
start in the person record), S1.221 (accumulators for searchers' counts); K-25 (zone distances).
**Goal**: open vacancies are indexed by their labour instance (occupation family × region) and the skill they ask, so
a searcher's reach is a handful of runs; each employer's vacancies are found by an index instance; a searcher is a
flag on its person, counted per (region, occupation family) at its changes; nothing is remapped or rebuilt daily.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/vacancies.rs` | `VacancyBook`: runs by (instance, skill), by employer, reach, the pull table |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/vacancies_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/vacancies.rs` | -F driver `fin.vacancies` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.vacancies]` `mb` 10, `reach_ns` 40 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The vacancy book (K-72)" |

**Design**:
- **Rows** are K-70's vacancy family (28 B: employer, instance, wage point, jobs open, asks = skill level and site
  zone, terms, posted day). A vacancy is open while its jobs open are more than none (LAB.2); the hire that takes its
  last job withdraws it in the same apply; its fill is recorded where the fact lives — the employment contract opened
  (K-53) — so the book keeps no fill history of its own (SET.16).
- **Runs.** A K-06 instance keyed (instance, skill level asked) — ≤ 16 skill levels an occupation family (POP.1's 4
  bits) — whose members are the open vacancies (8 B a member with its back-pointer). A searcher of skill s in region r
  and occupation family o reaches the runs (r·o, 0..=s): ≤ 16 runs, ≈ 15 vacancies at the design point.
- **Distance and pull.** Each reached vacancy's log-pull `w·ln wage` is read from a fixed-point table per (wage ladder,
  the labour kind's wage weight w), built at assembly, so no pull is recomputed per search (`hiring.rs`'s defect)
  and none is stored per vacancy; the distance term `−γ·km` from the searcher's zone to the vacancy's site zone is read
  from a per-(region, γ) table of fixed-point logs beside S1.301's `ZoneFactors`. REP.24's distance enters every
  search; a listing's score is the sum of the two, with no `exp`.
- **By employer.** A K-06 instance keyed by employer (8 B a vacancy) for the employer's own postings (S1.413), its
  layoffs' reads and its ending (K-97).
- **Searchers.** A person searches while its `search start` column holds a day (K-33); set at a separation or entry,
  cleared at a hire or leaving the labour force, each at its event. Counts per (region, occupation family) are K-39
  accumulators moved at those events (LAB reads, STA). Searchers act on their own days through K-43; nothing
  enumerates them in Stage 1, so the regional index instance is declared with its first enumerating reader (public
  agencies' placement, SOC.2, Stage 5) and costs nothing until then.
- **API**: `reach(searcher) -> impl Iterator<(VacancyRef, weight)>` (≤ 16 runs), `of_employer(party)`, `open`/`close`
  at 5d and at the hire's apply (K-70 intents).
- **Save/load**: rows and person columns saved; both K-06 instances and the pull table rebuilt at load in slot order.
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (open vacancies, runs, bytes); `ExecCounters::visited` on reach walks.
- **Replaces**: `vacancies`/`postings` compacted daily by `keep_vacancies` (`core_labour.rs`), `post`'s map
  of every vacancy, `Standing::new` twice a day, `searching: BTreeSet` — users
  move at S1.305.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no vacancy in reach: `reach` is empty and the searcher applies nowhere (MKT.10's "the vacancy stays open" on the
  other side) — `empty_reach`.
- E3: a person with no skill in an occupation family reaches its skill-0 runs only — `reach_is_runs_up_to_skill`.
- E6: indexes rebuilt equal — `rebuild_equals_maintained`.
- E10: an employer that ends: its vacancies withdrawn through `of_employer` (K-97) — `ending_withdraws_all`.
- E14: a hire and a withdrawal of one vacancy the same day: one apply, one writer —
  `second_intent_same_day_stops` (S1.296).

**Extension points**: S1.305, S1.321, S3.156, S8.124, S8.125, S8.134.
**Unit tests**: `reach_is_runs_up_to_skill`, `log_pull_from_point_table`, `distance_weighs_reach`, `empty_reach`,
`last_job_withdraws`, `ending_withdraws_all`, `rebuild_equals_maintained`, `searcher_flag_moves_counts`.
**Live checks**: none.
**Budget**: 200 k open vacancies over 200 labour instances; 90 k reaches a business day (0 NB), one a job search
(`[day.b] searches`), at ≤ 40 ns VM each
(`fin.vacancies.reach_ns` 40, added): adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.search_ns at 90 k / 0 / 90 k items (the reach is
inside S1.321's kernel part, 170 of the search's 300); posts and closes ≈ 30 k a day inside fin.fixed.pay_rounds
(S1.296's share). ledger line 17 (markets): +4.1 MB resident (two K-06 instances 200 k × 8 B × 2, keys and pull table
0.9 MB); with S1.296's vacancy rows 5.6 MB, `fin.vacancies.mb` 10. Traversal: reach reads on the pool from 5b handlers;
opens and closes by instance range at 5d.
**Guards**: `phx_market::vacancies` joins PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a per-day remap or rebuild of the book; a pull stored or recomputed per vacancy per search; a set of
searchers kept apart from the person column.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `VacancyBook` and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F vacancies` at the design point within `fin.vacancies.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "The vacancy book (K-72)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.305 — Vacancies and searchers onto the vacancy book

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: LAB.2 STATE
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The vacancy book (K-72)".
**Depends on**: S1.304 (the vacancy book), S1.238 (applications, offers and notices as messages, no daily remap); S1.232 (`post_one` on the agenda, still reading today's postings).
**Goal**: a vacancy is one K-70 row with its posted terms, open until its last job is filled or it is withdrawn
(LAB.2); searchers are a person column; the parallel vectors, the daily compaction and remap, the twice-daily
`Standing` and the searchers' set are gone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `vacancies`/`postings` and `searching` fields, `keep_vacancies`, `post`'s map, `Standing::new` deleted; posting, search and selection call K-70/K-72 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_default.rs` | `close_ended`'s scan of every vacancy → K-72 `of_employer` at the ending |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_agencies.rs` | the agency's scan of every vacancy → `of_employer` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/hiring.rs` | `Standing` deleted; `search` reads `VacancyBook::reach` (the kernel generalised at S1.321) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-96.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- `post_one`, moved onto the agenda at S1.232 still reading today's postings, reads the employer's own rows here
  (`of_employer`).
- A vacancy's row carries every term LAB.2 names — occupation family and region (its instance), skill required, hours,
  wage point, notice and severance terms (its interned terms), its site zone — posted with it at 5d; a hire reads its
  terms from the row, not from the law at the hire.
- A hire decrements its vacancy's jobs open in the hire's apply; the last job withdraws the row (LAB.2 "open until
  filled"); an employer's withdrawal is an intent applied at 5d; an ending withdraws through `of_employer`.
- A searcher is a person whose `search start` holds a day; the flag and the counts move at separations, entries, hires
  and exits (K-72); no set of searchers exists apart from the person column.
- The day's applications and offers are K-45 messages (S1.238) naming vacancy refs; a message whose vacancy has lapsed
  is refused by generation, so no daily remap exists.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (`BTreeSet`, `BTreeMap<PartyKey, Vec<usize>>`), `PC-96.toml` (every
  vacancy scanned) and `PC-99.toml` (`postings.clone()`, per-call `Vec`s).

**Edge cases**:
- E10: an employer's ending withdraws its vacancies and lapses messages naming them —
  `ending_lapses_vacancies_and_offers`.
- E14: a hire taking the last job and the employer's withdrawal the same day: one apply wins by stage order (the hire
  at its answer's apply, the withdrawal refused on a stale ref) — `stale_ref_refused` (S1.296).

**Extension points**: none beyond S1.304's.
**Unit tests**: `last_job_withdraws_row`, `terms_read_from_row`, `ending_lapses_vacancies_and_offers`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-21, LC-1-22 (vacancies, filled jobs, searchers) each business day.
**Budget**: removes `keep_vacancies`, the post map and `Standing` ×2 (≈ 0.9 s of the 5 M bench's `labour.posting` line
with its remap). Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows `labour.posting` and `labour.keep` gone or below
fin.fixed.pay_rounds (40 / 0 / 40 core-ms).
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a remap of messages by vacancy position.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Fields and functions deleted, users moved, tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench shows the spans gone; LAB.2's row in §13; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.
