### S1.306 — The posted-price meeting on the stall book's sum-trees

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: REP.22 PROCESS *(part: the choice among sellers by taste, capacity served by lot, the rest choose again;
completed at S1.321)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The posted-price meeting (K-73)".
**Depends on**: S1.301 (trees, zone factors, cheapest), S1.160 (want buckets and the meeting's per-worker scratch),
S1.161 (the buffers' lives in the day plan), S1.164 (the sum-tree), S1.170 (sale items scattered by seller range),
S1.169 (chunk plans for meeting jobs), S1.271 (a stall's capacity from free units, `holding_of`), S1.289 (production
owed to the day, `pending`).
**Goal**: a region's buyers of a product meet its stalls in rounds: each buyer draws a zone from its own zone's
distance-weighted cumulative and a stall from that zone's tree, with its own taste (REP.22), each seller serves those
who came in an order drawn by lot until its capacity runs out, and the rest choose again; a round costs in proportion
to its buyers, a sold-out stall leaves its tree in O(log n), and each sale is an 8 B item in its seller's range.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/meet.rs` | rewritten: `meet(instance job, wants, book, tastes, lots, out)` over the trees |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/wants.rs` | want segments per (chunk, instance), 10 B SoA (buyer, zone, amount; wide amounts and limit points aside) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/meet_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/retail.rs` | -F driver `fin.retail` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.retail]` `match_ns` 19.1, `work_per_sale` 4, `buffer_mb` 102; `[fin.kept] purchase_ns` removed |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The posted-price meeting (K-73)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carriers of MKT.6, MKT.16, MKT.17 (done at S0.18) and SRV.4, SRV.5 (done at S1.06) stay on the
  rewritten kernel.
- **Wants** (5b): a budget of money (HH.5's rest) or a quantity needed (HH.20) priced at its rule's limit point, so
  every want is money its buyer reserves at 5d (S1.309's till): buyer `PartyId` u32, zone u16 (REP.24), amount u32 —
  10 B SoA, the product and region being the segment's instance; an amount beyond 2³² and a quantity's limit point live
  in a sparse side list (no bound, no stop). A chunk's 5b handler writes its wants by instance in ascending order (a
  chunk-local counting placement); a job is one instance, its segments read in chunk order; jobs run in ascending
  instance order, so the pages behind the slowest running job return to the K-03 pool and the day's items are written
  into them: wants and items never exceed the wants' bytes plus the jobs in flight.
- **Round.** Each buyer still choosing draws two uniforms from its own stream (the kind's taste stream, addressed by
  (buyer, day, stage, round block); `Draws::x4` four at a time): its zone, `u₁ × C_b` over its zone b's cumulative
  (S1.301's `cumulative`, built once per (instance, buyer zone, round) where a buyer of that zone chooses and a total
  changed; f64 running sums over integer totals in zone order, never maintained, so deterministic), a binary search
  over ≈ 40 zones; its stall, `find` in that zone's tree at `⌊u₂ × total⌋`, then ≤ 8 positions scanned. The two stages
  give each stall the logit's chance `e^(−α ln p − γ km)` over the region's open stalls (Gumbel tastes: multinomial
  logit exactly, REP.22).
- **Affordability.** A budget buys only where a unit's price is within it (`units_wanted`), a quantity only at or below
  its limit point; a draw it cannot afford is rejected and both draws are made again (rejection keeps the logit
  conditional on the affordable set exact); after `REJECTS_BEFORE_SCAN` rejections (a kernel constant of
  representation, 4) the affordable weights of each zone are summed by a scan of the instance's blocks and the draw is
  made over them exactly; scans are counted (`fin.retail.ceiling_scans`).
- **Serve** (MKT.6, SRV.5, REP.22): the round's choices are counted per chosen stall (a count column over the
  instance's positions); a stall whose capacity covers its demand serves all in that pass; only stalls demanded beyond
  capacity have their buyers grouped (8-bit radix on position). A stall's first touch reads its capacity as a
  `Covered<Qty>` (the cover taken at the meeting, S1.278): the seller's free units (`holding_of`) with the production
  owed to the day (`pending`), consumed by the day's batch, or a service's capacity for the day (placeholder: today's
  `way_most` computation of the maker's day, retired by S1.325). Beyond capacity, buyers are served one at a time in an
  order drawn by lot (the kind's capacity-lot stream, addressed by (seller, round)) from their order by who they are;
  a buyer served short chooses again; a stall sold out or found empty is closed in its tree (S1.301).
- **Out.** Each sale is an 8 B item (stall u32, units u32; wider units in the side list; its buyer authorised and named
  by its want) into the job's seller-range buffers (K-12, 11-bit ranges). A leaving buyer's paid sum (`retail::paid`)
  goes as a 12 B spend item into buyer-range buffers, flush-applied into the per-household spend accumulator (a range's
  slice ≈ 38 KB, cache-resident). Print sums (Σ price × units at posted prices, i128; Σ units; count) accrue as it
  serves (S1.326). A buyer left with nothing it can buy goes without (MKT.10), nothing added to clear (MKT.17).
- **Scratch**: per worker, not per job or chunk: `left` and the touched bitmap over the running instance's positions,
  choosing records (32 B a buyer still choosing), zone cumulatives — ≤ 2 MiB a worker at the largest instance.
- Retires `[fin.kept] purchase_ns` (S1.119), replaced by `[fin.retail]`.
- **Measurement**: `ExecCounters::visited` (stalls touched, positions scanned); `meeting_work_per_sale` (≤ 4); rounds
  and rejections per instance in the trace.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no open stall in the region, or only unaffordable ones: the want goes unserved, recorded (MKT.10) —
  `no_stall_unserved`; a stall no buyer chose is never visited — `unchosen_stall_untouched`.
- E5: payday shopping at its heaviest day's buckets; rounds ∝ buyers — `rounds_scale_with_buyers`.
- E7: the same sales for any workers and any order of wants within a bucket — `same_sales_any_order`.
- E10: a seller ended since posting has no stall in the book — `withdraw_leaves_tree` (S1.301).
- E11: day one's meeting reads the stalls day zero posted — `day_zero_rows_stand` (S1.296).
- E14: a buyer served short chooses again only in the next round — `served_by_lot_then_rechoose`.

**Extension points**: S1.307, S1.308, S1.309, S1.424, S1.445, S1.448, S1.473, S2.148, S2.159.
**Unit tests**: `choice_frequencies_match_logit` (a hand-built book of a few stalls, arithmetic over many buyers),
`distance_weighs_zones`, `served_by_lot_then_rechoose`, `affordable_only_for_money`, `rejection_scan_exact`,
`sold_out_leaves_tree`, `no_stall_unserved`, `unchosen_stall_untouched`, `same_sales_any_order`,
`rounds_scale_with_buyers`, `pages_recycled_behind_frontier`, `spend_is_sum_of_paid`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-160 — each day, units bought equal units sold per match and every sale at a posted point
(MKT.13, REP.34); LC-1-162 — each day, every unserved want and failed meeting recorded per instance (MKT.10).
**Budget**: 6.75 M purchases B, NB and H at match 21 phone-ns (VM 19.1, k 1.1: want read 1, draws 3, zone 4, stall 5,
count and serve 2.5, item 1.5, spend item 1 ≈ 18; the chunk-local placement is inside fin.decide.spend_ns) —
`fin.retail.match_ns` 19.1 within `fin.retail.all_in_ns` 26.8 (S1.309), `work_per_sale` ≤ 4, misses ≤ 0.15 an item. Day
buffers (ledger line 21, the 6a live set): +67.5 MB (wants 6.75 M × 10 B, their pages recycled into the 8 B items; the
zone column is the 13.5 MB REP.24's distance adds); +16 MB (meeting scratch, ≤ 2 MiB × ≤ 8 workers); +18 MB (spend
accumulator, 2.2 M × 8 B) — `fin.retail.buffer_mb` 102. Traversal: one job per instance on the pool, in ascending
instance order, chunked by declared cost (K-11).
**Guards**: `phx_market::meet` on PC-92's hot list; no allocation in the kernel after warm-up (PC-99).
**Not allowed**: an alias table or weight table rebuilt per round or per sold-out place; a pass over every stall; a
stored quantity per stall; a taste drawn per seller; a buyer or seller of last resort; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel, want segments and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F retail` within `fin.retail.match_ns`, `work_per_sale`, `buffer_mb`, on B, NB and H.
- [ ] §7.11 "The posted-price meeting (K-73)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.307 — The between-firm meeting on price levels from the stall book

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Between firms (K-75)".
**Depends on**: S1.301 (open points per instance), S1.164 (count sum-trees), S1.306 (first-touch capacity, items,
print sums and the per-worker scratch).
**Goal**: firms, the state and investors buy at posted list prices from the same stalls: buyers' steps in an order
drawn by lot take from the cheapest level at or below their limit, a level's sellers drawn by lot, and a sold-out
seller leaves its level in O(log n) so no step walks it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/between.rs` | levels from the book's open points; a level's sellers in a count sum-tree |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/between_tests.rs` | unit tests (from `between.rs`'s three) |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/b2b.rs` | -F driver `fin.b2b` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.b2b]` `match_ns` 30 (added), `buffer_mb` 40 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Between firms (K-75)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carriers of MKT.6, MKT.9, MKT.10, MKT.16, MKT.17 (done at S0.18) and GDS.7 (done at S1.05) stay on
  the kernel.
- A job is one instance, met before its retail kind (K-21's declared order within 6a) on the same per-worker scratch,
  so a stall's capacity left after the between-firm meeting is what retail meets.
- Levels: the instance's open points, taken from its goods' trees and sorted once per meeting (≈ 270 stalls an
  instance at the design point); each level a K-05 count tree over its sellers with capacity.
- Buyers' steps — buyer u32, limit `PointWord` u32, units u32 (12 B; units beyond 2³² in a sparse wide list; both sides
  trade in the instance's declared lot, MKT.21) — are taken in an order drawn by lot (addressed by (instance, day)),
  highest limit first; each takes from the cheapest level at or below its limit, the level's sellers drawn by lot
  through the count tree, in whole lots; a seller whose capacity runs out leaves the level (one count delta); what no
  level serves goes unserved (MKT.10).
- Out: 12 B items (buyer u32, stall u32, units u32; wide units aside) into seller-range buffers; print sums as
  S1.306's.
- Measurement: `ExecCounters::visited` (levels and sellers drawn).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no level at or below a buyer's limit: its step goes unserved — `between_unserved_recorded`.
- E7: buyer order and level order by lot — `between_same_any_workers`.
- E14: one seller's between-firm and retail sales of one good share one capacity — `retail_meets_what_is_left`.

**Extension points**: S1.308, S1.309, S5.130.
**Unit tests**: `between_cheapest_level_first`, `between_level_by_lot`, `between_unserved_recorded`,
`between_same_any_workers`, `retail_meets_what_is_left`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-160 (S1.306's) each business day.
**Budget**: 3.3 M / 0.3 M / 3.3 M purchases at ≤ 30 ns VM a purchase (`fin.b2b.match_ns` 30, added), within
`fin.b2b.purchase_ns` 50 all in (S1.309). Day buffers (ledger line 21, the 6a live set): +39.6 MB (between-firm steps
3.3 M × 12 B, their pages recycled into the 12 B items) — `fin.b2b.buffer_mb` 40.
**Guards**: `phx_market::between` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a walk over a sold-out seller; a level rebuilt per step; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel change and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F b2b` within `fin.b2b.match_ns` and `buffer_mb`, on B, NB and H.
- [ ] §7.11 "Between firms (K-75)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.308 — The world's purchases onto the meetings

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The posted-price meeting (K-73)" and "Between firms (K-75)".
**Depends on**: S1.306 (the retail meeting), S1.307 (the between-firm meeting), S1.303 (stalls from the book).
**Goal**: every purchase the world makes — households', the state's, investment's, firms' inputs and services — meets
through K-73 and K-75 by instance jobs; the per-call want vectors are gone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `by_product_of` deleted; `meet_all` and its five callers route instance jobs; the `consumption.clone()` and per-product `places` gone |

| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | the sites this step removes |

- The spending, state, investment, input and services wants are written into the 5b want segments (S1.306's form)
  by their handlers today; `meet_all`'s calls become one routed pass of instance jobs.

  `PC-99.toml` (`sales().copied().collect()`, per-call `Vec`s).

**Budget**: removes `goods.buyers`' 1.5 s counting sort and `meet_all`'s per-call tables. Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p
5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows the purchases' spans within fin.retail.all_in_ns and fin.b2b.purchase_ns at the committed
resolution.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.

allocation per day.

### S1.309 — The sale as its payment: seller-range sweep and the (seller, good) batch

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Sales batch and delivery (K-74)"; follows §4 (stage 6b).
**Depends on**: S1.306 (the sale items), S1.307 (between-firm items), S1.301 (reopening at the batch), S1.240
(accounts' `pending` and `available`), S1.245 (commit mode and `ShardCredits`), S1.253 (levies fused), S1.254 (flow
tallies), S1.269 (on-account accrual into invoice rows), S1.271 (holdings' batch moves), S1.276 (lots: cost of what is
sold), S1.289 (production realised in the batch), S1.170 (apply by seller range and the sweep's hooks).
**Goal**: a sale is its own payment (SET.13; MON.5, E 26: netted, every payer and payee named): one sweep per seller
range adds each sale's revenue, units, tax, tally and the payee's credit into `pending`; each buyer's day spend is
debited once; each (seller, good) closes its day in one batch — production realised, one stock move, cost of sales
rounded once, delivery; a retail purchase is authorised at the till before delivery.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/sales/mod.rs` | `SalesDay`: shards, the seller sweep (generic over the sweep's hooks), the buyer sweep |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/sales/batch.rs` | the (seller, good) batch close |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/sales/tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/batches.rs` | -F driver `fin.batches`; `fin.retail` apply and all-in |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.retail]` `apply_ns` 7.7, `all_in_ns` 26.8; `[fin.b2b]` `purchase_ns` 50; `[fin.batches]` `batch_ns` 26.9 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Sales batch and delivery (K-74)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carrier of GDS.2 (done at S1.05) moves here.
- **Sale mode** per market kind (K-21 data, read once per job, never per sale): **cash** — the item is the money flow;
  **on account** (TCR.1) — no money leg, the amount accrues to the (seller, buyer) invoice row (K-59 `accrue`, the row
  found by binary search in the buyer's once-a-day sorted rows, written only from the seller's range).
- **Seller sweep** (6b, apply by seller range, ≤ 4 800 sellers a shard, items sorted by stall so the sellers' records
  stream in order, R12): per item, the stall resolves to seller, point and good; `paid = retail::paid(units,
  price(point), lot)` rounded once (REP.9); the reason's levy set fused (K-51: a sales tax rounded per sale); the
  seller's hot record gains the day's units and revenue and its sales since review (the attention trigger's fact, the
  test S1.351's); the flow tallies posted once, in K-52 only (K-39 reads K-52 at its period close); cash mode: the
  payee's `pending` += paid (K-47). Effects of higher crates (K-87's lines, K-88's `beside`) go through the sweep's hook
  parameter (`H: SweepHooks`, S1.170, composed by `phx-world`'s routing), so `phx-market` never calls `phx-acct`; until
  S1.328 the hook calls today's `recognise` once per (seller, good) batch (placeholder, retired by S1.329).
- **Buyer sweep** (6b, by buyer range, over the households that bought today — a K-07 change set): each household's
  day spend in the accumulator (S1.306's flushed spend items) is debited once — from the buyer party's own account
  until S1.406's split to persons (E 48); between-firm items scattered by buyer range put the units into the buyer's
  inline input stock at what it paid (K-60 `receive_batch`). A household's purchase is used up (SET.9's consumption,
  naming the buyer, in the batch's legs).
- **Batch** (6b end, per (seller, good) with sales): K-68 realises production to the day, one K-60 `deliver_batch` of
  the units sold, cost of sales from its lots (K-62: FIFO or average, the firm's choice, ACC.6) rounded once per batch
  by its convention (REP.9; no spec text changes), the gains tally where the reason declares one (S1.276), and the
  stall's reopening for tomorrow decided in the same apply (S1.301).
- **The till** (Law 1; TIME.8; commit mode, S1.245, S1.252): a buyer's retail and service wants of the day are its
  authorisation — the spending view that sizes them holds its persons' `available = balance + limit + min(pending, 0)`
  (K-47), and the reservation is fused into that view (S1.406's) and expires with the day's `pending` commit; a want
  beyond `available` is refused there, visibly (reason `Payer`), before any meeting. A purchase within its want is
  authorised whatever order the meetings run in and debited once at 6b; retail buyers are never short at 7b; on a
  non-business day the debit is the commitment to the next business day.
- **Retention**: retail items (8 B × 6.75 M) live from 6a to the seller sweep and are released there; between-firm items
  live until the close on business days (S1.310's source). Flush-applying the seller side would touch a range's ≈ 4 800
  sellers' records at random (≈ 1 miss an item against 0.15), so it keeps the range sweep; only the buyers' 12 B spend
  items are flush-applied.
- **Measurement**: `ExecCounters::visited` per shard; `StoreStats` of the day buffers.
- **Replaces** (users moved at S1.311): `book_sale` (`core_goods.rs`), `deliver_sales`, `note_sold`
  (`core_plant.rs`), per-delivery `recognise` ×3.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a seller with no sale has no batch and is not visited — `no_sale_no_batch`.
- E3: a buyer with no money: its retail wants are refused before any meeting, any day — `want_beyond_available_refused`.
- E5: payday: 10 M items at the seller sweep's unit — `payday_items_at_unit` (-F on H).
- E7: shard sums are integers, order-free — `same_books_any_workers`.
- E8: a day's revenue per seller beyond i64 stops the run; world totals i128 — `revenue_beyond_i64_stops`.
- E14: one seller's retail and between-firm sales of one good close in one batch — `one_batch_per_seller_good`.

**Extension points**: S1.310, S1.311, S1.351, S1.424, S1.453, S2.111, S5.105, S5.108.
**Unit tests**: `mass_short_reversal_by_range`, `paid_rounded_once_per_sale`, `tax_fused_per_sale`, `cost_rounded_once_per_batch`,
`on_account_accrues_no_flow`, `spend_debited_once_per_household`, `want_beyond_available_refused`,
`retail_never_short_at_7b`, `same_books_any_workers`, `no_sale_no_batch`, `payday_items_at_unit`,
`revenue_beyond_i64_stops`, `one_batch_per_seller_good`, `tallies_posted_once_in_k52`, `hooks_post_lines`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-160 and LC-1-32 (every household payment reaches named sellers) each day; LC-0-09 (every close
ran every declared family — Money, Units, Flows — and found nothing) each day.
**Budget**: seller-shard apply 10.05 M / 7.05 M / 10.05 M items at 10 phone-ns (`fin.retail.apply_ns` 7.7 VM); retail
all in 31 phone-ns (`fin.retail.all_in_ns` 26.8: match 19.1 + apply 7.7 — item gather sorted by stall 2, paid and tax
2, seller adds 1.5, `pending` 1, tally 0.5, batch share 0.7); between-firm all in 60 (`fin.b2b.purchase_ns` 50);
batches 1.2 M / 0.9 M / 1.2 M at 35 phone-ns (`fin.batches.batch_ns` 26.9, production and reopening inside it). The
buyer sweep adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.spend_ns at 472 k / 472 k / 472 k items (one debit a household, inside the
occasion's 215 with S1.406's reservation). ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 MB at the 6a live set (S1.306's and
S1.307's 141.1 MB hold the items); after 6b +39.6 MB (between-firm items to the close).
**Guards**: the batch API is the only public mutator (R6, compile level); `recognise` not callable per item.
**Not allowed**: a per-sale delivery, cover or record word; a value-keyed failure map; a per-item income call; an
allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The sweeps, batches, modes, hooks and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F retail,b2b,batches` at the design point within `fin.retail.apply_ns`, `all_in_ns`,
  `fin.b2b.purchase_ns`, `fin.batches.batch_ns`, B, NB and H.
- [ ] §7.11 "Sales batch and delivery (K-74)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.310 — Failed between-firm sales reversed before the close

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Sales reversed (K-74)"; follows §4 (stage 7b).
**Depends on**: S1.309 (the retained between-firm items and batches), S1.248 (short payers re-derived at 7b, outcome by
place).
**Goal**: a between-firm buyer short in stage 7 has its cash purchases re-derived in its payment order, and each failed
sale is undone before the close — units and their cost back to the seller, revenue, tax and the payee's credit reversed,
the fail recorded with its cause — so SET.4 holds at the close.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/sales/reverse.rs` | `reverse(outcome, items, hooks)`: reversal batches by seller range |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/sales/reverse_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/batches.rs` | the reversal driver (E1's day) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Sales reversed (K-74)" |

**Design**:
- At 7b K-49 re-derives a short payer's items in its payment order (MON.5) from their places in the seller shards;
  each failed between-firm cash item is handed to `reverse` by place.
- Reversal per seller range, one batch per (seller, good): the units and the cost they left with return to the
  seller's holding (K-60 `receive_batch` at their lots' cost, K-62), the buyer's received units leave its inline stock,
  revenue, the sales tax (K-51, reversed as it was rounded) and the payee's `pending` credit are taken back, K-52's flow
  tallies reversed by place, the lines through the sweep's hooks; the fail is recorded with its cause (SET.3) and the
  contract's consequence follows its rule (S2.114).
- Retail never reaches here (authorised at the till, S1.309); an on-account sale has no money leg to fail.
- **Measurement**: reversals counted per cause; `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a bank failing leaves many firm buyers short: reversals by seller range on the pool —
  `mass_short_reversal_by_range`.
- E3: a between-firm buyer with no money: every cash purchase of the day fails and is reversed —
  `failed_sale_reversed_units_and_cost`.
- E7: reversals are integer sums by range — `reversal_same_any_workers`.
- E14: a seller whose several buyers fail the same day: one reversal batch per (seller, good) —
  `one_reversal_batch_per_seller_good`.

**Extension points**: S1.311.
**Unit tests**: `failed_sale_reversed_units_and_cost`, `mass_short_reversal_by_range`, `reversal_same_any_workers`,
`one_reversal_batch_per_seller_good`, `tallies_reversed_by_place`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-22 (settlement values) and LC-0-09 each business day.
**Budget**: unit ≤ 50 phone-ns a reversed item (38.5 VM, as `fin.settle.short_ns`); design count ≤ 20 k / 0 / 150 k
items (B / NB / H: the short payers' between-firm items), inside fin.fixed.fixed_point's re-derivation (S1.248's
share). ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (the items S1.309 keeps).
**Guards**: `reverse` is reached only from K-49's outcome (compile level).
**Not allowed**: a reversal of a settled instruction (SET.5: only a failed one is undone before the close); a
value-keyed failure map; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The reversal and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F batches -D H` within `fin.settle.short_ns`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Sales reversed (K-74)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.311 — Booking and delivery onto the sales batch

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "Sales batch and delivery (K-74)".
**Depends on**: S1.309 (the sales batch), S1.310 (reversals), S1.278 (cover and pledges on liens), S1.270 (taxes at
emission); S1.249 (failed sales read by place; today's release, which moves here).
**Goal**: the world's sales are booked, paid and delivered only through K-74; the per-sale booking, the deliveries
list, the value-keyed failure matching and the per-delivery recognition are gone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `book_sale`, `deliveries`, `deliver_sales` (its failure map and two `Stocks::totals`) deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_plant.rs` | `note_sold` deleted; plant sales read the seller's day units |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_accounts.rs` | per-delivery `recognise` calls removed (one per batch, S1.309's placeholder) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day.rs` | 6b and 7b routed to K-74 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-99.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- Every `meet_all` caller's sales go to K-74's shards; `arise_tax` per sale ends (K-51 fused, S1.270); `cover_sale →
  Stocks::bind` ends (the meeting's first touch covers).
- 7b's failures are K-49's outcome by place; the value-keyed `unpaid` lookup is gone.
- Services' delivery as made: a service's batch delivers the day's sales of it; unsold capacity perishes by
  construction (S1.325).
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (the failure `BTreeMap`, `traded`'s write per sale) and `PC-99.toml`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a bank failure day with many short firm buyers: reversals by seller range — `mass_short_reversal_by_range`
  (S1.309).
- E6: nothing of the day's sales is saved (instructions die at the close, SET.13) — LC-0-35 (every save reads back to
  its close's world hash).

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: none new (S1.309's); the world's audit reads the Units and Money families (LC-0-09).
**Live checks**: LC-1-160, LC-1-32 and LC-0-09 each day.
**Budget**: removes the 5 M bench's booking (2.7 s) and delivering (2.0 s) spans. Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d
1 -t 300` shows `goods.book` and `settle.deliver` replaced by K-74's spans within their `[fin.fixed]` rows.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a second record of a sale.

### S1.312 — The call auction

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The call auction (K-76)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (orders as offers), S1.298 (the admission hook), S1.172 (apportionment with a named residue),
S1.160 (the day's order buffers).
**Goal**: one kernel meets every market that meets at a moment (MKT.3): schedules aggregated by exact sums per price
level, one price where posted supply meets posted demand, the quantity rationed at it by the market's declared rule,
ties by lot; declared variants cover issues, buybacks, tenders, book-builds, closing calls and default lots; unfilled
quantity is not issued, an event, never absorbed.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/call.rs` | `call(instance, orders, variant, lots, out)` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/call_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/call.rs` | -F driver `fin.call` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.call]` `order_ns` 130 (all in, the call's fixed cost included), `call_us` 3 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The call auction (K-76)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carrier of MKT.3 (done at S0.18) moves here.
- **Orders**: participant u32, side, limit price in ticks (i64 on the instance's tick grid, MKT.21; negative where the
  market allows, ENE.8), quantity i64 in the instance's lots (a sell side `Covered<Qty>`), priority class u8 where the
  variant declares classes; day orders in the day's buffers, standing ones K-70 rows. Every order is its poster's
  limit (MKT.16); no order is "whatever is left at any price" (MKT.17).
- **Schedules**: orders radix-sorted by tick; cumulative demand D(p) (bids at or above p) and supply S(p) (asks at or
  below p) as exact integer sums per level (Law 11: every household's bid counts as itself, SOV.4).
- **Price**: the level maximising min(D, S); where several do, the market's declared tie rule (POLICY of its operator,
  MKT.21: e.g. the least imbalance, then the level nearest the last print) chooses; no cross → no print, the failure
  recorded (MKT.10).
- **Rationing** at the price, per the variant's declared rule: pro rata in whole lots by largest remainder (K-16's
  `apportion`, residue by lot on the market's stream addressed by (instance, day)) or priority (class, then time, then
  lot).
- **Variants** (declared data, K-21): two-sided call (commodity sessions, interbank sessions, the closing call of a
  book, MKT.4); issue — the issuer's sell order is its own offered quantity at its own reserve (SOV.6: it may cut the
  size; what is not sold is not issued, a K-36 event); reverse (buybacks, tenders with the buyer's quantity);
  book-built with an underwriter's commitment as its own order; default lots (DRV). Uniform price or own price paid,
  declared per variant.
- **Out**: fills as items to K-74's apply or to K-50 commitments on the market's settlement convention (SET.2); the
  print (price, quantity, form) and depth to K-86 (S1.326).
- Complexity O(n) radix plus O(levels); one call per instance on the pool.
- **Measurement**: `ExecCounters::visited` (orders), calls and failures per kind in the trace.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: bids with no offer, offers with no bid, no overlap: no print, a recorded failure; an issue with no bid is not
  issued — `no_cross_no_print`, `issue_unsold_not_issued`.
- E7: rationing's residue by lot addressed by (instance, day) — `same_allotment_any_order`.
- E8: sums in i128 per level; a quantity beyond i64 stops the run — `quantity_beyond_i64_stops`.
- E12: a missing reference print leaves the tie rule's next criterion or a refusal, never a zero —
  `missing_reference_not_zero`.
- E14: one participant's bid and offer at one call: fills that only net its own orders are refused (`OwnOrders`) —
  `own_orders_refused`.

**Extension points**: S1.313, S1.314, S1.315, S1.316, S2.155, S2.157, S3.121, S3.125, S3.135, S3.168, S4.112, S4.119,
S4.163, S5.163. A new variant is declared data.
**Unit tests**: `price_maximises_volume`, `tie_rule_declared`, `pro_rata_largest_remainder`, `priority_rationing`,
`no_cross_no_print`, `issue_unsold_not_issued`, `same_allotment_any_order`, `own_orders_refused`,
`quantity_beyond_i64_stops`, `missing_reference_not_zero`.
**Live checks**: none (its users').
**Budget**: 4.5 k calls and 0.2 M orders (B), 6 k and 0.3 M (H), 0 (NB); ≤ 130 ns VM an order all in — the radix, the
schedules and each call's fixed cost (≤ 3 µs, `call_us` 3) spread over its orders are counted inside the order count
(`fin.call.order_ns` 130; with S1.298's 20 ns admission, fin.fixed.securities' 150 an order); design count 0.2 M / 0 /
0.3 M orders (B / NB / H) in 4.5 k / 0 / 6 k calls, ≤ 10⁵ orders in one call. The users carry the shares (count × unit).
ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (orders in the decided intents' buffers).
**Guards**: `phx_market::call` on PC-92's hot list (the dead `call.rs` entry becomes live).
**Not allowed**: a float price; an absorber of unsold quantity; a residue dropped.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F call` at the design point within `fin.call.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "The call auction (K-76)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.313 — The bill auction onto the call auction

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The call auction (K-76)".
**Depends on**: S1.312 (the call auction), S1.282 (bills as instruments with holdings and events).
**Goal**: the sovereign's bill auction is an issue variant of K-76: banks' bids are orders on the bill's tick grid,
the treasury's offered face its own sell order, rationing at the price by largest remainder with a named residue,
unsold face not issued as an event; the hand-written f64 clearing is gone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules.rs` | `clear` deleted; `size` and `bid` stay rules, emitting order intents |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/kinds.rs` | `Bid`, `Allotment` (f64 prices) deleted; `BillKind::clear` removed |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_bills.rs` | `auctions`: bids and the offer posted as K-76 orders at 5b/5d, met at 6a |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/declare.rs` | the bill market kind: form call, variant issue, uniform price, pro rata, tick grid |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-99.toml`, `PC-100.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- A bill's market instance is its issue (`InstrumentId`, S1.282); its kind declares the call's issue variant, uniform
  price, pro-rata rationing and the tick grid (POLICY of the treasury as operator, MKT.21).
- `sys_sov::rules::bid` returns steps in ticks and whole bills (no `floor_to_i64(...).unwrap_or(0)`); the treasury's
  size is its sell order at its own reserve (SOV.6: it may cut the size); orders pass K-70's admission.
- The defect fixed: `clear`'s pro-rata truncation left demanded face neither allotted nor named (MON.16);
  K-76's largest remainder allots it with the residue by lot. Its f64 price becomes the tick price.
- Fills settle as holdings of the issue (K-65) on the bill's convention; the print and the cover stay today's auction record in
  `core_bills.rs` until S1.327 moves them onto K-86;
  the unsold face is a K-36 event ("not issued").
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-99.toml` (`Vec<Bid>` per auction) and `PC-100.toml` (`unwrap_or(0)` on bids).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no bid: no print, the auction's failure recorded, nothing issued — `no_bid_nothing_issued` (logic level over the
  rule's orders).
- E8: face beyond i64 stops the run — `quantity_beyond_i64_stops` (S1.312).

**Extension points**: bond auctions and the treasury's answer to a failed auction (S3.121, S3.122) use the same kind
with other variants.
**Unit tests**: `bids_in_ticks_and_whole_bills`, `no_bid_nothing_issued`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-31 (auctions held, bills issued and redeemed, debt read from the register) on auction days.
**Budget**: ≤ 3 auctions a week per country; negligible. Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` unchanged
within its lines.
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses an f64 price in `if-state`'s bill types (deleted).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a clearing written in a system.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, kind, routing, tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench unchanged within its lines; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.314 — The network call: a transport model over lines

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: ENE.8 PROCESS *(part: one call across a grid's regions, a price per region subject to each line's capacity
between the two regions it joins, negative prices; the market's declarations and generators' offers are Stage 2's)*;
MMK.6 PROCESS *(part: the linked call's clearing; the money market's kinds are Stage 3's)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The network call (K-77)".
**Depends on**: S1.312 (the call's orders, tie rules and rationing), S1.187 (lines as segments with capacity),
S1.188 (the day's use of lines and segments).
**Goal**: one kernel clears a call over declared nodes joined by capacitated links, maximising the surplus of the posted
steps, as one min-cost flow per country and day with every block a separate commodity of the same network: where no
link binds, nodes share a price; a congested link leaves two prices; prices may be negative; the result is the same for
any starting basis, so the warm start from yesterday's basis only saves time.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/network.rs` | `network_call(country, nodes, links, blocks, orders, rules, basis, out)`: network simplex, canonical outputs |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/network_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/call.rs` | the network driver in `fin.call` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.call]` `network_ms` 3 (added: one country's call, both blocks, warm-started, VM) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The network call (K-77)" |

**Design**:
- **Model** (ENE.8: a transport model): nodes are a grid's regions (≈ 8 a country; for the linked call, the declared
  markets); a link joins two nodes and carries up to its capacity in either direction (the line's capacity that day
  from K-26: a closure or a catastrophe lowers it). Offers and bids are steps (price in ticks, i64, negative allowed;
  quantity in whole lots) at a node and a block.
- **One flow per country and day.** The declared blocks (peak, off-peak: separate products delivered the same day) are
  separate commodities of one network: each block's subgraph shares the country's nodes and links but not their
  capacity (a line's capacity is per block, ENE.8), so the blocks decouple and are solved as disjoint components of one
  min-cost flow in one call — one setup, one basis, one pass over the orders.
- **Clearing**: maximise Σ accepted bids' value − Σ accepted offers' cost subject to each node's balance and each link's
  capacity — source → offer steps at their price; links at no cost within capacity; bid steps at minus their price →
  sink — by network simplex over integer lots with a candidate-list pricing rule. Node prices are its potentials on the
  tick grid.
- **Warm start**: yesterday's basis (per country, derived scratch, ≈ 20 k arcs) seeds today's; the arcs of changed steps
  are re-priced; after a load the first day starts cold. ≈ 25 nodes and 20 k arcs: a warm call is a few hundred pivots.
- **Canonical result**: prices — where a node's potential is a range, the market's declared tie rule (as K-76) picks the
  tick; quantities — steps strictly in the money filled, marginal steps rationed by the declared rule (largest
  remainder, lot for the residue); link flows — the least-index feasible flow of the resulting net positions (a small
  max-flow over the nodes, deterministic order). So a warm and a cold start give the same world (E6).
- **Out**: each node's and block's print (price, volume) to K-86; fills as K-50 commitments on the market's convention
  (non-business days settle on the next business day, ENE.8); congestion rents (price difference × flow) as the link
  owner's amount, read by S2.210's rule; bids no offer can reach are unfilled (ENE.9's shedding is S2.211's) and the failure
  recorded (MKT.10).
- **Measurement**: pivots and time per call in the trace; `ExecCounters::visited` (steps and links).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a node with no offer reached by no link: its bids unfilled, no print there — `unreached_node_no_print`.
- E5: electricity meets every day including non-business days (TIME.8) — `nb_call_same_cost` (-F on NB).
- E6/E7: outputs canonical whatever the basis and workers — `warm_and_cold_start_agree`.
- E8: surplus sums in i128; lots beyond i64 stop the run — `lots_beyond_i64_stop`.
- E12: a line whose capacity is not declared is not a link (never capacity 0 or infinite by default) —
  `undeclared_capacity_refused`.

**Extension points**: S2.209 (the wholesale electricity market: kinds, generators' offers ENE.5, imbalance ENE.10),
S3.101 (the money market's linked call with the central bank's tenders at stage 8, MMK.6, CB.14); an interconnector between
countries is one more declared link.
**Unit tests**: `no_binding_line_one_price`, `congested_line_two_prices`, `negative_price_when_must_run_exceeds`,
`surplus_is_maximal` (a hand-built three-node case against brute force), `blocks_are_independent_commodities`,
`warm_and_cold_start_agree`, `marginal_step_rationed_by_rule`, `unreached_node_no_print`, `lots_beyond_i64_stop`,
`undeclared_capacity_refused`, `nb_call_same_cost`.
**Live checks**: none (S2.209's).
**Budget**: ≈ 20 k offer and bid steps and links per country per day, both blocks, every day (B, NB, H), ≤ 3 ms VM a
country's call warm-started (`fin.call.network_ms` 3, added; k = 1.0); design count 3 / 3 / 3 calls a day (B / NB / H:
one a country, both blocks), and 3 linked calls a business day at stage 8 (S3.101). The users carry the shares: S2.209
on fin.fixed.calls (3 × 3 ms = 9 / 9 / 9 core-ms), S3.101 on fin.fixed.fund. ledger line 17 (markets): +2 MB resident
(links and the three countries' bases, 60 k arcs × 32 B).
**Guards**: `phx_market::network` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a flow-based (transfer distribution) model; a price floor or cap; a result that depends on the
starting basis; a call per block; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F call` within `fin.call.network_ms`, on B and NB.
- [ ] §7.11 "The network call (K-77)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.315 — The continuous book with its closing call

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: MKT.4 PROCESS
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The continuous book (K-78)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (standing orders), S1.298 (admission), S1.176 (the day's arrival order drawn on a named
stream), S1.312 (the closing call).
**Goal**: limit orders rest in price-then-time priority; the day's orders arrive in an order drawn by lot and an
incoming order that crosses trades at the resting price; nobody reacts within the day; the book ends in a closing call
auction whose price is the day's close.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/book.rs` | `Book`: levels per side, FIFO per level, `arrive`, `close` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/book_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/book.rs` | -F driver `fin.book` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.book]` `order_ns` 130, `mb` 5 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The continuous book (K-78)" |

**Design**:
- **Resting orders** are K-70 standing-order rows (32 B: poster, instance, price ticks, quantity — a sell side
  `Covered<Qty>` —, side and generation, next in level). Per book side, levels sorted by price (price i64, total i64,
  head u32, tail u32 = 24 B), found by binary search; a level's orders a FIFO through `next`. A resting order is one
  level insert: a binary search over the side's levels (≈ 20 at the design point's 40 orders a book), an append at the
  level's tail, a new level shifting at most the side's levels — the book's rows and levels stay in L1 while its job
  runs. Orders by poster: a K-06 instance (8 B an order).
- **The day** (6a, per book on the pool): the day's admitted limit orders (5d, MKT.16: no market orders) arrive in an
  order drawn by lot (stream `MKT.arrival`, addressed by (instance, day)); each crosses resting orders of the other
  side at their prices, best level first, FIFO within a level, whole lots, until its limit or quantity ends; the rest
  rests (or lapses at the close if a day order). At-close orders wait for the close.
- **The close** (MKT.4, MKT.12): resting orders flagged for it and the at-close orders go to K-76's two-sided call
  (the operator's declared closing rule); its price is the day's close and the book's mark.
- **Out**: each trade an item to K-74's apply or a K-50 commitment on the market's convention (T+n, SET.2); each trade
  a print into K-86's day sums (and its individual print where a fixing method names the market).
- A crossing with the same poster on both sides is refused (no trade with oneself).
- **Measurement**: `ExecCounters::visited` (levels and orders touched); `StoreStats` (levels, orders).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a one-sided book trades nothing and its close forms no price: the last print shows its age (MKT.2, MKT.10) —
  `one_sided_no_close`.
- E5: a crash day's order flow (10⁵ orders on one book) at O(log levels) an order — `crash_day_orders_log_levels`.
- E7: arrival by lot keyed (instance, day) — `same_trades_any_workers`.
- E10: a poster that ends: its resting orders withdrawn through the by-poster instance (K-97) —
  `ending_withdraws_orders`.
- E11: day-zero orders stand into day one (GEN.13) — `day_zero_rows_stand` (S1.296).

**Extension points**: S3.145, S3.147, S4.116, S4.120, S4.121, S4.122.
**Unit tests**: `crosses_at_resting_price`, `price_then_time_priority`, `arrival_by_lot`, `close_is_call_price`,
`one_sided_no_close`, `no_trade_with_oneself`, `same_trades_any_workers`, `crash_day_orders_log_levels`,
`ending_withdraws_orders`.
**Live checks**: none (S3.147's).
**Budget**: 5 k books, 200 k resting orders; 0.2 M / 0 / 0.25 M orders a day at ≤ 130 ns VM an order, crossing included
(`fin.book.order_ns` 130; with S1.298's 20 ns admission, fin.fixed.securities' 150 an order); design count 0.2 M / 0 /
0.25 M orders (B / NB / H) on 5 k books; the closing call's cost is S1.312's unit. The users carry the shares (count ×
unit). ledger line 17 (markets): +4 MB resident (levels ≈ 100 k × 24 B, by-poster instance 200 k × 8 B; the orders' 6.4
MB are S1.296's) — `fin.book.mb` 5.
**Guards**: `phx_market::book` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a market order; a reaction within the day; a close from anything but the closing call.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F book` within `fin.book.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "The continuous book (K-78)" written; MKT.4's row in §13; the two reviews; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S1.316 — The dealer market

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: MKT.5 PROCESS; MKT.19 FORBID
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The dealer market (K-79)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (two-way quotes), S1.298 (admission), S1.312 (interdealer redistribution through a call).
**Goal**: dealers post two-way quotes from their own state; clients, in an order drawn by lot, ask the dealers in
their reach and take the best quote with size left; dealers trade with each other through a call; a dealer at a
binding limit quotes nothing, which clients see as a failed meeting; no spread is ever applied to a mid.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/dealer.rs` | `Quote` (constructible from two posted prices only), `rfq`, the interdealer order |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/dealer_tests.rs` | unit tests, compile-fail `no_mid_spread_constructor` |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/dealer.rs` | -F driver `fin.dealer` |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/mid_spread.rs` | PC-108 |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.dealer]` `quote_ns` 150, `mb` 1 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The dealer market (K-79)" |

**Design**:
- **Quotes** are K-70 two-way rows (dealer, instance, bid, ask, bid size, ask size — the ask size a `Covered<Qty>`
  from inventory), posted at 5d by the dealer's rule (DLR.4) from its inventory, funding and limits. `Quote::new(bid,
  ask, sizes)` is the only constructor: there is no type or function taking a mid and a spread or a spread table
  (MKT.19, compile level). A dealer whose limit binds (K-93 headroom handed to the admission hook) posts none.
- **Index**: quotes by instance (a K-06 instance, 8 B a quote), ≈ 4 dealers an instrument; a request reads its
  instance's run once (≈ 4 quotes, one cache line of refs and their rows) and takes the best with size by a scan, so a
  request costs a handful of loads, not a walk over the dealers. A quote is the dealer's standing state, reposted by
  its rule only when its inventory or the instrument's mark changes (DLR.4), never recomputed per request.
- **Requests** (6a, per instance on the pool): clients' requests (side, quantity, limit), admitted at 5d, taken in an
  order drawn by lot (the kind's stream, addressed by (instance, day)); each asks the dealers in its reach (declared
  per client kind: those it has a relationship with, or all quoting the instance) and takes the best price within its
  limit with size left, then the next, in whole lots; ties by lot; a quote's size falls as it trades. A client with no
  quote in reach or none within its limit fails visibly (MKT.10).
- **Interdealer**: dealers' orders to rebalance inventory go to a K-76 two-sided call of the instance (S3.168).
- **Out**: items to K-74's apply or K-50 commitments (T+n); prints to K-86, where a fixing method (MKT.20) takes the
  day's trades (S1.326's day prints).
- **Measurement**: `ExecCounters::visited` (quotes asked); requests failed per instance.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a crash day: dealers at their limits post none; requests fail visibly, never filled from nowhere (MKT.17) —
  `no_quote_fails`.
- E2: an instrument no dealer quotes: its requests fail — `no_quote_fails`.
- E7: request order by lot — `same_fills_any_workers`.
- E10: a dealer that ends: its quotes withdrawn (declared sweep of 50 k rows on that day) — `ending_withdraws_quotes`.

### S1.317 — The bilateral protocol

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: REP.22 PROCESS *(part: the asker's choice among lenders, insurers and counterparties by its taste)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The bilateral protocol (K-80)".
**Depends on**: S1.237 (typed messages with deadlines), S1.296 (market kinds and instances).
**Goal**: one protocol serves every negotiation between named parties: an asker asks one or several responders, each
answers from its own state or declines at a declared stage, and the asker accepts the one its taste and state make
best, counters or walks away; every step is a typed message with a deadline, so nothing is re-derived by hand in a
system.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/bilateral.rs` | message kinds, the thread, `ask`, `answer`, `choose`, `counter`, `walk` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/bilateral_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/bilateral.rs` | -F driver `fin.bilateral` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.bilateral]` `ask_ns` 500 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The bilateral protocol (K-80)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carrier of MKT.7 (done at S0.18) moves here.
- **Messages** (K-45): ask, quote, decline, accept, counter, walk — each naming the thread (a negotiation id u32 in
  the message), sender and addressee, its payload (terms interned through K-55, an amount, the asker's disclosed facts
  by reference) and its deadline: the stage and day the market kind declares for the answer (an answer issued at stage
  9 is due no earlier than the next business day, TIME.7). Unanswered messages lapse at 1b.
- **Ask** (the asker's decision, 5b/5c): to the responders in its reach (declared per kind: its bank, the lenders it
  deals with, insurers in its region, a failed bank's bidders), as many as its own rule chooses.
- **Answer** (at the declared stage, by responder range on the pool): each responder's rule (MKT.9) quotes or declines
  from its own state; the kernel only carries the answer.
- **Choose** (the asker, when its quotes are in or their deadline passes): among quotes, the one its taste makes best
  (REP.22: a taste per alternative drawn from its type's distribution on the kind's stream addressed by (asker, day)),
  or a counter, or a walk; accept opens the contract through its family (K-53) at the stage's apply; the others lapse.
- **Rounds** are bounded by deadlines the kind declares, never by a count invented in the kernel.
- **Measurement**: asks, answers, accepts, walks and lapses per kind; `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no responder in reach, or every one declines: a refusal recorded (MKT.10: "the borrower is refused") —
  `decline_all_is_refusal`.
- E7: answers by responder range, choices by asker range, tastes by address — `same_outcome_any_workers`.
- E10: a responder that ends mid-negotiation: its messages lapse (K-97 → K-45); an accept on a lapsed quote is refused
  by generation — `accept_on_lapsed_quote_refused`.
- E14: two quotes accepted by one asker the same day: one accept per thread (the second refused) —
  `one_accept_per_thread`.

**Extension points**: S1.318, S1.347, S2.103, S2.107, S2.115, S2.130, S2.151, S2.155, S2.183, S2.197, S2.198, S2.213,
S3.108, S3.124, S3.125, S3.133, S3.136, S3.138, S3.140, S3.152, S3.195, S8.110, S8.114, S4.102, S4.105, S4.114, S4.135,
S4.161, S4.173, S4.177, S4.178, S5.143, S5.182, S5.184, S6.110, S6.123. A new negotiation is a declared kind with its
message payloads and deadlines.
**Unit tests**: `ask_answer_accept_opens_contract`, `decline_all_is_refusal`, `choice_by_taste`,
`counter_then_accept`, `deadline_lapses`, `accept_on_lapsed_quote_refused`, `same_outcome_any_workers`,
`one_accept_per_thread`.
**Live checks**: none (its users', e.g. LC-1-25).
**Budget**: unit ≤ 500 ns VM an ask with its ≈ 4 answers' carriage, rules apart (`fin.bilateral.ask_ns` 500, added);
design count 10 k / 0 / 20 k asks (B / NB / H). The users carry the shares (count × unit, on fin.fixed.institutions
and fin.fixed.osearch). ledger line 16 (messages): +0 B (within K-45's rows, S1.237).
**Guards**: `phx_market::bilateral` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a quote written without its responder's rule; an accept without a quote; a round count in the kernel.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The protocol and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F bilateral` within `fin.bilateral.ask_ns`.
- [ ] §7.11 "The bilateral protocol (K-80)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.318 — The lending round onto the bilateral protocol

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The bilateral protocol (K-80)".
**Depends on**: S1.317 (the protocol), S1.262 (owed balances as side aggregates, read in place of `debts_of`).
**Goal**: a firm's application for a loan is a K-80 negotiation — asks to the lenders in its reach, each lender's quote
or decline from its own rule, the applicant's choice by its taste — and nothing hand-built in `core_lending` remains of
the round.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_lending.rs` | `apply_for_loan` and `cover` (`debts_of` per application) deleted; routing to K-80 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_lending.rs` | `Credit.lenders`' `quoted`/`declined` counters become K-80's counts per responder |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | the loan negotiation kind: payloads (principal, term, disclosed accounts), deadlines |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-99.toml`, `PC-100.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- The ask carries principal, term and the applicant's disclosed facts by reference; the applicant's debt service is
  read from its maintained owed sums (K-54), not by walking families per application.
- Each asked lender's quote rule (`sys-bnk`, BNK.4–BNK.6) answers at the declared stage from its own state; the kernel
  carries quote or decline; the applicant chooses by its Gumbel taste (the kind's stream, as today's `taste`), and the
  accept opens the loan (K-53) at the stage's apply.
- The reach is the applicant's (K-80): its bank relationships and the banks of its region's reach (BNK.6: a borrower
  asks the lenders it can reach); no count is drawn from published shares, and `law.lenders_asked` with its draw is
  deleted (any count is the applicant's own rule's, S1.425).
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (`BTreeMap` lenders' lookups on the path), `PC-99.toml` (per-call
  `Vec`s of quotes and tastes) and `PC-100.toml` (`cover`'s absent-as-zero).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: every lender declines: the refusal is recorded (MKT.10) and the firm's shortfall follows its rule (S1.427) —
  `decline_all_is_refusal` (S1.317).
- E10: a lender that ends mid-round: its quote lapses; the accept is refused by generation —
  `accept_on_lapsed_quote_refused` (S1.317).

**Extension points**: S1.425 (the lending round's rules on the protocol).
**Unit tests**: `debt_service_from_aggregates`, `asks_every_lender_in_reach` (logic level over the ask's builder).
**Live checks**: LC-1-25 (applications, declines, quotes and loans per bank) each business day.
**Budget**: ≈ 10 k asks × ≤ 4 lenders a business day at `fin.bilateral.ask_ns` 500: its share of
fin.fixed.institutions: +0 (the lending round's share is S1.425's). Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300`
shows `credit.apply` within S1.425's share, no `debts_of` in the profile.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a quote made outside the lender's rule.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Deleted and routed, tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench within its line; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.319 — The administered form

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "The administered form (K-81)".
**Depends on**: S1.296 (instances), S1.298 (the shared admission hook), S1.179 (dated policy schedules).
**Goal**: an institution that stands behind a facility declares its rate or price as a dated schedule and meets the
quantity that comes to it, within declared limits admitted through the shared hook; forward pricing at the next value
is a declared variant, the one exception to MKT.16.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/administered.rs` | `Facility` declarations, `request`, `meet`, the forward-priced variant |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/administered_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/administered.rs` | -F driver `fin.administered` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.administered]` `request_ns` 100 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "The administered form (K-81)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carrier of MKT.8 (done at S0.18) moves here.
- **A facility** (a market instance of an administered kind, K-21): the standing institution, its side (it takes or
  gives), its rate or price as a `PolicySchedule` (K-20: owner, announced and effective day), eligibility (declared
  participant kinds), the collateral it accepts as declared data, its settlement convention and the stage it meets at
  (CB facilities at 8d after the money market; benefits at their declared dates).
- **Requests**: participants' requests (quantity; the collateral offered) posted by their rules, admitted by S1.298's
  hook with each participant's headroom (K-93's limits as data from S1.338; a collateral need valued by the declared
  rule); every admitted request is met in full at the rate in force (MKT.8's quantity response); a refused one is
  recorded (MKT.10).
- **Forward-priced variant** (FND.6, FND.7, MKT.16's exception): requests recorded as commitments (K-50) and filled at
  the next value the fund computes at stage 9 (a read of formed prices, FND.5), never a price the fund makes.
- **Out**: positions as contract rows on one shared schedule per facility (K-55: an overnight position's return due
  the next business day on the wheel, not a schedule per position per day) and their flows through the day's batch.
- **Measurement**: requests met and refused per facility; `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a facility no participant uses meets nothing and forms no print (an administered rate is not a print, MKT.14) —
  `no_print_from_rate`.
- E3: a participant with no eligible collateral is refused visibly — `refused_beyond_headroom`.
- E5: a heavy settlement day's facility requests (every short bank at 8d) are ≈ 35 requests; benefits at month-end are
  the heavy line (30 k) — `month_end_requests_at_unit` (-F on H).
- E12: a schedule with no value in force for the day is a violation at assembly, never a zero rate —
  `no_rate_in_force_refused`.

**Extension points**: S1.320, S2.185, S3.112, S3.115, S3.116, S3.122, S3.185, S3.194, S5.184.
**Unit tests**: `met_in_full_at_rate_in_force`, `refused_beyond_headroom`, `rate_change_effective_on_its_day`,
`forward_priced_at_next_value`, `no_print_from_rate`, `month_end_requests_at_unit`, `no_rate_in_force_refused`.
**Live checks**: none (its users', e.g. LC-1-27).
**Budget**: unit ≤ 100 ns VM a request (`fin.administered.request_ns` 100, added); design count 30 k / 1 k / 30 k
requests (B / NB / H). The users carry the shares (count × unit, on fin.fixed.fund and fin.fixed.institutions).
ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (≈ 100 facility rows in K-70's instances).
**Guards**: `phx_market::administered` on PC-92's hot list; an administered rate type distinct from a print (compile
level: no `Print` constructible from a `Facility`).
**Not allowed**: a rate that is not a dated schedule; a request met in part without a declared limit; the fund setting
its own dealing price.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F administered` within `fin.administered.request_ns`.
- [ ] §7.11 "The administered form (K-81)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.320 — The central bank's facilities onto the administered form

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "The administered form (K-81)".
**Depends on**: S1.319 (the administered form), S1.260 (dated families on the contract store), S1.262 (collateral as
side aggregates of the firm-loan family).
**Goal**: the central bank's deposit and lending facilities are K-81 facilities: a bank's request reads its collateral
from maintained sums, positions open on one shared overnight schedule and return on the wheel; no pass sums every firm
loan or walks every position.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_central.rs` | `requests` (every firm loan summed into a `BTreeMap` per bank), `returns` (every open position walked, `issuers` searched per edge), `open_position` (a schedule per position per day), `targets`, `opened` deleted |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/declare.rs` | the two facilities: rates from the corridor's schedule, eligibility, collateral, stage 8d |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-96.toml`, `PC-100.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- A bank's collateral for the lending facility is its maintained sum of firm-loan balances (K-54 per (bank, family,
  side)), read in O(1); its request (`sys_bnk::points::REQUEST`) posts to the facility at 8d, admitted by the hook.
- Positions are rows of the overnight family on the facility's one shared schedule (K-55); their return is due the
  next business day through the wheel (K-42), interest by the calendar's day count (TIME.4) from the row's own opening
  day — never `unwrap_or(day)` (`core_central.rs`, a position with no opening day accruing none).
- The treasury-and-agency money class check by name is S1.141's; nothing here compares kind names.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (`BTreeMap`s), `PC-96.toml` (`open_slots` over the loan family and
  positions) and `PC-100.toml` (`unwrap_or(day)`).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a bank failure day: its positions' returns follow its ending (K-97), its requests refused —
  `failed_bank_requests_refused`.
- E12: a position's opening day is a column of its row; absent is a violation — `absent_opening_day_stops`.

**Extension points**: the corridor and the central bank's collateral framework (S2.185, S3.112), the lender of last
resort (S3.115).
**Unit tests**: `collateral_from_aggregates`, `return_due_next_business_day`, `failed_bank_requests_refused`,
`absent_opening_day_stops` (logic level).
**Live checks**: LC-1-27 (facilities used, positions returned, income remitted) each business day.
**Budget**: ≤ 35 requests and ≤ 35 returns a business day: its share of fin.fixed.fund: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB
/ H). Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300` shows
`central.requests` and `central.returns` within fin.fixed.fund (22 / 0 / 30).
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a schedule opened per position.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Deleted and routed, tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench within its line; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.321 — Search and match

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: REP.22 PROCESS
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Search and match (K-82)".
**Depends on**: S1.304 (the vacancy book, reach, pulls), S1.237 (applications and offers as messages), S1.169 (chunk
plans for the searchers' draws), S1.235 (hazards over counts for meeting processes), S1.302 (reach's declared closed
set).
**Goal**: one kernel meets searchers and named listings through a declared meeting process — applications drawn from
the searcher's own tastes over the listings in reach, or meetings arriving at a hazard over counts — in rounds over
their occasions; the lister selects by its rule, equals by lot; the chosen accepts against its reservation with the
match's quality as its taste.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/search.rs` | `apply`, `meetings`, `select`, `accept` (generalising `hiring.rs`, which stays until S1.322) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/search_tests.rs` | unit tests (`hiring_tests.rs`'s carried over) |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/vacancies.rs` | the search driver in `fin.vacancies`; other searches in `fin.decide` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.vacancies]` `search_ns` 170; `[fin.decide]` `search_ns` 300, `osearch_ns` 350; `[fin.kept] search_ns` and `mb` removed |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Search and match (K-82)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carrier of LAB.8 (done at S1.08) moves here.
- **A search kind** (declared, K-21): searchers (persons searching work, households seeking dwellings, singles, buyers
  of firms), listings (vacancies K-72, listings K-70, persons by region, firms for sale), the reach (index runs and the
  zone factors of S1.304), the meeting process, the lister's ranking key, the stages of each step, and its streams.
- **Applications** (process one, LAB.8, HSG.10): a searcher due today applies to as many listings as its own rule says
  (LAB.5; the count k is the rule's output, handed in), drawn without replacement with the logit's chances over
  w·ln(wage) − γ·km (Plackett–Luce, REP.22) as the Gumbel top-k, exact by construction: each listing in reach scores
  its log-pull + distance term (S1.304's tables) + a standard Gumbel taste drawn in Philox ×4 batches from the
  searcher's own stream addressed by (searcher, day), and the k highest are kept by a k-bounded insertion — no `exp`,
  no draw per round; the reservation filter is a compare on the stored wage point. Each application is a K-45 message
  due at the lister's selection stage. S1.416's pay rounds read the same top-k for an employee's best vacancy.
- **Meetings over counts** (process two, POP.7, CHN.3's meetings): a region's meeting count for the day drawn from the
  hazard over its searchers' count (K-44 over counts), each meeting pairing searchers or a searcher and a listing drawn
  by lot from the region's index; a meeting is an occasion (K-43) for both.
- **Selection** (LAB.7): the lister's rule ranks its applicants by its declared key (skill, experience), equals by lot
  (stream addressed by (lister, day)), and offers up to its open count; offers are K-45 messages due next stage.
- **Acceptance** (LAB.5, LAB.8, REP.22): the searcher draws a match taste for each offer from its type's declared
  distribution (the job offer's taste is the match's quality) and accepts the best whose worth with its taste beats its
  reservation; the other offers lapse and their jobs return to their vacancies at the apply.
- Integer wage points throughout (no f64 wage); pulls from S1.304's point table.
- Retires `[fin.kept] search_ns` (S1.119), replaced by `[fin.vacancies] search_ns`, and `[fin.kept] mb` with the last
  kept kernel.
- **Measurement**: applications, offers, acceptances, meetings per kind; `ExecCounters::visited` (listings weighed).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no listing in reach, or no applicant: nothing sent, the listing stays open (MKT.10) — `nothing_in_reach`.
- E5: a mass layoff wakes many searchers the next business day, each at its own unit cost —
  `many_searchers_at_unit` (-F on H).
- E7: draws addressed by searcher and lister; the same matches for any chunking — `same_matches_any_chunking`.
- E10: a listing withdrawn or a lister ended before selection: its applications refused by generation —
  `application_to_withdrawn_refused`.
- E14: two offers to one searcher: the best with its taste accepted, the other lapses — `best_of_two_offers`.

**Extension points**: S1.322, S1.414, S1.415, S2.150, S3.156, S8.117, S8.124, S8.125, S8.135, S5.144. A new search is
a declared kind.
**Unit tests**: `search_topk_equals_plackett_luce`, `plackett_luce_matches_logit`, `distance_weighs_applications`,
`only_above_reservation`, `select_by_key_equals_by_lot`, `taste_is_match_quality`, `best_of_two_offers`,
`meetings_over_counts_rate`, `nothing_in_reach`, `same_matches_any_chunking`, `many_searchers_at_unit`,
`application_to_withdrawn_refused`.
**Live checks**: none (S1.322's).
**Budget**: unit ≤ 170 ns VM a job search's kernel part with ≈ 15 in reach (the reach's 40, 15 × ≈ 8 ns scoring, ≤ 10
top-k; `fin.vacancies.search_ns` 170), so a search all in is ≤ 300 ns with the decision core's handler 30 and view 90
(`fin.decide.search_ns` 300) and an other search over ≈ 20 listings ≤ 350 ns (`fin.decide.osearch_ns` 350); design count
90 k / 0 / 90 k job searches (`[day.b] searches`, the search days S1.414 states) and 90 k / 0 / 90 k other searches (B / NB / H), 50–150 k K-45 applications. The users
carry the shares (count × unit). Traversal: searchers in agenda chunks on the pool; selections by lister range; answers
by searcher range. ledger line 16 (messages): +0 B (within K-45's rows).
**Guards**: `phx_market::search` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: an aggregate matching function; a pull recomputed per search; an f64 wage; a searcher visited on a day
it is not due; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F vacancies,decide` within `fin.vacancies.search_ns`, `fin.decide.search_ns` and
  `fin.decide.osearch_ns`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Search and match (K-82)" written; REP.22's row in §13; the two reviews; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S1.322 — Labour's rounds onto search and match

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration

**Budget**: removes `labour.search`'s serial call and the rounds' clones. Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t
300` shows the labour spans within fin.decide.search_ns × the day's searchers.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day.

### S1.323 — Rationed queues

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: SOC.4 PROCESS *(part: waits when demand exceeds capacity; the services and their capacity are Stage
5's)*; FND.2 STATE *(part: a gate carrying redemption requests forward; the fund kinds are Stage 3's)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Rationed queues (K-84)".
**Depends on**: S1.159 (generation-checked claimants), S1.165 (queue memberships by claimant), S1.176 (the lots'
streams).
**Goal**: demand a server cannot meet waits in a queue per (server, service, region): served in the order joined, ties
by lot, at the server's capacity each day, a request carried forward and never dropped, a claimant who dies, moves or
ends leaving at once.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/queues.rs` | `Queues`: `join`, `serve(queue, capacity)`, `leave`, `waiting` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/queues_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/queues.rs` | -F driver `fin.queues` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.queues]` `op_ns` 50, `mb` 4 (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Rationed queues (K-84)" |

**Design**:
- **Queue** per (server, service, region) instance: a FIFO of entries in a K-04 block list (head, tail, count, units
  waiting in its header, 24 B). **Entry** (SoA): claimant `GenRef` 8 B, day joined u32, units wanted i64 (a place is
  one; a redemption its units) = 20 B.
- **Serve** (at the server's declared stage, each day it serves): capacity for the day (from K-85 or the server's
  declared rule) serves from the head; the entries joined on one day are served in an order drawn by lot (stream
  addressed by (queue, day)); a divisible request at the margin takes its share by largest remainder (K-16) and the
  rest stays queued (FND.11: never dropped); served claimants are woken (K-43).
- **Leave**: memberships by claimant (a K-06 instance, 8 B an entry): a death, a move to another region or an ending
  removes its entries at that event (REP.14: no total changes); an entry whose claimant's generation is stale is also
  refused when reached.
- **Measure**: waiting counts and waiting days per queue (SOC's measures) read from headers and joined days.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: an empty queue serves nothing; capacity unused perishes (K-85) — `empty_queue_serves_nothing`.
- E7: order within a day by lot — `same_service_any_workers`.
- E10: a claimant who dies or moves leaves at once — `claimant_leaves_on_move`.
- E12: a server with no declared capacity for the day serves none (absent is not unlimited) —
  `no_capacity_serves_none`.

**Extension points**: S3.192, S4.133, S4.152, S5.112, S5.123, S5.128, S5.178, S6.108.
**Unit tests**: `fifo_by_day_then_lot`, `divisible_margin_by_largest_remainder`, `request_carried_not_dropped`,
`claimant_leaves_on_move`, `stale_claimant_refused`, `same_service_any_workers`, `empty_queue_serves_nothing`,
`no_capacity_serves_none`.
**Live checks**: none (S5.123's).
**Budget**: unit ≤ 50 ns VM an operation (`fin.queues.op_ns` 50, added); design count 20 k served and 20 k joined a
day (B / NB / H alike), 50–150 k waiting. The users carry the shares (count × unit). ledger line 17 (markets): +4 MB
resident (150 k entries × 20 B, memberships 150 k × 8 B, headers) — `fin.queues.mb` 4.
**Guards**: `phx_market::queues` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a request dropped; a queue order by anything but joined day and lot; a scan for a claimant's entries.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The kernel and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F queues` within `fin.queues.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Rationed queues (K-84)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.
