### S1.324 — Perishable daily capacity

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Perishable daily capacity (K-85)".
**Depends on**: S1.166 (epoch bitsets: a use touched today), S1.196 (kind stores: the owner's maintained staff hours
and plant capacity from which a day's capacity is read).
**Goal**: every capacity that perishes with the day — a provider's service hours, a carrier's vehicle room, a line's
day — holds only what was used today, with a day's epoch bit, so unused capacity is lost by construction and nothing
resets it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/capacity.rs` | `Capacity`: `use_(resource, qty, day) -> Result<Covered<Qty>, Short>`, `left`, `used_today` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/capacity_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/capacity.rs` | -F driver `fin.capacity` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.capacity]` `use_ns` 3, `mb` 10 (added) |
| `perf/design.toml` | `[store]` `capacity_resources` 1_152_000; `[day.*]` `capacity_uses` 5_000_000 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Perishable daily capacity (K-85)" |

**Design**:
- **Resources** are the owners of perishable capacity, one row per firm slot (dense: a firm that sells no perishable
  output never touches its row): `used` i64 (8 B) and a bit in a K-07 epoch bitset of the day (1.15 M bits = 144 KB,
  cleared as a whole at 10e — the bitset's epoch, not a pass over parties). A row whose bit is unset reads `used` as
  none: a stale day reads unused. Capacity itself is never stored: it is a read of the owner's declared source (K-21
  data per output kind: staff hours × the way's output per hour from K-54's maintained hours, plant capacity from
  K-67, held vehicles' room — the least of them, CAP.9), computed once a day per owner through K-35's day-stamped
  cache.
- `use_` checks `used + qty ≤ capacity` and returns the covered quantity (a sale's cover at the meeting, S1.306);
  beyond it is `Short`, which the caller turns into a buyer served short (SRV.5).
- Lines and segments keep their own daily use in K-26 (S1.188); a transit line declared at S2.172, with no K-26 row, uses this base.
- **Unused capacity** is lost with the day (SRV.1); what was lost is a read (capacity − used) where a measure needs it
  (SRV.7, statistics), accumulated for the owners touched and from K-39's capacity totals maintained at their events.
- **Save/load**: `used` and the bitset are the day's state; a save between days holds none of today's (the bitset is
  cleared at 10e, before the save slot), so nothing is saved but the column's zero rows' absence (logical hash over
  `used` where the bit is set).
- **Measurement**: `StoreStats` (resources used today); `ExecCounters::visited`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a provider with no staff or plant has capacity none; every buyer is served short — `use_beyond_capacity_short`.
- E7: uses fall within one meeting job per instance, and a provider's uses across instances are applied by owner range
  at 6b — the same for any workers — `uses_same_any_workers`.
- E8: `used` beyond i64 stops the run — `used_beyond_i64_stops`.
- E12: an output kind with no declared capacity source is refused at assembly — `no_capacity_source_refused`.
- E14: two meetings using one provider's capacity the same day see each other's uses in K-21's declared meeting order
  — `meetings_share_capacity_in_order`.

**Extension points**: S1.325, S1.451, S5.112, S5.123, S5.128, S5.178.
**Unit tests**: `stale_day_reads_unused`, `use_beyond_capacity_short`, `capacity_read_is_least_of_sources`,
`bitset_epoch_clears_day`, `uses_same_any_workers`, `used_beyond_i64_stops`, `no_capacity_source_refused`,
`meetings_share_capacity_in_order`.
**Live checks**: none (S1.325's LC-1-17).
**Budget**: unit ≤ 3 ns VM a use (`fin.capacity.use_ns` 3, added); design count 5 M / 5 M / 5 M uses (B / NB / H),
fused in the meetings' first touch: adds 0 phone-ns to fin.retail.all_in_ns at 6.75 M / 6.75 M / 6.75 M items (inside
the serve's share, S1.306). ledger line 17 (markets, the perishable-capacity row): +9.4 MB resident (1.15 M × 8 B +
a 144 KB bitset) — `fin.capacity.mb` 10.
**Guards**: `phx_market::capacity` on PC-92's hot list.
**Not allowed**: a reset pass; a stored capacity; a service carried as a stock.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The base and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F capacity` within `fin.capacity.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Perishable daily capacity (K-85)" written; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.325 — Services' capacity onto perishable capacity

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: SRV.1 STATE
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "Perishable daily capacity (K-85)".
**Depends on**: S1.324 (perishable capacity), S1.228 (firms' visits on their schedule, so no daily pass is needed to
make a service).
**Goal**: a service provider's capacity per day is read from its staff hours, seats, beds or vehicles, used by its
sales and lost when unused; no pass closes services over every firm and no map carries what was owed.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `close_services` (every service firm daily, its `BTreeMap<u32, i64>`), `services_owed` deleted |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/meet.rs` | the service stall's capacity reads K-85 (retires S1.306's placeholder) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | carriers' room reads K-85 (the vehicle room per day) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-96.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- A service's stall capacity at the meeting is `K-85::left(provider)` for the day; each sale uses it at the meeting's
  apply; a service is delivered as it is made and never held (SRV.8), so its (seller, good) batch has no stock move.
- A service's inputs used are read at its batch from the day's sales (the way's inputs per unit, K-68's standing rate
  for the rest), not from an owed map carried across days.
- Retires S1.306's placeholder (a service stall's capacity from today's `way_most` computation of the maker's day).
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (the two `BTreeMap`s) and `PC-96.toml` (every service firm daily).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a provider no buyer reaches uses nothing; its capacity is lost (SRV.1) — `service_capacity_lost_unused`.
- E5: payday: services' capacity binds; buyers served short choose again (SRV.5) — `served_by_lot_then_rechoose`
  (S1.306).

**Extension points**: none beyond S1.324's.
**Unit tests**: `service_capacity_lost_unused` (logic level over the reader), `service_batch_moves_no_stock`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-17 (services sold, capacity lost) each day.
**Budget**: removes `goods.close_services` (1.19 s on the 5 M bench). Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1 -t 300`
shows the span gone.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a service carried to the next day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Deleted and routed, tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.
- [ ] The bench shows the span gone; SRV.1's row in §13; the two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.326 — Prints, marks, fixings and market measures

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: MKT.15 MEASURE; IDX.2 STATE *(part: the day's individual prints kept for a declared fixing method; the
benchmark's publisher and method are Stage 3's)*
**Architecture**: writes §7.11 "Prints, marks and fixings (K-86)".
**Depends on**: S1.167 (horizon rings), S1.180 (markets' forms and mark rules), S1.160 (the day's print buffers),
S1.161 (their lives in the day plan), S1.296 (market instances).
**Goal**: every market instance keeps its last print with its age, its day's exact sums, its mark by its form's
declared rule — for a posted-price market the day's sales at their posted prices as their mean weighted by units sold
— its measures (MKT.15), and its daily mark and volume for the declared horizon; fixings are kept by publisher and
method, from the day's individual prints where a method names the market.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/prints/mod.rs` | `Prints`: live rows, `form_day` at 6c, `mark`, `last`, `measures` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/prints/history.rs` | encoded daily (mark, volume) series in K-08 rings |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/prints/fixings.rs` | fixings by (publisher, method), the day's print buffers |
| `crates/kernel/phx-market/src/prints/tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/marks.rs` | -F driver: `fin.valuation.mark_ns`, `fin.marks` |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.valuation]` `mark_ns` 7.7; `[fin.marks]` `mb` 27, `bytes_per_day` 4.05 (added) |
| `perf/design.toml` | cites `perf/design.toml`'s `[resolution]` `horizon_marks_instruments_days` and `horizon_marks_goods_labour_days` (730 each; DRV.10's floor 250) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.11 "Prints, marks and fixings (K-86)" |

**Design**:
- The `#[clause]` carriers of MKT.2, MKT.10, MKT.12 (as amended) and MKT.14 (done at S0.18) move here.
- **Instances that print, at the design point** (`perf/design.toml` `[store] market_instances` 58 000, the capacity):
  ≈ 13 k goods, services and labour markets; the instrument register's printing part at its peak — bonds, CP and CDs ≈
  5 k, sovereign lines and bills ≈ 0.3 k, listed and bank equity ≈ 0.2 k, fund units ≈ 5 k, tranches ≈ 1 k — and ≈ 16 k
  listed derivative series at their steady state (S4.115's `listing_steady_state`), ≈ 41 k in all; a series' instance
  is released when it has expired and its history is past its horizon. The register's other rows print nothing and
  hold no history: ≈ 50 k patents (S6.108), OTC positions valued by named valuers (MKT.20).
- **Live row per instance** (58 k, 64 B): last print (price i64, quantity i64, day u32, form u8), today's sums
  (value Σ price × units at the prices that traded, i128; units i64; count u32), today's mark (i64 or absent),
  meetings and failed meetings today, measures' inputs.
- **Prints** are formed at 6c for instances that met, from the sums the meetings added as they matched (S1.306,
  K-76–K-79): nothing is added per sale here. A print always comes from a match (MKT.14): a quote, an order, a rate or
  a valuation is never one (no constructor from them, compile level).
- **Mark rules** (MKT.12, declared per form): call — its price; continuous book — its closing call's price; dealer and
  bilateral — the fixing of the named publisher's declared method (MKT.20); posted price — Σ(price × units) ÷ Σ units
  over the day's sales at their posted prices, rounded once by the market's convention (REP.9). No match, no new print
  and no mark: the last print shows its age (MKT.2, MKT.10), never 0 (Law 8).
- **Measures** (MKT.15) per instance per day: depth and bid–offer width read at 6c from its book or quotes (K-78,
  K-79; none for forms that have none), turnover (units and value), the share of meetings that failed, the age of its
  last print.
- **Histories** (SET.13): each instance's daily (mark, volume) kept for its market kind's declared horizon (RESOLUTION,
  never shorter than a keeper's POLICY — DRV.10's window, BNK.21, STA.5; a listed series' horizon is S4.115's
  `DRX.series_mark_days`, 20 business days): 4-day sub-blocks with their own bit widths (zig-zag mark deltas, volumes)
  inside 64-day frames (first day, base mark and volume, a day mask for sparse series; frame boundaries staggered by
  instance, so the resident total holds on average a half frame past the horizon) in K-08 rings, pruned by whole frames
  past the horizon; the open 4 days staged raw (64 B an instance). `history(instance, from, to)` decodes frames in
  order; `mark_on(instance, day)` in O(log frames + 4).
- **Fixings** (MKT.20, IDX.2, FX.5): a fixing is (publisher, method, instance, day) → value; methods are declared data
  (a trimmed volume-weighted mean with its trim, a median of the day's prints, …); for instances a declared method
  names, the day's individual prints (price i64, quantity i64) are kept in a K-03 day buffer from 6a and released at
  10e; fixings are formed at 6c (business days) and kept in the rings as marks are.
- **Reads** follow TIME.10 (stage 5 yesterday's, stage 9 today's). **Day zero** (GEN.5, E 38): each market's single
  latest value at the snapshot is its last print dated the snapshot — a series of one, not a default.
- **Save/load**: live rows, staging rows, histories and fixings saved; decoded caches none. **Measurement**:
  `StoreStats` (instances, frames, bytes a market-day); `ExecCounters::visited` at 6c.

**Edge cases**:
- E2/E12: a market that never met has no print and no mark: its readers get `Missing` with its age, never 0 —
  `no_print_no_mark`.
- E5: the day's printing instances formed at 6c on the pool; a crash day's many prints are the same sums —
  `crash_day_prints_same_sums`.
- E6: histories round-trip equal — `history_round_trip`.
- E9: histories grow to their horizon and are flat after (frames pruned) — `pruned_past_horizon`.
- E11: day zero's prints are the snapshot's latest values — `opening_series_of_one`.

**Extension points**: S1.327, S1.332, S1.335, S1.336, S1.449, S2.106, S2.116, S2.141, S2.209, S3.101, S3.103, S3.107,
S3.109, S3.112, S3.121, S3.127, S3.131, S3.132, S3.135, S3.141, S3.147, S3.162, S3.169, S3.177, S3.179, S3.181, S3.184,
S3.203, S8.105, S4.101, S4.106, S4.115, S4.122, S4.131, S4.132, S4.161, S4.162, S4.171, S4.180, S5.112, S5.165, S6.132.
**Unit tests**: `posted_mark_is_unit_weighted_mean`, `call_mark_is_its_price`, `book_mark_is_close`,
`fixing_by_declared_method`, `no_print_no_mark`, `print_only_from_match`, `measures_per_instance`,
`history_round_trip`, `pruned_past_horizon`, `opening_series_of_one`, `crash_day_prints_same_sums`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-161 — each day, every print traced to its match and no mark without a print (MKT.14, MKT.2).
**Budget**: prints and marks formed at 6c for the instances that met, 21 k / 13 k / 21 k (B / NB / H: goods and labour
every day, ≈ 30 % of printing instruments and series on business days) at ≤ 7.7 ns VM with measures
(`fin.valuation.mark_ns` 7.7): its share of fin.fixed.calls: 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H). At the design
point's declared settings (`perf/design.toml` `[resolution]` `horizon_marks_instruments_days` and
`horizon_marks_goods_labour_days` 730, restored; `DRX.series_mark_days` 20): ledger line 17 (markets): +62.3 MB
resident (live rows 58 k × 64 B = 3.7 MB; staging 58 k × 64 B = 3.7 MB; histories 13.37 M market-days × ≤ 4.05 B =
54.1 MB — goods and labour 13 k × (730 + 32) = 9.91 M, register instruments 11.5 k × (730 + 32) × 30 % = 2.63 M,
listed series 16 k × (20 + 32) = 0.83 M, each horizon with its mean half frame; fixings 0.7 MB) — `fin.marks.mb` 63,
`fin.marks.bytes_per_day` 4.05 (added); the listed series' marks are these, none kept elsewhere. At the keepers'
floors (goods and labour 182, instruments 250, DRV.10's): 26.7 MB. saved: +62.3 MB. ledger line 21 (day buffers): the day's fixing prints ≤ 0.5 M × 16 B = 8 MB on a busy day, released at 10e.
**Guards**: `phx_market::prints` on PC-92's hot list; PC-28, re-aimed here, guards the live `Print`; no `Print`
from a quote, rate or valuation (compile level).
**Not allowed**: a mark averaged over posted prices not sold at; a print kept beyond the day except as the mark and
the fixings' inputs; a zero for an absent print.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The base and tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F marks` within `fin.valuation.mark_ns` and `fin.marks.*`.
- [ ] §7.11 "Prints, marks and fixings (K-86)" written; MKT.15's row in §13; the two reviews; `done`, section removed.

### S1.327 — Traded sums and marks onto prints and marks

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: follows §7.11 "Prints, marks and fixings (K-86)".
**Depends on**: S1.326 (prints and marks), S1.311 (sales booked through K-74, which no longer write `traded`); S1.313 (the bill call, whose print and cover move here).
**Goal**: every reader of a mark reads K-86; the `traded` and `marks` maps, the float marks and the catastrophes'
clones of every mark are gone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `traded` and `marks`, their per-sale write and the day's mark loop deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | `weigh` and the basis read K-86 marks by instance |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_weather.rs` | `Weather::shocks`' clone of every mark and its daily scan → K-86 history reads on the catastrophe's day |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_outlooks.rs` | public series fed from K-86's prints at 5a |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_bills.rs` | the bill call's print and cover, left in today's auction record by S1.313, written to K-86 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml`, `PC-100.toml` | the sites this step removes |

**Design**:
- Every mark read becomes `Prints::mark(instance)` (yesterday's at stage 5) or `mark_on(instance, day)`; an absent
  mark is `Missing` and each reader states its answer (VAL.10); no f64 mark remains.
- A catastrophe's price response is read from K-86's history between its day and today, so nothing is cloned or
  scanned daily; the rises recorded once each (`note_rises`) read the history.
- The public outlooks' series (K-92 from S1.336) take each instance's print at 5a; until then `core_outlooks` reads
  K-86.
- Removes its sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` (`BTreeMap`s) and `PC-100.toml` (absent marks read as zero).

**Edge cases**:
- E9: `Weather::shocks` grew with every catastrophe; histories are bounded by their horizon — `pruned_past_horizon`
  (S1.326).
- E12: a region with no mark for a product reads `Missing` in the shipper's gap, never zero — `mark_missing_not_zero`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `mark_missing_not_zero` (logic level over a reader).
**Live checks**: LC-1-161 and LC-1-20 (freight against gaps) each day.
**Budget**: removes the per-sale `traded` write and the catastrophes' clones. Bench: `tools/bench.sh -p 5000000 -d 1
-t 300` shows `goods.marks` within S1.326's share of fin.fixed.calls and no `BTreeMap` in the profile's goods spans.
**Guards**: the ratchet files above lowered.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a mark kept outside K-86.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Deleted and routed, tests; fmt, clippy, tests, `phx-check`; ratchet files lowered.

#### Books, outlooks, risk, endings, minds, the audit, saves and the close (S1.328–S1.360)

This group builds the core's last bases: the books every owned party keeps (`phx-acct`: lines, equity and net assets,
carrying values, statements, valuations), public outlooks and the investor schedule (`phx-val`), books and limits,
margin and exact linear aggregates (`phx-risk`), estates, the ending kernel, the waterfall and resolution
(`phx-end`), the decision core, attention and minds (`phx-mind`), the audit engine (`phx-audit`), snapshots of every
base (`phx-world::save`), and the run's measurement recorder (`phx-record`). Each base is built for its last user in
Stages 2–8, measured alone at the design point (`tools/bench.sh -F <base>`), and today's users in `phx-world` move onto
it in the migration step that follows it. `phx-check` refuses any
waterfall walker outside `phx-end` (PC-112, S1.345) and any new store or per-party pass in `phx-world` (PC-102,
S1.355). The group ends with the core's close (S1.360), a major step: every `fin` ratchet at the design point, the
stage lines, turns, memory ledger and saves summed from every step's own figures, `tools/bench.sh -g`, and N8.7's
finding put to the owner if a sum misses.

**Exit**: `phx-world` holds no store and no per-party pass beyond the `core_*.rs` rule modules each listed with the
Stage 1 step that deletes it; every core base (K-01–K-106) exists, is saved and rebuilt,
is audited by its family, and meets its ratchets at the design point; the day (B, NB, H, B') and the two worst turns
compose within `[fin.day]` and `[fin.turn]`, and the peak within `[fin.mem]` (4 349 MB) — or the close states N8.7's
finding and puts it to the owner.

**Placeholders**: none introduced. Retired: S1.285's period-end kink for plant wear, which S1.328's close pass takes
over; S1.267's books with no world user, which S1.344's endings adopt.

### S1.328 — Account lines (K-87)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.12 "phx-acct" — its subsection "Account lines" written (design first).
**Depends on**: S1.180 (the kind catalogue: each kind's lines declared as data); S1.196 (typed columns: the lines live
in the party's cold record); S1.248 (settlement's stage 7 sweep, one of the three places lines are posted); S1.170
(partitioned apply and its `SweepHooks` parameter: posts reach a party in its range's shard through a hook); S1.227 (the agenda: a party's own period end is a due
reason); S1.285 (plant wear realised at the period end: its placeholder kink moves into this close pass).
**Goal**: every party with books holds its current period's income-statement lines as `i64` columns in its cold record,
declared per kind, stamped with the period, posted only inside the fused chains' shard sweeps and on accrual dates, and
closed on the party's own period end; no world code posts a line per event.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/lines.rs` | `LineH`, `LineSet` (a kind's declared lines), `LinesShard` (a range's mutable view), `close_period` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-ledger/src/recognition.rs` | `Recognition`, sealed, with constructors from `phx-ledger`'s own flow items only |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/lines_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/Cargo.toml` | depends on `phx-store`, `phx-exec`, `phx-core`, `phx-pop`, `phx-agenda`, `phx-ledger` (layer L1.12) |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/lines.rs` | -F module: 1.15 M firms' lines; posts at the chains' daily counts; 1.15 M closes on H |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.valuation] close_ns = 23.1`; `[fin.lines] post_ns = 1.5` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.12 "Account lines" |

**Design**:
- The step carries ACC.9 (done at S0.19): its `#[clause]` carrier moves from settlement (`phx-ledger/src/settle.rs`) to the lines' period close.
- **Declaration**: each kind that keeps books declares its lines (K-21 `LineSet`: a list of `LineH` with a sign — income
  or expense — and the reason handles that post to it); a firm's ten are revenue, cost of sales, goods lost, services
  used, wages, taxes, interest paid, interest received, written off, depreciation (FRM.13's named cost lines); banks'
  and institutions' sets are their kinds' declarations. A household keeps no lines (ACC.4: net worth only; its incomes
  are read from the contracts that paid, HH.2). Which kinds keep books is the legal form's declared flag, never a kind
  name.
- **Layout**: `n_lines × i64` in the cold record by slot (a firm's 80 B of its cold part inside `fin.parties.firm_bytes`),
  plus the period stamp `u16` (period index of the party's own fiscal calendar, K-19) in the record's flags word.
  Amounts in the party's own money (ACC.9), whole smallest units; overflow stops the run (`capacity_exceeded!`, E8).
- **Posting API** (the only writer), reached through the sweep's hook (S1.170): the lower crates that run the sweeps
  (`phx-ledger`'s 2b stream and 7a apply, `phx-market`'s 6b seller-shard sweep) take a `SweepHooks` tuple as a generic
  parameter and never name `phx-acct`; `phx-acct` implements `LinesHook`, and `phx-world`'s routing composes it into each
  slot's sweep. The hook receives `LinesShard<'r>`, the mutable view of one party range, and `add(slot, line: LineH,
  rec: Recognition)`, where `Recognition` is a sealed token of `phx-ledger` constructible only from its own flow item types —
  a delivered sale item (K-74's sale enters the ledger as a flow item, so `phx-market`'s 6b sweep builds the token
  through `phx-ledger`'s constructor and `phx-ledger` never names `phx-market`), a streamed due on its accrual date, an applied receipt: income without one does not compile
  (ACC.13, R6). `post_pair(item, payee_line, payer_line)` posts both named sides of a two-sided item in the same sweep
  (FRM.17). No `recognise(party, …)` per event is public.
- **Where it runs**: 2b (dated items: wages, interest, rent, premiums — the payee's income and the payer's expense in
  the stream's range sweep), 6b (the seller-shard sweep: revenue and cost of sales on delivery), 7a/7c (decided flows and
  a failed sale's reversal, K-74). Each post first compares the party's stamp with today's period (1 compare): a stale
  stamp means the period close has not run — a contract violation (the close is due-driven below).
- **Period close**: on the party's own period end — a quarter of the fiscal year the party chose (RAT.2, RAT.8), K-43
  reason `books` — at 9b, in one pass per party. The pass first runs the close hooks composed into it through
  `SweepHooks`, in declared order: plant wear realised (S1.285, whose period-end kink this pass takes over) posts its
  depreciation line before anything reads the lines. The lines are then handed to K-90's statement writer (S1.333),
  which builds and appends the statement in the same traversal, and to K-88 (S1.330) for ACC.11; then zeroed and the
  stamp advanced. O(lines) per party; on the pool by party range.
- **Which day**: a fiscal year ending at a calendar quarter end puts every one of its quarter closes on a calendar
  quarter end, so the H count is the parties whose chosen year-end falls in March, June, September or December. The
  design point takes all 1.15 M firms on H as its bound; `-F lines` reads the opening's fiscal-year draw and reports the
  count.
- **Save/load**: lines and stamps are primary columns (saved); nothing rebuilt.
- **Replaces**: `phx-world/src/core_accounts.rs` (`Income`, 10 × i128 in a `PartyMap`) and `recognise`;
  the migration is S1.329.

**Edge cases**:
- E3 a party with no lines (a household): `LineSet` empty; a post to it is refused at compile level (no `LinesShard`
  for a kind without books) — `no_shard_for_kind_without_books`.
- E5 a quarter end with 1.15 M closes on one H day: chunked on the pool — `close_spread_by_calendar` and -F H.
- E6 a close hook's post lands before the statement reads the lines — `close_hooks_run_before_statement`.
- E7 posts partitioned by payee range, joined in range order — `posts_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E8 an `i64` line overflowing stops with NUM.6 — `line_overflow_stops`.
- E10 a party ending mid-period: its lines close into its estate's first statement at the ending (S1.343) —
  `close_on_ending_hands_lines`.
- E14 two posts to one line of one party the same day add in item order within the shard — `posts_commute`.

**Extension points**: a new line is a declaration in the kind's `LineSet` within the cold record's width (a width change is a ratchet change stated in its step); a later mechanism posts through `LinesHook` from its own item types. Steps that depend on it: S1.329, S1.330, S1.333, S1.434, S1.457, S2.102, S2.177, S3.117.
**Unit tests**: `line_set_declared_per_kind`, `recognition_only_from_delivery_accrual_or_receipt` (compile-fail),
`post_pair_moves_both_sides`, `no_shard_for_kind_without_books` (compile-fail), `posts_same_for_any_chunking`,
`posts_commute`, `line_overflow_stops`, `stale_stamp_stops`, `close_zeroes_and_advances_stamp`,
`close_on_ending_hands_lines`, `close_spread_by_calendar`, `close_hooks_run_before_statement`.
**Live checks**: none (the Accounts family, S1.331, reads the lines).
**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 1.5 VM-ns to `fin.retail.apply_ns`, `fin.b2b.purchase_ns` and `fin.dues.item_ns` at their items
  (`fin.lines.post_ns`, added): posts ride the chains' units, inside those units' figures.
- its share of fin.fixed.close_books: 0 / 0 / 34 core-ms (B / NB / H) — 1.15 M closes on H at
  `fin.valuation.close_ns` (23.1 VM-ns), the statement written in the same pass (S1.333) included; miss budget 0.15 a
  close. The wear realised in the pass is S1.285's own share of the line.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot: the cold record's lines, inside `fin.parties.firm_bytes`); ledger line 6
  (institutions): +0 B (banks' and institutions' lines in their records).
- `StoreStats` implemented (rows, bytes, growth); the close's traversal reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: `recognise`-style per-party mutators absent from `phx-acct`'s public API (PC-15 snapshot); PC-92's day-path
list (S1.120) covers `lines.rs`.
**Not allowed**: a line posted outside a shard sweep or an accrual date; an `i128` or `Option` line column; a line kept
in a map; a kind-name test for "keeps books".
**Done when**:
- [ ] `lines.rs` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F lines` at the design point: `post_ns` ≤ 1.5, `close_ns` ≤ 23.1, closes on H within 34 core-ms.
- [ ] §7.12 "Account lines" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.329 — Income recognition onto lines

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: ACC.13 FORBID; FRM.17 INVARIANT; FRM.20 FORBID
**Architecture**: §7.12 "Account lines" followed; §8's accounts paragraph restated.
**Depends on**: S1.328 (the lines and their posting API); S1.311 (booking and delivery onto the sales batch: the seller
sweep that now posts revenue and cost of sales); S1.264 (reckoning onto shared plans: the dated-item stream that now
posts wages, interest and rent); S1.270 (taxes onto the levy engine: tax lines from the fused levies); S1.200 (the line and equity words that replaced `PartyMap`).
**Goal**: every recognition today made per event through `recognise` (onto the kind's line words since S1.200) is made
by the fused chains through K-87's shard API; `recognise`, `account_flows` and `account_moves` are deleted, and no income can be posted
without a delivery, an accrual or a receipt naming both parties.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_accounts.rs` | `Income`, `Line`, `recognise`, `account_flows`, `account_moves` deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `deliver_sales`' three `recognise` calls per delivery removed: revenue and cost of sales post in K-74's sweep |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_taxes.rs` | `accrue_taxes`' recognitions removed: tax lines post with the fused levy (K-51) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_freight.rs` | carriage recognitions moved to the sales batch's carriage items |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/lines_tests.rs` | `failed_sale_reverses_its_lines`, `write_off_posts_from_the_loan_event` |

**Design**:
- Users move by function: `book_sale`/`deliver_sales` (revenue, cost of sales, goods lost) → K-74's seller-shard sweep
  calls `LinesShard::post_pair` with the sale item (payee revenue, payer's cost line where the payer keeps books);
  wages, interest, rent, premiums → the dated-item stream's range sweep (K-55/K-42) posts from each item; tax on
  products and withholding → K-51's fused levy posts the collector-side and payer-side lines; `account_moves`'
  write-offs and repayments (BNK.12 lines) → the contract event's own post at 7c (K-56/K-54); depreciation → K-67's
  wear kink (S1.285) posts at 4a.
- A failed payment's sale is reversed before the close by K-74 (S1.309), which posts the negated pair in the same sweep,
  so revenue stays recognised only on a settled delivery (ACC.1's delivery rule); `account_flows`' value-keyed failure
  map (`core_accounts.rs`) has no successor.
- ACC.13 holds at compile level (`Recognition` constructors, S1.328); FRM.20's "no revenue without a buyer, no cost
  without a payee" holds because every `Recognition` carries both parties; FRM.17 holds by `post_pair` and is checked by
  the Accounts family (S1.331): Σ income lines moved by reason today = Σ settled items by reason (K-52 tallies), an
  independent recount.
- Bench: `settle.books` (0.4 s at 5 M) and the recognitions inside `deliver_sales` (part of its 2.0 s; the profile's
  3 % income recognition) fall to the fused posts; `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution shows `books` gone.

**Edge cases**:
- E14 a sale delivered and its payment failed the same day: the reversal nets the lines to zero —
  `failed_sale_reverses_its_lines`.
- E10 a seller ending before settlement: its items settle against its estate (SET.7) and its lines close into the
  estate's statement (S1.343) — `ending_seller_lines_close_into_estate`.
- E12 a delivery whose cost is absent (a goods move that failed) is a contract violation at K-60, never a zero cost line
  (the `cost.unwrap_or(0)` sites in `deliver_sales` and `close_services` go with their callers) —
  `absent_cost_is_violation`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `failed_sale_reverses_its_lines`, `write_off_posts_from_the_loan_event`,
`ending_seller_lines_close_into_estate`, `absent_cost_is_violation`,
`tax_line_posted_with_the_levy`, `revenue_needs_a_buyer` (compile-fail).
**Live checks**: LC-1-06 (FRM.17's family clean) and LC-0-33 (Accounts clean for every party with an equity account),
re-aimed at S1.331's family.
**Budget**:
- no share of its own: the recognitions move into `LinesHook` (S1.328), counted in `fin.lines.post_ns` inside the
  chains' units.
- ledger line 1 (process): +0 B (the deleted `phx-world` state's bytes freed).
**Guards**: removes `core_accounts.rs`' recognition sites from `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-92.toml` and
`PC-99.toml`; PC-29 re-aimed at `phx-acct` (`lines.rs`, `equity.rs`) as the only writers of lines and equity accounts.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a recognition matched to a failure by value; a line posted from a flow that names one party.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The users moved; `Income`, `recognise`, `account_flows`, `account_moves` deleted; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution shows the `books` span gone and `deliver_sales` reduced; no ratchet broken (a measure of
  code, never read as the world's).
- [ ] §8's accounts paragraph restated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.330 — Equity accounts and maintained net assets (K-88)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: ACC.4 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.12 "Equity and net assets" written.
**Depends on**: S1.328 (the lines, whose sum is the period's income so far, folded into equity at the close); S1.243 (money accounts and their maintained totals:
the balances read at the test); S1.271 (holdings by holder: inline stocks at cost); S1.273 (unit totals: goods moves
emit their cost); S1.285 (capital classes: plant at cost less wear); S1.261 (side aggregates: a side's own-amount
changes); S1.166 (change sets: the parties touched today); S1.170 (the
sweeps' hook parameter); S1.227 (the agenda: a crossing wakes its party); S1.162 (the save contract and the round-trip harness).
**Goal**: every party whose legal form has owners keeps an equity account moved only by named events, and a maintained
word of its net assets beside money, so that "net assets below zero" is detected at 9b for the parties the day touched,
at O(1) each; a household's net worth is a read.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/equity.rs` | `EquityEvent`, `EquityShard`, `NetBeside` (the maintained word), `test_touched`, `net_worth` (the household read) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/equity_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/audit_view.rs` | `AccountsView` (the handed values: equity, the day's fold, a slice's recount inputs) and the pure checks of ACC.10 and ACC.11 over them, which S1.331 runs and S1.354 registers as the Accounts family |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/equity.rs` | -F module: 1.17 M owned parties; deltas at the chains' counts; the 9b test over 2.0 M / 1.0 M / 5.0 M touched |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.valuation] equity_ns = 60` (added; a crossing), `delta_ns = 2` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.12 "Equity and net assets" |

**Design**:
- **Who**: kinds whose legal form declares owners (the legal form's feature `has_owners`, read through K-21, Law 10; the kind-name branch in
  `owned` is removed at S1.144): firms, banks, funds, insurers,
  clearing houses, and a central bank, whose capital its treasury holds (it can lose equity, L3); a treasury, a public
  agency, a household and an estate have no owners, and their net worth is a read (ACC.4).
- **Layout**: equity `i64` and `beside: i64` (net assets other than money: goods at cost, plant at carrying value,
  holdings at carrying value, contract sides' own amounts receivable less payable) in the firm's warm record — the 16 B
  freed there by attention's move to the agenda (S1.350); banks' and institutions' in
  their records. A flags bit `below_zero`.
- **Equity events** (ACC.4's list, the only writers): `PaidIn`, `Returned`, `Income` (the period's net income, once,
  in S1.328's close pass), `Distributed`, `Buyback`, `ToEquity` (a revaluation the basis sends to equity, S1.332).
  Between closes the period's income so far is the sum of the party's lines (S1.328, one cold line), so no line post
  touches equity: `equity_now` = equity + Σ lines, a read. Each
  names its counterparty; capital events also add to the period's capital tally handed to the close (ACC.11, S1.331).
- **`beside`** is `#[maintained(writer = phx_acct::equity)]`: deltas arrive through the sweeps' hook parameter
  (S1.170's `SweepHooks`, composed by `phx-world`'s routing; no lower crate names `phx-acct`) from the sweeps that change
  a non-money position, one delta per party where that sweep already holds the party's record: a seller's batch in the
  retail seller-range sweep (goods at cost less the batch's cost of sales), a b2b purchase's apply (the buyer's goods
  at cost; the seller's goods into a receivable), a principal repayment in S1.261's own-amount update, K-67's wear at
  the close, K-89's carrying moves — ≤ 2 VM-ns each. A retail item, a wage or an interest due changes no non-money
  position, so it carries no delta. It is `#[saved(skip, rebuild = recount_beside)]`: rebuilt at load
  after K-54's aggregates, in slot order (≈ 1.2 M parties × ≤ 50 ns ≈ 60 ms of the load). The audit never reads it (R4).
- **The test** at 9b: for each owned party in today's change set (K-07), `net = beside + Σ its accounts' balances`
  (its record's account and side rows, ≤ 2 reads); a sign change flips `below_zero` and appends a `Crossing { party,
  day, net }` to a K-03 day buffer; the readers registered for it (FRM.15's balance-sheet test, S2.122; INS.7's and
  PEN.5's solvency tests, S4.136, S4.152) wake their party through K-43. A continuous watch on money is impossible by design (accounts have no
  owner column), and none is needed: money moves only on days the party is touched.
- **Net worth** of a household (ACC.4): `net_worth(household)` sums its persons' accounts, holdings and contract sides
  through their person chains, O(k), on demand; never stored.
- **Audit view**: `AccountsView` carries only handed values; its checks never take `beside` (R4). S1.331 runs them on
  the world; S1.354 registers them on the engine.
- **Missing**: an absent carrying value (a fair-value holding never printed nor valued) makes the party's net assets
  absent: K-89 counts absent inputs per party in its sparse rows and the test reads `Missing`, never 0.

**Edge cases**:
- E1 10 % of firms cross below zero on one day: 115 k crossings × 60 ns — `mass_crossing` in -F.
- E3 an owned party with no account (an estate-owned shell): its net is `beside` alone; a missing account row is a
  Names finding, not 0 — `no_account_net_is_beside`.
- E6 `beside` rebuilt at load equals the maintained word — `rebuild_equals_maintained`.
- E7 deltas partitioned by party range — `deltas_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E14 a sale and a payment of one firm the same day: both deltas land in its range's sweep; the test reads the day's
  end — `test_reads_day_end_state`.

**Extension points**: `EquityEvent` for owners' capital moves; `Crossing` readers registered by the solvency tests; a new owned kind is a `has_owners` declaration. Steps that depend on it: S1.331, S1.332, S1.333, S2.122, S2.186, S3.117, S3.163, S3.182, S8.104, S4.102, S4.111, S4.126, S4.136, S4.153, S5.165.
**Unit tests**: `equity_moved_only_by_named_events` (compile-fail), `income_folds_into_equity_at_close`,
`equity_now_is_equity_plus_lines`, `one_beside_delta_per_seller_batch`, `capital_tally_kept_apart`,
`deltas_same_for_any_chunking`, `rebuild_equals_maintained`, `crossing_flips_once`, `test_reads_day_end_state`,
`net_worth_is_a_read`, `absent_input_reads_missing`, `no_account_net_is_beside`,
`checks_take_no_maintained_field` (compile-fail).
**Live checks**: none (S1.331's family).
**Budget**:
- `-F` cases: `mass_crossing`.
- adds ≤ 2.6 phone-ns (2 VM) to `fin.decide.batch_ns` at 1.2 M / 0.9 M / 1.2 M items (retail sellers' batches; no
  delta per retail item) (`fin.valuation.delta_ns`, added).
- adds ≤ 2.6 phone-ns to `fin.b2b.all_in_ns` at 1.0 M / 0.1 M / 1.0 M items (b2b purchases' apply).
- adds ≤ 2.6 phone-ns to `fin.contracts.agg_update_ns` at ≈ 0.1 M / 0 / 3.3 M items (principal repaid on owned
  parties' sides; wages, interest and rent carry none).
- together ≈ 6 / 3 / 14 core-ms (B / NB / H) on those units, against ≈ 34 / 18 / 85 were every retail, b2b and dues item
  to carry a delta.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 5 / 2 / 10 core-ms (B / NB / H) — the 9b test over ≈ 0.9 M / 0.4 M / 1.9 M touched
  owned parties at ≤ 5 ns (on a non-business day over the sellers the retail sales touched); crossings ≤ 60 VM-ns
  (`fin.valuation.equity_ns`, added).
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot: equity and `beside`, 16 B inside `fin.parties.firm_bytes`).
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B.
- `StoreStats` implemented; the 9b test reports rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: PC-101's `#[maintained]` rule (S1.128) covers `beside`; PC-22 (re-aimed at S1.128) refuses the audit reading
it.
**Not allowed**: equity moved by a write outside `EquityEvent`; net assets stored for a household; a daily pass over
every owned party; a K-46 threshold on money.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `equity.rs` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F equity` at the design point `delta_ns` ≤ 2 VM-ns a party batch or principal update,
  `equity_ns` ≤ 60, the 9b test within 5 / 2 / 10 core-ms, 0 bytes above `fin.parties.firm_bytes`; no ratchet broken.

### S1.331 — The accounts audit onto recounts

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: migration
**Clauses**: ACC.10 INVARIANT; ACC.11 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: §7.12 followed; §15's Accounts family paragraph restated.
**Depends on**: S1.330 (equity accounts and `beside`); S1.171 (declared sweeps and rolling cursors: the rolling full
recount); S1.166 (change sets: the day's touched owned parties); S1.144 (the kind-name branch `owned` removed); S1.200 (the line and equity words that replaced `PartyMap`).
**Goal**: `audit_accounts`' daily recomputation of `net_assets` for every firm and bank is replaced by the Accounts
family's two checks — the day's touched owned parties from an independent fold of the day's items, and a rolling
thirtieth recounted in full from source rows — and ACC.11 at each party's period close.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_accounts.rs` | deleted: `net_assets`, `deposits`, `open_accounts`, `audit_accounts` (`owned` removed at S1.144) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day.rs` | 10c routes the day's fold and the rolling slice to S1.330's checks (registered on the engine at S1.354) |

**Design**:
- **Daily (ACC.10 on what the day changed)**: for each owned party touched today, Δequity today = Δ(assets − liabilities)
  today, where the right side is the audit's own fold of today's items per party (the chains' sale items, dues,
  decided flows, goods moves at cost, contract events, carrying moves — folded in K-03 by party range, R12), never
  `beside` (R4). 7.7 ns VM a party.
- **Rolling (ACC.10 in full)**: a K-14 cursor over owned parties by slot range, one thirtieth a day (the cycle is the
  audit's RESOLUTION, S1.353): each party's net assets recounted from source rows — its accounts, inline stocks and
  plant, holdings through its lists, contract sides through its block lists and person chain, and list-less sides
  through one filtered sweep of each such family's ends column for the day's slot range (0.4 ns a row) — against its
  equity account. `beside` and K-54's sums are not read.
- **ACC.11 at the close**: at each party's period close (S1.328), income for the period (the lines handed) = Δequity
  over the period − capital events (paid in, returned, distributed, buybacks) − revaluations to equity, from the equity
  events' period tally kept apart; exact, whole smallest units (Law 7).
- **Findings**: family `Accounts`, clause, owner (the party), size in its money, day (N1); the audit never repairs.
- Users moved: `audit_accounts` → the family's two checks; the opening's equity word (S1.200) → the opening writes the equity
  account directly (S1.330's `PaidIn` at the opening, GEN.7).
- Bench: `books.audit_accounts` (373 ms at 5 M, every firm and bank every day) falls to ≤ 10 ms of the audit's
  stage 10; `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution shows the span gone.

**Edge cases**:
- E5 a payday touches most firms: the daily check degrades to a dense sweep of set words (K-07), still O(rows/64) —
  `payday_dense_fold`.
- E6 the rolling cursor is saved, so the cycle continues across a load (SET.15) — `cursor_continues_after_load`.
- E10 a party ended today: checked against its estate's opening balance (S1.344) — `ended_party_checked_once`.
- E11 day zero: the opening passes the family (GEN.7) — `opening_passes_accounts`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `daily_identity_from_fold`, `rolling_recount_from_rows`, `acc11_at_close`, `capital_excluded_from_income`,
`injected_equity_error_lights_accounts_only`, `ended_party_checked_once`, `opening_passes_accounts`, `payday_dense_fold`,
`cursor_continues_after_load`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-33 (Accounts clean for every party with an equity account) re-aimed at this family; LC-1-40 (day
one passes every family, GEN.7).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.recount: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) — the Accounts family's ≈ 9 / 4 / 17 (the identities
  of 0.9 M / 0.4 M / 1.9 M owned touched parties at `fin.audit.ident_ns`, and the rolling cycle's ≈ 39 k parties and
  their rows at `fin.audit.recount_ns_per_row`) are inside S1.353's whole line.
- ledger line 1 (process): +0 B (the deleted audit's state freed).
**Guards**: removes `audit_accounts`' sites from `exceptions/PC-92.toml` and `PC-96.toml`; PC-22 (re-aimed at S1.128) refuses `phx-acct`'s audit view reading `#[maintained]` fields.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; the audit reading `beside` or K-54's sums; a tolerance.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `audit_accounts` deleted; the family's checks and tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution shows `books.audit_accounts` gone; no ratchet broken (a measure of code, never read as the
  world's).
- [ ] §15's Accounts paragraph restated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.332 — Carrying values, provisions and unrealised differences (K-89)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: ACC.3 STATE; ACC.8 PROCESS; ACC.7 PROCESS *(part)*
**Architecture**: §7.12 "Carrying values" written.
**Depends on**: S1.330 (carrying moves feed `beside` and `ToEquity`); S1.326 (prints and marks: the latest price a
difference reads); S1.276 (lots: the cost a sale consumes); S1.271 (holdings: the basis bits in the instrument word);
S1.257 (the contract store: the basis and grade bits in a family's status word); S1.170 (the sweeps' hook
parameter).
**Goal**: every position has a carrying basis chosen at acquisition, a carrying value read by that basis, an unrealised
difference readable wherever a price exists, a sale that realises it in full on the day, write-downs limited to cost,
and a loan's expected-loss provision as a read whose every move is an income event.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/carrying.rs` | `Basis` (2 bits), `acquire`, `carrying_value`, `unrealised`, `realise`, `WriteDowns` (sparse), `provision`, `ProvisionMove` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/basis.rs` | kept: the permitted bases per legal form and purpose (ACC.17) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/carrying_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/carrying.rs` | -F module |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.valuation] provision_ns = 30`, `unrealised_ns = 10`, `writedown_mb = 1` (added); `mark_ns = 7.7` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.12 "Carrying values" |

**Design**:
- The step carries ACC.2, ACC.15 and ACC.17 (done at S0.19): their carriers in `phx-acct/src/basis.rs` and `phx-core/src/accounting.rs` move to `carrying.rs`.
- **Basis** (ACC.2): 2 bits — fair value through income, amortised cost, lower of cost and net realisable value, cost
  less depreciation and impairment — held in spare bits of words that exist: an instrument holding's instrument word
  (K-60, the id's spare high bits), a contract side's status word (loans' arrears word, K-56), a kind's inline stocks and
  plant by the kind's declared basis for goods and plant. `acquire(position, basis)` takes the holder's choice and
  refuses a basis its legal form does not permit for the purpose (`basis.rs`, ACC.17); there is no default basis.
- **Carrying value** (a read): fair value → the latest mark (K-86) or a named valuer's valuation (K-91, labelled);
  amortised cost → the contract's own amount (K-53) less its provision; lower of cost and NRV → cost less the position's
  write-down; cost less depreciation → K-67's carrying amount less write-down.
- **Unrealised difference** (ACC.3): `unrealised(position) -> Missing<Money>` = units × (latest price − carrying value per
  unit), rounded by the holder's convention; absent where no price exists (Law 8); never stored (ACC.15).
- **Fair value through income**: holders on that basis are a K-06 instance keyed by instrument; at 9a, for each
  instrument whose mark moved today, each such holding's Δmark × units posts to its holder's line and `beside` (Stage 3's
  dealers and funds; 0.9 M positions at the design point).
- **Realisation** (ACC.8): a sale's batch apply (K-60) hands `realise(consumed_cost, proceeds)` per holder through the
  sweep's hook parameter (S1.170; `phx-hold` never names `phx-acct`, `phx-world`'s routing composes the hook); the whole
  difference posts that day to the holder's line (a goods sale's revenue and cost of sales; an instrument's realised
  gain), and the holding's carrying value leaves with the units.
- **Write-downs** (ACC.7 part): `WriteDowns` sparse rows (position ref u32, written down i64) in a block tree keyed by
  position; a write-down is a charge to income on its day; a recovery reverses it only up to the row's amount, so
  carrying never exceeds original cost; ≤ 1 MB at the design point.
- **Provision** (ACC.7 part, BNK.15): `provision(loan) = round(own_amount × rate(holder, grade))`, where the grade (u8,
  the lender's own assessment, in the loans' status word) and the rate per (holder, grade) (the holder's own estimate,
  kept by K-93, S1.338) are the holder's; the rounding is the holder's convention. Every event that changes an input
  (repayment, drawdown, regrading, a re-estimated rate) computes old and new reads and emits `ProvisionMove { holder,
  class, Δ }` into a K-03 day buffer: the Δ posts to the holder's line (an income event) and `beside`, and K-93 folds
  it into its book total. A re-estimated rate for a grade revalues that holder's loans of the grade by a declared sweep
  (K-14) of the loans family's ends on that date (rare). No per-loan provision column.
- **Missing**: absent inputs counted per party in a sparse row, read by S1.330's test.

**Edge cases**:
- E2 no print ever for an instrument: `unrealised` absent, fair-value carrying from a valuation or absent — never 0 —
  `absent_price_absent_difference`.
- E3 a position with no basis chosen: refused at `acquire` — `no_default_basis`.
- E8 `units × price` in `i128` then rounded to `i64`; overflow stops — `product_overflow_stops`.
- E14 a write-down and a sale of one position the same day: the sale consumes the written-down carrying value —
  `sale_after_writedown_realises_from_written_value`.

**Extension points**: `acquire` with a basis; `unrealised` and `carrying_value` reads; `ProvisionMove` folded by books; `WriteDowns` for write-downs to cost; a new basis is ACC.17's declaration within the 2 bits. Steps that depend on it: S1.338, S1.357, S2.102, S2.104, S2.114, S2.116, S3.117, S3.134, S3.163, S3.182, S4.101, S4.153, S4.163, S5.165.
**Unit tests**: `no_default_basis`, `basis_refused_where_form_forbids`, `unrealised_is_units_times_price_less_carrying`,
`absent_price_absent_difference`, `sale_realises_in_full`, `recovery_stops_at_cost`,
`sale_after_writedown_realises_from_written_value`, `provision_is_a_read`, `provision_move_is_income`,
`regrade_moves_provision_by_difference`, `product_overflow_stops`.
**Live checks**: none until its first users (S2.102, S2.104).
**Budget**:
- kernel units, the shares are its users' (S3.163, S3.182, S4.101 mark fair-value holdings; S2.102 moves provisions):
  fair-value marks at `fin.valuation.mark_ns` over ≈ 0.9 M positions at the design point; provision moves 100 k / 0 /
  100 k ≤ 30 VM-ns (`fin.valuation.provision_ns`, added; inside the contract events' sweeps); unrealised reads ≤ 10
  VM-ns (`unrealised_ns`, added).
- ledger line 13 (liens and processes): +1 MB resident (write-down rows ≤ 60 k × 16 B; `writedown_mb`, added); +0 B on
  rows (named slots: the grade and basis bits of the loans' status word).
- `StoreStats` implemented for the write-down rows; the fair-value pass and the regrading sweep report rows through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: a `Basis` has no `Default` (PC-14); PC-29 lists `carrying.rs` as the only writer of write-down rows.
**Not allowed**: a stored unrealised difference; a stored provision per loan; carrying above cost for goods of a
non-dealer (ACC.15); a basis read from a kind's name.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `carrying.rs` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F carrying` at the design point within its ratchets.
- [ ] §7.12 "Carrying values" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.333 — Statements (K-90)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: ACC.16 FORBID
**Architecture**: §7.12 "Statements" written.
**Depends on**: S1.328 (the period close hands the lines, in whose pass the statement is written); S1.330 (the equity
account and its period's capital tally); S1.215 (the records store: closed statements kept for their horizon, by
audience); S1.216 (the block codec a filer's accounts and a non-filer's kept lines share).
**Goal**: at each party's own period close a compact statement — income, balance sheet, cash flow, in its own money — is
built as a read of its lines and positions in the close's own pass, checked (ACC.11), and kept as a record for its
declared horizon; no reported number exists that the records do not produce.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/statements.rs` | `Statement` (compact), `Statement::close` (sole constructor), `cash_flow` (indirect), `file` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/statements_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/statements.rs` | -F module: 1.15 M statements on H inside the lines' close; the private records at their horizon |
| `data/shared/ACC.toml` | `ACC.kept_lines`: the statement lines a later read names, kept past the close |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.statements] write_ns = 7`, `private_mb = 17` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.12 "Statements" |

**Design**:
- **Statement** (ACC.9 read): the period's lines as handed (S1.328); the balance sheet read at the close — money
  (accounts), goods and plant at carrying values, holdings, receivables and payables by family (contract sides' own
  amounts), borrowings, equity (S1.330); the cash flow by the indirect method from this statement and the party's
  previous one (read back from K-37). `Statement::close(&lines, &positions)` is the only constructor: no field can be
  set from anything else (ACC.16, compile level), and nothing smooths.
- **Written in the close's pass** (one traversal): the lines' close (S1.328) calls `Statement::close` and appends the
  row, ≤ 7 VM-ns a statement, inside `fin.valuation.close_ns`.
- **Kept** (SET.13): the statement is appended to K-37 as a typed record (publisher = the party, subject = the party,
  period, audience): public when its legal form files (RAT.8, S2.108; the filed accounts in K-37's records line),
  private otherwise; each audience's horizon is a RESOLUTION primitive (SET.17) declared in `perf/design.toml`, never
  shorter than a record-keeping law's POLICY where one is declared. A filer's statement is kept whole as its filed
  accounts (S1.216). A non-filer's private statement is kept only as the lines a later read names (`ACC.kept_lines`:
  turnover, operating profit, interest, net income, and the balance-sheet positions the next cash flow and a lender's
  review read — money, receivables, payables, inventories, plant, borrowings, equity), in S1.216's block codec with
  the audience a column: ≈ 24 B a statement, ≈ 0.7 M non-filers at one period ≈ 17 MB. The rest of a private statement
  is handed to the close's readers in the pass and not kept; a later reader of another line declares it kept, with
  its bytes.
- **When**: 9b, on each party's period end (K-43 reason `books`), on the pool by party range.
- **Missing**: an absent carrying value makes the statement's affected lines absent, reported unreadable; never 0.

**Edge cases**:
- E5 a calendar quarter end closing most firms: 1.15 M statements on H inside the close's pass — `close_pass_writes_statement`.
- E9 private statements grow to their horizon, then flat — `horizon_prunes_whole_chunks`.
- E10 a party ending mid-period: its last statement closes into its estate — `ending_closes_last_statement`.
- E11 the first close after the opening reads the opening's latest filed statement (GEN.5) as its previous one —
  `first_cash_flow_from_opening`.
- E12 an absent carrying value: the affected line absent — `absent_value_absent_line`.
- E13 a later read of a private line not declared kept: refused at assembly — `unkept_private_line_refused`.

**Extension points**: `Statement` records read by audience; a new statement line is a `LineSet` or position
declaration; a new audience is a K-37 declaration with its horizon. Steps that depend on it: S1.334, S1.486, S2.105, S2.108, S2.116, S2.119, S2.186, S2.196, S3.117, S3.137, S3.209, S8.104, S5.104, S5.110, S5.165.
**Unit tests**: `statement_only_from_lines_and_positions` (compile-fail), `cash_flow_indirect_reconciles_to_money`,
`close_pass_writes_statement`, `ending_closes_last_statement`, `first_cash_flow_from_opening`,
`horizon_prunes_whole_chunks`, `absent_value_absent_line`, `unkept_private_line_refused`, `private_kept_lines_round_trip`.
**Live checks**: none (first readers S2.105, S2.108).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.close_books: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms of its own (B / NB / H) — the statement's write
  (`fin.statements.write_ns` ≤ 7 VM-ns, added) is inside S1.328's share and `fin.valuation.close_ns`.
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +17 MB resident (0.7 M private statements' kept lines × 24 B;
  `private_mb`, added).
- saved: +17 MB.
- `StoreStats` implemented through K-37's record kinds; the close's traversal reports rows through
  `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: PC-29 lists `statements.rs` as the only constructor of a `Statement`.
**Not allowed**: a statement field set by hand; a smoothed or interpolated figure; a second traversal of the parties for
the statements.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `statements.rs` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F statements` at the design point: `write_ns` ≤ 7, private statements ≤ 17 MB; no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §7.12 "Statements" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.334 — Consolidation (K-90)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: ACC.5 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.12 "Statements" — its paragraph "Consolidation" written.
**Depends on**: S1.333 (members' closed statements); S1.283 (owners onto equity holdings: control is read over them);
S1.280 (holders by instrument: each member's equity holders); S1.254 (settlement tallies by reason: intra-group sales
for eliminations).
**Goal**: a group's consolidated statement is a pure read at its reporting date — control as the least fixed point over
equity votes, intra-group claims and trades eliminated, minorities shown — spread over each group's own reporting lag;
each member keeps its own books and nothing consolidated is stored.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/consolidate.rs` | `control` (least fixed point), `consolidate(group, day) -> Consolidated` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/consolidate_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/consolidate.rs` | -F module: 1 k groups of ≤ 100 members over a report season |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.statements] consolidate_us = 50` (added) |

**Design**:
- **Control** (ACC.5): `control(party)` is the least fixed point of control over equity holdings (K-65's holders of each
  member's equity instrument), a party controlling another where its own and its controlled members' votes pass the
  accounting standard's declared threshold (POLICY, ACC.17); computed by a worklist from direct holdings at the group's
  reporting date.
- **Consolidate**: sums the members' closed statements (S1.333), eliminates contracts whose two ends are both members
  (walking members' lists and person chains) and the period's intra-group sales (a K-52 tally keyed (member,
  counterparty member), declared only for parties in a group), and shows the minority's share of equity and income.
- **When**: each group's reporting date is its period end plus its own declared reporting lag, so a report season's
  consolidations spread over its business days (N8.9); 9b, on the pool by group.

**Edge cases**:
- E10 a member ending mid-period: control re-read without it — `ended_member_leaves_group`.
- E13 a group spanning two currencies: members' statements translated at the day's fixing (FX, from S5.159); until then
  a group is within one country — `one_currency_group_until_fx`.
- E14 a cross-holding loop (two members holding each other): the least fixed point terminates — `cross_holding_terminates`.

**Extension points**: `consolidate` and `control` read by a group's tests and reports. Steps that depend on it: S1.360, S3.157, S3.209.
**Unit tests**: `control_is_least_fixed_point`, `eliminations_remove_intra_group_claims_both_sides`, `minority_share_shown`,
`ended_member_leaves_group`, `one_currency_group_until_fx`, `cross_holding_terminates`.
**Live checks**: none (first readers S3.157).
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.consolidation (each group's reporting date = its period end + its declared lag): ≈ 50 core-ms a
  report season spread over its business days, ≤ 5 core-ms on the heaviest day (≈ 100 groups × ≤ 50 VM-µs,
  `fin.statements.consolidate_us`, added); joins H | B′ at ≤ 5 core-ms.
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (a pure read).
- Traversals report rows through `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: PC-29: no consolidated statement stored.
**Not allowed**: a stored consolidated statement; limited liability pooled across members; a group read by a kind's name.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `consolidate.rs` and its tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F consolidate` at the design point within its ratchet; no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §7.12's consolidation paragraph written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.335 — Valuations and curves (K-91)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: kernel
**Clauses**: MKT.20 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §7.12 "Valuations and curves" written; §8's valuation paragraph restated.
**Depends on**: S1.326 (prints, marks and fixings: every input a valuation reads); S1.180 (the kind catalogue: valuers'
methods declared as data, MKT.21); S1.215 (records: published valuations kept with their audience).
**Goal**: named valuers value positions that have no print of their own by published methods whose inputs are prints,
each valuation labelled with its inputs and their ages; curve publishers fit labelled curves from the day's fixings and
publish the day's discount-factor tables; no valuation ever becomes a print.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/valuation.rs` | `ValuerDecl`, `Valuation` (value, valuer, method, inputs with ages, label), `value` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/curve.rs` | `Curve` (publisher, day, points labelled traded/interpolated/extrapolated), `CurveMethod` (closed set), `fit`, `DfTable` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-acct/src/valuation_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/curves.rs` | -F module: 30 curves from the instruments' fixings (`perf/design.toml` `[store] instruments`); 1 M valuations |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.valuation] curve_us = 100`, `df_us = 50`, `value_ns = 50`, `position_ns = 4`, `df_mb = 2` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.12 "Valuations and curves" |

**Design**:
- **Valuers** (MKT.20, MKT.21): a `ValuerDecl` names the valuer (a party), its published method (a closed set the
  kernel implements as pure functions, each labelled: a clearing house's settlement price from members' trades and
  submissions, a pricing service's fixing, comparable sales, a statutory roll, discounting at the day's traded rates),
  and the prints or fixings the method may read; declared by the valuer's system as POLICY of the valuer. A method
  outside the set is a kernel step of its own.
- **`Valuation`** carries `value: Money` (rounded by the valuer's convention), the valuer, the method, up to eight
  inputs as (print or fixing ref, age in days), and its label (traded, interpolated, extrapolated). It has no
  conversion to `Print` (K-86): it cannot enter a market, an index or a mark (MKT.14, VAL.20), compile level. Readers
  (margin, NAV, LTV, tax bases, provisions, resolution) take it where their rule says so.
- **By instrument, not by position**: a method is applied once per (valuer, instrument, method) on a valuation day,
  giving a unit value (`Fixed`, unrounded); a position in that instrument is `units × unit value`, rounded once by the
  valuer's convention. For a payoff linear in the units held this equals valuing the position whole, since the method
  would multiply the same unit price by the same units before its one rounding. A payoff that is not linear in what is
  held (an option, a credit default swap, a contract whose terms are its own) is valued per contract. A valuation a rule reads later
  is written to K-37 with its audience (an assessor's roll, a settlement price); otherwise it is a transient value.
- **Curves** (6c): a publisher's `fit(method, fixings) -> Curve` on the day's fixings (K-86) — points at traded tenors
  labelled traded, between them interpolated, beyond the longest traded point extrapolated by the publisher's declared
  method; a curve never takes its own earlier output as an observation (SOV.9 holds by the type: `fit` reads fixings
  only). `DfTable`: discount factors on a day grid to the curve's longest traded point (`Fixed` i64), beyond it by the
  method's extrapolation formula; one table per curve per day, today's only (history is the fixings', K-86).
- **Absent**: no fixing for a tenor leaves the point absent; a valuation whose inputs are all absent is absent (Law 8),
  never 0; its inputs' ages always shown.
- **Where**: curves and tables at 6c (B, markets that met); valuations at 9a on each valuer's dates, on the pool by
  valuer.

**Edge cases**:
- E2 a market that met without a trade: its tenor absent, the curve interpolates across it and labels it —
  `untraded_tenor_interpolated_and_labelled`.
- E11 day zero: the opening's fixings are series of one (GEN.5); curves fit from them — `curve_from_opening_fixings`.
- E13 a currency with no traded tenor at all: no curve that day; readers see the last one with its age —
  `no_trade_no_curve`.
- E7 valuers on the pool by valuer; each valuation a pure function of handed inputs — `valuation_pure`.
- E12 a valuation whose inputs are all absent: absent, never 0 — `absent_inputs_absent_valuation`.
- E3 a position in an instrument whose payoff is not linear in units: valued per contract — `nonlinear_valued_per_contract`.

**Extension points**: `ValuerDecl` with a method from the closed set; `Valuation` read where a rule says so; `Curve` and `DfTable` read by discounting. Steps that depend on it: S1.340, S1.341, S1.347, S2.103, S2.106, S2.133, S2.141, S2.196, S3.107, S3.115, S3.127, S3.143, S3.170, S3.184, S4.106, S4.112, S4.133, S4.134, S4.136, S4.140, S4.152, S5.112, S7.101.
**Unit tests**: `valuation_cannot_become_a_print` (compile-fail), `inputs_ages_carried`,
`beyond_longest_traded_point_extrapolated`, `untraded_tenor_interpolated_and_labelled`, `curve_never_reads_itself`
(compile-fail), `df_table_monotone_where_rates_positive`, `curve_from_opening_fixings`, `no_trade_no_curve`,
`valuation_pure`, `absent_inputs_absent_valuation`, `position_value_is_units_times_instrument_value`,
`nonlinear_valued_per_contract`.
**Live checks**: none (first users S2.106).
**Budget**:
- kernel units, the shares are the users' (S3.127, S3.169, S4.106 fit curves; every valuer's step values): a fit ≤ 100
  VM-µs (`fin.valuation.curve_us`, added) and its table ≤ 50 VM-µs (`df_us`, added), ≈ 30 curves a business day at the
  design point; a unit value or a per-contract valuation ≤ 50 VM-ns plus its inputs' reads (`value_ns`, added), a
  position ≤ 4 VM-ns (`position_ns`, added). At the design point's heavy valuation day (1 M valuations): ≤ 20 k unit
  values and ≈ 0.1 M non-linear or own-terms contracts at `value_ns`, ≈ 0.9 M fair-value positions at `position_ns` ≈
  10 VM-ms, against ≈ 50 VM-ms valued position by position.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +2 MB resident (today's tables, ≤ 30 curves × ≤ 11 k days × 8 B; `df_mb`, added).
- `StoreStats` implemented for the day's tables; fits and valuations report items through `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: `Valuation` has no `Into<Print>`; PC-28 re-aimed at K-86's `Print` as the only price a mark or index reads.
**Not allowed**: a valuation stored as a mark; a curve point unlabelled; a discount factor from a rate no fixing
produced; an exponential per flow at valuation (valuers read the table).
**Done when**:
- [ ] `valuation.rs`, `curve.rs` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F curves` at the design point: `curve_us` ≤ 100, `df_us` ≤ 50, `value_ns` ≤ 50, `position_ns` ≤ 4,
  tables ≤ 2 MB.
- [ ] §7.12 "Valuations and curves" written, §8's paragraph restated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the
  section removed.

### S1.336 — Public series and methods (K-92)

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: base
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.13 "phx-val" — its subsection "Public series" written.
**Depends on**: S1.326 (prints and marks: yesterday's prints each series takes); S1.215 (records: published statistics
as published by day d); S1.167 (the horizon ring: yearly means); S1.165 (keyed index: registered pairs by series).
**Goal**: every public series a party forecasts is a dense slot with its header, its yearly means and one cell per
(memory type, age window) in use holding each heuristic's outlook, width and performance, formed once per new print or
release at 5a and read by every party using the method; registered instrument series and series pairs are cells of the
same store.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-val/src/series.rs` | `SeriesKey`, `SeriesDir` (dense per family), `SeriesHead`, `MethodCell`, `take_print`, `outlook_of` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-val/src/pairs.rs` | declared series pairs: a pair's beta per (pair, method) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-val/src/registered.rs` | re-based: registered (method, instrument) pairs as a K-06 instance (its `BTreeMap`s gone) |
| `crates/kernel/phx-val/src/series_tests.rs` | unit tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-fin/src/outlooks.rs` | -F module: 10 k series, their cells, 0.2 M registered pairs; 12 k prints a day B, 6.3 k NB |
| `perf/budget.toml` | `[fin.outlooks] cell_ns = 25`, `core_ms_b = 30`, `core_ms_nb = 8`, `mb = 7` (added) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §7.13 "Public series" |

**Design**:
- The step carries VAL.23 (done at S1.05): its carriers in `phx-world/src/core_outlooks.rs` move to `phx-val/src/series.rs`.
- **Keys and directory**: a series is (family handle, place) — a product's mark per region, a published statistic per
  country, a rate, an instrument (Stage 3), a house price per region (Stage 2); per family a dense directory where the key space
  is dense (250 products × 25 regions), a sorted key column otherwise; slot u32.
- **Header** (≈ 64 B, `Fixed` i64 values, PC-12): last print's day, last and previous print, anchor level as sum and
  count, the direction and the print it last turned at, the sum of squared changes, the current year's sum and count;
  yearly means in a K-08 ring only for series some party reads through an age window (≈ 34 household-read
  series; a year's mean at its close; the ring's horizon the longest age window, never before the snapshot, VAL.23); each age class's experienced level (i32 each) recomputed at a year's close from the
  means — per series, never per household.
- **Cells** (`MethodCell`, per (series, memory type, window) in use): four heuristics' outlooks (`Fixed` i32 relative to
  the last print), four performances (i32), the method's surprise width (i32), a `behind` nibble — 40 B. Only windows
  some party reads exist: households read age windows of their countries' public variables; firms read the no-window
  cell of their products' marks; registered instrument pairs (from S3.134) are 24 B cells in a K-06 instance keyed by series
  (replacing `registered.rs`' two `BTreeMap`s). Series pairs (HH.7's betas, S6.128) are declared pairs whose cell per
  (pair, method) holds the beta and its width, formed on days either series prints (≈ 20 pairs × 120 methods).
- **Forming** (5a, VAL.23, TIME.10): for each series with a print or release yesterday, on the pool by series: the
  header takes the print, each cell forms each heuristic's next outlook (`method::outlook`, the menu's sealed trait),
  scores the last one, updates the width; a cell's surprise wider than its declared sensitivity stamps the cell with
  its day and width (read by K-101's `catch_up` at each party's next visit, S1.350). f64 arithmetic in registers through `libm`, stored `Fixed`; a result no
  `Fixed` holds stops (NUM.6).
- **Reading**: `outlook_of(series, method) -> Missing<Outlook>`, O(1): a method = (heuristic, memory type, window);
  a party's own view of a registered series is its method's plus its own deviation, caught up in O(1) (existing
  `registered.rs` arithmetic kept).
- **Missing**: a series with no print yet has absent outlooks; a decision reading one states what it does while absent
  (VAL.10).

**Edge cases**:
- E2 a market that formed no price: no print, no update; the header's day shows its age — `no_print_no_update`.
- E11 day zero: each series holds GEN.5's single value; heuristic records absent — `opening_series_of_one`.
- E9 yearly means grow one a year to the ring's horizon — `ring_prunes_past_longest_window`.
- E7 series formed on the pool, each by its own slot — `forming_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E13 a country with no rate series: its households' rate outlooks absent, never 0 — `no_series_absent_outlook`.

**Extension points**: a new public variable is a series family declaration; a new pair is a pair declaration; readers call `outlook_of`; registered pairs apply through the K-06 instance. Steps that depend on it: S1.337, S1.350, S1.357, S2.145, S2.146, S2.161, S2.195, S2.201, S3.103, S3.104, S3.105, S3.111, S3.112, S3.113, S3.119, S3.120, S3.131, S3.134, S3.148, S3.165, S3.184, S3.187, S3.204, S3.211, S3.218, S8.108, S8.197, S4.116, S4.131, S4.132, S4.134, S4.150, S4.165, S5.139, S5.140, S5.154, S5.183, S6.106, S6.117, S6.128.
**Unit tests**: `method_cell_forms_each_heuristic`, `score_after_print`, `age_window_never_before_snapshot`,
`yearly_mean_at_year_close`, `registered_pair_counts_by_apply`, `pair_beta_formed_when_either_prints`,
`no_print_no_update`, `opening_series_of_one`, `ring_prunes_past_longest_window`, `forming_same_for_any_chunking`,
`fixed_overflow_stops`, `no_series_absent_outlook`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-02 (no outlook formed after the stage that uses it, VAL.11) and LC-1-04 (no common expectation,
VAL.16) re-aimed at the store.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 30 / 8 / 30 core-ms (B / NB / H) — 12 k / 6.3 k / 12 k prints a day, each its cells
  at ≤ 25 VM-ns a cell (`fin.outlooks.cell_ns`, `core_ms_b`, `core_ms_nb`, added).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +6.8 MB resident (≈ 10 k series × 64 B, 31 k firm cells and 1.2 k household cells
  × 40 B, 0.2 M registered pairs × 24 B, pairs; `fin.outlooks.mb` 7, added).
- `StoreStats` implemented; the 5a pass reports series and cells through `ExecCounters::visited`.
**Guards**: PC-33 (outlooks formed by the menu from what they are handed) re-aimed at `series.rs`; PC-92 covers it;
`registered.rs`' map sites removed from `exceptions/PC-92.toml`.
**Not allowed**: a series per household; a `Vec` allocated per print; an outlook formed by reading a party's private
state; a window reaching before the snapshot.
**Done when**:
- [ ] `series.rs`, `pairs.rs`, the re-based `registered.rs` and their tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F outlooks` at the design point within its ratchets.
- [ ] §7.13 "Public series" written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
