### S1.140 — Balances written at endings become flows

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §9.1 (endings) followed.
**Depends on**: none.
**Goal**: when a firm or a household ends, the money in its account moves to its estate by a flow that settlement
applies (Law 5), never by writing both balances; the estate opens with an empty account at the same bank.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_default.rs` | `end_firm` issues the passing flow |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_pop.rs` | `end_household` issues the passing flow |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_day.rs` | `open_estate` begins the estate with an empty account; the day's close checks no ended account holds a residue |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/consts.rs` | `reason::PASSED`, a flow reason |

**Design**:
- The defect: `end_firm` (`core_default.rs`) and `end_household` (`core_pop.rs`) read the ended party's balance and
  pending, begin the estate with that balance (`open_estate`, `core_day.rs`, `store.begin(…, Opening { bank, balance:
  money })`) and set the ended account to zero — money moved with no instruction (SET.11) and no flow the money audit
  reads (MON.8).
- `passing_flow(ended, estate, (balance, pending), ccy) -> Option<Flow>`: a pure function; the whole money the ended
  party holds at its ending, payer the ended party, payee its estate, reason `PASSED`, in its currency; none when it
  holds none. It is pushed onto the day's pending flows. Both endings run before the day's settlement (hazards at stage
  3, defaults in labour), so it settles that day (on a closed day it is committed, as every flow is); SET.7: an
  instruction naming a party that ended during the day is settled against its estate.
- The flow carries the highest payment order (`Flow::order`), so any other flow naming the payer that day settles or
  fails first (SET.6).
- `open_estate` begins the estate with `Opening { bank, balance: 0 }`.
- At the day's close, before the slots of the day's endings are released, an ended party's account holding anything
  is a contract violation (SET.7) naming it and the amount — the check that the flow carried all of it.
- The direct balance writers left in `phx-world` after this step: none (the save's fault-injection test harness,
  `save/inject.rs`, is test-only); S1.158 re-aims PC-25 at settlement's apply.
- Moved first by S1.344 (endings onto the ending kernel, K-97, which moves every row naming the party).
- It carries SET.11, MON.8, SET.7 (done at S0.15) and PTY.9 (done at S0.25).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a household with no money and no shares opens no estate and issues no flow — `zero_money_passes_nothing`.
- E1: many endings on one day each issue one flow, grouped like any other — `many_endings_one_flow_each`.
- E14: an ending and a wage due to the same household the same day: the wage settles to the household's account and
  the passing flow, ordered last, carries it on — `passing_ordered_last`.
- E10: the ended slot is released only after the day's settlement, so the flow never names a reused slot —
  `residue_after_close_stops`.
- E5: on a closed day the flow is committed with the day's others and final on the next business day — LC-0-18 (the
  money identity) over a run crossing a weekend.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `ending_money_passes_by_flow`, `zero_money_passes_nothing`, `many_endings_one_flow_each`,
`passing_ordered_last` (the flow's payment order), `residue_after_close_stops`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-18 (the money identity) and LC-0-53 (estates' standing) keep passing; from the first ending.
**Budget**: no share of any `[fin.*]` line (today's code; S1.344 carries endings at the design point); resident bytes:
none. One flow an ending.
**Guards**: none here; S1.158 re-aims PC-25 at the writers that remain.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a balance or pending written outside settlement's apply or the opening; an estate begun with money.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The flow, the check and the tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's run at fewer persons passes with LC-0-18 and LC-0-53 read and at least one ending of each kind, and
  reads the budget with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.148 — Numeric literals in mechanisms declared

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §16 (drift guards) written: PC-06 no longer exempts array lengths and indices.
**Depends on**: S1.147 (the agencies' declared activity); S1.144 (the issuer's classes read by form).
**Goal**: no mechanism carries as a literal a count of money classes, a labour state's place, a dataset's column or an
iteration count; each is a typed enumeration of what the spec names or is read from its declaration, and the opening's
fixed point is solved exactly rather than iterated to a hidden bound.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_central.rs`, `core_day.rs` | the issuer's money classes as `IssuerClass` |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/consts.rs` | `LabourState` (employed; unemployed and searching; out of the labour force), replacing `LABOUR_STATES` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_stats.rs` | `labour_force` counts by `LabourState` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/consts.rs`, `core_firms.rs`, `core_jobs.rs`, `core_goods.rs`, `opening/asked.rs` | public administration's column found by `SOC.agency_activity`; `PUBLIC_ADMINISTRATION` deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/opening/leontief.rs` | `solve(inputs, finals) -> Result<Vec<f64>, Refusal>`, the exact solution of x = A·x + f |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/literals.rs` | PC-06 without the array-length and index exemption |

**Design**:
- The issuer's money classes: `[i128; 3]` in `Central::recorded`, `issuer_held` (`core_central.rs`) and `money_breaks`
  (`core_day.rs`), with its names array and `if class == NOTES { "MON.9" } else { "MON.7" }`, become
  `IssuerClass { Reserves, StateAccounts, Notes }` — the three MON.7 and MON.9 name — with `ALL`, `COUNT`, `name()` and
  the clause its identity checks; arrays are `[i128; IssuerClass::COUNT]`, indexed by the class.
- Labour states at literal places 0, 1, 2 (`labour_force`, `core_stats.rs`): `if-state`'s `LabourState`, a person's
  state counted at its variant.
- `PUBLIC_ADMINISTRATION = 21` (`consts.rs`), read by `open_firms`, `open_jobs`, `open_goods` and `Asked`
  (`opening/asked.rs`): the column found by `SOC.agency_activity`'s code in the accounts' activity list at the opening,
  refused where absent.
- The opening's fixed point `for _ in 0..n * n` (`open_expected`, `core_goods.rs`): what the ways use to make the final
  demand is x = (I − A)⁻¹ f, solved by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting over the n products (at the opening
  only); a matrix with no non-negative solution (not productive) is refused at the opening naming the country. No
  iteration count, no tolerance.
- PC-06 today exempts array lengths and indices; it refuses them above 2 in mechanism code, with the engineering
  constants of a crate's `consts` item exempt as today.
- Moved first by S1.243 (maintained money totals, K-47), S1.221 (statistics accumulators) and the steps opening
  firms and jobs (S1.483, S1.412), which keep the enumerations and the declared column.
- It carries NUM.3 (done at S0.09), MON.7 and MON.9 (done at S0.15).

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a country whose accounts lack the declared activity is refused — `agency_activity_column_missing_refused`.
- E12: a singular or non-productive input matrix is refused, never iterated — `non_productive_matrix_refused`.
- E11: the opening solves once and no day reads the solver — `leontief_solves_exactly`.

**Extension points**: a later money class (a foreign issuer's deposits, S5.159) is an `IssuerClass` variant with its clause;
a later labour state (S6.115) a `LabourState` variant.
**Unit tests**: `leontief_solves_exactly` (a 2×2 and a 3×3 with known inverses), `non_productive_matrix_refused`,
`issuer_classes_indexed_by_variant`, `labour_state_counted_at_its_variant`, `agency_activity_column_missing_refused`,
`pc06_refuses_array_length_three`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-26 (the issuers' money classes) and LC-1-37 keep passing with the same values.
**Budget**: no share of any `[fin.*]` line (today's code); resident bytes: none. The opening's fixed point falls from up
to n² sweeps to one solve.
**Guards**: PC-06 extended as above; the sites removed.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an iteration bound or tolerance standing for an exact solution; a dataset column by position.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The enumerations, the solver, PC-06 and the tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's run at fewer persons passes, the committed setup opening with the same expected demands to the
  solver's rounding, and reads the budget with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §16 states PC-06's reach; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.149 — An employment's notice cleared on every close

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.18 followed.
**Depends on**: S1.145 (the jobs families by their declared flag).
**Goal**: a job under notice that closes by any path — separation, the employer's ending, quitting, retirement, the
person leaving or its household ending — leaves no notice behind, so a later hire into the reused contract slot is seen
by `staff_of` and `lay_off`.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `close_job`, the one closing path of a job; `hire` refuses a slot under notice |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_pop.rs`, `core_default.rs`, `core_agencies.rs` | their job closes go through `close_job` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour_tests.rs` | the unit tests below |

**Design**:
- The defect: `labour.noticed: BTreeSet<u32>` (`core_labour.rs`) holds the edge slots of jobs under notice; `separate`,
  `close_contracts` (`core_default.rs`) and `quit_jobs` (`core_agencies.rs`) remove them, but `leave_jobs`,
  `person_left` and `end_household` (`core_pop.rs`) close jobs under notice and leave the slot in the set. The edge
  slot is reused by a later hire, which `staff_of`, `review_wages` and `lay_off` then skip until the old separation
  date.
- `close_job(&mut self, family: FamilyH, edge: Slot)`: removes the notice and closes the contract; every close of a
  contract in a jobs family goes through it (the loops of `person_left` and `end_household` over every family call it
  for jobs families by S1.145's flag).
- `hire` opening a job in a slot still in `noticed` is a contract violation (LAB.16) naming the slot: the check that no
  path is missed.
- Moved first by S1.266 (arrears, grace and notice onto status, K-56: notice a contract's own status, gone with its
  row).
- It serves LAB.1 (done at S1.08; S4.145 retires its placeholder) and carries LAB.16 (done at S1.08).

**Edge cases**:
- E10: a slot closed and reused on the same day starts with no notice — `close_job_clears_notice`,
  `hire_into_noticed_slot_stops`.
- E14: a notice given and the person retiring the same day close the job once, through one path —
  `notice_and_retirement_close_once`.
- E6: `noticed` is saved as it is; no index to rebuild — `noticed_round_trips`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `close_job_clears_notice` and `hire_into_noticed_slot_stops` (a hand-built jobs `Family` fixture of a
few contracts and a notice set), `every_jobs_close_goes_through_close_job` (the closers' family filter by flag),
`notice_and_retirement_close_once`, `noticed_round_trips`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-21 (LAB.13's employment identity) and LC-1-22 (LAB.14) keep passing; from the first separation.
**Budget**: no share of any `[fin.*]` line (today's code; S1.266 carries notice at the design point); resident bytes:
none.
**Guards**: none.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a second path that closes a job.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The path, the check and the tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's run at fewer persons at `-d 60` (retirements and separations under notice both reached) passes and
  reads the budget with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.150 — Measurement histories held by declared horizons

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §11 (persistence) followed: what is saved stays within its horizon.
**Depends on**: none.
**Goal**: five histories that grow without bound over a run — the tax sample, the surprise responses, the deaths, the
followed catastrophes and the published releases — each keep only the records within a declared horizon (RESOLUTION),
and each reader reads within it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/shared/SET.toml` | `SET.horizon_days` per history: tax sample, surprise responses, deaths, shocks, releases |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_taxes.rs`, `core_outlooks.rs`, `core_pop.rs`, `core_weather.rs`, `core_stats.rs` | each history dated and pruned at the day's close |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/horizon.rs` | `expired(dates, today, horizon) -> usize` and the amortised prune |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/{core,outlooks,geo,lives}.rs` | their reads stated over the horizon |

**Design**:
- The stores: `Taxes::sample` (one row a sampled wage, written by `withhold`), `Outlooks::responses` (written in
  `core_goods.rs` after a surprise), `Core::deaths` (`core_pop.rs`), `Weather::shocks` (`weather_day`,
  `core_weather.rs`, each with a clone of the day's marks, and walked by `note_rises` every day for every shock ever),
  `CoreStats::published` (`stats_day`, `core_stats.rs`).
- Each record carries its day (the sample and the responses gain it); each history declares its horizon in days, a
  RESOLUTION primitive (SET.17), set at two years, and never shorter than what its readers compare (none follows a
  POLICY). At the day's close records older than the horizon are dropped: the history is appended in day order, so they
  are a prefix, found by binary search; the prefix is drained once it is at least half the store, so each record moves
  at most once on average and no day moves the whole store.
- `note_rises` walks only the shocks within their horizon; a shock's base marks stay those of its day (GDS.11 follows
  every market's rise).
- The live checks reading them (`deaths_destined`, `responses_by_size`, the tax sample check, the shocks' reads, the
  life tables) read the records within the horizon; a gate run's reads are over its last two years.
- Moved first by S1.167 (the horizon ring, K-08), S1.214 (deaths and weather records onto the event log), S1.218
  (releases onto records) and S1.221 (samples in statistics' frames), whose horizons these declarations become.
- It carries SET.13 and SET.17 (done at S0.20).

**Edge cases**:
- E9: over a run longer than a horizon each store stays flat at its horizon — `pruned_store_flat_after_horizon`, and
  the bench's `StoreStats` rows ever against rows live.
- E6: a save holds the records within the horizon and the load prunes nothing more —
  `saved_history_within_horizon_round_trips`.
- E11: an empty history on day zero prunes nothing — `expired_of_empty_is_none`.

**Extension points**: S1.167's ring takes these horizons as its capacity by days.
**Unit tests**: `expired_counts_the_old_prefix`, `expired_of_empty_is_none`, `prune_moves_each_record_once_amortised`,
`pruned_store_flat_after_horizon`, `saved_history_within_horizon_round_trips`, `horizon_read_from_register`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-53, LC-1-15, LC-1-44 and LC-1-51 read within the horizon and keep passing.
**Budget**: no share of any `[fin.*]` line (today's code; S1.167 and S1.214–S1.221 carry histories at the design
point); resident bytes: bounded by the horizons, none added. A binary search a history a day; drains amortised O(1) a
record.
**Guards**: none.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a history with no declared horizon; a daily walk of every record ever kept.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The horizons, the pruning and the tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's run at fewer persons passes and reads the budget with no ratchet broken; a run past a horizon shows
  the five stores' `StoreStats` rows ever and live apart.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.151 — Dates placed by the calendar, not counted

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §6.6 (cost bounds) followed: O(log n) per operation.
**Depends on**: none.
**Goal**: every date the day's code finds by counting from the start — a hire's first pay date, a project's ready day,
a release's business day, a bill issue's place, the audit's births and deaths — is placed by the calendar or an index
in O(log n) or O(1), whatever the run's length.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/calendar/period.rs` | `ScheduleDates::first_after(calendar, day) -> u32` |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/src/calendar/mod.rs` | `Calendar::nth_business(country, from, k)` over a per-country business-day ordinal of the window |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs`, `core_plant.rs`, `core_stats.rs`, `core_bills.rs`, `core_audit.rs` | the sites below |
| `crates/kernel/phx-core/public-api.txt` | the snapshot |

**Design**:
- `hire` (`core_labour.rs`) counts dates from the schedule's first (`while dates.nth(…, nth) <= day { nth += 1 }`),
  linear in the schedule's age. `first_after`: `nth` is non-decreasing in n, so an exponential then binary search finds
  the first date after `day` in O(log n).
- `start_project` (`core_plant.rs`) adds the lead one day at a time: `calendar.plus(day, Period::days(lead))`.
- `release_day` (`core_stats.rs`) steps business days one by one: `nth_business` reads the k-th business day from a
  per-country ordinal of the calendar's window (2 bytes a day a country, built with the window, rebuilt at load, moved
  with `move_window`).
- `Bills::issues` is searched linearly by `open_bill` and summed by filter for what matures by `offer`
  (`core_bills.rs`), and grows forever: issues are kept per country sorted by maturity (binary insertion among the live
  issues, about a year's weekly issues a country), the day's issue found at its place, what matures in (day, next]
  summed over the range found by binary search, and an issue leaves on its maturity (the live check reads only live
  issues).
- `audit` (`core_audit.rs`) folds every day's births and deaths: running totals of born and gone, advanced where the
  day's record is written.
- Moved first by S1.178 (the calendar's per-day facts, K-19), S1.264 (reckoning onto shared plans), S1.282 (bills
  onto instruments) and S1.220 (per-day records onto the day ledger).
- It carries TIME.4 (done at S0.08).

**Edge cases**:
- E11: a schedule whose first date is after today gives n = 0 — `first_after_before_first_date`.
- E5: a release on a month opening with closed days lands on its k-th business day — `nth_business_skips_closed_days`.
- E9: a two-year run's hire costs the same as day one's — `first_after_is_logarithmic` (counts the `nth` calls).
- E6: the ordinal is rebuilt at load and the calendar hashes equal — `ordinal_rebuilt_equal`.

**Extension points**: `first_after` and `nth_business` serve every schedule of K-55 (S1.263) and K-19 (S1.178).
**Unit tests**: `first_after_before_first_date`, `first_after_matches_linear_count`, `first_after_is_logarithmic`,

### S1.154 — Production, orders and the opening's needs return actions, not floors

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.18 followed.
**Depends on**: none.
**Goal**: where a firm's making, a buyer's order or the opening's dealing of jobs can be "nothing", the rule returns
that action instead of flooring a number at zero by comparison.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `planned` returns `Plan::{Make(q), Rest}` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/inputs.rs` | `order` returns `Order::{Buy(units), None}` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_jobs.rs` | `net_needs` returns each firm's `Need::{Jobs(x), MetByOwners}` |

**Design**:
- The sites, each `if x > 0.0 { x } else { 0.0 }`: `planned` (`core_goods.rs`), `order` (`sys-frm`'s inputs rule),
  `net_needs` (`core_jobs.rs`). Clippy already refuses `min`, `max` and `clamp`; these are the same floor written as a
  comparison.
- None of FRM.4, FRM.7 or GDS.5 states a floor. What each decides is a choice among actions, one of which is to do
  nothing: a firm makes some quantity or rests (FRM.4; a stock above its aim is run down by selling, the price review's
  clearing, FRM.5); a buyer orders some units of an input or none (GDS.5; stock above the plan is held, and a
  stockist's sale is GDS.6's); a firm's owners meet its need or it takes jobs (the opening's dealing, a count of jobs).
  Each returns its action as an enum variant; the caller matches it.
- Moved first by the production and input-order rules of S1.443 and S1.444, which keep the action enums ("doing
  nothing is the rule's action").
- It carries FRM.7 (done at S1.08) and NUM.8 (done at S0.09), and serves FRM.4 (completed at S1.443) and GDS.5
  (completed at S1.444).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a market with no buyer leaves a firm's stock above its aim; it rests, and the price review clears it —
  `overstocked_firm_rests`.
- E12: an action is never read as a number where the rule rests — `rest_is_not_zero_units`.
- E11: day zero's first plans are the same actions — `opening_plan_is_an_action`.

**Extension points**: every later decision states "nothing" as an action of its option set (Stage 4 on, K-100/K-102's
`OptionSet`).
**Unit tests**: `overstocked_firm_rests`, `rest_is_not_zero_units`, `order_none_when_covered`, `owners_meet_need`,
`opening_plan_is_an_action`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-05 and LC-1-07 keep passing with the same values.
**Budget**: no share of any `[fin.*]` line (today's code); resident bytes: none.
**Guards**: none here; S1.155 adds PC-110.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a floor, cap or clamp by comparison.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The actions and the tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's run at fewer persons passes and reads the budget with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.155 — The bill offer returns an action; no floor by comparison

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: repair
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §16 (drift guards) written: PC-110.
**Depends on**: S1.154 (the other floors gone, so PC-110 passes on the tree).
**Goal**: the treasury's bill offer returns "no offer" as an action; the one floor left, inside a declared placeholder,
is listed by name; and `phx-check` refuses any new floor or cap by comparison in mechanisms.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules.rs` | `size` returns `Offer::{Face(f), None}`; its outflow floor listed as the placeholder's |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/floors.rs` | PC-110 and its tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/exceptions/PC-110.toml` | the named placeholder floor |
| `perf/ratchets.toml` | `phx_check.exceptions_pc110` |

**Design**:
- `size` (`sys-sov`'s rules) floors the offered face at zero and its week's outflow at zero. SOV.3 states no floor: the
  treasury offers some face or none, `Offer::None` when nothing is needed.
- The outflow floor (a week of net inflow read as no outflow) is part of the rule the code declares a placeholder naming
  TRS; it stays, listed by name in `exceptions/PC-110.toml` with "placeholder naming TRS, retired by the treasury's
  funding plan (S3.119)".
- **PC-110** — no floor or cap by comparison in mechanisms: in mechanism code (`sys-*`, `phx-world`, the kernel
  crates), refuses an `if`/`else` whose one arm is the compared value and whose other is a literal zero (`0`, `0.0`;
  `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`; either order of the comparison), and the same with the arms swapped. It does not match an arm
  that builds an enum variant: a function returning a declared option or action enum states that doing nothing is an
  action. Exceptions are listed by function in `exceptions/PC-110.toml`, each with its clause or placeholder, never
  exempt by pattern; the file's count is the down-ratchet `phx_check.exceptions_pc110`.
- Moved first by the bill auction's sizing (S3.119), which retires the placeholder and its exception.
- It serves SOV.3 (completed at S3.119).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a treasury whose cash covers its buffer offers nothing — `offer_none_when_cash_suffices`.
- E12: an exception without its clause or placeholder is refused — `pc110_exception_needs_its_clause`.

**Extension points**: every later mechanism is held to PC-110.
**Unit tests**: `offer_none_when_cash_suffices`, `pc110_refuses_value_or_zero`, `pc110_refuses_swapped_arms`,
`pc110_passes_action_enum`, `pc110_exception_needs_its_clause`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-29 keeps passing with the same values.
**Budget**: no share of any `[fin.*]` line (today's code); resident bytes: none.
**Guards**: PC-110; `exceptions/PC-110.toml` holds one entry.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a floor, cap or clamp by comparison; an exception by pattern.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The action, PC-110, its exception file, its ratchet and the tests; the fast checks pass on the current tree.
- [ ] The bench's run at fewer persons passes and reads the budget with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] §16 states PC-110; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.158 — Vacuous `phx-check` rules re-aimed

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: tool
**Clauses**: none

**Depends on**: S1.140 (no balance is written outside settlement's apply, so PC-25's re-aim passes).

writers of what they protect; PC-27 loses its entry for deleted files; each base step that later moves a target
carries the rule with it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/ledger_writes.rs` | PC-24 re-aimed |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/money_moves.rs` | PC-25 re-aimed |

**Design**: each rule, what it names today (none of which exists) and what it guards after:
- **PC-24** (`ledger_writes.rs`: `RelationshipRows`, `Lots`, `NamedUnits`, `phx-pop/src/holder.rs`): holdings are
  written by the goods kernel alone — no code outside `phx-core/src/goods.rs` and `units.rs` assigns a `Holding`'s
  fields or builds a `Holding`; world code changes holdings only through `Stocks`' methods. S1.271 and S1.272
  (holdings, K-60) move the target to `phx-hold`.
- **PC-25** (`money_moves.rs`: the ledger's `add_row`, `set_count` …, `LegDigest`): balances and pending are written by
  settlement's apply (`phx-core/src/settle.rs`) and by an account's opening (`KindStore::begin`, `open_account`, from
  opening code) alone; refuses `.balance.set(`, `.pending.set(` and a mutable slice of either elsewhere in world
  crates. The save's fault-injection harness (`save/inject.rs`, test-only) is outside world code. S1.240 and S1.244
  (money accounts, K-47) move the target to `phx-ledger`.
- **PC-27** (`batches.rs`: `phx-ledger`'s `stream.rs`, `fixed_point.rs`, `apply_batch.rs`, `batch.rs`): the entry is

### Stage 1 on the core

---

### Stage 1 on the core (S1.400–S1.499)

After the core's close (S1.360) every base the world needs exists and the per-party structures `phx-world` held are
gone, but the Stage 0–1 rules still sit in `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_*.rs`, reading the bases. This group
moves each rule into its `sys-*` crate as a pure function over the views a base hands it, with `phx-world` keeping only
the routing (one mechanism a step; a `core_*.rs` module is deleted with its last mechanism); completes the Stage 1
clauses that are built wrong, partly or not at all; maps the opening's remaining sources from the data in hand, one
mapping a step; brings firm births into Stage 1 (Part O's exit: firms are born and die); builds the estimators the
stage's exit reads (N3, N4); and closes the stage at its gate.

**Exit** (Part O, Stage 1): households earn wages and spend them at firms that pay wages, firms are born and die,
banks lend and are repaid, the treasury taxes and spends, the world keeps doing so without anything imposed, and a
simulated year of it at the play resolution meets N8, measured as N8.8 says: on the stage's own world by
`tools/bench.sh -g`, and at the design point by `tools/bench.sh -F all`.

**Order.** Stage 1's reads frozen (S1.400); population and persons (S1.401–S1.406); the institutions' opening
(S1.407–S1.410); labour (S1.411–S1.424); banks, money and the state (S1.425–S1.435); firms' costs and production
(S1.436–S1.447); households, prices and outlooks (S1.448–S1.456); capital (S1.457–S1.461); weather, freight and
distribution (S1.462–S1.473); statistics and the reads that need them (S1.474, S1.475–S1.477, S1.478, S1.479, S1.480); firms'
opening, founding and day zero (S1.481–S1.491); routing only (S1.492, S1.493); the estimators and liveness
(S1.494–S1.498); the gate (S1.499).

### S1.400 — Stage 1's macro reads frozen

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: docs
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §14.5 (gates: a stage's reads frozen before its code) written.
**Depends on**: S1.358 (the recorder: the series a read names exist and are stamped); S1.360 (the core's close).
**Goal**: before any other code of Stage 1 on the core, the macro reads its gate reports are written into
`data/observer/READS.toml` and frozen by hash: the exit's reads (wages earned and spent, firms born and ended, loans
made and repaid, taxes raised and the state's spending, by month), the released series of S1.475–S1.480 (prices,
labour force, money, national accounts, realised rates), and each with its declared relationship to real economies and
its source (Appendix E 25). The gate reads them and never writes them.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/observer/READS.toml` | Stage 1's reads added, each `id`, `title`, `unit`, `measure`, relationship and `source_ref` |
| `perf/reads/S1.400-frozen.toml` | the file's hash after this step |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §14.5 | a stage's reads frozen by its first step; the gate refuses a changed file |

**Design**:
- Follows N2 and N3 (the reads a gate reports are declared before the run; §2.24).
- Each read names a measure the observer already takes or a series the recorder (K-106) stamps; a read whose measure
  the Stage 1 world cannot yet produce is written with the step that makes it (its first report says "not yet" until
  that step).
- The relationships (Okun's, the Phillips relation, consumption against income, investment's share, wages against
  productivity, credit against output) are written as signs and ranges with their sources, never as targets.
- The freeze: PC-90 already requires each read's definition to precede its first report; the recorded hash makes the
  gate refuse a `READS.toml` changed after this commit.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: a read whose measure no step has built yet reports "not yet" — n/a: a docs step; checked by PC-90 at S1.498.

**Extension points**: S1.498, S1.499.
**Unit tests**: none (docs).
**Live checks**: none (the gate reads them).
**Budget**: none (no code).
**Guards**: PC-90 (a read's definition precedes its first report).
**Not allowed**: a read chosen or changed after seeing a run; a relationship written as a target; a store, index, map or
per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The reads written with their relationships and sources; the hash recorded; §14.5 written.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.401 — Hazards' chances and their following in sys-dem

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-dem's paragraph: its rules and where the day routes them) written; §7.7 (phx-agenda, hazards
drawn ahead) and §7.18 (the day runner) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.235 (hazards drawn ahead: one next hit per subject and process, its wheels moved into `phx-agenda`);
S1.208 (persons on the person kind: the bit-field view a rule reads); S1.214 (hazard events on the event log); S1.186
(the runner routes stage 3b).
**Goal**: the chance of each declared process on each person of a household, and the following of a hit on its booked
day, are pure functions in `sys-dem`; `phx-world` only hands K-44's due hits and the persons' views to them and applies
what they return. Each hazard acts on each exposed person at that person's own rate (REP.7): the household is the
subject that books, the person is the one reached. `pop_rules.rs` is deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/rules/chances.rs` | `chances`: each exposed person's rate by band, the household's summed rate per process, the band's end |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/rules/follow.rs` | `follow`: which persons a booked hit reaches, and the next booking |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/processes.rs` | each process declares the kinds it acts on (`ActsOn` as data), its stream and event kind |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/nature.rs` | stage 3b routing: K-44 due hits by household range on the pool → the rules → outcomes (S1.402) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/pop_rules.rs` | deleted |

**Design**:
- Carries REP.7, REP.12, REP.25 (done at S0.28); CHN.4 (done at S0.10).
- `chances(view: &HouseholdView, process: &ProcessDecl, date: Date) -> Chances`: for each exposed person of the
  household the process's rate at its age, sex, health and labour state from the declared schedule (mortality, illness,
  conception, leaving school, retirement's chance); the household's summed rate for the process; the day the first
  band ends (a birthday, a schedule's next age). K-44 books one next hit per (household, process) at that summed rate,
  as S1.235 builds it, and redraws at the band's end.
- `follow(view, booking: Booking, draws: &mut Draws) -> Followed { reached: PersonSet, next: Booking }`: on the hit's
  day, each exposed person is reached with probability its own rate over the household's summed rate for that process,
  drawn from `DEM.<process>` addressed by (household, day, person ordinal); when no person is drawn, the one person
  reached is drawn by the same weights from the same stream (a hit reaches at least one). `next` rebooks from tomorrow
  at the summed rate. `PersonSet` is a bit set over the household's member list (≤ 64 bits); no allocation.
- `bind` (process ↔ kind by name) is replaced by each process's `acts_on` declaration, validated at assembly against
  the kind catalogue (K-21): a process acting on an undeclared kind is refused.
- Routing: stage 3b takes K-44's due (household, process) pairs for the day, chunked by household range (K-11); each
  chunk reads its households' views (K-33) and calls `follow`; hits are written into a (chunk, handler) day buffer
  (K-03) ordered by (household identity, process ordinal) and handed to S1.402's outcomes. A household whose persons'
  labour state changed (a hire, a separation) is redrawn from the next day through K-44's redraw (the old `touched` set
  is gone).

**Edge cases**:
- E7: draws by address and per-chunk buffers joined in chunk order — `follow_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E11: day zero draws nothing; the opening books every household's first hit per process at its phase —
  `first_booking_from_opening_date`.
- E14: two processes hitting one household the same day are handed to outcomes in process order —
  `hits_ordered_by_process`.
- E6: next hits are K-44's saved state; the rules hold none — `rules_hold_no_state` (a rule's output is a function of
  its inputs only).
- E13: a household with no person exposed to a process books no hit for it — `no_exposed_no_booking`.

**Extension points**: S1.402, S1.480, S1.489.
**Unit tests**: `chances_sum_exposed_rates_by_band`, `band_end_is_next_birthday`, `follow_reaches_only_exposed_persons`,
`follow_reaches_person_by_own_rate_share`, `follow_reaches_at_least_one`, `bind_refuses_process_on_undeclared_kind`,
`follow_same_for_any_chunking`, `first_booking_from_opening_date`, `hits_ordered_by_process`, `rules_hold_no_state`,
`no_exposed_no_booking`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-39 and LC-0-54 (realised rates against declared chances, per person), LC-0-41 (each hazard's hits
counted as events of its kind); applicable from the first day.
**Budget**:
- adds 68 k / 68 k / 68 k items to `fin.hazards.hit_ns` (the rule's share of the unit: `chances` and `follow` together,
  the rest being S1.402's outcomes and K-44's booking).
- adds 75 k / 75 k / 75 k items to `fin.hazards.redraw_ns`.
- ledger line 15 (hazards, streamed): +0 B (one booking per (household, process), K-44's own figure); views ≤ 2 cache
  lines a household, read in place.
**Guards**: `pop_rules.rs` removed from the S1.120–S1.125 ratchet files; `phx-check` refuses a process name read on a
day path (S1.123).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a `Vec` per household hit; a process bound by its kind's name; a chance read from a clock or by
iteration order; the persons a hit reaches drawn by lot with equal weights.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rules and their tests; `pop_rules.rs` deleted; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution reads the budget with no ratchet broken; LC-0-39, LC-0-41, LC-0-54
  pass.
- [ ] §3.5's sys-dem paragraph written; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.402 — Outcomes on persons and households in sys-dem

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POP.15 FORBID *(part: every death names where each thing the person held and owed went; completed with
inheritance in kind in Stage 2)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-dem) written; §7.15 (phx-end, the ending kernel) and §7.5 (phx-pop) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.401 (the day's hits in process order); S1.344 (endings onto the ending kernel and estates' lifecycle:
a person or household ending moves every row naming it); S1.207 (persons as parties: a birth's `begin`, O(1) moves);
S1.221 (the vital statistics' accumulators the outcomes feed); S1.348 (the decision core, for the household's decision
to try for a child).
**Goal**: what a hit does — a birth, a death, an illness, retirement's labour-state change, a household left with no
one — is a pure `sys-dem` rule returning the changes, applied through the person, ending and statistics bases; every
death is recorded with its cause and the destination of each thing it held and owed. `core_pop.rs` is deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/rules/outcomes.rs` | `outcomes`: a household's hits of the day → births, deaths, health and labour-state changes |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/points.rs` | `DEM.try_for_child` routed through the decision core (the household decides) |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/declare.rs` | the death record kind (cause, destination per holding kind), its horizon; the "retired" wake to LAB |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/nature.rs` | stage 3b apply by household range: K-33 writes, K-97 endings, K-39 increments, K-43 wakes |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_pop.rs` | deleted |

**Design**:
- Follows Law 13 for the persons' side: every death's holdings and debts go somewhere named.
- `outcomes(view: &HouseholdView, hits: &[Hit], date) -> Changes`: hits applied in process order, then by person
  identity; returns person writes (health, labour state, household role), births (a new person with its household, sex
  and birth date), deaths (person, cause) and whether the household is left with no living member. Pure; `Changes` is a
  fixed-capacity value (a household's members ≤ its declared capacity; overflow is `capacity_exceeded!`).
- Apply (by household range, K-12): a birth begins a person (K-31 identity, K-33 member); a death is a K-97 ending of
  the person — every account, holding and contract naming it moves to its destination by the kernel's declared
  adjacency (its estate, K-96, when it held or owed anything) — and the event (K-36) records the cause and, per kind of
  thing held or owed, the destination; a person who held nothing is recorded "nothing held" (POP.15). A household with
  no living member ends the same day through K-97 (PTY.11). An illness's onset and a death increment K-39's vital
  counters by (country, age class, health). A retirement (the labour state set to retired) wakes the person's
  retirement occasion on K-43 for S1.419; nothing here closes a job.
- The household's decision to try for a child (`sys_dem::points::try_for`) is taken at its head's birthday through
  `Core::decide` (decider: the household), and a yes redraws conception's chance through K-44.
- Streams: none new (the hit's draws are S1.401's).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe day's deaths are endings on the pool by ended-party range — `many_deaths_one_day_apply_in_order`.
- E3: a person with no account, holding or contract ends with "nothing held" —
  `death_with_nothing_records_nothing_held`.
- E4: a person's estate that cannot distribute stays open, visited only on its dates (K-96) — LC-0-53.
- E10: rows naming the dead person move at its ending; a stale reference resolves to its successor (K-31) —
  `death_changes_name_estate_as_successor`.
- E14: a birth and a death in one household the same day apply in process order — `birth_and_death_same_day`.

**Extension points**: S1.419, S1.422, S1.476, S1.492, S2.135, S2.147, S8.116, S8.121, S6.117, S6.126.
**Unit tests**: `death_names_destination_for_each_holding_kind`, `last_member_ends_household`,
`outcomes_order_is_process_then_identity`, `birth_adds_member_with_new_identity`,
`death_with_nothing_records_nothing_held`, `birth_and_death_same_day`, `retirement_wakes_not_closes`,
`many_deaths_one_day_apply_in_order`, `death_changes_name_estate_as_successor`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-53 (every death recorded with where what it held and owed went; each estate standing names why),
LC-0-63 (persons reconciled by births and deaths), LC-1-51 (the life table's inputs); applicable from the first death.
**Budget**:
- +0 items to `fin.hazards.hit_ns` (inside S1.401's 68 k hits; the outcomes are part of each hit's unit, adding
  nothing per hit beyond it).
- endings ≈ 330 persons and ≈ 250 households a day (B / NB / H alike): adds 580 / 580 / 580 items to
  `fin.waterfall.claim_ns` (K-97's re-pointed rows); K-39's increments ride `fin.stats.tally_ns`, fused.
- ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B (core attribute); line 20 (estates): +0 B (K-96's own figure).
**Guards**: `core_pop.rs` leaves the ratchet files; `phx-check` refuses a balance written outside settlement's apply
(PC-25 as re-aimed at S1.158).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a walk of every contract family for a person; a balance set to zero at an ending; a death without a
recorded cause.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, its routing and its tests; `core_pop.rs` deleted; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution reads the budget with no ratchet broken; LC-0-53, LC-0-63 and
  LC-1-51 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.403 — Extended households' members from the DHS

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: household composition from surveys)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed.
**Depends on**: none (the primitive `DEM.household_members` and its reader, the opening's household draw, exist).
**Goal**: whom an extended-family and a non-relatives household holds besides its head comes from the DHS household
structure of the group's countries, not from an assumption, for every group the surveys cover.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_pop.py` | the derivation below, writing `DEM.household_members` into each group's `people.toml` |
| `data/profiles/{emerging,developing}/people.toml` | `DEM.household_members`, `source = "measured"`, its `source_ref` |
| `data/profiles/developed/people.toml` | the primitive kept `assumed`, its `source_ref` saying no DHS survey covers the group |
| `data/shared/DEM.toml` | the shared entry removed (each group now holds its own) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `people/dhs_indicators` → `DEM.household_members`, this step |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `people/dhs_indicators` `for` gains S1.403 |

**Design**:
- Source: `people/dhs_indicators` (DHS aggregates, national, surveys from 2005): the share of households with a member
  65 and over, with three generations, of non-nuclear composition, and the household size distribution.
- Per country, its latest survey; per group, the median over its countries in the group's list (the same list the
  profile's other DHS reads use). For the extended-family row: relatives of 65 and over per extended household =
  (share of households with a member 65+ less that share among nuclear households, taken as the three-generation share
  of households) over the non-nuclear share, rounded to the nearest whole person (the table holds counts, one or none
  of each column); for the non-relatives row, the adults besides the head = the mean size of non-nuclear households less
  one, rounded. A value that rounds outside the table's columns is refused by the derivation, never clipped.
- The derivation writes each group's value with its `source_ref` (countries, surveys, medians); the assembly's check
  (`opening::economy::check`) refuses a row whose members exceed the household types' declared maximum.
- The developed group keeps the assumed row, its reason stated (no DHS survey in the group).

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a country whose latest survey lacks an indicator is left out of the median, never read as 0 — the derivation's
  own test `missing_indicator_leaves_country_out`.
- E13: a group with no covered country keeps its assumed value with the reason — `group_without_survey_keeps_assumed`.

**Extension points**: S1.404.
**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `members_from_shares_rounds_to_counts`, `missing_indicator_leaves_country_out`,
`refuses_value_outside_columns`, `group_without_survey_keeps_assumed`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-52 (households' composition drawn as declared) at the first day.
**Budget**: opening only; no day cost.
**Guards**: PC-91 (a primitive's scope and id) unchanged; the inventory row checked by `phx-check data`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a value typed by hand into `people.toml`; a household's composition drawn from an outcome table; a
default standing for a country with no survey.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The derivation and its tests; the profiles regenerated; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-0-52 passes.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.405 — Persons own their accounts and debts at the opening

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: PTY.3 STATE *(part: each person owns its accounts and debts from the opening; completed at S1.406)*
**Architecture**: §10.3 (the sheet's household sector) written; §7.8 (phx-ledger, money accounts) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.404 (the drawn persons); S1.240 (money accounts held by a person, never the household); S1.260 (dated
families on the contract store: loans naming a person as borrower); S1.268 (participations: a loan taken together
held in shares).
**Goal**: the country sheet's household sector — deposits, banknotes and loans — is apportioned over persons, not
households: each adult owns its accounts at its bank and owes its own loans; a loan taken together is a participation
of its borrowers. A household's money and debts are read as its persons' sum.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/households.rs` | `banked`, `apportion_accounts`, `apportion_loans`: which adults hold accounts, the sector's totals over them |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/opening/accounts.rs` | orchestration: accounts opened at persons (K-47), loans opened naming persons (K-53, K-58) |
| `data/profiles/*/law.toml` | `BNK.household_loan_years` kept, `shape = "placeholder:HSG"`, retired by Stage 2's mortgages |

**Design**:
- `banked(adults: &[PersonView], shares) -> PersonSet`: which of the drawn adults hold a bank account, by the declared
  banked share of adults per (country, income class) (the Findex figures the profile already holds), drawn on
  `BNK.opening_banked` addressed by (household, person ordinal); a rule of sys-bnk over the persons sys-dem drew.
- `apportion_accounts(total, persons: &[PersonIncome]) -> DayBuf<i64>`: the sector's deposits and banknotes shared over
  the country's banked adults by the declared wealth shape over incomes, with K-16's `apportion` (largest remainder,
  residue to the named last person in identity order) — exact to the smallest unit (Law 7). An unbanked adult holds
  banknotes only (MON.4). Children hold nothing.
- `apportion_loans`: each household loan drawn by BNK's rule is owed by its earning adults: one borrower when one
  earns, a participation of the earners in shares of their incomes otherwise (K-58), its terms under the placeholder
  `BNK.household_loan_years` (naming HSG).
- A household's money is the sum of its persons' accounts, read through K-33's member list — no household account is
  opened (E 46).
- Streams: `BNK.opening_loans` (unchanged); `BNK.opening_banked` (the banked draw, moved from the old opening).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: an unbanked adult: banknotes only — `unbanked_holds_notes_only`.
- E8: the apportionment is exact in i64 with the residue named — `apportion_exact_with_named_residue`.
- E13: a country whose sheet holds no household loans opens none — `no_loans_no_participations`.

**Extension points**: S1.406, S1.407, S1.488, S2.142 (retires `BNK.household_loan_years`), S2.178.
**Unit tests**: `apportion_exact_with_named_residue`, `unbanked_holds_notes_only`, `joint_loan_shares_by_income`,
`no_loans_no_participations`, `banked_by_declared_share`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-18 (money held equals the issuers' liabilities) and LC-0-62 (the opening's accounts reconcile to
the sheet) at day one.
**Budget**: opening only, no day cost; ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +0 B (the accounts are `[store] accounts`
in `perf/design.toml`, K-47's own figure).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses an account opened with a household kind as holder (an assembly refusal on K-47's holder
kinds, declared by the legal forms).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an account held by a household; a residue left unassigned; a loan without a named borrower.

### S1.406 — A household's payments drawn from its persons

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: PTY.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-hh) written; §7.8 (phx-ledger: flows, settlement's apply) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.405 (persons own their accounts and debts); S1.245 (flow batches: a payment's legs, commit mode);
S1.252 (non-business days' commitments by authorization against `available`); S1.248 (settlement's apply by payer
range); S1.172 (apportion with a named residue); S1.211 (the per-day cache: the spending view the persons' free money
is gathered into).
**Goal**: a household's shared payments — its spending, its rent and its share of what its persons owe together — are
drawn from its persons' accounts in proportion to each one's free money, each person's own debts paid from its own
account first (Appendix E 48); each person's income lands in its own account from its named payer.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/rules/draw.rs` | `split_payment`: a household payment over its persons' free money, own debts first |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/declare.rs` | the flow reasons whose payer is a household, declared as "drawn from persons" |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | stage 5d: the split and the persons' reservations written in the spending view's pass |

**Design**:
- A household never pays: a payment a household decides (a purchase, a shared due) is emitted as items whose payers are
  its persons. `split_payment(amount, persons: &[(PersonRef, free: i64, available: i64)]) -> Split`: each person's free
  money is its balance less what its own dues take before the household's next spending day (K-55 plans, K-54 owed
  sums); the amount is shared in proportion to free money, the one weight, with K-16's `apportion` (residue to the
  member with most free money, ties by identity); a member with no free money takes no share.
- `available` (K-47: balance + limit + min(pending, 0)) is only the authorisation bound: a share above its member's
  `available` is refused visibly (a `refused` event naming the member, the share and the bound, K-36), and that part of
  the want is not bought; it is never re-split onto another member to borrow on its behalf.
- The reservation is fused into the spending view (S1.448): the persons' free money is gathered there already, one read
  of their accounts in the same cache lines, and the split writes each member's share into its account's `pending` hold
  in that same pass. That hold is the till's authorization: no purchase within its want is refused later, and the sales
  apply as they flush during 6a against the reserved shares. The hold expires with the day's `pending` commit (K-47):
  settled at stage 7 on a business day (K-49), committed on a non-business day (K-48 commit mode, TIME.8); what was not
  spent is simply not in the commit. There is no separate release pass.
- Every payer is a named person (Law 5); nothing passes over households at stage 7.
- Income: every flow paying a person (wage, benefit, pension, interest) names the person as payee; nothing is paid to a
  household.
- The PTY.3 carrier: `#[clause("PTY.3")]` on `split_payment` and on K-47's holder-kind refusal's declaration.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a household whose persons hold nothing fails the payment as `NoMoney` (MON.12) —
  `split_with_no_money_fails_whole`.
- E5: a share above its member's `available` is refused visibly and not re-split — `share_above_available_refused`,
  `refused_share_not_resplit`; the unspent hold is gone after the commit — `hold_expires_with_commit`.
- E14: a person's own due and a shared payment the same day: its own first — `own_debt_first`.
- E7: the split is per household in its own chunk — `split_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E8: shares exact to the smallest unit — `split_exact_with_named_residue`.

**Extension points**: S1.414, S1.418, S1.435, S1.448, S1.454, S1.460, S8.107.
**Unit tests**: `split_proportional_to_free_money`, `own_debt_first`, `split_exact_with_named_residue`,
`split_with_no_money_fails_whole`, `split_same_for_any_chunking`, `share_above_available_refused`,
`refused_share_not_resplit`, `hold_expires_with_commit`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-18 and LC-1-32 (every household payment reaches named sellers; income from named payers) each
business day.
**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 5 phone-ns to `fin.decide.spend_ns` at 472 k / 472 k / 472 k items (the reservation's share of the spending
  occasion, itemised at S1.448: the split over ≈ 1.9 members and their holds written in the view's cache lines; the
  own-dues read is the view's, already counted there).
- 0 elsewhere: no release pass; stage 7 settles and the NB commit clears the holds inside `fin.ledger.apply_ns` and
  `fin.ledger.pending_ns` at their existing counts.
- ledger line 8 (accounts): +0 B (the hold is K-47's `pending`).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a flow reason with a household-kind payer that is not declared "drawn from persons".
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a payment made by a household party; a split by equal shares or by `available`; a refused share
re-split onto another member; a release pass over the day's reservations.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, its routing, its declarations and tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-18 and LC-1-32 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/post.rs` | `post(&PostIn) -> PostOut` takes the wanted staff from planned output and way; `offer_point` moved in |

  law's least wage (K-20). `PostOut`: per occupation family the number wanted beyond its staff, the wage point
  (`offer_point`: the lesser of the market's point by its fills and what a unit's month leaves over its cost, never
  below the law's least), and the terms (hours, notice days, severance rule) from the law in force as posted terms.
- The employer with no pension terms of its own posts none: `LAB.no_pension_terms` is declared SHAPE,
  `placeholder:PEN`, retired by Stage 4's pension terms.
- Intents (post, withdraw, reprice) written at 5b into (chunk, handler) buffers; applied at 5d through K-70 offers,
  indexed by K-72. The register is read by handle only (`FilingPrims::lot` compiled at assembly, S1.146).

  S1.296; counted by LC-1-21.
- E12: a missing price outlook: the rule states its answer — it posts at the market's point by its fills
  (VAL.10) — `missing_outlook_posts_at_market_point`.

### S1.414 — Searchers apply from their own reservation

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: LAB.5 DECISION *(part: how many visible vacancies to apply to and the reservation; moving and retraining
are Stage 6's)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-lab) written; §7.11 (search and match) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.321 (search and match: applications as messages, labour's users moved); S1.305 (the vacancy book
and searchers' flag); S1.208 (the person view without allocation); S1.406 (a person's own money and income, read for
its outside option).
**Goal**: each searcher's decision — which of the vacancies it can see in its region and reach to apply to, and the
reservation it accepts above — is `sys_lab::rules::search` over the searcher's own view, taken on its search days
through the decision core; no searcher is visited except on its due day.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/search.rs` | `search(&SearchIn) -> Applications` (fixed-capacity) and `reservation(&SearchIn) -> i64` |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/points.rs` | `LAB.search` with its schedule (searchers' search days) and decider (the person) |
| `data/shared/LAB.toml` | `LAB.reservation_share` kept `placeholder:HH` (retired by Stage 2's household outside option) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | stage 5b: due searchers from K-43, views, applications posted as K-45 messages |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `seekers`, `search_round`, `searching_persons` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries LAB.8 (done at S1.08); REP.22 (completed at S1.321).
- `SearchIn`: the person's skill by occupation family, its last wage point, its benefit if claiming (K-53), its
  household's other income (K-52 tallies of its persons), its price outlook (its household's stance, K-92), the
  vacancies in reach (K-72's run for its region and occupation families, at most the declared number the kernel hands
  over, each with its pull cached at posting, K-82) and each application's cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY).
- The reservation is the outside option (the benefit and the household's other income, the latter at
  `LAB.reservation_share` until Stage 2's households weigh leisure) over the price outlook to its next review; the
  searcher applies to the vacancies whose expected worth beats the reservation by more than an application costs, in
  order of expected worth, ties by lot (Plackett–Luce draws, K-82).
- Routing: due searchers only (K-43 search days, woken by a separation or a notice); applications as K-45 messages to
  the employer, due at its selection (S1.415).
- Streams: `LAB.search` addressed by (person, day).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no vacancy in reach: the searcher applies nowhere and searches again on its next day —
  `no_vacancy_applies_nowhere`.
- E3: a searcher with no benefit and no household income: its reservation is the law's least wage — asserted in
  `reservation_floor_is_law_least` only where LAB.11's law states it; otherwise the rule's value stands.
- E5: a mass layoff day wakes many searchers: they are due the next business day through K-43 (spread by nothing
  invented) — `woken_searchers_due_next_business_day`.
- E7: draws by address — `search_same_for_any_chunking`.

**Extension points**: S1.415, S1.416, S2.138 (retires `LAB.reservation_share`), S2.149, S8.117, S6.119.
**Unit tests**: `applies_only_above_reservation`, `order_by_expected_worth_ties_by_lot`, `no_vacancy_applies_nowhere`,
`reservation_from_outside_option`, `search_same_for_any_chunking`, `woken_searchers_due_next_business_day`,
`reservation_floor_is_law_least`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-22 (unemployment durations, job-to-job flows) from the first search day.
**Budget**:
- the searchers' occasions: ≈ 90 k / 0 / 90 k search days due a business day at the design point (the unemployed and
  those under notice or searching on the job, each due on its weekly search day, K-43), each `fin.decide.search_ns`'s
  searcher item (300 phone-ns all in, S1.321: kernel
  170 — reach, scoring and the Gumbel top-k that is the application draw — handler 30, view 90): the reservation is read
  in the view and the worth-over-reservation test is the kernel's scoring, so this rule adds +0 phone-ns to it.
  S8.117's weighing is stated there as its own addition at its count.
- adds 50–150 k / 0 / 50–150 k items to K-45's message post (the applications, counted at S1.237).
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (searchers are K-72's flag).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses `unpack` or a person attribute read by name on a day path (S1.123).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; every searcher visited daily; an aggregate matching function (LAB.15).
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, point, routing and tests; the searching functions gone from `core_labour.rs`; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-22 passes.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.415 — Selection, offers and hires

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: LAB.15 FORBID
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-lab) written; §7.9 (the contract store) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.414 (applications as messages); S1.321 (search and match's rounds); S1.260 (the employment family);
S1.264 (a new contract's first due from the shared schedule, not counted from day zero); S1.261 (side aggregates move
on the hire).
**Goal**: an employer's selection among its applicants, its offer, and the searcher's acceptance are `sys-lab` rules;
an accepted offer opens an employment contract naming the employer and the person; nothing else opens one, and no
unemployment rate, matching function or second channel from prices to wages exists anywhere.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/select.rs` | `select(&SelectIn)`: the employer's ranking by its rule, equals by lot |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/accept.rs` | `accept(&AcceptIn)`: the best offer beating the reservation |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/hire.rs` | `EmploymentOpen`, constructible only from an accepted `Match` (the LAB.15 carrier) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/lab15.rs` | PC-103: refuses an unemployment rate, a matching function or a wage indexed to prices in LAB/SOC data or code |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `select_applicants`, `answer_offers`, `hire` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries LAB.1, LAB.7, LAB.8 (done at S1.08).
- Selection (at the employer's due, stage 5c): `SelectIn` holds the vacancy's terms (read once a day from the per-day
  cache, K-35) and its applicants' skills and last
  points; the employer ranks by skill against the occupation's ask, then lot (K-82). Offers are K-45 messages due the
  next stage; the person answers with `accept` over all offers it holds (the best by worth over reservation, ties by
  lot).
- A hire: `EmploymentOpen::from(match)` opens the contract (K-53: sides employer and person, terms shape interned, start
  day, first due by the shared schedule's nth date, K-55), withdraws the filled vacancy (K-70), clears the person's
  searcher flag (K-72) and ends a benefit claim (S1.421's rule, woken). No `postings.clone()` or `laws.clone()`.
- LAB.15's carriers: the type above (no employment without an employer, compile level); PC-103 (no exogenous
  unemployment rate, no aggregate matching function, no price-indexed wage beside the contracts).
- Streams: `LAB.select`, `LAB.accept` addressed by (party, day).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a vacancy with no applicant stays posted; an applicant with no offer searches again — `no_applicant_no_offer`.
- E10: an employer ending between offer and answer: its offers lapse with it (K-97 → K-45) — `offer_lapses_at_ending`.
- E14: two offers to one person the same day: the best accepted, the other refused — `best_of_two_offers`.
- E8: the first due placed by the calendar's nth date — `first_due_by_nth_date`.

**Extension points**: S1.421, S1.478, S1.476, S8.117, S8.121, S8.135.
**Unit tests**: `select_by_skill_then_lot`, `best_of_two_offers`, `no_applicant_no_offer`, `offer_lapses_at_ending`,
`first_due_by_nth_date`; compile-fail `employment_without_match_refused`; PC-103's tests.
**Live checks**: LC-1-21, LC-1-23 (no employment without an employer) each day.
**Budget**:
- the employers' selections and the persons' answers are their own item in `fin.decide.search_ns`'s table: ≈ 50 k / 0 /
  50 k a business day (≈ 40 k vacancies with applicants due at their employers' weekly selection, `[store] vacancies`
  over five business days, and ≈ 10 k persons answering the offers they hold) at ≤ 200 phone-ns ≈ 10 core-ms;
  the employer reads each vacancy's view once a day from the per-day cache (K-35), not per applicant.
- adds 5.4 k / 0 / 5.4 k items to `fin.contracts.open_ns` (the hires).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (employment rows are `[store.contracts] "LAB.employment"`).
**Guards**: PC-103 added; the compile-fail test.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a contract opened outside `EmploymentOpen`; a schedule found by scanning a family.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rules, the type, PC-103, routing and tests; the functions gone from `core_labour.rs`; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-21 and LC-1-23 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.416 — Pay rounds at contracts' review dates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: LAB.9 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-lab) written; §7.9 (the contract store: a contract's wage term) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.233 (pay rounds on the decision agenda, the `reviews` map gone); S1.265 (a contract's notice state:
one under notice is not reviewed); S1.414 (the employee's reservation and the vacancies it sees); S1.263 (a
restructured wage is the contract's own new amount on its shape).
**Goal**: an employment contract's wage changes only at its review date — by the employer's offer, the employee's
answer and their agreement — or when the worker leaves; the rules are `sys_lab::rules::renegotiate`, taken at each
contract's review through the decision core, and the wage column has no other writer.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/renegotiate.rs` | `review` (the offer), `answer`, `conclude` over their views |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/wage.rs` | `WageChange`, constructible only by `conclude` at a review date or by a new contract (the LAB.9 carrier) |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/points.rs` | `LAB.review` (decider: the line's head, office of the employer) and `LAB.answer` (the person) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | stage 5c: contracts due for review from K-43, views, offers and answers as K-45 messages |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `review_due`, `review_wages`, `answer_reviews`, `raise_stale`, `set_last_point` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries LAB.6, LAB.11, LAB.17 (done at S1.08).
- Due: each employer's first round day is drawn within the review period at the opening (TIME.5 phases); each
  contract not under notice is reviewed once a period on its review date (K-43, per employer, one wheel entry).
- `review(&ReviewIn) -> Point`: the lesser of the point its fills show the market pays (K-72's fills record) and the
  most the job's month pays (its wage and what a unit leaves over its cost at the price it expects, for the units a
  month of the job's hours makes, K-35, K-92), never below the law's least (K-20); a firm expecting no sales offers
  its current point.
- `answer(&AnswerIn) -> Point`: from the employee's reservation (S1.414), the best vacancy its week's search would draw,
  and its price outlook compounded to the next round. `conclude(offer, answer, most) -> Missing<Point>`: agreement at
  the offer when the answer is at or below it; a counter the work cannot pay is no agreement — the employee works on
  at the offer and applies to the vacancies it saw (a job-to-job move through S1.414–S1.415), quitting to search when
  the offer is below its reservation.
- `WageChange` is the only way to write a contract's wage (compile level): LAB.9's carrier. Rounds of the day are
  answered together per country (one search each), never one by one.
- Streams: `LAB.review` for the first round day's phase (opening only).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a quarter's review dates stacked on a Monday after closed days are due that day, their cost in the pay rounds'
  share — `stacked_reviews_due_same_day`.
- E10: an employee who dies between offer and answer: the offer lapses with the contract (K-97) —
  `offer_lapses_with_contract`.
- E14: a review and a layoff notice for one contract the same day: the notice stops the review — `notice_stops_review`.
- E12: no fill yet in the market: the offer reads the most the job pays — `no_fill_offers_worth`.

**Extension points**: S1.478, S2.213, S8.118, S8.121, S8.136.
**Unit tests**: `offer_lesser_of_fill_and_worth`, `offer_never_below_law`, `counter_beyond_worth_is_no_agreement`,
`quit_when_offer_below_reservation`, `notice_stops_review`, `no_fill_offers_worth`, `stacked_reviews_due_same_day`,
`offer_lapses_with_contract`; compile-fail `wage_written_outside_review_refused`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-21 (staff and wage bill against contracts), LC-1-22 (the wage response to slack) from the first
review.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.pay_rounds: 15 / 0 / 15 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 18 k rounds a business day (the employment
  rows of `[store.contracts]` over a year's business days), each a K-43 take, `review`, `answer` and `conclude` at
  ≤ 800 phone-ns; the rest of the line is the boards' pay (S3.156) and the offices' (S8.134).
- ledger line 14 (wheel and agenda): +0 B (one agenda entry per employer, K-43's own figure).
**Guards**: the compile-fail test; `phx-check` refuses a write to the employment family's amount column outside
`sys_lab::wage` (an assembly refusal of a second writer).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a wage moved by a price index or by any path beside the review (LAB.15); `Standing::new` per round.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rules, the type, routing and tests; the round's functions gone from `core_labour.rs`; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-21 and LC-1-22 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.417 — Layoffs, notice and separations

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-lab) written; §7.7 (messages and notices) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.238 (notices on messages); S1.266 (notice as the contract's status, `labour.noticed` gone); S1.413
(the posting's staff wanted, whose negative is a layoff); S1.248 (severance paid as a flow).
**Goal**: an employer that wants fewer of an occupation than it holds lays off by lot with the law's notice; the
separation takes effect on its date with the severance for the years served, and the person searches again; the rules
are `sys-lab`'s and nothing visits every pending separation.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/lay_off.rs` | `lay_off(&LayOffIn) -> Notices` (fixed capacity): whom, by lot, with notice days |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/wages.rs` | `severance` (kept) read at the separation |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | stage 5c: notices posted (K-45, due at the separation date on K-42) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/open.rs` | stage 1a: separations due today taken from K-42 → contract closed, severance batch, searcher flag |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_labour.rs` | `lay_off`, `separate`, `searches_again` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries LAB.4, LAB.12, LAB.16 (done at S1.08).
- At the employer's posting visit (S1.413), an occupation family whose wanted count is below its staff not under
  notice yields `lay_off`: the surplus chosen by lot among that family's contracts (stream `LAB.lay_off`, addressed by
  (employer, day)), each a notice (K-45) with the law's notice days in force (K-20), the contract's status set to under
  notice (K-56).
- On the separation's date (a K-42 due): the contract closes (K-53, side aggregates move, K-54), severance for the
  years served is a flow from employer to person (K-48, LAB.12's rule, `severance`), the person's searcher flag is set
  (K-72) and its benefit occasion woken (S1.421).
- No pass over pending separations: each is one due on its date.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a firm ending mid-notice: its employees' separations happen at its ending, severance a claim on its estate
  (K-98) — `ending_turns_notice_into_claim`.
- E5: a heavy day's separations are dues of the day, sized by the wheel's H bucket — n/a here: the bucket is K-42's,
  sized at S1.225; read on the gate's H day.
- E14: a separation and a hire of the same person the same day: the separation first (stage 1a before 5c) —
  `separation_before_hire_same_day`.
- E3: an employer with no money for severance fails the flow into arrears (K-56), never skipped —
  `short_severance_goes_to_arrears`.

**Extension points**: S1.419, S1.421, S1.478, S1.476, S2.121, S2.138, S2.148, S8.121, S8.134.
**Unit tests**: `surplus_chosen_by_lot`, `notice_days_from_law_in_force`, `severance_by_years_served`,
`ending_turns_notice_into_claim`, `separation_before_hire_same_day`, `short_severance_goes_to_arrears`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-21, LC-1-23 each day.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.pay_rounds: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 5 k notices and separations a business day,
  each a due take and a row close.
- adds 5 k / 0 / 5 k items to `fin.contracts.close_ns`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (notices are the employment row's terms change; closed rows are S1.257's).
**Guards**: `separate`'s partition pass removed from the S1.121 ratchet file.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a set of noticed contracts outside K-56; a severance skipped when the employer is short.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, routing and tests; the functions gone from `core_labour.rs`; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-21 and LC-1-23 pass.

### S1.420 — The state pension claimed at retirement

**Status**: planned
