### S1.425 — The lending round

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.4 DECISION *(part: the quote from the bank's own cost of funds, its own assessment and the capital a
loan takes, the first two placeholders here)*; BNK.5 DECISION *(part: decline and tighten; capital and liquidity limits
in Stage 2)*; BNK.15 FORBID *(part: each lender's own assessment; the provision it drives in Stage 2)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-bnk) written; §7.11 (the bilateral protocol) and §7.14 (books and limits) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.318 (the lending round onto the bilateral protocol: asks, quotes and declines as messages, the reach
the applicant's); S1.339 (loan books and lenders' classes on K-93); S1.262 (owed balances on side aggregates); S1.329 (a
firm's income lines, the cover it discloses); S1.215 (records: the snapshot's present values, the interim disclosure).
**Goal**: a borrower asks its own bank and then more of the lenders in its reach while one more quote is worth its cost
to it; each bank quotes or declines from its own position by `sys_bnk::credit`, reading its own rate table, reviews its
standards monthly from its own book, and the borrower takes the best quote by its taste; `core_lending.rs` is deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/credit.rs` | `quote`, `decline`, `standard`, `learned`, `choose`, `class_of` (kept) over views; `rate_table` (new) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/asks.rs` | `ask_more(&AskIn) -> bool`: the borrower's rule for one more ask |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/points.rs` | `BNK.quote`, `BNK.decline` (decider: the loan officer's office), `BNK.standard`, `BNK.rates` (the bank's head: its standard and its rate table), `BNK.choose`, `BNK.ask_more` (the borrower); `BNK.standard` and `BNK.rates` declared `opening: true` (S1.491) |
| `data/profiles/*/law.toml`, `data/shared/BNK.toml` | `BNK.cost_of_funds` (`placeholder:BFL`: the policy rate), `BNK.risk_weight` (`placeholder:BCP`: 100 %) declared; `BNK.lenders_asked` deleted |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | the ask's routing (K-80), answers at the stage the protocol declares |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_lending.rs` | deleted |

**Design**:
- Carries BNK.6 and BNK.20 (done at S1.09).
- The ask (K-80 message) carries the amount, the term and the applicant's disclosed accounts: its last year's income
  lines (K-87); before a year has run, the snapshot's present value (K-37, S1.215) — a named interim until S1.486 opens
  each firm's latest filed accounts. A bank reads only what the borrower discloses and its own records of it (Law 12).
- How many to ask is the borrower's rule, not a draw: `ask_more` asks its own bank first, then the next lender in its
  reach (K-80: its relationships, then the banks of its region's reach in the order its own records rank them) while
  the expected gain of one more quote — the dispersion of the quotes it has received or, with none yet, of the
  published new-loan rates (K-37), times the loan's amount and term, times the chance another quote beats its best —
  exceeds what an ask costs it (hours at its own labour income, TECHNOLOGY), as LAB.5's applications do.
- `rate_table(&TableIn) -> ClassRates`: each bank's rate per (product, class) — its marginal cost of funds
  (`BNK.cost_of_funds`, placeholder:BFL), its learned default rate for the class (the published rate as prior
  loan-years with its own defaults and loan-years, `learned`), the loss given default (as S1.339 declares it), the
  capital the loan takes (`BNK.risk_weight`, placeholder:BCP) times its required return, and its cost of making a loan
  (hours, TECHNOLOGY) — recomputed only when one of its inputs changes (its monthly standard, its cost of funds, a
  published rate), held in its book's class rows (K-93).
- `quote(&QuoteIn) -> Missing<Rate>`: the applicant's class from its disclosed accounts (`class_of`) and the table's
  rate for it; `decline` when the class is worse than the bank's standard or the interest cover falls below it. Each
  bank's assessment is its own row in its book (K-93, BNK.15), never shared.
- `standard` on each bank's first business day of a month (K-43): its month's write-offs against what its classes'
  learned rates priced, a class tighter where it lost more, looser where less; the table is recomputed then.
- `choose`: the borrower takes the best quote by its taste (REP.22), whatever its required return when the loan meets
  dues; with every bank declining it goes without.
- Streams: `BNK.choose` (taste), addressed by (party, day). No stream draws how many banks are asked.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no bank in the reach quotes: the borrower goes without, recorded — `all_decline_goes_without`.
- E1: a bank failing (Stage 2) answers no asks; its asks lapse at its ending (K-97 → K-45) —
  `failed_bank_asks_lapse`.
- E12: an applicant with no income record yet discloses the snapshot's present value; with neither, its disclosed cover
  is absent and the bank's rule states its answer (declines on a missing cover) — `missing_cover_declines`.
- E7: answers by address, the borrower's choice ties by lot — `choice_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E13: a borrower whose reach holds only its own bank asks once — `reach_of_one_asks_once`.

**Extension points**: S1.426, S1.427, S1.430, S1.460, S1.476, S1.490, S1.491, S1.492, S2.101, S2.102, S2.106, S2.110,
S2.112, S2.117, S2.118, S2.143, S2.144, S2.179 (retires `BNK.cost_of_funds`), S2.181, S2.182, S2.184, S2.188, S2.190
(retires `BNK.risk_weight`), S2.200, S3.140, S3.201, S8.120, S8.161, S8.162, S8.163.
**Unit tests**: `rate_table_sums_its_parts`, `quote_reads_class_rate`, `decline_below_standard`,
`standard_tightens_on_losses`, `learned_rate_from_prior_and_own`, `ask_more_while_gain_beats_cost`,
`no_more_asks_when_cost_exceeds_gain`, `choose_best_by_taste_ties_by_lot`, `all_decline_goes_without`,
`failed_bank_asks_lapse`, `missing_cover_declines`, `choice_same_for_any_chunking`, `reach_of_one_asks_once`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-25 (applications, declines, quotes and loans per bank; asks per application) and LC-1-24 (books)
from the first ask.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 13 / 0 / 13 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 10 k applications a business day × ≈ 1.8
  asks expected at the design point (the own bank and, for about four in five, one more) × (a K-80 ask and a table-read
  quote ≈ 700 phone-ns); the tables' recomputation 35 banks × their classes monthly, ≤ 0.1 core-ms.
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B; the rate tables are K-93's class rows (+0 B, K-93's own figure).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a module named `core_lending`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a walk of the borrower's families per application; one assessment shared by lenders; a bank reading
a borrower's undisclosed state; a count of lenders asked drawn from published shares; a quote recomputed from its parts
per ask.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rules, points, placeholders, routing and tests; `core_lending.rs` deleted; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-24 and LC-1-25 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.426 — A firm's rate for new debt as its own position

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written; §7.5 (typed columns) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.425 (quotes a firm receives); S1.196 (a declared firm column); S1.218 (the snapshot's present values
as records).
**Goal**: what financing costs a firm at the margin is a position it holds (REP.20) — the rate of the latest quote it
took or was given, else its newest loan's — updated when it happens, so production, input orders and investment read
the firm's own rate rather than the country's or a zero.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the firm column `marginal_rate` (fixed-point, `Missing` while none observed) and its writer |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/funds.rs` | `rate_for_new_debt(&FundsView) -> Missing<Rate>` with the absent case stated |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | the column written at a quote's receipt or a loan's opening |

**Design**:
- Serves FRM.4 (completed at S1.443); GDS.5 (completed at S1.444); CAP.3 (completed at S8.138).
- Written on events only: a quote received (K-80 answer), a loan opened (K-53 terms) — the latest's rate. Read by the
  views of S1.443 (FRM.4), S1.444 (GDS.5) and S1.458 (CAP.3).
- `rate_for_new_debt` while the column is absent: the closest observed (VAL.10) — the latest published average rate on
  new loans to firms, read from K-37 as published by the day (Law 12): the snapshot's present value (GEN.5) — a named
  interim until S1.476's first monthly credit release publishes the world's own rate. A firm with neither states it: the
  rule returns `Missing`, and each reader states its answer (a firm that cannot price financing plans no stock beyond
  its cover's floor of its declared rule).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:

**Extension points**: S1.443, S1.444, S1.458, S1.472, S2.118.

`nothing_observed_is_missing`.
**Live checks**: none (read by S1.443's and S1.458's checks).

allocation per day; the country's rate standing for the firm's; a zero for an unobserved rate.

### S1.427 — A firm's shortfall borrowed from its own bank

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written; §7.8 (settlement: per-party nets) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.248 (settlement exposes each party's day net); S1.425 (the lending round the ask goes through);
S1.263 (a term loan's shape, amortising monthly from the next month's date).
**Goal**: a firm whose money today, with what it is paid today, falls short of what it pays today asks to borrow the
shortfall through the lending round, under a declared placeholder naming FRM for the firm's funding decision; the
shortfall is read from settlement's nets, never from a pass over the day's flows.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/funds.rs` | `shortfall(&NetView) -> Missing<i64>` |
| `data/shared/FRM.toml` | `FRM.shortfall_loan` declared `placeholder:FRM` (a term loan over the fewest years a loan runs), retired by Stage 2's FRM.9 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/settle.rs` | stage 7a: short firms from K-49's nets → K-80 asks answered in the stage → the loan's money leg in the batch before 7b |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_credit.rs` | `lend_shortfalls` and the loan families' fill removed |

**Design**:
- Carries BNK.17 (done at S1.09).
- At 7a, K-49's pass one exposes each party's day net; for firms (a declared kind attribute "applies for its
  shortfall", not a kind name) whose balance plus net is below zero on a business day of the currency, `shortfall`
  returns the amount. The ask carries it and the placeholder's term; answers are the banks' rules (S1.425), taken in the
  same stage; the loan opens (K-53, shape interned, first due the next month's date on the shared schedule) and its
  money leg joins the batch before the fixed point (7b). Where every bank declines, the firm goes without and what it
  cannot pay fails into arrears.
- Streams: the lending round's.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a payday's many short firms: asks answered on the pool by firm range; the fixed point then settles —
  `shortfalls_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E14: a firm short and paid late the same day: its net already counts what it is paid today —
  `net_counts_todays_receipts`.
- E3: a firm with no account: no shortfall computed; its flows fail as `NoMoney` — `no_account_no_shortfall`.

**Extension points**: S2.118 (retires `FRM.shortfall_loan`).
**Unit tests**: `shortfall_from_balance_and_net`, `no_shortfall_on_non_business_day`, `declined_goes_without`,
`shortfalls_same_for_any_chunking`, `net_counts_todays_receipts`, `no_account_no_shortfall`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-25 (loans lent) and LC-0-22 (settlement values) each business day.
**Budget**:
- adds 20 k / 0 / 150 k items to `fin.settle.short_ns` (the short firms, `[day.*] short`).
- its asks are among S1.425's applications, counted in its share of fin.fixed.institutions (+0 here).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (the loans opened are S1.257's `BNK.firm_loan` rows).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a pass over the day's flows outside K-49 (S1.121's ratchet lowered).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a `BTreeMap` of nets built from the flows; a loan that skips the lending round.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, placeholder, routing and tests; `lend_shortfalls` gone; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-0-22 and LC-1-25 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.428 — Default after grace

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.15 PROCESS *(part: default of payment into liquidation; balance-sheet insolvency and restructuring are
Stage 2's)*; HH.13 PROCESS *(part: a household's arrears held and asked again; their consequences Stage 2's)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written; §7.9 (status and arrears) and §7.15 (endings) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.266 (arrears, grace and notice onto the contract's status, an arrears agenda entry at grace expiry);
S1.344 (endings onto the ending kernel); S1.346 (estates' payments onto the waterfall with the country's ranks).
**Goal**: a firm whose arrears outlast its country's grace defaults on the grace's date and ends into an estate by the
ending kernel, its claims ranked by its country's insolvency law; a household's arrears are held and asked with its
next due; the solvent owner's close stays declared and blocked; `core_default.rs` is deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/insolvency.rs` | `defaults(&ArrearsView) -> bool` at the grace's date |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.close` kept declared, not routed; `FRM.voluntary_close` (`placeholder:MND`) in `data/shared/FRM.toml` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/resolve.rs` | stage 2d–2f: grace expiries from K-42 → `defaults` → K-97 ending |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_default.rs`, `core_default_tests.rs` | deleted |

**Design**:
- The arrears agenda entry (K-56) falls due on the date the oldest arrears reach `FRM.insolvency_grace_days` (POLICY,
  the country's); on that date `defaults` reads the contract's arrears still unpaid; a yes is the firm's default of
  payment, ending it at 2f through K-97 (its money moved to its estate by flows, its goods and contracts to the estate,
  its employees' contracts closing into claims at their rank, K-98).
- A household's failed due is held in arrears and asked again with its next due (K-56); no default follows in Stage 1
  (HH.21, Stage 2).
- The solvent owner's close (`sys_frm::rules::endings::closes`) is declared but not routed: `FRM.voluntary_close`,
  placeholder:MND, retired when the mind decides (Stage 8).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a tenth of the firms defaulting on one day: endings on the pool by ended-party range; the heavy day's `-F`
  carries it (K-97's budget) — `defaults_same_for_any_chunking`.
- E4: an estate holding goods it cannot sell stays open, visited only on its dates — LC-1-45.
- E14: a payment arriving on the grace's date: settlement at 7 of the previous day decides; arrears paid are not
  arrears — `paid_before_grace_no_default`.

**Extension points**: S1.490, S1.492, S2.101, S2.122, S8.144 (retires `FRM.voluntary_close`).
**Unit tests**: `default_on_grace_date`, `paid_before_grace_no_default`, `household_arrears_asked_again`,
`defaults_same_for_any_chunking`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-45 (no firm in arrears past its grace and a day; firms of every industry end over the run) at the
gate.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 750 grace expiries a business day, each a K-42 due
  and the default rule.
- adds 750 / 0 / 750 items to `fin.waterfall.open_estate_ns` and their rows to `fin.waterfall.claim_ns`; a mass-failure
  day stays within `fin.waterfall.mass_failure_core_ms`.
- ledger line 20 (estates): +0 B (`[store] estates`, K-96's own figure).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a module named `core_default`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a scan of every contract in arrears daily; the voluntary close routed.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, placeholder, routing and tests; `core_default.rs` deleted; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-45 passes or is not yet applicable.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.429 — The central bank's facilities and remittance

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.6 DECISION *(part: the eligible collateral and haircut, as placeholders)*; CB.7 PROCESS *(part: the
corridor at a fixed policy rate)*; CB.10 PROCESS *(part: net income remitted monthly; revaluations Stage 3's)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-cb) written; §7.11 (the administered form) and §7.18 (stage 8) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.320 (the central bank's facilities onto the administered form, collateral from side aggregates, one
shared overnight schedule); S1.243 (maintained money totals: each bank's reserves and deposits owed); S1.408 (the
central bank opened).
**Goal**: in stage 8 of each business day the central bank answers each bank's facility request at its administered
rates against eligible collateral, and on each month's first business day remits its net income to the treasury; the
rules are `sys-cb` functions, and the fixed policy rate, its corridor and the collateral are declared placeholders
naming CB.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/central.rs` | `corridor` (kept), `answer(&FacilityIn) -> Grant` (eligible collateral × (1 − haircut) bounds a loan), `remit(&IncomeView) -> Amount` |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/points.rs` | `CB.rule` (the corridor set from the fixed rate) and `CB.answer` (decider: the central bank's head's office); `CB.rule` declared `opening: true` (S1.491) |
| `data/profiles/*/law.toml`, `data/shared/CB.toml` | `CB.policy_rate_fixed`, `CB.corridor_spread`, `CB.loan_haircut`, `CB.eligible_collateral` (`placeholder:CB`) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/fund.rs` | stage 8: requests → answers (K-81) → positions (K-53 overnight family) → their settlement (K-49) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_central.rs` | `answer`, `remit`, `issuer_held`, `money_class` removed (the last two are K-47's maintained totals by declared class, S1.244) |

**Design**:
- Carries MON.3, MON.6, MON.7, MON.9 (done at S0.15).
- `answer`: the lending facility lends overnight up to the bank's eligible collateral (its firm loans' balances,
  `CB.eligible_collateral`, read from K-54's maintained sums, at `CB.loan_haircut`) at the lending rate; the deposit
  facility takes any placement at the deposit rate; rates are the corridor around `CB.policy_rate_fixed` (MKT.8:
  administered, real quantities respond). Positions open and return on the one shared overnight schedule.
- Remittance: on each month's first business day the central bank's recognised net income (K-87 lines) is paid to its
  treasury (CB.10); an unrealised gain is never remitted (none arises in Stage 1).
- Until S1.430 the banks' requests are still computed by `core_central.rs`'s `request`; the routing hands them to
  `answer` unchanged.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a country whose banks hold no firm loans: no eligible collateral, the lending facility lends nothing —
  `no_collateral_lends_nothing`.
- E5: a heavy day's fund stage runs after the heavy settlement; its cost stays its share — n/a: 35 answers a day at
  most; read on the gate's H day.
- E10: a bank ending with an open position: the position is a claim of its estate (K-97 → K-98) —
  `open_position_claims_on_estate`.

**Extension points**: S1.430, S1.491, S2.185, S3.104, S3.110, S3.111 (retires `CB.policy_rate_fixed`), S3.112 (retires
`CB.corridor_spread`, `CB.loan_haircut`, `CB.eligible_collateral`), S3.117, S3.144.
**Unit tests**: `loan_bounded_by_haircut_collateral`, `deposit_takes_any_placement`, `remit_net_income_only`,
`no_collateral_lends_nothing`, `open_position_claims_on_estate`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-27 (facilities used, positions returned, income remitted) and LC-1-26 (money created and destroyed
only by issuers) each business day.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.fund: 2 / 0 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≤ 35 answers a business day and the positions' opens and
  returns; the remittance on the month's first business day (3 countries, ≤ 0.1 core-ms).
- no pass over firm loans or accounts (collateral is K-54's maintained sum).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (the facilities' positions are S1.257's `CB.lending_facility` and `CB.deposit_facility` rows, small).
**Guards**: PC-25 (balances written only by settlement's apply).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; collateral summed over every firm loan; a new schedule per position per day; a kind's name compared
to class money.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rules, placeholders, routing and tests; the functions gone from `core_central.rs`; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-26 and LC-1-27 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.430 — A bank's request of the facilities

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.10 PROCESS *(part: a bank short after the facility is recorded as failed for liquidity; its resolution
is Stage 2's)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-bnk) written; §7.18 (stage 8) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.429 (the facilities' answer and the stage 8 routing); S1.425 (the banks' rules in `sys-bnk::credit`);
S1.243 (each bank's maintained reserves and deposits owed).
**Goal**: each bank decides its request of the central bank's deposit or lending facility from its own reserves after
settlement and its target, through the decision core; a bank still short after the answer fails its day's flows and
the failure is recorded. `core_central.rs` is deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/credit.rs` | `request(&RequestIn) -> Request` (kept) over the bank's maintained reserves and deposits |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/points.rs` | `BNK.request` (decider: the bank's head's office) |
| `data/profiles/*/law.toml` | `BNK.reserve_target` (`placeholder:BFL`), retired by S2.185 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_central.rs` | deleted |

**Design**:
- `RequestIn`: the bank's reserves after the day's settlement and its deposits owed (K-47's maintained per-bank
  totals), its target reserves ratio (`BNK.reserve_target`, placeholder:BFL), its open positions. `request` returns a
  deposit placement or a loan asked; the decision is the bank's (decider: its head's office, through `Core::decide`).
- A bank whose reserve account is still short after the facility fails its day's flows; the event is recorded (BFL.10's
  liquidity failure, K-36); resolution waits for Stage 2's SUP.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a bank short beyond its collateral: the rest fails and is recorded — `short_beyond_collateral_fails_rest`.
- E3: a bank at its target asks nothing — `at_target_requests_nothing`.

**Extension points**: S1.432, S1.492, S2.185 (retires `BNK.reserve_target`), S8.167.

**Live checks**: LC-1-27 each business day.
**Budget**: its share of fin.fixed.fund: 2 / 0 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≤ 35 requests a business day through the
decision core.
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B (a bank's request is a decision over its own record's reads).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a module named `core_central`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a bank's reserves recounted from its accounts.

### S1.431 — The treasury's position and cash buffer

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TRS.1 STATE; TRS.10 PRIMITIVE *(part: the declared payment order read from data; the parliament's order
Stage 3's)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-trs) written.
**Depends on**: S1.279 (the instruments register: the debt the treasury has issued read from it); S1.255 (the declared
payment order); S1.409 (the treasury opened).
**Goal**: the treasury is a party with its account at its central bank, a cash buffer target it declares, the debt it
has issued read from the register and the assets it owns; its position is read, never kept apart, and its funding when
cash falls short is a declared placeholder.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/lib.rs` | the treasury kind's declared columns: `cash_buffer` (POLICY schedule, TRS.9), its view `TreasuryView` (account, debt from K-64, owned holdings from K-60) with `#[clause("TRS.1")]` |
| `data/profiles/*/law.toml` | `TRS.cash_buffer` (POLICY), `TRS.never_borrows_from_cb` (`placeholder:CB`), `TRS.funding_rule` (`placeholder:TRS`: bills only, sized by S1.432) |

**Design**:
- Carries TRS.4, TRS.9 (done at S1.11).
- The treasury's account is its central bank's (K-47); its debt is the register's issued amounts of its instruments
  (K-64), never a sum kept apart; its assets are its holdings (K-60). `TreasuryView` reads them for the minister's
  `size` (S1.432) and for the observer.
- The buffer target (`TRS.cash_buffer`, POLICY, TRS.9) is the cash the minister keeps; when cash falls short the
  treasury does not borrow from its central bank (`TRS.never_borrows_from_cb`, placeholder:CB, Stage 3) and funds only
  by bills (`TRS.funding_rule`, placeholder:TRS, Stage 3); a payment its cash cannot meet fails in the declared order
  (TRS.10, K-21 payment order).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a treasury with no debt: its view reads none — `no_debt_reads_none`.
- E1: a treasury short on a payday: payments fail by rank, recorded — `short_fails_by_rank`.

**Extension points**: S1.432, S3.116 (retires `TRS.never_borrows_from_cb`), S3.119 (retires `TRS.funding_rule` (the
plan)), S3.122 (retires `TRS.funding_rule` (the shortfall half)), S3.123.
**Unit tests**: `debt_read_from_register`, `no_debt_reads_none`, `short_fails_by_rank`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-29 (the treasury's debt against its register), LC-1-31 each business day.
**Budget**: +0: 3 treasuries whose view is read inside S1.432's share and the observer's; ledger line 6 (institutions):
+0 B (the buffer is a POLICY schedule, K-20).
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a treasury debt figure kept beside the register; the treasury drawing on its central bank.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The declarations, view and tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-29 and LC-1-31 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.432 — Bills at auction

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.1 STATE *(part: bills; bonds and inflation-linked lines are Stage 3's)*; SOV.3 DECISION *(part: the
minister sizes each weekly auction from the treasury's cash; the funding plan is Stage 3's)*; SOV.4 DECISION *(part:
banks bid for their buffers; other bidders later)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-sov) written; §7.11 (the call auction) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.431 (the buffer target and `TreasuryView` the minister's `size` reads); S1.313 (the bill auction onto
the call auction); S1.282 (bills onto instruments and their events: an issue per auction, redemption by the events
engine); S1.349 (decisions through the decision core); S1.430 (the banks' reserve targets their bids read).
**Goal**: each week the treasury's minister sizes the bill auction from its cash and what matures, announces it, and
each bank bids from its own liquidity; the auction clears at a uniform price, what is unsold is not issued (an event),
and each bill is an instrument held by its buyer until its redemption; the rules are `sys-sov`'s, `core_bills.rs` is
deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules.rs` | `size(&SizeIn) -> Face` (the minister), `bid(&BidIn) -> Schedule` (a bank's price-quantity steps) |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/points.rs` | `SOV.size` (decider: the minister's office, read at founding preferences), `SOV.bid` (the bank's treasurer's office) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/fund.rs` | the auction's day: size → announcement (K-37 record) → bids → K-76 → issue (K-64/K-65) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_bills.rs` | deleted (`tail`, `price_at` into `sys-sov`; `audit_debt` is S1.282's register read) |

**Design**:
- Carries SOV.6 (done at S1.11).
- Calendar: the weekly auction day per country from the bill law (POLICY), announced a declared lead ahead as a record
  (K-37) public to all.
- `size`: the face to offer = what matures that week plus the cash the treasury's buffer lacks (S1.431), less nothing
  else; the minister's rule, a standing SHAPE listed with its source.
- `bid`: a bank's schedule from its reserves above its target and its outlook of the rate (its stance on the published
  auction yields, K-92), in price steps on the auction's tick; households' and others' bids wait for their portfolios.
- K-76 clears at one price; allotment pro rata at the margin by largest remainder, ties by lot; unsold face is not
  issued and recorded as an event (SOV.6); the tail and cover are published with the result (K-37).
- Streams: `SOV.allot` (the kernel's lot).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no bid: nothing is issued, the event recorded, the treasury's cash short falls on its payment order (S1.431) —
  `no_bids_nothing_issued`.
- E5: a maturity week on a payday: redemptions are instrument events at stage 2e, before the auction's settlement —
  `redemption_before_auction_settles`.
- E13: a country whose law issues no bills runs no auction — `no_bill_law_no_auction`.

**Extension points**: S1.433, S1.492, S2.195, S3.116, S3.118, S3.120, S3.166, S8.175.
**Unit tests**: `size_is_maturing_plus_buffer_gap`, `bid_steps_on_tick`, `no_bids_nothing_issued`,
`tail_and_cover_published`, `redemption_before_auction_settles`, `no_bill_law_no_auction`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-16, LC-1-29, LC-1-31 (auctions held, bills issued and redeemed, debt read from the register) from
the first auction.
**Budget**: its share of fin.fixed.fund: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H), on an auction day only: ≤ 3 auctions, ≤ 35
bids each at `fin.call.order_ns` and one call each.
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (the auction's bids are K-76 day items; bills are K-64's instruments, S1.279).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a module named `core_bills`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a linear scan of issues; unsold paper absorbed by anyone.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rules, points, routing and tests; `core_bills.rs` deleted; the fast checks pass.

**Status**: planned

**Architecture**: §10.0a followed.

| `data/profiles/*/profile.toml` | `SOV.debt_short_share` (short-term original maturity over the total), `SOV.holders` (shares by holder sector) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `bank/qpsd`, `bank/bis_debt_securities`, `bank/sovereign_investor_base` → the two primitives, this step |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `for` gains S1.433 |

**Design**:
- `bank/bis_debt_securities` (general government issues by original maturity, S short-term, L long-term): per country
  the short-term share of its securities outstanding; the group's value the median over its countries.
- `bank/sovereign_investor_base`: holders of central-government local-currency securities by sector (banks, central
  bank, non-bank residents, non-residents): the group's median shares.
- `bank/qpsd` (gross debt of central government, % of GDP) is the profile's drawn level (ENDOWMENT) already; this step
  splits it: the short-term share opens as bills (S1.432) maturing weekly over the bill's tenor in equal faces (the
  steady-path convention, GEN.5), their holders the banks by the banks' share, the rest held by the sectors Stage 1
  holds (the central bank's paper waits for CB.5, households' and non-residents' for their portfolios and XB: their
  shares are recorded in the opening report as not opened).
- A holder sector the world does not yet hold is reported, never reassigned to another.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a country missing the maturity split is left out of the median; a group with none keeps its assumption with the
  reason — `missing_split_left_out`.
- E13: a group whose banks hold no paper opens none at banks — `no_bank_share_opens_none`.

**Extension points**: S1.485, S3.142.
**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `short_share_from_bis`, `holder_shares_sum_to_one`, `missing_split_left_out`,
`no_bank_share_opens_none`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-16 (the opening's bills and their holders) at day one.
**Budget**: opening only, no day cost; ledger line 11 (holdings): +0 B (the bills' holdings are within `[store]
holdings`).
**Guards**: `phx-check data`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; bills opened weekly by assumption; an unheld share given to banks; a value typed by hand.
**Done when**:

- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-0-16 passes.

### S1.434 — A bill's discount accrued over its life

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ACC.1 STATE *(part: a bill's discount accrued as interest over its life in its holder's and its issuer's
accounts)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-sov) written; §7.12 (account lines: accruals on dates) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.263 (terms, shapes and due plans: an accrual leg on a discount instrument); S1.282 (bills as
instruments); S1.328 (account lines posted on accrual dates).
**Goal**: a bill bought below its face earns its discount as interest over its life in its holder's lines, and costs it
as interest in the treasury's, on the declared accrual dates; the treasury's bill is taken at its discount when sold,
never at face.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/declare.rs` | the bill family's accrual leg (discount straight-line or by yield, as the bill law's convention states) and its line mapping |

**Design**:
- At issue the holder's carrying value is its price (K-60 cost) and the treasury's liability the price (K-64 issued
  amount stays face; the discount is the difference). On each accrual date of the shape's plan (K-55: the month's end
  and maturity) the accrued part of the discount is posted: interest income to the holder, interest expense to the
  treasury (K-87 lines, stage 2a), the holding's carrying value and the liability raised by it, so at maturity both
  stand at face and redemption realises nothing.
- The convention (straight-line or yield) is the bill law's declared day count, rounded once by its convention (REP.9).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E6: accruals are dated, so a load mid-life resumes by the plan — no state beyond the holding's cost —
  `accrual_resumes_from_plan_after_load`.
- E14: an accrual date that is the maturity: the last accrual before the redemption event (stage 2a before 2e) —
  `last_accrual_before_redemption`.
- E8: amounts in i64 to the smallest unit; the last accrual takes the residue (the convention's) —
  `residue_at_last_accrual`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `accruals_sum_to_discount`, `residue_at_last_accrual`, `redemption_realises_nothing`,
`accrual_resumes_from_plan_after_load`, `last_accrual_before_redemption`.
**Live checks**: LC-0-33 (accounts identity) each day.
**Budget**: on fin.calendar.month_end (each month's last business day): ≈ 20 k accruals at `fin.dues.item_ns` ≈ 0.3
core-ms; joins H (the quarter-end payday carries it).
- ledger line 11 (holdings): +0 B (the discount accrues on the holding's own lot, S1.276).
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a bill carried at face before maturity.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The declaration and tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-0-33 passes.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.435 — Income and consumption tax rules in sys-tax

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: income tax on persons by bands and allowances, a tax on products at the till)*; TAX.2
PROCESS *(part: withheld at payroll, charged at the sale; returns and the VAT chain are Stage 5's)*
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-tax) written; §7.8 (the levy engine) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.270 (taxes onto the levy engine and collectors' payables); S1.253 (declared levy sets fused at
emission); S1.179 (dated policy schedules: bands and rates in force); S1.406 (income paid to persons).
**Goal**: the income tax's bands and allowances and the tax on products are `sys-tax` rules the levy engine calls when a
wage or a sale is emitted; the household's filing decision is `sys-tax`'s; the laws are read by handle; `core_taxes.rs`
and `core_credit.rs` are deleted.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | `withhold(&WageView) -> Levy` (bands on the person's year to date, K-52 tally), `on_product(&SaleView) -> Levy`, `file(&ReturnView)` |
| `data/profiles/*/law.toml` | `TAX.consumption_at_till` (`placeholder:TAX`: a tax on final sales only), `POL.values_standing` (`placeholder:POL`: the law's values unchanged by any parliament) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_taxes.rs`, `core_credit.rs` | deleted (the state's laws are read by their systems' handles) |

**Design**:
- Carries TAX.7 (done at S1.11); TAX.5 (completed at S1.270).
- `withhold`: the wage's tax by the country's bands and allowances in force (K-20) on the person's taxable income this
  tax year (the person's K-52 tally, `taxable`, and `withheld`), so the year's withholding is exact at each payday;
  rounded once by the law's convention; a withholding above the gross is a violation (TAX.2), never skipped.
- `on_product`: the accounts' tax on products for the buyer's final use (`GEN.product_taxes`), charged on top of the
  posted basic price at the sale, rounded once per sale; a sale between firms carries none under
  `TAX.consumption_at_till` (placeholder:TAX), retired when Stage 5 builds the VAT chain.
- `file`: the household's return on its filing day of choice (TAX.7's filing decision re-homed), settling the year's
  difference.
- Every POLICY value stands at its opening value until POL owns it: `POL.values_standing` (placeholder:POL).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E14: two wages of one person the same day: withheld on the year to date in the payroll's order by contract identity
  — `two_wages_withheld_in_contract_order`.
- E13: a country with no income tax: an empty levy set — `no_income_tax_empty_levy_set`.
- E12: a missing band table refuses assembly — `missing_bands_refused`.

**Extension points**: S1.492, S4.146, S4.148, S5.101, S5.103, S5.105 (retires `TAX.consumption_at_till`), S5.109, S5.143
(retires `POL.values_standing`).
**Unit tests**: `withheld_by_bands_on_year_to_date`, `withholding_above_gross_violates`,
`product_tax_on_top_rounded_once`, `no_tax_between_firms_until_vat`, `two_wages_withheld_in_contract_order`,
`no_income_tax_empty_levy_set`, `missing_bands_refused`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-28 (taxes arisen, remitted, owed), LC-0-29 (the levies' sample) each business day.
**Budget**:
- adds +0 phone-ns to `fin.retail.all_in_ns`: the product tax is the "paid and tax" part already inside retail's all-in
  unit (S1.309), fused in its sweep.
- adds +0 phone-ns to `fin.dues.item_ns`: withholding rides the dated item's fused "levy and income line" on paydays
  (`[day.h] dues`).
- on fin.calendar.filing_window (the law's filing months, each household's chosen day): ≈ 34 k returns a business day
  (the households over the window's business days) at ≤ 150 phone-ns ≈ 5 core-ms; joins neither (its days are the
  households' choice, spread over the window); its share of fin.fixed.household_reviews: 5 / 0 / 5 core-ms (B / NB /
  H) in the window.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (returns and withholding ride the tax payables' rows, S1.270, and the dated items).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses modules named `core_taxes`, `core_credit`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tax computed as a rate on an aggregate (TAX.7); a per-flow `Arising` row.

### S1.436 — Mining divisions apart

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §10.0a followed.
**Depends on**: none (the ways' table `TEC.ways` and its derivation exist).
**Goal**: coal and lignite, crude petroleum and natural gas, metal ores and other mining each have their own way —
output, value added, compensation and employment — from the OECD's mining divisions, where one mining industry's way
was shared between its resources by their users.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_tec.py` | B05–B08's ways split from the mining industry's (B09's support services folded into their users' inputs) |
| `data/profiles/*/economy.toml` | `TEC.ways` rows for the four divisions; `TEC.labour` columns |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `open/mining_divisions` → `TEC.ways`, this step; the "until S1.24" status retired |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `for` gains S1.436 |

**Design**:
- Carries TEC.2 (done at S1.02).
- Source: `open/mining_divisions` (B05 coal and lignite, B06 crude petroleum and natural gas, B07 metal ores, B08 other
  mining and quarrying, B09 support services; output, value added, compensation, employment; 2018–2020). Per group the
  median over its countries of each division's share of the mining industry's output, value added, compensation and
  employment, 2019.
- The mining industry's row of the accounts (its inputs, its uses) is split into the four divisions by those shares;
  each division's inputs are the industry's scaled by its output share, its labour hours by its employment share over
  the industry's, B09's output counted as an input of the divisions by their output shares. The accounts' identities
  (row sums, column sums) are checked by `opening::economy::check` after the split and a break refused.
- Each division's resource (coal, oil and gas, ore, stone) is extracted from its own deposits (GEO.6); oil and gas are
  one grade each, coal's grades come from S1.437.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a country missing a division is left out of the median; a group with none keeps the shared way with the reason —
  `missing_division_left_out`.
- E13: a division with no deposits in a country makes nothing there; its demand is met by the between-firms meetings —
  n/a here: a data split; LC-0-15 reads extraction only where deposits are.

**Extension points**: S1.437.
**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `split_preserves_row_and_column_sums`, `support_services_folded_as_input`,
`missing_division_left_out`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-05 (production by its way), LC-0-15 (extraction from deposits) at the first days.
**Budget**: opening only.
**Guards**: `phx-check data`.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a way typed by hand; one resource's way shared with another's; a break in the accounts' identities.

**Goal**: coal deposits open with their sizes and grades, and each grade declares its content per unit (its heat), from
the US mines' output, quality and reserves; oil and gas are one grade each, as their benchmark prices are quoted.

### S1.439 — Graded inputs used and valued by content

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written.
**Depends on**: S1.438 (a way's graded inputs in content); S1.184 (goods issued by the registry); S1.291 (production on
standing rates: a way's inputs consumed at realisation).
**Goal**: a firm running a way uses as many units of the grade it holds as the way's content needs, and values each
grade by what it yields, so a richer grade yields more and grades are priced against each other by what they yield.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/produce.rs` | `units_needed(content, grade_content) -> Qty` read into the plan's input rates |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/inputs.rs` | an input's value in use per unit of a grade = its content × the value of content |

**Design**:
- Carries GDS.1 (done at S1.05), as restated by the owner's answer on grades (§12).
- At the production visit the plan's input rate for each grade the firm holds is content ÷ that grade's content per unit
  (K-22's row), consumed from the oldest grade first by the holding's own order (never an average across grades).
- The inputs rule (S1.444) values a grade by its content: what a unit of the grade is worth in use is its content times
  what the firm's output makes of a unit of content, so a buyer's limit at the meeting differs by grade.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a firm holding none of any grade: the input is short and production is held to what the other inputs allow
  (CAP.9 by construction) — `no_grade_held_no_output`.
- E8: content ÷ grade content rounded up to whole units by the unit's declared rounding — `units_rounded_up_by_unit`.

**Extension points**: S1.440, S1.443, S1.444, S2.157.
**Unit tests**: `richer_grade_needs_fewer_units`, `value_in_use_by_content`, `no_grade_held_no_output`,
`units_rounded_up_by_unit`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-05 (every production by its way, graded inputs included) each day.
**Budget**: adds +0 phone-ns to `fin.decide.visit_ns` (a division per graded input inside the plan's and the inputs'
shares, S1.443) and +0 to `fin.batches.prod_ns` (the realisation reads the rate it is handed).
- ledger line 12 (units, cells, owner index): +0 B (grades are the units registry's ids, S1.183).
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; grades averaged into one.
**Done when**:

### S1.440 — A firm's unit cost as a sys-frm rule

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written; §7.5 (the per-day party cache) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.295 (a firm's unit cost once a day over maintained parts); S1.422 (working owners' hours and pay as
aggregates); S1.303 (the stall book's cheapest price per (product, region)); S1.439 (graded inputs in content).
**Goal**: a firm's cost of making a unit now — its labour, its inputs at what they cost it and its plant's capital
charge, over the units its staff and plant make — is `sys_frm::rules::way::unit_cost`, a `#[per_day]` rule computed at
most once a firm a day through the per-day cache, from maintained parts only.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/way.rs` | `unit_cost(&CostView) -> Missing<Price>`, `#[per_day]` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | the cost read through K-35's `get_or(day, unit_cost)` in every firm view |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `unit_cost`, `unit_cost_of` and `cost_at` removed (`staff_capacity` was retired at S1.262) |

**Design**:
- Carries FRM.14 (done at S1.08).
- The rule is built once, here: S1.295 only moved its callers onto K-35's day-stamped read and its parts onto the
  bases' maintained reads, leaving today's function in `core_goods.rs` until this step moves its body into `sys-frm`.
- `CostView`: the wage bill a day and staff hours by occupation family (K-54), the working owners' hours and pay (K-54,
  S1.422), what the staff make a day at its way's hours and its productivity, each input's cost to it — its holding's
  cost (K-60, K-62 by its declared FIFO or average) for an input it holds, else the least price its region's stall book
  posts for it among sellers with units (K-71), a price posted by a seller with nothing being no cost — its own product
  as an input grossed up, and its plant's capital charge (the period's depreciation and the charge at its rate for new
  debt, S1.426) over its capacity (K-67).
- Labour a unit = the wage bill and owners' pay a day ÷ what the staff make a day; the cost is never the stock's average
  cost. A missing part (no staff, no seller of an unheld input) returns `Missing`; each reader states its answer.
- Called only through K-35 (`#[per_day]`, R7): counter `unit_cost_per_firm_day` ≤ 1.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: an input no seller in the region posts: `Missing`, the reader's stated answer — `unheld_unposted_input_missing`.
- E3: a firm with no staff: labour cost `Missing` — `no_staff_missing_labour`.
- E14: a hire and a price review the same day read the stage's start state (the cache is stamped) —
  `cost_read_from_stamped_cache`.

**Extension points**: S1.441, S1.443, S1.447, S1.450, S1.458, S1.483, S2.205.
**Unit tests**: `labour_per_unit_from_bill_and_output`, `held_input_at_holding_cost`,
`unheld_input_at_least_posted_price`, `own_product_grossed_up`, `capital_charge_over_capacity`,
`unheld_unposted_input_missing`, `no_staff_missing_labour`, `cost_read_from_stamped_cache`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-07 (reviews read unit cost) each day.
**Budget**:
- ≈ 250 k / 30 k / 250 k first uses a day (a firm's first visit or review of the day), each computing `unit_cost` inside
  that occasion's view gather (the gather part of `fin.decide.visit_ns`, itemised at S1.443, and of
  `fin.decide.review_ns`, at S1.450): +0 phone-ns beyond those parts; later reads ride `fin.parties.cache_hit_ns`.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (the cached cost and its day stamp are K-35's 12 B, within `fin.parties.firm_bytes`).
- world counter `unit_cost_per_firm_day` ≤ 1.
**Guards**: `#[per_day]` refuses a direct call (S1.128).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; the cost computed more than once a firm a day; a walk of the employment list; a stock's average cost
standing for the cost of making.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, routing and tests; the functions gone from `core_goods.rs`; the fast checks pass.

**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written.
**Depends on**: S1.440 (a way's unit cost at the prices the firm faces); S1.285 (capital classes and maintained
capacity: which plant kinds the firm holds); S1.228 (the firm's schedule visit); S1.196 (the firm's reserve: `way`).
**Goal**: at each production visit a firm chooses, among the ways it knows that its plant supports, the one whose unit
cost at the input and labour prices it faces is least; the choice is its own through the decision core, and its plan
and orders follow the way chosen.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/way.rs` | `cheapest` (kept) over `supported(&WayView) -> WaySet` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.way` (decider: the head of the firm's line) on the production schedule |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the firm's `way` column (u8 index into its known way set, K-09's interned set) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | the choice at the visit before `FRM.produce` (S1.443) |

**Design**:
- `supported`: the firm's known ways (its interned way set, TEC) whose capital kinds it holds with capacity (K-67); each
  costed by S1.440's rule with that way's inputs and hours (the per-day cache holds one cost per firm; the other ways'
  costs are computed within the visit only, not cached). `cheapest` picks the least; ties go to the current way, then by
  way identity.
- A change of way writes the firm's `way` column; the plan (S1.443) and orders (S1.444) read it the same visit.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a firm whose plant supports one way: no choice, no cost of the others computed — `single_way_no_choice`.
- E12: a way whose cost is `Missing` is not a candidate; with none costed the current way stands —
  `missing_costs_keep_way`.
- E14: a way change and a price review the same visit: the review reads the new way's cost —
  `review_reads_new_way_cost`.

**Extension points**: S1.443, S1.461, S2.207, S8.130, S6.104, S6.107, S6.109, S6.111.
**Unit tests**: `cheapest_supported_way_chosen`, `ties_keep_current_way`, `single_way_no_choice`,
`missing_costs_keep_way`, `review_reads_new_way_cost`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-05 each day.
**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 50 phone-ns to `fin.decide.visit_ns` at 246 k / 30 k / 246 k items (the way choice; a firm with one supported
  way, most, costs nothing), itemised at S1.443.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +1 B a firm (`way`), within `fin.parties.firm_bytes`.
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a way chosen for a firm by its industry.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, point, declaration, routing and tests; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-05 passes.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.442 — Capacity's check declared in the Units family

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-cap) written; §7.17 (the audit: families and their checks) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.353 (the audit engine: the ten families as pure checks, each with its owner base); S1.285 (capital
classes and maintained capacity, K-67, the Units family's owner base); S1.291 (production realised on standing rates).
**Goal**: CAP.9's check — no realisation's units above what the plant, hours and inputs it used allow — is declared by
`sys-cap` as a check of the Units family (owner base K-67), not a new family, recounting from source rows and never
reading the maintained values it checks.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/audit.rs` | `capacity_check(&Realised, &Sources) -> Finding?` registered in the Units family |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/inject.rs` | `phx inject` gains the check's injection (a realisation above its plant) |

**Design**:
- Follows N1: the check is one of the Units family's checks (the family's owner base K-67), declared with its clause
  CAP.9; S1.353's families stay ten.

  capacity from K-67's holdings, the hours from K-53's employment rows and the inputs consumed from K-61's nature legs,
  and reports any excess with owner, size, day and clause; it never repairs.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a day with no realisation checks nothing — `no_realisation_no_check`.
- E8: a realisation exactly at capacity is no finding — `at_capacity_no_finding`.

**Extension points**: S1.443.

test `capacity_excess_lights_only_units`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-11 (the Units family clean) from S1.443 on.
**Budget**: its share of fin.fixed.recount: 2 / 1 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H), inside S1.353's whole-audit share (0 of its own in the table): the touched firms' recounts (≤ 400 k / 100 k
/ 400 k realisations' firms, at `fin.audit.recount_ns_per_row`).
- ledger line 12 (units, cells, owner index): +0 B (the check reads the Units family's rows).
**Guards**: `phx inject` covers the check.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a new audit family; the check reading the maintained capacity; a check that repairs.

### S1.443 — Production on the firm's schedule

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.4 DECISION; CAP.9 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written; §7.10 (standing rates) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.291 (production and spoilage onto standing rates); S1.441 (the way run); S1.442 (capacity's check in
the Units family); S1.426 (the firm's rate for new debt); S1.440 (unit cost); S1.439 (graded inputs by content).
**Goal**: at each production visit a firm decides how much to make a day from its expected demand, its stock, its
capacity, the inputs and labour it has, the margin at the prices it expects and what financing its work in progress and
stock costs it at the margin; the quantity is set as its standing rate; no output ever exceeds what its plant, labour
and inputs allow, and the audit's Units family shows it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/produce.rs` | `target(&ProduceIn) -> Produce` (kept), its inputs completed |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.produce` (decider: the line's head) on `FRM.production_days` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | the visit: view, rule, the rate written to K-68 at 5d; each realisation's record into the change set |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `make`, `making`, `stored_inputs` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries GDS.4 (done at S1.05); TEC.9 (completed at S1.273).
- `ProduceIn`: expected sales a day (its own sales outlook, REP.20), stock on hand (K-60, realised first, K-68), its
  cover target (management PREFERENCE), capacity (K-67, the scarcest kind), its staff's hours by occupation family
  (K-54) against the way's, each stored input held (K-60, in content for graded inputs, S1.439), the price it expects
  (its stance's outlook, K-92) and unit cost (S1.440), and the carrying cost of work in progress and stock at its rate
  for new debt (S1.426). Output: the rate a day, never above the least of capacity, labour and inputs a day (the rule's
  own arithmetic; when nothing is available, doing nothing is the rule's action, S1.154).
- The rate is a K-68 standing rate with its kink (an input reaching zero at the rate) on K-42; realisation is lazy and
  exact (units over [a, b] = ⌊r·b⌋ − ⌊r·a⌋), consuming inputs by the way; each realisation records (firm, units, days)
  in the day's change set, which S1.442's check reads.
- A missing financing rate or lead time is `Missing` in the view and the rule's stated answer applies (never 0).
- The firm visit's unit, `fin.decide.visit_ns`, itemised here (phone-ns an item): handler 30 + the view's gather 150
  (the day's unit cost on first use included, S1.440) + way choice ≤ 50 (S1.441) + this plan ≤ 100 + input orders
  ≤ 180 (S1.444) + posting ≤ 100 (S1.413) + services ≤ 50 (S1.445) = 660; left for later shares: S8.130's weighing
  ≈ 90 and S2.113's ≈ 40, = 790 of 800.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a firm with no stock, no input, no staff: rate 0 by the rule — `nothing_available_makes_nothing`.
- E14: a sale and a realisation on one holding the same day: realise, then apply (K-68) — `realise_before_sale_applies`.
- E1: a catastrophe destroying inputs: the kink re-derives the rate (K-68) — `lost_inputs_redraw_kink`.
- E12: `Missing` price outlook: plans for expected sales at its current price — `missing_outlook_plans_at_price`.

**Extension points**: S1.444, S1.445, S1.483, S2.121, S2.174, S2.207, S2.211, S2.213, S8.130.
**Unit tests**: `rate_never_exceeds_scarcest`, `carrying_cost_lowers_stock_target`, `nothing_available_makes_nothing`,
`missing_outlook_plans_at_price`, `realise_before_sale_applies`, `lost_inputs_redraw_kink`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-05 (productions by their way), LC-1-11 (no output beyond capacity: the Units family clean) each
day.
**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 100 phone-ns to `fin.decide.visit_ns` at 246 k / 30 k / 246 k items (the plan; the unit's itemisation above).
- adds 400 k / 100 k / 400 k items to `fin.batches.prod_ns` (the realisations, `[day.*] production`).
- ledger line 13 (liens and processes): +0 B (the rate and its kink are K-68's).
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a pass over every firm every day; stock grown daily for every firm.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, point, routing and tests; the functions gone from `core_goods.rs`; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-05 and LC-1-11 pass.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.444 — Input orders against the stall book

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: GDS.5 DECISION
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-frm) written; §7.11 (the between-firms meeting, the stall book) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.443 (the planned rate the orders serve); S1.426 (the firm's rate for new debt); S1.264 (what its
contracts take before its next visit, read from cached plans); S1.303 (stalls and cheapest onto the stall book); S1.439
(an input's value in use by content).
**Goal**: at each production visit a firm orders each stored input from its planned use over the lead and cover days
less what it holds, each at no more than the input is worth to it in use counting what financing that stock costs it at
the margin, within the money it holds beyond what its contracts take before its next visit; energy is bought as a plain
good under a declared placeholder naming ENE.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/inputs.rs` | `orders(&OrdersIn) -> Wants` (kept), `carried_cost` over the firm's own rate |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.inputs` (decider: the line's head) on the production schedule |
| `data/shared/GDS.toml` | `GDS.energy_as_goods` (`placeholder:ENE`), retired by Stage 2's energy markets |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/decide.rs` | orders written into the day's between-firms want buckets (K-03) at 5b |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `buy_inputs` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries FRM.7 (done at S1.08).
- `OrdersIn`: the way's use of each stored input per unit (in content for graded inputs), the planned rate (S1.443), the
  lead days (TEC, a refusal at assembly if absent) and cover days (management PREFERENCE), each input held (K-60), its
  value in use (the output's expected price less the other costs a unit, S1.440), the carrying cost at the firm's rate
  for new debt (S1.426) over the days held, and its free money: its balance less what its contracts take before its
  next visit (K-55 plans, K-54 owed sums), never `owed_until` walking families.
- Output: per input a quantity and a limit price (`Want::UpTo`); the firm's own product used as an input comes from its
  own stock, kept off its offer. Orders meet in the between-firms meeting (K-75/K-73) with price levels and limits.
- Energy products (electricity, gas) are goods at posted prices (`GDS.energy_as_goods`, placeholder:ENE).
- Streams: none (the meeting's own).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no seller of an input in reach: the want fails visibly and production is held to what inputs allow —
  `no_seller_want_fails_visibly`.
- E3: a firm with no free money orders nothing — `no_free_money_orders_nothing`.
- E12: a missing rate: the carrying cost is the rule's stated answer (S1.426), never 0 — `missing_rate_stated_answer`.

**Extension points**: S1.468, S1.472, S1.473, S1.483, S2.111, S2.163, S2.207 (retires `GDS.energy_as_goods`), S8.130,
S5.177.
**Unit tests**: `order_is_use_over_lead_and_cover_less_held`, `limit_is_value_in_use_less_carrying`,
`no_free_money_orders_nothing`, `own_product_from_own_stock`, `no_seller_want_fails_visibly`,
`missing_rate_stated_answer`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-05 (no production without its inputs) each day.
**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 180 phone-ns to `fin.decide.visit_ns` at 246 k / 30 k / 246 k items (input orders; the unit itemised at
  S1.443).
- adds 3.3 M / 0.3 M / 3.3 M items to `fin.b2b.purchase_ns` (the orders' purchases, `[day.*] b2b`).
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (the orders are the day's between-firm items at 12 B, S1.161's figure).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses `owed_until` or a family walk on a visit path.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a pass over every firm every day; an order beyond the money the firm holds free; a financing rate
read as 0.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, point, placeholder, routing and tests; `buy_inputs` gone; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-05 passes.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S1.445 — Services bought for what was made

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-srv) written; §7.11 (perishable daily capacity) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.325 (services' capacity onto perishable capacity); S1.443 (what the firm made or sold since its last
visit); S1.306 (the posted-price meeting).
**Goal**: a firm buys the services its way uses on its production schedule for what it made or sold, at posted prices,
from providers whose day's capacity is rationed by lot; the rule is `sys-srv`'s, and a provider's unused capacity is
lost by construction.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-srv/src/lib.rs` | `services_wanted(&ServicesIn) -> Wants`: each service input per unit made, as budgets |
| `crates/systems/sys-srv/src/points.rs` | `SRV.buy` (decider: the line's head) on the production schedule |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `buy_services`, the services' meeting call removed |

**Design**:
- Carries SRV.5 (done at S1.06); FRM.7 (done at S1.08); SRV.1 (completed at S1.325).
- `ServicesIn`: the way's service inputs per unit, the units made since the last visit (K-68's realised count), the
  firm's free money (as S1.444). Services are bought as whole units: each want is a quantity (the way's service units
  for what was made) with a limit point set by the rule at 5b — the highest point on the service's grid whose price
  times the quantity its free money covers; at 5d the firm reserves quantity × that point's price in its own `pending`
  (K-47), and the unspent remainder is released at 6b's end. Wants meet at the region's providers (K-73) with capacity
  from K-85 (a stale stamp reads as unused; what no sale took is lost).
- Streams: none (the meeting's own).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: every provider full: the want goes unmet, recorded (SRV.5) — `full_providers_turn_buyer_away`.
- E5: a busy day's services share the day's capacity by lot (K-73) — n/a here: the lot is K-73's own test at S1.306;
  LC-1-17.

**Extension points**: S1.483, S2.130, S2.163, S8.195.
**Unit tests**: `wanted_per_unit_made`, `full_providers_turn_buyer_away`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-16, LC-1-17 (services sold, capacity lost) each day.
**Budget**:
- adds ≤ 50 phone-ns to `fin.decide.visit_ns` at 246 k / 30 k / 246 k items (services wanted; the unit itemised at
  S1.443).
- its purchases are among `[day.*] b2b`'s items on `fin.b2b.purchase_ns` (+0 items: counted at S1.444's figure); K-85's
  uses are fused in them.
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 B (the services wanted are among S1.444's day items).
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a service stored.
**Done when**:

### S1.446 — Spoilage on standing rates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-gds) written; §7.10 (standing rates, lots) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.291 (spoilage onto standing rates); S1.276 (lots and their age).
**Goal**: goods that spoil lose units at their product's declared yearly rate over the days they are held, a physical
transformation to nature (SET.9), realised when the holding is read and at its kinks; the rate's function is
`sys-gds`'s and no party of any kind is visited for it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/rules/spoil.rs` | `spoilage_rate(product) -> Rate` from `GDS.spoilage_rate`, the K-68 rate a spoiling holding carries |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/declare.rs` | spoiling products declared to K-68 (a rate per spoiling holding, anchored at its lot's day) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `spoil` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries GDS.8 (done at S1.05); GDS.10 (done at S1.07).
- Every holding of a spoiling product carries a negative standing rate (units a day at `GDS.spoilage_rate`'s yearly
  rate over the held units, rational, K-68), anchored on the day it was last realised; a read, a sale or a delivery
  realises it first; each realisation is a nature leg (K-61's spoilage source) at the holding's cost (ACC).
- A lot's age (K-62) is the holding's own; storage is not modelled apart from the good (GDS.8's storage service is
  Stage 2's HSG/warehouse, a declared later point).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E4: an estate's goods spoil on read, exactly as any holder's — `estate_goods_spoil_on_read`.
- E9: the rate needs no daily visit; a holding never read realises at its kink — `unread_holding_realises_at_kink`.

**Extension points**: S1.472, S1.483.
**Unit tests**: `realised_units_exact_over_interval`, `estate_goods_spoil_on_read`, `unread_holding_realises_at_kink`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-32 (the goods identity by nature's legs) each day.
**Budget**: +0: spoilage realises inside the reads that already realise a holding (`fin.batches.prod_ns`, S1.443's
items) and at its kinks, whose entries are `fin.fixed.kinks`' (its share: 1 / 1 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H), ≈ 20 k spoiled
lots' kinks a day at the wheel's unit); no pass on period days.
- ledger line 11 (holdings): +0 B (spoilage is the lot's standing rate, S1.276, and its kink, line 14).
**Guards**: `phx-check` refuses a pass over parties of every kind (S1.121).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a pass on spoilage days; spoilage and storage as one number.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, declaration and tests; `spoil` gone; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-32 passes.
- [ ] §3.5 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/buffer.rs` | `spend(&SpendIn) -> Budget` (the buffer-stock rule, kept) |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/points.rs` | `HH.spend` (decider: the household) on `HH.spending_days` |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/audit.rs` | HH.15's check, registered in the Flows family (owner base K-48): each household touched today, its spend against sales to named sellers, its income against flows from named payers (recounted from the day's items) |
| `data/shared/HH.toml` | `HH.real_return` (`placeholder:BFL`) and `HH.income_growth` (`placeholder:HH`, retired at S1.454) kept |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `decide_spending` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries HH.1, HH.2, HH.4, HH.5, HH.18, HH.19, HH.20 (done at S1.12); `HH.real_return` in HH.4 is retired by
  S2.177.
- `SpendIn`: the household's cash on hand (its persons' `available` on K-47 — balance + limit + min(pending, 0)), what
  its contracts take before its next spending day (K-55, K-54), its income this period (its persons' K-52 tallies), its
  outlook of income and prices (its own and its stance's, K-92; income growth under `HH.income_growth` until S1.454),
  its patience and risk aversion (its preference type), the return on saving (`HH.real_return`, placeholder:BFL) and
  what it can borrow (nothing in Stage 1). Output: the period's spending, shared over products by its country's budget
  shares (the preference type's declared array), written straight into per-(chunk, product) want buckets (K-03) as money
  budgets, never quantities, their sum within the persons' free money; in the same pass S1.406's split writes each
  member's share as its `pending` hold — the till's authorization, so no purchase within its want is refused later — and
  the hold expires with the day's `pending` commit (K-47), with no release pass; no `household_decl.clone()`.
- Needs (HH.20) are the one household want in quantity: a need is a quantity of a good the preference type declares,
  carried with a limit point set by the rule at 5b — the highest price point on the product's grid (REP.34) whose price
  times the quantity the product's budget covers; in the same pass it holds quantity × that point's price in the
  persons' `pending` by S1.406's split, expiring with the commit as for money wants. A household that cannot cover its
  needs claims what it is eligible for (S1.421) and otherwise goes without, recorded as an event.
- HH.15's check (the Flows family, N1's ten unchanged): over the households the day touched (K-07), each want that
  became a sale names a seller party and each payment to a person names its payer; recounted from the day's sale items
  and flows, never from the maintained tallies; a finding names the household, size, day and clause.
- The spending occasion's unit, `fin.decide.spend_ns`, itemised here (phone-ns an item, 472 k items every day type):
  handler 30 (the decision core, `fin.decide.handler_ns`) + the view's gather 90 (the household's hot line and its
  persons' balances and dues, prefetched along the person chain in the agenda chunk's slot order) + the reservation ≤ 5
  (S1.406, in the gather's cache lines) + the rule 35 (the buffer-stock rule's exponential tabulated per preference type
  at assembly, read by interpolation) + wants 50 (the type's share array applied to the budget into per-(chunk,
  product) buckets, no per-product branch) = 210; the outlook update is +0 here (S1.454 updates it at income events).
  Left open for later shares: S8.107's weighing (its generator replaces the rule's 35 at 34, weights 5) and S5.181's
  remittances, each stating its offset against the 5 left under 215.
- Streams: none (the meeting's own).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a household with nothing: spends nothing and records going without — `nothing_held_goes_without`.
- E5: payday spending: occasions are due by schedule, not by payday; the meeting bears the day's volume —
  `occasions_due_by_schedule_not_payday`.
- E14: a spending occasion and a benefit claim the same day read the stage's start state —
  `spend_reads_stage_start_state`.

**Extension points**: S1.454 (retires `HH.income_growth`), S1.483, S2.137, S2.144, S2.173, S2.164, S2.165, S2.177
(retires `HH.real_return`), S2.207, S3.158, S8.107, S5.181, S6.129.
**Unit tests**: `spend_by_buffer_rule`, `shares_by_budget_array`, `nothing_held_goes_without`,
`occasions_due_by_schedule_not_payday`, `spend_reads_stage_start_state`; the check's injection test
`unnamed_seller_lights_only_hh15`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-18 and LC-1-32 each day; the Flows family clean.
**Budget**:
- adds 210 phone-ns to `fin.decide.spend_ns` at 472 k / 472 k / 472 k items (the itemisation above, S1.406's ≤ 5
  included; miss budget ≤ 1.4 a occasion).
- its share of fin.fixed.recount: 2 / 2 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H), inside S1.353's whole-audit share (0 of its own in the table): HH.15's check over the touched households at
  `fin.audit.ident_ns`.
- ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (named slot `spend`, inside S1.196's 174 B).
**Guards**: `phx inject` gains HH.15's check's injection.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a pass over every household every day; a spending decision read from an aggregate propensity.
**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule, point, family, routing and tests; `decide_spending` gone; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-1-18 and LC-1-32 pass.

### S1.449 — Posted-price marks by units sold

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.5 (sys-gds) written; §7.11 (prints and marks) followed.
**Depends on**: S1.327 (traded sums and marks onto prints and marks); S1.326 (per-market per-day exact sums).
**Goal**: the day's mark of a posted-price market is its sales' mean weighted by units sold — revenue ÷ units, from the
day's exact sums — declared as the posted-price form's mark rule; a market with no sale keeps its last mark with its
age; `mark` leaves `core_goods.rs`.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/declare.rs` | the retail and between-firms markets' mark rule `RevenueOverUnits` declared (K-21 market data) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/core_goods.rs` | `mark` removed |

**Design**:
- Carries MKT.2, MKT.12, MKT.14 (done at S0.18); MKT.12 as restated by the owner's answer on marks (§12: a posted-price
  mark is revenue ÷ units).
- K-86 accumulates each (market, day)'s Σ value and Σ units exactly; at 6b the declared rule divides once, rounding by
  the market's price convention (REP.9), and writes the mark with its day; a market with no sale keeps its last mark and
  its age shows (Law 8, MKT.14); the prints themselves are each sale at its posted price.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no sale: no new mark, the last's age grows — `no_sale_keeps_last_with_age`.
- E11: day zero: the snapshot's present value is the mark (GEN.5) — `day_zero_mark_is_snapshot`.

**Extension points**: S1.450, S1.467, S1.469, S1.489, S2.141.
**Unit tests**: `mark_is_revenue_over_units`, `no_sale_keeps_last_with_age`, `day_zero_mark_is_snapshot`.
**Live checks**: LC-1-08 (prices' reads) each day.
**Budget**: its share of fin.fixed.calls: 4 / 4 / 4 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 20 k (market, day) marks at ≤ 200
phone-ns, at 6b every day type (retail runs every day).
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (the marks are S1.326's rows).
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an average of posted prices standing for a mark; a mark of 0 for a market that did not trade.
**Done when**:
