### S2.104 — Enforcement, collection and write-offs

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.9 PROCESS *(part: enforcement and write-off; mortgages' enforcement at S2.158)*; BNK.12 INVARIANT;
HH.13 PROCESS *(part: collection and enforcement)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9c demands, 2c, 2f), §7.8 (K-48, K-49), §7.12 (K-89), §7.17 (K-103 families)
**Depends on**: S2.103 (the enforce choice), S2.102 (provisions held), S1.237 (K-45 demands due next business day),
S1.248 (K-49 settlement and failures), S1.277 (K-63 liens: collateral pledged to the lender), S1.332 (K-89 carrying
value), S1.353 (K-103 audit families), S1.344 (endings: a firm's default of payment opens its estate), S1.346 (estates'
payments by the waterfall)
**Goal**: enforcement accelerates the balance by a demand due the next business day; unpaid, it is the borrower's
default of payment with its contract's consequences. Collateral is sold for what it fetches, collection recovers what it
can, and a write-off removes the loan and books the loss not already provided — principal minus recovery minus
provisions — as a dated event naming lender, borrower and sizes.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/workout.rs` | message `EnforcementDemand` (lender → borrower, issued 9c, due next business day 2c, TIME.7) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/writeoff.rs` | `loss_to_capital(principal, recovery, provision) -> Money`; `continue_collection(value_left, cost) -> bool` |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | reason `BNK.writeoff` (a contract-closing instruction with no money leg: K-53 close + K-89 write-down + K-87 loss line); the collection review on K-43; audit family `BNK.loss_identity` (K-103) |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | collection costs in hours (TECHNOLOGY), recourse law after a collateral sale (POLICY) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_2_01.rs`, `lc_2_03.rs` | LC-2-01, LC-2-03 |

**Design**:
- **Demand** (TIME.7): the enforce decision (S2.103, 5c) posts `EnforcementDemand` at 9c for the accelerated balance; at
  the next business day's 2c it is a K-48 flow in the call batch (K-49); unpaid, the contract's default of payment:
  - a firm borrower: its default of payment (FRM.15) opens its procedure (S2.123; before it, S1.428's default after
    grace and its ending, S1.344); the lender is a secured creditor of its collateral's proceeds in the waterfall
    (K-98);
  - a mortgage: title transfer and foreclosure (S2.158); until then the loan stays in enforcement, counted
    (`sys_bnk.enforcements_waiting`), a placeholder naming HSG retired at S2.158;
  - unsecured household debt: **collection** — the lender's review (K-43, monthly) collects what the borrower's accounts
    pay against the balance (K-49 dues); the creditor's petition joins at S2.166.
- **Recovery** is money received: a collateral sale's proceeds (the sale is a market match, never a valuation) or
  collections, less costs paid to named parties.
- **Write-off** (BNK.9, BNK.12), in 2f's apply when the collateral's sale settles, the waterfall pays the lender's
  class, or `continue_collection` finds the collection's expected value below its cost: the contract closes (K-53); the
  carrying value is written to zero against the provision (K-89); the loss reaching capital = principal − recovery −
  provision, posted as a loss line (K-87) moving equity (K-88); an event on K-36 names lender, borrower, principal,
  recovery, provision and loss. The realised recovery updates the lender's recovery outlook per collateral class
  (S1.425's assessment learns).
- **Audit family `BNK.loss_identity`** (BNK.12): for each write-off of the day, from the source rows (the closed
  contract's last balance, the recovery flows, the provision column) — never from the maintained book (R4).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a thousand firms defaulting on one lender the same day — demands are K-45 posts, write-offs arrive over estates'
  distribution days, never in one pass (`writeoffs_follow_distributions`).
- E3: a borrower with no account — the demand fails as `NoMoney` and is recorded (MON.12)
  (`demand_without_account_fails`).
- E4: collateral that never sells — the loan stays in enforcement; nothing writes it off by a bound; counted
  (`unsold_collateral_stays_in_enforcement`).
- E10: a lender closed in resolution (S2.196) mid-enforcement — the loan's lender side moved with its book (K-57); the
  demand's sender resolves to the successor (`demand_sender_resolves_to_successor`).
- E6: an `EnforcementDemand` due tomorrow and loans waiting in enforcement are K-45 messages and K-56 statuses (saved);
  `demand_round_trip` shows a load between 9c and the next 2c pays or fails the same demand.

**Extension points**: `BNK.writeoff` is the one write-off instruction for S2.114 (none: sellers' losses are waterfall
shortfalls), S2.158 (foreclosure), S2.168 (discharge), S2.196 (resolution's write-downs).

**Unit tests**:
- `writeoff_loss_identity`: principal − recovery − provision with provisions above and below the loss.
- `demand_due_next_business_day` over given calendars (TIME.7); `continue_collection_stops_below_cost`;
  `writeoffs_follow_distributions`; `demand_round_trip`; `demand_without_account_fails`;
  `unsold_collateral_stays_in_enforcement`; `demand_sender_resolves_to_successor`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-01`: BNK.12 — the audit family is clean every close.
- `LC-2-03`: BNK.14 in practice — every recovery traces to a sale print or collections less costs paid to named parties;
  no recovery reads a declared rate; recovery dispersion per collateral class and quarter is published.

**Budget**:
- Demands and write-offs B / NB / H ≈ 1 k / 0 / 10 k × 200 ns (K-45 post, K-53 close, K-89, K-87) → < 1 / 0 / 2 core-ms;
  the audit family per write-off, fused (K-103).
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.2 / 0 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.mass_default (event): 0 core-ms; joins H and B′
- spread after fin.calendar.mass_default over 5 days: 4 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.resolve (100 k demands and write-offs
  on the estates' distribution days, S2.133's drawn phases)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-45's demands, K-56's status)
- Counters: `sys_bnk.demands`, `sys_bnk.writeoffs`, `sys_bnk.enforcements_waiting`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fixed recovery; a write-off that books a loss already provided; a recovery from a valuation.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, the audit family and unit tests written; fast checks pass; `phx inject` of the family reports
  the injected break.
- [ ] LC-2-01 and LC-2-03 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.105 — Covenant tests on received statements

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.7 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9b statements, 9c tests), §7.12 (K-90), §7.7 (K-45)
**Depends on**: S2.103 (the workout decision and `BNK.awaiting_workout`), S1.333 (K-90 statements closed on each party's
calendar), S1.237 (K-45 messages), S1.263 (K-55: covenants as declared terms of a loan shape)
**Goal**: a firm's loan carries covenants — the most leverage, the least interest cover, a reporting duty — as terms;
the borrower sends its lender its statement on the covenant's reporting dates, the lender tests it privately, and a
breach or a missed report wakes the lender's workout, which then decides exactly as for arrears. BNK.7 is complete: both
of its triggers reach the one decision.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/covenants.rs` | covenant terms (ratio kind, threshold, reporting period) declared per loan family's shape; message `CovenantStatement` (borrower → lender, carrying the K-90 statement's headline lines) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/covenants.rs` | `breaches(statement, covenants) -> BreachSet` (pure) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | slot 9c; reporting due on K-42 per loan (the covenant's period, anchored at the loan's start) |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | customary covenants per firm loan family (POLICY of the trade) with sources |

**Design**:
- **Sending**: on each covenant reporting date (a due on K-42 for the loan, not a pass), the borrower's latest closed
  statement (K-90, its own calendar) is posted to the lender as a `CovenantStatement` (K-45) — a read, not a copy of the
  books (Law 4: the message carries the statement's headline lines by reference).
- **Test** (9c): `breaches` compares each covenant's ratio, read from the statement's lines, with its threshold; a
  breach, or no statement by the due, inserts the loan into `BNK.awaiting_workout` and wakes the lender (9e apply); the
  workout (S2.103) decides by the same values, with "waive for a fee" curing the breach.
- **Households' loans** carry no financial covenants (declared: their families declare none).
- A demand following a breach is due the next business day (TIME.7) — the workout's enforce path (S2.104).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: reporting dates are anchored at each loan's start, so they spread over the calendar and none stacks on a
  quarter-end; a fixture of 400 k firm loans' dates shows the daily count flat (`reporting_dates_spread`).
- E11: day zero — the first reports use the snapshot's latest filed statements (GEN.5); none is due on day zero
  (`no_report_due_on_day_zero`).
- E12: a statement missing a line a covenant reads — the covenant is untestable and counted as a missed report, never
  passed by default (`missing_line_is_missed_report`).

**Extension points**: covenants read by S3.137 (bond covenants, CRD.6) through the same terms and rule.

**Unit tests**: `covenant_test_on_statement` (breaches found over given statements and terms);
`missing_line_is_missed_report`; `reporting_dates_spread`; `no_report_due_on_day_zero`.

**Live checks**: none (the workout's outcomes are read by LC-2-02 and the gate).

**Budget**:
- Covenant reports B / NB / H ≈ 6 k / 0 / 6 k (≈ 0.4 M firm loans reporting quarterly from their own starts) × 80 ns (a
  K-45 post and a test) → < 1 / 0 / < 1 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.5 / 0 / 0.5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (core attribute: the covenant terms are K-55's)
- Counters: `sys_bnk.covenant_tests`, `sys_bnk.covenant_breaches`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a lender reading a borrower's books other than the statement sent; a covenant tested daily.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.106 — The loan-book valuer

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.5 PROCESS *(part: the named valuer of a failing bank's loan book; resolution at S2.196–S2.199)*
**Architecture**: §7.12 (K-91 valuer declarations)
**Depends on**: S1.335 (K-91 valuations and valuer declarations), S1.326 (K-86 prints), S1.425 (accepted loans' rates as
prints of the loan market)
**Goal**: a named valuer publishes a method that values a loan or a lender's book entry from prints alone — the rates of
that class's loans accepted recently in the country and, per arrears stage, the prices of that class's loan sales — each
labelled with its age. Resolution (S2.196), an estate's administrator (S2.133) and loan sales (S2.107) appoint it; no
lender's outlook or quote is an input.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/valuers/loan_book.rs` | the method as a pure function over K-86 prints: contractual payments (K-55 plan) discounted at the class's accepted-loan rates; per stage, the class's loan-sale price ratio; nearest declared prints when a stage has none, labelled |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | `ValuerDecl` "loan book" (K-91): its owner (a named valuation firm per country), published method id, the prints it reads (market keys) |
| `data/<country>/gen/BNK.toml` | the valuer party per country (ENDOWMENT) |

**Design**:
- **Inputs**: the loan market's prints (each accepted loan is a print of its (class, term) market, K-86, from S1.425)
  and loan-sale prints (S2.107), both "as of day d" with ages. **Output**: a valuation (K-91) labelled traded / nearest,
  with the prints and their ages; it never enters a market or an index (VAL.20).
- **Serves** MKT.20 (completed at S1.335): the method is one valuer's declaration under it.
- **Method**: value = Σ contractual payments × discount factors from the class's accepted-loan rates (K-91 curve from
  prints; interpolated points labelled), times the stage's sale price ratio where the stage has a sale print, else the
  nearest stage's labelled "nearest".
- It is a method declaration and a pure function; the valuation kernel (K-91) runs it when an appointer asks.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no loan sale ever printed for a class — the stage factor is labelled missing, the valuation shows it; a reader's
  rule decides what a missing factor means (never 1, never 0) (`no_sale_print_labelled`).
- E11: day zero — prints are the snapshot's present values (GEN.5), one per loan market
  (`day_zero_values_from_snapshot_prints`).

**Extension points**: appointed by S2.107, S2.133, S2.196 (resolution valuation, SUP.5).

**Unit tests**: `loan_book_value_from_prints` (per stage, with labels); `no_sale_print_labelled`;
`day_zero_values_from_snapshot_prints`; `valuation_reads_no_outlook` (the function's signature takes prints only —
compile level).

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Valuations on appointment only (resolution, estates, loan sales): ≈ 0 / 0 / 0 a day at the design point, 1 ms a book's
  entries when appointed (K-91 curve reuse); no daily cost.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H); an appointment's cost is its appointer's (S2.107,
  S2.133, S2.196)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-91's declarations)
- Counter: `sys_bnk.loan_book_valuations`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a valuation reading a lender's outlook or quote; a valuation entering a market or an index.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Method, declaration, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.

### S2.107 — Loan sales and quotes on a loan side

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.10 PROCESS *(part: sales between banks; non-bank lenders buy at S3.199, vehicles at S4.161, where it
completes)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c, 7), §7.11 (K-80), §7.9 (K-57 side moves)
**Depends on**: S1.317 (K-80 bilateral protocol), S1.267 (K-57 `move_end` of a lender side), S2.102 (claim values under
the assessment), S2.106 (the loan-book valuer as the seller's reference), S1.248 (K-49 settlement of the price)
**Goal**: a bank that wants to shed loans asks the banks it can reach for quotes on its side of named loans, each asked
bank quotes from its own claim value under its own assessment or declines, and the seller takes the best quote at or
above its reservation; the lender side moves against the price in one settlement. The same quote rule (`quote_loans`)
answers a seller's factoring ask (S2.115).

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/sale.rs` | messages `LoanSaleAsk` (loans offered with terms and payment records), `LoanSaleQuote`; decision kinds `BNK.sell_loans`, `BNK.quote_loans`; reason `BNK.loan_sale` (a side move linked with a price flow, K-48 link group) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/loan_sale.rs` | `reservation(claim_value, shadow_cost) -> Money`; `quote(rows, own_assessment, required_return) -> Option<Money>` |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | slots 5c (ask, quote, accept); stream `BNK.loan_sale_lot`; the reservation's shadow-cost placeholder |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | first-price request for quotes (MKT.7) with its source |

**Design**:
- **Ask** (`BNK.sell_loans`, a lumpy decision on the bank's review or when its capital or liquidity binds — K-93 limit
  event): the loans it would shed and the banks in its reach; a `LoanSaleAsk` on K-80 to each.
- **Quote** (`BNK.quote_loans`, the asked bank's next 5c): its `loan_claim_value` of the loans under **its own**
  assessment of their class and payment records (BNK.15; PC-40), less its required return on the capital they would
  consume, or a decline.
- **Reservation**: the seller's own claim value less its shadow cost of the cash or capital the loans tie up. Until
  BFL's and BCP's shadow costs exist the term is absent and the reservation is the claim value alone — a SHAPE
  placeholder naming BFL and BCP, retired by S2.179 (the shadow cost of cash) and S2.188 (the shadow cost of capital).
- **Accept** (the seller's next 5c): the best quote at or above the reservation; ties by lot (`BNK.loan_sale_lot`). The
  acceptance writes one link group: `move_end` of the lender side of each loan (K-57, O(1) each) and the price as a flow
  buyer → seller, all or none at 7 (SET.4). The sale is a print of the loan-sale market (K-86), read by S2.106.
- The buyer's book (K-93) and provisions (S2.102) take the loans under its own assessment on the settle day.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no quote at or above the reservation — no sale, recorded as a failed meeting (MKT.10)
  (`no_sale_below_reservation`).
- E10: a loan whose borrower ended between ask and accept — the side moved is the estate's claim; its claim value is the
  buyer's own, the sale goes through or is declined by the rule (`sale_of_estate_claim_valued_by_buyer`).
- E14: a loan asked of two banks and sold to one — the other's quote lapses (K-45 lapse) (`unaccepted_quote_lapses`).
- E6: open asks and quotes are K-45/K-80 messages (saved) — `open_ask_round_trip` answers the same asks after a load.

**Extension points**: `quote_loans` is called by S2.115 (factoring) and, with its data extended, by the non-bank lenders
(S3.201) and the securitising banks (S4.161); the reservation's shadow-cost term is supplied by S2.179 and S2.188.

**Unit tests**: `loan_sale_reservation_net_of_shadow_cost` (falls as the shadow cost rises; a lower quote refused);
`best_quote_taken_ties_by_lot`; `no_sale_below_reservation`; `sale_is_one_link_group`; `open_ask_round_trip`;
`sale_of_estate_claim_valued_by_buyer`; `unaccepted_quote_lapses`.

**Live checks**: none (the gate's reads count sales; LC-2-03 reads their prints).

**Budget**:
- Loan-sale asks B / NB / H ≈ 20 / 0 / 100 (expected: banks shedding arrears and capital-short books), each answered by
  the banks in reach (≈ 35) at 500 ns a quote (K-80) plus the asked rows' claim values (1 µs a loan) → ≈ 1 / 0 / 5
  core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 1 / 0 / 5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-45's asks, K-80's quotes)
- Counters: `sys_bnk.loan_sales`, `sys_bnk.quotes` by ask kind.

**Guards**: none new (PC-40).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a loan sold without a buyer who valued it; a quote from another lender's assessment.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, the SHAPE entries and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The placeholder declared naming BFL and BCP and its retiring steps S2.179 and S2.188.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.108 — Filing decisions and the registry's filed accounts

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: RAT.8 STATE
**Architecture**: §3.1 (company law's filed accounts in `if-firm`), §6 (stage 9b statements, 9d publications), §7.6
(K-37 record kinds), §7.12 (K-90)
**Depends on**: S1.333 (K-90 statements closed on each firm's own fiscal calendar), S1.216 (K-37 records "as published
by day d"), S1.486 (each firm's latest filed accounts at the opening), S1.227 (K-43 decision agenda), S1.348 (K-100)
**Goal**: every incorporated firm files its annual accounts for the fiscal year it chose with its country's companies
registry, on a day it chooses before the law's deadline; the registry publishes each filing, abbreviated as the law
declares, after its lag, as a public record lenders and suppliers read. Filings spread across the calendar because each
firm's year and its choice of day are its own.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-firm/src/filings.rs` | record kind `FiledAccounts` (headline lines of the K-90 annual statement as the law abbreviates them: assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, profit, staff, cash), audience public, publisher the registry; decision kind `FRM.file_accounts` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/file.rs` | `filing_day(ready, deadline, this_year, last_filed, review_days) -> Day` (pure) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the decision's schedule (occasions: the annual statement ready; each review day until filed); the record kind's horizon (RESOLUTION, never below the registry's POLICY floor, SET.13); the fine as a reason |
| `data/<country>/RAT.toml` | company law: filing duty by legal form, window after the fiscal year-end, abbreviation, the registry's publication lag, late-filing fine, the default accounting reference date (POLICY); preparation lead time and filing cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY); sources |
| `data/<country>/gen/RAT.toml` | the registry as a named institution per country (ENDOWMENT) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the filing-day form (Givoly and Palmon 1982) with its source |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_2_46.rs` | LC-2-46 |

**Design**:
- **The year**: each incorporated firm's fiscal year-end is a declared attribute of its legal form's company law — the
  one it chose at founding (FRM founding, S1.490), else the law's default (the founding month's anniversary). Its annual
  statement closes on that date (K-90, 9b); the statement is **ready** after the preparation lead time.
- **The decision** (`FRM.file_accounts`, lumpy, the firm's finance office): woken when the statement is ready and on
  each of its review days until it files. The form — bad news filed late — files at the first review after the statement
  is ready when this year's profit is at least last year's filed profit, and otherwise at the last review day before the
  deadline. Reviewing costs hours (§2.21).
- **Filing** (9d): the firm's `FiledAccounts` record is appended to K-37 with publication day = filing day + the
  registry's lag; before it no reader sees it (Law 12, STA.4). A firm that has not filed by the deadline incurs the
  law's fine (a flow to the registry's owner, the treasury) and a breach event (K-36); it files later still.
- **Readers**: S2.112 (sellers' terms), S2.110 (lenders' assessments, with bought records), the funding and covenant
  steps; every reader asks K-37 "as published by day d". The snapshot's latest filed accounts (S1.486) are public from
  the snapshot date, so every firm has one from day zero (E11).
- Unincorporated firms (FRM.23) declare no filing duty: no record, nothing read by default (E12).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a filing window where many fiscal years end on one date — decisions are woken by the K-43 agenda over only the
  firms whose statement is ready or whose review falls that day; the `-F` case `deadline_cluster`: 50 k firms deciding on one
  day at 1 µs each.
- E9: records kept for the filings' horizon (`horizon_filings_years`, RESOLUTION, never below the registry's POLICY
  floor): ≈ 0.46 M a year, each filer's latest annual statement kept however old; pruned by K-37's block
  (`latest_filing_kept_past_horizon`).
- E10: a firm ending before it files — no filing (its estate files none); its last record stays readable to its horizon,
  naming an ended party (K-31 tombstone) (`ended_firm_files_nothing`).
- E11: day zero — every firm's snapshot filing is public from the snapshot date (`snapshot_filing_public_day_zero`).
- E12: an unincorporated firm declares no duty: no record, nothing read by default (`no_duty_no_record`).

**Extension points**: `FiledAccounts` read by S2.110, S2.112, S2.118, S3.209 (listed companies' reports, RAT.2, extend
the same statement), S8.124 (board reviews woken by the published filing); the record kind's horizon is a RESOLUTION
valve (E 41).

**Unit tests**: `filing_day_rule` (good results early, bad results late, both within the window);
`late_filing_fined_once`; `not_readable_before_publication`; `latest_filing_kept_past_horizon`;
`ended_firm_files_nothing`; `snapshot_filing_public_day_zero`; `no_duty_no_record`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-46`: every incorporated firm filed within its window or its breach is recorded; filings per day are published
  and spread across the calendar.

**Budget**:
- `-F` cases: `deadline_cluster`.
- Filing decisions B / NB / H ≈ 1.8 k / 0 / 1.8 k (0.46 M a year over the business days) × 1 µs; appends 50 ns
  (S1.216's `published_ns`) → ≈ 2 / 0 / 2 core-ms.
- adds 1.8 k / 0 / 1.8 k items to fin.decide.attend_ns
- on fin.calendar.filing_window_end (the busiest filing day, 50 k firms at one deadline): 55 core-ms; joins H
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0 MB — inside S1.216's filings 44 MB (0.92 M statements × 48 B, encoded,
  at the two-year `horizon_filings_years`)
- Counters: `sys_frm.filings`, `sys_frm.late_filings`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a filing read before its publication day; a filing date drawn rather than chosen.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] LC-2-46 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.109 — The credit bureau's records and the credit-record stage

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.21 STATE *(part: lenders report; buying a record at S2.110)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 10d records, 9d publications), §7.6 (K-37), §7.9 (K-56 histories copied at close), §7.5
(K-32 attributes)
**Depends on**: S1.265 (K-56 transitions and their copy to records at close), S1.217 (K-37 records with audience and
publication day), S1.257 (K-53 opens and closes of reported families), S1.196 (K-32 declared attributes), S1.225 (K-42
dated entries), S1.165 (K-06 subject index)
**Goal**: a named credit bureau per country receives, as its country's credit-reporting law requires, each lender's
report of every borrower's reported contracts, payment events and defaults; its records keep for the law's horizon per
event; and each household's and firm's credit-record stage (REP.41) is the worst of its published records within their
horizons, moving when a report is published or a record expires.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/bureau.rs` | the adverse event kinds of S1.217's bureau ring (arrears, default, write-off, collection; later insolvency entry and discharge) with audience the bureau, later a lender who buys it (S2.110); the credit-record stage values; the reporting law's schema |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/bureau.rs` | `stage_of(events_within_horizon, day) -> CreditStage`; `publication_day(event_day, lender_calendar) -> Day` |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | the reported families (loans, credit lines, mortgages — data); the rule's slot at the bureau's publication (stage 9d) |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | credit-reporting law: what is reported, the reporting calendar (monthly), horizon per event kind, the bureau's fee (POLICY); sources |
| `data/<country>/gen/BNK.toml` | the bureau as a named institution per country; its opening records from the drawn contracts and drawn arrears states (ENDOWMENT, GEN.5) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_2_47.rs` | LC-2-47 |

**Design**:
- **What is reported**: for each reported family, each K-56 transition (arrears stage, default), each write-off and
  collection, and from S2.166 an insolvency entry and discharge — S1.217's adverse events (≈ 12 B each, encoded ring).
  Contracts and payments that are performing are not copied: the bureau's record of a borrower's contracts is its
  reported families' open contracts as of each lender's last reporting date, read through the contract store's party
  index at purchase (a contract opened after the lender's last report is excluded by its start day). This step declares
  the event kinds, their audience and their **publication day** = the lender's next reporting date (the law's monthly
  calendar, spread by lender phase), so an event reaches the bureau on the report, not on the event (Law 14).
- **Subjects**: a record names the borrower party (a person for a household's loan, the firm for a firm's); its
  household is read through the person (K-33).
- **The stage** (REP.41) is S1.217's per-borrower summary attribute (worst stage 4 bits, months in arrears, defaults,
  last event day): `stage_of` over the subject's events within horizon as of the day, written into the summary on each
  publication and re-derived at a purchase (S2.110) when an event has passed its horizon since, so no dated entry is
  kept. A borrower with no summary has no adverse event within the horizon — its stage is clean by the record, not by
  default. Nothing else writes it.
- **Horizons** per event kind (POLICY, never below the law's floor, SET.13); pruning is K-37's, and a summary whose last
  event passed the horizon is pruned with it.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day adds up to 1.7 M transitions; their records publish on each lender's next reporting date,
  spread over the month (`mass_day_spread_by_reporting`).
- E6: the summaries and the event ring are saved; the subject index is rebuilt (`subject_index_rebuilt`).
- E9: ≈ 1.6 k adverse events a business day (derived: ≈ 1.5 k transitions, write-offs and collections), ≈ 0.7 M within
  the retention horizon (`bureau_events`), ≈ 0.5 M summaries (`bureau_borrowers`); flat after the horizon
  (`bureau_flat_after_horizon`).
- E10: a subject that ended — its events stay to their horizon, naming the ended party (K-31)
  (`ended_subject_events_kept`).
- E11: day zero — the opening's events (drawn arrears states) are published on the snapshot date and the summaries set
  from them (`opening_events_published_day_zero`).

**Extension points**: S2.110 (buying), S2.166, S2.168 (insolvency entries and discharge).

**Unit tests**: `record_stage_moves_with_reports`; `stage_clock_expires_at_horizon`; `mass_day_spread_by_reporting`;
`subject_index_rebuilt`; `bureau_flat_after_horizon`; `ended_subject_events_kept`; `opening_events_published_day_zero`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-47`: every household's and firm's credit-record stage matches its published records within their horizons, and
  every record ends at its horizon.

**Budget**:
- Events published B / NB / H ≈ 1.6 k / 0 / 10 k × 50 ns (append) plus the subject's summary rewritten (300 ns) → ≈ 0.6
  / 0 / 4 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.observer: 0.6 / 0 / 4 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.mass_default (event): 0 core-ms; joins H and B′
- spread after fin.calendar.mass_default over 21 days: 1 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.observer (the events publish on the
  lenders' next reporting dates, spread by lender phase)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0 MB — inside S1.217's `bureau_mb` 14 (0.5 M summaries × 12 B + 0.7 M
  events × 12 B, at BNK.21's POLICY floor); +0 B (core attribute: the stage is the summary's, S1.217)
- Counters: `sys_bnk.bureau_records`, `sys_bnk.stage_changes`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a credit score that is not a record; a record past its horizon; a stage written by any rule but
`stage_of`.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] LC-2-47 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.110 — Bought records read by lenders' assessments

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.21 STATE
**Architecture**: §3.1 (writer tokens: `BoughtRecord`), §6 (stage 5c)
**Depends on**: S2.109 (the bureau's records and stages), S2.108 (filed accounts), S1.425 (the lending round and its
assessment, which reads only what the borrower discloses and the lender's own lines), S1.248 (K-49 settles the fee)
**Goal**: a lender to whom a borrower applies buys that borrower's record from the bureau, paying its fee; its
assessment reads the record it bought, the applicant's filed accounts and its own lines — never another lender's data by
any other path. A seller weighing trade credit may buy a record the same way.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/bureau.rs` | `BoughtRecord` — constructible only by the purchase (PC-43): the subject's credit stage and its published records as of the purchase day |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/assess.rs` | extended: the class reads the bought stage and other lenders' reported events, and the filed ratios in steps |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | reason `BNK.record_fee` (applicant's lender → bureau); the purchase in the lending round's 5c answer |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_2_21.rs` | LC-2-21 |

**Design**:
- **The purchase**: when a lender answers an application (S1.425's round at 5c) it buys the applicant's record: a K-37
  query "as published by day d" over the subject index, returned as a `BoughtRecord`, and a fee flow to the bureau
  settled at 7 (Law 14). The assessment's class then counts the stage and other lenders' arrears and defaults.
- **Filed accounts**: a firm applicant's latest `FiledAccounts` (S2.108), public, read by every lender without a fee.
- **Extends** S1.425's assessment, which read only what the applicant discloses and the lender's own lines, with the
  record bought: its adverse events and summary (S2.109), and its open reported contracts as of each lender's last
  reporting date.
- **Sellers** (S2.112) may buy on the same terms; PC-43 does not distinguish buyers, only the path.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: an applicant with no record — the bought record is empty, a fact the class reads as "no history", not as clean or
  bad (`empty_record_is_no_history`).
- E6: nothing is kept after the decision (a record is bought per application; SET.16: the class it produced is written
  in the loan's terms) (`bought_record_not_kept`).
- E11: day zero — the opening's records are published on the snapshot date, so applications on day one can buy them
  (`day_one_application_buys_opening_record`).

**Extension points**: S2.112 (terms), S3.201's non-bank lenders (same purchase, data).

**Unit tests**: `bought_record_only_by_purchase` (compile-fail, PC-43); `empty_record_is_no_history`;
`class_counts_other_lenders_defaults`; `bought_record_not_kept`; `day_one_application_buys_opening_record`;
`performing_contracts_read_as_of_last_report`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-21`: Law 12 — lenders' assessments read only their own lines, records they bought and public filings (the
  read-trace).

**Budget**:
- Purchases = applications answered: B / NB / H ≈ 40 k / 0 / 40 k (≈ 10 k asks × ≈ 4 responders, K-80's `-F`) × 100 ns
  (K-37's as-published query) plus the fee item → ≈ 5 / 0 / 5 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 5 / 0 / 5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (nothing kept: the class is written in the loan's terms)
- Counter: `sys_bnk.records_bought`.

**Guards**: PC-43 — another lender's reported data reaches an assessment only through `BoughtRecord` (compile level).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; one assessment shared by lenders; a record read without its fee.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] PC-43 registered; LC-2-21 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.

### S2.111 — Invoices on terms

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TCR.1 STATE; TCR.5 INVARIANT; TCR.8 PRIMITIVE; FRM.18 INVARIANT; ACC.1 STATE
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`if-credit` trade credit), §6 (stage 6b accruals, 7a dues), §7.9 (the `invoices` and
`statements` families, K-59, K-54 side sums), §7.11 (K-74 sales on account), §7.17 (K-103 families)
**Depends on**: S1.269 (K-59: the `invoices` pair row, `statements`, `open_pair`, `accrue`, `carve`), S1.171 (K-14 the
statements sweep), S1.257 (K-53 families and side lists), S1.265 (K-56 status and the day's transitions), S1.261 (K-54
receivable and payable sums), S1.309 (K-74's declared "on account" sale mode sending the amount to `accrue`), S1.353
(K-103), S1.444 (input orders: the between-firm purchases)
**Goal**: a sale between firms in a trade that bills on terms accrues on the seller's invoice to that buyer for the
statement period — the seller's receivable and the buyer's payable, one record naming both — due at the period's end
plus the term; a trade billing per invoice has one invoice per sale. Revenue is recognised on delivery and every unpaid
amount is a receivable with a named counterparty, so the accrual basis is complete.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/invoices.rs` | the grant's terms (statement period, term point, discount point and days, limit per period) as the `invoices` row's `terms`; the trades' customary terms (TCR.8) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/invoice.rs` | `covers(row, amount, day) -> bool` (the open statement's accrual + amount ≤ the period's limit) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | the "on account" mode for the between-firm markets whose trade declares terms (K-74); audit families `TCR.receivables_payables` and `FRM.receivables`; the grant placeholder |
| `data/<country>/TCR.toml` | TCR.8: per trade, the statement period, customary term and discount points (POLICY of the trade), from `state/typed_late_payment_terms` (default and maximum periods between undertakings) and `state/enterprise_surveys` (share of sales on credit), with sources |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/derive/billing.rs` | the declared procedure for each trade's billing mode (below), run at the opening |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the billing-mode procedure with what it loses |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_2_04.rs`, `lc_2_26.rs` | LC-2-04, LC-2-26 |

**Design**:
- **The record** (S1.269's layout): one `invoices` row per (seller, buyer) pair on terms — `terms` (the grant),
  `open`/`open_period` (the open statement's accrual), `closed`/`closed_period` (the one closed statement awaiting its
  due), the payment record `paid`, `fails`, `late_days`. Beyond those two, a statement is a standalone `statements` row
  (payer, payee, terms, `own_due`, `own_amount`, `pair`) — a second closed statement, an overdue one, a carved one, or
  each sale of a per-invoice trade; its due is taken from the wheel on its own row and updates its pair's payment record
  through `pair`. A rule that needs a pair's standalone statements (a terms review of an overdue buyer, factoring, the
  buyer's end) marks the pair; one declared sweep a day over the `statements` family's `pair` column (K-14, ≈ 0.5 M rows
  × 1 ns) hands each marked pair its statements. Each statement — inline or standalone — is the invoice of its period
  (TCR.1): its own amount, due day (period end + term) and arrears.

- **On account** (6b, the seller's pairs): in K-74's seller-shard sweep each seller's pair rows are sorted by buyer in
  the range job's scratch and binary-searched for each between-firm sale item; a hit whose `covers` holds books the sale
  on account — `accrue(pair, amount, day)` (which rolls open → closed at a new period and carves any occupant of closed)
  in place of the money leg; goods deliver at 7d as for a paid sale (SET.4: the accrual is the sale's other leg). A miss
  or a sale past the limit pays at settlement. A retail market declares no terms (TCR.7: no sale settles instantly by
  construction where the trade gives terms).
- **Per-invoice trades inside the pair row**: a per-invoice trade's statement period is one sale day (the day's sales on
  account to one buyer share their due, so they are one invoice). The pair row holds the open and the one closed
  invoice; a sale while the closed one is still unpaid rolls open → closed and carves the occupant into a `statements`
  row — so a standalone row exists only for a third unpaid invoice of one pair.
- **Billing mode** (TCR.8): no source in `data/sources/raw/` says which trades bill per invoice. It is derived at the
  opening by a declared procedure: a trade bills by statement where its buyers' expected purchases from one seller
  within the customary term exceed one (from the opening's input-order cycles, S1.444), per invoice otherwise —
  statement billing is how recurring deliveries are consolidated. SHAPES.toml records what it loses: a trade's own
  convention where it differs.
- **Grants**: a pair opens only by the seller's decision (`open_pair`, TCR.2). Until S2.112 that decision is a SHAPE
  placeholder naming TCR — a seller grants the trade's customary terms, with no limit, to each buyer at its first cash
  purchase — retired at S2.112.
- **Dues**: the due of period p is filed on the wheel at p's first accrual; at 7a it is streamed like any due, its
  amount read from wherever p sits; paid → the payment record moves; failed → K-56 arrears (S2.114's notices).
- **Books** (ACC.1): revenue and cost of sales on delivery (K-74, K-87); receivables and payables are the statements'
  amounts on the two sides, summed per party by K-54.
- **Audit**: `TCR.receivables_payables` (TCR.5) — per statement both sides read one amount by construction, and per
  currency Σ receivables = Σ payables recounted from the rows; `FRM.receivables` (FRM.18) — each touched party's K-54
  receivable and payable sums equal the Σ of its statements, recounted (and a rolling slice).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a month-end with every statement due — ≈ 4.5 M invoice dues streamed and ≈ 2 M statements closed
  (`month_end_close_streams_dues`).
- E6: rows and standalone statements saved; the seller's sorted pairs are the range job's scratch, rebuilt each day
  (nothing to save) (`pairs_round_trip`).
- E8: a per-invoice trade carves a standalone row only for a pair's third unpaid invoice; by the billing procedure a
  per-invoice pair expects under one purchase a term, so live standalone rows stay within S1.257's `statements` count
  (`statements_capacity`, `per_invoice_carves_only_third_unpaid`).
- E10: a buyer or seller ending — its sides move to its estate (K-97); the statements become claims (S2.114)
  (`ending_moves_pair_sides`).
- E14: two purchases of one pair the same day accrue on one open statement (commute) (`same_day_accruals_commute`).

**Extension points**: S2.112 (grants and the record), S2.113 (payables' discounts), S2.114 (overdue), S2.115 (`carve`
and factoring), S2.120 (time requests); S5.106 (value-added tax at the statement).

**Unit tests**: `invoice_row_replaces_money_leg` (a sale on account, and past its limit); `accrual_rolls_period` (open →
closed, occupant carved); `per_invoice_carves_only_third_unpaid`; `receivables_equal_payables_recount`;
`billing_mode_by_purchases_per_term`; `statements_capacity` (the bench's live standalone rows against
`[fin.contracts.statements]`); `month_end_close_streams_dues`; `pairs_round_trip`; `ending_moves_pair_sides`;
`same_day_accruals_commute`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-04`: TCR.5 and FRM.18 — both audit families are clean every close.
- `LC-2-26`: TCR.7 — every statement's due day is after its sale days; no receivable names an ended debtor except as a
  claim on its estate.

**Budget**:
- Sales on account B / NB / H 3.3 M / 0 / 3.3 M: the accrual replaces the sale's money leg inside S1.269's unit.
- adds 0 phone-ns to fin.b2b.all_in_ns at 3.3 M / 0 / 3.3 M items
- Statement dues 0.2 M / 0 / 4.5 M, inside the design point's dues (3.0 M / 0 / 22.5 M, whose H counts the month-end's
  4.5 M invoice dues, S1.269).
- adds 0 / 0 / 0 items to fin.dues.item_ns
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.5 / 0 / 0.5 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the declared statements sweep, 0.5 M rows × 1 ns)
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 MB — inside S1.269's `invoices` 253 MB (5 M pairs × 50.7 B) and `statements` 14 MB (0.5
  M live × 28 B)
- Counters: `sys_tcr.pairs_open`, `sys_tcr.on_account_sales`, `sys_tcr.standalone_statements`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a statement per purchase in a trade that bills by statement; a receivable without its payable; a
pair opened by anything but the seller's decision.

**Done when**:

  the injected breaks.
- [ ] LC-2-04, LC-2-26 registered; the grant placeholder declared naming S2.112.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.112 — A seller's terms per buyer

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TCR.2 DECISION *(part: the grant per buyer on review, overdue and a cash purchase; the time request at
S2.120)*
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`if-credit` decision points), §6 (stage 5c), §7.16 (K-100, K-101)
**Depends on**: S2.111 (the `invoices` pair rows and their payment record), S1.269 (`open_pair`), S2.108 (filed
accounts), S2.110 (a record bought), S1.350 (K-101 attention), S1.348 (K-100), S1.425 (the seller's own bank quote as
its cost of funds)
**Goal**: a seller decides per buyer whether to give terms, how long and up to what limit, from what it has seen of that
buyer — its payments on this seller's invoices, its filed accounts and, if the seller buys one, its bureau record — and
from its own cash and cost of funds; it tightens when worried. The grant is the pair row's `terms`; a new pair opens by
this decision (`open_pair`).

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/decisions.rs` | decision `TCR.grant_terms` (the seller's; lumpy) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/terms.rs` | `grant(record, filed, bought, own_cash_outlook, cost_of_funds, margin, grid) -> Grant { term, discount, limit }` |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | review schedule and attention stake (K-101) on the `grant_terms` slot; occasion: a buyer's cash purchase with no pair (the seller's sales shard notes it) |
| `data/<country>/TCR.toml` | review schedule and cost in hours (PREFERENCE, TECHNOLOGY), each management's memory for dormant accounts (PREFERENCE) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the terms form (Petersen and Rajan 1997; Wilner 2000) with its source |

**Design**:
- **The record** (SET.16): the pair row's `paid`, `fails` and `late_days`, written by settlement's outcome on each
  statement's due (S1.265) — the seller's own experience of the buyer, state in the row since the pair opened.
- **When**: the seller's terms review by attention (K-101: a stake per seller, woken by a surprise such as an overdue),
  and on an occasion: a buyer without a pair buying for cash (an overdue, S2.114, and a buyer's time request, S2.120,
  are added as occasions by the steps that create those messages). One review visits the seller's pairs (the seller-side
  block list of `invoices`).
- **Grant**, per pair: the buyer's expected loss = the seller's own loss outlook for buyers like it (an adaptive outlook
  per class, VAL.6), the class read from its record on this seller's invoices and the buyer's latest filed ratios
  (S2.108) and, when bought, its bureau stage (S2.110); the term is the longest point of the trade's grid whose cost —
  the receivable financed at the seller's marginal rate plus that expected loss — is below the margin it expects on the
  sales terms bring; the limit is the purchases it expects over that term within its own cash buffer target; both fall —
  shorter term, lower limit, or none — as its cash outlook worsens or the class's losses rise.
- **New pairs**: a buyer buying for cash with no pair is an occasion; the grant decides whether to `open_pair` for it.
- **Dormant pairs** with no statement open or unpaid and no purchase within the management's memory are closed by the
  review (E9).
- **Retires** S2.111's placeholder (customary terms, no limit, at a first cash purchase).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a buyer with no filed accounts (unincorporated) and no record — the class reads "no history" (declared), never a
  default grade (`no_history_class`).
- E6: the record is on the row (saved); nothing kept elsewhere (`record_on_pair_round_trip`).
- E11: day zero — the opening's pairs carry the trade's customary terms (GEN.5 snapshot of contracts); the first review
  decides (`opening_pairs_customary_until_review`).
- E14: an overdue and a time request of one buyer the same day — one review of the pair (`one_review_per_pair_per_day`).

**Extension points**: S2.114 adds the "overdue" occasion and S2.120 the "time request" occasion of `TCR.grant_terms`
(the buyer's disclosed cash outlook, S2.121).

**Unit tests**: `terms_tighten_with_record_and_cash`; `terms_on_trade_grid`; `no_history_class`;
`dormant_pair_closed_after_memory`; `cash_buyer_occasion_opens_pair`; `record_on_pair_round_trip`;
`opening_pairs_customary_until_review`; `one_review_per_pair_per_day`.

**Live checks**: none (LC-2-05 at S2.128 reads the terms' course).

**Budget**:
- Seller reviews B / NB / H 46 k / 0 / 46 k (1.15 M sellers at a monthly mean; the rate is attention's), each over its
  pairs (≈ 5 M pairs a month → 240 k a day) at 60 ns a pair (the record read and three comparisons on the row) → 14 / 0
  / 14 core-ms.
- adds 300 phone-ns to fin.decide.attend_ns at 46 k / 0 / 46 k items (the reviews themselves are among the 246 k
  attention decisions)
- +0 B (named slot `grant_terms`, S1.227)
- Counters: `sys_tcr.terms_reviews`, `sys_tcr.grants_tightened`, `sys_tcr.pairs_closed`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; terms as a share of sales or a fixed days-payable; a seller reading a buyer's private accounts.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass; S2.111's placeholder removed.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.113 — Paying early for the discount

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TCR.3 DECISION *(part: the buyer's choice; factoring at S2.115)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5b on the firm's visit, 7a decided flows)
**Depends on**: S2.111 (invoices with discount terms and the buyer's payables list), S1.228 (the firm's schedule visit),
S1.348 (K-100), S1.248 (K-49 decided flows)
**Goal**: a buyer holding an invoice whose discount window is open pays early when the discount's implied annual rate
beats its own marginal cost of funds; otherwise it uses the credit to the due date.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/pay_or_discount.rs` | `implied_rate(d, term, discount_days)`, `pay_early(rate, cost_of_funds) -> bool` |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | decision `TCR.pay_or_discount` (continuous, on the buyer firm's visit); reason `TCR.early_payment` (buyer → seller, the balance less the discount; closes the invoice, SET.4) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | cost of forgone discount (Ng, Smith and Smith 1999) with its source |

**Design**:
- On the buyer's schedule visit (S1.228), for each of its pairs whose discount window is open (the buyer side's lazy
  block list, S1.269): `implied = (d ÷ (1 − d)) × (days in year ÷ (term − discount days))`; the buyer's marginal cost of
  funds is its deposit rate when it has cash beyond its buffer target, else its credit line's rate (S2.117) or its last
  loan quote.
- Paying early is a decided flow at 7 (the 0.45 M "decided flows" line) linked with the invoice's close; the seller's
  revenue line takes the discount as a price reduction on the day (ACC.1).
- A buyer short of cash pays nothing early — no rule forbids it; the cash test is settlement's.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a buyer with no spare cash — its cost of funds is its line's rate, possibly `Missing` with no line and no quote;
  then no early payment (`missing_cost_no_early_payment`).
- E14: early payment and the period's close the same day — the close applies to what remains, zero
  (`early_payment_then_close_zero`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `discount_vs_cost_of_funds` (2/10 net 30 against rates above and below it);
`missing_cost_no_early_payment`; `early_payment_then_close_zero`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Discount comparisons B / NB / H 1 M / 0 / 1 M (246 k visits × ≈ 4 payables) at 10 ns → 10 / 0 / 10 core-ms.
- adds 40 phone-ns to fin.decide.visit_ns at 246 k / 0 / 246 k items
- Early payments B / NB / H 50 k / 0 / 50 k decided flows.
- adds 50 k / 0 / 50 k items to fin.dues.item_ns
- +0 B (core attribute: the pair row's terms)
- Counter: `sys_tcr.discounts_taken`.
**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a days-payable target.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.114 — Overdue invoices and losses on named sellers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TCR.4 PROCESS; TCR.7 FORBID
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 2d, 2f), §7.15 (K-98 claims)
**Depends on**: S2.111 (invoices), S2.112 (the seller's review woken), S1.265 (K-56 transitions), S1.237 (K-45), S1.344
(endings move payables to the estate), S1.346 (the waterfall pays ordinary claims), S1.332 (K-89 write-downs)
**Goal**: an invoice unpaid at its due is a real overdue state that leaves the seller's cash short by what did not
arrive; the buyer receives a collection notice and the seller's terms review is woken. When a buyer ends, its invoices
become unsecured claims in its estate, and whatever the estate does not pay is each named seller's recorded loss — no
receivable survives its debtor.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/invoices.rs` | message `CollectionNotice` (seller → buyer: invoice, overdue, days) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/overdue.rs` | `notice_for(transition)`; `loss_on_close(balance, paid) -> Money` |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | slot 2d (after K-56); the "overdue" occasion of `TCR.grant_terms` (S2.112); the `invoices`/`statements` claim class in the waterfall (ordinary unsecured, the law's, K-98); the close-with-loss at the estate's final distribution |

**Design**:
- **Overdue** (2d): each K-56 transition on an `invoices` or `statements` row posts a `CollectionNotice` to the buyer —
  a need occasion for its distress (S2.121) — and wakes the seller's terms review (K-43, once per seller a day). Nothing
  tops up the seller: the cash did not arrive, and its own dues fail if it cannot pay them (SET.3).
- **Default** (TCR.4): a buyer that ends passes its payable sides to its estate (K-97); each unpaid statement is a claim
  of the law's ordinary unsecured class (K-98). At the estate's distributions each seller is paid its share (K-16
  largest remainder; the residue to the law's named party).
- **Loss** (TCR.7): when the estate's final distribution settles, each pair and statement closes; the unpaid amount is
  written off the seller's receivable (K-89, ACC.7) as a loss line (K-87) and an event naming seller, buyer's estate and
  amount (K-36, L1) — the loss that can push the seller into distress (S2.121, S2.122). No invoice survives its debtor.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: 10 % of firms ending on one day — their payables move at their endings (K-97, 15 ns a row); notices are not sent
  to estates (no distress rule); losses land over the estates' distribution days, never in one pass
  (`losses_land_on_distribution_days`).
- E4: an estate that never distributes — its invoices stay claims, the sellers' receivables stand (impaired only by
  their own write-down tests, S2.116), counted (`undistributed_estate_claims_stand`).
- E10: a seller ending with receivables — its seller sides move to its estate, which collects (S2.133)
  (`ended_seller_estate_collects`).
- E14: an overdue and a payment on one invoice the same day — K-56's order (payment settles first at 7; the next 2d sees
  none) (`payment_before_overdue_same_day`).

**Extension points**: the loss event is read by S2.128 (chains of distress).

**Unit tests**: `notice_on_overdue`; `losses_sum_to_shortfall` (over given claims and a distribution, each seller's loss
is its unpaid share); `no_invoice_after_estate_end`; `losses_land_on_distribution_days`;
`undistributed_estate_claims_stand`; `ended_seller_estate_collects`; `payment_before_overdue_same_day`;
`overdue_wakes_terms_review`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-26` (S2.111) reads this step's closes; no new check.

**Budget**:
- Overdue notices B / NB / H 5 k / 0 / 50 k (H the month-end's failed statements) at 60 ns → 0.3 / 0 / 3 core-ms; losses
  on estate distributions 25 k / 0 / 25 k claims a day (≈ 30 claims an estate) at 100 ns → 2.5 / 0 / 2.5 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 2.8 / 0 / 5.5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.mass_default (event): 8 core-ms; joins H and B′ (10 % of firms' payables, 0.5 M pair sides moved to
  their estates at 15 ns: Law 1 on the day; the losses spread over the distribution days, in the line above)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-56's status on the pair row)
- Counters: `sys_tcr.overdue`, `sys_tcr.losses`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a receivable surviving its debtor; a loss drawn or paired by lot (every claim names its seller).

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.115 — Factoring closed invoices

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TCR.3 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c, 7), §7.11 (K-80), §7.9 (K-57)
**Depends on**: S2.111 (invoices), S1.269 (K-59 `carve`), S2.107 (`quote_loans`), S1.317 (K-80), S1.267 (K-57
`move_end`), S1.348 (K-100)
**Goal**: a seller short of cash may sell its receivables of closed statement periods to a bank: it asks the banks it
can reach, each quotes by its own assessment of the buyers, and the seller takes the best quote above its own value of
waiting. The buyer then owes the bank.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/invoices.rs` | message `FactoringAsk` (closed statements offered, with their buyers' payment records on the seller's pair rows) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/factor.rs` | `value_of_waiting(expected_collections, own_cost_of_funds)`; `accept(quotes, value) -> Option<Quote>` |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | decision `TCR.factor` (the seller's; lumpy; occasion: its cash outlook short of its buffer, raised at its visit); stream `TCR.factor_lot`; reason `TCR.factoring` (link group: seller sides moved + price) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | a request for quotes against the seller's own value of waiting (Klapper 2006) |

**Design**:
- **Ask** (5c): only **closed** statements (so nothing accrues onto a sold one); to the banks in the seller's reach
  (K-80).
- **Quote**: each bank answers at its next 5c by `quote_loans` (S2.107) — its claim value of the invoices under its own
  assessment of each buyer's class (BNK.15, PC-40) less its required return on the capital — or declines.
- **Accept**: the best quote at or above the value of waiting (expected collections discounted at the seller's marginal
  cost of funds); ties by lot (`TCR.factor_lot`). At 7 each sold statement is carved into its own `statements` row
  (`carve(pair, period)`, K-59) and its payee moved to the bank (`move_end`, K-57), linked with the price bank → seller
  in one group (SET.4). The buyer pays that statement's due to the bank; its pair's record counts only what the seller
  still holds.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no quote above the value — no sale, a failed meeting (MKT.10) (`no_factoring_below_value`).
- E6: open asks saved in K-45/K-80 (`open_factoring_ask_round_trip`).
- E10: a buyer ending between ask and accept — the claim moves with the side (`factored_claim_moves_with_side`).

**Extension points**: S3.199 (non-bank lenders answer factoring asks through `quote_loans`).

**Unit tests**: `factoring_offers_closed_periods_only`; `accept_best_above_value_of_waiting`;
`open_factoring_ask_round_trip`; `no_factoring_below_value`; `factored_claim_moves_with_side`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Factoring asks B / NB / H 250 / 0 / 500 (expected: sellers short of cash; H the month's end), each quoted by the banks
  in reach (≈ 35) at 500 ns a quote plus the invoices' claim values → 20 µs an ask → 5 / 0 / 10 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 5 / 0 / 10 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-45's asks, K-57's moved sides)
- Counters: `sys_tcr.factoring_asks`, `sys_tcr.factored`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an open period's invoice sold; a factoring price not quoted by a buyer.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.116 — Write-downs of inventory and plant

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ACC.7 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9b statements), §7.12 (K-89 carrying values, K-90 statements)
**Depends on**: S1.332 (K-89 carrying values, write-downs refused above cost, unrealised reads), S1.333 (K-90 statements
on each party's own calendar), S1.326 (K-86 marks), S1.285 (K-67 plant by class), S2.102 (loan provisions, ACC.7's first
part)
**Goal**: when each of its statements is prepared a firm tests its inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable
value and, on an indication of impairment, its plant against what the plant is worth to it; a shortfall is written down
as a charge to income on the day, and a later recovery reverses it only up to the original cost. With loans' provisions
(S2.102), every write-down ACC.7 names exists.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/writedown.rs` | `nrv(mark, cost_to_sell) -> Money`; `impairment_indicated(period)`; `plant_recoverable(view) -> Money` (VAL.8 plant value) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the tests on the statement-ready occasion (the K-42 dated entry after the preparation lead time, S2.108); lines "write-down" and "reversal" (K-87) |
| `data/<country>/ACC.toml` | the accounting standard's impairment indicators and cost-to-sell rule (POLICY, ACC.17) with sources |

**Design**:
- **Inventory** (ACC.2's lower of cost and NRV), when each statement is prepared (its preparation lead time after the
  close; recognised that day, ACC.7): for each inventory holding, NRV = units × the latest mark of its market (K-86;
  MKT.12's posted-price mark: the day's revenue ÷ units) less the cost to sell; below the carrying value → a write-down
  to NRV (K-89); above a written-down value → a reversal up to cost. A holding whose market has no mark keeps its
  carrying value, and the absence is shown (E2, E12).
- **Plant** (cost less depreciation and impairment): at the annual statement, only where the standard's indicators hold
  (an operating loss, a fall in the product's mark, idle capacity), the recoverable amount is the firm's own value of
  the plant (VAL.8: expected output at expected prices less running costs over its remaining life, discounted at its
  marginal cost of money); below carrying → write-down.
- Every move is an income line of its day (K-87) moving equity (K-88); none is a flow. Households keep no accounts and
  are not tested.

**Edge cases**:
- E2/E12: no mark: no test, `no_mark_no_writedown`.
- E5: a quarter-end: the tests come at each statement's preparation, spread over the following weeks, none on the
  close's H day (`tests_spread_after_close`).
- E11: the opening's carrying values are GEN.5's; the first test at the first close
  (`opening_carrying_values_until_first_close`).

**Extension points**: S2.130 (plant review) reads written-down carrying values; S2.133 (estate inventories) reads NRV.

**Unit tests**: `writedown_to_nrv_and_reversal_refused_above_cost`; `impairment_only_on_indication`;
`no_mark_no_writedown`. Edge cases: `tests_spread_after_close`; `opening_carrying_values_until_first_close`.

**Live checks**: `LC-2-25` (S2.102) covers every write-down and its refusal above cost.

**Budget**:
- Inventory tests at statements' preparation B / NB / H 150 k / 0 / 150 k reads (1.15 M firms × 4 statements a year × ≈
  8 holdings) at 10 ns → 1.5 / 0 / 1.5 core-ms; plant tests on indication at the annual statement 5 k / 0 / 5 k at 1 µs
  → 5 / 0 / 5 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 6.5 / 0 / 6.5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.statement_preparation (the business days after a quarter's close, 1.5 M reads): 15 core-ms; joins B′
  (a lead time after a close can land on the first business day after four closed days)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-63's holdings, K-89's carrying values)
- Counters: `sys_frm.writedowns`, `sys_frm.reversals`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a reversal above cost; a write-down without a mark or a value it read.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.117 — Credit lines drawn, repaid and cut

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.18 STATE; BNK.2 STATE *(part: facilities drawn and repaid, the undrawn part a commitment both books
read; its capital and liquidity at S2.186)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c decisions, 7 settlement, 7a charging dates, 7c limit cuts), §7.8 (K-47's `facility`,
`accrual` and `statement` slots)
**Depends on**: S1.240 (K-47 account facilities: `limit`, `terms`, accrual slots, `set_limit`), S1.243 (the bank's
maintained Σ limit and Σ drawn), S1.263 (K-55 the facility's interned terms), S1.248 (K-49: draws and repayments are
payments; a payment beyond −limit fails), S1.265 (K-56 arrears on an account), S1.425 (the lending round writes
facilities)
**Goal**: a revolving facility or credit line — a firm's line, a household's credit card or overdraft — is a facility on
the borrower's account with its bank: drawn and repaid at the borrower's choice up to its limit, its undrawn part a
commitment both books read, charged interest on what is drawn and a fee on the limit; the lender may cut the undrawn
limit where the contract allows, which is how credit tightens for borrowers who already have lines.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/lines.rs` | the facility's terms per product (debit rate fixed or a margin over a reference, commitment-fee rate, `committed`/`cancellable`, charging dates; for a card the statement schedule and minimum-payment rule) as K-55 terms; message `LimitCut` |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/lines.rs` | `cut_to(limit, drawn, standards, terms) -> Option<Money>` (a new limit ≥ drawn, only where the terms allow) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/declare.rs` | the facility products (data); the lender's line review on its K-43 schedule; the charging date per (bank, product) on K-42 |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | customary facility terms per product (POLICY of the trade): fee points, cancellation clauses, card minimum payments, with sources |

**Design**:
- **The facility** (S1.240's layout): the account's `facility` slot holds `limit` and `terms`; drawn is a read,
  `max(−balance, 0)`, and undrawn = limit − drawn (Law 4) — the commitment both books read (REG.10), folded into the
  bank's maintained totals (S1.243). A firm's revolving facility is the same facility on its account (BNK.18).
- **Draws and repayments** are ordinary payments settled at 7 (K-49's apply only): a payment that takes the balance
  below −limit fails (MON.3, MON.12). Who draws is the borrower's own decision — a firm's funding (S2.118) and distress
  (S2.121), a household's borrowing (S2.144); an overdraft is simply a payment the facility covers.
- **Charges**: on each product's charging date (a K-42 due per (bank, product)) the 7a sweep charges each facility
  account: interest on drawn and the fee on limit from the accrual slots (round(B × J + s)); a charge that would breach
  the limit fails and is recorded as arrears on the account (K-56), which S2.101 notifies. A card's minimum payment is a
  dated item from its `statement` slot, paid on its due from the holder's paying account.
- **Cuts** (the lender's decision, on its line review — its standards moved, S2.189; its assessment of the borrower
  worsened, S2.102): a cancellable facility's limit is cut to `cut_to` (never below drawn — a limit below drawn stops
  the run, BNK.18: only the undrawn part is cut), applied by `set_limit` at 7c; a `LimitCut` notice is a need occasion
  for the borrower. A committed facility's terms forbid the cut before its term.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a household with no facility: a payment beyond its balance fails as before (`no_facility_payment_fails`).
- E5: a payday: payments covered by facilities are settlement's own path, fused (`payday_facility_path_fused`).
- E8: a facility's accrual in i128 slots, S1.240 (`facility_accrual_i128`).
- E10: a lender in resolution: the accounts move with its book, K-57 (`facility_moves_with_book`).
- E14: a draw and a repayment the same day net in settlement (`draw_and_repay_net`).

**Extension points**: S2.118, S2.121, S2.144 decide draws; S2.189's standards feed cuts; S3.112's CB standing facilities
are another product (data).

**Unit tests**: `cut_never_below_drawn`; `cut_only_where_cancellable`; `charge_breaching_limit_is_arrears`. Edge cases:
`no_facility_payment_fails`; `payday_facility_path_fused`; `facility_accrual_i128`; `facility_moves_with_book`;
`draw_and_repay_net`.

**Live checks**: none (REG.10's reads are the core's).

**Budget**:
- Draws and repayments are payments inside settlement's own units (0 added). The facility accounts at the design
  point, from the data in hand: households' cards and overdrafts 1.52 M (`[store] households` 2.21 M × 45.8 %, the
  weighted share of SCF 2019 households carrying a card balance or another line, `CCBAL` or `OTHLOC` > 0, × the
  per-person margin 1.5) and firms' lines 0.45 M (the borrowers of `BNK.firm_loan`'s 0.45 M rows, no source in hand
  giving firms' lines apart) — 1.97 M. Charging dates stream them: ≈ 2 M a month, spread by product date.
- adds 150 k / 0 / 150 k items to fin.dues.item_ns
- Line cuts on the banks' reviews B / NB / H 5 k / 0 / 5 k at 200 ns.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the line cuts)
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +0 B (inside S1.241's figure: 1.97 M `Facility` slots, their `Accrual`
  slots — two for a rate at a margin over a reference, one more for a firm's commitment fee — and the cards'
  `Statement` slots)
- Counters: `sys_bnk.line_cuts`, `sys_bnk.facility_charges_failed`.
**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a drawn amount stored beside the balance; a cut below drawn or on a committed facility.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
