### S2.118 — A firm's funding decision

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.9 DECISION *(part: retained cash, trade credit, credit lines and bank loans; bonds, paper and shares at
S3.153)*
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`if-credit` decision points), §6 (stage 5c)
**Depends on**: S2.117 (lines), S2.113 (the implied rate of a discount forgone), S1.425 (loan applications and quotes),
S1.426 (a firm's rate for new debt as its own position), S1.427 (its shortfall placeholder), S1.453 (the firm's cash
outlook), S1.350 (K-101 attention)
**Goal**: a firm funds itself from the cheapest source it can reach, taking sources in order of what each costs it now
until its need is met or the next would carry its debt past the leverage its management tolerates. It replaces the Stage
1 placeholder by which a firm borrowed its day's shortfall from its own bank.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/decisions.rs` | decision `FRM.finance` (the firm's finance office; lumpy) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/finance.rs` | `need(outlook, dues, planned_investment, cash, buffer)`; `plan(sources: &[Source], need, debt, tolerance) -> FundingPlan` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the sources as declared data (retained cash, trade credit, undrawn line, new loan — each with its cost read); the `finance` slot (S1.227): the financing review (attention) and a shortfall in the cash outlook as its occasion |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | leverage tolerance (`FRM.leverage_tolerance`, `placeholder:MND`, retired by S8.140) and cash buffer (weeks of outgoings) distributions of managements (PREFERENCE), review cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | pecking order within a leverage tolerance (Myers 1984; Myers and Majluf 1984) |

**Design**:
- **When**: the firm's financing review (K-101 attention, a monthly mean) and an occasion when its cash outlook shows a
  shortfall within its horizon (the outlook is its own, S1.453) — both on the one `finance` slot, so a firm has one
  `FRM.finance` decision a day at most by construction. The rule reads the view the attention handler gathers for the
  occasion (cash, outlook, dues, the firm's lines): no second gather. The rule first tests the need (40 ns: the
  outlook's shortfall and planned investment against cash beyond the buffer, all in the view); only a firm with a need
  gathers its sources' costs and builds the plan (360 ns). The prune is exact: a plan only funds a positive need, so a
  need at or below zero yields the empty plan for every weighing of the sources — their order and costs decide which
  sources fund a need, never whether a zero need is funded — and the plan carries no per-occasion taste.
- **Need** = outgoings, dues (K-54 owed sums, K-55 plans) and planned investment over the horizon, less cash beyond its
  buffer target.
- **Sources** (declared data, Law 10), each at its marginal cost now: retained cash — the deposit rate forgone; trade
  credit — the implied rate of the discounts it would forgo (S2.113); an undrawn line — its rate (S2.117); a new loan —
  the best quote from the banks it asks (BNK.6), an application sent now and answered at their 5c.
- **Plan**: sources cheapest first until the need is met, stopping at the source that would carry its debt (K-54 owed
  sums over its net assets, K-88) past its management's tolerance — a placeholder `FRM.leverage_tolerance`
  (`placeholder:MND`), the management type's declared value, until S8.140 makes it the holder's weighing of distress and
  retires it. The plan's draws are instructions; its loan application goes into the lending round (S1.425). What is not
  funded is not funded: the firm's dues then fail (FRM.21).
- **Retires** `FRM.shortfall_loan` (S1.427). Bonds, paper and shares join as sources at S3.131 and S3.153 (data).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a firm with no bank relation: no line, the loan source asks the banks in reach, possibly none
  (`no_relation_asks_banks_in_reach`).
- E12: a source whose cost is `Missing` — no quote yet — is skipped, never priced at 0, `missing_cost_skipped`.
- E11: day zero: the opening's lines and loans are GEN.5's; the first review decides (`opening_lines_until_review`).

**Extension points**: S2.121 (distress calls the same sources), S2.131 (investment's funding), S3.131 and S3.153
(sources by data); S3.108 and S4.116 read the same `FRM.finance` view (+0 on the gather).

**Unit tests**: `need_test_equals_full_gather` (over given views, the pruned result equals the full plan's);
`funding_cheapest_within_tolerance` (the sources taken and the stop at the tolerance); `missing_cost_skipped`;
`unfunded_need_stays_unfunded`. Edge cases: `no_relation_asks_banks_in_reach`; `opening_lines_until_review`.

**Live checks**: none (the gate reads funding by source).

**Budget**:
- Financing decisions B / NB / H 75 k / 0 / 75 k, the attention rule's count at the design point (55 k reviews at a
  monthly mean over 1.15 M firms, items of the 246 k attention decisions, and 20 k shortfall occasions): each tests its
  need at 40 ns; those with a need — the 20 k shortfalls and ≈ 11 k reviews with a planned investment in the horizon
  (S1.458's investment occasions, ≈ 10 k a day) — gather sources and plan at 360 ns → 3 + 11.2 = 14.2 / 0 / 14.2
  core-ms. S3.108 reads the need test's cash surplus and S4.116 takes its own early-out on the same view (+0 gather).
- adds 20 k / 0 / 20 k items to fin.decide.attend_ns (the shortfall occasions)
- adds 190 phone-ns to fin.decide.attend_ns at 75 k / 0 / 75 k items (40 ns each, and 360 ns at the 31 k with a need)
- Loan applications ride S1.425's lending round (its own share).
- +0 B (named slot `finance`, S1.227)
- Counters: `sys_frm.financing_decisions`, `sys_frm.funding_by_source`, `sys_frm.no_need_reviews`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a leverage target imposed from outside management's tolerance; funding beyond what a source grants;
a shortfall topped up.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass; `FRM.shortfall_loan` removed
  from the register.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.119 — A firm's payout

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.10 DECISION *(part: dividends; buybacks and the record and payment dates at S3.151)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9b statements, 2e instrument events), §7.10 (K-65 events engine), §7.14 (K-93 declared
limits)
**Depends on**: S1.333 (K-90 statements), S1.280 (K-65 holder lists), S1.281 (K-65's events engine: dividends to
holders of record), S1.283 (each firm's equity instrument held by persons), S1.338 (K-93 declared limits), S1.453 (the
cash outlook), S2.118 (planned funding)
**Goal**: after each statement a firm decides its dividend: it moves from the last one toward the free cash its own
plans leave, at its management's speed, and is paid only within the law's distributable reserves, pro rata to the
holders of its equity.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-firm/src/decisions.rs` | decision `FRM.payout` (continuous; occasion: a statement of its payout frequency ready — the K-42 dated entry at statement-ready that filing uses) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/payout.rs` | `free_cash(cash, outgoings, dues, buffer, own_funded_investment)`; `dividend(last, target, speed, distributable) -> Money` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the distributable-reserves limit per legal form (company law, K-93 declared limit on equity); the dividend event on the firm's instrument (K-65) |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | adjustment speed and payout frequency (annual, half-yearly, quarterly) distributions of managements (PREFERENCE); company law's distributable reserves rule (POLICY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | Lintner (1956) partial adjustment with a target from the firm's own cash and plans |

**Design**:
- **Target** `D* = cash − expected outgoings and dues over the horizon − buffer target − the investment it plans to fund
  itself`; **dividend** `D = D_last + s·(D* − D_last)` with s its management's speed; paid only within distributable
  reserves (K-93 limit; binding is an event the firm sees, Law 6) and not while D is negative. No payout ratio is a
  parameter; S3.151 keeps this target and adds only the buyback branch on the residual free cash and the record and
  payment dates.
- **Payment**: a dividend event on the firm's equity instrument (K-65's events engine, S1.281) dated its payment day;
  holders of record at that day's start are paid pro rata by largest remainder with the residue to a named party (K-16);
  money legs at 7.
- The last dividend is a read of the firm's equity instrument's last dividend event (K-65's events, S1.281; its record,
  K-37, S1.215) — no column on the firm (Law 4).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a year-end: decisions come when each statement is ready — the preparation lead time after the close — so none
  falls on the close's H day; payment days spread by each firm's choice within the law's window; a dividend day's holder
  rows are K-65's line (`payout_after_statement_ready`).
- E13: an unincorporated firm: its owners' drawings are S1.422's working owners' pay; its form declares no dividend, so
  no event (`unincorporated_no_dividend`).
- E3: no cash: D ≤ 0, nothing paid (`no_cash_no_payout`).

**Extension points**: S3.151 adds buybacks (FRM.10 completes there); S2.188's banks read their own payout near the
capital line (BCP).

**Unit tests**: `payout_partial_adjustment_within_reserves`; `no_dividend_when_negative`; `pro_rata_with_named_residue`.
Edge cases: `payout_after_statement_ready`; `unincorporated_no_dividend`; `no_cash_no_payout`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Payout decisions B / NB / H 3 k / 0 / 3 k (1.15 M firms, mostly annual) at 100 ns.
- adds 3 k / 0 / 3 k items to fin.decide.attend_ns
- on fin.calendar.year_end_statements (the weeks after a year's close, 50 k decisions a day): 5 core-ms; joins B′ (a
  lead time after the year's close can land on the first business day of January)
- Holder payments on K-65's events, 3 k dividends × ≈ 20 holders at 15 ns.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 1 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (holder payments on business days)
- its share of fin.fixed.holder_rows: 0 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (holder payments on H)
- +0 B (the last dividend read from K-65's events)
- Counters: `sys_frm.dividends`, `sys_frm.dividends_limited`.
**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a payout ratio as a primitive; a dividend beyond distributable reserves.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.120 — A buyer's time request wakes its seller's terms review

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TCR.2 DECISION
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`if-credit` messages), §6 (stage 5c)
**Depends on**: S2.112 (`TCR.grant_terms` and its rule), S1.237 (K-45 messages), S1.227 (K-43 wakes; the `grant_terms`
slot)
**Goal**: a buyer may ask a seller for more time on its invoices; the request is a message carrying the term asked and
the buyer's disclosed cash outlook, and it wakes the seller's terms review for that pair, which grants a longer term
when the sales it keeps are worth more than the added financing and expected loss, else refuses. S2.121's distressed
firms send it.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/invoices.rs` | message `TimeRequest` (buyer → seller: the pair, the term asked, the buyer's disclosed cash outlook) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | the "time request" occasion of `TCR.grant_terms` (a K-43 wake of the seller for that pair) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/terms.rs` | `grant` gains the disclosed outlook as an input for the asking pair: the added term's value to the seller = the margin on the sales it keeps − the financing of the longer receivable − the expected loss at the disclosed outlook's class |

**Design**:
- **The request** (K-45, 5d apply of the sender's decision) is due at the seller's next 5c; it wakes the seller's
  `grant_terms` slot for that day (one review a seller a day however many requests, S2.112's E14).
- **The answer** is the grant for that pair with the disclosed outlook read in place of the seller's class outlook for
  the buyer where it is worse (a buyer's disclosure is believed only downward; a better one does not raise the grant,
  SET.16: the seller's own record stands). The new grant is written in the pair's `terms`; a refusal leaves them.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E14: two requests to one seller the same day — one review over both pairs (`requests_one_review`).
- E10: a buyer ending between request and answer — the request lapses with the side's move (`request_lapses_on_ending`).
- E6: an open request saved in K-45 (`time_request_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: S2.121 sends the request.

**Unit tests**: `longer_term_when_kept_sales_outweigh_cost`; `disclosure_believed_only_downward`; `requests_one_review`;
`request_lapses_on_ending`; `time_request_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: none (LC-2-04's families stay clean; the gate reads time requests granted).

**Budget**:
- Requests B / NB / H 2 k / 0 / 10 k (distressed buyers, S2.121) at 300 ns (the pair's grant re-read) → 0.6 / 0 / 3
  core-ms; the reviews are items S2.112 already counts.
- adds 300 phone-ns to fin.decide.attend_ns at 2 k / 0 / 10 k items
- +0 B (named slot `grant_terms`, S1.227)
- Counter: `sys_tcr.time_requests_granted`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a grant raised by a buyer's own claim; a term granted outside the seller's decision.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, the rule's input and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.121 — A firm in distress

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.12 DECISION *(part: every act but seeking a buyer, which S4.179 adds)*
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`if-credit` decision points), §6 (stage 5c)
**Depends on**: S2.118 (sources), S2.117 (draws), S2.120 (the time request and the seller's answer), S2.103 (a lender's
workout answering a request), S2.101 and S2.114 (arrears and collection notices), S1.417 (layoffs), S1.450 (price
reviews: stock at a lower point), S1.443 (production cut)
**Goal**: a firm in distress acts: it takes the actions open to it in order of the value each loses per unit of cash it
raises until the shortfall is covered — cut production and inputs, lay off, sell stock at a lower price, draw its lines,
borrow at any quote, ask suppliers for time, ask lenders to restructure.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/decisions.rs` | decision `FRM.distress` (lumpy; occasions: an arrears or collection notice, a failed payment, a cash shortfall within the horizon); message `RestructuringRequest` (borrower → lender: wakes its workout on `BNK.workout`'s declared "woken" occasion, S2.103) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/distress.rs` | `actions(view) -> [Action; n]` each with (cash raised, value lost); `choose(actions, shortfall) -> Vec<Action>` into a day buffer |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the action set as declared data; placeholders "seek a buyer" (naming MNA) and "sell plant" (naming CAP) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | distressed firms' responses ordered by cost (Asquith, Gertner and Scharfstein 1994) |

**Design**:
- **Actions** (declared data, each with the cash it raises and the value it loses): cut production and input orders (the
  margin forgone, S1.443); lay off staff (S1.417, severance as owed); sell stock at a lower posted point (a price review
  occasion, S1.450); draw its lines (S2.117); borrow at any quote (S1.425); ask suppliers for time (a `TimeRequest` to
  the sellers on its invoices, S2.120, whose terms review grants or refuses); ask its lenders to restructure (a
  `RestructuringRequest` waking their workout, S2.103).
- **Choice**: in order of value lost per unit of cash raised until the shortfall is covered; each chosen action becomes
  that action's own instruction or occasion (5d apply).
- **Placeholders**: "sell plant" is not offered until the plant's resale market (S2.130) — naming CAP, retired at
  S2.130; "seek a buyer" is not offered until Stage 4's sale of a firm — naming MNA, retired at S4.179. Nothing stands
  in for either.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day wakes no distress decision on the day: the ended firms' estates have no rule, and the
  survivors' shortfalls arise as their losses land on the estates' distribution days, spread by S2.133's drawn phases
  (`mass_day_distress_spread`).
- E14: two notices of one firm the same day — one decision (`one_decision_per_firm_per_day`).
- E3: a firm with nothing to sell and no line: no action raises cash; its dues fail, S2.122 follows
  (`no_action_raises_cash`).

**Extension points**: S2.125 (the answer to a lender's offer compares against these values); S4.179 adds "seek a buyer".

### S2.122 — Insolvency tests and the duty to file

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.15 PROCESS *(part: the two tests)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9b thresholds, 2e), §7.12 (K-88 threshold index), §7.9 (K-56 default after grace)
**Depends on**: S1.330 (K-88 net assets maintained with a threshold index at zero), S1.239 (K-46 wakes on crossing),
S1.428 (default after grace), S1.225 (K-42 the filing-duty date)
**Goal**: a firm fails in two ways, either without the other: default of payment (a due still unpaid after its grace)
and balance-sheet insolvency (liabilities over assets at its own carrying values). Each is a dated fact; the country's
law says what follows — a duty to file within its period, or a creditor's right to petition.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-firm/src/insolvency.rs` | the insolvency law's triggers and filing duty as declared data (POLICY): which fact opens which procedure, who may open it, the period to file |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/insolvency.rs` | `fact(trigger) -> InsolvencyFact`; `duty_breached(fact_day, today, filed) -> bool` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the K-88 threshold at zero registered for every firm with an equity account (once, at its begin); the fact as an event kind; the filing-duty due on K-42 |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | the insolvency law: triggers, the duty's period, who may petition (POLICY) with sources |

**Design**:
- **Balance-sheet test**: K-88 keeps each firm's net assets from its one writer per delta, and its threshold index wakes
  a firm whose net assets cross zero (K-46, 9b) — no pass over firms (N8.6). The crossing is the fact "balance-sheet
  insolvent" (K-36 event, dated); a crossing back up ends it.
- **Default of payment**: K-56's default after grace (S1.428) is the fact "default of payment".
- **What follows** is the law's (POLICY): the debtor's **duty to file** within the declared period — a K-42 due at fact
  + period; if the firm has neither filed nor recovered by then, the breach is an event (the law's consequence, e.g.
  directors' liability, out of scope, Appendix D) — and the creditors' right to **petition** (S2.123). The fact is a
  need occasion for the firm's procedure decision (S2.123).
- Nothing here ends a firm: S1.428's direct ending after grace is superseded by S2.123's procedures.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe crossing 10 % of firms' thresholds at once: 115 k wakes, O(log n + k) K-46 query, 100 ns each
  (`threshold_crossings_query_cost`).
- E14: both facts the same day: one occasion carrying both triggers (`both_facts_one_occasion`).
- E6: thresholds rebuilt on load from K-88, `thresholds_rebuilt`.
- E11: a firm insolvent at the opening: the fact dated the snapshot day, GEN.5 (`insolvent_at_opening_dated_snapshot`).

**Extension points**: S2.123 reads the facts; S2.192's bank solvency fact is SUP's, not this.

**Unit tests**: `insolvency_tests_either_without_other`; `duty_breached_after_period`; `thresholds_rebuilt`. Edge cases:
`threshold_crossings_query_cost`; `both_facts_one_occasion`; `insolvent_at_opening_dated_snapshot`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-28`: no firm whose liabilities exceed its assets at its carrying values stays outside a procedure longer than
  its law allows, unless it recovered.

**Budget**:
- Insolvency facts B / NB / H 1 k / 0 / 5 k crossings (K-46's threshold wakes at 9b; K-56's defaults after grace) at 200
  ns → 0.2 / 0 / 1 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.2 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.mass_default (event): 23 core-ms; joins H and B′ (115 k facts recognised on the day, Law 1: the duty
  clock starts)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-36's dated facts, K-42's duty due)
- Counters: `sys_frm.insolvency_facts` by trigger, `sys_frm.duty_breaches`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a solvency test over every firm; an exit rate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] LC-2-28 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.123 — Insolvency procedures: liquidation, or restructuring under a stay

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.15 PROCESS *(part: the procedures and their opening)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 2e/2f), §7.15 (K-97 endings, K-96 estates), §7.9 (K-56 statuses)
**Depends on**: S2.122 (the facts), S2.104 (a lender's enforcement as a creditor's petition), S1.344 (endings into
estates), S1.263 and S1.265 (a stay is a re-intern of the debtor's obligor rows' terms with `Terms.stay`, whose dues the
wheel's take skips; lifted in bulk over the debtor's listed rows at confirmation or liquidation), S1.348 (K-100), S1.165
(K-06 index instances: `FRM.in_procedure`), S1.225 (K-42 dated entries: the plan deadline), S1.227 (the firm's `finance`
slot: the opening decided on its review)
**Goal**: under its country's law, a firm in either failure enters a procedure — opened by its own choice or duty, or by
a creditor's petition — that is either a liquidation into an estate or a restructuring under a stay, in which the
debtor's obligations stop falling due while creditors decide on a plan.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-firm/src/insolvency.rs` | procedures per law (liquidation, restructuring), openers, the stay's scope, the plan deadline; decision `FRM.open_procedure` (the debtor's); message `Petition` (creditor → court, a named institution) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/procedure.rs` | `open(fact, law, debtor_choice, petitions) -> Procedure` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the K-06 instance `FRM.in_procedure` (key: firm; value: procedure kind and opening day; ≈ 3 k members) — no column on the firm; the plan deadline is a K-42 due; the stay as `Terms.stay` re-interned on the debtor's obligor rows (K-55); the court as a declared institution |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | procedures, openers, fees (legal POLICY) and hours (TECHNOLOGY) |

**Design**:
- **Opening** (2e): the debtor decides on its next `finance` review after the fact (K-101 attention), and at the latest
  on the duty's due at fact + period (`FRM.open_procedure`: restructuring when its own going-concern value — S2.124's
  plan value — exceeds its estimate of liquidation, else liquidation) or files as its duty requires; a creditor may
  petition where the law allows (a lender's unpaid enforcement, S2.104; any unpaid creditor by data, e.g. a tax
  collector at Stage 5). The law says which petition opens which procedure.
- **Liquidation**: the firm ends at 2f into an estate (K-97, S1.344): staff released through their notice and severance
  (S1.417), holdings and sides moved; the estate administers (S2.133).
- **Restructuring**: every contract on which the debtor owes (its obligor sides, found by K-53's side lists) takes the
  terms re-interned with `Terms.stay` (K-55, 0 B): its dues are not raised while stayed (the take skips it); the
  debtor's own receivables still pay. The plan deadline is a K-42 due; S2.124 proposes, votes, confirms or liquidates.
- Fees to named parties (the court, the administrator) are flows (Law 14).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: 10 % of firms insolvent on one day open their procedures over the law's duty period, each on its own `finance`
  review; each opening's stays re-intern ≈ 30 rows a firm, 20 ns a row (`stays_reintern_rows`).
- E6: a procedure spanning days: its `FRM.in_procedure` entry and stayed terms saved (`procedure_round_trip`).
- E10: a creditor ending during the stay: its claim moves to its estate, still stayed (`ended_creditor_claim_stays`).
- E14: a petition and the debtor's own filing the same day: one procedure, the law's order
  (`petition_and_filing_one_procedure`).

**Extension points**: S2.124 (plan), S2.126 (unincorporated owners), S2.168 (a household's procedure reuses the stay).

**Unit tests**: `procedure_by_law_and_opener`; `stay_suspends_debtor_dues_only`; `procedure_round_trip`. Edge cases:
`stays_reintern_rows`; `ended_creditor_claim_stays`; `petition_and_filing_one_procedure`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-27`: every procedure names its trigger, its opener and the law's procedure; every restructuring has a plan, each
  class's votes and an outcome on the dates the law gives (applicable from S2.124).
- `LC-2-07`: PTY.9 — every firm that ended has an estate or a successor.

**Budget**:
- Openings B / NB / H 500 / 0 / 500 (≈ 115 k firm exits a year) × 1.6 µs (the choice, 1 µs, and ≈ 30 stayed rows
  re-interned at 20 ns) → 0.8 / 0 / 0.8 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.8 / 0 / 0.8 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.mass_default (event): 0 core-ms; joins H and B′
- spread after fin.calendar.mass_default over 15 days: 12 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.resolve (7.7 k openings a day, each
  on its firm's own `finance` review within the law's duty period)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.1 MB resident (3 k open procedures × 24 B, `FRM.in_procedure`)
- Counters: `sys_frm.procedures` by kind and opener, `sys_frm.rows_stayed`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a firm that cannot fail; a stay on a contract where the firm is not the obligor.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] LC-2-07 and LC-2-27 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.124 — The plan, the creditors' votes by class and confirmation

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.15 PROCESS *(part: plans, votes and confirmation; the liquidation horizon's destination at S2.132)*
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`if-firm`: plans and votes; a lender's vote through `sys-bnk`), §6 (stage 5c, 2e, 7), §7.6 (K-41
tallies)
**Depends on**: S2.123 (the restructuring and its deadline), S1.224 (K-41 tallies by class), S1.237 (K-45 messages),
S1.263 (K-55 new shapes), S2.102 (`loan_claim_value` under a lender's assessment), S2.104 (write-offs), S2.112 (a
supplier's loss outlook per buyer class, from its grant), S2.114 (the overdue invoices)
**Goal**: the debtor proposes one plan distributing its going-concern value over its claims by the law's priority, class
by class; each creditor votes from its own value of the plan against its own estimate of what liquidation would pay it;
a class accepts by the law's majorities of value and count; the plan is confirmed when every class accepts or the law's
rule for dissenting classes allows, and otherwise the firm is liquidated. A lender's vote is registered by `sys-bnk`
through `if-credit` (PC-40: only `sys-bnk` values a claim on a lender's book) — this step's one file outside `sys-frm`.
FRM.15 is complete.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-firm/src/insolvency.rs` | messages `Plan` (new terms per class, the debtor's statement of affairs) and `Vote`; decisions `FRM.propose_plan` (debtor), `FRM.vote_on_plan` (creditor; one rule per creditor kind) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/plan.rs` | `plan(going_concern, classes, law) -> Plan` by absolute priority; `vote(plan_value, liquidation_estimate) -> bool` for non-lender creditors |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/vote.rs` | a lender's `vote_on_plan` over its `LoanAssessment` (PC-40), registered by `sys-bnk` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the confirmation instruction (old claims closed, new contracts with their shapes, one link group); stream `FRM.plan_tie_lot` |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | voting majorities by value and count, dissenting-class rule, deadlines (POLICY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | a plan by absolute priority with class voting (Franks and Torous 1989; Bebchuk 1988) |

**Design**:
- **Crates**: the lender's vote is `sys-bnk`'s one lender-value function over its `LoanAssessment` (PC-40), the
  allowance §0.2 names; every other rule is `sys-frm`'s.
- **Plan** (5c after opening): the debtor's going-concern value (VAL.8 firm value over its expected margins after the
  plan) is distributed by the law's priority over its claim classes (K-98's class order); each class is offered new
  terms (on the lenders' points) or a haircut. Below its own estimate of liquidation proceeds it proposes none and is
  liquidated (S2.123's path).
- **Votes** (the creditors' next 5c): yes when the plan's claim value to the creditor ≥ its own estimate of liquidation
  recovery — the law's waterfall over the statement of affairs the plan carries, at its own valuation of the assets
  (K-91 valuer). A lender's values come only from its assessment (PC-40); a supplier's from its loss outlook per buyer
  class; others' from their own outlooks. Ties among equal claims by `FRM.plan_tie_lot`.
- **Tally** (K-41) per class by value and count; **confirmation** at the next 2e when every class accepts or the
  dissenting-class rule allows; the instruction at 7 closes the old claims and opens the new (new shapes, K-55); each
  creditor's loss is recognised at its next 2e (S2.104 for lenders, K-89 for others). Failing: liquidation.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a class with no voters — the law's rule; `empty_class_by_law`.
- E6: open plans and votes saved in K-45, tallies rebuilt, `plan_round_trip`.
- E10: a creditor ending before its vote: its estate votes, or its vote lapses by the law
  (`ended_creditor_estate_votes`).
- E14: equal claims — lot (`equal_claims_by_lot`).

**Extension points**: S3.138's bondholder votes (CRD.6) through the same tally; S2.168 reuses the claim class order.

**Unit tests**: `plan_by_absolute_priority`; `restructuring_vote_by_class` (value and count majorities, a dissenting
class under each law's rule); `lender_vote_reads_assessment_only` (compile level); `plan_round_trip`. Edge cases:
`ended_creditor_estate_votes`; `equal_claims_by_lot`.

**Live checks**: `LC-2-27` (S2.123) becomes applicable with the first plan.

**Budget**:
- Plans B / NB / H 100 / 0 / 100 (the restructurings among ≈ 460 procedures a business day), ≈ 30 claims each → votes 3
  k / 0 / 3 k at 2 µs → 6 / 0 / 6 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 6 / 0 / 6 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-45's plans and votes, K-55's new shapes)
- Counters: `sys_frm.plans_proposed`, `sys_frm.plans_confirmed`, `sys_frm.votes`.

**Guards**: none new (PC-40 covers the lender's rule).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a restructuring outcome written as a rule; a vote from any value but the voter's own.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules (both crates' — the lender's vote is `sys-bnk`'s by PC-40), declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit
  tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.125 — A firm's answer to a lender's offer

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.12 DECISION *(part: the firm's answer to a lender's restructuring offer; seeking a buyer at S4.179)*
**Architecture**: §3.1 (`answer_restructuring`'s rule per decider kind)
**Depends on**: S2.103 (`RestructuringOffer` and its placeholder answer), S2.121 (the distress routes' values), S1.453
(the firm's outlook)
**Goal**: a firm answering a lender's restructuring or extension offer accepts when the offer is worth more to it than
the best of its other distress routes; the placeholder answer for firms is retired.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/answer.rs` | `accept(offer_value, best_route_value) -> bool`; the offer's value is the firm's going-concern value under the new terms, its cash-flow outlook discounted at its marginal cost of money |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the firm's rule for `answer_restructuring` (decider: the finance office) |

**Design**:
- Serves BNK.7 (the lender's offer, S2.103) and retires its `answer_restructuring` placeholder for firms. on the offer's
  occasion (its next 5c), the rule values the offer as above and compares it with the best value among the distress
  actions (S2.121) including letting the lender enforce; accept → the new shape applies to that contract (K-55); refuse
  → the loan returns to the lender's workout. The comparison is S2.121's, listed in `SHAPES.toml` with it. **Retires**
  S2.103's placeholder for firms (naming FRM).

**Edge cases**:
- E6: an offer open across a load, answered after it — K-45 (`offer_answered_after_load`).
- E14: two offers from two lenders the same day: each answered on its own value, the second reading the first's
  acceptance through the firm's updated state next day — no two decisions of one kind the same day read each other,
  K-100 (`second_offer_reads_first_acceptance`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `answer_restructuring_against_distress_routes` (taken only when it beats the best). Edge cases:
`offer_answered_after_load`; `second_offer_reads_first_acceptance`.

### S2.126 — Owners who answer without limit

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.23 STATE *(part: unlimited liability of unincorporated firms' owners; the rest at S6.104)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (K-98 waterfall end), §7.9 (K-58 participations)
**Depends on**: S2.123 (liquidation into an estate), S1.346 (the waterfall), S1.422 (working owners of an unincorporated
firm), S1.268 (K-58 participations), S1.180 (legal forms declare limited liability)
**Goal**: when the estate of an unincorporated firm — a sole trader or a partnership, no party separate from its owners
— falls short at its final distribution, what its creditors are still owed becomes a claim on its owners, as the law of
such businesses has it, and they pay it from their own accounts or fail and meet their own consequences.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/unlimited.rs` | `owner_claims(shortfalls, owners, law) -> claims` (several by share, or joint and several) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | family `FRM.owner_liability` (creditor, owner person or a K-58 group of owners; `Balance`) and its due (the law's term) |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | the law of unincorporated businesses: several by shares or joint and several (POLICY) |

**Design**: at the final distribution (2f) of an estate whose legal form declares unlimited liability (K-21), each
unpaid claim is closed against the estate and reopened as an `FRM.owner_liability` contract on the owners — each owner
for its share (K-16 largest remainder, residue to a named party) or all owners jointly as one K-58 participation group,
as the law declares — due on the law's term. Unpaid, it is arrears like any debt (K-56): a person's own arrears actions
and, from S2.166, personal insolvency. Limited-liability forms declare none of this.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: an owner with nothing — the claim fails and stands in arrears (`owner_with_nothing_in_arrears`).
- E10: an owner who died — the claim is its estate's, in its waterfall (`dead_owner_claim_on_estate`).
- E13: a country whose law has no unincorporated form: nothing declared (`no_unincorporated_form_nothing_declared`).

**Extension points**: S2.168 (a person's insolvency ranks these claims by the law).

**Unit tests**: `shortfall_split_by_shares_with_residue`; `joint_group_when_law_says`. Edge cases:
`owner_with_nothing_in_arrears`; `dead_owner_claim_on_estate`; `no_unincorporated_form_nothing_declared`.

**Live checks**: none (LC-2-08 at S2.136 covers every ending's destinations).

**Budget**:
- Unincorporated estates' shortfalls B / NB / H 200 / 0 / 200 a day × ≈ 10 claims → 2 k opens at 60 ns
  (`fin.contracts.open_ns`) → 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms.
- adds 2 k / 0 / 2 k items to fin.contracts.open_ns
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (inside S1.257's owner liability, 1.0 MB)
- Counter: `sys_frm.owner_claims`.
**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a shortfall that vanishes; a limited-liability owner charged.

### S2.127 — Goods aboard a failed carrier

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRT.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §7.10 (K-69 processes with carrier and vehicle refs), §7.15 (K-97)
**Depends on**: S1.287 (K-69 shipments), S1.344 (the carrier's ending), S1.467 (shippers and their carriage contracts),
S1.346 (the waterfall's claims)
**Goal**: if a carrier fails with cargo aboard, the goods remain their owner's and are recovered from the carrier's
estate after the law's delay and at a cost; lost cargo is the carrier's liability, a claim in its estate.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frt/src/rules/recovery.rs` | `recovery(shipment, law) -> (day, cost)`; `cargo_claim(shipment, terms) -> Money` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frt/src/declare.rs` | the ending hook on K-69 processes whose carrier ref names the ended party; reason `FRT.recovery_cost` (owner → estate); the carrier's liability as a claim of the law's class |
| `data/<country>/FRT.toml` | recovery delay (POLICY) and cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY); carriage terms' liability for lost cargo (POLICY of the trade) |

**Design**: when a carrier ends (K-97 re-points its processes' carrier refs to its estate), each shipment it carries
keeps its owner (K-69's owner ref is the goods' owner); its arrival is re-dated to the recovery day (the law's delay,
K-42), at the place the vehicle stands (its route's last node reached, K-26), and the owner pays the recovery cost to
the estate (a flow at 7). Cargo already lost to a hazard (FRT.7) while in the carrier's charge is a claim of the owner
on the carrier by the carriage terms' liability, ranked in the estate's waterfall (K-98).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a carrier with thousands of shipments: one pass over its processes at its ending, K-97's cost
  (`carrier_processes_one_pass`).
- E10: an owner that ended too: its estate recovers (`ended_owner_estate_recovers`).
- E14: arrival due the day the carrier ends: the ending's order in 2f — arrival at 4a next day is re-dated
  (`arrival_redated_after_ending`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `goods_stay_owners_and_redated`; `lost_cargo_claim_by_terms`. Edge cases: `carrier_processes_one_pass`;
`ended_owner_estate_recovers`; `arrival_redated_after_ending`.

**Status**: planned

**Depends on**: S2.111–S2.114 (invoices, their closes and losses), S2.122–S2.124 (facts and procedures), S2.121
(distress actions), S1.490 (firm births), S1.344 (endings), S1.221 (K-39 accumulators), S1.213 (K-36 subject index)
**Goal**: the observer reports days of payment by trade and their course over the cycle, chains of distress from a
buyer's default to its suppliers' own arrears, and the firm population's size, growth, age and productivity
distributions, entry and exit by industry, age and cause (cash or solvency), margins and markups and the share in
distress. Measures are read, never enforced.

**Files**:

### S2.129 — Plant failures by age

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CAP.6 PROCESS *(part: the failure hazard; repair at S2.130)*
**Architecture**: §7.7 (K-44 hazards over counts), §7.10 (K-67 capital classes, condition, maintained capacity)
**Depends on**: S1.285 (the failed band of the condition chain), S1.235 (K-44 hazards drawn ahead, over counts), S1.285
(K-67 classes with condition and age class, capacity maintained on every change), S1.457 (wear on its kinks: one
depreciation schedule), S1.464 (damage by hazards at named places)
**Goal**: a unit of plant fails by its kind's failure hazard, which rises with its age; a failed unit stops serving
until its owner repairs or scraps it. With wear by use and age (S1.457) and damage by hazards (S1.464), every way CAP.6
names for a unit to lose service exists, and repair is its owner's decision (S2.130).

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/rules/failure.rs` | `failure_rate(kind, age_class) -> Rate` from the kind's retirement pattern |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/declare.rs` | hazard `CAP.failure` (subject: a holder's (kind, age class) holding of plant; rate × units in service; outcome: one unit to S1.285's failed band); the owner's occasion `CAP.failed_unit` |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the failure hazard by age as a share of the kind's mean service life (CAP.13), one entry, a standing SHAPE: `source_ref` BEA's modified Winfrey S-3 discard density (`state/typed_winfrey_s3`) over each kind's service life (`cap/`), stating that the curve counts retirements for any reason, so it overstates physical failure and counts owners' scrapping (CAP.4) twice, and that it stands because no physical-failure table is in `data/sources/raw/` |
| `docs/PROJECT_PHOENIX.md` | CAP.13's standing SHAPE — the failure hazard read from a discard curve, with its reason — listed in Appendix C's SHAPE row |

**Design**:
- **The hazard** (CHN, Law 15): per plant holding by (kind, age class) the rate is the Winfrey S-3 discard density at
  that age class over the kind's mean life, times units in service — a hazard over counts on K-44 (one next hit per
  subject, redrawn when units or the age class change). A failure is an event naming the holder and the unit's class.
- **Source, and what it loses** (Law 1, Law 2): the Winfrey S-3 curve is BEA's discard density — it counts units retired
  for any reason, owners' scrapping (CAP.4) included — so a hazard read from it overstates physical failure and counts
  some scrapping twice. No engineering failure table is in `data/sources/raw/`, so the mapping stands as a declared
  SHAPE with that loss stated in SHAPES.toml and in the primitive's `source_ref` in the register; no live check or gate
  read credits the stock's age profile (GEN.10).
- **Outcome**: one unit moves to S1.285's failed band (efficiency 0) (K-60 holding move within the class chain, K-67
  capacity recomputed for that holder only) and the owner receives the occasion `CAP.failed_unit`, answered by its plant
  review (S2.130). Until then the unit gives no service; its depreciation continues on its schedule (S1.457).
- Named units (power plants, infrastructure, K-66) fail by the same hazard declared on their kind.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe day's damage is S1.464's, not this (`catastrophe_damage_not_failure`).
- E6: next-hit days saved, K-44 (`next_hit_round_trip`).
- E11: age classes at the opening are GEN's drawn vintages (`opening_vintages_drawn`).
- E13: a kind with no failure pattern declared: refused at assembly, never a zero rate (`no_failure_pattern_refused`).

**Extension points**: S2.130 (repair or scrap), S2.159 (dwellings' wear and repair use the same condition chain),
S2.202's power plants (ENE.1, data).

**Unit tests**: `failure_rate_follows_winfrey_by_age`; `failed_unit_leaves_capacity`. Edge cases:
`catastrophe_damage_not_failure`; `next_hit_round_trip`; `opening_vintages_drawn`; `no_failure_pattern_refused`.

**Live checks**: none (CAP.8's identity is the core's family).

**Budget**:
- Failures B / NB / H 2.7 k / 2.7 k / 2.7 k a day (≈ 5 % of ≈ 20 M units a year over 365 days; plant fails idle or not)
  at 670 ns (a hit, a K-60 move and K-67's capacity for one holder) → 2 / 2 / 2 core-ms.
- adds 2.7 k / 2.7 k / 2.7 k items to fin.hazards.hit_ns
- +0 B (core attribute: K-44's next hits; the failed band's cells are S1.285's, ledger line 24)
- Counter: `sys_cap.failures`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a failure drawn per unit per day; a depreciation rate standing for failures.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data mapping and unit tests written; fast checks pass; the standing SHAPE registered once
  and listed in the spec's Appendix C in the same change.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.130 — The plant review and its resale market

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CAP.4 DECISION; CAP.6 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c, 6a), §7.11 (K-70 offers, K-80 bilateral)
**Depends on**: S2.121 (retires its "sell plant" placeholder), S2.129 (failed units), S2.116 (written-down carrying
values), S1.458 (investment's plant value), S1.296 (K-70 standing offers), S1.317 (K-80), S1.445 (services bought:
repair services at posted prices)
**Goal**: an owner decides at its plant review, and when a unit fails, whether to keep, maintain, repair, sell or scrap
it, by what each is worth to it; plant is sold bilaterally to buyers who can use it, through the plant's resale market.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-firm/src/decisions.rs` | decision `CAP.review` (lumpy; the owner's; occasions: its review, a failed unit, a distress action "sell plant") |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/rules/review.rs` | `values(unit_view) -> {keep, maintain, repair, sell, scrap}`; `choose` |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/declare.rs` | the resale market per (capital kind, region) — bilateral asks (K-70 offers) answered by buyers' quotes (K-80); reasons for repair purchases and scrap |
| `data/shared/CAP.toml` | repair and maintenance technologies per kind (hours, parts) (TECHNOLOGY); review schedule (PREFERENCE) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the owner's comparison (a unit's value in its alternative uses) with its source |

**Design**:
- **Values** (VAL.8 plant value, the owner's own): keep — its service over the remaining life at its expected prices
  less running costs; maintain — the same with slower wear, less the maintenance's cost; repair (a failed or worn unit)
  — service restored less the repair service's price (a purchase at posted prices from repairers, S1.445); sell — the
  best quote it gets; scrap — the scrap value of its content (GDS.1) less the cost. The highest value is taken; ties by
  lot (`CAP.review_lot`).
- **The resale market**: an owner selling posts an ask (K-70) per (kind, region); buyers who can use the unit (firms
  whose ways use that kind, their own investment decision, S1.458) quote from their own value of it; the seller takes
  the best at or above its value of keeping, else lowers its ask a point at its next review. A sale moves the unit
  (holding and its condition, age class) at a price, both legs at 7; CAP.12: the plant moves with its new owner's site.
- **CAP.6 completes here**: failure (S2.129), wear by use and age (S1.457's curve over the holding's use) and repair or
  maintenance by the owner's choice.
- **Retires** S2.121's "sell plant" placeholder (naming CAP).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no buyer: the ask stands; MKT.10 (`no_buyer_ask_stands`).
- E4: an estate's plant with no buyer: S2.133's descending ask (`estate_plant_descending_ask`).
- E6: open asks saved, K-70 (`open_plant_ask_round_trip`).
- E10: a buyer ending before settlement: its quote lapses (`ended_buyer_quote_lapses`).

**Extension points**: S2.133 (estates sell plant here), S2.160 (infrastructure's private owners use the same review).

**Unit tests**: `review_takes_best_value`; `repair_bought_at_posted_price`; `resale_ask_moves_down`. Edge cases:
`no_buyer_ask_stands`; `estate_plant_descending_ask`; `open_plant_ask_round_trip`; `ended_buyer_quote_lapses`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Plant reviews B / NB / H 8 k / 0 / 8 k (≈ 5 k scheduled a business day over 1.15 M firms a year, and ≈ 3 k failed
  units) at 2 µs → 16 / 0 / 16 core-ms; resale asks ≈ 2 k live on K-70.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 16 / 0 / 16 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (named slot `investment`, S1.227: `CAP.review` is the firm's investment occasion)
- Counters: `sys_cap.reviews` by choice, `sys_cap.resales`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a resale price not quoted by a buyer; a scrapped unit whose content vanishes.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass; S2.121's CAP placeholder
  removed.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.131 — Investment at the cost of money, and projects drawn in stages

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CAP.13 PRIMITIVE *(part: capital kinds, lives, lead times, wear curves and managements' horizon; the hurdle
is the deciding holder's weighing at S8.138)*
**Architecture**: §7.8 (K-50 commitments), §7.10 (K-69 processes)
**Depends on**: S1.458 (investment on its occasion, CAP.3), S1.459 (projects bought from named producers, paid in
stages), S2.118 (the funding plan), S2.117 (a committed line), S1.251 (K-50 commitments on both books)
**Goal**: a firm's investment is weighed against what money costs it at the margin now — its bank's quote for new debt
and its funding mix — by its management's own hurdle and horizon drawn from the measured distributions; a project it
starts is a commitment on both books, drawn stage by stage within its builder's capacity.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/rules/invest.rs` | extended: the hurdle and horizon read from the management's type; the cost of money from S2.118's marginal sources |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/declare.rs` | the project's undrawn budget as a K-50 commitment (owner ↔ builder), drawn at each stage payment |
| `data/shared/FRM.toml` | management hurdle (`CAP.hurdle`, `placeholder:MND`, retired by S8.138) and horizon distributions (PREFERENCE), mapped from `state/typed_hurdle_rates`, `state/typed_planning_horizon`, `state/typed_capital_budgeting_methods` |

**Design**:
- **Placeholder** `CAP.hurdle` (`placeholder:MND`): until S8.138 the hurdle is the management type's declared value
  below; S8.138 makes it the deciding holder's weighing and retires it.
- **Hurdles and horizons** (CAP.13): each management type (NUM.4, drawn at founding, S1.490) carries a hurdle over the
  cost of money and a planning horizon, the types discretising the surveyed distributions (Graham's surveys: mean hurdle
  over WACC by firm characteristic; years over which plans are judged reliable; appraisal methods' shares).
- **The comparison** (CAP.3, S1.458): the project's value over the horizon beats the marginal cost of money — the
  cheapest source S2.118 would take for it — by at least the hurdle, and the firm can fund it (the funding plan).
- **Projects** (REG.10, CAP.5): the contract with the builder is a K-69 process whose unpaid budget is a K-50 commitment
  on both books, drawn at each stage payment within the builder's capacity net of its other work (S1.459); a line drawn
  for it is S2.117's.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a type with no hurdle mapped: refused at assembly (`no_hurdle_refused`).
- E10: a builder failing mid-project: the process passes to the builder's estate at cost; the owner's commitment stands
  against the estate, S2.133 sells or completes (`builder_estate_takes_process`).

**Extension points**: S2.156 (builders' dwelling projects), S2.212 (energy investment reads this comparison, ENE.7).

**Unit tests**: `hurdle_and_horizon_from_type`; `project_commitment_drawn_by_stage`. Edge cases: `no_hurdle_refused`;
`builder_estate_takes_process`.

### S2.132 — The insolvency law's classes, the owners' residual and the heirless destination

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: L3 *(part: the insolvency law's classes by each claim's own terms and the owners' residual)*; FRM.15
PROCESS; POP.9 PROCESS *(part: the unsold remainder's destination)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (K-98 classes as declared POLICY), §7.3 (K-20 dated schedules, K-21 families' claim class)
**Depends on**: S1.345 (K-98 classes in declared order, proceeds per currency, residue to a named party), S1.346
(estates' payments onto the waterfall), S1.179 (K-20 the law as a dated POLICY schedule), S1.280 (K-65 holders of a
firm's equity), S1.281 (K-65's events engine: the owners' residual paid as an event), S1.143 (`DEM.heirless_to`, the
inheritance law's heirless destination per country, a POLICY read here)
**Goal**: every estate's proceeds are paid in the order its country's insolvency law declares — secured claims from
their own collateral, then preferential (employees, taxes, deposits and the deposit insurer where the law prefers them),
ordinary unsecured (senior debt, trade creditors, close-out claims, other deposits), subordinated, and equity — in every
currency the party held; what remains after the creditors goes to the owners, and a person's estate with no heir, or
what a firm's estate did not sell by the law's horizon, goes to the party the law names.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/declare.rs` | the seniority term (K-55: senior / subordinated) on the loan and bond families' terms, and the lien's rank for secured claims (K-63); each family's claim class where the law ranks by creditor kind (wages, taxes, deposits) (Law 10); the class order per country; the owners' residual class (the equity instrument's holders, K-65); the unsold remainder's destination |
| `docs/PROJECT_PHOENIX.md` | FRM.15 gains, after "or a **liquidation** into an estate (L3)": "; what the estate has not sold by that law's horizon passes in kind to the party the law names". POP.9's sentence of S1.143 is extended to: "An estate with no heir passes what it leaves to the party the inheritance law names (POLICY); what an estate could not sell by that law's horizon passes in kind to its heirs, or with none to that party." |
| `data/<country>/EST.toml` | insolvency law: class order, which deposits and the deposit insurer are preferred, the liquidation horizon and the destination of what a firm's or institution's estate did not sell, each with its source (`state/doing_business` resolving-insolvency indicators for the order where they give it) |

**Design**:
- **Where a claim ranks** is read from the contract's own terms where its family declares a seniority term — a loan or
  bond is senior or subordinated by its terms (a second lien, a subordinated or an intra-group loan ranks by what it
  says), and a secured claim by its lien's rank on the collateral (K-63) — and from the family only where the law ranks
  by creditor kind: an employment's unpaid wages and severance preferential; a tax payable preferential or ordinary by
  law; a deposit preferred or ordinary by law; an invoice ordinary. K-98 reads the declaration; no class is inferred
  from an instrument type (L3's "silently broken by").
- **Secured** claims are paid from their own collateral's sale proceeds first; any shortfall joins the ordinary class.
- **Owners' residual**: after every creditor class, the residue goes to the holders of the firm's equity pro rata (K-65
  holders of record, paid as a K-65 event, S1.281; K-16 largest remainder); the old waterfall's single class and
  treasury residue are retired.
- **Destinations**: a person's estate with no heir — S1.143's `DEM.heirless_to`, read and never declared here; a firm's or
  institution's estate — what it has not sold at the law's horizon goes to the named party (not a valuation paid out:
  the units themselves pass).
- The law is a dated POLICY schedule (K-20): a change applies to estates opened after its effective day.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a country with no preference for deposits: the class list lacks it; a unit test with it absent
  (`absent_class_skipped`).
- E12: a family with no declared class: refused at assembly (`family_without_class_refused`).
- E4: an estate that never sells: at the horizon its units pass to the destination, so none waits forever — the law's
  horizon, not a bound: a declared POLICY limit (`unsold_units_pass_at_horizon`).

**Extension points**: S2.133, S2.135, S2.136; S2.196 (bail-in layers, BCP.8), S4.111 (a clearing house's waterfall) and
S4.166 (tranche waterfalls declare their own class orders to K-98).

**Unit tests**: `waterfall_order_with_preferred_deposits`; `secured_from_own_collateral_then_ordinary`;
`owners_residual_pro_rata`; `subordinated_loan_ranks_below_senior`; `second_lien_after_first_on_collateral`;
`family_without_class_refused`. Edge cases: `absent_class_skipped`; `family_without_class_refused`;
`unsold_units_pass_at_horizon`.

**Live checks**: none (LC-2-08 at S2.136).

**Budget**:
- No new volume: K-98's ≈ 25 k claims a day are S1.346's share; reading a claim's rank from its interned terms costs
  nothing added.
- +0 B (core attribute: the seniority term is interned in K-55's terms, 0 B a row)
- Counters: none new.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a claim ranked by instrument type; a residue with no named holder.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations and data with sources written; unit tests over K-98's arithmetic with these orders; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.133 — Estate administration: what to sell and the descending ask

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POP.9 PROCESS *(part: a person's estate sells only what its debts need)*; L3 *(part: estates sell into real
markets under a deadline)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c, 6a), §7.15 (K-96 estates' dates), §7.11 (K-70 offers)
**Depends on**: S2.132 (the law's classes and horizon), S1.342 (K-96 estates visited on proceeds or dates), S1.296 (K-70
offers), S2.130 (plant's resale market), S2.115 (factoring), S2.107 (loan sales), S2.106 (the loan-book valuer), S1.335
(K-91 valuers), S1.450 (posted prices: stock where it always sold)
**Goal**: every estate is administered: a firm's or institution's estate sells everything but money into real markets to
real bidders; a person's estate sells only what its debts, taxes and costs need, in the order that loses the heirs
least. Each ask starts at the estate's valuation and moves down a point when the time left to the law's horizon is
shorter than the time the administrator expects a sale to take at that ask. What it fetches is an outcome.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/rules/administer.rs` | `sale_set(holdings, debts, kind) -> set` (everything for a firm; for a person the least loss to heirs); `ask(valuation, points, time_left, time_to_sell) -> point` |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/declare.rs` | decision `EST.administer` (decider: the estate's administrator office; occasions: the claims call at a phase drawn per estate (`TIME.schedule_phase` on the estate's key), proceeds or answers arriving (K-96), each ask's lowering date on K-42 — business days only (K-19); no scheduled review); administration fees as a preferential cost; placeholders for dwellings (naming HSG) and securities (naming EQY) |
| `data/<country>/EST.toml` | review schedule, administration fees and hours (POLICY, TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | a descending ask under a deadline (Shleifer and Vishny 1992) |

**Design**:
- **What to sell**: a firm's or institution's estate — everything but money: stock at a posted point (K-70, where it
  always sold), plant through the resale market (S2.130), receivables by factoring (S2.115) or by collecting them as
  they fall due, loans by loan sale (S2.107) or collection. A person's estate — first its money; then the holdings that
  raise the cash its debts, taxes and costs need with least loss of value to the heirs: the most liquid first, a
  divisible holding only in the quantity needed, an indivisible unit (a dwelling, a vehicle, a business) only when the
  rest does not suffice. Everything else passes in kind (S2.135).
- **Asks**: the administrator lists at the estate's named valuer's valuation (K-91) and, at each review, moves the ask
  down one point of the trade's table when time left to the law's horizon < its outlook of time on market at that ask
  (from the market's published records). No floor.
- **Placeholders** (named, not standing in): estates' dwellings and land wait for the housing and land markets (naming
  HSG, retired at S2.152 and S2.155); estates' securities with no market wait (naming EQY, retired at S3.147 for shares
  and S3.166 for bonds). Their count is reported.
- **Claims call**: at its first review the administrator calls for claims — each lender with a loan on the estate is
  woken for it (`BNK.workout`, S2.103), so an ended borrower's workouts fall on the estates' drawn phases, never all on
  the day of the endings (S2.101).
- **When** (REP.38): between its events an estate has nothing to decide, so its attention gives it no scheduled review;
  it is woken on its occasions only — its first review (the claims call) at a phase drawn per estate within the law's
  claims period (`TIME.schedule_phase` on the estate's key), proceeds or an answer arriving (K-96), and each ask's next
  lowering date, filed on the wheel (K-42) when the ask is posted as the day its time left falls below its outlook of
  time on market. An occasion on a closed day moves to the next business day (K-19).
- The estate is visited only on its dates and when proceeds arrive (K-96); nothing visits every estate every day.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: 86–115 k estates opened in one turn: each estate's claims call at its own drawn phase, so they spread over the
  following business week (`mass_opening_reviews_spread`); no estate is reviewed between its occasions
  (`estate_woken_only_on_occasions`).
- E2: no bidder: the ask falls to the horizon; then S2.132's destination (`ask_falls_to_horizon`).
- E4: an estate with only unsellable units: counted, ends at the horizon (`unsellable_estate_ends_at_horizon`).
- E6: asks saved in K-70 (`estate_ask_round_trip`).
- E10: a buyer ending before settlement: the match fails, SET.3 (`ended_buyer_match_fails`).

**Extension points**: S2.135 (what passes in kind), S2.136 (the end), S2.168 (a personal insolvency's estate uses the
same administration with exemptions), S3.147/S3.166 (securities).

**Unit tests**: `estate_sells_only_what_debts_need` (an indivisible unit sold only when the rest falls short);
`ask_moves_toward_deadline`; `firm_estate_sells_all_but_money`. Edge cases: `mass_opening_reviews_spread`;
`estate_woken_only_on_occasions`; `ask_falls_to_horizon`; `unsellable_estate_ends_at_horizon`; `estate_ask_round_trip`;
`ended_buyer_match_fails`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-09`: L3 — every estate sale is a match in a market at its price; no estate distributed a valuation.

**Budget**:
- Woken estates B / NB / H: claims calls 1.2 k (≈ 300 k estates opened a year) at 2 µs, proceeds and answers 3 k at 500
  ns, ask lowerings 5 k (≈ 50 k live asks, each lowered about every two weeks) at 200 ns → 2.4 + 1.5 + 1 = 4.9 / 0 / 4.9
  core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 4.9 / 0 / 4.9 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.mass_default (event): 0 core-ms; joins H and B′
- spread after fin.calendar.mass_default over 5 days: 46 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.resolve (23 k claims calls a day at
  2 µs, the ≈ 115 k new estates on their drawn phases; the lenders' woken workouts are S2.103's spread)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-96's dates, K-70's asks; the lowering dates are wheel entries of the asks, K-42)
- Counters: `sys_est.sales`, `sys_est.asks_lowered`, `sys_est.waiting_on_placeholder` by system.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an estate that values rather than sells; a person's estate selling what its debts do not need; a
floor under an ask.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data, the SHAPE entry and unit tests written; fast checks pass; placeholders declared with
  their retiring steps.
- [ ] LC-2-09 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.134 — Kin of adult children living elsewhere at the opening

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: kin of adult children living elsewhere at the opening)*
**Architecture**: §7.9 (K-53 kin family, `Pair` rows between persons)
**Depends on**: S1.404 (households and persons drawn by sys-dem, with `DEM.grown_children`), S1.257 (K-53 families)
**Goal**: at the opening, every person's kin — parents and adult children living in other households — are contracts
between the persons (REP.3, POP.1), drawn with the households from mothers' expected living children less those the
opening places at home, so an estate's heirs are named persons from day zero.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/opening/kin.rs` | `adult_children_elsewhere(mother_age, living_children, at_home) -> count`; the pairing of a mother (and her partner) with adult persons of the right ages in other households of her region |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/declare.rs` | family `DEM.kin` (S1.257's `DEM.kin` row, 16 B, Chain / Chain, both sides persons); stream `DEM.kin_pairing` |
| `data/profiles/<level>/people.toml` | the co-residence of older persons with an adult child by group (38.6, 51.4, 54.5 %), mapped from `un/older_persons`, checking the drawn households against it |

**Design**:
- Serves POP.1 (kin as contracts between persons) and POP.9 (heirs named from day zero).
- For each opening household with a mother of age a, her expected living children at each adult age
  (`DEM.grown_children`) less the children the opening placed in her household is the count of adult children living
  elsewhere; each is paired with a person of that age in another household of her region (REP.23: the pairing is a
  place-like draw of who among the eligible, on `DEM.kin_pairing`, never a party to a new contract without one).
- Each pair is one `DEM.kin` row (parent person ↔ child person). The share of older persons co-resident with an adult
  child is read against `un/older_persons` as a check of the draw (a finding if off, never a rescale).
- Kin rows are kept by births (S1.402) and moves; nothing ages them.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no eligible person of the age in the region: the kin is absent, counted, not invented (`no_eligible_kin_absent`).
- E7: the pairing's draw keyed by (mother, child age), the same for any workers (`kin_draw_worker_independent`).
- E9: kin rows ≈ 1.2 M, S1.257's `DEM.kin` rows (`[store.contracts] "DEM.kin"`) (`kin_rows_capacity`).

**Extension points**: S2.135 (heirs from kin), S6.120 and S6.121 (formation and leaving home keep kin across moves),
S5.182 (migration).

**Unit tests**: `children_elsewhere_arithmetic`; `no_eligible_no_kin`. Edge cases: `no_eligible_kin_absent`;
`kin_draw_worker_independent`; `kin_rows_capacity`.

**Live checks**: none (LC-2-29 at S2.135 reads heirs named).

**Budget**:
- Opening only: ≈ 1.2 M rows at 60 ns (`fin.contracts.open_ns`) ≈ 72 core-ms of the opening's span; no daily cost.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (inside S1.257's `DEM.kin` row: 1.2 M × 16 B = 19.2 MB)
- Counter: `sys_dem.kin_rows`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; an allocation per day; kin drawn at a
death; a household (not a person) as a side of a kin row.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Opening rule, family, data mapping and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution: the opening's span within its ratchet in `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.135 — Inheritance in kind

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POP.9 PROCESS *(part: distribution in kind to named heirs; estates' securities sold at S3.147 and S3.166,
where it completes)*; POP.15 FORBID
**Architecture**: §7.15 (K-98 distribution), §7.9 (K-58 joint holdings)
**Depends on**: S2.133 (what the estate sold), S2.134 (kin rows), S2.132 (the heirless destination), S1.402 (deaths'
destinations recorded), S1.268 (K-58 participations for a unit held jointly), S1.172 (K-16 apportionment)
**Goal**: what a person's estate did not need to sell passes to its heirs in kind by the inheritance law: divisible
holdings by share exactly, an indivisible unit whole to one heir with money differences to the others, or held jointly
where the estate lacks the money and the law so provides; each heir then keeps, sells or runs what it received by its
own decisions. With no heir, the law's destination takes it. No death is left without a destination for everything.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-pop/src/estate.rs` | the inheritance law as declared data: heirs' classes and shares from kin rows, the order for indivisible units, joint holding rule; occasion `Inherited` |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/rules/heirs.rs` | `heirs(kin, law) -> shares`; `distribute_in_kind(holdings, money, shares, law) -> transfers` |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/declare.rs` | stream `EST.heir_order` (among equal claims to an indivisible unit); the distribution instruction (one link group) |
| `data/<country>/EST.toml` | inheritance law (POLICY) with sources |

**Design**:
- **Heirs**: the kin rows naming the deceased (S2.134; spouse through its household role) by the law's classes and
  shares; an heir who has died is its own estate's (chains of estates).
- **In kind** (after the waterfall has paid the debts, S2.132): divisible holdings split by share exactly (K-16, residue
  to a named heir by the law's order); an indivisible unit whole to one heir drawn by the law's order among equals
  (`EST.heir_order`, a lot, not a decision), the others receiving the difference in money where the estate has it, and
  otherwise holding it jointly as a K-58 group; one link group at 7 (SET.4).
- Each heir's household gets an `Inherited` occasion for the unit: a dwelling reaches its where-to-live decision
  (S2.146), a business its owner's decisions; until those exist the unit is held.
- **No heir**: the law's destination (S2.132). **POP.15** is complete: S1.402 records every death's destinations; this
  step gives every holding one.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: an estate with nothing left: no transfer, the death's record says so (`empty_estate_no_transfer`).
- E10: an heir dead before distribution: its share to its estate (`dead_heir_share_to_estate`).
- E14: two estates naming each other's persons as heirs the same day: each distributes on its own date, chains in
  rounds, K-98 (`mutual_heirs_in_rounds`).

**Extension points**: S6.123 (formation reads inherited dwellings); S5.114 (inheritance tax, a claim ranked in the
estate).

**Unit tests**: `inheritance_in_kind_to_heirs` (shares, whole units and money differences); `joint_when_no_money`;
`no_heir_to_destination`. Edge cases: `empty_estate_no_transfer`; `dead_heir_share_to_estate`; `mutual_heirs_in_rounds`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-29`: POP.9 — every person's estate names its heirs and what each took in kind; no indivisible unit was sold
  while its divisible holdings would have covered its debts, taxes and costs, and no divisible holding beyond need.

**Budget**:
- Distributions B / NB / H 300 / 0 / 300 a day (≈ 75 k deaths a year) × ≈ 10 transfers at 100 ns → 0.3 / 0 / 0.3
  core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- +0 B (core attribute: K-60's moves)
- Counters: `sys_est.in_kind_transfers`, `sys_est.to_destination`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an inheritance paid as a share of a valuation; heirs other than named kin.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, data and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] LC-2-29 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.136 — Holdings resolved and the estate's end

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: L3 *(part: every estate ends, its units resolved)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (K-96 end, K-97), §7.10 (K-65 cessation, REG.12)
**Depends on**: S2.133, S2.135 (sales and distributions), S2.132 (destinations), S1.281 (K-65's events engine: every
holding in a ceasing instrument resolved at cessation), S1.342 (K-96 lifecycle), S1.194 (K-31 tombstones)
**Goal**: when an estate's last distribution settles, every holding it held has ended as cash, a holding of an heir or a
destination, a recovery paid by the waterfall, or a recorded loss; the estate ends with no successor and references to
it resolve as ended. Every ending distributes.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/rules/end.rs` | `resolved(estate_view) -> bool`; the end instruction |
| `crates/systems/sys-est/src/declare.rs` | the estate's end on K-96 (state "ended", K-31 tombstone); audit family `EST.destinations` |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_2_08.rs`, `lc_2_30.rs` | LC-2-08, LC-2-30 |

**Design**:
- After the final distribution settles (7), at the next 2f: every unpaid claim closes with its holder's recorded loss
  (S2.114 for invoices, S2.104 for loans, K-89 for others — an event each, L1); every instrument issued by the estate's
  party ceases (K-65, REG.12: each holding resolves to cash paid, a recovery claim paid or a loss); the estate ends
  (K-96 → K-31 tombstone with its end day, SET.13).
- **Audit family `EST.destinations`** (L3, PTY.10): every row the ended party held or owed has a named destination
  recorded (from the endings' K-36 records and the estate's closes), recounted for the estates ended that day.

**Edge cases**:
- E4: an estate whose units never sell ends at the horizon through S2.132's destination
  (`unsold_securities_pass_at_horizon`).
- E9: estates open ≈ 90 k steady against K-96's declared capacity (S1.342), reported per year (`estates_open_capacity`).
- E10: a record naming the ended estate resolves as ended, K-31 (`ended_estate_reference_resolves`).

**Extension points**: S2.199 (a failed bank's remainder estate ends the same way), S2.168.

**Unit tests**: `holdings_resolve_to_named_ends`; `end_after_final_distribution_only`. Edge cases:
`unsold_securities_pass_at_horizon`; `estates_open_capacity`; `ended_estate_reference_resolves`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-2-08`: L3, PTY.10 — every ended party's positions landed on a successor or its estate; none vanished; every estate
  that ended resolved each holding.
- `LC-2-30`: REG.12 — every holding in an ended estate resolved to cash, an heir's holding, a paid claim or a recorded
  loss.

**Budget**:
- Estate ends B / NB / H 1.2 k / 0 / 1.2 k (≈ 300 k a year) × ≈ 30 rows at 15 ns, audit fused → 0.6 / 0 / 0.6 core-ms.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.6 / 0 / 0.6 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 20 (estates): +0 MB — 90 k open estates inside K-96's line
- Counters: `sys_est.estates_open` by kind, `sys_est.mean_life_days` by kind, `sys_est.ended`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an estate ending with a holding unresolved; a claim left open against an ended estate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, declarations, the audit family and unit tests written; fast checks pass; `phx inject` of the family reports
  the injected break.
- [ ] LC-2-08 and LC-2-30 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; counters ratcheted.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
