### S2.183 — Interbank term loans asked for and chosen

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.6 DECISION *(part: borrowing term funds bilaterally from another bank)*; MMK.1 STATE *(part:
unsecured term loans between named banks, bilateral)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (the bilateral protocol), §6.1 (stages 5c, 7).
**Depends on**: S2.182 (the answers); S1.317 (K-80: ask, quote, decline, accept); S1.237 (K-45: messages with
deadlines); S1.341 (K-95: the maturity ladder); S1.348 (K-100); S2.179 (the borrower's marginal cost of the
alternative source).
**Goal**: a bank short of term funding asks the banks in its declared reach; the borrower takes the lowest quote its
own value accepts, and the loan between two named banks settles its principal the next day in the large-value
system.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/interbank.rs` | the borrower's ask (amount, tenor from its gap and ladder) and its choice |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/declare.rs` | decision `BFL.interbank` (office: the bank's chief executive; woken by S2.184's action) |

| `data/<country>/BFL.toml` | reach among banks (declared), tenors (POLICY of the market's conventions), review cost in hours |

**Design**:
- **Ask** (the borrower, from S2.184's action): amount = the gap it chose to fund this way; tenor from its maturity
  ladder (K-95) and horizon; sent at 5c as a K-80 ask to every bank in its declared reach, answers due at the next
  business day's 5c (TIME.7).
- **Choice**: the lowest quote its own value accepts (its marginal cost of the alternative source, S2.179), ties by
  lot (`BFL.interbank_lot`), at the following 5c; the row opens and the principal settles at 7 (MON.5: reserves move).
- **Streams**: `BFL.interbank_lot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no bank quotes: the market failed for the borrower (MKT.10), an event it sees; its next action follows

- E6: asks and quotes pending across days are saved messages: K-45's `messages_roundtrip` (S1.237).
- E14: two asks by one bank the same day are one ask of the summed amount (one decision a kind a day, K-100):
  `one_ask_a_day`.

**Extension points**: S8.167 (the choice converted to options).
**Unit tests**: `lowest_quote_accepted_ties_by_lot`; `tenor_from_ladder`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-105` (second part): every interbank loan names both banks and settled its principal at stage 7
of the day after the choice.

**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an interbank rate from a formula; a borrower reading a lender's private state.

### S2.184 — A bank short of funding acts in order of cost

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.6 DECISION *(part: borrowing bilaterally from banks, pledging at the facility, selling loans,
bidding for deposits and shrinking new lending)*
**Architecture**: §7.16 (the decision core and attention), §6.1 (stages 5c, 5d, 8).
**Depends on**: S1.348 (K-100: the decision, its office); S1.350 (K-101: the review and the wake); S2.179 (each
action's marginal cost and the shadow cost of cash); S2.180 (the gap: liquid assets against the buffer); S2.181 (the
deposit-rate review it wakes); S2.183 (the interbank ask); S2.107 (loans offered for sale); S1.425 (the lending
round's standards and required return, which read the bank's lending restraint); S1.277 (K-63: free eligible
collateral pledged for stage 8).
**Goal**: when a bank's liquid assets fall below its buffer, it closes the gap by the actions open to it, cheapest
first — borrow from another bank, pledge assets at the facility, sell loans, bid for deposits, shrink new lending —
each at the marginal cost it reads from its own position.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/shortfall.rs` | the action list's costs and the least-cost order |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/declare.rs` | decision `BFL.shortfall` (office: the bank's chief executive; review and wake; not an opening decision); `ShortfallAction` declarations (how each action's cost and capacity are read); the bank's `lending_restraint` fact |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bfl.rs` | the wake at stage 9 when the surplus after settlement is negative; 5c decision, 5d intents |
| `data/<country>/BFL.toml` | the actions each lender form may take (POLICY of management); review cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | least cost first among a bank's liquidity actions (Cornett, McNutt, Strahan and Tehranian, 2011), with source |

**Design**:
- **Occasions**: the liquidity review (S2.180's schedule) and a wake (K-43 `wake`) at stage 9 of any business day on
  which the bank's liquid surplus after settlement is negative (S2.180's fact, re-read at 9b).
- **Actions are data** (`ShortfallAction`: its marginal cost read, its capacity read): interbank term borrowing (its
  own outlook of the rate it was last quoted); a pledge at the facility (the lending rate plus the shadow value of the
  collateral tied up; capacity its free eligible collateral × haircut); loan sales (the value lost below claim value
  per unit of cash, S2.107's quotes; capacity its saleable loans); bidding for deposits (the expected rise in the
  deposit rate × the deposits it would reprice, per unit of inflow its response outlook gives); shrinking new lending
  (the margin forgone per unit not written; capacity its expected lending). S3.110 adds the money market and repo as
  declared actions.
- **The rule**: order the available actions by marginal cost; take each up to its own capacity until the gap closes.
  Outputs at 5d: an interbank ask (S2.183), loans offered for sale (S2.107), a wake of the deposit-rate review
  (S2.181) with the need, a pledge instruction for stage 8 (S2.185), and the `lending_restraint` fact — the rise in
  required return and standards the lending round's quote and decline read (BNK.5's tightening on funding).
- **Streams**: none (costs are compared exactly; equal costs go by the actions' declared order).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: many banks short on one day: each decides from its own state; no rule reads another bank's gap:
  `decisions_independent_across_banks`.
- E2: no action available (no counterparties, no collateral, nothing saleable): the gap stands; the day's shortfall
  goes to the facility and, failing that, to failure (S2.185): `no_action_gap_stands`.
- E11: not an opening decision: day zero opens with no gap recorded: `shortfall_not_on_day_zero`.
- E14: a review and a wake the same day are one decision (K-100): `review_and_wake_one_decision`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `actions_taken_cheapest_first`; `stops_when_gap_closed`; `each_action_to_its_own_capacity`;
`restraint_raises_required_return`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-106`: every negative liquid surplus after settlement was followed, at the next business day's
5c, by the bank's shortfall decision, and every action it took names its marginal cost at the decision.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.01 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H) (5 decisions × 8 actions × 200 ns)
- counters `phx_bfl.shortfall_decisions`, `phx_bfl.shortfall_actions` (by kind)
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0003 MB resident (35 banks × 8 B: lending restraint)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an order of actions fixed by rank instead of cost; unlimited or uncollateralised central-bank
credit.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-106 passes.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.185 — The facility request, reserves as the residue of payments, and failure for liquidity

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.8 PROCESS; BFL.11 INVARIANT; BFL.10 PROCESS *(part: short after the central bank's facility)*
**Architecture**: §7.8 (money accounts), §7.11 (the administered form), §7.17 (audit families), §6.1 (stages 7, 8,
9c).
**Depends on**: S1.429 (the fund stage, the facilities and intraday credit's close to an overdue claim); S1.430 (the
bank's request, whose `BNK.reserve_target` this retires); S1.319 (K-81:
the facilities as administered forms); S1.277 (K-63: collateral pledged); S1.248 (K-49: settlement, the one writer of
a reserve balance, and its per-party nets); S1.353 (K-103: the reserves family); S1.213 (K-36: the failure event);
S2.180 (the buffer's reserve part); S2.184 (a pledge instruction).
**Goal**: a bank's reserve position each day is what everybody's payments left; at stage 8 each bank asks the
central bank's facility for what it lacks against its free eligible collateral, or places its excess; a bank that
still cannot repay its intraday credit has failed for liquidity, whatever its capital, and the failure is a recorded,
public event the supervisor reads the same day.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/facility.rs` | the bank's request (lending or deposit facility) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/declare.rs` | decision `BFL.facility` (office: the bank's chief executive; continuous at stage 8); the bank's `liquidity_failed` fact; event kind `BFL.liquidity_failure` (public) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/audit.rs` | the reserves family: each bank's reserve change equals its net of settled legs |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bfl.rs` | stage 8 requests; the failure fact at the end of stage 8 |

**Design**:
- **Reserves** (BFL.8, BFL.11): a bank's reserve balance is its account at the central bank (K-47), written only by
  K-49's apply; no rule writes it and no bank chooses it. The audit's reserves family (K-103) recounts each bank's
  change of the day from K-49's per-party nets over the day's settled legs, over the change set (K-07), and reports a
  difference as a finding with its size (II.5). PC-25 (re-aimed at settlement's apply, S1.158) refuses any other
  writer at compile level.
- **The request** (stage 8, the bank's own, MKT.9): reserves after stage 7 below the buffer's reserve part (S2.180)
  → a request at the lending facility for the difference, against free eligible collateral (liens, K-63; the haircut
  in force, K-20), plus any pledge S2.184 instructed; above it → the excess placed at the deposit facility. The
  facility answers by its administered rule (K-81) and settles in stage 8. Retires `BNK.reserve_target`.
- **Failure for liquidity** (BFL.10): at the end of stage 8, a bank whose intraday credit the core's close turned into
  an overdue claim of the central bank (S1.429) has `liquidity_failed` set with the day and the shortfall, and a public
  event `BFL.liquidity_failure` (K-36) naming it. The supervisor's 9c reads it (S2.192) and triggers resolution
  (S2.196) whatever the bank's capital. S3.110 puts the money market before the facility.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: several banks failing the same day: each its own fact and event, each resolved (S2.196):
  `failures_independent`.
- E2: no free collateral: the lending facility lends nothing; the shortfall stands and fails (MKT.10):
  `no_collateral_no_draw`.
- E5: a heavy payday's stage 8 sees every bank's position after the day's flows: one request per bank:
  `one_request_per_bank`.
- E6: `liquidity_failed` and the overdue claim are saved; a load between D's stage 8 and D+1 resumes resolution:
  K-99's `resolution_roundtrip` (S1.347).
- E13: a country whose central bank declares no deposit facility: the excess stays as reserves:
  `no_deposit_facility`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `request_is_gap_against_free_collateral`; `excess_to_deposit_facility`; `failure_only_after_facility`;
`reserves_family_detects_injected_write` (an injected reserve change without a leg is found); the edge-case tests
above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-13`: BFL.11 — every change of a bank's reserve balance is a leg of a settled instruction;
`LC-2-36`: every liquidity failure followed the facility's use at stage 8 and went to resolution (not yet seen until
the run has one).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.fund: 0.04 / 0 / 0.04 core-ms (B / NB / H) (35 requests × 1 µs)
- its share of fin.fixed.recount: 0.04 / 0 / 0.04 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the reserves family, 35 recounts × 1 µs; reserves do not move on NB)
- counters `phx_bfl.facility_draws`, `phx_bfl.deposit_placements`, `phx_bfl.liquidity_failures`
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0004 MB resident (35 banks × 12 B: failure day, shortfall)
**Guards**: PC-25 (re-aimed at S1.158) holds the one writer.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a reserve balance written outside settlement; unlimited, unpriced or uncollateralised facility
credit; a failed bank that keeps paying.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-13 passes and
  LC-2-36 is registered.
- [ ] `BNK.reserve_target` gone; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.186 — Capital in layers, and requirements computed from each bank's books

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BCP.2 STATE; BCP.5 PROCESS; BNK.2 STATE; BCP.1 STATE *(part: equity, subordinated debt, senior and
uninsured layers)*; BCP.9 PRIMITIVE *(part: requirements and risk weights)*
**Architecture**: §7.14 (books and declared limits), §7.12 (equity accounts), §7.15 (the waterfall's classes), §6.1
(stage 9b).
**Depends on**: S1.330 (K-88: the equity account, moved only by named events); S1.338 (K-93: books per (bank, book
class), declared limits); S1.345 (K-98: claim classes in declared order); S1.279 (K-64: the bank's subordinated debt
as instruments); S1.333 (K-90: statements on reporting dates); S1.171 (K-14: the large-exposure sweep on reporting
dates); S1.179 (K-20: the supervisor's requirements and weights as dated POLICY); S2.102 (provisions posted before
the ratios); S2.180 (liquid assets and the run-off outflows).
**Goal**: a bank's capital is its equity account and the layers beneath it — contingent capital, subordinated debt,
senior creditors and uninsured depositors — which absorb losses in that order. On its reporting dates and review days
the risk-weighted, leverage, large-exposure and liquidity ratios are computed from its own books.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-banking/src/capital.rs` | layers as declared claim classes; requirement kinds; the rule handle `risk_weight(asset class, inputs)`; the capital facts' types (ratios by requirement, the binding one) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/requirements.rs` | the four ratios as pure functions over a bank's books |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/declare.rs` | the bank kind's capital columns; the large-exposure and liquidity limits (K-93); the layers' classes; the large-exposure sweep; placeholder `BCP.group_is_bank` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bcp.rs` | 9b on reporting dates and review days |
| `data/<country>/BCP.toml` | requirements, risk weights by asset class, the large-exposure limit, the reporting calendar (POLICY of the supervisor) |
| data series | `bank/brss_2019`, `bank/brss_2019_questions` (capital requirements, risk weights, large-exposure limits) |

**Design**:
- **Layers** (BCP.1): the bank's liabilities carry declared claim classes (K-98's order from the country's insolvency
  law with BCP.1's banking order): equity (K-88), contingent capital (S3.132, S3.139), subordinated debt (instruments,
  K-64, the opening's from S2.187), senior creditors and uninsured depositors. Before resolution losses fall
  on equity, and on contingent capital when its own trigger ratio is crossed (S3.139); the other layers act only in
  resolution (S2.196).
- **Capital** (BCP.5): the equity account, moved only by named events — booked losses and provisions through income
  (S2.102, S2.104), distributions (S2.119), retained income, issuance (S3.152). No capital column exists apart from it;
  every ratio reads K-88.
- **Requirements** (BCP.2), computed at 9b after 9a's provisions, on the bank's reporting dates (the supervisor's
  calendar) and its review days:
  - risk-weighted: equity ÷ Σ over the bank's book classes (K-93) of balance × `risk_weight(class)`, the weight a
    handle over the class and its declared inputs (loan-to-value band at origination; ratings from S3.214), so a
    sectoral weight change (S2.201) re-weighs classes, never rows;
  - leverage: equity ÷ total exposure (K-93 balances plus undrawn facilities);
  - large exposure: each counterparty's exposure ÷ capital, against the declared limit (K-93): at quote time, the
    borrower's own contracts with this bank (its side list, O(its contracts)); on each reporting date, one declared
    sweep of the loan rows for all banks at once (K-14), reduced by (bank, counterparty) (K-13);
  - liquidity: liquid assets after haircuts (S2.180) ÷ the outflows its funding classes would run off at the
    supervisor's declared rates.
  Results are the bank's capital columns (K-32): each ratio, its requirement, the binding one.
- **Facilities** (BNK.2 completes): a facility's undrawn part is a real obligation that consumes the bank's capital —
  in the leverage exposure, and in the risk-weighted exposure at the supervisor's declared conversion factor for
  undrawn commitments — and its liquidity, as an outflow at the supervisor's declared rate (S2.180).
- **On the group**: until S3.157 writes the group fact the group is the bank alone (`BCP.group_is_bank`).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day: provisions land at 9a, the ratios read them at 9b the same day: `ratios_read_day_provisions`.
- E5: reporting dates fall on quarter-ends (H): the sweep runs once for every bank: `sweep_once_per_reporting_date`.
- E8: ratios as exact rationals of i64 sums (K-16), never a float stored: `ratio_exact`.
- E12: a missing weight for a class refuses at assembly; a bank with no exposure has a leverage ratio `Missing`, not
  infinite: `weight_absent_refused`, `no_exposure_missing_ratio`.
- E13: a class with no loans contributes nothing: `empty_class_contributes_nothing`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `ratios_from_books`; `weight_change_reweighs_classes`; `large_exposure_from_borrower_contracts`;
`capital_is_equity_account` (no second writer compiles); the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-40`: every bank had every requirement computed from its own books on every reporting date;
none is exempt; `LC-2-39` (second part): every bank's capital equals its equity account.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.01 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H) (ratios, 35 banks × 20 book classes on review days)
- on fin.calendar.bank_reporting (the supervisor's reporting dates, quarter-ends): 11 core-ms; joins H (one sweep of 2.25 M loan rows × 5 ns for every bank at once)
- counters `phx_bcp.ratio_computations`, `phx_bcp.exposure_rows_swept`
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.001 MB resident (35 banks × 40 B: four ratios, binding requirement)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a capital pot; an exempt bank; a bank's own risk model in place of the supervisor's weights; a
weight stored per loan.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-40 and LC-2-39
  (second part) pass.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.188 — The capital buffer each bank chooses, and what it does near its line

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BCP.3 DECISION; BCP.7 MEASURE; BCP.9 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.16 (the decision core), §6.1 (stages 5c, 9b).
**Depends on**: S1.348 (K-100); S1.350 (K-101: the capital review, woken by a loss or a requirement change); S2.186
(ratios, requirements, the gap); S2.102 (the bank's loss outlook from its provisions); S2.119 (the payout rule the
dividend restriction reads); S2.107 (loans offered for sale; the reservation's capital term); S1.425 (the quote's
required return); S1.475 (the agency's releases, for BCP.7's measures).
**Goal**: each bank holds a buffer above its requirements chosen from its own caution and the cost of equity; near its
line it restricts dividends, sheds risk-weighted assets and prices loans dearer through the shadow cost of capital,
so losses slow its lending.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/rules/{buffer,near_line}.rs` | the buffer choice; the dividend restriction, shedding order and shadow cost of capital |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/declare.rs` | decision `BCP.buffer` (office: the bank's chief executive; monthly review; wake on a loss or a requirement change; opening decision); the capital facts `buffer_target`, `gap`, `shadow_cost_of_capital`; the measures' published series |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bcp.rs` | 5c review, 5d facts, the sale offers through S2.107 |
| `data/<country>/BCP.toml` | capital appetite and the dividend adjustment speed (PREFERENCE of management); review cost in hours |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | buffer choice under costly breaches (Milne and Whalley, 2001; Peura and Keppo, 2006); shrinking risk-weighted assets (Gropp, Mosk, Ongena and Wix, 2019); the bank capital channel (Van den Heuvel, 2002) |

**Design**:
- **The buffer** (lumpy, monthly and woken): the target buffer where the chance that losses over its horizon (its loss
  outlook's mean and width) carry its ratio below requirement, times the cost of a breach (the supervisor's declared
  consequences, S2.192), equals the cost of holding the buffer (its required return less the cost of the debt it would
  otherwise use), scaled by its capital appetite (PREFERENCE; BCP.9 completes).
- **Near the line** (the gap = ratio − requirement − target, read at each decision):
  - dividends: the payout rule (S2.119) pays no dividend that would carry the ratio below requirement plus target, and
    none while a supervisor's restriction stands (S2.192); S3.151 extends the same restriction to buybacks;
  - shedding: loans offered for sale (S2.107) until the gap closes, the most risk-weighted assets freed per unit of
    value lost below claim value first;
  - pricing: the **shadow cost of capital** — the rise in expected breach cost per unit of risk-weighted assets — is a
    fact the quote adds to its required return (S2.190) and S2.107's reservation adds (retiring its capital term).
- **Measures** (BCP.7): which requirement binds per bank, payouts and lending of banks near their line against the
  rest, and capital ratios over the cycle, published by the agency on its calendar (S1.475's releases).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: day zero: the buffer is an opening decision from the snapshot's ratios: `capital_buffer_day_zero`.
- E12: no loss history yet: the loss outlook starts at its opening value (GEN.5), never zero width:
  `loss_outlook_opening_width`.
- E14: a loss wake and the monthly review the same day are one decision: `review_and_wake_one_decision`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `buffer_rises_with_loss_width_and_breach_cost`; `near_line_restricts_dividends`;
`shedding_most_rwa_per_value_lost_first`; `shadow_cost_zero_far_from_line`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-15`: BCP.7 — which requirement binds per bank, payouts and lending near the line, and capital
ratios over the cycle are published.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.004 / 0 / 0.004 core-ms (B / NB / H) (2 decisions × 2 µs)
- counters `phx_bcp.buffer_reviews`, `phx_bcp.near_line_days`, `phx_bcp.loans_offered_for_capital`
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.001 MB resident (35 banks × 32 B: buffer target, gap, shadow cost of capital, loss outlook)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a buffer as a declared share of requirement; a payout cut by a clamp instead of the rule's own gap.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-15 passes.
- [ ] S2.107's capital term retired; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.189 — The capital a loan consumes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.4 DECISION *(part: the capital the loan consumes, a handle over the lender's regime)*
**Architecture**: §7.3 (rule handles), §6.1 (stage 5c).
**Depends on**: S2.186 (weights and requirements); S2.188 (the target buffer); S1.179 (K-20: rule handles).
**Goal**: the capital a loan consumes is a handle over the lender's declared regime: its exposure × its risk weight ×
the lender's target ratio (requirement plus its chosen buffer).

**Files**:

| path | purpose |

- **The regime** is declared per lender form: for banks the supervisor's requirements (S2.186); S3.199's non-bank

  (the handle's signature is `if-banking`'s).

### S2.190 — Quotes, declines and standards read capital and liquidity

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.4 DECISION; BNK.5 DECISION
**Architecture**: §7.16 (the decision core), §6.1 (stage 5c).
**Depends on**: S1.425 (the lending round: quote, decline, standards, borrower classes); S2.189 (the charge); S2.179
(the marginal cost of funds); S2.102 (the one assessment: default probability and loss given default); S2.186 (the
large-exposure limit); S2.188 (the shadow cost of capital); S2.180 (the liquid surplus); S2.184 (the lending
restraint).
**Goal**: every quote is built from the lender's own marginal cost of funds, its own assessment of the borrower, the
capital the loan consumes times the return it requires on that capital, and its cost of making the loan; a bank
declines when the loan is not worth it, fails its standards, or when its own capital or liquidity will not carry it,
and tightens its standards when its own losses, funding or outlook worsen.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/{quote,decline,standard}.rs` | the quote reads the charge and the shadow cost of capital; declines for capital, large exposure and liquidity; standards read the capital gap, the lending restraint and the loss outlook |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | `BNK.risk_weight` removed |

**Design**:
- **The quote** (S1.425's rule): its funding cost (S2.179) + the expected loss from its own assessment (S2.102) + the
  charge (S2.189) × its required return on capital (BNK.16) + the shadow cost of capital per unit of risk-weighted
  assets (S2.188) + its operating cost per loan. Retires `BNK.risk_weight`.
- **Declines** (BNK.5), each a recorded reason (MKT.10): not worth it; standards failed (loan-to-value, income
  multiple, coverage — S1.425's); capital (the loan's risk-weighted amount would carry the ratio below requirement +
  target); large exposure (the limit binds, an event the bank sees, Law 6); liquidity (the amount exceeds its liquid
  surplus beyond its buffer).
- **Tightening**: the standards' rule reads the capital gap, the lending restraint (S2.184) and its loss outlook, so
  worse losses, funding or outlook tighten them.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: every bank declines a borrower: the borrower goes without (BNK.6), an event it sees: `all_decline_goes_without`.
- E12: a `Missing` cost of funds declines (S2.179): `missing_cost_declines`.
- E14: two applications to one bank the same day each read the day's facts at 5c's start; their combined effect on
  the ratio is the next day's: `same_day_applications_read_start_state`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `quote_components_sum`; `decline_reasons_each_recorded`; `large_exposure_binds_quote`;
`standards_tighten_with_gap`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-107`: every decline names its reason, and every quote's components (funding, expected loss,
capital charge × required return, shadow cost, operating cost) are in its record.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.04 / 0 / 0.04 core-ms (B / NB / H) (10 k quotes × 2 extra cached reads, 4 ns)
- counters `phx_bnk.declines` (by reason)
- +0 B (core attribute)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; one assessment shared by lenders; a rate from a spread over a reference as a primitive.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-107 passes.
- [ ] `BNK.risk_weight` gone; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.191 — A bank's decision to raise capital, recorded

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BCP.4 DECISION *(part: the decision to raise and its value)*
**Architecture**: §7.16 (the decision core), §6.1 (stage 5c).
**Depends on**: S1.348 (K-100); S2.186 (ratios and requirements); S2.188 (the buffer target and the gap); S1.215
(K-37: the record of the decision); S1.453 (the bank's own earnings outlook, from which VAL.8 values its shares).
**Goal**: a bank whose capital gap persists weighs raising capital: it decides to issue when restoring its buffer is
worth more to it than the dilution the issue costs its owners at its own valuation. Until the markets that sell the
issue exist, the decision is recorded, counted and unmet, and its capital rises only by retained income.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/rules/raise.rs` | the raise decision's value |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/declare.rs` | decision `BCP.raise` (office: the bank's board; woken by the buffer review when the gap persists, and by a demanded plan; not an opening decision); record kind `BCP.raise_decided` (public); placeholder `BCP.raise_unmet` (naming EQY and CRD) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bcp.rs` | 5c decision; 9d record |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | issuance under asymmetric information (Myers and Majluf, 1984), with source |

**Design**:
- **Occasion**: the buffer review (S2.188) wakes it when the gap has stayed negative over the bank's declared horizon
  of reviews; a supervisor's demanded plan (S2.192) wakes it.
- **Value**: restoring the buffer is worth the expected breach cost avoided (S2.188's) plus the lending the gap now
  forgoes; the issue costs the dilution of existing owners — the shortfall of the price the bank expects the issue to
  fetch below its own value of the shares (VAL.8 over its own earnings outlook), plus the issue's fees. It decides to
  raise the amount that closes the gap when the value exceeds the cost.
- **Placeholder** `BCP.raise_unmet`: the decision is recorded (K-37, public: an announcement readers see, VAL.6) and
  counted; nothing is issued; capital rises only by retained income (BCP.5). S3.154 (shares) and S3.132 (subordinated
  debt, contingent capital) retire it by routing the same decision to an issue that can fail if investors will not buy.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: many banks deciding to raise on one day: each its own record: `raise_records_independent`.
- E11: no raise on day zero (not an opening decision): `raise_not_on_day_zero`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `raises_when_breach_value_beats_dilution`; `no_raise_when_own_value_below_price`; the edge-case tests
above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-108`: every raise decision is recorded with its amount and value, and counted as unmet while the
placeholder stands.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.001 / 0 / 0.001 core-ms (B / NB / H) (0.1 decisions a day × 2 µs)
- counters `phx_bcp.raise_decided`, `phx_bcp.raise_unmet`
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0 MB resident (tens of records a year)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; capital raised from nowhere; an issue settled without a buyer.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-108 passes.
- [ ] The placeholder listed in the register with its retirers; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S2.192 — The supervisor and the resolution authority; tests, consequences and the solvency fact

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.1 STATE; SUP.3 STATE; BCP.6 PROCESS; SUP.4 PROCESS *(part: banks)*
**Architecture**: §7.5 (parties and offices), §7.7 (messages), §6.1 (stages 9c, 9e, 2c).
**Depends on**: S1.180 (K-21: the authority kinds and their offices); S1.209 (K-34: heads' offices, empty); S1.407
(institutions opened by their systems); S1.423 (agencies' appropriation and funding); S1.348 (K-100: decisions through founding preferences while the office is
empty); S1.237 (K-45: demands due the next business day); S1.213 (K-36: public events); S2.186 (the ratios); S2.185
(the liquidity failure); S2.191 (a plan answered by a raise).
**Goal**: each country has a named supervisor and a named resolution authority, each a party with its accounts and a
head's office. On each bank's reporting dates the supervisor tests its ratios; a breach issues its declared
consequence, due the next business day: a restriction on distributions, a demanded plan, and below the point of
non-viability, resolution. The supervisor's solvency fact per bank is what the central bank's lending reads.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-banking/src/supervision.rs` | the solvency fact; demand kinds (`Restriction`, `PlanDemanded`); the resolution trigger message |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/{declare,supervisor}.rs` | authority kinds (supervisor, resolution authority) with their offices; the test rule; placeholder `SUP.heads_unfilled` (naming POL) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | 9c tests on reporting dates, 9e demands, 2c demands due |
| `data/<country>/SUP.toml` | supervisory rules, reporting dates, each breach's consequence, the point of non-viability, the solvency line (POLICY of the supervisor) |
| data series | `bank/brss_2019`, `bank/brss_2019_questions`, `bank/brss_2019_currency` (supervisory powers, consequences, reporting) |

**Design**:
- **Parties** (SUP.1, SUP.3): per country a supervisor and a resolution authority, opened by `sys-sup`'s opening
  contribution (S1.407's path) as institutions with accounts at the central bank, funded as public agencies through
  S1.423's appropriation. Each declares its head's office
  (PTY.16); the office stays empty until S5.144 fills it (`SUP.heads_unfilled`, naming POL), and the authority decides
  through its founding preferences meanwhile (MND.20).
- **Tests** (SUP.4, part), at 9c on each bank's reporting dates (the declared calendar, N8.9): the ratios of S2.186
  against the requirements in force. A breach issues its declared consequence as a demand (K-45) due the next business
  day (TIME.7), applied at 9e:
  - a **restriction on distributions**: a fact on the bank that the payout rule reads (S2.188, S2.119) until the ratio
    is restored;
  - a **demanded plan**: a message that wakes the bank's buffer review and raise decision (S2.188, S2.191); the plan
    it records answers it;
  - below the **point of non-viability**, or on a liquidity failure (S2.185): the **resolution trigger**, handed to
    the resolution authority (S2.196) the same 9c.
- **The solvency fact**: per bank, the supervisor's judgement from its latest test — capital at or above the declared
  solvency line — a column the central bank's facility (S1.429) and its lender of last resort (S3.115) read.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: several banks breaching on one reporting date: each its own demand; triggers handled per bank (S2.196):
  `breaches_independent`.
- E5: reporting dates bunched at a quarter-end: ≈ 35 tests that day: `tests_per_reporting_date`.
- E6: demands pending across a save are messages; the restriction fact is a saved column: K-45's
  `messages_roundtrip` (S1.237).
- E10: a bank resolved while a demand is pending: the demand lapses by its declared rule at the bank's closing:
  `demand_lapses_at_closing`.
- E11: day zero: the latest solvency fact is the snapshot's (GEN.5); no test runs: `solvency_fact_day_zero`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `breach_issues_declared_consequence_next_day`; `below_pnv_triggers_resolution`;
`solvency_fact_from_latest_test`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-109`: every bank was tested on every reporting date, every breach's consequence was due the
next business day, and every restriction stood until its ratio was restored.
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.bank_reporting (the supervisor's reporting dates, quarter-ends): 0.07 core-ms; joins H (35 tests × 2 µs)
- counters `phx_sup.tests`, `phx_sup.breaches`, `phx_sup.demands`
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.02 MB resident (six authorities × 3 KB, 35 banks × 8 B: restriction, solvency fact)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a consequence applied the same stage it is demanded; an exempt bank.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-109 passes.
- [ ] The placeholder registered with its retirer S5.144; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.193 — Deposit insurance and the resolution fund

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.2 STATE; BFL.14 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.8 (money accounts and their facilities: the backstop), §6.1 (stages 9c, 2c).
**Depends on**: S1.180 (K-21: the insurer kind; the uninsured-depositor claim class); S1.407 (institutions opened);
S1.240 (K-47: the backstop, a facility on the insurer's account, BNK.18); S1.268 (K-58: joint accounts in shares);
S1.237 (K-45: premiums and levies as demands); S2.192 (the authorities and the resolution authority); S2.186 (ratios
for the risk class); S2.180 (funding facts for the risk class).
**Goal**: each country's deposit insurer is a party whose fund is built from premiums charged to banks by risk, which
covers each depositor up to a limit per person, and which has a backstop facility from the treasury; the resolution
authority keeps a resolution fund built from a levy on banks.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-banking/src/insurance.rs` | the coverage rule (per person, in the declared coverage order over a person's balances at one bank); premium classes |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/insurer.rs` | premiums by risk class; the backstop's draw rule; the resolution levy |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/declare.rs` | the insurer kind; the backstop facility (treasury → insurer) on K-47; reasons `SUP.premium`, `SUP.resolution_levy`, `SUP.backstop_draw` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | quarterly premiums at 9c, paid at the next business day's 2c |
| `data/<country>/SUP.toml` | the insurance limit per person, coverage order, premium schedule by risk class, the backstop's limit and terms, the resolution levy (POLICY) |
| data series | `bank/deposit_insurance_2013` (coverage limits, coinsurance, backstops), `bank/typed_deposit_insurance_premiums_2003` (premium bases and rates), `bank/brss_2019` (payout, backstop) |

**Design**:
- **The insurer** (SUP.2): a party per country; its fund is its own money account at the central bank (K-47), never a
  pot apart. It covers each depositor per legal person (a person, a firm, any other party) up to the limit, over the
  person's balances at one bank in the declared coverage order (sight, then term); a joint account counts in its
  holders' shares (K-58, PTY.3). Coverage is computed only at a failure (S2.199, K-99's per-person split), never stored
  per account.
- **Premiums**: quarterly per bank by the risk class its ratios (S2.186) and funding facts (S2.180) put it in (POLICY
  schedule), issued at 9c as a demand, paid at the next business day's 2c (TIME.7); an unpaid premium is a fail with
  its contract's consequence.
- **Backstop**: a facility on the insurer's account (K-47's facility side row, BNK.18) granted by the treasury, limit
  POLICY; drawn when the fund is short at a payout (S2.199): a fiscal cost with a named payer.
- **The resolution fund**: the resolution authority's account, built by a levy on banks on the same calendar (POLICY);
  it pays no-creditor-worse-off compensation (S2.199).
- **BFL.14 completes**: the insurance limit (SUP's POLICY) joins the liquidity minimum and buffer appetite (S2.180).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a depositor with no balance at the failed bank has no cover to compute: `no_balance_no_cover`.
- E8: per-person sums in i64; a person holding at several banks is covered at each separately:
  `cover_per_bank_per_person`.
- E11: day zero: funds at their opening balances; the first premium on the first quarter's date:
  `first_premium_on_quarter`.
- E13: a country whose law declares no insurer: the insurer kind is absent and every deposit is uninsured (declared,
  visible): `no_insurer_all_uninsured`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `insured_split_by_person` (limit per person across sight and term in coverage order);
`joint_account_in_shares`; `premium_by_risk_class`; `backstop_drawn_only_when_short`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-42`: the insurance fund equals its opening balance plus premiums plus recoveries plus backstop
draws minus payouts; no insured payout to a person exceeded the limit.
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.deposit_premiums (quarter-ends): 0.07 core-ms; joins H (70 premium and levy demands × 1 µs)
- counters `phx_sup.premiums`, `phx_sup.levies`, `phx_sup.backstop_draws`
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.01 MB resident (three insurers × 3 KB, 35 banks × 1 B: premium class)
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +0 MB resident (three backstop facilities in side rows)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; insurance without a fund and a limit; cover stored per account; a fund that is not an account.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-42 registered
  (its fund identity checked every quarter; payouts from S2.199).
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.195 — Banks' safety as depositors see it, their choice of bank, and runs

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.9 PROCESS; BFL.12 MEASURE; BFL.13 FORBID; BFL.7 DECISION *(part: another bank, banknotes and bills)*
**Architecture**: §7.13 (public series), §7.16 (attention), §7.2 (declared sweeps), §6.1 (stages 5a, 5c, 7, 10a).
**Depends on**: S1.336 (K-92: a public series per (bank, method)); S1.213 (K-36: public events of withdrawals, queues
and failures); S1.215 (K-37: banks' published funding and capital figures); S1.171 (K-14: the declared sweep of
K-47's bank column on a surprise day); S1.227 (K-43: the next review redrawn); S1.350 (K-101: attention read from the
widened outlook); S1.348 (K-100); S1.240 (K-47: accounts opened and closed; product rates); S1.248 (K-49: the
transfer settles all or none); S1.432 (bills at auction); S2.177 (products and rates); S2.193 (the insurance limit);
S1.452, S1.451 (households' and firms' attention); S1.476 (the agency's money releases).
**Goal**: depositors move their money on what they can observe — the rates banks offer, what banks publish and the
public events of withdrawals, queues and failures at their bank and at banks like it — weighing the expected loss on
their uninsured balance and the cost of switching; withdrawals take reserves, which forces dearer funding and sales,
which is observable and prompts more withdrawals, so runs emerge and insurance removes the insured's reason to run.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-banking/src/decisions.rs` | decision point `bank_choice` (households for their persons' accounts, firms, institutions) |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/{safety,bank_choice}.rs` | the safety methods over published figures and events; the choice |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/declare.rs` | the public series `BFL.safety(bank)` and its methods; the similarity declaration (region, size class, business kind); event kinds `BFL.withdrawals`, `BFL.queue` (public by OBS.3's declared rule); the sweep `BFL.safety_wake`; the measures' series |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bfl.rs` | 5a series; the wake sweep; 5c choices; 7 transfers; 10a events |
| `data/<country>/BFL.toml` | switching cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY); taste distributions over banks (PREFERENCE); review cost |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | deposit choice with insured and uninsured balances and switching costs (Egan, Hortaçsu and Matvos, 2017; Klemperer, 1987); information contagion among banks alike (Chen, 1999; Acharya and Yorulmazer, 2008) |

**Design**:
- **Safety outlook** (a public series, K-92): per (bank, method) the chance a depositor puts on losing uninsured money
  there, formed once per method at 5a on days with a new input — the bank's published funding and capital figures (K-37,
  on its reporting dates) and public events (K-36) at the bank and at banks declared similar. No depositor's state is
  read (VAL.23).
- **Wake**: on a day a bank's series surprises (VAL.4), the declared sweep `BFL.safety_wake` (K-14) reads K-47's bank
  column once for every such bank, and for each holder found redraws the next review of `bank_choice` (K-43
  reschedule, O(1)) at the rate its attention rule reads from the series' widened outlook (K-101, REP.38), so reviews
  spread over days (REP.35), never all at once.
- **The choice** (lumpy; on review and wake): alternatives — keep; each bank in reach offering the holder's class a
  product; banknotes; bills at the next auction (S1.432). Value = the alternative's rate (K-47's product rate, S2.177)
  − the expected loss on the balance above the insured limit per person (S2.193) under the depositor's method's safety
  outlook − the switching cost in hours at its value of leisure (firms: its staff's hours) + a taste per alternative
  (REP.22, `BFL.bank_taste`); the best is taken. A switch is a transfer instruction settled at stage 7: an account
  opened at the new bank (K-47), the balance moved (reserves move, MON.5), the old account closed when empty; a failed
  transfer changes nothing (SET.4). Banknotes: a withdrawal to the holder's banknote account at the issuer.
- **Runs** (BFL.9) are not coded: withdrawals take reserves (S2.185), shortfall actions bring dearer funding and sales
  (S2.184), their publication and the events `BFL.withdrawals` and `BFL.queue` (produced at 10a from the day's state by
  OBS.3's declared rule) surprise the series and wake more depositors.
- **Measures** (BFL.12), published by the agency (S1.476's money releases): outflows by holder class (stickiness), the
  maturity gap (K-95), funding costs by bank, outflows by insured and uninsured balance, and after a failure by
  similarity to the failed bank.
- **BFL.13 completes**: products by holder class and term (S2.177), priced collateralised facilities (S2.185), and here
  every deposit able to leave. S3.187 adds money-fund units as an alternative.
- **Streams**: `BFL.bank_taste`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a failure day: the sweep runs once for all banks surprised that day; the holders' next reviews are redrawn and
  then spread: `wake_spreads_reviews`.
- E2: no bank in reach offers the class a product: keep, banknotes and bills remain: `no_bank_in_reach`.
- E6: next reviews saved (K-43); transfers pending at a save are commitments: K-50's `commitments_roundtrip`
  (S1.251).
- E10: a bank closed for resolution: switches from it wait with its other payments (pending, S2.196):
  `switch_from_closed_bank_pending`.
- E14: a switch and a payment from the same account the same day: settlement's payment order decides:
  `switch_and_payment_same_day`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `insured_depositor_weighs_only_uninsured`; `switch_value_with_cost_and_taste`;
`switch_only_on_settlement`; `similarity_event_moves_series`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-14`: BFL.12's measures published; `LC-2-37`: depositors' choices read only offered rates,
published figures and public events (Law 12, the read-trace); `LC-2-38`: when the run has a catastrophe in one bank's
region, its losses reach its statements, and every withdrawal that follows at it and at banks like it names the
review, the outlook it read and the insured and uninsured parts moved (not yet seen until the run has one).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.osearch: 1.5 / 0 / 1.5 core-ms (B / NB / H) (10 k reviews × 150 ns: the banks' safety is formed once per method at 5a, so a choice is a compare over the banks in reach)
- on fin.calendar.bank_run (a bank's safety series surprises; event): 34 core-ms; joins H and B′ (the sweep 9.75 M rows × 0.4 ns = 4, and 3 M next reviews redrawn × 10 ns = 30)
- spread after fin.calendar.bank_run over 10 days: 90 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.osearch (the woken holders' next reviews drawn at the attention rule's raised rate, mean 5 business days; the heaviest is the first day's 0.6 M reviews × 150 ns; the ≈ 86 % that land in these days, 2.6 M × 150 ns = 387 core-ms)
- then spread over the following days: 12 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.osearch for the ≈ 14 % that land later (day 11's 81 k reviews × 150 ns, falling by a fifth a day; 0.42 M × 150 ns = 63 core-ms in all, so the wake's 3 M reviews cost 450 core-ms)
- adds 50 k / 0 / 50 k items to fin.settle.flow_ns on the tail's heaviest day (switches)
- counters `phx_bfl.bank_choices`, `phx_bfl.switches`, `phx_bfl.safety_wakes`, `phx_bfl.wake_sweep_rows`
- +0 B (named slot bank_choice)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.02 MB resident (35 banks × methods × 16 B of K-92 entries)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a withdrawal rate; a depositor reading another's account or a bank's private state; a switch made
before its transfer settles; all depositors woken to review at once.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-14 and LC-2-37
  pass; LC-2-38 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.196 — Resolution opened: the bank closed, its book valued, the hole written down by layer

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BCP.8 FORBID; SUP.5 PROCESS *(part: trigger, closing, valuation and write-down)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (the resolution engine, the waterfall), §6.1 (stages 9c, 9e, 2b, 2f).
**Depends on**: S1.347 (K-99: trigger, closed fact, pending legs, valuation, write-down by layer); S1.345 (K-98: the
classes in order); S1.333 (K-90: D's statement); S1.335 (K-91: the authority's appointed valuers); S2.106 (the
loan-book valuer's method); S2.186 (the layers); S2.192 (the trigger); S2.185 (failure for liquidity); S1.353 (K-103:
the layers family).
**Goal**: a bank that failed for liquidity or that the supervisor finds below its point of non-viability is closed by
the resolution authority: its payments wait; the next day its book, taken from its statement, is valued by the valuers
the authority appoints, never by its own provisions, and the hole is written down through its layers in order —
equity, contingent capital, subordinated debt, then senior creditors as needed.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/resolution.rs` | the authority's declarations to K-99: valuers appointed, the valuation's inputs, the liquidation counterfactual, the layer order |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/audit.rs` | the layers family (no loss skips a layer) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | 9c trigger → 9e closing; D+1 2b valuation; 2f write-downs |
| `data/<country>/SUP.toml` | resolution tools and the valuers' appointment (POLICY) |

**Design**:
- **D, 9c → 9e**: on the trigger (S2.192) the authority opens a resolution on K-99: the bank's `closed` fact from 9e;
  from then K-49 holds every leg to or from its customers pending (their outgoing payments on their accounts, payments
  to them on the payer's side, excluded from the payer's funds); a closed bank makes no payment of its own. A bank that
  failed at stage 8 has its statement of D drawn that day (K-90).
- **D+1, 2b — valuation** (SUP.5): the book from D's statement; loans valued per (bank, book class, arrears stage)
  totals by the appointed loan-book valuer's method (S2.106, K-91) from prints — no loan row read, no provision or
  outlook of the bank's an input; other positions at their marks (K-86) or their named valuers. The hole = liabilities
  − the valued assets. The authority also values a liquidation (the valuer's liquidation method through K-98's
  waterfall) for the no-creditor-worse-off test (S2.199).
- **Write-down** (2f): the hole through the layers in K-98's declared order — equity (K-88), contingent capital
  converted or written down (from S3.139), subordinated debt, senior debt as needed — as named instructions.
- **Layers family** (BCP.8 completes): on each resolution the write-downs follow the order, checked from K-99's record
  (K-103); no capital pot (S2.186) and no exempt bank (S2.186, S2.192).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: two banks failing the same day, or one during another's D+1: independent resolutions on K-99, each its own
  timetable; an acquirer failing after a transfer is resolved in its turn: `resolutions_independent`.
- E6: a save between D and D+2 holds the closed fact, pending legs, valuation and invited bids: K-99's
  `resolution_roundtrip` (S1.347).
- E10: every reference to the closed bank resolves; nothing ends until the transfer settles (S2.199):
  `closed_bank_refs_resolve`.
- E12: a class with no print: the valuer's method labels it by its declared fallback (MKT.20: interpolated, with the
  age of its input), never a zero value: `unpriced_class_labelled`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `writedown_by_layer_order`; `hole_from_valuation_not_provisions`; `closed_bank_payments_pending`; the
edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-39` (first part): no loss skipped a layer; `LC-2-41`: every resolution ran on D, D+1 and D+2 at
the stages above (D+2, D+3 where its transfer failed once), and a closed bank made no payment of its own (not yet seen
until the run has a failure).
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.resolution_d1 (the business day after a bank's closing; event): 2 core-ms; joins H and B′ (valuation over 0.1 M class totals × 20 ns)
- counters `phx_sup.resolutions`, `phx_sup.writedowns`
- +0 B (core attribute): K-99's resolution state
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a failed bank's book valued by its own provisions or outlooks; a loss that skips a layer; a closed
bank that keeps paying.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-39 and LC-2-41
  registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.197 — The acquirer's bid for a failed bank

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.5 PROCESS *(part: an invited acquirer bids from its own value, or declines)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (the bilateral protocol), §6.1 (stage 5c on D+1).
**Depends on**: S1.317 (K-80: bids and declines); S1.348 (K-100); S2.196 (the valuation offered); S2.102 (each
bidder's own assessment, `loan_claim_value`); S2.189 (the capital the assets would consume).
**Goal**: an invited bank bids for a failed bank from its own value of what it would take — the loans under its own
assessment, less the insured deposits it would assume and the cost of the capital they consume — or declines.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-credit/src/decisions.rs` | decision point `bid_for_failed_bank` (the acquirer's; it values loans under the bidder's own assessment) and the message kinds `BidInvitation`, `Bid` |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/bid.rs` | the acquirer's bid |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bnk.rs` | D+1 5c: answers to invitations |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | first-price sealed bids from own valuation (Granja, Matvos and Seru, 2017) |

**Design**:
- **The bid** (each invited bank's own decision, office: its chief executive; occasion: a `BidInvitation`): its own
  value of the assets offered — each loan class's `loan_claim_value` under its own assessment (S2.102), other positions
  at their marks — less the insured deposits it would assume and the capital they consume (S2.189's charge × its
  required return), bid at that less its required return; or a decline (MKT.9). The review costs staff hours (Law 14).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: every invited bank declines: none bids; S2.198 takes the payout path: `all_decline`.
- E6: bids pending at a save are messages: K-45's `messages_roundtrip` (S1.237).
- E14: an invited bank that itself fails on D: its bid lapses at its closing: `bid_lapses_at_bidder_closing`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `bid_from_own_assessment`; `decline_when_value_below_required_return`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-110` (first part): every bid names its bidder's own valuation (not yet seen until the run has a
failure).
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.resolution_d1 (the business day after a bank's closing; event): 2 core-ms; joins H and B′ (35 bids × 50 µs, due at D+1's 5c by the timetable)
- counters `phx_bnk.bids`, `phx_bnk.bid_declines`
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB resident (35 bids inside K-45's count)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a bid from the failed bank's own provisions; an acquirer assigned rather than bidding.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`.

### S2.198 — Invitations, the insurer's paying bank, and the authority's least-cost choice

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.5 PROCESS *(part: acquirers invited and the authority's selection)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (the resolution engine), §6.1 (stages 9e, 5c, 6a).
**Depends on**: S1.347 (K-99: the sealed-bid and least-cost selection slots); S1.317 (K-80: invitations); S1.348
(K-100); S2.196 (the valuation); S2.197 (the bids); S2.186 (eligibility: capital after the purchase); S2.193 (the
insurer's payout cost, the reserve); S2.195 (the safety series the insurer reads).
**Goal**: the banks eligible to acquire a failed bank are invited; the insurer chooses the safest eligible bank to pay
insured deposits through; the resolution authority selects by its own least-cost rule — the highest bid at or above the
insurer's cost of paying out, or the payout path when none reaches it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-banking/src/resolution.rs` | decision point `choose_paying_bank` (the insurer's) |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/{insurer,resolution}.rs` | the paying-bank rule; the invitations; the least-cost rule declared to K-99 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | D 9e invitations; D+1 5c the insurer's choice; D+1 6a selection |
| `data/<country>/SUP.toml` | the least-cost rule and resolution tools (POLICY); review cost of the choice in hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the paying agent the safest eligible bank (FDIC, Resolutions Handbook, 2019) |

**Design**:
- **Invitations** (D, 9e): to every bank licensed in the country whose capital after the purchase would meet its
  requirements (S2.186's ratios on its books plus the offered assets and assumed deposits), as K-80 asks due at D+1's
  5c.
- **The paying bank** (the insurer, D+1 5c): among the eligible banks, the safest by its own method's reading of the
  public safety series (S2.195), ties by lot (`SUP.paying_bank_lot`).
- **Selection** (the authority, D+1 6a; POLICY, not a market form): reserve = the insurer's cost of paying the insured
  deposits out (S2.193's per-person split over the bank's accounts, from K-99); the highest bid at or above the reserve
  wins and pays its bid, ties by lot (`SUP.bid_lot`); with none, the payout path through the paying bank. The choice
  goes to S2.199's transfer.
- **Streams**: `SUP.bid_lot`, `SUP.paying_bank_lot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: two resolutions the same D+1: selections are separate; a bank bidding for both is judged eligible against its
  capital after each in the order of the failed banks' identity: `two_resolutions_same_day`.
- E2: no eligible bank, or every invited bank declines: the payout path; with no eligible paying bank either, insured
  depositors are paid into banknote accounts at the issuer by the insurer (MON.4), as the law's tools declare:
  `payout_without_paying_bank`.
- E6: invitations pending at a save are messages: K-45's `messages_roundtrip` (S1.237).

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `least_cost_reserve_selects_or_declines` (the highest bid at or above the reserve pays its bid, none
below it); `paying_bank_safest_ties_by_lot`; `eligibility_after_purchase`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-110` (second part): every resolution's invitations went only to eligible banks, and the
selection took the highest bid at or above the reserve, or the payout path (not yet seen until the run has a failure).
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.resolution_d1 (the business day after a bank's closing; event): 0.1 core-ms; joins H and B′ (35 invitations and one selection)
- counters `phx_sup.selections`, `phx_sup.payout_paths`
- +0 B (core attribute)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a selection off the declared rule; an ineligible bank invited.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-110 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.199 — The transfer: insured deposits to a successor, the rest to an estate, the insurer and compensation paid

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.5 PROCESS; SUP.6 PROCESS; SUP.8 FORBID; SUP.7 INVARIANT *(part: banks and the deposit insurer)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (the resolution engine, endings, estates), §7.9 (book moves), §6.1 (stages 7, 2b, 10c).
**Depends on**: S1.347 (K-99: the transfer instruction, the per-person split, the retry); S1.267 (K-57: book moves);
S1.245, S1.248 (K-48, K-49: the link group, all legs or none); S1.240 (K-47: accounts re-pointed and per-person sums);
S1.171 (K-14: the sweep of K-47's bank column for the failed bank's accounts); S1.343, S1.342 (K-97, K-96: the rest
of the bank ends into an estate); S1.345 (K-98: the uninsured depositors' claims in their class); S2.132, S2.133,
S2.136 (the insolvency law's classes, administration, the estate's end); S2.193 (fund, backstop, resolution fund);
S2.196 (valuation, liquidation counterfactual); S2.198 (the winner or the payout path); S2.177 (interest to date).
**Goal**: on D+1 the transfer settles as one instruction: the acquirer takes the assets it bid for and the insured
deposits, or the insurer's paying bank takes the insured deposits; the rest of every deposit is a claim on the estate;
the insurer pays what the estate cannot and becomes its creditor, drawing its backstop if short; a creditor worse off
than in a liquidation is compensated by a named payer. Nothing vanishes, and every payer is named.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/resolution.rs` | the transfer's composition declared to K-99; the no-creditor-worse-off test |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/audit.rs` | the resolution family (SUP.7's bank and insurer terms) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | D+1 7 transfer; D+2 2b retry or payout path; the estate at 2f |

**Design**:
- **The instruction** (D+1, stage 7; K-99 → one K-48 link group, SET.4): the loan books the acquirer bid for move by
  K-57 book moves; the bank's accounts are found by the declared sweep of K-47's bank column (K-14) and each person's
  balances split at the insured limit per person (K-99's per-person sums, S2.193's coverage order): the insured part and
  its pending payments move to the acquirer or the paying bank (the account re-pointed), the rest becomes a claim row on
  the estate in the uninsured depositors' class (K-98); pending payments beyond the insured part fail visibly against
  the claim (MON.5). Interest to D is credited before the split (S2.177). The consideration is a leg: the acquirer
  pays its bid; the estate or the insurer pays the insured deposits' difference.
- **The insurer** (SUP.6): pays what the estate cannot of the insured deposits, from its fund, drawing the treasury
  backstop (S2.193) when short — a fiscal cost with a payer — and holds a claim on the estate in its declared class.
- **Compensation**: a creditor class whose resolution outcome is below its liquidation outcome (S2.196's
  counterfactual) is paid the difference in the same instruction, from the resolution fund, or the treasury where the
  fund is short (SUP.5, SUP.8): named payers.
- **The rest** (D+1 2f after settlement): the bank ends (K-97) into an estate (K-96): its reserve account and what the
  transfer left pass to it; it sells the remaining loans (S2.107) and pays by the law's order (S2.132, S2.133), and ends
  when distributed (S2.136).
- **A failed transfer** (a leg its payer cannot fund at D+1's 7b): nothing moves; the bank stays closed; at D+2's 2b the
  authority takes the next bid at or above its reserve, or the payout path, and the transfer settles at D+2's 7;
  customers pay through their receiving bank from D+3.
- **Resolution family** (SUP.7, part): what the acquirer took, what the insurer paid, what the estate realised and what
  holders lost sum to the hole the valuation found — checked on the transfer and completed when the estate ends (K-103).
  S4.183 extends it to every resolution kind.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: the largest bank's rows re-pointed on the pool; two failures in one week resolve independently:
  `transfer_largest_bank` (a fixture of a few thousand rows asserting the split and the identity).
- E3: a depositor with nothing above the limit has no claim; one with no insured part only a claim:
  `insured_part_and_claim_split`.
- E4: an estate whose loans never sell stays open with its claims (K-96), counted: `LC-2-50`.
- E6: a save between D+1's 7b failure and D+2 resumes the retry: K-99's `resolution_roundtrip` (S1.347).
- E10: every contract, account, offer and message naming the bank resolves to the acquirer, the paying bank or the
  estate; a dangling reference after the pass is a Names finding: `LC-2-17`.
- E14: a customer's payment pending since D and the transfer the same stage: the pending payment follows its account:
  `pending_follows_account`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `resolution_identity` (the four parts sum to the hole); `no_creditor_worse_off_paid`;
`failed_transfer_takes_next_bid_or_payout`; `backstop_drawn_when_fund_short`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-16`: SUP.7 holds in every bank resolution; `LC-2-17`: SUP.8 — no failed bank's positions vanish;
every bail-out and every compensation names its payer (not yet seen until the run has a failure).
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.resolution_d1 (the business day after a bank's closing; event): 109 core-ms; joins H and B′ (for the largest bank: the sweep 9.75 M × 0.4 ns = 4, 3.5 M rows re-pointed × 20 ns = 70, the audit's identities of the parties touched 3.5 M × 10 ns = 35; the link group's legs are settlement's)
- the event's sum for fin.calendar.resolution_d1 across S2.196–S2.199: 113.1 core-ms
- counters `phx_sup.rows_transferred`, `phx_sup.transfers_failed`, `phx_sup.compensations`
- ledger line 20 (estates): +0 MB resident (the failed bank's estate and its claims, K-96 and K-98's rows, released as it distributes)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; positions vanishing; a bail-out without a payer; a part of the transfer settling without the rest;
insured cover stored per account.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-16 and LC-2-17
  registered, and LC-2-36, LC-2-39, LC-2-41, LC-2-42 applicable from here.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.200 — Banks founded and licensed

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.9 PROCESS *(part: banks)*
**Architecture**: §7.5 (parties begin), §6.1 (stages 5c, 3b).
**Depends on**: S1.490 (firm births: the founding occasion and path); S1.180 (K-21: the bank legal form with its
minimum capital); S1.348 (K-100); S1.240 (K-47: the capital subscribed from named accounts); S2.192 (the supervisor);
S2.186 (the requirements a new bank meets); S2.181 (deposit rates); S1.425 (loan rates and standards); S1.215 (K-37:
banks' published returns).
**Goal**: a founder — a person, a firm, a fund, or a group of them — founds a bank when its own value of the venture
beats the return it requires on the capital, subscribing the minimum capital from its own named accounts; the
supervisor licenses it by declared criteria, and the bank begins the next day. So the banking sector grows and changes
as banks are founded and fail.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-banking/src/decisions.rs` | decision point `found_bank` (the founder's) |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/licensing.rs` | the founder's value of a bank; the licence rule by declared criteria |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/declare.rs` | the bank venture declared among the ventures a founding occasion weighs |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | 5c founding and licence; the next day's 3b begin |
| `data/<country>/SUP.toml` | licensing criteria and minimum capital (POLICY); the review cost in hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| data series | `bank/brss_2019` (minimum entry capital, licensing criteria) |

**Design**:
- **The venture** (FRM.16's path, S1.490): on its founding occasion a founder (a person, a firm, a fund, or a group of
  them, E 46) weighs a bank among the ventures it can see: its value (VAL.8) of the bank from the spreads it can
  observe — loan rates (S1.425) against deposit rates (S2.181) and the published returns of banks (K-37) — against its
  required return on the minimum capital. It founds when the value beats it and its own named accounts hold the capital.
- **The licence** (the supervisor, 5c): criteria declared (capital subscribed at least the minimum, the founders not in
  procedure; POLICY); the capital moves from the founders' accounts at stage 7 as paid-in capital (ACC.4); the bank
  begins at the next day's stage 3 (K-31, K-32) with its accounts at the central bank and its products' rates set by
  its opening decisions (S2.181 as an opening decision of a new party). A refusal is a recorded outcome the founder
  sees.
- **Streams**: none (the founding occasion's own).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no founder sees value: no bank is founded; N2 counts foundings, a zero reported with the run's length:
  `LC-2-50`.
- E8: a new bank's identity is never a reused one (K-31): K-31's `ids_never_reused` (S1.194).
- E11: no founding on day zero: `no_founding_day_zero`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `founds_when_value_beats_required_return`; `licence_refused_below_minimum`;
`group_of_founders_subscribes_from_own_accounts`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-111`: every bank founded names its founders, the capital's paying accounts and its licence date;
bank foundings per year are reported (N2).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (100 founding occasions weigh the bank venture × 1 µs)
- counters `phx_sup.licences`, `phx_sup.licence_refusals`
- +0 B (core attribute)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a bank created without its founders' capital; a founding rate; a household as a founder.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-111 passes.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.201 — Macroprudential limits set by the supervisor

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SUP.10 DECISION; SUP.12 PRIMITIVE; SUP.11 MEASURE *(part: banks)*
**Architecture**: §7.3 (dated policy schedules), §7.14 (declared limits), §6.1 (stages 5c, 9d).
**Depends on**: S1.179 (K-20: each change a dated POLICY value with its announcement and effective day); S1.338 (K-93:
limits that bind lenders, binding an event); S1.336 (K-92: the supervisor's own outlook of published credit and
house-price series); S1.348 (K-100); S2.186 (the countercyclical buffer and sectoral weights enter the requirements);
S2.190 (declines when a cap binds); S2.143 (mortgage standards read the caps); S2.161 (house-price series); S1.476
(the money and credit releases).
**Goal**: the supervisor sets caps on loan-to-value and debt-to-income for new mortgages, a countercyclical capital
buffer and sectoral risk weights from its own outlook of credit and house prices, each change announced with the day it
takes effect; each binds lenders as a declared limit, and a lender that meets one refuses or reprices.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/macroprudential.rs` | the reaction rule over the supervisor's outlooks |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/declare.rs` | decision `SUP.macroprudential` (office: the supervisor's head; quarterly review; opening decision); the limits' declarations on K-93; SUP.11's published series |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sup.rs` | 5c review; 9d announcement records |
| `data/<country>/SUP.toml` | the macroprudential tools and their reaction schedules (POLICY: piecewise linear in the outlook, after the Basel Committee's guide, 2010); review cost |
| data series | `bank/bis_credit_gap` (the credit gap at the snapshot, the outlook's opening value, GEN.5) |

**Design**:
- **The rule** (quarterly; woken by a surprise in its series): from its own outlooks (K-92 methods) of the published
  credit-to-output gap and house-price growth, each tool's value by its declared reaction schedule (POLICY). Each change
  is a K-20 dated value with its announcement day (the decision) and effective day (declared lead), so lenders'
  announcement heuristics read it ahead (VAL.6).
- **Binding**: the caps are K-93 limits per lender on new mortgages (read by S2.143's standards and S2.190's
  declines); the countercyclical buffer adds to the requirement (S2.186); sectoral weights re-weigh book classes
  (S2.186). A binding is an event of the lender it bound (Law 6), counted.
- **SUP.12 completes**: supervisory rules (S2.192), licensing (S2.200), insurance limits and premiums (S2.193),
  resolution tools (S2.196, S2.198), macroprudential tools (here) — all POLICY with their owner.
- **Measures** (SUP.11, banks): failures and their clustering, each resolution's cost and who bore it, the insurance
  fund through the run, and bindings of each limit per quarter, published by the agency.

- E13: a country declaring no tool: the rule has nothing to set: `no_tools`.

the edge-case tests above.

a recorded event of the lender it bound; `LC-2-18`: SUP.11 (banks) published.
