### S2.202 — Power plants, storage, fuels, the grid and its system operator

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.1 STATE; ENE.2 STATE; ENE.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.10 (named units), §7.4 (networks and routes), §7.5 (parties), §6.1 (stages 3a, 4a).
**Depends on**: S1.284 (K-66: plants, storage and lines as named units); S1.187 (K-26: power lines as network
segments with capacity); S1.180 (K-21: the plant, storage and line kinds, the system operator's kind, the power
products); S1.183 (K-22: power as a special unit, MWh per (region, day, block)); S1.192 (K-30: the day's weather per
region); S1.235 (K-44: equipment failure on held units); S1.285 (K-67: the failed condition band); S2.129 (plant
failures and repairs by age); S2.157 (fuels as commodities of their grades, and their call); S1.447 (extraction);
S1.407 (institutions opened); S1.483 (the opening's firms, among them generators and grid owners).
**Goal**: electricity is produced by named plants — fuel-fired, hydro, nuclear, wind, solar — and held only by storage
plants; each plant has its technology, capacity, efficiency, fuel, ramp limit and running cost, and renewable output
follows the day's weather. Fuels are commodities like any other. Each country's grid is infrastructure — transmission
lines between regions with capacities, and distribution to consumers — owned by named parties and run by a named
system operator.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-energy/src/{plants,grid}.rs` | technologies as declared data; the power products per (region, day, block); the system operator's facts |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | plant, storage and line kinds (K-66 declared columns: technology, capacity, efficiency, fuel, ramp limit, running cost, availability source; storage: energy capacity, power, round-trip efficiency); the operator kind; the power segment mode |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/availability.rs` | a plant's available capacity from the day's weather × capacity, less units failed |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/storable.rs` | PC-42: a product declared not storable has no holding except on a unit kind declared as storage |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | technologies, efficiencies, ramp limits, running costs, line losses (TECHNOLOGY) |
| data series | `open/atb_electricity`, `open/typed_pcge2020_plants`, `open/typed_ene_assumptions` (technologies: heat rates, efficiencies, running costs, storage round trip, lifetimes) |

**Design**:
- **Plants** (ENE.1): named units (K-66) of generator firms, each row's kind-declared columns carrying its technology's
  data; the age class from its commissioning year (CAP.1). Available capacity each day = capacity × the day's weather
  factor for its technology (wind, sun, river level from K-30; 1 for dispatchable kinds) less units in the failed band
  (K-67, S2.129): a read at stage 4a, never stored.
- **Storage** (ENE.1): a named unit with energy capacity, power and round-trip efficiency; its state of charge is its
  holding of the power unit (K-60), the only holding of a non-storable product the declarations allow (PC-42).
- **Fuels** (ENE.3): coal, oil, gas, uranium are the commodities S2.157 declares (graded, their content per unit),
  extracted (S1.447), stored, carried by pipeline, ship or rail and traded like any good; a plant buys them as inputs
  through S1.444's input orders.
- **The grid** (ENE.2, GEO.4): per country, power lines are network segments (K-26, mode `power`) between regions, each
  a named unit with capacity (MW) and loss coefficient. Every line's owner is assigned by the opening's derivation from
  the data (S2.203); a line the derivation cannot assign an owner is refused at assembly (E12), never given one by
  default. Distribution to consumers is each region's node. A named **system operator** per
  country (an institution) runs the grid, balances it and settles imbalances (S2.210).
- **Streams**: none (failures on K-44's declared streams).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe destroying plants or lines: units lost (K-60/K-66 `lose_batch`), capacity falls; lines closed
  (K-26) for their repair days: `availability_after_loss`.
- E8: MWh and MW in i64 at the declared precision: `energy_units_boundary`.
- E12: a technology with no efficiency, a plant without a site cell, or a line without an owner refuses at assembly:
  `technology_absent_refused`, `line_without_owner_refused`.
- E13: a country with no hydro or no storage has none: `no_storage_country`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `availability_from_weather`; `storage_only_holding_of_power` (PC-42 refusal); the edge-case tests
above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-112`: every plant, storage unit and line has a named owner and every country a system operator;
no holding of power exists outside storage.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.real: 0.06 / 0.06 / 0.06 core-ms (B / NB / H) (availability, 3 k plants × 20 ns)
- counters `phx_ene.plants_available`, `phx_ene.lines_closed`
- ledger line 12 (physical units, cells, owner index): +0.2 MB resident (3.2 k named units × 72 B)
**Guards**: PC-42 (non-storable products held only on storage units).
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; electricity stored outside storage plants; a grid without an owner; an owner assigned by default;
availability drawn rather than read from the weather.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; PC-42 registered; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`;
  LC-2-112 passes.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.204 — The retail supply contract and the consumer's choice of supplier

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.6 DECISION *(part: retail suppliers selling at posted tariffs, fixed or variable, bearing the
difference, and each consumer's choice of supplier or of buying wholesale)*
**Architecture**: §7.9 (contract families), §7.11 (standing offers), §6.1 (stages 5c, 7a).
**Depends on**: S1.257 (K-53: the family `energy_supply`); S1.263 (K-55: tariff terms, billing period); S1.225 (K-42:
bills due); S1.296 (K-70: each supplier's posted tariff per (region, carrier, kind)); S1.348 (K-100); S1.350 (K-101:
the supplier-choice review); S2.202 (the power unit and the regions' nodes).
**Goal**: the retail supply contract exists as declared data — a contract between a consumer and a retail supplier per
carrier, billed each period at the supplier's posted tariff, fixed for the contract's term or variable, reset at each
period's start — with the consumer's rule for choosing its supplier, or, for a firm, buying wholesale. No row opens
until S2.207, where consumption begins with its billing.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | family `energy_supply` (consumer, supplier; terms: carrier, tariff kind, billing period; own due: next bill; own amount: the period's unit price); reason `ENE.bill`; decision `ENE.supplier_choice` (households, firms; need occasions: formation, a move, a founding; review; opening decision); the tariff market keys `ENE.retail(region, carrier, kind)` |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/{supplier_choice,bill}.rs` | the consumer's choice (a supplier by taste, or wholesale for a firm); the bill's amount |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/ene.rs` | 5c choices; bills streamed at 7a (routed from S2.207) |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | tariff kinds and billing periods (POLICY of each supplier's terms); taste distributions over suppliers (PREFERENCE); the cost in hours of switching and of participating in the wholesale market (TECHNOLOGY) |

**Design**:
- **The contract** (K-53, the energy-supply layout: ends, terms, own due, own amount, person chain): one per (consumer,
  carrier). Its interned terms (K-55) carry the tariff kind and the period's unit price: **fixed** (one price for the
  contract's term) or **variable** (at each bill the row is re-pointed to the terms of the supplier's tariff posted that
  day, so a period's price never changes within it — the declared term); the same terms carry the consumer's use
  coefficients (S2.207). The row's own amount holds its use accumulator (S2.207).
- **The bill** (a due on K-42 at each period's end, streamed at 7a like any due, from S2.207): amount = the period's
  unit price × the use realised over the period (S2.207), rounded once by the terms' convention; unpaid, it is arrears on the row (K-56) with the contract's consequences.
- **Choice** (households, firms; lumpy): on formation, a move, a founding, or a review: among the suppliers posting in
  its region, by value = −expected bill + taste (REP.22, `ENE.supplier_taste`), switching costing hours (Law 14); a firm
  may choose **wholesale** (buying at S2.209's call through S2.208's bids) when its expected saving beats the
  participation cost. A switch closes the old row at its period end and opens the new one.
- **Streams**: `ENE.supplier_taste`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no supplier posting in a region: consumers there cannot contract (MKT.10), an event:
  `no_supplier_failed_meeting`.
- E10: a supplier ending: its rows move to its estate or successor (K-97), and its consumers' next need occasion chooses
  anew: `supplier_end_moves_rows`.
- E14: a switch and a bill the same day: the old row bills its period, then closes: `switch_after_bill`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `bill_is_period_price_times_consumption`; `variable_price_fixed_within_period`;
`supplier_choice_with_taste_and_cost`; `firm_goes_wholesale_when_saving_beats_cost`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: none (LC-2-113 at S2.207, when rows open).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.household_reviews: 0.27 / 0 / 0.27 core-ms (B / NB / H) (from S2.207: 1.8 k households' supplier choices × 150 ns, a compare over the suppliers posting in the region)
- adds 0.2 k / 0 / 0.2 k items to fin.decide.attend_ns (from S2.207: the firms' own supplier choices, a supplier or wholesale, taken at their attention)
- counters `phx_ene.supplier_choices`, `phx_ene.switches`
- +0 B (named slot supplier_choice)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a price that changes inside a period; a supply row opened before consumption is billed.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.207 — Supply begins: energy as an input in every way that uses it, and a household good driven by the weather

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.4 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.10 (standing rates), §7.14 (exact linear aggregates), §6.1 (stages 3a, 4a, 7a).
**Depends on**: S1.263 (K-55: the use coefficients by (composition, dwelling class) in the row's interned terms);
S1.257 (K-53: the row's own amount as the use accumulator); S1.289 (K-68: a firm's production realised, which carries
its energy use); S1.192 (K-30: degree-days per region per day, with their running sum); S1.341 (K-95: Σ rates per (supplier, region, carrier)); S1.441, S1.443
(ways and production: power inputs in physical units); S1.448 (household spending: the expected bill as an outlay);
S1.444 (input orders, whose `GDS.energy_as_goods` this retires); S2.204 (the supply rows, their bills and the choice);
S2.205 (tariffs); S2.206 (access at the opening); S2.202 (the power unit).
**Goal**: supply rows open — at the opening for every household and firm with access, by each consumer's day-zero
choice, and thereafter on its need occasions — and consumption begins with its billing: every way that uses energy
consumes it in physical units, and households consume it as a good whose need rises with heating and cooling
degree-days; the weather moves demand without visiting any household, and the consumption billed and balanced is
exactly the sum of each consumer's own.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/use.rs` | a household's use coefficients from its composition and dwelling class; the accumulator's update at a change; a firm's use from its production realised |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | the use coefficients' terms (by composition class, dwelling class, carrier); the K-95 sums per (supplier, region, carrier); the opening's supply rows |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/declare.rs` | energy carriers no longer bought at stalls (`GDS.energy_as_goods` retired in its own crate) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/ene.rs` | bills at 7a; kinks at 4a |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | energy need per degree-day and base use by household composition and dwelling class (TECHNOLOGY of living) |
| data series | `households/recs2020` (use by degree-days, dwelling type and composition) |

**Design**:
- **Rows open**: at the opening each household and firm with access (S2.206) holds a supply row with the supplier it
  chooses on day zero (S2.204's opening decision, GEN.13), not drawn; thereafter rows open on the choice's need
  occasions.
- **Households**: a household's use of each carrier is base use + need per heating and cooling degree-day, by its
  composition and dwelling class (TECHNOLOGY of living): these coefficients are the row's interned terms (K-55), shared
  by every household of the same classes. Use to date is `r · D(t) + s`, where D is the region's running sum of
  degree-days (K-30) and `s` is the row's own amount: at a change of classes on day t (a birth, death or move, a change
  of dwelling) the row is re-pointed to the new terms and `s −= Δr · D(t)` (Abel summation, exact); at the bill,
  use = `r · D(c) + s`, then `s ← −r · D(c)`. The day's weather changes nothing stored, and no anchor day is kept. Its
  spending rule (S1.448) reads the expected bill as a committed outlay.
- **Firms** (TEC.2): a way's power input per unit of output; the firm's use is realised with its production (K-68's
  realisation adds units × input to the row's own amount), never by a daily visit.
- **Sums**: each rate change updates K-95's Σ per (supplier, region, carrier), so a region's day's demand is Σ
  coefficient × the day's degree-days (Law 11: the exact sum of each consumer's own, re-ordered).
- **Bills**: from here S2.204's bills stream at 7a.
- **Retired**: `GDS.energy_as_goods`.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a heat wave or cold snap: nothing visited; demand per region is a read: `weather_moves_no_row`.
- E3: a household without access holds no row and consumes no grid power (recorded, declared): `no_access_no_row`.
- E5: bills cluster on billing days: rows billed on each row's own billing day as its terms declare:
  `bills_on_own_day`.
- E6: rows, their terms and own amounts, and the sums saved: K-53's `contracts_roundtrip` (S1.257), K-55's
  `terms_roundtrip` (S1.263).
- E11: day zero: rates from the opening composition and dwellings; realisation from the first day: `use_day_zero`.
- E14: a move and a birth the same day: one re-derivation from the day's end state (realise, then apply):
  `same_day_kinks_commute`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `use_over_period_from_cumulative_degree_days`; `sum_of_rates_equals_sum_of_uses`; `firm_use_from_lines`;
the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-113`: every consumer with access has a supply row or buys wholesale, and every bill equals its
period's price × its consumption realised; `LC-2-114`: for a rolling slice of consumers, the billed consumption equals
rate × degree-days over the period recounted from K-30's series.
**Budget**:
- adds 2 phone-ns to fin.dues.item_ns at 0.24 M / 0 / 1.65 M items (the bills are the design point's energy dues, inside its 3.0 M / 0 / 22.5 M: each row bills on its supplier's declared cycle day, a third of the rows on month-end cycles, so 1.65 M on H and the rest spread over the month's business days; the 2 ns read the use accumulator)
- its share of fin.fixed.kinks: 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H) (10 k households' class changes × 20 ns: terms re-pointed, accumulator written)
- adds 2 phone-ns to fin.batches.prod_ns at 0.4 M / 0.1 M / 0.4 M items (a firm's use added to its row with its production realised)
- counters `phx_ene.bills`, `phx_ene.use_changes`
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (terms and own amount): 4.95 M energy-supply rows inside the contracts mix
- ledger line 10 (terms): +1.4 MB resident (57 k supply terms × 24 B: suppliers × tariff kinds × carriers × composition and dwelling classes)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.01 MB resident (K-95 sums, 25 regions × carriers × suppliers)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a household visited because the weather changed; demand at a representative household;
consumption without its bill.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-113 and LC-2-114
  pass.
- [ ] `GDS.energy_as_goods` gone; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.208 — Generators' offers, storage, and demand bids for the next day

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.5 DECISION *(part: offers from running costs and the fuel outlook)*; ENE.6 DECISION *(part:
suppliers' and large consumers' wholesale bids)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (standing offers), §6.1 (stage 5b, every day).
**Depends on**: S1.296 (K-70: orders per (grid, region node, day, block)); S1.348 (K-100: continuous decisions); S1.453
(the firm's own outlooks: fuel and power prices, degree-days); S2.202 (availability, running costs, ramps, storage);
S2.207 (suppliers' Σ rates); S2.204 (wholesale buyers); S2.157 (fuel prices formed at the commodity call).
**Goal**: every day, for delivery the next day, each generator offers its available capacity per block at its own
avoidable cost — below zero where stopping costs more — storage buys where it expects cheap and sells where dear, and
suppliers and large consumers bid their expected needs up to their value.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-energy/src/decisions.rs` | decision points `offer_power`, `bid_power`, `store` |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/{offer,bid,storage}.rs` | the three rules |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/ene.rs` | 5b every day (TIME.8), orders posted at 5d |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | blocks, offer steps, minimum stable output, start costs, subsidies (POLICY, TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | offers at own avoidable cost (Wolak, 2000; Green and Newbery, 1992); storage arbitrage (Sioshansi, Denholm, Jenkin and Weiss, 2009) |

**Design**:
- **Offers** (generators, per plant and block): a step curve at the plant's avoidable cost — its own fuel-price outlook
  × heat rate plus variable costs — in ramp-feasible quantities of its available capacity; an inflexible plant offers the
  output it cannot stop at minus its stopping and restarting cost; a subsidised plant at minus its subsidy.
- **Storage**: buys in the blocks where its own outlook of the price is below its outlook of a dearer block's price net
  of round-trip losses, and offers what it holds where above, within its power and energy capacity.
- **Bids**: a retail supplier bids its outlook of its customers' consumption for each block (its degree-day outlook ×
  its Σ rates, S2.207), price-taking up to its value of serving (its tariff less its other costs); a large consumer bids
  its production's need up to the energy's value in use.
- All orders are K-70 standing orders keyed (country grid, region node, day, block), posted at 5d, every day including
  non-business days (TIME.8). S4.122's power contracts add contract positions to a generator's revenue without
  changing its offer rule.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no offers in a block: the call clears nothing and demand is shed (S2.211): `no_offers_clears_nothing`.
- E5: a non-business day runs these (TIME.8); orders are about constant in count every day: `offers_on_nb_day`.
- E11: day zero posts the first day's orders (opening decision): `offers_day_zero`.
- E12: no fuel price yet formed: the outlook's opening value (GEN.5), never zero: `fuel_outlook_opening`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `offer_at_avoidable_cost`; `negative_offer_when_inflexible`; `storage_buys_low_sells_high_net_of_losses`;
`supplier_bid_from_degree_day_outlook`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-115`: every offer step names its plant's avoidable cost at the outlook it read.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 9 / 9 / 9 core-ms (B / NB / H) (30 k orders × 300 ns, every day)
- counters `phx_ene.offers`, `phx_ene.bids`
- ledger line 17 (markets): +1.2 MB resident (30 k standing orders × 40 B)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an offer at a formula price; a bid for power held outside storage.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-115 passes.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.209 — The wholesale market: one call a day per grid

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.8 PROCESS; ENE.12 MEASURE
**Architecture**: §7.11 (the network call, prints), §6.1 (stage 6a every day; 6d).
**Depends on**: S1.314 (K-77: surplus maximised as a min-cost flow, transport model, integer lots, warm start from
yesterday's basis; `fin.call.network_ms`); S1.326 (K-86: prints per (region, day, block)); S1.245 (K-48: trades as
flows, committed on NB days); S1.251 (K-50: commitments to the next business day); S2.202 (lines' capacities); S2.208
(orders); S1.475 (the agency's price releases, for ENE.12).
**Goal**: the wholesale market meets every day, for delivery the next day, as one call across all regions of each
country's grid in declared blocks: surplus over the offer and bid steps is maximised subject to each line carrying at
most its capacity between the two regions it joins; each region's price is its node's; unconstrained regions share a
price, a congested line separates two; the price is negative when output that cannot stop exceeds demand.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | the market `ENE.day_ahead` (form: network call; meets every day; settlement convention: next business day on NB; participants; tick grid; blocks as commodities of one call); ENE.12's published series |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/ene.rs` | 6a the call per country; 6b prints; 6d positions and flows |

**Design**:
- **The call** (6a, every day): one K-77 call per country, warm-started from yesterday's basis, over the day's orders;
  the declared blocks are separate commodities of the one call (each block's lines carry up to their capacity in that
  block), nodes are regions and arcs the power lines (a transport model, §12's owner answer), integer lots on the tick
  grid, ties by `ENE.clear_lot`; each (region, block)'s price is its node's potential. Line losses are not in the call:
  the operator buys them at delivery (S2.210).
- **Results**: each participant's position per (region, day, block) and its money leg (K-48, reason `ENE.trade`); on a
  non-business day committed to pending and settled on the next business day (TIME.8, K-50). Prints per (region, day,
  block) with volume (K-86).
- **Measures** (ENE.12): spare capacity against price per block and region; renewable output against price level and
  volatility; fuel and power prices against producer and consumer prices through a shock — published by the agency on
  its calendar (S1.475's releases carry the power prices).
- **Streams**: `ENE.clear_lot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no overlap in a block: no trade, a failed meeting (MKT.10); demand unmet goes to S2.210's balancing and S2.211:
  `no_overlap_failed_meeting`.
- E5: every day's call is the same size (3 countries); NB trades are commitments: `nb_trades_committed`.
- E7: the call's result identical for any worker count (K-77's determinism; lots by address): K-77's
  `call_workers_equal` (S1.314).
- E8: prices on the tick grid in i64; negative prices allowed (Law 6): `negative_price_when_inflexible_exceeds_demand`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `one_price_per_unconstrained_region`; `congested_line_separates_prices`;
`blocks_independent_in_one_call`; `call_matches_brute_force_small`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-20`: ENE.12's measures published; `LC-2-45`: when the run has a fuel-output event (depletion,
failure or catastrophe), the event is dated and named, every plant's offer after it reads the fuel outlook it moved,
producers' price reviews name their energy share, and fuel, power, producer and consumer prices are published through
it (not yet seen until the run has one).
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 9 / 9 / 9 core-ms (B / NB / H) (3 calls a day × 3 ms VM warm-started, S1.314's `fin.call.network_ms`)
- adds 3 k / 0 / 3 k items to fin.settle.flow_ns (trades)
- adds 0 / 3 k / 0 items to fin.ledger.pending_ns (NB trades committed)
- on B′ the closed days' committed trades settle: adds 12 k items to fin.settle.flow_ns (0.3 core-ms)
- counters `phx_ene.calls`, `phx_ene.congested_lines`, `phx_ene.trades`
- ledger line 17 (markets): +1.2 MB resident (25 regions × 2 blocks × 730 days × 32 B of prints)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an energy price from a path or formula; a line carrying more than its capacity; a cold start each
day.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-20 passes; LC-2-45
  registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.210 — Delivery, balancing, losses and imbalances

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.10 PROCESS; ENE.11 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: §7.10 (standing rates, named units), §7.17 (audit families), §6.1 (stages 4a, 7).
**Depends on**: S2.209 (positions); S2.202 (availability, lines, losses); S2.207 (actual consumption per region);
S2.208 (the day-ahead steps standing as balancing offers); S2.205 (the network charge joins the suppliers' unit cost);
S1.245 (K-48: imbalance, balancing and network-charge flows; physical legs of production, SET.9); S1.248 (K-49);
S1.353 (K-103: the balance family); S1.192 (K-30: the day's weather, stage 3a).
**Goal**: on the delivery day plants produce their accepted quantities as their availability allows; the system
operator balances the differences in merit order and buys the lines' losses, paying from network charges its
customers pay per unit taken; each party whose delivery or take differs from its position settles the difference at
the day's imbalance price; per region and day, produced plus imported equals consumed plus exported plus lost plus
stored, and no line carries more than its capacity.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/dispatch.rs` | the operator's balancing in merit order; losses per line and flow; the imbalance price |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/audit.rs` | the ENE.11 family |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | reasons `ENE.imbalance`, `ENE.balancing`, `ENE.network_charge` (a declared cost line of suppliers' unit cost); the day's dispatch record kind |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/ene.rs` | 4a dispatch after 3a's weather; 7 flows |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | imbalance pricing, balancing market design, network charges per unit taken (POLICY); loss per line and flow (TECHNOLOGY) |
| data series | `wb/EG.ELC.LOSS.ZS` (the loss coefficient per unit of line length, a declared derivation from each country's transmission and distribution loss share, its procedure in `SHAPES.toml`; because the coefficient comes from it, the loss share is never a gate read or a realism credit, GEN.10, N7) |

**Design**:
- **Dispatch** (4a, every day): each plant produces min(accepted, available today); production is a physical
  transformation — fuel consumed from the plant's holding, power produced (SET.9) — and consumption is S2.207's day
  amount per region. The operator balances each region's difference by calling remaining offer steps up or accepted
  steps down in merit order (the day-ahead steps stand as balancing offers, POLICY), and buys the lines' losses
  (TECHNOLOGY per line and flow) the same way; the flows over lines are the call's plus balancing's, each within
  capacity.
- **Money** (settled at 7; on NB committed): balancing purchases and sales at their steps' prices; each party's
  imbalance (delivered or taken − position) at the day's imbalance price (the marginal balancing step, POLICY); network
  charges per unit taken paid by suppliers and wholesale buyers to the operator — the operator's costs of losses and
  balancing are paid from them (named payers).
- **ENE.11 family** (K-103): per region and day, produced + imported = consumed + exported + lost + stored, from the
  dispatch record; no line's flow above its capacity; a difference is a finding with its size.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe on 3a takes plants or lines out: availability falls before dispatch; what balancing cannot meet is
  shed (S2.211): `dispatch_after_outage`.
- E2: no balancing step available: the shortfall goes to S2.211: `no_balancing_step_sheds`.
- E5: every day; NB money committed to pending: `nb_imbalance_committed`.
- E14: a plant failing and its imbalance the same day: imbalance at the day's price: `failure_and_imbalance_same_day`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `losses_bought_at_balancing`; `imbalance_at_marginal_step`; `balance_identity_per_region`;
`network_charges_pay_operator_costs`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-19`: ENE.11 — per region and day the balance holds and no line is over capacity; `LC-2-44`
(first part): every imbalance is settled with the operator, and the operator's purchases of losses and balancing are
paid from network charges with named payers.
**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.real: 1 / 1 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (3 k plants, 25 regions, 200 lines)
- adds 5 k / 0 / 5 k items to fin.settle.flow_ns (imbalance, balancing and network-charge flows)
- adds 0 / 5 k / 0 items to fin.ledger.pending_ns (NB flows committed)
- on B′ the closed days' committed flows settle: adds 20 k items to fin.settle.flow_ns (0.5 core-ms)
- counters `phx_ene.dispatched`, `phx_ene.imbalances`, `phx_ene.losses_bought`
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.1 MB resident (the day's dispatch record per region in K-38)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an imbalance left unsettled; losses without a payer; a line above its capacity.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-19 and LC-2-44
  (first part) pass.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.211 — Load shedding with named losers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.9 PROCESS; ENE.13 FORBID
**Architecture**: §7.2 (declared sweeps), §7.1 (day buffers and the sum-tree), §7.9 (contract rows), §6.1 (stage 4a).
**Depends on**: S1.171 (K-14: the declared sweep of the supply rows' region column on a shedding day); S1.160 (K-03: the
day buffer holding the region's cumulative use by class); S1.164 (K-05: the draw, built for the event and released at
the close); S1.257 (K-53: a shed household's day taken out of its row's use accumulator); S1.289 (K-68: a shed
firm's production lost that day); S1.213 (K-36: the shedding event with its subjects);
S2.210 (the shortfall after balancing); S2.207 (the day's use per consumer); S2.204 (the supply rows); S1.443 (a
firm's production for the day, lost where it needed the power).
**Goal**: when a region's supply with imports cannot meet its demand after balancing, the system operator sheds load by
the country's declared priorities, and within a class by lot; the consumers cut off are named, the output that needed
the power is lost that day as a dated event, and nobody pays for energy not delivered.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/shed.rs` | the order of classes and the draw within a class up to the shortfall |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | the sweep `ENE.shed_sweep` (reason: a shortfall; over `energy_supply`'s region column); event kind `ENE.shed` (public) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/ene.rs` | 4a after balancing; kinks for the shed day |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | load-shedding priorities by consumer class (POLICY) |

**Design**:
- **When**: after S2.210's balancing, a region whose supply with imports falls short of its demand by Δ. On such a day
  only, the declared sweep `ENE.shed_sweep` (K-14) reads the supply rows' region column once and builds, in a day buffer
  (K-03), the region's consumers by priority class with their use today; nothing is resident on any other day.
- **Who**: classes in the country's declared priority order (POLICY: e.g. firms of declared industries before
  households, hospitals last); within the class reached, consumers drawn by lot (`ENE.shed_lot`) from a K-05 tree built
  over that buffer for the event, until the drawn use covers Δ; the last drawn in whole (a consumer is supplied or not).
- **Consequences**: each shed consumer's use that day is zero — a household's day is taken out of its row's use
  accumulator (`s −= r · dd(t)`, one write), so the bill counts only supplied days and no payment runs without its energy
  leg; a firm's production that needed the power is lost that day (its production kink, units named in the event, and
  with it the use it would have carried); a household's energy consumption goes without, recorded as its
  shortfall (HH.4). One public event `ENE.shed` per region and day names every consumer cut off, the cause (the
  shortfall and the plants or lines out) and the date.
- **ENE.13 completes**: no power stored outside storage (PC-42, S2.202); no energy price from a path or formula (the
  call, S2.209); no grid without an owner (S2.202); no outage without a named cause — plant and line failures are
  hazard events (K-44) and sheds are named here.
- **Streams**: `ENE.shed_lot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe shedding a whole region: the draw takes classes whole in order: `shed_whole_classes_in_order`.
- E2: nothing to shed in a class: the next class: `empty_class_next`.
- E5: the sweep's buffer is sized by the first shedding day and kept (K-03): K-03's `buffer_kept_after_heavy_day`
  (S1.160).
- E6: the day's accumulator writes and kinks are saved with their rows; the buffer and tree are not saved (released at
  the close): K-53's `contracts_roundtrip` (S1.257).
- E14: a consumer shed and moving the same day: realise, then apply: `shed_and_move_same_day`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `shed_by_priority_then_lot_names_losers`; `shed_consumer_not_billed`; `production_lost_that_day`; the
edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-44` (second part): every shed load names its consumers, its dated loss and its cause.
**Budget**:
- on fin.calendar.shed (a region's shortfall after balancing; event): 12 core-ms; joins H and B′, and NB since electricity runs every day (the sweep 4.95 M × 1 ns = 5, the tree and draws 1, accumulator writes and kinks 0.1 M × 50 ns = 6)
- counters `phx_ene.shed_days`, `phx_ene.shed_consumers`, `phx_ene.shed_mwh`
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +0 MB resident (a 4a buffer of the region's consumers, 6 MB at the shed day's peak, below the line's 6a peak)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a resident index of consumers by region; an outage without a named cause; a shed consumer billed; a
share of consumers cut instead of named ones.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-44 (second part)
  registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S2.212 — Investment in plants, storage and lines

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: ENE.7 DECISION; ENE.14 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.10 (processes, named units), §6.1 (stage 5c).
**Depends on**: S1.458 (investment on its occasion, CAP.3's form); S2.131 (investment at the cost of money, hurdles,
staged projects); S1.459 (projects bought from named producers, paid in stages); S1.287 (K-69: a project in progress);
S1.284 (K-66: the completed unit); S2.202 (technologies, lines); S2.209 (the prices the investor's outlooks read);
S1.179 (K-20: energy policy as dated POLICY).
**Goal**: a generator firm builds a plant or storage, and a grid owner a line, when its own value of it beats what the
money costs it, under the country's energy policy; the new unit enters service when its project completes.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/invest.rs` | the project's value for a plant or storage (its own price outlooks by block and region, its availability, its running costs) and for a line (the regulated return on its capacity) |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/declare.rs` | energy projects declared among the investment options S1.458 weighs; energy policy's terms (subsidies, regulated returns) |
| `data/<country>/ENE.toml` | energy policy: subsidies by technology, the regulated return on lines (POLICY); construction lengths and costs (TECHNOLOGY) |
| data series | `open/typed_pcge2020_lcoe`, `open/atb_electricity` (investment costs by technology), `open/typed_ene_assumptions` (construction lengths, lifetimes) |

**Design**:
- **Plants and storage** (ENE.7): on the firm's investment occasion (S1.458), a candidate plant of each technology its
  kind declares is valued by VAL.8 — its expected output by block at its own price outlooks over its life, less running
  costs, plus the policy's subsidy — against its marginal cost of money (S2.131, CAP.3), by at least its hurdle; the
  best that beats it and can be funded starts a project (S1.459) paid in stages.
- **Lines**: a grid owner values a line between two regions at the regulated return on its capacity (POLICY) against
  its cost of money, on the same occasion.
- **Completion**: the project completes (K-69) and the unit enters service (K-66) with its site, capacity and age
  class; its first offer is the next day's (S2.208). S4.122's power contracts enter the investor's revenue outlook.
- **ENE.14 completes**: technologies and ramps (S2.202), climate (K-30's ENDOWMENT), market design (S2.209, S2.210),
  shedding rules (S2.211), energy policy (here), the opening fleet and grid (S2.202).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no candidate beats the hurdle: no plant is built; N2 reports investment counts: `LC-2-116`.
- E10: an investor ending mid-project: the project passes to its estate at cost (K-69): K-69's
  `process_passes_to_estate` (S1.287).
- E11: no investment decided on day zero beyond the opening's projects in progress: `invest_not_on_day_zero`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: `plant_value_from_block_outlooks_and_subsidy`; `line_at_regulated_return`; the edge-case tests above.
**Live checks**: `LC-2-116`: every plant, storage unit and line built names its investor, its valuation at the decision
and its project's stages.
**Budget**:
- adds 12000 phone-ns to fin.decide.visit_ns at 5 / 0 / 5 items (investment occasions of generator and grid firms, 6 candidates × 2 µs each)
- counters `phx_ene.projects_started`, `phx_ene.units_commissioned`
- +0 B (core attribute)
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; capacity added by a rule instead of an investor's project; a plant without a project.
**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks clean; the bench's 20-day run within `perf/budget.toml`; LC-2-116 passes.

### S2.213 — Collective bargaining, unions and strikes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: LAB.10 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §7.9 (contract families and shared terms), §7.11 (the bilateral protocol), §6.1 (stages 5c, 4a, 7).
**Depends on**: S1.180 (K-21: the union kind with its leader's office); S1.257 (K-53: the collective-agreement family
between a union and an employer or an employers' association); S1.263 (K-55: covered employment contracts share the
agreement's wage terms, REP.3); S1.317 (K-80: offers and counters across days); S1.348 (K-100); S1.253 (K-51: union
dues withheld at payroll for members); S1.416 (pay rounds: covered contracts take the agreement's wage); S1.443
(production: covered lines stop during a strike); S1.265 (K-56: a covered row's status during a strike); S2.108 (the
employer's filed accounts, public); S1.475 (the price and wage releases).
**Goal**: where a union represents workers of an occupation at an employer or an industry, wage terms are negotiated
between named parties and bind the contracts they cover until the next round; a strike is a real stoppage with real
losses on both sides.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/declare.rs` | the union kind (a party with its accounts and its leader's office); the agreement family (union, employer or association; coverage: occupation × employer or industry; term); the member flag on employment rows; reasons `LAB.union_dues`, `LAB.strike_pay`; decisions `LAB.bargain` (union and employer), `LAB.strike` (union) |
| `crates/systems/sys-lab/src/rules/bargain.rs` | offers and counters; acceptance; the strike decision |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/lab.rs` | 5c rounds, 4a stoppage kinks, 7 dues and strike pay |
| `data/<country>/LAB.toml` | bargaining rounds' calendar and coverage rules (POLICY of labour law); impatience and strike costs (PREFERENCE of the parties) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | alternating offers (Rubinstein, 1982), with source |

**Design**:
- **Parties**: unions are parties with accounts, dues from members withheld at payroll (a declared levy on employment
  rows whose member flag is set, K-51) and a leader's office (PTY.16; empty until S5.144 fills offices, founding
  preferences meanwhile). A new hire into a covered occupation at a covered employer is covered.
- **The agreement**: a K-53 row between the union and the employer (or the employers' association for an industry
  agreement); covered employment contracts point to its wage terms (K-55 shared terms), so one agreement reprices them
  all at its effective date (LAB.9: existing wages change only at renegotiation); it binds until its term ends.
- **Bargaining** (a round opens on the agreement's end date, K-42): alternating offers across business days through
  K-80 (TIME.7: an answer is due no earlier than the next business day). The union's offer reads its own outlooks of
  prices and wages (published series) and the employer's public filed results (S2.108); the employer's counter reads its
  own state (unit cost, sales outlook). Each side accepts when the offer beats its value of continuing, with its declared
  impatience (PREFERENCE).
- **Strike** (the union's decision at a rejected offer): when its value of striking — the expected gain in the
  settlement less members' lost wages over the expected length, net of strike pay — beats accepting. During a strike,
  covered contracts' wage dues are suspended (status on the row, K-56), covered lines' production rates are zero (K-68
  kinks: output lost), strike pay flows from the union to members; the strike ends when an offer is accepted. Both

**Status**: planned

**Architecture**: §7.6 (statistics accumulators, records), §6.1 (stages 9d, 10d).

paid); S2.102 (banks' income lines); S1.423 (agencies' staff and appropriations).
**Goal**: each statistics agency publishes quarterly national accounts on its calendar beside the monthly ones; the
income measure includes the financial sector's value added — banks' services charged through the margin between their
lending and deposit rates — and the government's, its staff's pay and the wear of its capital; and income is read from
the accounts firms file as they are published.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sta/src/national_accounts.rs` | the quarterly release; the financial sector's service output (the interest margin on loans and deposits over a declared reference rate, allocated to the users of the services); the government's output at cost |

  deposits, from their interest lines (K-87) and the reference rate the agency declares; allocated to users by their
  balances' shares — the convention stated (SNA's measure of financial intermediation services).
- **Government**: output at cost — compensation of its staff and consumption of its fixed capital (K-67's wear).

- E13: a country without a release day in a month: none that month: `no_release_day`.

## 6. Stage 3 — Money and capital markets

### Money markets, the central bank, sovereign and corporate debt (S3.100–S3.144)

**Exit** (spec Part O): the policy rate reaches loan rates, asset prices and investment through markets; a margin
spiral and a fund run can happen. The gate is S3.219.

This half builds, on the core's bases, the money market and repo (MMK), the central bank in full but for its asset
purchases (CB), the treasury's funding and the sovereign's debt (TRS, SOV) and corporate and bank debt (CRD, BNK.3).
Equity, dealers, funds, non-bank lenders, indices, ratings and the gate follow (S3.145–S3.219).
The mechanisms (S3.101–S3.141) run first on Stage 1's opening — bills only, no bond line, no corporate debt, no
agreement — and the three data steps that close the half (S3.142–S3.144) open the sovereign's bond lines, firms' and
banks' debt and the money market's positions from the data in hand.

**Conventions every step of the stage follows** (§2.21, §2.22):
- **Orders are schedules from values** (MKT.9, MKT.16). A financial order is its poster's schedule: the investor
  schedule (K-105, S1.357, a pure `phx-val` kernel) at the poster's own value (VAL.8, done
  arithmetic) unless the step names another form. Every limit is the poster's own; nobody posts "at market".
- **A bank's claims are valued through `sys-bnk`** (PC-40): every value a bank puts on a claim — an interbank or repo
  counterparty, a bill or bond it bids for, paper it underwrites, a syndicate share, an exchange offer — is read
  through the rule handle `loan_claim_value` (its one assessment of the obligor, Stage 2). A rule another system
  registers for the bank's decision reads that handle; it never values the claim itself.
- **Every decision goes through the decision core** (K-100, S1.348), decider named: an institution's office (K-34);
  public offices — a central bank's committee, a treasury's minister — stay empty until S5.144 fills them and decide
  from their institution's founding preferences (MND.16, MND.20); a firm's or a bank's chief executive is appointed
  by S3.156's boards. Institutions' reviews are due on
  their declared schedules (K-43) and on wakes (K-46 triggers, K-45 messages), and cost their staff's hours.
- **Where things happen** (TIME.6, K-23): institutions decide at stage 5 (5c); calls, books and dealers meet at 6a;
  prints and fixings at 6b; the curve and discount-factor tables at 6c; trades settle on their market's convention
  (MKT.21, SET.2) at stage 7, as dated commitments (K-50) until then; the money market and the central bank's
  tenders post at 8a, meet in one network call at 8b and settle at 8c, facilities at 8d–8e, a shortfall ends at 8f;
  tests, calls and demands at 9c, applied at 9e, due the next business day (TIME.7); publications at 9d. No financial
  market meets on a non-business day (TIME.8).
- **Instruments and holdings are the core's**: every issue is an instrument (K-64, S1.279), every holding of it an instrument holding (S1.280),
  every coupon, redemption, conversion and default an instrument event (K-65, S1.281) to holders of record at the
  day's start; every loan, repo, agreement and syndicate share a contract (K-53) between named parties.

**Placeholders.**

| Placeholder | Clauses | Introduced | Retired by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The fixed policy rate and corridor, `CB.policy_rate_fixed`, `CB.corridor_spread` (naming CB) | CB.4, CB.7 | S1.429 | S3.111 (the rate), S3.112 (the corridor) |
| The declared eligible collateral and loan haircut, `CB.eligible_collateral`, `CB.loan_haircut` (naming CB) | CB.6 | S1.429 | S3.112 |
| The treasury never borrowing from the central bank, `TRS.never_borrows_from_cb` (naming CB) | CB.3, CB.9 | S1.431 | S3.116 |
| The treasury's funding rule, `TRS.funding_rule` (naming TRS) | TRS.2, TRS.3 | S1.431 | S3.119 (the plan) and S3.122 (a shortfall) |
| The shortfall protocol's deferral of discretionary purchases (naming SOC) | TRS.3 | S1.431 | S5.145 |
| The shortfall protocol's fixed order, standing for the minister's choice among the options (naming POL) | TRS.3 | S3.122 | S5.145 |
| A bank's decision to raise capital recorded and unmet (naming CRD and EQY) | BCP.4 | S2.191 | S3.132 (subordinated debt and contingent capital); S3.154 (shares) |
| The central bank's collateral eligibility reads no rating (naming RAT) | RAT.4 | S3.112 | S3.215 |
| A central bank's committee unfilled: its decisions taken at its founding preferences (naming POL, PTY.17); the treasury's minister stays as S1.432 left it | PTY.16, PTY.17 | S3.111 | S5.144 |

**The stage's lines** (ARCHITECTURE §13, keys in `perf/design.toml`): the money market, tenders and facilities
share fin.fixed.fund; institutions' decisions (central banks, treasuries, banks' funding, issuers, underwriters)
fin.fixed.institutions; financial orders fin.fixed.securities; auctions, book-built calls and the curve fin.fixed.calls;
repo margin, covenant and trigger tests fin.fixed.valuation; instrument events fin.holdings.holder_ns. Each step's
**Budget** states its share of each line it uses, B / NB / H, in ARCHITECTURE §13's forms; no Stage 3 work runs on a
non-business day (TIME.8).

### S3.100 — Stage 3's macro reads frozen

**Status**: planned

series); S1.494, S1.495 (the estimators the reads use).
**Goal**: before any Stage 3 code, the stage's macro reads are declared in `data/observer/READS.toml`, each with its

writes them.

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/observer/READS.toml` | Stage 3's reads, frozen; their hash recorded in `perf/reads/S3.100-frozen.toml` |

**Design**:
- The reads (Appendix E 25), each with its statistic, its relationship and its source; reported, never tuned:
  - money market (MMK.9): the spread between the strongest and weakest names' overnight prints; repo haircuts by
    basket through the cycle; the term premium; the pass-through of corridor changes to overnight prints (source

### S3.101 — The money market's markets and its network call at stage 8

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.1 STATE; MMK.6 PROCESS; MMK.11 PRIMITIVE; MMK.10 FORBID *(part: no assignment of lenders to borrowers)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (stage 8's slots), §7.11 (phx-market: K-77, K-70, K-86), §7.9 (phx-contract), §8
**Depends on**: S1.314 (K-77 network call: the clearing), S1.296 (K-70 offers: the day's orders), S1.257 (K-53: the
agreement family and new rows), S1.263 (K-55: the overnight terms shape), S1.338 (K-93: limit lines as declared
limits), S1.180 (K-21: market declarations), S1.185 (K-23: stage 8's slots), S1.248 (K-49: settlement at 8c),
S1.326 (K-86: prints), S2.182 (the interbank loan family this step extends with overnight terms)
**Goal**: each country's money market is declared markets keyed by segment, tenor and borrower, meeting at 8b of a
business day in one network call over the orders posted at 8a; each match settles at 8c as an interbank or repo row.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/lib.rs` | the system; `declare`: markets, families, shapes, slots, streams |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/markets.rs` | market keys (country, segment, tenor, borrower); the network assembly rule |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/network.rs` | pure: the day's orders, lines and agreements → K-77's network |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/network.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/mmk.rs` | 8a orders gathered, 8b the call routed to K-77, 8c matches to K-48 and K-49 |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | segments (unsecured; repo per operator basket), tenors, lots, ticks, settlement, eligible collateral per basket (POLICY) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/mmk.rs` | LC-3-51 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/market_clearing.rs` | PC-51: no `sys-*` crate calls `phx-market`'s matching, clearing or allocation |

**Design**:
- **Markets** (K-21 declarations, MKT.21): per country one market per (segment, tenor, borrower); segment is
  `Unsecured` or `Repo(basket)` for each basket the operator declares; tenors (overnight, one week, one and three
  months), lots, ticks and each basket's eligible securities are POLICY of the operator (MMK.11); form K-77; meeting
  days the country's business days; settlement same day at 8c; participants: banks, and parties with a master
  agreement (repo). A loan is lender + borrower + terms (Law 9), so a doubted borrower's market prices apart.
- **Families**: the interbank family (S2.182) gains the overnight shape (K-55, one shared schedule: principal and
  interest due the next business day by the country's convention, TIME.3); the **master agreement** family (K-53
  `Pair` row, cold columns: re-use allowed u8, margin threshold i64, eligible baskets u16 mask, liquidation horizon
  u16 days) between two named parties; the repo family is S3.106's.
- **Network assembly** (`network.rs`, pure): inputs the day's money-market offers (K-70, posted at 8a by S3.104,
  S3.105, S3.108, S3.113), the lenders' limit headroom per counterparty (K-93 used vs amount), agreements (K-53
  view), each borrower's collateral assignment (S3.104). Nodes and edges as K-77 takes them: source → lender `l`
  (capacity: its lendable cash, its own order's total) → offer node `(l, t)` (cost: its offer schedule) → edge
  `(l, b, s, t)` only under a limit line (unsecured), an agreement (repo) or the collateral framework (a tender,
  S3.113), capacity its headroom, cost the lender's spread record (S3.102) → market node `(b, s, t)` → borrower node `(b, t)`
  (capacity: the cash its collateral assigned to `s` raises at the lender's haircuts, S3.103; none for unsecured) →
  sink (cost: minus its bid schedule). Integer lots, no multiplying edge: one pure min-cost flow.
- **When**: 8b of each country's business day, K-77 warm-started from yesterday's basis; each market's price is its
  node potential on the tick grid; where a range is optimal MKT.3's tie rule picks nearest the market's last print
  (K-86), then the lower rate; flow ties by lot on stream `MMK.path_lot` (subject: the country, day).
- **Outputs**: matches → a K-48 batch per country (reason `MMK.money_market`) settling at 8c (K-49), each opening its
  row between the named lender and borrower; prints to K-86. MMK.10 (part): only `phx-market` clears (PC-51).

**Edge cases**: E2 — a market with bids and no offers, or no edge under any line, clears nothing: the empty match set
(`network_empty_sides`). E6 — orders live 8a–8c and never cross a save; agreements, lines and rows are saved by their
bases (`contracts_roundtrip`, S1.257; `rebuild_equals_maintained`, S1.338); the warm start rebuilt cold gives the
same optimum (`network_same_after_cold_start`; K-77's `warm_and_cold_start_agree`, S1.314). E7 — flow ties by address,
never by input order (`network_order_free`). E10 — a line or agreement naming an ended party resolves stale and adds no
edge (`network_skips_stale_line`). E11 — day zero runs stage 5 only, so the first call is day one's, its tie anchored
on the opening's print (`network_tie_nearest_last_print`). E13 — one bank alone has no unsecured edge; before S3.144's
opening data, repo segments meet empty (`network_empty_sides`). E14 — a borrower in several segments has one borrower
node per tenor, so its bid is met once (`borrower_node_one_per_tenor`).

**Extension points**: S3.104, S3.105, S3.108, S3.113 (the tender node), S3.187 (money funds), S4.138 (insurers) and
S5.179 (foreign banks) register their decider kinds as posters.

**Unit tests**: `network_edges_only_under_lines_and_agreements`; `network_capacities_are_cash_on_lots`;
`network_empty_sides`; `network_order_free`; `network_skips_stale_line`; `overnight_shape_due_next_business_day`;
`network_same_after_cold_start`; `network_tie_nearest_last_print`; `borrower_node_one_per_tenor`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-51 — every money-market match settled in stage 8 of a business day, opened one row between its
named lender and borrower, and no money market met on a non-business day (applicable from the first match).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: one call a business day per country over ≈ 10 k edges (assembly ≈ 1 ms; K-77 ≈ 5 ms VM warm-started,
`fin.call.network_ms`); ≈ 300 matches settled at 8c. Counters `phx_mmk.network_edges`, `phx_mmk.matches`.
its share of fin.fixed.fund: 18 / 0 / 18 core-ms (B / NB / H)
adds 600 / 0 / 600 items to fin.settle.flow_ns
ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.1 MB resident (≈ 4.5 k master agreements × 21 B: 8-B pair row + re-use u8, threshold
i64, baskets u16, liquidation horizon u16)

**Guards**: PC-51 — no `sys-*` crate calls a matching, clearing or allocation function of `phx-market`; a market is
met only by the runner routing it to its kernel.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; surplus banks assigned to lend; an edge that multiplies a flow; a market rate set equal to the
policy rate; a match on a non-business day.

### S3.102 — Lenders' limits and spreads per counterparty

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.5 DECISION *(part: limits and spreads)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (rule handles), §7.14 (phx-risk: K-93), §8
**Depends on**: S3.101 (edges read limits), S1.338 (K-93: declared limits with binding events), S1.239 (K-46: wakes
on public events), S1.213 (K-36: public events), S1.348 (K-100), S2.179 (the marginal cost of funds), S2.102 (each
bank's one assessment and the handle `loan_claim_value`), S2.186 (the large-exposure limit), S2.192 (authorities'
facts as public events)
**Goal**: every lender sets, on its weekly review and when its view of a counterparty worsens, a limit and a spread
per counterparty and tenor from its own assessment, so a doubted name loses funding before it loses solvency.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/points.rs` | the decision point `set_limits` (office: the lender's chief executive) |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/mmk.rs` | 5c reviews and wakes; 5d limits and records written |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/limits.rs` | limit and spread from PD, LGD and the exposure the lender carries |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/limits.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | review schedule and hours (TECHNOLOGY); management's expected-loss appetite per counterparty (PREFERENCE) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Afonso, Kovner and Schoar, 2011; Basel Committee, 2014) |

**Design**:
- **When**: the lender's weekly review (K-43) and wakes (K-46 on the counterparty): a public liquidity failure or
  resolution at a like bank (K-36), a fail of the counterparty's payment to it (K-56), later a rating change (S3.216).
- **Inputs**: the lender's PD and LGD of the counterparty through the handle `assessment(lender, obligor)`: for a
  bank it resolves to its one loan assessment (`sys-bnk`, PC-40); for a non-bank to its own outlook of failures seen
  and recoveries (registered by S3.103; until then a non-bank sets no line). Its marginal cost of funds (S2.179). Its declared exposure appetite `A`
  (PREFERENCE) and large-exposure limit (S2.186).
- **Rule**: spread for tenor T = the rate at which `loan_claim_value` of a loan of tenor T equals its principal, less
  its cost of funds; limit `L = A ÷ (PD × LGD)` within the large-exposure limit; where `PD × LGD` is zero the rule does
  not divide and the large-exposure limit is the limit. A PD above the lender's appetite gives a limit of zero.
- **Outputs**: a K-93 declared limit (owner lender, subject counterparty, amount) — binding is an event the lender
  sees (Law 6) — and a K-37 record of its spreads by tenor, audience the pair, which the network reads (S3.101).

**Edge cases**: E1 — a bank failure wakes only the lenders with a line to it (`limit_wakes_only_counterparties`). E6 — limits are
K-93 rows (`rebuild_equals_maintained`, S1.338), spreads K-37 records (`save_round_trip_as_published`, S1.215),
pending wakes K-46/K-43 state (`save_round_trip_runs`, S1.239). E10 — a counterparty ended: its limit resolves stale
and yields no edge (`network_skips_stale_line`, S3.101). E12 — an assessment absent (a new counterparty) is Missing:
no line until assessed (`limit_missing_assessment_no_line`). E14 — two wakes the same day review once
(`two_wakes_one_review`).

**Extension points**: S3.103 registers non-banks' assessment; S3.216 adds a rating change as a wake; S3.187's money
funds register their decider kind.

**Unit tests**: `limit_falls_as_pd_rises`; `limit_zero_product_takes_large_exposure_limit`;
`spread_equates_claim_value_to_principal`; `limit_zero_above_appetite`; `limit_wakes_only_counterparties`; `limit_missing_assessment_no_line`; `two_wakes_one_review`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-16 at S3.109 reads refusals).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 200 / 0 / 200 limit reviews (35 banks × ≈ 20 counterparties weekly, plus wakes) × ≈ 2 µs. Counter
`phx_mmk.limit_reviews`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.4 / 0 / 0.4 core-ms (B / NB / H)
ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-93 limits): +0.3 MB resident (≈ 10 k limit rows × 32 B)
ledger line 18 (records): +0.5 MB resident (spread records, ≈ 10 k a week within their horizon × ≈ 48 B)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; one limit shared by every lender; a bank's counterparty valued outside `loan_claim_value`.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Limits and spreads set by each lender; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; the form
  listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.103 — Non-banks' counterparty outlooks and every lender's haircuts

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.5 DECISION
**Architecture**: §4.9 (records with a pair audience), §8
**Depends on**: S3.102 (the point and its handle), S1.215 (K-37: records addressed to a pair), S1.326 (K-86: turnover
and depth, MKT.15), S1.336 (K-92: the lender's outlook width of a security's price change), S1.340 (K-94: haircuts
read by margin)
**Goal**: non-bank lenders assess counterparties from failures and recoveries they have seen, and every lender sets
a haircut per security and per borrower from its own view of the price's movement and how long it would take to
sell, published to that borrower before 8a.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/haircuts.rs` | the haircut per (security, borrower) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/nonbank_view.rs` | a non-bank's PD and LGD outlook of a counterparty |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/haircuts.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | confidence z and share of turnover a lender expects to sell per day (PREFERENCE) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms (Brunnermeier and Pedersen, 2009; Gorton and Metrick, 2012) |

**Design**:
- **Non-bank view**: PD its method's outlook (K-92 cell) of the published failure series of the counterparty's class
  (public failures and resolutions, K-36, VAL.5), starting from the snapshot's published failure statistics (VAL.10,
  GEN.5); LGD its method's outlook of published recoveries; registered as the non-bank resolution of S3.102's
  `assessment` handle.
- **Haircut** per (security, borrower) on the same review: `h = z·σ·sqrt(T_liq)`: σ the lender's outlook width of the
  security's daily price change (K-92 over K-86 marks), `T_liq` its outlook of the days to sell the borrower's
  expected delivery at the security's recent turnover (K-86 MKT.15 read) and its own share of turnover sold a day, z
  its confidence. A borrower above the lender's appetite gets a limit of zero (S3.102).
- **Output**: a K-37 record per (lender, borrower) with the haircuts, audience the pair, published at 5c before 8a;
  the network (S3.101) and repo margin (S3.107, K-94) read it. Completes MMK.5: limits per counterparty and haircuts
  per collateral and borrower, widened on a worse view.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a security with no print: width and turnover Missing, no haircut, the security raises nothing at that
lender (`haircut_missing_print`). E6 — haircut records are K-37 rows (`save_round_trip_as_published`, S1.215); the
outlooks K-92 cells (`fixed_overflow_stops`, S1.336, and its store round trip). E9 — records kept for their declared
horizon, pruned by chunk (`haircut_record_horizon_declared`). E11 — day zero: marks are GEN.5's single values, so the
width is Missing until prints accumulate (`haircut_missing_print`). E13 — a basket with no eligible security raises
nothing (`empty_basket_raises_nothing`).

**Extension points**: S3.112 uses the same form for the central bank's framework; S3.175 (securities loans) reads the
record.

**Unit tests**: `haircut_rises_with_width_and_size`; `haircut_missing_print`; `nonbank_pd_from_failures_seen`; `haircut_record_horizon_declared`; `empty_basket_raises_nothing`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-52 — every repo edge's haircut names the record its lender published to that borrower, and no
two borrowers read one lender's record (applicable from the first repo).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 12 k / 0 / 12 k haircuts (≈ 3 k lenders weekly × ≈ 20 securities) × ≈ 200 ns. Counter
`phx_mmk.haircuts`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

### S3.104 — Banks' overnight reserve orders

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.4 DECISION *(part: banks overnight)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (8a), §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100), §8
**Depends on**: S3.101 (the markets), S3.102 (its lines), S3.103 (the haircuts published to it), S1.348 (K-100: the
decision core), S1.240 (K-47: reserves after stage 7), S1.248 (K-49: per-party day nets), S1.336 (K-92: the bank's
own outlook of its net flow), S1.296 (K-70: orders), S1.277 (K-63: free collateral), S2.180 (the buffer's reserve
part), S2.185 (the facility request after the market), S1.429 (the corridor's rates in force)
**Goal**: after stage 7, every bank posts at 8a, from its own position, what it would borrow or lend overnight at
each rate strictly inside the corridor, and assigns its free collateral to the repo segments it reaches. Nothing
assigns a bank to a side.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/points.rs` | the decision point `fund_position` (office: the bank's chief executive) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/reserves.rs` | the Poole schedule; collateral assignment to segments |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/reserves.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | review hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Poole, 1968; Bindseil, 2004; Whitesell, 2006) |

**Design**:
- **When**: 8a of each business day, for every bank of a country whose business day it is (≈ 12 a country).
- **Inputs** (a view of the bank's own state only, REP.5): reserves after stage 7 (K-47, BFL.8); its reserve target
  for tomorrow's close — the buffer's reserve part (S2.180) plus, where the country declares requirements, the
  average still owed over the maintenance period (S3.114; a country with none declares none); its own outlook of
  tomorrow's net payment flow, mean μ and width σ (K-92 own-variable outlook, VAL.6, over its own day nets from K-49);
  the corridor's two rates (public records, K-37); its free collateral by security (its instrument holdings, S1.280, minus K-63) at its marks
  (K-86); the haircuts lenders published to it (S3.103) and its lines (S3.102).
- **Form**: a unit more held overnight costs `r − i_DF` and saves `(i_LF − i_DF)·P(short)`; with the outlook normal,
  `R*(r) = T + μ + σ·Φ⁻¹(1 − (r − i_DF) ÷ (i_LF − i_DF))` on the ticks strictly inside the corridor; the order at `r`
  is `R*(r) − R`, a bid where positive, an offer where negative; nothing at the corridor's edges (MMK.8's
  alternatives). With no flow history its outlook is Missing: it posts nothing and meets 8d (E11).
- **Collateral assignment**: each free unit to the segment where it raises most cash net of its encumbrance cost —
  zero on units beyond the buffer's need, `(i_LF − i_DF)·P(short)` on units the buffer counts; ties by security id.
  The assignment is the borrower node's capacity per segment (S3.101).
- **Outputs**: one bid schedule at the borrower node and one offer schedule (K-70 offers, lapse at 8c); the decision
  recorded with its decider (K-100). Review cost `MMK.funding_review_hours` from the bank's staff hours.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a bank ended at 2f has no agenda entry and posts nothing (`ended_bank_posts_nothing`). E3 — a bank with no
free collateral posts only unsecured bids (`assignment_empty`). E5 — a heavy day's nets are read once per bank
(`one_net_read_per_bank`). E6 — the flow outlook is the bank's saved column (`save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`,
S1.196); the order never crosses a save. E11 — no flow history: the outlook is Missing and the bank posts nothing
(`poole_missing_outlook`). E12 — a corridor rate absent is refused at assembly (`corridor_rate_absent_refused`).

**Extension points**: S3.105 adds term tenors on the same point; S3.114 supplies the maintenance average; S3.110
reads what the market leaves.

**Unit tests**: `poole_schedule_falls_with_rate`; `poole_nothing_at_corridor_edges`;
`poole_schedule_centred_by_target_and_outlook`; `poole_missing_outlook`; `assignment_to_segment_raising_most`;
`assignment_empty`; `ended_bank_posts_nothing`; `one_net_read_per_bank`; `corridor_rate_absent_refused`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-15 — every money-market order names its poster's decision point, and every order of
`fund_position` lies strictly inside the corridor; the share of banks that only lent or only borrowed over each year
is reported (from the first order).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 35 / 0 / 35 decisions × ≈ 20 µs (Φ⁻¹ over ≈ 50 ticks); ≈ 70 posts (K-70). Counter `phx_mmk.orders`.
its share of fin.fixed.fund: 0.7 / 0 / 0.7 core-ms (B / NB / H)
ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0003 MB resident (35 banks × 8 B: net-flow outlook mean and width, `Fixed` i32 each)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an order outside the corridor; a bank told to lend or borrow; an order at 5c reading stage 8's
positions.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `fund_position` posts from each bank's own state; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken;
  LC-3-15 passes; the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.105 — Term bids and offers in the money market

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.4 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c, 8a), §8
**Depends on**: S3.104 (the point and the overnight schedule), S3.101 (term markets), S1.227 (K-43: the weekly
funding review), S1.336 (K-92: the outlook of the overnight rate), S1.179 (K-20: announced policy changes by
effective day), S2.180 (the buffer's term funding gap)
**Goal**: on its weekly funding review each bank bids for term funding up to its term gap and offers term lending,
both from its own outlook of the compounded overnight rate and its own rollover risk, so the term premium is an
outcome.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/term.rs` | term bid and offer schedules |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/term.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | the review schedule (TECHNOLOGY), review hours |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Poole's, extended over the tenor) |

**Design**:
- **When**: the bank's funding review (K-43 schedule, weekly, phase drawn per bank at the opening) and each tender at
  its tenor (S3.113); orders post at 8a of that day and lapse at 8c.
- **Bid for tenor T** up to the term funding gap (S2.180's buffer held against outflows beyond T) at rates up to
  `E[r_on over T] + P_roll·(i_LF − E[r_on])`: the compounded overnight outlook (K-92 own outlook of its clearing
  rate; announced corridor changes enter from their effective day, K-20) plus its outlook `P_roll` of the share of
  its overnight bids left unfilled (its own record: filled over posted, K-52 tally by party).
- **Offer for tenor T** at rates from `E[r_on over T] + P_need·(i_LF − E[r_on])`, `P_need` its outlook of needing the
  cash (from S3.104's flow outlook). The borrower's expected loss is the edge's spread (S3.102), never in the offer.
- **Output**: schedules at the term borrower node and offer node (K-70). This step completes MMK.4: every bank posts
  from its own position at every tenor it reaches.

**Edge cases**: E6 — term rows (`contracts_roundtrip`, S1.257), the fill tallies (`tally_roundtrip`, S1.254) and the review's
next day (`rebuild_takes_same`, S1.227) are saved or rebuilt. E11 — no record of fills: `P_roll` Missing; the bid posts
at the compounded outlook alone if that exists, else nothing (`term_missing_record`). E12 — a tenor the operator does
not declare is refused at assembly (`undeclared_tenor_refused`). E14 — a review on a tender day posts one schedule per
tenor market (`one_schedule_per_tenor`).

**Extension points**: S3.113 registers tenders' tenors for this rule.

**Unit tests**: `term_schedule_prices_rollover_risk`; `term_offer_excludes_expected_loss`;
`term_bid_bounded_by_gap`; `term_missing_record`; `undeclared_tenor_refused`; `one_schedule_per_tenor`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-15 covers term orders' decision points (S3.104).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 7 / 0 / 7 reviews (35 banks weekly) × ≈ 30 µs. Counter `phx_mmk.term_orders`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-52 party tallies): +0.0006 MB resident (35 banks × 16 B: overnight bids posted and
filled this period, i64 each)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a term rate read from a published curve instead of the bank's own outlook; expected loss inside
an offer.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Term schedules post on reviews; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; the form listed.
