### S3.106 — Repo contracts: title, income passed back and re-use chains

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.2 STATE; MMK.10 FORBID
**Architecture**: §7.9 (phx-contract), §7.10 (phx-hold: K-60, K-63, K-65), §7.8 (phx-ledger: link groups), §7.17
(K-103: an audit family), §8
**Depends on**: S3.101 (matches in repo segments), S3.103 (the haircut at the start), S1.257 (K-53: the repo family),
S1.263 (K-55: repurchase terms), S1.245 (K-48: link groups, all-or-none), S1.248 (K-49), S1.280 (instrument holdings, built there),
S1.277 (K-63: received-under-title rows and their source), S1.281 (K-65: income events to holders of record),
S1.253 (K-51: a declared follow-on reason), S1.265 (K-56: a failed repurchase), S1.353 (K-103: the Collateral family)
**Goal**: a repo is one contract between its named lender and borrower: at the start the cash lender takes title to
the collateral less its haircut, income on the collateral is passed back as a manufactured payment, the repurchase
returns both legs together, and every re-use of received units is a traceable chain. No unit is ever free on both
sides.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/repo.rs` | the repo family and its shape; start, repurchase and manufactured-payment reasons |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/audit.rs` | the Collateral audit family (pure check over handed values) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/repo.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/mmk.rs` | 8c start legs; the repurchase due in stage 7 |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | repo conventions per market: day count, settlement, re-use default (POLICY, MMK.11) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/mmk.rs` | LC-3-02 |

**Design**:
- **Family** (K-53 `Balance` row, 24 B): sides lender and borrower (any kinds the agreement family admits), shape
  (K-55: start day, repurchase day, repo rate, day count from the terms), own amount = cash lent; cold columns:
  collateral `UnitId`, units i64, haircut at start (from S3.103's record), agreement `ContractRef`, re-use allowed u8.
- **Start leg** (8c, from a repo match): one K-48 link group settling all-or-none (SET.4): cash lender → borrower;
  units borrower → lender (instrument holdings' batch moves, S1.280); a K-63 row of kind received-under-title on the
  lender's holding (from party: borrower, via: the repo, units, source: the borrower's own received row if its units
  were themselves received). Title passes; the repo row opens with the settlement.
- **Re-use**: where the agreement allows, the received units are the lender's free units; each onward repo, pledge or
  sale writes a received row on the next holder whose source is this row, so the chain runs to its end holder. Where
  it does not, the units are bound (K-63 committed) and cannot move. The borrower holds none of them: its right to
  their return is the repo's unit leg, never a free unit (MMK.10).
- **Income passed back** (REG.11, MMK.2): an instrument event pays the lender as holder of record at the day's start
  (K-65, stage 2e); the repo family declares a follow-on reason `MMK.manufactured` (K-51): per received row naming
  that instrument, an owed payment lender → borrower of the event's amount on the row's units (K-16 apportion over
  rows, residue by row id), due the event's settlement day, settled at stage 7 in the day's batch.
- **Repurchase** (K-42 due on the repurchase day, stage 7): one link group — cash borrower → lender (principal plus
  interest by the terms' day count, TIME.4), units lender → borrower (or the chain's end holder returns them first
  along the chain, each link its own contract leg); the received row closes. A leg that cannot settle fails the
  group (SET.3), recorded at the next 2d (K-56); S3.107 acts on it.
- **Collateral family** (K-103, INVARIANT under MMK.10 and REG.16): per holding Σ received and pledged units ≤ held;
  every received row's source chain ends at a holder; no unit free for two holders; recounted daily over the rows the
  day changed (K-07) and in the rolling cycle.
- **MMK.10 completes**: no assignment of lenders (PC-51, S3.101), no market rate at the policy rate by construction
  (orders inside the corridor, S3.104), no collateral counted by both sides (this family).

**Edge cases**: E6 — repo rows (`contracts_roundtrip`, S1.257), received rows (`binds_round_trip`, S1.277) and dues
(`refile_after_load_equals`, S1.225) are saved or rebuilt; chains rebuild from their sources
(`reuse_chain_rebuilt_from_sources`). E8 — a chain's length is unbounded by code and reported
(`reuse_chain_max_reported`). E10 — the collateral's issuer defaults during the repo: the received row follows REG.12's
resolution (`received_row_follows_cessation`); a party ending moves its side to its estate
(`repo_side_moves_to_estate`). E14 — an income event and the repurchase the same day: the event to the holder of
record at 2e, the manufactured payment owed back, the repurchase at 7 (`income_and_repurchase_same_day`).

**Extension points**: S3.107 (margin and default); S3.175's securities loans and S3.179's prime brokerage write
received rows the same way; S4.168's pledged tranches.

**Unit tests**: `repo_legs_pass_title_all_or_none`; `manufactured_payment_apportioned_over_rows`;
`reuse_chain_links_every_onward_use`; `no_reuse_binds_units`; `received_row_follows_cessation`;
`income_and_repurchase_same_day`; `collateral_family_flags_double_free` (an injected double count is reported); `reuse_chain_rebuilt_from_sources`; `reuse_chain_max_reported`; `repo_side_moves_to_estate`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-02 — MMK.10: the Collateral family reports no finding, and every received unit's chain ends
at a holder (from the first repo).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 300 / 0 / 300 repo opens and closes; ≈ 600 legs in the stage-7 batch; manufactured payments ≈ 1 k on
event days. Counters `phx_mmk.repos_open`, `phx_mmk.reuse_chain_max`.
adds 300 / 0 / 300 items to fin.contracts.open_ns
adds 600 / 0 / 600 items to fin.settle.flow_ns
ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.2 MB resident (≈ 4.5 k repos × 47 B: 24-B balance row + collateral unit 4, units 8,
haircut 2, agreement ref 8, re-use 1)
ledger line 13 (liens and processes): +0.1 MB resident (≈ 4.5 k received rows × 24 B)

**Guards**: none new (PC-51 is S3.101's).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a repo's collateral left free at the borrower; a leg settling without its pair; income kept by
the lender.

### S3.107 — Repo margin calls and a defaulted repo's collateral sold

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §7.14 (phx-risk: K-94), §6.1 (9c, 9e, 2c), §9.3 (a margin call unmet)
**Depends on**: S3.106 (repo rows), S1.340 (K-94: netting sets per agreement, VM, calls due next business day),
S1.326 (K-86: marks), S1.335 (K-91: a named valuer's valuation), S1.237 (K-45: the call), S1.265 (K-56: a failed
repurchase), S1.296 (K-70: sale orders), S1.257 (K-53: a shortfall claim), S1.357 (K-105, the investor schedule: the
lender's sale limits)
**Goal**: each repo agreement's netting set is marked at 9c; a gap beyond its threshold issues a margin call due the
next business day; an unmet call or a failed repurchase defaults the agreement, and the lender keeps the collateral
and sells it by its own orders over its declared horizon, claiming any shortfall and returning any excess.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/repo_margin.rs` | the margin test and call; the default and the sale rule |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/repo_margin.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/mmk.rs` | 9c test, 9e call, 2c payment, 5c sales |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | review hours (TECHNOLOGY); each lender's liquidation horizon (POLICY of the lender) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the sale rule's form (a liquidation slice at the lender's own limit) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/mmk.rs` | LC-3-17 |

**Design**:
- It serves MMK.2 (repo's haircut and income, S3.106) and the L2 chain's door of a funding line withdrawn.
- **Netting set** (K-94): one per master agreement; positions its open repo rows; collateral value at the day's marks
  (K-86) or, where a security has no print, a named valuer's valuation labelled as such (K-91, MKT.20).
- **Test** (9c, a declared K-94 sweep over agreements with open repos): gap = cash lent × (1 + haircut) − collateral
  value; beyond the agreement's threshold, a call (K-45 message, TIME.7) due at the next business day's 2c for cash or
  further units (a link group); applied at 9e. Excess collateral returned on the borrower's request by the same
  message kind.
- **Default** (2d, from K-56: a call unmet at 2c or a failed repurchase): the agreement's positions close as defaulted;
  the lender keeps the received units (title already its own; the received row released) and owes the borrower any
  excess.
- **Sale** (the lender's decision, 5c on each business day of its liquidation horizon): the day's slice (remaining
  units ÷ remaining days) offered in the security's declared secondary market at limits from the investor schedule
  with its value and width (VAL.8) — never "at any price" (MKT.17); unsold units carry to the next day. A security
  whose secondary market does not yet meet (S3.166's dealers) rests unsold, a failed meeting (MKT.10).
- **Close-out**: when sold or the horizon ends, proceeds against cash owed: a shortfall opens a claim contract
  (K-53, ordinary class, L3) lender on borrower; an excess is paid to the borrower. The funding line withdrawn is L2's
  door: the borrower's sales it forces are its own (S2.184's shortfall actions).

**Edge cases**: E1 — a crash day calls every set whose gap crosses its threshold, calls ≤ open sets (K-94's `crash_day_calls`,
S1.340). E2 — no bid for the collateral: nothing sold, the units stay the lender's (`sale_no_bid_keeps_units`). E3 — a
borrower with no cash and no free units fails the call (`call_unmet_without_means`). E6 — calls are K-45 messages
(`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237); a sale's remaining days a saved agreement column (`contracts_roundtrip`,
S1.257). E14 — a call and a repurchase one day: the repurchase at 7, the next call reads what is left
(`call_after_repurchase_reads_rest`).

**Extension points**: S3.179's prime brokerage and S3.175's securities loans reuse the same test through K-94.

**Unit tests**: `repo_call_from_marks_and_threshold`; `repo_call_uses_labelled_valuation_without_print`;
`default_keeps_units_and_owes_excess`; `sale_slice_over_horizon`; `sale_no_bid_keeps_units`;
`shortfall_becomes_claim`; `call_unmet_without_means`; `call_after_repurchase_reads_rest`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-17 — every repo call names the marks or valuation it read; every unmet call ends in the
lender's sales and a settled shortfall claim or excess (from the first call).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 4.5 k positions in ≈ 1 k netting sets × 10 ns at 9c; ≈ 50 calls a day. Counters `phx_mmk.repo_calls`,
`phx_mmk.collateral_sales`.
its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H)
ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.01 MB resident (≈ 4.5 k master agreements × 2 B: remaining liquidation days u16)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a call paid the day it is issued; a sale at any price; the shortfall dropped; a margin payment
without a cash test.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Margin, default and sale rules; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-17 passes;
  the sale form listed.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §9.3 states repo's path; two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.108 — Non-banks' cash placement

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.3 STATE *(part: firms; money funds at S3.187, insurers at S4.138)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c, 8a), §8
**Depends on**: S3.101 (repo markets and the agreement family), S3.103 (non-banks' views and haircuts), S1.348
(K-100), S1.350 (K-101: the review's occasion), S1.317 (K-80: an agreement asked of a bank), S2.118 (the firm's cash target in its funding decision), S2.177 (term deposits)
**Goal**: a firm with cash beyond its own target places it — in term deposits or, if it holds a master agreement, in
repo to its counterparties, and in the alternatives later steps declare — by its own yields; a firm opens an agreement only when the
placements it expects are worth the hours the agreement costs.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/points.rs` | the decision point `place_cash` (office: the firm's chief executive) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/cash.rs` | the placement across alternatives; repo offers; opening an agreement |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/cash.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/mmk.rs` | 5c review, 8a offers |
| `data/<country>/MMK.toml` | review hours, agreement hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Miller and Orr, 1966) |

**Design**:
- **When**: on the occasions of the firm's financing review (S2.118's `FRM.finance`: its attention review and a
  cash-outlook occasion) when its need is a surplus — no lumpy kind of its own: the placement is the surplus branch of
  that review's rule, over the view it already gathers (its cash, its target, ≈ 4 alternatives' yields); firms with an
  agreement also post daily at 8a.
- **Inputs**: its money (K-47), its own cash target (S2.118's precautionary target), its outlooks of each
  alternative's yield — its bank's term-deposit product rates (K-47's product rates, S2.177), the repo rate (its outlook over repo prints,
  K-86) — and its costs (review and agreement hours). The alternatives are declared data: later steps add bills and
  bonds at auction (S3.120) and corporate paper and bonds (S3.134), each with its yield read.
- **Placement**: cash beyond the target to the alternative with the best yield net of its costs, in lots, by the
  form's return-point rule; term deposits by opening the deposit contract (S2.177).
- **Repo offers** (a firm holding an agreement, 8a): the surplus offered as a schedule from its best other alternative's
  yield upward, only on edges to its agreement counterparties (S3.101).
- **Opening an agreement**: when its expected surplus × (repo yield − its best other yield) over its horizon exceeds
  `MMK.agreement_hours` at its staff's cost, it asks its banks (K-80); a bank accepts when its `set_limits` view gives
  the firm a positive limit (S3.102); the agreement row opens (S3.101's family).

**Edge cases**: E2 — no repo counterparty: repo is not among its alternatives (`no_counterparty_no_repo`). E3 — a firm with no
surplus places nothing (`surplus_to_best_net_yield`). E6 — agreements and deposits are saved contracts
(`contracts_roundtrip`, S1.257). E10 — its bank ending: the agreement moves to the estate or successor and posts no
edge (`network_skips_stale_line`, S3.101). E11 — no prints yet: yields from GEN.5's values; a Missing yield leaves its
alternative out (`missing_yield_left_out`).

**Extension points**: S3.187's money funds and S4.138's insurers register their decider kinds for repo offers here
(S4.138 completing MMK.3); S3.120 and S3.134 add placement alternatives by declaration.

**Unit tests**: `surplus_to_best_net_yield`; `agreement_opened_only_when_worth_hours`; `repo_offer_from_alternative`; `no_counterparty_no_repo`; `missing_yield_left_out`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-15 names orders' decision points).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: the surplus branch of S2.118's review on ≈ 55 k / 0 / 55 k occasions (≈ 4 yields compared in the
review's own gather); ≈ 3 k repo offers at 8a × 150 ns. Counter `phx_mmk.cash_offers`.
adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.attend_ns at 55 k / 0 / 55 k items (folded: the placement is S2.118's plan's own output for a negative need, over the sources it already reads in its one view)
its share of fin.fixed.fund: 0.5 / 0 / 0.5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; cash placed for a firm by anything but its own decision; a repo offer to a party without an
agreement.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `place_cash` places and offers; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; the form listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.109 — A doubted name pays more or finds no lender; the money market's measures

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.7 PROCESS; MMK.9 MEASURE
**Architecture**: §8, §12 (observation), §14.2 (live checks)
**Depends on**: S3.101 (the call's results), S3.102 (spreads by counterparty), S1.326 (K-86: prints and failed
meetings per market), S1.213 (K-36: public events), S1.239 (K-46: wakes)
**Goal**: a borrower market with bids and no fill is a recorded failure the borrower and the public see, and the
money market's spreads, haircuts, term premium and pass-through are reported from its own prints.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/failures.rs` | the failure record and the borrower's wake |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/failures.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/mmk.rs` | LC-3-01, LC-3-16 |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/reads/mmk.rs` | the MMK.9 reads as S3.100 froze them, computed from public records |

**Design**:
- **Failure** (8b, after the call): each borrower market `(b, s, t)` with a bid and no fill writes K-86's failed
  meeting and a K-36 event `MMK.no_lender` (public: the borrower and tenor, not the bid) and wakes the borrower's
  shortfall actions for 8d (S3.110, S2.184). A doubted name pays more by the spreads lenders set (S3.102): no rule
  here adds a premium.
- **Measures** (MMK.9), read by the observer from public records: the spread between the strongest and weakest names'
  overnight prints per country; repo haircuts through the cycle (S3.103's records, their distribution by quarter);
  the term premium (term prints less the compounded overnight prints over the term); the pass-through of each
  corridor change (S3.112) to overnight prints over the following days.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a market with no bid is no failure (`failure_only_with_bid_and_no_fill`). E6 — failures are K-36 events
(`save_round_trip_events`, S1.213). E11 — the pass-through read is not applicable before a corridor change (LC-3-01).
E13 — a country with no money-market prints reports its measures absent, never zero (LC-3-01).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `failure_only_with_bid_and_no_fill`; `failure_wakes_borrower_once`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-01 — MMK.9: the spread between strongest and weakest names, haircuts by basket, the term
premium and the pass-through of corridor changes are reported (applicable after the first corridor change).
LC-3-16 — MMK.7 and BFL.10: every borrower market with bids and no fill is a published failure; a borrower still

liquidity failure followed the market, the facility and 8f in that order and went to resolution (from the first

### S3.110 — The market before the facility, and the bank that cannot pay

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MMK.8 PROCESS; BFL.6 DECISION; BFL.10 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6.1 (8a–8f), §9.2 (a bank's failure), §8
**Depends on**: S3.104, S3.105 (orders inside the corridor), S3.109 (the failure wake), S2.179 (declared funding
sources), S2.184 (shortfall actions in cost order), S2.185 (the facility request at stage 8 and failure for
liquidity), S2.196 (resolution opened by the failure), S1.429 (the facilities)
**Goal**: the money market's routes join each bank's cost of funds and its shortfall actions as declared sources, a
same-day shortfall meets the market at 8b before the facility at 8d, and a bank still short after both fails for
liquidity at 8f whatever its capital.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/src/rules/sources.rs` | the routes' marginal rates as funding sources |
| `crates/systems/sys-mmk/tests/sources.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/mmk.rs` | stage 8's order: 8b before 8d; 8f reads reserves after 8e |
| `data/<country>/BFL.toml` | the money market's routes as declared sources and shortfall actions |

**Design**:
- **Sources** (S2.179's extension point, declared data): overnight unsecured at the bank's own outlook of its
  clearing rate (K-92 over its prints); term and repo at their rates plus its rollover risk `P_roll` (S3.105); repo
  only while it has free eligible collateral at its lenders' haircuts. A doubted bank's dearer funding reaches its
  loan and deposit quotes through `marginal_cost_of_funds` (L4).
- **Shortfall order** (S2.184, BFL.6): the market route is a declared action costed at its bid's rate; with
  pledging (repo), asset sales, bidding for deposits, shrinking new lending and the facility, each bank takes them in
  the order its own costs and eligibility make best. This completes BFL.6.
- **Stage 8's order** (MMK.8): orders post at 8a strictly inside the corridor (S3.104), the call meets at 8b, the
  facility requests (S2.185) at 8d read the reserves after 8c, so banks use the facilities only for what the market
  left them; the lender-of-last-resort slot at 8d is declared here and empty until S3.115.
- **The bank that cannot pay** (8f, BFL.10): reserves below zero after 8e with no route left is a failure for
  liquidity, a public event, and S2.185's path opens resolution for the next day's 2b (S2.196). Completes BFL.10.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a failing bank's unpaid legs become others' fails the next day, never today
(`failure_fails_next_day`). E2 — the market refuses: the bank goes to the facility and without collateral fails
(`facility_reads_reserves_after_the_call`). E6 — nothing of stage 8 crosses a save but its settled rows
(`contracts_roundtrip`, S1.257). E14 — a bank short in the market and at the facility the same day meets them in
stage order (`stage_order_market_then_facility`).

**Extension points**: S3.115 fills the lender-of-last-resort slot; S3.132 adds certificates and paper as sources.

**Unit tests**: `market_route_costed_with_rollover_risk`; `repo_source_needs_free_collateral`;
`facility_reads_reserves_after_the_call`; `failure_fails_next_day`; `stage_order_market_then_facility`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-16 (S3.109) reads the order market → facility → 8f.

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 35 / 0 / 35 source values a day through K-35 × ≈ 1 µs. Counter `phx_bfl.liquidity_failures`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.04 / 0 / 0.04 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a facility drawn before the market meets; a facility drawn without the bank's request; a bank
kept alive past 8f by any route not declared.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Sources and actions declared; stage 8 ordered; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken;

### S3.111 — The central bank's committee sets its rate

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.2 STATE; CB.4 DECISION; CB.16 PRIMITIVE *(part: mandate, target and the rate rule)*
**Architecture**: §4.6 (policy values), §4.7 (decision points), §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S1.348 (K-100: the committee's decision and its founding-preference fallback), S1.209 (K-34: the
committee office), S1.179 (K-20: the dated policy schedule, announced and effective), S1.227 (K-43: the meeting
calendar), S1.336 (K-92: the central bank's own outlooks over public series), S1.215 (K-37: releases as published by
day d; the decision's record), S1.429 (retires its placeholder `CB.policy_rate_fixed`)
**Goal**: each central bank's committee meets on its own calendar and sets its policy rate from its own outlooks of
inflation and activity against the mandate and target its parliament set, by the rule it declares; the decision is a
dated announcement effective the next business day.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/points.rs` | the decision point `set_rate` (office: the central bank's committee) |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/rate.rs` | the declared rule over the committee's outlooks |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/rate.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/cb.rs` | 5c on meeting days; the announcement at 5d |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | mandate, target, employment weight (POLICY of parliament); rule, neutral real rate, inertia, rate grid, meeting calendar (POLICY of the central bank); committee hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the rule's form listed as POLICY of the central bank (Taylor, 1993; Clarida, Galí and Gertler, 2000; Orphanides, 2003) |

**Design**:
- **Mandate and target** (CB.2): price stability and, where the parliament gives it, employment; the target π*; each a
  K-20 schedule owned by the parliament. The rate decision is the central bank's alone.
- **When**: 5c on the committee's declared meeting days (K-43 dated entries from the calendar, TIME.3).
- **Inputs** (the committee's own view, Law 12): its outlook of inflation on the published consumer index with its
  lag (K-92 cell of the central bank's method over K-37 releases as published by that day, IDX.3 done at S1.14); its outlook
  of activity — the published unemployment rate and output — against its own experience-weighted long mean of each
  (the anchor heuristic; at the opening the snapshot's latest releases, VAL.10); the neutral real rate r̂ (POLICY,
  reviewed on its declared schedule, never an outlook of its own output); the previous rate.
- **Rule** (POLICY of the central bank, CB.16): `i* = r̂ + π̂ + φ_π·(π̂ − π*) + φ_u·(û* − û)`, then
  `i = ρ·i_prev + (1 − ρ)·i*`, rounded to the rate grid by its declared convention; φ_u is zero where the mandate
  names no employment goal — data, not a branch (Law 10). A country may declare another rule under the same point.
- **Output**: a K-20 schedule entry (owner the central bank, announced today, effective the next business day,
  VAL.6), a public K-37 record, the decision recorded with its decider (the committee's office is empty until S5.144:
  founding preferences, the placeholder in the stage's table). Retires `CB.policy_rate_fixed`.
- Review cost `CB.committee_hours` a meeting.

**Edge cases**: E5 — a meeting on a heavy day is one decision (`one_decision_per_meeting`). E6 — the schedule is K-20's saved
state (`schedule_roundtrip`, S1.179). E11 — the first meeting reads the snapshot's releases
(`first_meeting_reads_snapshot`). E12 — an index not yet published: the last published value, never a later one
(`rule_reads_the_lagged_index`).

**Extension points**: S3.112 (corridor widths follow the decision), S3.113 (the minimum bid rate), S3.178's purchases
read `i*` below the grid's floor; S8.173 converts the decision to an option generator.

**Unit tests**: `taylor_rule_inertia_and_grid`; `rule_reads_the_lagged_index`; `employment_weight_zero_by_mandate_data`;
`announcement_effective_next_business_day`; `one_decision_per_meeting`; `first_meeting_reads_snapshot`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-53 — every policy rate in force names its decision, its meeting day and the releases it read,
each published before that day (from the first meeting).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 8 meetings a year a country, ≈ 50 µs each. Counter `phx_cb.rate_decisions`.
on fin.calendar.cb_meeting (the committee's declared meeting days): 0.15 core-ms; joins H and B′
ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0001 MB resident (3 central banks × 16 B: inflation and activity outlooks and their
long means, `Fixed` i32 each)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a decision reading an unpublished index; a neutral rate read from the central bank's own output;
a branch on the mandate's kind.

### S3.112 — The corridor follows the rate; the central bank's collateral framework

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.6 DECISION; CB.7 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §4.6, §7.11 (K-81 administered form), §6.1 (5c, 8d, 8e), §8
**Depends on**: S3.111 (the rate), S3.103 (the haircut form), S1.319 (K-81: administered facilities with admission
hooks), S1.277 (K-63: liens on pledged collateral), S1.179 (K-20), S1.336 (K-92: the central bank's outlook widths),
S1.326 (K-86: marks and turnover), S1.429 (the facilities; retires its placeholders `CB.corridor_spread`,
`CB.eligible_collateral`, `CB.loan_haircut`), S2.185 (banks' own
requests at 8d), S1.239 (K-46 thresholds: a public default of an eligible
issuer wakes the framework review)
**Goal**: the deposit and lending facilities' rates move with each rate decision by the corridor's declared widths
and are met, with real quantities, only on banks' own requests at 8d; the central bank chooses on its framework
review which collateral it accepts and at what haircut, and publishes it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/points.rs` | the decision point `set_framework` (office: the central bank's committee) |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/collateral.rs` | eligibility and haircuts |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/markets.rs` | the two facilities as administered markets; their rate schedules follow `set_rate` |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/collateral.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | corridor widths, eligible asset classes and issuer kinds, z and liquidation horizon, review schedule (POLICY of the central bank) |

**Design**:
- **Corridor** (CB.7): deposit-facility rate = policy rate − its declared width, lending-facility rate = policy rate +
  its width, written as K-20 entries with the decision's effective day. The deposit facility pays its rate on
  reserves placed at 8d; the lending facility lends overnight at 8d against eligible collateral at its haircut,
  pledged as a K-63 lien released at repayment the next business day; both through K-81 with their quantity responses,
  only on a bank's own request (S2.185). Retires `CB.corridor_spread`.
- **Framework** (CB.6), on its quarterly review and on wakes (a public default of an eligible issuer, K-46):
  eligibility is declared data (asset classes, issuer kinds); a security's haircut is `z_cb·σ·sqrt(T_cb)` with σ the
  central bank's outlook width of its daily price change (K-92 over K-86) and `z_cb`, `T_cb` POLICY; bank loans it
  declares good for lender of last resort (S3.115) carry the same form over a named valuer's valuation (K-91). The
  framework is a public K-37 record and its haircuts a K-20 schedule in force. Retires `CB.eligible_collateral` and
  `CB.loan_haircut`.
- **Placeholder introduced**: eligibility reads no rating (naming RAT), retired by S3.215.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a security with no print: no haircut, not accepted until it has one (`framework_missing_print`). E3 — a
bank with no free eligible collateral gets nothing at the lending facility (K-81's `refused_beyond_headroom`, S1.319).
E6 — the framework record and schedules are saved (`schedule_roundtrip`, S1.179; `save_round_trip_as_published`,
S1.215). E13 — a country declaring no issuer kind of a class accepts none (`empty_class_accepts_none`).

**Extension points**: S3.113 (the tender's edges use the framework), S3.115 (loans declared good), S3.215 (ratings).

**Unit tests**: `corridor_moves_with_decision_by_widths`; `haircut_from_width_and_horizon`; `framework_missing_print`;
`lien_released_at_repayment`; `empty_class_accepts_none`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-54 — every facility use was a bank's request at 8d, at the rate in force that day, and every
lending-facility loan is pledged within the framework's haircuts (from the first use).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 150 / 0 / 150 facility requests × 100 ns (K-81); framework reviews quarterly, ≈ 2 k securities ×
200 ns. Counter `phx_cb.facility_uses`.
its share of fin.fixed.fund: 0.02 / 0 / 0.02 core-ms (B / NB / H)
on fin.calendar.cb_framework_review (quarterly, declared day): 0.4 core-ms; joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a facility drawn without a request; lending without collateral, rate or limit; one haircut for a
whole class.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Corridor and framework decided and applied; the three placeholders retired; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench
  with no ratchet broken; LC-3-54 passes.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.113 — The central bank's tenders inside the money market's call

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.12 MEASURE; CB.14 DECISION *(part: the regime and the tenders)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c, 8a–8c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.101 (the network call), S3.105 (banks' bids at the tender's tenor), S3.106 (repo rows), S3.112
(the framework's haircuts), S1.240 (K-47: the treasury's account and banknotes as maintained totals), S1.215 (K-37:
the treasury's announced auctions and redemptions), S1.336 (K-92)
**Goal**: the central bank declares how it implements its rate — a corridor with scarce reserves or a floor with
ample ones — and runs regular repo tenders sized from its own forecast of autonomous factors, met as one lender in
the money market's call, so market rates track the policy rate through the corridor and banks' own schedules.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/points.rs` | the decision point `size_operation` (office: the central bank's committee) |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/operations.rs` | tender size from the autonomous-factor forecast |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/markets.rs` | the tender node declared into the money market's markets |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/operations.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/cb.rs` | LC-3-03, LC-3-21 |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | regime, ample level, tender calendar and tenors, fine-tuning sensitivity (POLICY of the central bank); hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Bindseil, 2004) |

**Design**:
- **When**: 5c of each tender day (the declared calendar, K-43) and of any day its forecast's surprise exceeds its
  declared sensitivity (fine-tuning, a wake at 5c from yesterday's autonomous factors).
- **Size** under a corridor: `R_target − R_now − ΔA`, `ΔA` its adaptive outlook of the autonomous factors until the
  next tender (changes in the treasury's account and in banknotes, from K-47's maintained totals, with the treasury's
  announced auctions and redemptions entering on their dates from K-37), `R_target` its outlook of banks' demand at
  the policy rate (required reserves from S3.114 where declared, plus its outlook of the excess banks hold). Under a
  floor `R_target` is the declared ample level and the tender runs at full allotment.
- **In the call** (8a–8b): a lender node with capacity the size, an offer schedule from the minimum bid rate (the
  policy rate) upward, edges to banks' market nodes in the framework's repo segment under its haircuts (S3.112); at
  full allotment the rate is fixed and the capacity all the cash banks' assigned collateral raises — an administered
  price met inside the call (MKT.8). Banks bid by S3.105's term rule at the tender's tenor. Ties by `MMK.path_lot`.
  Matches settle at 8c as repo rows with the central bank as lender (S3.106, re-use not allowed).
- **CB.12** (measure): market rates track the policy rate because of the corridor and the banks' schedules, and the
  transmission of each decision to overnight prints, loan quotes, asset prices, investment and inflation with its
  lags, read from public records.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no bank bids: the tender allots nothing, a published result (`tender_no_bids_allots_nothing`). E6 — the
calendar and forecasts are saved (`rebuild_takes_same`, S1.227; `save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`, S1.196). E11 — no
record of autonomous factors: `ΔA` Missing, the tender sized only if the target exists (`tender_missing_forecast`).
E13 — a country declaring no tenders runs none (`no_tenders_declared_none`).

**Extension points**: S3.114 (required reserves in `R_target`); S5.179's foreign banks as participants.

**Unit tests**: `tender_size_from_autonomous_factors`; `tender_node_capacity_and_haircuts`;
`full_allotment_fixed_rate`; `fine_tuning_on_surprise_only`; `tender_no_bids_allots_nothing`; `tender_missing_forecast`; `no_tenders_declared_none`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-03 — CB.12: the transmission of rate decisions to overnight prints, bank funding costs, loan
quotes, asset prices, investment and inflation, with lags, is reported (asset-price and investment links registered,
not applicable until S3.147's share books print). LC-3-21 — each tender's forecast error of autonomous factors and banks'
facility use are published (from the first tender).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 1 tender a week a country (sizing ≈ 50 µs) and one lender node in the call. Counter
`phx_cb.tender_bids`.
on fin.calendar.cb_tender (the declared weekly tender day): 0.2 core-ms; joins H and B′
ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0001 MB resident (3 central banks × 16 B: autonomous-factor and excess-reserve
outlooks, mean and width, `Fixed` i32)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tender allotted outside the call; a market rate set equal to the policy rate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Tenders sized and met in the call; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-21 passes;
  LC-3-03 passes for the links that exist; the form listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.114 — Reserve requirements held on average

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.14 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6.1 (8e, 9c, 9e), §8
**Depends on**: S3.113 (the regime), S3.104 (`fund_position` reads the average owed), S1.243 (K-47: deposits owed per
bank and holder class), S1.196 (K-32: the bank's period columns), S1.237 (K-45: the penalty demand), S1.178 (K-19:
maintenance periods), S2.180 (the buffer reads the average owed)
**Goal**: where a country declares reserve requirements, each bank's requirement is set on its reservable
liabilities at each maintenance period's start and held on average over the period; a shortfall at its end is a
penalty demand due the next business day.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/requirements.rs` | the requirement, the running average, the penalty |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/requirements.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/cb.rs` | 8e close counted; 9c test; 9e demand |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | ratio, reservable classes, period calendar, penalty rate (POLICY of the central bank) |

**Design**:
- **Requirement** at the period's first business day: the declared ratio × the bank's reservable liabilities (K-47's
  maintained deposits owed by the declared classes), a bank column (K-32) for the period.
- **Average**: at 8e each business day, each bank's closing reserves are added to its period sum (a bank column;
  ≈ 35 banks, due-driven by the business day); non-business days count the last business day's close by the
  period's declared convention (POLICY). The average still owed to the period's end is the input `fund_position`
  (S3.104) and the buffer (S2.180) read.
- **Test** at 9c on the period's last day: shortfall × days × the penalty rate is a demand (K-45) due the next business
  day, applied at 9e; paid at stage 7 or failing as any demand. This completes CB.14.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a bank ending mid-period: its demand goes to its estate (`penalty_to_estate`). E5 — a period ending on a
heavy day tests ≈ 35 banks (`maintenance_average_owed`). E6 — period sums are saved columns
(`save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`, S1.196). E13 — a country with no requirement declared: nothing runs
(`no_requirement_none`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `maintenance_average_owed`; `penalty_on_shortfall_only`; `closed_days_count_by_convention`; `penalty_to_estate`; `no_requirement_none`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-55 — every penalty names its period, its requirement and the bank's average (from the first
period end).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 35 / 0 / 35 period sums at 8e × 20 ns; 35 tests × 1 µs on a period's last day. Counter
`phx_cb.reserve_penalties`.
its share of fin.fixed.fund: 0.001 / 0 / 0.001 core-ms (B / NB / H)
on fin.calendar.maintenance_end (each declared period's last business day): 0.04 core-ms; joins H and B′
ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0006 MB resident (35 banks × 18 B: requirement i64, period sum i64, days counted u16)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a requirement read as a floor on a balance; a penalty paid the day it is issued.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Requirements set, averaged and tested; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-55
  passes or is not yet applicable.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.115 — The lender of last resort

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6.1 (8d), §9.2, §8
**Depends on**: S3.110 (the slot after the lending facility), S3.112 (the framework, loans declared good), S1.319
(K-81: the admission hook), S1.277 (K-63: liens), S1.335 (K-91: a valuer's valuation of loans), S2.106 (the loan-book
valuer), S2.184 (the bank's shortfall actions), S2.192 (the supervisor's solvency fact)
**Goal**: a bank still short after the market and the lending facility may ask its central bank; it is lent freely
against good collateral at a penalty rate when the supervisor holds it solvent that day, and refused otherwise, when
it goes to resolution. The four conditions are declared, visible data.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/markets.rs` | the lender-of-last-resort market (K-81) and its admission hook |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/lolr.rs` | the hook over the declared conditions |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/lolr.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | the conditions and the penalty (POLICY of the central bank) |
| `data/<country>/BFL.toml` | the request as a declared shortfall action after the facility |

**Design**:
- **Request** (8d, the bank's own action in its shortfall order, S2.184): its remaining shortfall after the lending
  facility.
- **Admission hook** (K-81), the declared conditions in order: the supervisor's solvency fact that day says solvent
  (S2.192); collateral from the framework and loans it declares good (S3.112), each at its haircut over its mark or a
  named valuer's valuation (K-91, S2.106); rate = lending-facility rate + declared penalty; quantity = what the
  collateral carries after haircuts ("freely"). A country may declare other conditions; the list is a public record.
- **Grant**: a loan row of the central bank's facility family (K-53) with liens (K-63), repaid the next business day
  or rolled on a new request; settled at 8e. **Refusal**: the bank fails at 8f (S3.110) and goes to resolution.

**Edge cases**: E1 — several banks at once: each request meets the hook alone and they commute
(`lolr_requests_commute`). E2 — no collateral left: nothing lent, refused (`lolr_quantity_what_collateral_carries`).
E6 — the loan rows are saved (`contracts_roundtrip`, S1.257). E12 — no solvency fact for the day: refused by the
declared condition (`lolr_missing_fact_refuses`).

**Extension points**: S5.184's swap lines lend foreign currency through the same form.

**Unit tests**: `lolr_conditions_as_data`; `lolr_quantity_what_collateral_carries`; `lolr_missing_fact_refuses`; `lolr_requests_commute`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-19 — CB.8: every lender-of-last-resort loan went to a bank the supervisor held solvent that
day, and every refused request's bank entered resolution (from the first request).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 0 / 0 / 0 on an ordinary day; on a run day ≈ 35 requests × ≈ 1 µs. Counter `phx_cb.lolr`.
on fin.calendar.bank_run (an E1 event day): 0.04 core-ms; joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; lending to a bank without the solvency fact; lending without collateral or penalty; an insolvent
bank kept alive.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The hook and loans; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-19 passes or is not yet
  applicable.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.116 — The financing regime and the treasury's direct borrowing

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.3 STATE; CB.9 PROCESS; CB.13 FORBID; CB.16 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §4.6, §6.1 (8d, 8e), §8
**Depends on**: S3.112 (the lending forms), S1.319 (K-81), S1.338 (K-93: the regime's limit), S1.179 (K-20: the
regime as a dated schedule owned by the parliament), S1.432 (the primary auction's participants), S1.431 (retires its placeholder `TRS.never_borrows_from_cb`)
**Goal**: each country's parliament declares whether its central bank may never fund the treasury, may buy its debt
only in the secondary market, or may lend to it directly within a limit and at a rate; the treasury's direct loan is
its own request met by the administered form within that regime, and the central bank never bids at its own
sovereign's primary auctions.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/markets.rs` | the treasury's direct facility (K-81) with the regime's limit |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/regime.rs` | the regime read as limits and eligibility, never a branch |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/regime.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc52.rs` | PC-52 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc140.rs` | PC-140 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/cb.rs` | LC-3-18 |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | the financing regime: secondary purchases allowed, direct lending limit and rate (POLICY of the parliament) |

**Design**:
- **Regime** (CB.3): declared values in a K-20 schedule owned by the parliament: a K-93 declared limit on the central
  bank's direct claims on its treasury (zero where direct lending is not allowed), the rate of direct lending, and
  whether its own sovereign's debt is in the purchases' eligible set (read by S3.178's purchases). Retires
  `TRS.never_borrows_from_cb`.
- **Direct lending** (CB.9): the treasury's request at 8d (its decision, S3.122) met by K-81 within the limit's
  headroom at the declared rate, settled at 8e: the treasury's account rises; reserves and deposits are created as it
  spends (settlement, MON.6). Purchases create reserves and sales destroy them by the same settlement (S3.178
  trades them).
- **CB.13**: no participation in its own sovereign's primary auctions (PC-52); no lending without collateral, rate and
  limit (PC-140); no financing beyond the regime (the K-93 limit binds, an event); no purchase sized by an auction
  (S3.178's purchases name their programme); no market rate equal to the policy rate by construction (S3.104).
- **CB.16** completes: mandate, target and regime (parliament); rule, framework and implementation regime (the
  central bank), each a primitive with its owner.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a request beyond the headroom lends only the headroom (`direct_lending_bound_by_regime`). E6 — the
regime schedule is saved (`schedule_roundtrip`, S1.179). E12 — no regime declared is refused at assembly
(`regime_absent_refused`). E13 — a regime of "never": every request refused (`never_regime_refuses`).

**Extension points**: S3.122 (the request), S3.178's purchases (eligibility), S5.166's regime changes by
parliament (POL).

**Unit tests**: `direct_lending_bound_by_regime`; `never_regime_refuses`; `regime_changes_on_effective_day`; `regime_absent_refused`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-18 — CB.13: no central-bank order at its own primary auction; every central-bank loan is
collateralised within its haircuts, priced at an announced rate and within the regime's limit (from the first loan).

**Budget**:

### S3.117 — The central bank's income and its remittance

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.1 STATE *(part: the domestic balance sheet; foreign reserves and claims on central banks at S5.165)*;
CB.10 PROCESS *(part: remittance and a loss kept against equity; S3.126 makes it good)*
**Architecture**: §7.12 (phx-acct: K-87, K-88, K-89, K-90), §6.1 (9b, 9c, 9e), §8
**Depends on**: S1.328 (K-87: lines), S1.330 (K-88: equity), S1.332 (K-89: unrealised differences never remitted),
S1.333 (K-90: the central bank's statements on its calendar), S1.237 (K-45: the remittance due), S1.429 (the Stage 1
remittance this replaces)
**Goal**: the central bank's balance sheet is its accounts, holdings and contracts as they are; on each remittance
date its realised net income is due to the treasury the next business day, unrealised gains stay in equity, and a
loss is carried against equity, which may fall below zero.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/remit.rs` | realised net income from the period's statement; the remittance |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/remit.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/cb.rs` | 9c on remittance dates; 9e the demand |

**Design**:
- **Balance sheet** (CB.1, a read): reserves, banknotes and the treasury's account (K-47 accounts at the issuer);
  securities (instrument holdings, S1.280); loans to banks and the treasury (K-53); equity (K-88).
- **Remittance** (9c on each declared date): realised net income of the period from its statement (K-90 close at 9b;
  K-87 lines: interest earned on loans and securities, paid on the deposit facility and reserves, operating costs) —
  unrealised revaluation (K-89) excluded — is a demand from the treasury (K-45) due the next business day, applied at
  9e, paid at stage 7. A negative realised result is no remittance: the loss stays against equity (K-88), which may go
  below zero (Law 13).

**Edge cases**: E6 — statements and the due demand are saved (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237). E11 — the first period
starts from the opening's balance sheet (`first_period_from_opening`). E14 — a remittance date on a rate-decision
day: the statement closes before 9c (`statement_before_remittance`).

**Extension points**: S3.126 reads the equity against the floor; S5.165 adds foreign reserves and their revaluation
account.

**Unit tests**: `remittance_excludes_unrealised_gains`; `loss_kept_against_equity`; `first_period_from_opening`; `statement_before_remittance`.

auction)
**Goal**: besides bills, each sovereign issues fixed-coupon and inflation-linked bonds, each a line that can be
reopened; the line and every tranche added to it are distinct records, and an indexed bond's principal follows the
published consumer index with its declared lag.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/families.rs` | the fixed and indexed bond families (K-21 declarations, K-55 shapes); the tranche record kind |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/tests/families.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/SOV.toml` | coupon frequency, day count, indexation lag, benchmark maturities (POLICY of the treasury, SOV.10) |

**Design**:
- **Families** (K-21, REG.5): bill (discount, S1.432), fixed-coupon bond (coupons on the schedule placed by advancing
  dates, TIME.3; day count by the terms, TIME.4; bullet redemption), inflation-linked bond (principal × index ratio,
  the index read "as published by day d" with the declared lag, K-55's indexed leg; the current fixing a term,
  REG.5). Every family: pari passu, no covenants, not callable (SOV.2's terms), cross-default across the issuer's lines
  by terms (read by S3.123).
- **Line and tranche**: a line is one K-64 instrument; a reopening raises its issued amount by the named event
  "tranche" (REG.3), and each tranche is a K-37 record (line, issue day, amount, auction price, settlement day). Coupons
  and redemptions are K-65 events on their dates to holders of record at the day's start (REG.11).
- **Issue**: a new line is issued (K-64 `issue`) at its first auction's settlement, never before.

**Edge cases**: E6 — instruments, tranche records and events are saved (`issued_changed_only_by_events`, S1.279;
`holders_rebuilt_equal`, S1.280; `save_round_trip_as_published`, S1.215). E8 — lines and tranches grow only with
auctions: ≈ 1.5 k lines and ≈ 4 k tranche records over two years, never reused (`ids_never_reused`, S1.279). E12 — an
index not yet published for the lag month: the fixing stays the last published (`indexed_principal_with_lag`). E13 —
before S3.142's opening data the sovereign holds bills only; its first bond line opens at its first bond auction
(`first_line_at_first_auction`).

**Extension points**: S3.121 auctions lines; S3.125 buys back and switches them; S3.166's dealers trade them;
S4.120's bond futures deliver them.

**Unit tests**: `indexed_principal_with_lag`; `reopening_adds_tranche_record_and_amount`;
`coupon_dates_by_advancing`; `first_line_at_first_auction`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-22 at S3.121 reads issued amounts).

**Budget**:

largest line). Counter `phx_sov.line_events`.

### S3.119 — The treasury's forward funding plan and its auction calendar

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TRS.2 DECISION; SOV.3 DECISION
**Architecture**: §4.6, §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.118 (families and lines), S1.348 (K-100: the treasury's minister), S1.227 (K-43: the plan's
review), S1.239 (K-46: surprise wakes), S1.336 (K-92: its own outlooks of outlays and receipts), S1.254 (K-52: its
receipts and outlays by reason and period), S1.341 (K-95: redemptions and coupons by exact date), S1.240 (K-47: its
cash), S1.215 (K-37: announcements), S1.431 (retires its placeholder `TRS.funding_rule`, the plan)
**Goal**: the treasury forecasts its own outlays, receipts and redemptions, keeps a buffer it chooses under its
mandate, and schedules auctions of chosen sizes and maturities ahead of the money leaving, announced in advance.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/points.rs` | the decision point `plan_funding` (office: the treasury's minister) |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/plan.rs` | need, buffer, split and calendar |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/tests/plan.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/trs.rs` | 5c review; 5d announcements |
| `data/<country>/TRS.toml` | plan horizon and review schedule, notice period, auction days per family (POLICY of the treasury); review hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (IMF and World Bank, 2014; Williams, 2004) |

**Design**:
- **When**: the plan's quarterly review (K-43) and wakes (K-46): a failed auction (S3.121), a surprise in receipts or
  outlays beyond its declared sensitivity.
- **Inputs**: its own outlooks of outlays and receipts per category and calendar period (K-92, adaptive over its own
  records of the same period, K-52 tallies, VAL.6); redemptions and coupons over the horizon (K-95 exact sums by date
  over its instruments); announced policy changes from their effective day (K-20); its cash (K-47); its mandate
  (TRS.9: issuance shares by family and maturity, benchmark sizes, cover `z_T`).
- **Need** over horizon H: redemptions + its outlook of the deficit + the buffer it chooses − cash.
- **Buffer, chosen** (TRS.2's "a buffer it chooses"): the level B where the treasury's own outlook of the chance that
  cumulative net outflows over an auction interval exceed B (mean and width of its outlook of its own surprises),
  times its own outlook of what a shortfall costs it (an extra auction's cost, or direct central-bank lending where the
  regime allows), equals the carry of holding B (its borrowing cost at the plan's maturities less what its account
  earns), scaled by the treasury's buffer appetite (PREFERENCE, its founding preferences until S5.144 fills the
  minister's office). The mandate's cover (TRS.9, POLICY) is a K-93 declared limit: a chosen B below it binds the
  limit, an event the treasury sees (Law 6), and it holds the cover.
- **Sizes and maturities, chosen**: the need is spread over bills, fixed and indexed bonds and benchmark maturities
  inside the ranges the mandate's issuance shares declare, by the treasury's own outlook of each maturity's cost
  (the day's curve, S3.127 from its build, else its outlook over auction prints) plus its outlook of rollover risk
  (the width of its outlook of that maturity's yield at the next roll); a benchmark line is reopened until it reaches
  its declared size, then a new line. The form — a forward funding plan choosing cost against refinancing risk with a
  precautionary buffer (IMF and World Bank, 2014; Williams, 2004; Poole, 1968 for the buffer) — is listed.
- **Calendar** (SOV.3): auctions on the declared days per family, each sized as its share of the need, announced as a
  public K-37 record at least the notice period before; the auction's meeting is a dated K-42 entry for its market.
- Retires `TRS.funding_rule` for the plan (its shortfall half at S3.122). The minister's office is read at the treasury's founding
  preferences until S5.144 fills it (as S1.432 left it). Replaces `SOV.size` (S1.432's minister's size) by the plan's
  calendar.

**Edge cases**: E6 — announcements and the plan's columns are saved (`save_round_trip_as_published`, S1.215;
`save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`, S1.196). E11 — the first review reads the opening's records and the snapshot's
fiscal releases (`plan_first_review_reads_snapshot`). E13 — a mandate that admits no indexed share: none issued
(`no_indexed_share_none`). E14 — a wake on the review day is one decision (`one_decision_per_day`).

**Extension points**: S3.122 (shortfall), S3.126 (an outlay for the central bank's loss), S5.146 (the minister's
options).

**Unit tests**: `plan_need_and_buffer`; `buffer_chosen_by_cost_and_carry`; `cover_binds_as_event`;
`maturity_mix_by_cost_and_rollover_risk`; `plan_reopens_until_benchmark_size`; `calendar_respects_notice`; `plan_first_review_reads_snapshot`; `no_indexed_share_none`; `one_decision_per_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-23 — TRS.2 and TRS.8: every auction was announced at least its notice before; the treasury
account never closed below zero; every outlay names its recipient (from the first plan).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 3 treasuries, quarterly reviews and wakes, ≈ 100 µs each with K-95 reads over ≈ 1 k dates. Counter
`phx_trs.plan_reviews`.
on fin.calendar.trs_plan_review (each treasury's declared quarterly day): 0.3 core-ms; joins H and B′
ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0002 MB resident (3 treasuries × 72 B: outlooks of outlays and receipts by eight
categories, mean and width `Fixed` i32; buffer target i64)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a deficit target that sets anything; an auction sized by anything but the plan.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The plan and calendar decided; placeholder retired for the plan; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no
  ratchet broken; LC-3-23 passes; the form listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.120 — Bidders' own schedules at sovereign auctions

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.4 DECISION *(part: banks and firms; households at S3.158, funds at S3.191, primary dealers at S3.171,
insurers at S4.137, pension schemes at S4.155, reserve managers at S5.169)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (rule handles), §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.118 (lines), S3.119 (announcements), S3.108 (firms' placements, to which this step adds bills and bonds at auction as a declared
alternative), S1.357 (K-105: the
investor schedule), S1.348 (K-100), S1.296 (K-70: orders), S1.336 (K-92: outlooks of short rates and of the
sovereign's default), S1.179 (K-20: announced rates), S2.102 (`loan_claim_value`), S1.432 (the bank's bill bid
kept)
**Goal**: at every auction each bidder posts a schedule from its own value of the line, its funding and what it
holds; banks value through their own assessment, other bidders through their own outlooks, and nobody bids for
anyone else.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/points.rs` | the decision point `SOV.bid` (S1.432's), a rule per bidder kind registered by data |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules/bid.rs` | the value and the schedule |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/tests/bid.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sov.rs` | 5c bids on auction days |
| `data/<country>/SOV.toml` | bidder kinds admitted per family; risk aversion per bidder kind (PREFERENCE) |

**Design**:
- **When**: 5c of each auction day, for each party whose kind the auction admits and whose own decision asks for it:
  every bank; a firm whose placement chose bills or bonds at this auction (the alternative this step declares for
  S3.108, its yield the firm's outlook over auction prints); later kinds as they register.
- **Value** (VAL.8): the line's claim value — its coupons and redemption discounted at the bidder's outlook of short
  rates (announcements from their effective day, K-20), weighted by its outlook of the sovereign's default and
  recovery over its horizon; for a bank through `loan_claim_value` under its one assessment of the sovereign (PC-40;
  sovereign defaults are public events). A bank's bill bids keep S1.432's liquidity form. A non-bank bidder's value
  is its method's: computed once per (bidder method, line) a day and read by every bidder using it (K-92 cells).
- **Order**: the investor schedule (K-105) at that value with the bidder's outlook width, risk aversion, holding, funds
  and free units; a K-70 order into the auction's call. The issuing country's central bank is refused by the
  participants rule (PC-52).

**Edge cases**: E3 — a firm with no placement posts nothing (`no_order_without_decision`). E6 — orders live 5c→6a only and
never cross a save (`orders_do_not_cross_save`). E12 — no default seen: the recovery term is the snapshot's published
statistics, never zero (`bid_from_claim_value_and_default_outlook`). E14 — a bank at two lines' auctions one day
posts one order per line from one view (`one_view_two_orders`).

**Extension points**: S3.158 (households), S3.171 (primary dealers), S3.191 (funds), S4.137 (insurers), S4.155
(pension schemes), S5.169 (reserve managers)

### S3.121 — Bond auctions and the auction that fails

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.10 PRIMITIVE; SOV.9 FORBID *(part: no forced buyer, no residual absorber, no yield that sets a
price)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-76 call auction), §6.1 (6a, 6b), §8
**Depends on**: S3.118, S3.119, S3.120, S1.312 (K-76: uniform price, largest-remainder rationing, unfilled not
issued), S1.313 (the bill auction on K-76), S1.251 (K-50: settlement commitments), S1.213 (K-36: the failure event),
S1.326 (K-86: prints)
**Goal**: bonds and indexed bonds are sold, like bills, in uniform-price call auctions of the declared format; weak
demand shows as a higher yield, a long tail and low cover or as the treasury cutting the size; unsold paper is not
issued and is an event.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/markets.rs` | auction markets per line; the format; the primary-dealer contract family |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules/supply.rs` | the treasury's supply schedule at its reservation |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/tests/auction.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/sov.rs` | LC-3-22 |
| `data/<country>/SOV.toml` | format, lots, ticks, settlement, the primary-dealer contract's terms (POLICY of the treasury, SOV.10) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the supply rule's form |

**Design**:
- **Market** per line (K-21, MKT.21): K-76 uniform price at 6a of the announced day; rationing at the price by largest
  remainder, ties by lot on `SOV.allot` (subject: the line, day); settlement on the declared convention (K-50
  commitments until then, SET.2).
- **Supply**: the treasury's order is the announced size at prices at or above its reservation — its own outlook of its
  cost of borrowing at that maturity from its alternatives (the next auction, direct central-bank lending where the
  regime allows, S3.116) — so a weak book issues less, "the treasury cutting the size" (SOV.6).
- **Results** (6b): the print (K-86); cover (bids ÷ size) and tail (average accepted less the stop-out price) as
  public K-37 records; unsold size is not issued and is a K-36 event (MKT.10) that wakes the plan (S3.119), and later the
  shortfall protocol that registers for it. Yields are statistics of prices, never inputs.
- **SOV.10 completes**: formats, the primary-dealer contract family (undertaking to bid at every auction; privileges as
  terms; its dealers' side is S3.171) and the indexation lag (S3.118) are the treasury's declared POLICY.

**Edge cases**: E2 — an auction with no orders issues nothing: the whole size is the failure event (`auction_zero_orders`). E6 —
commitments until settlement are K-50 rows (`commit_roundtrip`, S1.251). E7 — rationing ties by lot, never by arrival
(K-76's `same_allotment_any_order`, S1.312). E13 — a family a country does not issue has no market
(`no_family_no_market`).

**Extension points**: S3.125's reverse auctions; S3.171's primary dealers.

**Unit tests**: `supply_cuts_below_reservation`; `auction_zero_orders`; `cover_and_tail_from_orders`;
`unsold_not_issued`; `no_family_no_market`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-22 — SOV.6 and SOV.9: every auction's issued amount equals what it sold; every unsold offer is a
published event; every order names its bidder's decision point (from the first bond auction).

steps) × 100 ns + 2 µs a call. Counters `phx_sov.auctions`, `phx_sov.failed_auctions`.

### S3.122 — The treasury's answer to a failed auction

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TRS.3 DECISION *(part: the buffer drawn, the extra auction and central-bank financing; the choice among
them as the minister's options and the deferral of outlays at S5.145)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c, 8d), §8
**Depends on**: S3.119 (the plan), S3.121 (the failure event), S3.116 (direct lending within the regime), S1.319
(K-81: the request), S1.239 (K-46: the wake), S1.431 (retires its placeholder `TRS.funding_rule`, the shortfall half)
**Goal**: when an auction falls short, the treasury, on the next business day, pays from its buffer, returns at
another size or maturity, or — where its country's regime allows — asks for central-bank financing, by its declared
protocol and its own outlooks of each option's cost.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/shortfall.rs` | the protocol |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/tests/shortfall.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/trs.rs` | 5c after the failure; 8d the request |
| `data/<country>/TRS.toml` | the protocol's order and the buffer's minimum (POLICY of the treasury) |

**Design**:
- **When**: 5c of the business day after an auction that sold less than offered (K-46 wake by the event).
- **Protocol** (POLICY of the treasury): (1) draw the buffer down to its declared minimum (the next days' statutory
  outlays from its outlook); (2) for the rest, the cheapest by its own outlooks of: an extra auction the next business
  day at another size or maturity (a longer bill, a reopened bond line), and, where the regime allows, direct lending
  at the regime's rate within its limit (a K-81 request at 8d, S3.116); (3) defer discretionary purchases (the
  placeholder naming SOC, retired by S5.145). The protocol's fixed order stands for the minister's choice among these
  options (a placeholder naming POL, retired by S5.145, which completes TRS.3). The form is listed with the plan's.
- **Outputs**: an announced extra auction (K-37, K-42 entry) or a request; the plan's next review woken.
- Retires `TRS.funding_rule`'s shortfall half (S1.431).

**Edge cases**: E2 — the extra auction fails too: the protocol runs again the next day (`protocol_reruns_after_failure`). E6 —
the request and announcements are saved dated rows (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237). E13 — a regime of "never":
direct lending is not an option (`regime_excludes_direct_lending`).

**Extension points**: S5.145 (the minister's options, completing TRS.3).

**Unit tests**: `shortfall_protocol_order`; `return_at_another_maturity`; `regime_excludes_direct_lending`; `protocol_reruns_after_failure`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-23, LC-3-25 read the outcomes).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: one decision after each failed auction (0 on most days) × ≈ 50 µs. Counter `phx_trs.shortfalls`.
on fin.calendar.failed_auction (the business day after an auction that sold less than offered): 0.05 core-ms; joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an automatic central-bank overdraft; a statutory payment cut outside the declared priority.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The protocol answers failures; placeholder retired; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.123 — Debt service in the declared payment priority, and sovereign default

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TRS.8 FORBID; TRS.10 PRIMITIVE; TRS.5 PROCESS *(part: default in the sovereign's own currency; foreign
currency at S5.170)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c, 7, 2d, 2e), §9.1 (the sovereign's ending), §8
**Depends on**: S3.118 (cross-default terms), S3.122 (the funding it can reach), S1.248 (K-49: suffix failure by
payment order), S1.180 (K-21: reasons' payment order), S1.281 (K-65: the default event on the instruments), S1.265
(K-56: missed payments and grace), S1.213 (K-36: public events), S1.431 (the treasury's flows and TRS.10's part)
**Goal**: a treasury whose cash, reachable funding and outlook of receipts fall short of a day's payments pays in
the order its parliament declared; a coupon or redemption it cannot pay fails, and past the bond's grace is the
sovereign's default on every line — which in its own currency happens only where the regime and the market leave it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/service.rs` | the day's payments ranked by the declared priority |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/default.rs` | a failed service past grace → the sovereign's default |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/tests/service.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/trs.rs` | 5c the day before a service date; 2e the default |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/trs.rs` | LC-3-25 |
| `data/<country>/TRS.toml` | the payment priority (POLICY of the parliament, TRS.10) |

**Design**:
- **Priority** (TRS.10): the parliament's order — for example statutory payments, debt service, wages, benefits,
  purchases — is the payment order of the treasury's reasons (K-21 data), which settlement applies when the treasury
  is short (K-49's suffix failure by payment order, SET.6). There is no other default decision (TRS.5).
- **The day before a service date** (5c): if its cash plus funding still reachable (settling auctions, the regime's
  headroom) plus its outlook of receipts fall short of the next day's payments, the payments are posted in that
  priority; the treasury account has no facility (MON.3) and never closes below zero (TRS.8).
- **Default** (2d/2e): a coupon or redemption failed at stage 7 is recorded at 2d against the instrument's event
  (K-56); past the terms' grace it is the sovereign's default at 2e: a K-65 default event on every line by
  cross-default, and a public K-36 event naming the failed leg, the regime and the funding it could not reach.
  Holdings keep their claims; each later event fails as it falls due until an exchange (S3.124).
- **TRS.8 completes**: no automatic overdraft, no forced buyer (S3.121), no deficit target (S3.119), no outlay or
  receipt to an aggregate (every flow names its counterparty, S1.431).

**Edge cases**: E1 — default on every line at once: one event per line (`cross_default_every_line`). E6 — arrears and events
saved (`history_before_free`, S1.265; `holders_rebuilt_equal`, S1.280). E10 — holders that are estates keep their
claims (`estate_holder_keeps_claim`). E14 — two payments of one rank the same day: ties by lot in settlement (K-49's
`order_then_lot`, S1.248).

**Extension points**: S3.124 (the exchange), S5.170 (foreign-currency default completes TRS.5).

**Unit tests**: `payment_priority_as_data`; `default_only_past_grace`; `cross_default_every_line`; `estate_holder_keeps_claim`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-25 — TRS.5 and TRS.10: every sovereign default names its failed leg, its country's regime, the
funding it could not reach and the declared priority that left the leg unpaid; a run with no default passes it
vacuously, and the report says so.

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: the day before each service date (≈ 3 a week) one ranking × ≈ 10 µs; a default is one event a line.
Counter `phx_trs.defaults`.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

### S3.124 — The exchange offer after a default, holdouts and collective action

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TRS.5 PROCESS *(part: the exchange offer, holdouts and collective action; foreign-currency default at S5.170)*
**Architecture**: §7.6 (K-41 tallies), §7.11 (K-80 protocol), §6.1 (5c, 7), §8
**Depends on**: S3.123 (the default event), S3.118 (the new lines' families), S1.317 (K-80: offer and answers with a
deadline), S1.237 (K-45), S1.224 (K-41: acceptances by face per line), S1.280 (K-65: holders of record), S1.279 (K-64:
old units retired, new issued), S1.245 (K-48: one link group per line), S1.357 (K-105), S2.102 (`loan_claim_value`)
**Goal**: after a default the treasury offers new bonds sized to what it can service; each holder accepts or holds
out by its own values; where acceptances reach a line's collective-action threshold every holder of that line is
bound, and otherwise holdouts keep the defaulted bonds.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/points.rs` | `offer_exchange` (office: the treasury's minister); `answer_exchange` (every holder kind) |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules/exchange.rs` | the offer's terms; the holder's answer |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/tests/exchange.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sov.rs` | 5c offer; answers by deadline; 7 settlement |
| `data/<country>/SOV.toml` | the offer's horizon and deadline (POLICY of the treasury); answer hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms (IMF, 2013; Pitchford and Wright, 2012) |

**Design**:
- **Offer** (5c after the default, the minister): new bonds whose service over the declared horizon fits its
  outlook of receipts less statutory outlays: face reduced by `1 − PV(affordable service) ÷ PV(contractual service)`,
  discounted at its outlook of its pre-default borrowing cost; a K-80 offer to every holder of record of each
  defaulted line (K-65 holder list) with the deadline.
- **Answer** (each holder, by the deadline): accept when its own value of the new bond (VAL.8 at its outlooks; a
  bank's through `loan_claim_value`) is at least its value of holding out — the old claim at its own recovery outlook
  (recoveries it has seen; with none, the offer itself, VAL.10). An estate answers in its administrator's office like
  any holder. A non-bank holder's two values are its method's, computed once per (holder method, line).
- **Tally** (K-41) by face per line at the deadline; at or above the line's terms' threshold every holder is bound;
  below it only acceptors exchange. Settlement at stage 7: one link group per line — old units retired and new issued
  (K-64's named events), holdouts untouched; their bonds' events keep failing.
- Market exclusion is never declared: bidders' own assessments carry the default (S3.120).

**Edge cases**: E2 — no holder accepts: nothing exchanged, the line stays defaulted (`below_threshold_only_acceptors`). E4/E10 — an
estate holder answers through its administrator; a holder ending before the deadline answers through its estate
(`estate_answers_through_administrator`). E6 — the offer and answers are saved messages (`save_round_trip_messages`,
S1.237). E14 — a holder of several lines answers per line (`answers_per_line`).

**Extension points**: S3.125's switches reuse the answer rule; S5.148 takes the offer as the minister's options;
S5.170 completes TRS.5 for foreign-currency debt; S8.176 converts the holders' answers.

**Unit tests**: `exchange_haircut_from_affordable_service`; `holdout_versus_accept`;
`collective_action_threshold_binds_line`; `below_threshold_only_acceptors`; `estate_answers_through_administrator`; `answers_per_line`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-56 — every exchange names its offer, the acceptances by face and the threshold; bound holders
only where the threshold was met (vacuous without a default, and the report says so).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 0 on an ordinary day. Counter `phx_sov.exchange_answers`.
on fin.calendar.exchange_deadline (an offer's deadline, a count of business days after a sovereign default): 1 core-ms (≈ 50 k holders of every line × ≈ 20 ns, each comparing its method's value with the offer); joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a holder answering for others; a declared market exclusion; holdouts retired.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Offer, answers, tally and settlement; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-56 passes
  or is vacuous; forms listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
