### S3.125 — Buybacks and switches

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.2 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-76 reverse call, K-80), §6.1 (5c, 6a), §8
**Depends on**: S3.118 (lines, not callable), S3.119 (buffer target), S3.124 (the answer rule), S1.312 (K-76: the
reverse variant), S1.317 (K-80), S1.357 (K-105), S1.279 (K-64: buyback retires units)
**Goal**: the treasury manages its curve by buying back lines maturing soon when its cash exceeds its buffer, in
reverse call auctions limited at its own value, and by offering holders switches into new lines they accept or
refuse by their own values; its debt stays pari passu, covenant-free and uncallable.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules/operations.rs` | the buyback order and the switch ratio |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/tests/operations.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sov.rs` | 5c review; 6a reverse call; 5c switch answers |
| `data/<country>/SOV.toml` | smoothing horizon, notice (POLICY of the treasury) |

**Design**:
- **When**: the monthly operations review of the minister (K-43).
- **Buyback**: with cash above its buffer target (S3.119), lines maturing within the declared smoothing horizon are
  bought in a K-76 reverse call at 6a; the treasury's bid is limited at its own value (discounted at its funding-cost
  outlook); holders' offers are their investor schedules (K-105) by S3.120's rule on the sell side; ties by lot on
  `SOV.operations_lot`. Bought units retire (K-64 "buyback").
- **Switch** (MKT.7): the treasury offers holders of an old line units of a new line at a ratio of its own values
  (K-80, deadline the next 5c); each holder answers by S3.124's answer rule over its values of both lines.
- **SOV.2 completes**: pari passu, no covenants, not callable (S3.118's terms), and the curve managed by these
  operations.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no holder offers: nothing bought (`reverse_auction_limit_at_own_value`). E6 — switch offers are saved
messages (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237). E13 — no cash above the buffer: no buyback (`no_surplus_no_buyback`).

**Extension points**: S5.149 takes buybacks and switches as the minister's options.

**Unit tests**: `reverse_auction_limit_at_own_value`; `switch_answer_from_own_values`; `buyback_retires_units`; `no_surplus_no_buyback`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-22 covers every auction's order provenance).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: a monthly operation a country, ≈ 2 k offers × 100 ns + 2 µs. Counter `phx_sov.buybacks`.
on fin.calendar.trs_operations (each treasury's declared monthly day): 0.2 core-ms; joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a call on a line; a switch forced on a holder.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Buybacks and switches; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.126 — The treasury makes good a central bank's loss

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.10 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.117 (the loss kept against equity, published in the central bank's statements), S3.119 (the plan
that funds the transfer), S1.348 (K-100), S1.215 (K-37: the central bank's published statement)
**Goal**: when its central bank's published equity is below the floor its mandate names, the treasury decides on its
plan's review a transfer restoring it, funded as an outlay to a named party; a floor declared absent leaves the loss
carried.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/points.rs` | `make_good_cb_loss` (office: the treasury's minister) |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/cb_loss.rs` | the transfer |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/tests/cb_loss.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/TRS.toml` | the central bank's equity floor, or none (POLICY of the parliament) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Stella, 2005) |

**Design**:
- **When**: the plan's review (S3.119) reading the central bank's latest published statement (K-37).
- **Rule**: if equity < floor, a transfer of `floor − equity` is an outlay of the plan's next period to the central
  bank (a named recipient, TRS.4), paid at stage 7 on its date; the central bank's equity rises by the transfer (K-88,
  a named event). No floor declared: nothing. This completes CB.10.

**Edge cases**: E6 — the planned outlay is a saved dated row (`refile_after_load_equals`, S1.225). E12 — no statement published
yet: nothing decided (`no_statement_no_decision`). E13 — no floor declared: the loss is carried
(`no_floor_carries_loss`).

**Extension points**: S5.147 (the minister's options).

**Unit tests**: `cb_loss_made_good_to_floor`; `no_floor_carries_loss`; `no_statement_no_decision`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-20 reads remittances; LC-3-23 reads named outlays).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 3 decisions a quarter × ≈ 10 µs, on the plan's review. Counter `phx_trs.cb_transfers`.
on fin.calendar.trs_plan_review (each treasury's declared quarterly day): 0.03 core-ms; joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

### S3.127 — The curve publisher and the day's discount-factor tables

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.9 FORBID; SOV.7 PROCESS *(part: the curve over auction prints; S3.170 completes it from the dealer fixings)*
**Architecture**: §7.12 (K-91 curves and discount-factor tables), §6.1 (6c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.121 (auction prints), S1.335 (K-91: labelled curves, the day's discount-factor tables), S1.326
(K-86: the day's prints and their ages), S1.180 (K-21: the publisher's method as a declared valuer)
**Goal**: one publisher per country fits the sovereign curve at 6c through the day's traded prices only, labels every
point traded or interpolated, and publishes the day's discount-factor table that valuers of untraded claims read;
it never reads its own earlier curve.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/rules/curve.rs` | the bootstrap over the day's prints |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/tests/curve.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/sov.rs` | 6c fit; K-91 record |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/sov.rs` | LC-3-24 |
| `data/<country>/SOV.toml` | the publisher's method: instruments admitted, interpolation (POLICY of the publisher, MKT.21) |

**Design**:
- **Publisher**: a firm with the publisher's declared method (K-21 valuer), named by the opening's data (S3.142).
- **Fit** (6c of each business day, per country): zero rates bootstrapped from the day's prints of bills and bonds
  (auction prints here; dealer fixings from S3.169), linear in the zero rate between traded maturities, nothing
  beyond the longest, every point labelled traded or interpolated with its print's age (MKT.20). It reads only the
  day's prints (K-86), never its own earlier output (SOV.9). Fewer than two traded points: no curve that day, and the
  last shows its age.
- **Output**: a K-91 curve record (a valuation input, never a print, MKT.14) and the day's discount-factor table per
  curve (K-91), read by claim values of untraded bonds (VAL.8), repo and central-bank haircuts' valuations, S4.152's
  funding curves.
- **SOV.9 completes**: no forced buyer (S3.121), no yield that sets a price (S3.121), no curve fed its own output.

**Edge cases**: E2 — fewer than two prints: no curve that day, never carried forward as new (`curve_absent_below_two`). E6 —
curves are K-91's saved records within their horizon (`history_round_trip`, S1.326). E11 — day zero: no curve until a
day with two prints; valuers read GEN.5's values (K-91's `curve_from_opening_fixings`, S1.335). E13 — bills only: a
bill-only curve; before S3.142 names a publisher none is published (`no_publisher_no_curve`).

**Extension points**: S3.170 completes SOV.7 from S3.169's fixings; S4.106 fits the swap curve beside it by its own method;
S4.136, S4.152 and S5.171 discount at its tables.

**Unit tests**: `curve_labels_traded_and_interpolated`; `curve_reads_no_prior_curve`; `discount_factors_from_zero_rates`;
`curve_absent_below_two`; `no_publisher_no_curve`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-24 — SOV.7: every curve point is labelled, and no fit read an earlier curve (the read-trace)
(from the first curve).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 3 curves a business day × ≈ 1 ms VM (K-91) with their discount-factor tables. Counter
`phx_sov.curve_points_traded`.
its share of fin.fixed.calls: 3 / 0 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a curve point unlabelled; a curve entering an index or a market as a print.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The daily curve and tables; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-24 passes.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

**Goal**: the treasury's deficits in downturns, issuance's footprint in auction prices and interest cost, the fiscal

### S3.129 — Debt instruments of every form, with covenants and seniority

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.1 STATE *(part: every form but preferred shares, at S3.145)*; CRD.11 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.10 (K-64), §7.9 (K-55 terms), §7.15 (K-98 classes), §8
**Depends on**: S1.279 (K-64: instruments), S1.263 (K-55: fixed, floating, discount, step-up, PIK legs; conversion
and write-down terms), S1.281 (K-65: events), S1.345 (K-98: the claim classes of the waterfall), S1.180 (K-21:
families), S2.132 (the insolvency law's classes)
**Goal**: firms and banks can hold and issue senior and subordinated bonds, floating-rate notes, commercial paper,
convertibles and banks' contingent capital, each with the covenants its type carries and a seniority the estate
honours; every term is the parties' own to each issue.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/lib.rs` | the system; `declare` |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/families.rs` | the debt families (K-21) and their term sets (K-55); covenant terms; seniority classes |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/families.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/shared/CRD.toml` | which legal forms may issue which family (declared data); CP's longest tenor by convention (POLICY of the market) |

**Design**:
- **Families** (REG.5, K-21 on K-64): senior bond, subordinated bond, floating-rate note (a margin over a named
  transacted reference, K-55's floating leg; its reset reads the reference as S3.203's benchmark step makes it, the IDX
  placeholder it names), commercial paper (discount, a tenor up to the market's convention), convertible (an elective
  conversion leg into the issuer's ordinary shares at a ratio in declared windows), contingent capital (a bank's: a
  named published ratio, a level, convert or write down). Preferred shares are S3.145's (EQY).
- **Covenants** where a type has them: declared covenant terms (a ratio of the issuer's published statements, a level,
  a test calendar) interned in the issue's terms (K-55, REP.3 storage only). **Seniority**: each family's claim class
  in the waterfall (K-98: senior, subordinated), so a junior bond is paid only after senior in the estate (L3).
- **CRD.11**: no primitive of its own; covenants, fees and terms are chosen per issue by the parties (S3.130,
  S3.133); only which legal form may issue which family is declared data.

**Edge cases**: E6 — terms and instruments saved (`terms_roundtrip`, S1.263; `issued_changed_only_by_events`, S1.279). E8/E9 — the
register grows by issues less retirements (≈ 20 a business day plus paper rolls), ids never reused (`ids_never_reused`,
S1.279). E12 — a floating note whose reference has no fixing keeps its current fixing term, never zero
(`floating_reset_keeps_fixing`). E13 — a legal form that may issue no family issues none (`form_without_family_none`).

**Extension points**: S3.130–S3.139 issue and service them; S3.145's preferred shares and S3.160's convertibles' election; S4.160's
tranches as debt instruments.

**Unit tests**: `seniority_orders_payout_not_price`; `covenant_terms_interned_per_issue`; `floating_reset_keeps_fixing`; `form_without_family_none`.

**Live checks**: none new.

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: declarations only; no day work.
+0 B (core attribute) — its share of S1.279's register: ≈ 5 k live bonds, paper programmes and certificates (≈ 30 k
issued over two years, retired at maturity) inside the register's ≈ 66 k × 32 B

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a covenant or fee as a world-wide primitive; a seniority that changes the price but not the
payout.

**Done when**:

- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.130 — The issuer decides: size, tenor, form, walk-away and refinancing

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.2 DECISION; CRD.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.129 (families), S1.348 (K-100), S1.341 (K-95: its debt
maturing by date), S1.225 (K-42: the wake ahead of a maturity), S1.281 (K-65: redemption)
**Goal**: an issuer decides the size, tenor and form of an issue from its need, its leverage tolerance and what each
costs it now, and posts its own reservation so that a book clearing too wide issues nothing; maturing debt is
refinanced at today's price.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/points.rs` | `issue_debt` (office: the issuer's chief executive) |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/issue.rs` | size, tenor, form and reservation |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/issue.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | 5c issue decisions |
| `data/<country>/CRD.toml` | tenors the market's conventions allow (POLICY of the market); review hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Myers and Majluf, 1984; Graham and Harvey, 2001) |

**Design**:
- **When**: woken when a funding choice picks a bond or paper (the sources S3.131 and S3.132 declare), and ahead
  of each maturity of its own debt by the declared notice (a K-42
  entry from K-95's maturities, CRD.8).
- **Size**: the funding need (the programme, the maturing debt, the shortfall). **Tenor**: its management's
  preference for matching the life of what it funds (PREFERENCE) over the conventional tenors. **Form**: the family
  with the lowest cost after its terms (a convertible's lower coupon against the dilution it expects; a subordinated
  note's cost against the capital it counts as).
- **Walk-away**: its order in the book is the full size at prices at or above its reservation — the price at which the
  next-cheapest source would cost as much; a book clearing below it issues nothing (MKT.10).
- **Refinancing** (CRD.8): maturing debt is retired by its redemption event (K-65) from the new issue's proceeds at
  today's price, or from other sources if the issue fails; nothing rolls automatically.
- **Output**: a mandate request (S3.133) with the plan of the issue; the decision recorded with its decider.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no underwriter answers: the issue is not made, the need returns to S2.118's plan (`no_mandate_need_returns`).
E6 — the issue's plan is a saved message across days (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237). E11 — the first decision
reads GEN.5's prints (`issue_reads_opening_prints`). E14 — a maturity and a new need the same day: one decision of
summed size (`maturity_and_need_one_decision`).

**Extension points**: S3.152's equity issues use the same walk-away.

**Unit tests**: `walk_away_below_reservation`; `tenor_matches_asset_life`; `form_cheapest_after_terms`;
`refinancing_at_todays_price`; `no_mandate_need_returns`; `issue_reads_opening_prints`; `maturity_and_need_one_decision`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-26 reads issues).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 20 / 0 / 20 issue decisions × ≈ 20 µs. Counters `phx_crd.issues`, `phx_crd.walkaways`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.4 / 0 / 0.4 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an issue without a reservation; debt rolled automatically.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Issue decisions and refinancing; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; the form listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.131 — Bonds and paper among a firm's funding sources

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.9 DECISION *(part: bonds and commercial paper; shares at S3.152)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (rule handles), §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.129 (the families), S3.130 (the issue decision it wakes), S2.118 (the funding decision and its
declared sources), S1.326 (K-86: its own
bonds' prints), S1.336 (K-92: its outlook of the yield its paper would clear at)
**Goal**: a firm whose legal form may issue public debt compares a bond and commercial paper with its other sources at
what each would cost it now, so the cheapest source within its leverage tolerance wins and a rate rise reaches a firm
that borrowed years ago when it refinances.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/source_cost.rs` | the cost read of a bond and of paper for S2.118's plan |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/source_cost.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | bonds and paper as declared sources with their cost reads |

**Design**:
- **Bond source**: its own outlook of the yield its bond would clear at — its outstanding bonds' latest prints or
  fixings (K-86); with none, comparable issuers of its own choosing (the prints of its industry's issuers, VAL.10) —
  plus the fee it expects (its record of fees paid, else the trade's fee points), at the tenor its management prefers.
  **Paper**: its outlook of paper yields at the market's tenors. Available only to legal forms S3.129 admits.
- The plan (S2.118) is unchanged: sources cheapest first within the leverage tolerance. When a bond or paper is
  chosen, the firm's issue decision is woken (S3.130). The choice is its marginal cost of money that CAP.3 and FRM.4
  read (L4).

**Edge cases**: E11 — day zero: the opening's prints (`bond_cost_from_own_prints_else_comparables`). E12 — no print and no comparable
issuer: the cost is Missing and the source skipped, never zero (`missing_cost_skipped_for_bond`). E13 — a firm whose
form may not issue: the sources are not in its list (`form_may_not_issue_no_bond_source`).

**Extension points**: S3.152 adds shares as a source the same way.

**Unit tests**: `bond_cost_from_own_prints_else_comparables`; `missing_cost_skipped_for_bond`; `form_may_not_issue_no_bond_source`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-05 reads spreads by issuer).

S2.118's ≈ 55 k occasions) × ≈ 50 ns.

### S3.132 — Banks' certificates, subordinated debt and contingent capital

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.2 STATE; BCP.4 DECISION *(part: contingent capital and subordinated debt; shares at S3.152)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.129 (families), S3.130 (the issue decision it wakes), S3.110 (the money market's routes among
sources), S2.179 (declared funding
sources), S2.186 (capital layers and requirements), S2.188 (the bank's buffer choice), S2.191 (the raise recorded
and unmet, `BCP.raise_unmet`: this retires it for debt), S1.326 (K-86)
**Goal**: a bank's wholesale funding is interbank loans, repo, certificates of deposit, commercial paper and bonds it
issued, each maturing and needing to be rolled; when it judges more capital worth its price it can raise it by
contingent capital or subordinated debt, which can fail if investors will not buy.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/bank_sources.rs` | the cost reads of certificates, bank paper and bonds; capital by layer |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/bank_sources.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/BFL.toml` | certificates, paper and bonds as the bank's declared sources |
| `data/<country>/BCP.toml` | contingent capital and subordinated debt as declared capital sources |

**Design**:
- **Funding sources** (S2.179's extension point): certificates and paper at the bank's outlook of their yields; senior
  bonds at its outlook of its bonds' clearing yield (its prints, else comparables), each plus its expected fee.
  With S2.182's interbank loans and S3.106's repo, this completes BFL.2.
- **Capital** (S2.188's review, BCP.4): when the review asks for capital, the options are costed per unit of capital
  counted — contingent capital (its coupon outlook plus the dilution it expects at conversion), subordinated debt (its
  coupon outlook against the capital it counts as, S2.186's layers) — beside shedding assets (S2.188); the cheapest wins
  and wakes the issue decision (S3.130) with the capital constraint. Retires S2.191's placeholder for debt; its share
  half stays for S3.152.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a bank near failure: its costs rise through its own outlooks of its prints; nothing floors them
(`capital_cost_per_unit_counted`). E6 — the capital need is the bank's saved review state
(`save_round_trip_rebuilds_indexes`, S1.196). E12 — no print: Missing cost, the source skipped
(`certificate_missing_print_skipped`).

**Extension points**: S3.152's shares as a capital source.

**Unit tests**: `capital_cost_per_unit_counted`; `certificate_source_cost`; `certificate_missing_print_skipped`.

### S3.133 — Underwriters and syndicates choose their risk

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.3 DECISION
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-80), §4.7 (rule handles), §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.130 (the mandate request), S1.317 (K-80: request, answers, acceptance across days), S1.237 (K-45),
S1.338 (K-93: each bank's position limit), S1.251 (K-50: the underwriting commitment), S1.172 (K-16: shares of a
syndicate), S2.102 (`loan_claim_value`), S2.189 (the capital charge)
**Goal**: an issuer asks the banks it reaches to take its issue; each answers from its own view whether to commit to
buy what the book does not take — for a larger fee and within its own limit — or only to build the book; a large
issue is shared by a syndicate of named banks.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/points.rs` | `underwrite` (office: the bank's chief executive); the issuer's choice |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/underwrite.rs` | the answer's basis and fee; the syndicate's shares |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/underwrite.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | 5c requests, answers, acceptance |
| `data/<country>/CRD.toml` | fee points (POLICY of the trade); hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Smith, 1977) |

**Design**:
- **Protocol** (MKT.7, K-80): the issuer's request at 5c to the banks it reaches (its lenders from K-54 sides and its
  declared reach); each answers at the next 5c; the issuer accepts at the 5c after.
- **A bank's answer**: underwritten when its fee covers the value of the put it writes — its expected loss on unsold
  paper, valued through `loan_claim_value` under its one assessment of the issuer against its outlook of the book's
  demand (its own record of recent books' cover and prices) — plus its operating cost and its required return on the
  capital the unsold paper would consume (S2.189), within its position limit (K-93); otherwise best effort at its
  operating cost; or no answer. Fees on the trade's fee points.
- **Syndicate**: a size beyond the lead's limit is shared — the lead invites banks (K-80), each answering by the same
  rule within its own limit; shares by K-16 largest remainder, residue to the lead.
- **Choice**: the issuer takes the lowest all-in cost, ties by lot on `CRD.mandate_lot`. An underwritten mandate is a
  K-50 commitment of each underwriter to buy its share of the unsold size at the committed price (REG.10).

**Edge cases**: E2 — no answer: no issue (`no_mandate_need_returns`, S3.130). E6 — requests, answers and commitments across days
are saved (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237; `commit_roundtrip`, S1.251). E7 — the issuer's ties by lot
(`mandate_ties_by_lot`). E10 — an underwriter ending before the book: its commitment passes to its estate or
successor (`commitment_follows_underwriter_estate`).

**Extension points**: S3.152's equity issues and S4.163's tranches use the same protocol.

**Unit tests**: `underwritten_fee_covers_put_value`; `best_effort_below_put_value`; `syndicate_shares_sum_to_size`; `mandate_ties_by_lot`; `commitment_follows_underwriter_estate`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-26 (at S3.135) reads each issue's answers.

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 20 requests × ≈ 10 banks = ≈ 200 / 0 / 200 answers × ≈ 2 µs. Counter `phx_crd.mandates`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.4 / 0 / 0.4 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an underwriter carrying no risk for an underwritten fee; a bank's value outside
`loan_claim_value`.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Mandates answered and chosen; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; the form listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.134 — Investors value debt and post their orders

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.4 DECISION; BNK.15 FORBID
**Architecture**: §4.7, §6.1 (5c, 9a), §8
**Depends on**: S3.129 (seniority), S1.357 (K-105: the investor schedule), S1.348 (K-100), S1.336 (K-92: class
default outlooks), S1.215 (K-37: filed accounts and published default statistics), S2.108 (filed accounts), S2.102
(`loan_claim_value` and provisions), S2.179 (cost of funds), S2.189 (capital charge), S1.332 (K-89: amortised cost
and provisions)
**Goal**: every investor in a book bids from its own value of the issue — its own assessment of default and recovery,
its cost of funds, the capital the holding consumes and its mandate — and a default anywhere revises investors' class
outlooks, which moves other issuers' spreads.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/points.rs` | `invest_debt`, a rule per investor kind registered by data |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/invest.rs` | values by class, seniority and cost of funds |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/invest.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `data/<country>/CRD.toml` | the classes' ratio steps (PREFERENCE of each investor kind's management); mandates (declared data); hours |

**Design**:
- **When**: 5c on a book's day and a paper placement (S3.135, S3.136 route them), for the investors the issue
  reaches: banks, and firms whose placement chose the family (this step declares corporate bonds and paper as an
  alternative of S3.108's placement); funds, insurers and pensions register later.
- **A bank's value**: `loan_claim_value` under its assessment of the issuer, discounted at its marginal cost of funds
  (S2.179) plus the capital charge times its required return (S2.189). **Another investor's**: the claim value at its
  own outlook of the issuer's default — the issuer's class by steps of its filed or reported ratios (S2.108; ratings
  from S3.217), each class's default frequency an adaptive outlook of defaults seen or published (from the snapshot's
  published statistics, VAL.10) — and its own recovery outlook by seniority, at its cost of funds, within its mandate.
- **Projection** (the extension point): the claim's cash flows are projected by the method its instrument family
  declares (K-21 data per family, read here); the default is its terms' schedule (K-55). A family may declare another
  method as data — S4.165's tranches declare K-98's `run_steps` (S1.345) over the deal's declared waterfall under the
  investor's own outlook paths of defaults, prepayments and recoveries — and this rule reads it without change.
- **Shared values**: a non-bank investor's value is its method's (K-92 method cells), so each (investor method, issue)
  value is computed once a day and read by every investor using the method; each investor's own order follows from
  it by K-105.
- **Order**: the investor schedule (K-105) at that value.
- **Reassessment**: each public default (S3.137) revises every class outlook that counts it (VAL.4), so spreads of
  similar names widen through investors' own values (CRD.9, LC-3-48).
- **BNK.15**: a bank's bonds held to collect are carried at amortised cost with an expected-loss provision
  from the same assessment (K-89, S2.102's rule over holdings), moved at 9a.

**Edge cases**: E6 — class outlooks are K-92 cells, saved (`fixed_overflow_stops`, S1.336, with its store's round trip). E11 — no
defaults seen: the snapshot's statistics (`class_outlook_from_snapshot`). E12 — an issuer with no filed accounts: its
class is Missing and the investor posts nothing (`missing_class_posts_nothing`). E14 — two books the same day: one view,
two orders (`one_view_two_orders`).

**Extension points**: investor kinds register: funds S3.191, insurers S4.137, pension schemes S4.155; S4.165 declares
the tranche family's projection method (above).

**Unit tests**: `investor_claim_value_by_seniority`; `bank_value_through_loan_claim_value`;
`class_outlook_revised_by_default`; `class_outlook_from_snapshot`; `missing_class_posts_nothing`; `one_view_two_orders`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-48 — CRD.6: after each default, the reassessments of other issuers' holders and investors (their
classes' default outlooks revised) and the change in those issuers' spreads are traceable in events; vacuous without
a default, and the report says so.

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 20 books and ≈ 500 paper placements a business day; values once per (investor method, issue),
≈ 1.2 k × 1 µs; orders ≈ 12 k × 150 ns. Counter `phx_crd.book_orders`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 1.2 / 0 / 1.2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
its share of fin.fixed.securities: 1.8 / 0 / 1.8 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fixed recovery; a price from a spread; one assessment shared by every lender.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Investors' values and orders; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-48 passes or is
  vacuous.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.135 — Book-built issues and taps

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.10 FORBID; CRD.5 PROCESS *(part: book-built issues and taps; paper at S3.136; dealers at S3.166)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-76 book-built variant), §6.1 (6a, 6b, 7), §8
**Depends on**: S3.130 (the issuer's order), S3.133 (the commitment), S3.134 (investors' orders), S1.312 (K-76: the
book-built variant with an underwriter's commitment), S1.251 (K-50: commitments until settlement), S1.279 (K-64:
issue and tap events), S1.326 (K-86: the print), S1.213 (K-36: an issue not made)
**Goal**: a primary issue is a call auction on the underwriter's book: investors' schedules, the issuer's walk-away and,
under an underwritten mandate, the underwriters' commitment meet at 6a; what sells is issued, a tap adds to an
existing line, and nothing unsold lands on a best-effort agent.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/markets.rs` | the book-built market per issue; the tap |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/book.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | 6a the call; 6b results; settlement on the convention |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/crd.rs` | LC-3-26 |
| `data/<country>/CRD.toml` | lots, ticks, settlement convention (POLICY of the market) |

**Design**:
- **The call** (6a of the announced day, K-76 book-built variant): investors' orders (S3.134); the issuer's supply at
  or above its reservation (S3.130); under an underwritten mandate each underwriter's commitment (K-50) is its order
  for its share of the whole size at the committed price — a limit it chose, a real risk; under best effort the agent
  posts nothing. Rationing at the price by largest remainder, ties by lot on `CRD.book_lot` (subject: the issue, day).
- **Results**: the clearing price is the issue's first print (K-86); sold units are issued (K-64 issue, or tap on an
  existing line) and settle on the convention (K-50 until then, SET.2) with the fee to the underwriters; an issue
  clearing below the reservation or with no demand is not made, a K-36 event (MKT.10).
- **CRD.10 completes**: orders are prices, never spreads; recoveries are investors' own (S3.134); seniority changes
  the payout (S3.129's class); an underwriter keeps what its commitment bought; a best-effort agent holds nothing.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a book with no investor: an underwritten issue lands wholly on its underwriters; a best-effort one is not
made (`best_effort_leaves_nothing_on_agent`). E6 — commitments until settlement saved (`commit_roundtrip`, S1.251).
E7 — rationing ties by lot (K-76's `same_allotment_any_order`, S1.312). E10 — an issuer ending between the book and
settlement: the legs fail and are recorded (`issuer_ends_legs_fail`).

**Extension points**: S3.152's equity issues and S4.163's tranches use the same variant.

**Unit tests**: `underwritten_book_leaves_unsold_on_underwriter`; `best_effort_leaves_nothing_on_agent`;
`tap_adds_to_line`; `issuer_ends_legs_fail`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-26 — CRD.10: every underwritten issue's unsold amount sits on its underwriters' books; no
best-effort agent holds paper from its own book; every issue names its underwriters' answers (applicable from the
first issue).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 20 books a business day × ≈ 600 orders × 100 ns + 2 µs a call. Counter `phx_crd.books`.

+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a price from a spread; unsold paper absorbed by anyone without a commitment.

### S3.136 — Commercial paper rolled or not

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.5 PROCESS *(part: paper placed by bilateral quote; through dealers at S3.166)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-80), §6.1 (5c, 7), §8
**Depends on**: S3.130 (maturing paper as need), S3.134 (investors' schedules), S3.108 (cash investors'
placements), S1.317 (K-80), S1.279 (K-64), S1.281 (K-65: redemption at maturity), S2.121 (distress when paper cannot
be rolled)
**Goal**: an issuer rolls its paper at maturity by its own decision, placing it by quote to the cash investors it
reaches, who answer from their own schedules; paper that cannot be rolled leaves a maturing payment the issuer must
meet from cash, lines or distress.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/paper.rs` | the placement request and the taking of answers |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/paper.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | 5c requests and answers; 7 settlement |

**Design**:
- **Roll** (S3.130's decision ahead of the maturity): the issuer asks at 5c, by K-80, the cash investors it reaches
  (firms with a placement admitting paper, S3.108; money funds from S3.187); each answers at the next 5c with its
  investor schedule at its own value (S3.134's rule); the issuer takes the best up to its need at or above its
  reservation, ties by lot on `CRD.paper_lot`; each issuer's paper is one programme instrument (K-64): a placement adds a tranche (the
  named issue event, a tranche record) settling on the convention, and the maturing tranche redeems at maturity
  (K-65).
- **Not rolled**: what is unplaced leaves the maturing redemption to be met from cash, lines or the firm's distress
  actions (S2.121); a failed redemption is S3.137's missed payment.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no answer: nothing placed, the redemption stands (`unrolled_paper_leaves_redemption`). E5 — a quarter-end cluster of
maturities: requests follow maturing issues one to one (`requests_one_per_maturity`). E6 — requests across days are
saved (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237).

**Extension points**: S3.166's dealers (completing CRD.5) and S3.187's money funds.

**Unit tests**: `best_answers_taken_to_need`; `unrolled_paper_leaves_redemption`; `requests_one_per_maturity`.

### S3.137 — Missed payments and covenant breaches as events holders see

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.6 PROCESS *(part: events and defaults; holders' votes at S3.138)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (2d, 2e, 9c, 9e), §9.1, §8
**Depends on**: S3.129 (covenant terms, seniority), S1.281 (K-65: the default event, one writer of the instrument's
state), S1.265 (K-56: missed payments and grace), S1.333 (K-90: statements on the issuer's calendar), S1.239 (K-46:
thresholds on published ratios), S1.213 (K-36), S2.108 (filed accounts), S2.123 (the procedure's stay), S2.124 (the
restructuring vote), S2.133 (estates)
**Goal**: a missed payment past its grace is a default and a breached covenant is an event, each public to holders;
default makes the claim a claim on an estate or a class in a restructuring, and while a procedure is open the bonds'
events are stayed.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/events.rs` | covenant tests over published statements; default past grace; the stay |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/events.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | 2d/2e defaults; 9c tests, 9e events |

**Design**:
- **Missed payment**: a coupon or redemption leg failed at stage 7 is recorded at 2d against the instrument's event
  (K-56); past the terms' grace it is a default at 2e — a K-65 default event (the instrument's state has one writer)
  and a public K-36 event naming the issuer, the line and the leg.
- **Covenant**: at 9c on the issuer's statement or filing day (K-90, S2.108), one handler tests each covenant's ratio
  of the published statements against its level (a K-46 threshold on the published series) and issues the breach
  event, applied at 9e (TIME.7).
- **Consequences**: default makes each holding a claim in the issuer's estate at its seniority (K-98, S2.133) or a
  class in the restructuring vote (S2.124); while the issuer's procedure is open (S2.123's stay) the bonds' events are
  suspended — an event intent `sys-crd` declares and K-65 applies. Holders' acceleration and waivers are S3.138's.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a cluster of defaults: one event per line (`one_event_per_line`). E6 — arrears, events and stays saved
(`history_before_free`, S1.265; `holders_rebuilt_equal`, S1.280). E10 — a holder that is an estate keeps its claim
(`estate_holder_keeps_claim`, S3.123). E11 — no statement yet: no covenant test (`no_statement_no_test`). E14 — a
missed payment and a breach the same day: two events (`two_events_same_day`).

**Extension points**: S4.119's credit default swaps read the default events; S3.138 reads the events.

**Unit tests**: `default_only_past_grace`; `covenant_breach_from_published_ratio`; `events_suspended_under_stay`; `one_event_per_line`; `no_statement_no_test`; `two_events_same_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-27 (at S3.138).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: covenant tests on filing days, ≈ 200 / 0 / 2 k × ≈ 1 µs; defaults rare. Counter `phx_crd.defaults`.
its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.2 / 0 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
+0 B (core attribute) — its ≈ 30 k covenant thresholds × 12 B are S1.239's live rows

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a default drawn or decided outside the payment's failure; a covenant read from unpublished books.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Events, defaults and the stay; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken.

### S3.138 — Holders vote: acceleration and waivers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.6 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §7.6 (K-41), §7.11 (K-80), §6.1 (5c), §8
**Depends on**: S3.137 (the events), S3.134 (holders' values), S1.224 (K-41: votes by face), S1.317 (K-80: the
issuer's consent offer), S1.280 (K-65: holders of record), S1.281 (acceleration as an

**Goal**: after a missed payment or a breach each holder votes, from its own values, to accelerate or to accept a

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/points.rs` | `holder_vote` (every holder kind); `offer_consent` (the issuer's chief executive) |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/holders.rs` | the vote and the consent fee |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/holders.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/crd.rs` | LC-3-27 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the holder's vote as its claim-now value against its wait value (Gilson, John and Lang, 1990); the issuer's consent fee against its refinancing cost (Kahan and Tuckman, 1993) |

**Design**:
- **Issuer** (5c after the event): offers a consent fee when avoiding acceleration is worth more to it than the fee
  (its cost of refinancing the accelerated principal now, from its own sources, S3.131), by K-80 to every holder of
  record (K-65).
- **Holder** (by the deadline): accelerate when its value of claiming now (its recovery outlook × face) exceeds its
  value of waiting (the claim value at its revised assessment; a bank's through `loan_claim_value`), unless the fee
  exceeds that difference; an estate votes in its administrator's office. A non-bank holder's values are its
  method's, computed once per (holder method, issue).
- **Tally** (K-41) by face against the terms' threshold: acceleration makes the whole principal due the next business
  day (a K-65 event, TIME.7), failing which S3.137's default follows; a waiver pays the fee to every holder of record
  pro rata (K-16) and the breach lapses.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no votes: the terms' default rule, no acceleration (`no_votes_no_acceleration`). E6 — votes across days are saved
messages (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237). E10 — holders ending before the deadline vote through their estates
(`estate_answers_through_administrator`, S3.124).

**Extension points**: S2.124's restructuring votes are the other path; S4.119 reads accelerations.

**Unit tests**: `acceleration_by_threshold`; `waiver_when_fee_exceeds_difference`; `consent_fee_offered_only_when_worth_it`; `no_votes_no_acceleration`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-27 — CRD.6: every acceleration follows a public event and names its holders' vote; every
contingent conversion names the published ratio that triggered it (vacuous without an event, and the report says so).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: 0 on an ordinary day. Counter `phx_crd.votes`.
on fin.calendar.debt_event_vote (the deadline, a count of business days after a missed payment or breach): 0.25 core-ms (≈ 10⁴ holders × ≈ 25 ns: a comparison of its method's values, tally 5 ns a vote, K-41); joins H and B′
+0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; acceleration without a vote; a fee paid to some holders only.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Votes, waivers and acceleration; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-27 passes or
  is vacuous; forms listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.139 — Contingent capital converts or writes down at its trigger

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BCP.1 STATE; CRD.7 PROCESS *(part: contingent capital; convertibles' election and conversion at S3.160)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (9c, 9e, 2e), §9.2, §8
**Depends on**: S3.129 (contingent capital terms), S3.132 (banks issue it), S1.239 (K-46: the trigger on the
published ratio), S1.281 (K-65: conversion and write-down events), S1.283 (the issuer's equity instrument), S1.172
(K-16: cash in lieu), S2.186 (the bank's published capital ratios), S2.196 (resolution's write-down by layer)
**Goal**: a bank's contingent capital converts into shares or writes down automatically when its trigger ratio, read
from the issuer's published accounts, crosses the stated level; in resolution the authority converts or writes it
down after equity, in the layers' order.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/trigger.rs` | the trigger test and the event |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/trigger.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | 9c test, 9e event, the next day's 2e application |

**Design**:
- **BCP.1 completes**: capital is layered, and before resolution losses fall on equity, and on contingent capital
  when its own trigger ratio is crossed (this step); the other layers act only in resolution (S2.186, S2.196).
- **Trigger**: each issue registers a K-46 threshold on its issuer's published ratio series (the ratio its terms name,
  as the bank publishes it, S2.186); a publication crossing the level wakes 9c's handler, which issues the event,
  applied at 9e and effective to holders of record at the start of the next business day (TIME.7, REG.11).
- **Event** (K-65): conversion — the issue's units retire and the issuer's ordinary shares issue at the terms' ratio,
  fractional shares paid as cash in lieu by K-16 with the residue to the issuer — or write-down — principal reduced by
  the terms, the holders' loss recorded.
- **Resolution**: the authority's write-down by layer (S2.196) reads the issue's layer (BCP.1) and converts or writes
  it down after equity.

**Edge cases**: E1 — several banks' ratios crossing on one release day: one event each (`one_event_per_issue`). E6 — thresholds are
K-46 saved rows (`save_round_trip_runs`, S1.239). E12 — a ratio not published: no test, never an estimate
(`unpublished_ratio_no_test`). E14 — a trigger and a coupon the same day: the coupon at 2e to holders of record, the
conversion the next day (`trigger_and_coupon_same_day`).

**Extension points**: S3.160's convertibles (holder's election and conversion, completing CRD.7).

**Unit tests**: `contingent_trigger_from_published_ratio`; `conversion_cash_in_lieu_residue_to_issuer`;
`write_down_records_loss`; `one_event_per_issue`; `unpublished_ratio_no_test`; `trigger_and_coupon_same_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-27 (at S3.138) names the published ratio behind each conversion.

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 100 thresholds; a crossing is tested only on a publication, ≈ 1 µs.
its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.001 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H)
ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-46): +0.001 MB resident (≈ 100 thresholds × 12 B)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a trigger read from unpublished books; a conversion effective the day its trigger is tested.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Triggers and events; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.140 — Syndicated loans: one set of terms, a contract for each lender

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.9 (K-53, K-55 shared terms), §7.11 (K-80), §8
**Depends on**: S1.257 (K-53: each share its own contract), S1.263 (K-55: one interned shape for the syndicate),
S1.165 (K-06: a declared index instance by syndicate), S1.317 (K-80: invitations), S1.224 (K-41: the majority
clause's tally), S1.172 (K-16: pro-rata cuts), S1.425 (each bank's own quote), S2.186 (the large-exposure limit),
S2.102 (provisions per share), S2.107 (a share sold)
**Goal**: a loan beyond the lead bank's own limit is arranged: the lead invites banks, each joins when the terms beat
its own quote and takes a share within its limit; each lender's share is its own contract with the borrower under
the one set of terms, held against its own capital, provisioned and worked out by that lender, bound by the terms'
majority clause.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/rules/syndicate.rs` | the invitation, the join rule, the pro-rata cut, the majority clause |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/tests/syndicate.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bnk.rs` | 5c invitations and answers |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | arrangement fee points (POLICY of the trade); hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form (Sufi, 2007) |

**Design**:
- **Arrangement**: a loan the lending round (S1.425) would grant beyond the lead's large-exposure limit (S2.186) is
  arranged at 5c: the lead invites the banks it reaches (K-80); each joins when the terms' rate is at least its own
  quote for that borrower (BNK.4, under its own assessment) and takes a share within its limit;
  oversubscription is cut pro rata by K-16, ties by lot on `BNK.syndicate_lot`.
- **Contracts** (REP.3, BNK.3): each share is its own loan contract between its lender and the borrower (K-53),
  all sharing one interned shape (K-55); a syndicate id in a sparse cold column and a K-06 instance keyed by it list
  the shares. Payments are each contract's own dues; the lead takes the fee at closing.
- **Majority clause**: a waiver or enforcement is voted by the shares' balances (K-41 over the instance); each lender
  provisions and works out its own share (S2.102, S2.103) bound by the result; a share can be sold (S2.107).

**Edge cases**: E2 — not enough banks join: the loan is granted only up to what joined, or not at all by the borrower's choice
(`partial_syndicate_borrower_chooses`). E6 — shares and the index rebuilt from the cold column (K-06's
`rebuild_equals_incremental`, S1.165). E10 — a lender ending: its share moves to its estate (`stale_ref_none`, S1.257).
E14 — a payment to every share the same day: each its own due (`shares_due_commute`).

**Extension points**: S4.161's securitisations read shares as ordinary loans.

**Unit tests**: `syndicate_shares_within_limits_sum_to_loan`; `join_only_when_terms_beat_own_quote`;
`majority_clause_by_balances`; `partial_syndicate_borrower_chooses`; `shares_due_commute`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-28 — BNK.3: every syndicated loan's shares sum to its principal, each within its lender's limit
(from the first syndicate).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: ≈ 10 arrangements × ≈ 10 banks = ≈ 100 / 0 / 100 answers × ≈ 2 µs. Counter `phx_bnk.syndicated_loans`.
its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.04 MB resident (≈ 10 k syndicated shares × 4 B: syndicate id u32, a sparse cold column)
ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-06 instance): +0.1 MB resident (≈ 10 k members × 8 B)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; one contract with many lenders; a share taken beyond its lender's limit.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Syndication arranged and run; unit tests pass; fast checks; bench with no ratchet broken; LC-3-28 passes; the
  form listed.
- [ ] Two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.142 — The opening's sovereign bond lines, their holders and the curve publisher

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: the sovereign's long-term debt)*; GEN.5 STATE *(part: its lines' present values)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed
**Depends on**: S3.118 (the families), S3.119 (the mandate's benchmark maturities), S3.127 (the publisher's method),
S1.433 (the short-term share and holders' shares)
**Goal**: the opening's government debt beyond the bills' tenors opens as fixed and inflation-linked lines at the
mandate's benchmark maturities, held by the sectors the world holds, each with its snapshot price, and each country
has its curve publisher — all from the debt statistics in hand.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_sov_bonds.py` | the derivation below |
| `data/profiles/*/profile.toml` | `SOV.long_share_by_maturity`, `SOV.indexed_share`, `SOV.bond_yield` (present value) |
| `data/<country>/gen/SOV.toml` | the curve publisher (a financial-services firm the opening names) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `bank/bis_debt_securities`, `bank/qpsd`, `bank/sovereign_investor_base`, `bank/imf_mfs_ir`, `bank/imf_mfs_cbs` → the primitives, this step |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `for` gains S3.142 |

**Design**:
- **Long-term debt** = the profile's central-government debt (`bank/qpsd`) less S1.433's short-term share, split across
  the mandate's benchmark maturities by `bank/bis_debt_securities`' remaining-maturity profile where reported (the
  group's median), each line's issue dates spread over its life by the steady-path convention (GEN.5); the indexed
  share where `bank/qpsd` reports it by instrument, else none opened and the gap reported (E12).
- **Coupons and present values**: each line's coupon the government bond yield (`bank/imf_mfs_ir`) of its issue date
  under the steady-path convention; its opening print the price at the snapshot's yield — a present value (GEN.5).
- **Holders**: banks and firms by `bank/sovereign_investor_base`'s sector shares; the central bank's holdings from
  `bank/imf_mfs_cbs` (claims on central government); funds', insurers', households' and non-residents' shares
  reported as not opened until their holders' steps (S3.158, S3.191, S4.137, S5.169) — never reassigned.
- **Publisher**: one financial-services firm per country, the largest of its industry at the opening, declared the
  curve publisher (a deterministic choice by size; ties by party id).

**Edge cases**: E11 — day one's curve reads these present values until prints arrive (LC-3-57). E12 — a country missing a split is left
out of its group's median; a group with none opens no bonds and reports it (`missing_split_left_out`). E13 — a country
with no long-term debt opens no line (`no_long_debt_no_line`).

**Extension points**: S5.170's foreign-currency lines (`bank/bis_international_debt`).

**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `long_share_complements_short`, `holder_shares_sum_to_one`, `missing_split_left_out`; `no_long_debt_no_line`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-57 — at day one, every opening line's holdings sum to its issued amount and every line has its
dated present value (applicable at day one).

**Budget**:
B / NB / H: opening only, no day work.
on fin.calendar.opening (the opening, before day zero): 5 core-ms; joins neither
+0 B (inside S1.280's holdings, count ≈ 50 k opening sovereign bond holdings)

**Guards**: `phx-check data`.

**Not allowed**: a value typed by hand; an unheld share given to another sector; a present value that is not dated the
snapshot's date.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The derivation and tests; the profiles regenerated; fast checks; the opening's span within its ratchet (the bench at the
  committed resolution); LC-3-57 passes.

### S3.143 — The opening's corporate and bank debt, paper and syndicated loans

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data

carrying values)*

**Goal**: the opening's firms and banks owe the bonds, notes and paper the statistics in hand show, drawn onto issuers
by a declared procedure, held by banks and firms, and the large loans banks share are opened as syndicates; every

### Equity, dealers, funds, indices and ratings; the Stage 3 gate (S3.145–S3.219)

**What this group builds.** Shares as residual claims with votes, priced on continuous books by investors with their
own values, issued, paid out and bought back by firms' own decisions, with groups read from holdings (3E, S3.145–
S3.162); dealers as parties with their own equity, quotes, interdealer calls, fixings, securities lending and prime
brokerage (3F, S3.163–S3.181); funds of every declared kind, their net asset value, forward-priced dealing, runs,
exchange-traded funds, private equity and non-bank lenders (3G, S3.182–S3.201); benchmarks read from transactions,
market indices as reads, ratings, reports and estimates (3H, S3.203–S3.218); and the Stage 3 gate (S3.219).

**Exit** (spec Part O): the policy rate reaches loan rates, asset prices and investment through markets; a margin
spiral and a fund run can happen. S3.219 judges it by §2.24's gate.

**How every step of this group works.** Each is an activation step (§2.22) in one `sys-*` crate: its rules and
declarations, its `if-*` vocabulary, its `phx-world` route, its live checks and at most one `phx-check` rule.
Decisions are rules taken through the decision core (S1.348), each naming its decider's office (E 50); Stage 8's steps
convert them to options in place (each step's Extension points names its converter). Orders are the poster's schedule
from its own value (MKT.9) through the investor schedule (K-105, S1.357); nobody posts "at market" (MKT.16), the one
exception being dealing in an open-ended fund at its next value (MKT.8, S3.185). No financial market meets on a
non-business day (TIME.8). Institutions' reviews are paid in their staff's hours (§2.21). Publishers (the pricing
service, benchmark administrators, index publishers, rating agencies, analyst units) are firms with a publisher facet
declared as kind data, reading only public records and what they bought (Law 12).

**Placeholders** retired and introduced here:

| placeholder | clauses | introduced by | retired by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Estates' securities with no market wait (naming EQY) | POP.9 | S2.133 | S3.147 (shares), S3.166 (bonds, bills, paper) |
| A bank's decision to raise capital recorded and unmet (naming EQY for shares) | BCP.4 | S2.191 | S3.154 |
| A management's leverage tolerance is its type's declared value, `FRM.leverage_tolerance` (naming MND), read by S3.153 | FRM.9 | S2.118 | S8.140 |
| A bank's group is the bank alone (naming EQY) | FRM.3 | S2.186 | S3.157 |
| A floating reference's reset reads its series' last published value (naming IDX) | IDX.2 | S1.263 | S3.203 |
| The central bank's collateral eligibility reads no rating (naming RAT) | RAT.4 | S3.112 | S3.215 |
| Listing reads a firm's filed accounts as its reports (naming RAT) | EQY.2 | S3.145 | S3.210 |

A clause completes at the step that retires the last placeholder standing in it: POP.9 therefore completes at S3.166,
FRM.9 at S8.140 and RAT.4 at S4.138.

**Budget frame.** The volumes are `perf/design.toml`'s: `day.*.fin_orders` (0.45 M B / 0 NB / 0.6 M H), `call.calls`
(4.5 k B, 6 k H), `book.books` and `book.standing` (5 k, 200 k), `dealer.dealers`, `dealer.quotes`,
`dealer.requests` (50, 50 k, 50 k), `holdings.securities` and `holdings.lots` (4.95 M, 1.1 M) over
`holdings.instruments` (20 k), `holdings.holder_rows_h` (restated from S3.150's count), `valuation.positions` (0.9 M)
and
`valuation.margin_accounts` (10 k). Each step's **Budget** states its share of the `fin.fixed` line it runs in, the
units it adds to `fin.decide`, its calendar days and its resident bytes as ledger lines (ARCHITECTURE §13), in the
forms §2.11 states.

### S3.145 — Share classes, free float and listing

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.1 STATE; EQY.12 PRIMITIVE; CRD.1 STATE; EQY.2 STATE *(part: listing on the exchange's declared conditions; the condition of published reports completes at S3.210)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9b); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-64 families, K-65 holder lists); §7.3 (phx-core: K-20, K-21)
**Depends on**: S1.279 (instrument register: a share class is an instrument of a declared family); S1.280 (holder
lists, which the free float reads); S1.283 (each firm's equity instrument held by persons); S1.180 (families, market
declarations, legal forms); S1.179 (the exchange's rules as dated POLICY schedules); S1.215 (listing records); S1.216
(filed accounts, which listing reads as reports); S2.108 (the filing decision); S1.227 (the exchange's review
dates); S1.315 (the continuous book a listed share trades on); S3.129 (debt forms, of which
preferred shares are the last)
**Goal**: ordinary and preferred shares exist as instrument families with votes by class and, for preferred, a stated
dividend ranking ahead; each share's free float is a read of its holder list; a firm is listed when the exchange,
applying its declared rules on its own dates, admits its shares to a book.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/decl.rs` | families `EQY.ordinary`, `EQY.preferred` (K-64: class, votes per share, stated dividend, cumulative flag, rank); the listing record kind (K-37) with its horizon; the exchange's review schedule |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/float.rs` | EQY.1: the free float as a pure read over a holder list |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/listing.rs` | EQY.2: admission and delisting tests |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/listing.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | the exchange's reviews at 9b, the rules handed their views |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-60 |
| `data/<country>/EQY.toml` | listing and short-selling rules (EQY.12: POLICY of the exchange and of the supervisor, owners named) |

**Design**:
- **Families** (REG.6 is the core's): `EQY.ordinary` and `EQY.preferred` are K-64 families; a class's terms (votes per
  share, a preferred's stated dividend per share and whether it is cumulative, its rank above ordinary) are its shape
  (K-55); counted in shares, perpetual; the issued amount moves only by the named events (REG.3, S3.150). Preferred
  shares are the last of CRD.1's listed forms (the others are S3.129's), completing it.
- **Free float** (EQY.1): `free_float(holders, issuer) -> Qty` = issued amount − units held by insiders (holders that
  hold an office in the issuer, K-34's person → offices index), by a parent (the issuer's controlling party, read from
  S3.157's group fact once it exists; none before) and by strategic holders (a stake above the exchange's declared
  strategic share, POLICY). A read, never stored; taken at the exchange's reviews and by index weights (S3.204).
- **Listing** (EQY.2): the exchange — the operator of each country's share books (MKT.21), opened by S3.146 —
  decides in its listing office. On each declared review date (K-43) and on a firm's application
  (S3.152's initial offering), it admits a share whose free float and holder count meet its declared minima and whose
  issuer has published reports; until S3.210 the reports read are the issuer's latest filed accounts (S2.108; the
  placeholder naming RAT). Admission writes a listing record (K-37) and opens the share's book market key (K-78);
  delisting (conditions failed at a review, or the issuer's ending) closes it with a record. Unlisted shares change
  hands only by bilateral negotiation (MKT.7, K-80).
- **Rules** (EQY.12): minima, record-date notice, meeting windows, tick sizes, short-sale conditions and settlement
  convention, each a dated POLICY schedule with its owner; an absent one is refused at assembly (NUM.8).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E10 — an issuer ending: its shares cease (REG.12) and the listing record closes the same day
(`delisting_on_issuer_end`). E11 — day zero: listed shares are S3.146's opening (LC-3-60 reads their records from day
one). E12 — an issuer with no filed accounts is not admitted, absent never zero (`listing_refuses_absent_report`).
E13 — a country with no listed share admits nothing and its float read is empty (`float_empty_holder_list`). E6 —
listing state is K-37 records, saved and reloaded (`listing_record_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: `EQY.toml`'s rules are declared data read by S3.147 (ticks, convention), S3.149 (short-sale
rules), S3.151 (record-date notice), S3.155 (meeting windows); the float read by S3.204. The listing office is
converted to options by S8.160.

**Unit tests**: `free_float_excludes_insiders_parents_strategic`; `preferred_ranks_above_ordinary`;
`listing_admits_on_declared_minima`; `listing_refuses_absent_report`; `delisting_on_issuer_end`;
`float_empty_holder_list`; `listing_record_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-60 — every listed share has a listing record naming the review that admitted it, and every book
market key belongs to a listed share; applicable from day one.

**Budget**: listing reviews ≈ 10 a business day (≈ 2300 listed shares reviewed yearly), each a holder-list read of
≈ 1000 rows at `fin.holdings.holder_ns`.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.3 MB resident (6000 listing records × 48 B); +0 B on party records

**Guards**: assembly refuses a share family with no class votes, or a preferred with no stated dividend.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a stored free float; a listing by kind branch; an issuer admitted without the declared test.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks (`fmt`, `clippy`, tests, `phx-check`) pass; the bench at the committed
  resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-60 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.146 — The opening's listed shares, their free floats and last closes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: which of the opening's firms are listed)*; GEN.5 STATE *(part: listed shares' last closes)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed
**Depends on**: S3.145 (the share families and the listing record); S1.283 (each firm's equity instrument and its
holders at the opening); S1.486 (each firm's latest filed accounts at the opening)
**Goal**: at the opening each country's largest firms are listed, as many as its listed companies count, with free
floats and last closes drawn from the market statistics in hand.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_eqy.py` | the derivation below |
| `data/profiles/*/profile.toml` | `EQY.listed_count`, `EQY.cap_to_gdp`, `EQY.turnover` |
| `data/<country>/gen/EQY.toml` | the exchange (the largest financial-services firm the opening names) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `markets/CM.MKT.LDOM.NO`, `markets/CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS`, `markets/CM.MKT.TRNR` → the primitives, this step |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `for` gains S3.146 |

**Design**:
- **Listed**: the `EQY.listed_count` largest incorporated firms by equity (their filed accounts, S1.486) are listed at
  the opening, each with a listing record dated the snapshot.
- **Free float**: each listed share's holders are S1.283's; the float is S3.145's read over them, never set.
- **Last close** (GEN.5, a present value): each listed firm's close the capitalisation-to-GDP share its equity carries
  (`EQY.cap_to_gdp` × GDP apportioned by book equity) over its shares; `EQY.turnover` gives the opening's market depth
  read as MKT.15's first figure.

**Edge cases**: E12 — a country missing the listed count is left out of its group's median and reported
(`missing_listed_count_left_out`). E13 — a country with no listed company opens none (`no_listed_company_no_book`).
E11 — the first day's books read these present values until they print (LC-3-60).

**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `listed_count_from_source`, `close_from_capitalisation_share`,
`missing_listed_count_left_out`, `no_listed_company_no_book`.

**Budget**: opening only; the opening's span within its ratchet.
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.1 MB resident (2300 listing records × 48 B)

**Guards**: `phx-check data`.

**Not allowed**: a value typed by hand; a close that is not dated the snapshot's date; a free float written rather than
read.

### S3.147 — Share books and the closing call

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.6 PROCESS *(part: listed shares trade on continuous books with a closing call; market makers complete it at S3.174)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5d, 6a, 6b, 6d, 7); §7.11 (phx-market: K-78, K-76, K-86); §7.8 (phx-ledger: K-50)
**Depends on**: S1.315 (the continuous book and its closing call through K-76); S1.326 (prints and the close as
mark); S1.251 (trades as commitments until their settle day); S1.248 (settlement of DvP legs); S1.280 (instrument
holdings moved at settlement); S3.145 (listing opens a book); S2.133 (estates' administration, whose shares now sell
here)
**Goal**: each listed share has a continuous book meeting every business day at 6a: orders posted in the day's decide
stage arrive in an order drawn by lot, trade at the resting price in price–time priority, and end in a closing call
whose price is the day's close and the share's mark; trades settle on the exchange's convention.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/markets.rs` | the equity book market declaration: continuous with a closing call, business days only, settlement T+n from `EQY.toml`, price points, streams |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/decl.rs` | reasons `EQY.trade` (a DvP link group) and `EQY.fee` |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/markets.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | the day's book orders to K-78 at 6a; matches to K-48/K-50 at 6d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-61 |

**Design**:
- **Market** (MKT.4, core): one K-78 book per listed share class; order kinds `Continuous` and `AtTheClose`, each with
  its poster's own limit (MKT.16). Arrival order drawn on `EQY.arrival_lot` (subject: the book; day); the closing
  call's rationing ties on `EQY.close_lot`. No book meets on a non-business day.
- **Close and mark** (MKT.12, done): the closing call's price is the day's close, K-86's mark for every holder whose
  basis marks to it; a book with no trade shows the last close with its age (Law 8).
- **Settlement**: each match is a DvP link group (SET.4): money buyer → seller, units seller → buyer, a K-50
  commitment settling on day + n business days of the exchange's convention (SET.2); both sides' pending amounts stand
  on their books meanwhile (REG.10).
- **Estates** (retires S2.133's placeholder naming EQY for shares): an estate's administrator (S2.133) posts its
  shares' sell orders on the book at its own descending ask, like any seller.
- **Fees**: the exchange's fee per trade (POLICY), a flow under `EQY.fee` to the exchange.

**Edge cases**: E2 — orders on one side only: no print, the close shows its age (`one_sided_book_no_print`). E5 —
index rebalance days crowd the closing call, O(orders) (`closing_call_cost_linear_in_orders`). E7 — arrival order by
address, never by worker (`arrival_lot_independent_of_workers`). E10 — a poster ending: its resting orders lapse with
its offers, K-97 (LC-3-61 finds no print from a lapsed order). E14 — a party buying and selling one share the same
day: both legs settle, nets commute (`dvp_link_group_all_or_none`). E6 — a trade matched before a save and settling
after it: its K-50 commitment and both books' pending amounts are live rows (`dvp_commitment_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: the book market declaration is data S3.148, S3.151, S3.158, S3.174, S3.191, S3.194, S3.206 post
on; none added to a base.

**Unit tests**: `market_declaration_refuses_nb_meeting`; `dvp_link_group_all_or_none`; `one_sided_book_no_print`;
`close_is_mark_with_age`; `closing_call_cost_linear_in_orders`; `arrival_lot_independent_of_workers`;
`dvp_commitment_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-61 — every equity print came out of a book match or its closing call (MKT.14), and every trade
settled on the exchange's convention or failed visibly; applicable from the first trade.

**Budget**: book orders 200000 B / 0 NB / 250000 H in all, of which 37100 are posted by S3.151, S3.158, S3.174,
S3.176, S3.180 and S3.191 and stated there as items of `fin.book.order_ns`; this step's own, investors' orders from
S3.148's values, are 162900 B / 0 NB / 212900 H at `fin.book.order_ns` 150 phone-ns all in (S1.315's 130 plus 20 for
admission): 24.4 / 0 / 31.9 core-ms; DvP commitments 100000 a day at K-50's post 30 phone-ns: 3 / 0 / 3; the kernel
carries none. Closing calls 2300 a business day at `fin.call.call_us` 3 µs: 7 / 0 / 7.
- its share of fin.fixed.securities: 27.4 / 0 / 34.9 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 7 / 0 / 7 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.crash_day (event): 0 core-ms beyond its share on the day; joins H and B′ (the orders a crash causes
  are the woken reviews' and close-outs', posted from the next day and stated by S3.180 and S3.191)
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 MB (resting orders are K-70's `book.standing` rows, already counted)

**Guards**: assembly refuses a book market declared to meet on a non-business day.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an order at market; a close computed rather than cleared; a trade settled before its settle day.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-61 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
