### S3.148 — Investors' equity values and orders

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.3 DECISION *(part: investors buy below and sell above their own value; index trackers complete it at S3.206)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5a, 5c, 5d); §7.13 (phx-val: K-92, K-105); §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100)
**Depends on**: S3.147 (the books orders go to); S1.357 (the investor schedule, K-105: the order from a value); S1.336
(public series of reports and prints; registered instrument outlooks); S1.165 (the registration instance); S1.348
(the decision core); S1.227 (review days); S1.338 (declared portfolio limits); S3.134 (investors' debt values: the
required return's short-rate outlook and the shared value arithmetic)
**Goal**: institutions that hold or may hold shares — banks within their regulated portfolios, firms with stakes or
treasury cash — value each share in their reach by their own outlook of its distributions or earnings discounted at
their own required return, and post the investor schedule of that value on the book.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/value.rs` | EQY.3, VAL.8: a share's own value; comparables where there is no history (VAL.10) |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/points.rs` | decision point `EQY.invest_equity` (lumpy; review days and wakes) |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/decl.rs` | registrations of candidates: a K-06 instance keyed by instrument over (party, method) |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/value.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | 5c reviews; 5d orders posted |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-62 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc150.rs` | PC-150 |
| `data/<country>/EQY.toml` | review schedule and hours (TECHNOLOGY); the required-return form's parameters (PREFERENCE per decider kind) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the value form (dividend discount over own outlooks; Fama and French, 2002) |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the institution's investment office (PTY.16; its founding preferences until filled, E 47).
- **Value** (VAL.8): `v = D̂ ÷ (r̂ − ĝ)` per share, with `D̂` its own outlook of the next distribution (from the
  issuer's published distributions, or its earnings where it pays none, as published — filed accounts, reports from
  S3.209), `ĝ` its outlook of their growth, and `r̂ = own outlook of the short rate + γ·σ²` (γ its risk aversion,
  PREFERENCE; σ² its outlook width of the share's returns). Where `r̂ ≤ ĝ` the form does not apply and the decider
  values by comparables. With no history of the issuer (VAL.8's "compared with what it has seen similar things fetch",
  VAL.10), the value is the median of its industry peers' last closes per unit of their published earnings times the
  issuer's earnings — a reservation, never a price (VAL.20); nothing absent is read as zero.
- **Outlooks**: the method's public-series outlook per registered (method, instrument) from K-92, formed at 5a only on
  a day with a new print or report; the decider's own deviation for the asset class added (VAL.23), caught up when it
  reads.
- **Order**: the investor schedule of `v` with σ², γ, its fees and position (K-105), bound by its declared portfolio
  limits (K-93: a bank's regulated equity limit, a firm's treasury policy), posted as `Continuous` limit orders; a sell
  side only as `Covered<Qty>` (S3.149).
- **When**: the decider's declared review schedule (K-43, its institution-kind slot) and wakes by a surprise on a
  share it holds or has registered (REP.35, S3.218); review hours `EQY.invest_review_hours` from its staff.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no share in reach: no order (`empty_reach_posts_nothing`). E11 — day zero: outlooks from the
opening's closes and filed accounts (`first_value_from_snapshot`). E12 — an issuer with no published earnings and no
peers: no value, no order (`no_history_no_peer_no_order`). E14 — a surprise and a review the same day: one review
(`one_review_per_day`). E6 — registered cells and own deviations saved, the registration instance rebuilt at load
(`registrations_rebuilt_equal`).

**Extension points**: the value rule (a pure function in `sys-eqy`) is read by S3.151 (management's own value per
share), S3.152 (the issue price against own value), S3.158 (households), S3.165 (desks' view), S3.191 (fund managers).
`EQY.invest_equity` is converted to options by S8.159.

**Unit tests**: `value_dividend_discount_on_own_outlooks`; `required_return_short_rate_plus_premium`;
`comparables_when_no_history`; `rhat_below_ghat_values_by_comparables`; `empty_reach_posts_nothing`;
`first_value_from_snapshot`; `no_history_no_peer_no_order`; `one_review_per_day`; `registrations_rebuilt_equal`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-62 — every institutional equity order names its decider, its value and the outlooks it read;
none read a price not yet formed; applicable from the first review.

**Budget**: ≈ 1000 institutional reviews a business day (≈ 20000 holders of equity reviewing monthly) over ≈ 30
candidates each (value 150 phone-ns, schedule 150).
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 9 / 0 / 9 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.5 MB resident (15000 × 32 B: own outlook deviation per asset class, 8 × `Fixed` i32);
  the review's next day +0 B (named slot `EQY.invest_equity`, institution kinds)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-06 registrations): +3.2 MB resident (600000 members × 5.33 B)

**Guards**: PC-150 — a financial order's limit is typed as K-105's output, so no rule writes a limit of its own making
(a signature check on every decision point posting to K-76, K-78 or K-79).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a **price** from a multiple, a book value, a discounted cash flow or a target (EQY.11); a value
read as a price (VAL.20); a value shared across deciders beyond the method's public-series outlook.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the value form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed
  resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-62 registered; PC-150 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.149 — Shorts only on covered units

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.11 FORBID; EQY.9 PROCESS *(part: an offer only of covered units; borrows and their fees complete it at S3.175)*
**Architecture**: §7.10 (phx-hold: K-63 `Covered<Qty>`); §7.11 (phx-market: K-70, K-78); §7.17 (phx-audit: K-103)
**Depends on**: S1.277 (K-63 free units, `Covered<Qty>` and its guard PC-53); S3.147 (the book's sell side); S1.280
(distributions only through instrument events); S1.353 (audit families)
**Goal**: every sell order on a share book carries a `Covered<Qty>` built only from free units its poster holds, bought
or borrowed, so no short exists without a borrow; no price forms but by a meeting; and a shareholder receives income
only from a distribution.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/cover.rs` | the sell side of every equity order built from `Covered<Qty>` |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/audit.rs` | the `EQY.income` family: shareholder income only by distribution reasons |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/cover.rs` | logic-level tests, the compile-fail one included |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-29 |

**Design**:
- **Cover** (REG.16, EQY.11): a sell order's quantity type is `Covered<Qty>`, which `phx-hold` constructs from a
  holding's free units (held − committed − pledged, K-63) and commits at posting; units lent out are not held, units
  borrowed are (title passes, S3.175). Uncovered is a compile-level refusal (PC-53, the core's guard). The exchange's
  short-sale rules (EQY.12) are read from S3.145's POLICY.
- **Prices** (EQY.11): no rule may write a share's print; K-86 accepts prints only from K-78/K-76 matches (MKT.14), so
  a price from a multiple, a book value, a discounted cash flow or a target has no path; values are reservations
  (VAL.20).
- **Income**: the only reasons that pay a holder as holder of an equity instrument are S3.150's distribution events
  (dividends, cash in lieu, liquidation distributions); the `EQY.income` family checks, over the day's change set, that
  each flow to an equity holder from its issuer carries one of them (K-103).

**Edge cases**: E3 — a party holding nothing posts no sell side (`no_free_units_no_offer`). E10 — units pledged since
posting cannot be used twice: committed at posting (`commit_at_posting_blocks_pledge`). E14 — two sell orders on one
holding the same day: the second covered only by what the first left free (`second_offer_covered_by_remainder`).

**Extension points**: none added; `Covered<Qty>` is the core's (S1.277).

**Unit tests**: `offer_refuses_uncovered_quantity` (compile-fail); `no_free_units_no_offer`;
`commit_at_posting_blocks_pledge`; `second_offer_covered_by_remainder`; `income_family_flags_undistributed_payment`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-29 — EQY.11 and REG.16: no offer without covered units; no holding below zero; no income to a
holder but by a distribution; applicable from the first equity order.

**Budget**: one K-63 free check per sell order on ≈ 100000 sell orders a business day; the family over ≈ 10000 equity
flows fused at `fin.audit.ident_ns`.

### S3.150 — Equity events and shareholders last

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.7 PROCESS; EQY.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 2e, 2f, 7, 9); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-65 events engine); §7.15 (phx-end: K-98 waterfall)
**Depends on**: S1.281 (the instrument events engine: events applied to holders of record in its one holder walk a
record day, pro-rata legs with a named residue); S1.224 (an electorate taken from a holder list at a record date);
S1.172 (apportionment); S1.345 (claims
classes in the declared order); S3.145 (share families and their terms)
**Goal**: dividends are paid to the holders of record at the start of their record day; issuance raises the issued
amount and buybacks cancel units; a split changes the count and nothing else, its fractions paid as cash in lieu; in
insolvency shareholders are paid only after every creditor, preferred before ordinary, and their holdings end at zero,
never below. Its per-row work rides the core's one holder walk a record day (S1.281).

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/decl.rs` | event kinds on the equity families: `dividend` (record, payment day), `split` (ratio), `issue`, `cancel`; reasons `EQY.dividend`, `EQY.cash_in_lieu`, `EQY.liquidation`; the record-day rule (one record day per issuer occasion) |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/events.rs` | the split's unit arithmetic and cash in lieu; the class ranks handed to the waterfall |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/events.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | the dividend's per-row work handed to S1.281's record-day walk |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-30, LC-3-32 |

**Design**:
- **Record day**: an issuer's dividend and its meeting (S3.155) share one record day by the declared company-law rule
  (the meeting's record day is the final dividend's); on it the core's holder walk (S1.281) reads each holder row once
  (the holders at the start of that day) and hands it to every rider: this step's per-row work is the dividend
  entitlement (units × rate, kept as the event's apportion weights); S3.155's is the electorate entry and its vote.
- **Dividend** (EQY.7, REG.11 core): declared by the payer's decision (S3.151); K-65 pays at 2e of the payment day the
  entitlements fixed on the record day, pro rata by K-16's apportion with the residue to the issuer (Law 7); money legs
  join stage 7's batches; a holder with no account in the currency fails visibly (MON.5).
- **Issue and cancel**: an issue raises the issued amount by the units delivered at settlement (REG.3); units the issuer
  buys back are cancelled at their settlement — never held as an asset.
- **Split** (unit-only event at 2e): each holding's units × ratio, rounded down; the fractions aggregated per
  instrument and paid as cash in lieu at the last close (K-86) with the residue to the issuer; lots scaled by the same
  ratio (K-62); nothing else changes.
- **Insolvency** (EQY.8): the equity families declare their claim classes (`preferred` above `ordinary`, both below
  every creditor class of the country's insolvency law, K-98); the waterfall pays them only what remains; an instrument
  whose class receives nothing ceases (REG.12) with each holding's loss recorded.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a mass-default day ceases many issuers' shares: one cessation per instrument, O(its holders)
(LC-3-30). E4 — an estate holding shares receives dividends and votes as any holder of record
(`estate_holder_paid_and_votes`). E5 — the busiest record day: the dividend rides S1.281's one walk
(`dividend_rides_record_day_walk`).
E8 — split ratios overflow checked (`split_overflow_stops`). E10 — a holder ended since the record day: the leg goes to
its estate, SET.7 (`ended_holder_paid_to_estate`). E13 — an issuer with no holders of record: no legs
(`no_holders_no_legs`). E6 — a dividend declared before a save with its record or payment day after it: the event is a
K-42 entry rebuilt from K-65's events, entitlements saved once fixed (`declared_dividend_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: event kinds are declared data read by S3.151 (dividends, cancel), S3.152 (issue), S3.161
(conversion issue); S3.155's and S8.127's votes ride the same walk.

**Unit tests**: `dividend_pro_rata_residue_on_issuer`; `split_rounding_cash_in_lieu`; `split_changes_count_only`;
`buyback_cancels_units`; `insolvency_pays_shareholders_last`; `split_overflow_stops`;
`dividend_rides_record_day_walk`; `estate_holder_paid_and_votes`; `ended_holder_paid_to_estate`;
`no_holders_no_legs`; `declared_dividend_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-30 — REG.11 and REG.12 for equity: every event paid its holders of record at the start of its
record day; every ceased share's holdings resolved to cash or a recorded loss. LC-3-32 — EQY.8: in every insolvency,
shareholders received nothing until every creditor class was paid. Applicable from the first event / insolvency.

**Budget**: the entitlement per holder row (a multiply and an append to the event's weights) on the rows S1.281's
walk reads. No record day is tied to the quarter-end: a listed firm's is its declaration day plus the exchange's
notice, its declaration after its report (reports spread across the windows, S3.209); an unlisted firm's falls when
its statement is ready (S2.119); a coupon's by its schedule from the line's issue day (TIME.3). Record-day row events
a year, from S1.280's 4950000 holdings: listed shares 1800000 rows (households' 1200000 of S3.159's 2000000, funds'
500000 of S3.183's 900000, institutions' 100000) × 2.5 record days = 4500000; bonds 1050000 rows (households' 500000,
funds' 400000, S3.142's and S3.143's 150000) × 2 coupons = 2100000; fund units 350000 × 1 distribution = 350000;
unlisted owners
1500000 × 1 (S2.119's) = 1500000; 8450000 in all over 250 business days. So the H record days reach 34000 holder rows,
the mean business day's share (1 in 250 of the year's row events), inside S1.281's walk. The busiest record day
follows the reporting peak by the notice: 13 % of the quarter's listed dividend rows (the reporting peak's 300 of
2300) plus the mean day's others, 162000 rows. The split of S3.159's holdings by class is the design estimate the
bench's `-F holdings -D H` measures.
- its share of fin.fixed.holder_rows: 0.03 / 0 / 0.03 core-ms (B / NB / H), inside S1.281's walk
- on fin.calendar.record_peak (the reporting peak plus the exchange's notice): 0.15 core-ms (162000 rows); joins B′
- ledger line 11 (holdings and lots): +0 MB resident (entitlements are K-65 event weights in day buffers, released at
  payment)

**Guards**: assembly refuses an equity family without claim classes.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a holder walk of its own; a dividend to holders at payment day rather than
record day; a treasury-share holding; a holding below zero.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-30 and LC-3-32 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.151 — Payouts gain buybacks and record dates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.10 DECISION; EQY.4 DECISION *(part: buybacks from cash not needed; issuing completes it at S3.153)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 5d, 2e); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-65); §7.11 (phx-market: K-78)
**Depends on**: S2.119 (the payout rule: its free-cash target, partial adjustment and distributable-reserves limit);
S2.188 (a bank's payout restriction near its line); S3.150 (dividend and cancel events, record days); S3.148 (the value
rule management applies to its own shares); S3.147 (the book buyback orders go to); S1.348 (the decision core)
**Goal**: a firm's payout keeps S2.119's rule — the dividend moves from the last toward the free cash its own plans
leave, at its management's speed, within distributable reserves — and gains two things: free cash left beyond the
dividend buys back shares when their price is below management's own value per share, by limit orders at that value,
or is retained; and a listed firm's dividend carries record and payment days the exchange's notice apart.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/payout.rs` | FRM.10: S2.119's rule gains the buyback branch on the residual free cash and the dates |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | decision point `FRM.payout` gains its buyback output |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/tests/payout.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/frm.rs` | the declared dividend handed to K-65 with its dates; the buyback orders to K-78 at 5d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/frm.rs` | LC-3-63 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the buyback form (Ikenberry, Lakonishok and Vermaelen, 1995) beside S2.119's (Lintner, 1956) |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the firm's chief executive's office (PTY.16; founding preferences while empty, E 47), on S2.119's
  occasion (a statement of its payout frequency ready).
- **Dividend** (S2.119, unchanged): target `D* = cash − expected outgoings and dues over the horizon − buffer target −
  the investment it plans to fund itself`; `D = D_last + s·(D* − D_last)` with `s` its management's speed; `D_last` is
  a read of its equity instrument's last dividend event (K-65); paid only within distributable reserves and not while
  `D` is negative; a bank's dividend obeys S2.188's restriction near its line. No payout ratio is a parameter.
- **Buyback** (FRM.10's buybacks, EQY.4): the residual `F = D* − D`, when positive and the firm listed: if its last
  close is below management's own value per share `v_own` (S3.148's rule at management's outlooks and required
  return), it posts `Continuous` buy orders for `F ÷ v_own` shares limited at `v_own`; otherwise `F` is retained.
  S2.188's restriction binds buybacks as it binds dividends (a bank near its line buys back nothing). Unlisted firms
  retain `F`. Filled shares are cancelled at settlement (S3.150).
- **Dates**: a listed firm's record day = declaration day + the exchange's notice (EQY.12, S3.145); its payment day by
  the declared payment lag; the final dividend's record day is its meeting's (S3.150). Unlisted firms keep S2.119's
  payment day.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E3 — no free cash: `D ≤ 0` and `F ≤ 0`, nothing paid or bought (`no_free_cash_no_payout`). E11 — day
zero: `D_last` is the opening's last dividend event (`first_payout_reads_opening_dividend`). E12 — an unlisted share
has no close: no buyback branch, never a price of zero (`unlisted_retains_residual`). E10 — an issuer ending between
record and payment day: its estate owes the declared dividend as a claim (K-98; LC-3-63 traces it). E14 — a dividend
and a buyback in one review: both from one cash figure (`dividend_and_buyback_share_one_cash_figure`).

**Extension points**: `FRM.payout`'s buyback output is converted to options by S8.143.

**Unit tests**: `buyback_only_below_own_value`; `buyback_from_residual_after_dividend`;
`bank_restriction_binds_buybacks`; `no_free_cash_no_payout`; `first_payout_reads_opening_dividend`;
`unlisted_retains_residual`; `dividend_and_buyback_share_one_cash_figure`; `record_day_respects_notice`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-63 — every dividend names the review that declared it and was paid to the holders of record at
its record day; every buyback order's limit is its firm's own value per share; applicable from the first payout.

**Budget**: the buyback branch adds a comparison to S2.119's reviews (≈ 3000 a business day); ≈ 200 buyback orders a
day.
- adds 20 phone-ns to fin.decide.attend_ns at 3000 / 0 / 3000 items
- adds 200 / 0 / 200 items to fin.book.order_ns (its share of fin.fixed.securities: 0.03 / 0 / 0.03 core-ms (B / NB / H) at 150 phone-ns an order)
- ledger: +0 B (the last dividend is read from K-65's events)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a payout ratio as a primitive; a dividend beyond distributable reserves; a buyback "at any price";
treasury shares held.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed resolution
  within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-63 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.152 — Share offerings: initial, secondary and pre-emptive

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.4 DECISION *(part: the offering executed; the choice of shares as the cheapest source completes it at S3.153)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a, 7); §7.11 (phx-market: K-76 book-built variant, K-80); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-64, K-65)
**Depends on**: S3.133 (underwriters and their commitment); S3.135 (the book-built issue on the underwriter's book);
S3.145 (listing on an initial offering); S3.148 (management's own value per share); S3.150 (the issue event);
S1.317 (bilateral offers to existing holders)
**Goal**: a firm that has decided to raise equity offers its shares: a listed firm or an initial offering through a
book-built call on its underwriter's book with its own walk-away price, an unlisted firm to its existing holders in
proportion to their holdings; unsold shares are not issued, and a failed offering is an event.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-securities/src/equity.rs` | the handle `equity_cost(firm, n)` other systems read (the cost of an issue to the firm) |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/issue.rs` | EQY.4: the offering's form, size at the outlook price, walk-away price; `equity_cost` |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/points.rs` | decision point `EQY.issue_equity` (the chief executive's office) |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/issue.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | offerings to K-76 at 6a; pre-emptive offers as K-80 asks |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-64 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | issue timing (Baker and Wurgler, 2002) |

**Design**:
- **Cost of equity to the issuer**: `equity_cost(firm, n) = (v_own − p̂) · n + fee(n)`, with `p̂` its outlook of the
  clearing price (its last close, or for an initial offering comparable issuers' closes per unit of published
  earnings, VAL.10), `v_own` management's own value per share (S3.148), `n` the shares needed at `p̂`, `fee` its
  underwriter's quote (S3.133). Exposed through `if-securities` for the funding choice (S3.153) and a bank's raise
  (S3.154).
- **Offering** (decider: the chief executive's office): listed or initial — a book-built call (S3.135) with the
  underwriter's commitment and the issuer's walk-away price `p_min` (management's PREFERENCE over `v_own`), ties on
  `EQY.offering_lot`; an initial offering applies for listing (S3.145). Unlisted — an offer to existing holders in
  proportion to their holdings (pre-emption, company law's POLICY) by K-80, each holder accepting by its own value and
  cash.
- **Failure** (MKT.10): demand below `n` at or above `p_min` → the unsold part is not issued (MKT.17), an event; the
  programme waits for the next funding review.

**Edge cases**: E2 — an offering with no bids is not issued and the event recorded (`offering_no_bids_not_issued`).
E10 — an issuer ending during its book: the offering lapses with its offers, K-97 (`offering_lapses_on_issuer_end`).
E11 — an initial offering with no history prices from comparables (`ipo_price_outlook_from_comparables`). E12 — no
comparable: no initial offering, never a price of zero (`ipo_refused_without_comparable`). E6 — an offering whose call
is pending across a save: its orders are live K-70 rows (`offering_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: the handle `equity_cost` (read by S3.153 and S3.154); `EQY.issue_equity` is converted by
S8.158.

**Unit tests**: `equity_cost_value_transfer_plus_fee`; `walk_away_price_refuses_below`; `preemptive_offer_pro_rata`;
`offering_no_bids_not_issued`; `offering_lapses_on_issuer_end`; `ipo_price_outlook_from_comparables`;
`ipo_refused_without_comparable`; `offering_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-64 — every share issue names the programme it funded, its book and its clearing price; every
failed offering is an event; applicable from the first issue.

**Budget**: ≈ 5 offerings a business day over ≈ 1000 orders each on K-76.
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 0.8 / 0 / 0.8 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; unsold shares absorbed beyond the underwriter's commitment; a price for the offering but the
call's.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed resolution
  within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-64 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.153 — Shares among a firm's funding sources

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.9 DECISION *(part: shares among the funding sources; the holder's weighing of distress at S8.140)*; EQY.4 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c); §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100)
**Depends on**: S2.118 (the funding decision: sources ranked by all-in cost within the management's leverage
tolerance); S3.131 (bonds and paper among the sources); S3.152 (`equity_cost` and the offering); S2.131 (the
investment programme a funding review funds)
**Goal**: a firm's funding review ranks new shares beside retained cash, trade credit, loans, bonds and paper by what
each costs it now, and issues shares when a programme needs funding and equity is its cheapest acceptable source.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/funding.rs` | FRM.9: shares added to S2.118's ranking through `equity_cost` |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/tests/funding.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/frm.rs` | a choice of shares handed to `EQY.issue_equity` |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the chief executive's office on S2.118's funding review (the firm's `finance` slot).
- **Choice** (FRM.9, EQY.4): for a programme to fund (an investment project, S2.131) the ranking of S2.118 gains
  shares at `equity_cost(firm, n) ÷ n`'s per-unit cost against each debt source's all-in rate, within the leverage its
  management tolerates (shares lower leverage, which is what makes them acceptable when debt is not); the cheapest
  acceptable source is chosen; if shares, S3.152's offering runs. The tolerance read is S2.118's placeholder
  `FRM.leverage_tolerance` (naming MND), retired by S8.140.
- EQY.4 completes here: a firm issues shares when equity is its cheapest way to fund a programme it has (this step),
  and buys back or pays dividends from cash it does not need (S3.151).

**Edge cases**: E12 — a firm whose `equity_cost` is absent (no close and no comparable) does not rank shares
(`shares_absent_cost_not_ranked`). E2 — no source acceptable: the programme waits for the next review
(`no_acceptable_source_waits`). E14 — a funding review and a payout review the same day read one cash figure
(`funding_and_payout_one_cash_figure`).

**Extension points**: the ranking's shares branch is converted by S8.140.

**Unit tests**: `shares_chosen_only_when_cheapest`; `shares_accepted_when_debt_beyond_tolerance`;
`shares_absent_cost_not_ranked`; `no_acceptable_source_waits`; `funding_and_payout_one_cash_figure`.

**Budget**: one more source in S2.118's ranking (≈ 1000 funding reviews a business day).

### S3.154 — A bank raises capital by issuing shares

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BCP.4 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c); §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100)
**Depends on**: S2.191 (a bank's decision to raise capital, recorded); S2.186 (the capital layers a new share adds
to); S3.132 (contingent capital and subordinated debt, the other instruments); S3.152 (`equity_cost` and the
offering)
**Goal**: a bank whose capital review decides to raise capital issues shares or contingent capital, whichever it
judges worth the price; the issue can fail if investors will not buy, and a failed raise leaves the bank's near-line
responses running.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/rules/raise.rs` | BCP.4: the recorded decision executed through shares or contingent capital by price |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/tests/raise.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/bcp.rs` | a raise by shares handed to `EQY.issue_equity` |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the bank's chief executive's office, on S2.191's recorded decision, whose placeholder
  `BCP.raise_unmet` this retires for shares.
- **Choice** (BCP.4): the bank compares `equity_cost(bank, n)` for the capital it needs with contingent capital's cost
  (S3.132) and raises through the cheaper that its requirement accepts as the layer it lacks; it raises nothing when
  neither is worth the price to it (its shadow cost of capital, S2.188, against the issue's cost), leaving its
  near-line responses to run.
- **Failure**: an offering that fails (S3.152) is an event; the need stays recorded for the next review.
- Retires S2.191's placeholder for shares (contingent capital and subordinated debt were retired by S3.132).

**Edge cases**: E2 — the offering fails: the need stays recorded (`failed_raise_stays_recorded`). E1 — several banks
raising on one stress day each run their own offering (`raises_independent_per_bank`). E12 — no close and no
comparable: no share raise, contingent capital only (`raise_without_share_price_uses_coco`).

**Extension points**: the raise choice is converted by S8.169.

`raises_independent_per_bank`; `raise_without_share_price_uses_coco`.

### S3.155 — Shareholder meetings and votes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.5 DECISION *(part: votes at meetings; takeover acceptances complete it at S4.174)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 9b, 9d, 10a); §7.6 (phx-record: K-41 tallies, K-37 records)
**Depends on**: S1.281 (the record day's one holder walk, which the electorate rides); S3.150 (the shared record day);
S1.224 (ballots and tallies); S3.145
(meeting windows, notice); S3.148 (a holder's own value, which a resolution changes); S1.227 (meeting days); S1.215
(results as records)
**Goal**: each issuer holds its meeting on a day it sets within the declared window after its year end; the holders of
record at the record day vote on its resolutions by class when their stake times what the resolution changes for them
exceeds their cost of voting; resolutions pass by the declared majorities of votes cast.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/vote.rs` | EQY.5: a holder's vote on a declared resolution kind |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/decl.rs` | resolution kinds as data (approve a distribution, authority to issue, authority to buy back, elect board seats); majorities |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/vote.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | meeting day: the electorate from S3.150's pass, ballots, tally, result |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-65 |
| `data/<country>/EQY.toml` | meeting windows and notice; majorities per kind (POLICY of company law); voting hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the vote form (Downs, 1957) |

**Design**:
- **Meeting day**: set by the issuer's board at its annual report, the first business day after the declared notice
  within the window (the named firm slot `EQY.meeting`, K-43); record day = the final dividend's (S3.150).
- **Electorate**: taken as a rider of S1.281's record-day walk (K-41 entries with votes by class) — no read of its own.
- **Vote** (decider: each holder's own — a household's adults, an institution's investment office): votes when
  `stake × |Δv| > h_vote × w`, with `Δv` the change in its own value of its holding the resolution brings, computed
  once per (resolution, holder's method) and caught up by its own deviation (each resolution kind declares how its
  proposal enters the value rule: a distribution now against its value retained at the holder's required return;
  authority to issue at the announced size and the holder's outlook of the issue price; board candidates by S3.156's
  reading of their records); `h_vote` `EQY.vote_hours`, `w` its value of time; votes for when `Δv > 0`. The filter
  runs inside the walk, so an abstaining row costs one comparison.
- **Tally**: K-41 by (resolution, choice), weight = votes; passes by the declared majority of votes cast; the result a
  record and a public event (OBS.3). Estates vote by their administrator's rule like any holder.
- Streams: none (a tie of votes fails the resolution by the declared rule).

**Edge cases**: E4 — an estate holder votes (`estate_holder_votes`). E5 — the meeting season's record days: the
electorate rides S1.281's one walk (`electorate_from_record_day_walk`). E10 — a holder ended after the record day: its
estate's vote (`ended_holder_votes_through_estate`). E13 — a resolution with no votes cast fails (`no_votes_fails`).
E14 — a holder selling after the record day still votes, holder of record (`seller_after_record_day_votes`). E6 — a
meeting whose record day is before a save: the electorate is a saved K-41 entry set (`electorate_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: resolution kinds are declared data: S3.156 (board seats), S4.174 (takeover acceptances, EQY.5's
completion). The vote rule is converted by S8.127.

**Unit tests**: `vote_only_above_cost`; `vote_for_when_value_higher`; `delta_v_once_per_method`;
`majority_of_votes_cast`; `no_votes_fails`; `estate_holder_votes`; `electorate_from_record_day_walk`;
`ended_holder_votes_through_estate`; `seller_after_record_day_votes`; `electorate_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-65 — every vote counted was cast by a holder of record at its record day, weighted by class
terms; every result is a record; applicable from the first meeting.

**Budget**: the electorate entry and the voting-cost comparison per holder row, and 5 % of rows voting against the
per-method `Δv`, on the record days S3.150 counts: 34000 rows on the mean business day and on H (1700 voting), 162000
on the busiest record day (8100 voting).
- its share of fin.fixed.holder_rows: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H), inside S1.281's walk
- on fin.calendar.record_peak (the reporting peak plus the exchange's notice): 0.2 core-ms (162000 rows); joins B′
- ledger: +0 B (named slot `EQY.meeting`); ballots in K-41's day buffer

**Guards**: assembly refuses a resolution kind without a declared majority.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a holder walk of its own; a vote from a holder not of record; a result drawn.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed resolution
  within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-65 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.156 — Boards and chief executives appointed

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.1 STATE; PTY.16 STATE *(part: firms' and banks' boards and chief executives held by named persons under appointment contracts)*; PTY.17 PROCESS *(part: a board by its owners' votes, a chief executive by its board)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 5d, 9d); §7.5 (phx-pop: K-34 offices); §7.11 (phx-market: K-72, K-82); §7.9
(phx-contract: K-53)
**Depends on**: S1.209 (offices per institution, holder refs, the person → offices index); S3.155 (board elections as
a resolution kind); S1.413 (vacancies posted from the employer's own state, on the occupation's wage points); S1.304
(the vacancy book); S1.321 (search and match); S1.257 (the appointment family); S1.348 (the decision core resolves an
office's holder)
**Goal**: each incorporated firm's and bank's board members are persons its owners elect at their meetings, and its
chief executive a person its board appoints from the applicants' records, each under an appointment contract that
pays them; a vacancy by death, resignation or term's end is filled the same way, and an office reads its founding
preferences only while its filling runs.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/appoint.rs` | the board's choice of a chief executive; its posted pay; renewal at term's end |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/decl.rs` | offices per legal form (board seats, term, chief executive); the family `FRM.appointment`; the executive occupation for postings |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | decision point `FRM.appoint_executive` (the board chair's office) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/tests/appoint.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/frm.rs` | vacancies posted at 5d; appointments opened at 7 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/frm.rs` | LC-3-66 |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | offices by legal form, terms (POLICY of company law); review hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the selection form (ranking by record against pay; Bertrand and Schoar, 2003) |

**Design**:
- **Offices** (PTY.16, FRM.1): the legal form declares `board × k` seats with a term and one chief executive; an
  owner-managed firm's offices stay its owner's (S1.486). With the board and the chief executive in office the
  incorporated firm's FRM.1 description is complete.
- **Board** (PTY.17): seats expiring at a meeting are resolutions of kind `elect_board` (S3.155); candidates are the
  sitting members standing again and persons nominated by holders above the declared nomination share; holders value
  candidates by the record reading below.
- **Chief executive**: on a vacancy (death — K-34 vacates every office at once; resignation — its holder accepting
  another appointment; term's end without renewal) the board posts the office in the vacancy book (K-72, occupation
  `executive`, the firm's seat's region) at a pay that is its own value of the office — the results it expects a
  holder to bring (VAL.8) — on the executive occupation's wage points, as any vacancy is posted (S1.413), competing
  with other boards' postings. Applicants arrive by K-82; the board's rule ranks each by its record — experience (the
  tenure and industry of its current employment, read from its contract row), offices held now (K-34), skills (its
  person columns) — against the pay asked; ties on `FRM.appoint_lot`. No life record is read (K-40). The chosen
  accepts against its own reservation (K-82); the appointment is a K-53 row paying `FRM.office_pay`, and the office's
  holder is written (K-34).
- **Renewal** at term's end: the board renews when the firm's published results over the term beat its own outlook at
  appointment (declared form), otherwise posts the office. Removal mid-term by minds is S8.124's.
- **Decider**: the board's decisions are taken in its chair's office (declared by the form), reading its holder's
  preferences, founding preferences while empty (E 47).

**Edge cases**: E2 — no applicant: the office stays empty, read at founding preferences, the posting stands
(`no_applicant_office_stays_empty`). E10 — a holder's death vacates all its offices the same day, K-34
(`death_vacates_all_offices`). E11 — day zero: the opening's offices are filled by its holders (LC-3-66 reads them).
E14 — a person chosen by two boards the same day accepts one, by its own reservation order
(`one_acceptance_per_person_per_day`). E6 — a posting open across a save: a live K-70 offer
(`office_posting_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: `FRM.appoint_executive` is converted by S8.124; the board-seat resolution by S8.127; public
offices complete PTY.16 and PTY.17 at S5.144.

**Unit tests**: `rank_by_record_against_pay`; `posted_pay_is_boards_own_value_on_wage_points`;
`renewal_when_results_beat_outlook`; `no_applicant_office_stays_empty`; `death_vacates_all_offices`;
`board_seats_by_votes`; `one_acceptance_per_person_per_day`; `office_posting_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-66 — every filled office of an incorporated firm or bank names its holder, the vote or board
decision that filled it and an appointment contract paying it; an office is empty only while a posting for it is open;
applicable from the first vacancy.

**Budget**: appointments ≈ 1400 a business day (≈ 1400000 offices of incorporated firms and banks, four-year terms),
one K-82 search of ≈ 20 applicants each; life-record reads 0.
- adds 1400 / 0 / 1400 items to fin.decide.search_ns
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 MB (appointment rows are S1.257's `FRM.appointment`, in its family mix); offices are
  line 7's

**Guards**: assembly refuses a legal form that declares a decision in an office it does not declare.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an office filled by a draw; a chief executive appointed without a contract paying it; a pay set as
a declared share of anything.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed resolution
  within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-66 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.157 — Groups: control, intra-group contracts and limited liability

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FRM.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 9b, 10c); §7.12 (phx-acct: K-90 control and consolidation); §7.15 (phx-end: K-97);
§7.17 (phx-audit: K-103)
**Depends on**: S1.334 (consolidation: control as the least fixed point over equity votes; consolidated statements as
a pure read); S1.283 (equity holdings between parties); S1.343 (the ending kernel moves only a party's own adjacency);
S1.353 (audit families); S2.186 (the supervisor's requirement, whose placeholder `BCP.group_is_bank` this retires in its own
crate)
**Goal**: a firm is a parent or a subsidiary exactly when it controls, or is controlled through, a majority of votes
held directly or through parties it controls; intra-group loans, sales and guarantees are ordinary contracts; and each
member keeps limited liability unless a contract of its own makes it answer for another's debt; a bank's requirement
is tested on its consolidated group.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/decl.rs` | the group read's statement dates (each member's own); the group record kind |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/audit.rs` | the `FRM.liability` family: no party paid another's debt except by a contract naming it |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/tests/groups.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/systems/sys-bcp/src/rules/requirement.rs` | S2.186's placeholder retired in its own crate (§0.2's allowance): the test reads the consolidated statement over the group record |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/frm.rs` | the group read taken at 9b on statement dates and handed to its readers |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/frm.rs` | LC-3-31 |

**Design**:
- **Control** (PTY.7 core, FRM.3): K-90's control read on a party's statement date — `P` controls `S` when the votes
  held by `P` and by parties `P` controls exceed half of `S`'s votes (least fixed point, identity order); never stored
  as an attribute; recorded as a group record (parent, members, date) for the readers of that date.
- **Intra-group contracts**: ordinary rows of their families; consolidation (ACC.5, core) eliminates a row whose two
  sides are in one group, by reading the group record — no flag on any row.
- **Limited liability**: a member's ending (K-97) moves only its own accounts, holdings and contract sides; the
  `FRM.liability` family checks, over the day's change set, that every flow paying a party's creditor comes from that
  party or from a contract naming the payer (a guarantee).
- **Consolidated test** (retires S2.186's placeholder naming EQY, "a bank's group is the bank alone"): at 9c on each
  capital test date S2.186's ratios are computed from the consolidated read (ACC.5, K-90) over the members the group
  record names; a bank with no subsidiary is its own group and reads as before.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a parent failing with its subsidiaries: each ends by its own trigger
(`parent_end_leaves_subsidiary`). E10 — a subsidiary ended: dropped from the fixed point
(`ended_member_dropped_from_control`). E13 — a party with no equity holdings is its own group
(`no_holdings_single_member_group`). E14 — cross-holdings: the fixed point, not arrival order
(`control_least_fixed_point_with_cross_holdings`). E6 — group records are K-37 records, saved
(`group_record_round_trip`); a bank with no subsidiary tests as before (`single_bank_group_unchanged`).

**Extension points**: the group record is read by S3.145 (a parent out
of the float), S3.163 (a desk's parent), S3.209 (group reports), S4.172–S4.174 (takeovers change control).

**Unit tests**: `control_least_fixed_point_with_cross_holdings`; `no_holdings_single_member_group`;
`parent_end_leaves_subsidiary`; `ended_member_dropped_from_control`; `creditor_paid_only_by_debtor_or_guarantor`;
`group_record_round_trip`; `requirement_on_consolidated_group`; `single_bank_group_unchanged`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-31 — ACC.5 and FRM.3: every group's consolidated statement eliminates its intra-group positions
and passes the Accounts family; no party paid a group member's debt except by a contract naming it; applicable from
the first group statement date.

**Budget**: control reads at statement dates for ≈ 20000 parties holding equity in other firms (≈ 50000 holdings) at
≈ 50 phone-ns a holding.
- its share of fin.fixed.close_books: 0 / 0 / 2.5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.51 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H) (statement dates on business days)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +1 MB resident (20000 group records a quarter × 8 quarters × 6 B)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a stored group attribute; an intra-group flag on a contract row; a parent paying a subsidiary's
debt by rule.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-31 registered; S2.186's placeholder naming EQY gone.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.158 — Households choose holdings

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: HH.7 DECISION *(part: banknotes, bills, bonds and shares held directly, by yield, risk, liquidity and trust; funds at S3.188; dwellings and pensions complete it at S6.128)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 5d, 6a); §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100, K-101); §7.13 (phx-val: K-92, K-105); §7.10
(phx-hold: K-65, K-16's apportion)
**Depends on**: S1.196 (the household record's reserve: its columns); S1.448 (households' spending with the buffer
target: the wealth beyond it); S1.452 (households' attention: a lumpy kind added by declaration); S1.357 (the investor
schedule, K-105); S3.148 (the share value rule); S3.134 (the debt value rule); S3.147 (share books); S3.120 (auction
bidders by kind); S2.137 (preference types: risk aversion); S1.350 (attention and surprises); S1.172 (apportionment
among members); S1.240 (banknotes as an account at the issuer, withdrawn from a bank)
**Goal**: a household reviews how it holds its savings on the occasions its attention sets: it enters a class only
when the gain beats the hours of opening it, weights the classes by its own outlooks of return and width, picks
instruments in its reach by its own value against price and its taste, and orders through its bank as broker at limits
from its own values; its members hold what their money bought.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/rules/portfolio.rs` | HH.7: class weights, entry, instrument choice, orders, banknotes withdrawn or paid in |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/points.rs` | decision point `HH.choose_holdings` (lumpy, the named household slot `portfolio`) |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/decl.rs` | the lumpy kind and its attention rule; `HH.holding_classes` (banknotes, bills, bonds, shares, against deposits as the alternative) |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/tests/portfolio.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/hh.rs` | 5c reviews; orders to K-78, K-79 and K-76 at 5d; banknote exchanges at the bank |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/hh.rs` | LC-3-49 |
| `data/<country>/HH.toml` | review and entry hours, instruments in reach (TECHNOLOGY); taste spread (PREFERENCE) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | class weights (Merton, 1969), entry cost (Vissing-Jørgensen, 2002), instrument logit (McFadden, 1974) |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the household (its adults together, E 50), on its attention-drawn review day (the named slot
  `portfolio`, K-43) or woken by a surprise on a class or instrument it holds (REP.35).
- **Inputs** (HH.7): wealth beyond the buffer target (S1.448: liquidity first); its outlooks of each class's return and
  width — the method's registered outlooks of instruments in its reach (K-92) plus its own deviation; deposit rates;
  bill yields as published; its trust, its own record: losses it took on a class widen that class's width (VAL.9); its
  bank's brokerage fee points; its risk aversion γ (its preference type, S2.137).
- **Classes**: weights `w_k = (E[r_k] − r_d) ÷ (γ·σ_k²)` of the wealth beyond the buffer; a class it does not hold is
  entered only when the certainty-equivalent gain exceeds `HH.brokerage_entry_hours` at its value of leisure.
  Banknotes (MON.4) are the class a household holds for its own reasons against the bank it doubts: the amount
  weighed against deposits is withdrawn or paid in at its bank.
- **Instruments**: among the listed shares, bonds and bills in its reach (`HH.holding_reach`, TECHNOLOGY), logit over
  its own value's excess over price with its taste on `HH.holding_taste` (subject: the household; day).
- **Orders**: the investor schedule of its own value (K-105) with the no-trade band its fees give, so it trades rarely;
  posted through its bank as broker (a flow `HH.brokerage_fee` to the bank); bills as bids at auctions (S3.120); sales
  only as `Covered<Qty>`. Cash needs below the buffer sell by the same rule.
- **Who holds** (E 46, E 48): the purchase is paid from the adults' accounts in proportion to what each holds, and each
  member holds the units its money bought (K-16's apportion, residue to the household's reference person, declared).
- Review hours `HH.portfolio_review_hours` from the adults' leisure (§2.21).

**Edge cases**: E3 — no wealth beyond the buffer: no class entered (`no_surplus_no_entry`). E5 — a surprise day waking
many households: spread by attention, never all at once (`surprise_wakes_spread_by_attention`). E6 — open orders
saved, taste draws by address (`portfolio_review_round_trip`). E11 — day zero: holdings and participation from
S3.159's opening; no own loss record yet, absent not zero (`first_review_without_loss_record`). E12 — an instrument
with no
price and no value is not a candidate (`unvalued_instrument_not_candidate`). E14 — members' shares apportioned
exactly (`members_hold_what_they_paid`).

**Extension points**: `HH.holding_classes` is declared data extended by S3.188 (fund kinds) and S6.128 (dwellings,
pensions); `HH.choose_holdings` is converted by S8.111; S5.118 adds gains tax to sale timing.

**Unit tests**: `portfolio_weights_mean_variance_beyond_buffer`; `participation_only_above_entry_cost`;
`no_trade_band_from_fees`; `losses_widen_own_width`; `banknotes_against_doubted_bank`; `members_hold_what_they_paid`;
`no_surplus_no_entry`; `surprise_wakes_spread_by_attention`; `portfolio_review_round_trip`;
`first_review_without_loss_record`; `unvalued_instrument_not_candidate`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-49 — HH.7: every household-held security traces to a `choose_holdings` decision or to the
opening; participation by wealth and age reported; applicable from the first review.

**Budget**: ≈ 35000 reviews a business day (2200000 households at attention-drawn intervals; none on NB, TIME.8) at 240
phone-ns and ≈ 10000 instrument choices at 800.
- its share of fin.fixed.household_reviews: 16 / 0 / 16 core-ms (B / NB / H) until S8.111 replaces it (0 in the finished world, `perf/design.toml`)
- adds 6000 / 0 / 6000 items to fin.book.order_ns (its share of fin.fixed.securities: 0.9 / 0 / 0.9 core-ms (B / NB / H) at 150 phone-ns an order)
- ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (the household reserve: own-loss width per class, 5 × u16); +0 B (named slot
  `portfolio`)

**Guards**: none new (PC-150 covers the orders).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a household holding what it did not choose; a household's order placed by its bank; holdings in
the household's name rather than its members'.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the forms listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed resolution
  within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-49 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.159 — Households' direct holdings at the opening

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: households' direct holdings of shares, bonds and bills by wealth and age)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed
**Depends on**: S3.158 (the holding classes); S1.404 (households and persons drawn); S3.146 (the listed shares
held); S3.142 (the bond lines held)
**Goal**: the opening's households hold shares, bonds and bills directly in the shares by wealth and age the household
surveys in hand report, each held by the adults whose wealth it is.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_hh_holdings.py` | the derivation below |
| `data/profiles/*/profile.toml` | `HH.participation_by_wealth_age`, `HH.direct_share_by_wealth` |

- **Participation**: the share of households holding each class by wealth decile and the reference person's age class

**Status**: planned

| path | purpose |

| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/convert.rs` | CRD.7: the holder's election |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/points.rs` | decision point `CRD.convert` (the holder's decider) |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/convert.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | elections at 5c; conversion events queued for the next 2e |

**Design**:
- **Election** (decider: the holder's own — its investment office, or the household): on each conversion date its
  terms declare (K-43 wakes from the shape) and when woken by a surprise on the issuer, it elects to convert its whole
  free holding of the line when `ratio × v_share > v_bond` at its own values (S3.148, S3.134).
- The election is a record and a queued unit-only event for the next business day's 2e (TIME.7), which S3.161
  applies.

**Edge cases**: E6 — an election before a save converting after it: a K-42 entry (`election_round_trip`). E10 — the
issuer ended before conversion: no election applies; the claim is on its estate (`no_election_after_issuer_end`). E12
— no share value (no close, no comparable): no election (`no_share_value_no_election`).

**Extension points**: `CRD.convert` is converted by S8.157.

**Unit tests**: `convert_when_shares_worth_more`; `election_only_on_terms_dates`; `election_round_trip`;
`no_election_after_issuer_end`; `no_share_value_no_election`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-27 at S3.139 reads conversions, after S3.161).

**Budget**: ≈ 50 elections a business day at ≈ 400 phone-ns.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.02 / 0 / 0.02 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an election outside the terms' dates.

### S3.161 — Conversions into shares

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.7 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 2e); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-65 unit-only events)
**Depends on**: S3.160 (the holder's election); S3.139 (contingent capital's trigger, which converts into shares here
or writes down there); S3.150 (the issue event and cash in lieu); S1.281 (unit-only events at 2e)
**Goal**: each conversion — elected by a convertible's holder, or triggered for every holder of contingent capital —
retires the bond's units and issues the shares to the same holder at 2e, fractions paid as cash in lieu.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/events.rs` | the conversion issue: shares per bond unit by the ratio, cash in lieu |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/conversion.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/eqy.rs` | conversion events applied at 2e |

**Design**:
- **Event**: a unit-only event at 2e: K-65 retires the bond units (the line's issued amount falls, REG.3) and issues
  `⌊n × ratio⌋` shares to the holder (the share's issued amount rises); fractions paid as cash in lieu at the last
  close with the residue to the issuer (S3.150's arithmetic).
- **Contingent capital**: S3.139's trigger names a conversion into shares; this event converts it for every holder of
  record, with no election.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no close for the share: cash in lieu at the terms' fallback, never zero
(`cash_in_lieu_fallback_by_terms`). E14 — an election and a trigger the same day: one conversion of the units held at
2e (`one_conversion_per_unit`). E6 — a triggered conversion pending across a save (`conversion_round_trip`).

### S3.162 — Equity measures

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.10 MEASURE
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 10d); §7.11 (phx-market: K-86 histories); §7.6 (phx-record: K-37 reports)
**Depends on**: S3.147 (closes); S1.326 (mark histories within their horizon); S1.215 (reports and surprises as
records)
**Goal**: returns' tails, autocorrelation, volatility clustering and its rise after falls, and price moves on earnings
surprises are read from the run and reported, never enforced; market capitalisation is a read.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/cap.rs` | market capitalisation as a read: issued units × last close, with the close's age |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/tests/cap.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/eqy.rs` | LC-3-06: the measures from closes and reports |

**Design**:
- **Market capitalisation**: `cap(share) = issued × close`, with the close's age; never stored (Law 4); read by index
  weights (S3.204) and the observer.
- **Measures** (EQY.10) over each listed share's close history (K-86, its horizon) and each report's surprise (VAL.4,
  S3.218): kurtosis of daily returns; lag-1 autocorrelation; autocorrelation of absolute returns; the correlation of
  returns with the next period's volatility; the mean price move against the report's surprise by size of surprise.
  Reported with the run's length; a measure far from real markets is a finding about a mechanism, never tuned (N7).

**Edge cases**: E11 — fewer closes than a measure needs: "not enough history" with the count, never zero
(`short_history_reported_absent`). E13 — a country with no listed share reports none (`no_listed_share_no_measure`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `cap_is_read_with_age`; `kurtosis_and_acf_arithmetic`; `short_history_reported_absent`;
`no_listed_share_no_measure`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-06 — EQY.10: the measures above reported (measured, never enforced); applicable once a share has
60 closes.

**Budget**: read after the run by the check; 0 in the day.
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a stored market capitalisation; a measure fed back into any decision.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-06 registered.

### S3.163 — Dealer desks as parties

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.1 STATE; DLR.12 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 2a, 9b, 9c); §7.3 (phx-core: K-21 legal form); §7.12 (phx-acct: K-88, K-89); §7.14
(phx-risk: K-93)
**Depends on**: S1.180 (the dealer legal form declared); S1.283 (the parent's equity holding in its desk); S1.330 (the
desk's own equity account); S1.332 (fair-value basis of its inventory); S1.338 (declared limits and binding events);
S2.179 (the parent's marginal cost of funds, pricing the intra-group line); S2.200 (licensing, which a desk passes);
S3.106 (repo, a desk's funding as borrower); S3.157 (the parent's consolidated group); S2.122 (insolvency tests)
**Goal**: a dealer is a party of the dealer form — a bank's subsidiary or an independent broker-dealer — with its own
equity, books and inventory at fair value, funded by an intra-group line whose interest runs by day count at its
parent's marginal cost
of funds and by repo, carrying the capital allocation and position limits its bank and supervisor declare, and able to
fail like a firm.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | the dealer form (offices: head of desk; basis fair value; no deposits); the family `DLR.intra_group_line`; limit kinds; covered asset classes as data |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/limits.rs` | the capital allocation and position limits read as K-93 limits |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/desks.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | the line's interest paid at 2a of its dates; limits and group tests at 9c |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-33 (desk part) |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | position limits and capital allocations per desk (DLR.12: POLICY of each bank and of the supervisor, owners named) |

**Design**:
- **Form** (DLR.1, Law 10): the dealer legal form declares a separate party with limited liability, no deposits, a
  fair-value basis for inventory (ACC.2), the head-of-desk office, and how it ends (as a firm, FRM.15). No mechanism
  asks whether a desk is a subsidiary.
- **Equity**: its own equity account (K-88); a subsidiary's shares held by its parent (K-65).
- **Funding**: an intra-group loan line (K-53, revolving with a limit and a drawn part, K-55) from its parent at the
  parent's marginal cost of funds (S2.179's handle), reset on the line's terms, interest read by day count and paid
  at quarter-ends — the
  funding cost of its inventory paid every day it holds it, settled on the line's dates; repo as a borrower at stage 8
  (S3.106); other lenders by their own quotes.
- **Limits** (DLR.12): a capital allocation on risk-weighted inventory (POLICY of the parent, within the desk's
  equity), position limits per instrument and in total (POLICY of the parent and the supervisor) — each a K-93 declared
  limit whose binding is an event the desk sees (Law 6). The parent's requirement is tested on its consolidated group
  (S3.157).
- **Failure**: losses fall on the desk's equity; one that cannot pay its line or its repo is tested by S2.122 and ends
  as a firm does, its parent losing its shares and the line's shortfall (L3).

**Edge cases**: E1 — a parent bank resolved: its desk's shares and line move with the bank's book, K-57
(`desk_follows_parent_resolution`). E3 — a desk with no inventory accrues nothing and quotes by its limits
(`empty_desk_accrues_nothing`). E6 — limits' binding state saved (`limit_state_round_trip`). E10 — a desk ended: its
quotes lapse, K-97 (LC-3-33 finds no quote from an ended desk). E12 — a desk with no declared limit is refused at
assembly, never unlimited (`missing_limit_refused`).

**Extension points**: the dealer form and limit kinds are declared data read by S3.165–S3.181 and S4.117; the head of
desk's decisions are converted by S8.187.

**Unit tests**: `line_interest_by_day_count_at_parent_cost`; `limit_binding_is_event`; `desk_follows_parent_resolution`;
`empty_desk_accrues_nothing`; `limit_state_round_trip`; `missing_limit_refused`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-33 (desk part) — every desk's equity is its own equity account; its funding cost was charged
each day it held inventory; every limit is declared with its owner; applicable from day one.

**Budget**: 50 desks: the lines' interest read by day count and paid at quarter-ends, limit reads fused in quoting
(S3.165), group tests at quarter-ends.
- adds 0 / 0 / 50 items to fin.dues.item_ns
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.0012 MB resident (50 × 24 B: allocation used, line ref, head-of-desk office); ledger
  line 9 (contracts): +50 rows of `DLR.intra_group_line`

**Guards**: assembly refuses a dealer form that may take deposits or a desk with no declared limit.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a desk exempt from its bank's capital and funding (DLR.11); an infinite balance sheet; a desk that
cannot fail.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-33's desk part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.164 — The opening's dealer desks and the pricing service

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: the dealer desks, their parents, equity, inventories and lines)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed
**Depends on**: S3.163 (the dealer form); S1.407 (banks opened); S3.142 (the bond lines a desk's inventory holds)
**Goal**: each bank the primary-dealer lists name opens a desk subsidiary, with its equity, its inventory of the
country's lines and its intra-group line, and each country names its pricing service.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_dlr.py` | the derivation below |
| `data/<country>/gen/DLR.toml` | the desks, their parents and lines; the pricing service (the largest financial-services firm after the curve publisher) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `markets/primary_dealers` → the desks, this step |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `for` gains S3.164 |

**Design**:
- **Desks**: one desk per bank on the country's primary-dealer list (`markets/primary_dealers`) that the opening holds
  (matched by rank of assets where names differ); a country with no list opens one desk for each of its largest banks
  up to the median count of its group.
- **Balance sheet**: each desk's inventory is its parent's share of the lines' dealer holdings (S3.142's sector
  shares); its equity the capital allocation its parent's policy declares for that inventory; the rest is its
  intra-group line.
- **Pricing service**: one financial-services firm per country (deterministic by size; ties by party id).

**Edge cases**: E12 — no primary-dealer list: the group's median count, reported (`no_list_group_median`). E13 — a
country with no bond lines opens no desk (`no_lines_no_desk`).

**Extension points**: none.

`no_lines_no_desk`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-33's desk part at day one.

**Budget**: opening only; the opening's span within its ratchet.
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.2 MB resident (50 desks × 3 kB)

**Guards**: `phx-check data`.

**Not allowed**: a value typed by hand; a desk without a parent's line or its own equity.

### S3.165 — Dealers' quotes

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.4 DECISION *(part: quotes on bonds, bills, paper and shares; the quote form extended to derivatives completes it at S4.117)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 5d); §7.11 (phx-market: K-70, K-79); §7.14 (phx-risk: K-93); §7.13 (phx-val: K-92)
**Depends on**: S3.163 (desks, their limits and funding); S1.316 (the dealer market's quote table); S1.296 (quotes as
standing offers); S1.298 (the shared admission hook over limits); S1.277 (`Covered<Qty>` offer sides); S3.134 (the
debt value
rule); S3.148 (the share value rule); S1.336 (heuristic outlooks of prints; each market's published widths and
turnover); S1.348 (the decision core)
**Goal**: each business day each desk quotes both sides of every instrument it covers from its own state: its own
value, skewed by its inventory, widened by risk and adverse selection, each side sized by its headroom under its limits
and funding, and a side with no headroom not quoted; the bid–offer is the output.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/quote.rs` | DLR.4: reservation, half-width, sizes |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/points.rs` | decision point `DLR.quote` (the head of desk's office) |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | instrument classes with their risk unit (data); the desk's request record window |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/quote.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | quotes posted to K-79 at 5d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-33 (quote part) |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | γ and τ per desk management (PREFERENCE); quote hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the quote form (Ho and Stoll, 1981; Glosten and Milgrom, 1985; Avellaneda and Stoikov, 2008) |

**Design**:
- **Coverage**: the instruments of the desk's declared classes it holds, or that clients asked it about within its
  record's window (its own record of requests, a K-32 windowed column group sized by the requests it received).
- **View** `v`: its own value by the class's value rule at its own outlooks, never a market mid; its heuristic outlook
  of prints where the class declares that method.
- **Reservation** `r = v − q·γ·σ²·τ` for inventory `q` (long inventory lowers both sides); **half-width**
  `δ = ½·γ·σ²·τ + (1/γ)·ln(1 + γ/κ) + a`, with κ its adaptive outlook of how fills respond to its width and `a` its
  outlook of the loss per unit after a client trade (its markouts); γ, τ PREFERENCE of its management; σ² its outlook
  width in the class's risk unit.
- **No record yet** (VAL.10): with no fills or markouts of its own, κ and `a` start from its closest observations — the
  class's published widths and turnover (MKT.15, K-86) at the opening's snapshot (GEN.5) — labelled as such, and learn
  from its own fills thereafter.
- **Sizes**: each side's size is its headroom under the instrument limit, the total limit, the capital allocation and
  its funding, through K-70's admission hook over K-93 (binding raises the desk's event); zero headroom → that side is
  not posted (DLR.4: shrinks or stops). The offer side is `Covered<Qty>`.
- **Output**: two limit orders per (desk, instrument) into K-79's quote table; the width is an output (MKT.19). A
  quote is the desk's standing state (S1.316): it is re-derived only when the instrument's mark, the desk's inventory in
  it or a limit's headroom changed that day. Review hours `DLR.quote_hours` per quote re-derived, from the desk's staff.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a desk with no headroom on either side posts nothing and the market can fail, MKT.10
(`side_stops_at_binding_limit`). E6 — quotes lapse at day end; κ and markout outlooks saved (`quote_state_round_trip`).
E11 — no own fills yet: κ and `a` from the class's published widths and turnover at the snapshot
(`first_quote_without_markouts`). E14 — a limit binding mid-posting: headroom in lot order by the admission hook
(`headroom_in_lot_order`).

**Extension points**: instrument classes with their risk unit are declared data: S3.174 (shares), S4.117
(derivatives), S5.163 (currency pairs) declare theirs; `DLR.quote` is converted by S8.187.

**Unit tests**: `quote_skews_with_inventory`; `quote_widens_with_risk_and_markouts`; `side_stops_at_binding_limit`;
`first_quote_without_markouts`; `headroom_in_lot_order`; `quote_state_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-33 (quote part) — DLR.11: every quote names its desk's decision and lies within its limits; a
desk with no headroom on a side posted nothing on it; applicable from the first quote.

**Budget**: a quote is the desk's standing state (S1.316), re-derived only when the instrument's mark or the desk's
inventory in it changed that day (K-07's change flag): 20000 re-derivations a business day of the 50000 quotes, at 450
phone-ns each (value 150, quote 300); none on NB.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 9 / 0 / 9 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.8 MB resident (50 desks × 16000 requested instruments × 1 B window stamp, plus κ
  and markout per class)

**Guards**: none new (PC-150 holds the sides).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a quote because a market needs one; a spread applied to a mid; a side quoted beyond headroom; a
default κ or markout with no observation behind it.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; the bench at the committed resolution
  within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-33's quote part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.166 — The dealer markets for bonds, bills and paper

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CRD.5 PROCESS *(part: bonds, bills and paper trade after issue in dealer markets; paper sold through dealers by its issuer completes it at S3.167)*; POP.9 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5d, 6a, 6b, 6d, 7); §7.11 (phx-market: K-79); §7.8 (phx-ledger: K-50)
**Depends on**: S1.316 (the dealer market: requests by lot to dealers in reach, the best quote with size left); S3.165
(desks' quotes); S3.158 (households' bill and bond orders through their bank); S3.134 (institutions' debt values);
S2.133 (estates' bonds, bills and paper, whose placeholder this retires); S3.147 (estates' shares, the placeholder's
other part); S1.432 (bills held by their buyers); S1.251 (trades as commitments)
**Goal**: bonds, bills and commercial paper trade after issue in dealer markets: each client's request goes to the
dealers in its reach with its own limit, is taken by lot and filled at the best quote with size left; a request no
quote meets is unfilled, and a market with requests and no trade records its failure.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/markets.rs` | dealer market declarations per debt class (bonds, bills, paper): form, business days, settlement convention, clients' reach per client kind, streams |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/markets.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | requests to K-79 at 6a; matches to K-48/K-50 at 6d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-67 |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | clients' reach counts (TECHNOLOGY); settlement conventions (POLICY of each market's operator) |

**Design**:
- **Markets** (MKT.5 core, MKT.21): one dealer market per debt instrument, meeting business days only; settlement T+n
  by class (SET.2) as K-50 DvP commitments.
- **Requests**: a client's order (its own limit, from K-105 at its own value) to the `DLR.reach.<client kind>` dealers
  of its reach, drawn per request on `DLR.reach_draw` among those covering the instrument; requests taken in an order
  drawn on `DLR.rfq_lot`; each fills at the best quote with size left, ties on `DLR.client_tie_lot`; the unfilled part
  is unfilled (MKT.10), recorded per market.
- **Clients**: institutions (S3.134), households through their bank (S3.158), estates' administrators (retires
  S2.133's placeholder for bonds, bills and paper), the central bank from S3.178.
- **Bills**: bills, which S1.432's buyers held to redemption, now trade after issue here.
- POP.9 completes here: with estates' shares on the books (S3.147) and their bonds, bills and paper sold through
  dealers, the last of S2.133's placeholders is retired.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no dealer covers an instrument: every request unfilled, the failure recorded
(`request_unfilled_without_quote`). E5 — a quarter-end with estates' sales and paper rolls: `dealer.requests` on H
(`requests_linear_in_count`). E6 — DvP commitments across a save, K-50 (`dealer_trade_round_trip`). E7 — request order
by lot per market, subject the market and day (`rfq_order_independent_of_workers`). E10 — a dealer ended: its quotes
lapsed, not in the table (LC-3-67 finds no fill against an ended desk).

**Extension points**: market declarations per class are declared data: S3.167 (issuers' paper), S4.118, S4.119
(swaps, CDS), S5.163 (currency pairs) declare theirs.

**Unit tests**: `client_takes_best_among_its_dealers`; `request_unfilled_without_quote`;
`dealer_market_refuses_nb_meeting`; `requests_linear_in_count`; `dealer_trade_round_trip`;
`rfq_order_independent_of_workers`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-67 — every dealer-market print names its request, its dealer's quote and both parties' own
limits; every unfilled request is recorded with its market; applicable from the first request.

**Budget**: `dealer.requests` 50000 B / 0 / 60000 H, each reading its instrument's run of 4 standing quotes once at
`fin.dealer.quote_ns` 150 phone-ns: 7.5 / 0 / 9 core-ms; commitments 30000 at K-50's post (in K-50's line).
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 7.5 / 0 / 9 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 13 (liens and processes): +0 B (commitments inside K-50's line)

**Guards**: assembly refuses a dealer market with no reach declared for a client kind that posts in it.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a request filled at a price no quote offered; a buyer or seller of last resort.
