underwriter's book); S3.166 (the paper's dealer market)
**Goal**: an issuer rolling commercial paper chooses by its own cost between placing it directly by bilateral quote and
selling it through dealers; paper that does not sell is not issued, and what matures must still be paid.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/paper.rs` | CRD.5: the route (direct placement or dealers) by the issuer's own cost; the sell request at its walk-away yield |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/tests/paper.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/crd.rs` | the issuer's sell request to K-79 at 5d |

**Design**:
- **Route** (decider: the issuer's treasury office, on S3.136's roll): its outlook of the all-in cost by each route —
  direct placement (S3.136's bilateral asks) and a sale through dealers (its outlook of the dealers' bid less their
  fees) — and the cheaper is taken; through dealers, a sell request at its walk-away yield in S3.166's market.
- Unsold paper is not issued (MKT.17), an event; its maturing paper must still be paid (S3.136). With S3.135's primary
  issues and taps and S3.136's placement, CRD.5 is complete.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no dealer bid within the walk-away yield: not issued, event recorded
(`paper_unsold_not_issued`). E14 — a roll and a maturity the same day: the maturity paid from cash, the roll by its
route (`roll_and_maturity_same_day`).

**Extension points**: S8.154 (the route converted as a term of the roll's options).

**Unit tests**: `paper_route_by_own_cost`; `paper_unsold_not_issued`; `roll_and_maturity_same_day`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-67 lists paper sold through dealers).

**Budget**: ≈ 500 paper rolls a business day, ≈ 150 of them through dealers.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; paper sold at any price.

### S3.168 — Interdealer calls

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.7 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a); §7.11 (phx-market: K-76)
**Depends on**: S3.165 (each desk's value, width and inventory); S1.312 (the call auction); S3.163 (limits)
**Goal**: dealers redistribute inventory among themselves in a call per instrument each business day, each posting its
reservation schedule — at each price the inventory at which that price is its reservation, less what it holds — bound
by its limits, with no target position.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/interdealer.rs` | DLR.7: the reservation schedule |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/markets.rs` | the interdealer call per instrument: desks only, business days, stream |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/interdealer.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-68 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the interdealer form (Ho and Stoll, 1983) |

**Design**:
- **Schedule**: at each price point `p` of the instrument's grid, `x(p) = (v − p) ÷ (γ·σ²·τ) − q` — positive to buy,
  negative to sell (a `Covered<Qty>` sell side) — each bound by the desk's limits through K-70's admission hook; the
  same `v, γ, σ², τ` as its quote (S3.165).
- **Call**: one K-76 call per instrument with at least two desks posting, at 6a before client requests (the stage's
  declared order), rationed pro rata by largest remainder, ties on `DLR.interdealer_lot`; its price is a print of the
  interdealer market, read by fixings (S3.169).

**Edge cases**: E2 — one desk only: no call (`single_desk_no_call`). E7 — calls per instrument on the pool, joined in
instrument order (`calls_independent_of_workers`). E14 — a desk's call fill and its client fills the same day draw on
one headroom, the call first by the stage order (`call_before_client_fills`).

**Extension points**: the schedule is converted by S8.187.

**Unit tests**: `interdealer_order_from_reservation_schedule`; `single_desk_no_call`; `schedule_bound_by_limits`;
`calls_independent_of_workers`; `call_before_client_fills`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-68 — every interdealer trade names both desks' schedules at the print; no desk traded beyond its
limits; applicable from the first call.

**Budget**: 3000 interdealer calls a business day (4000 H) over 40000 schedule points (53000 H): points at
`fin.call.order_ns` 150 phone-ns (6 / 0 / 8 core-ms) plus calls at `fin.call.call_us` 3 µs (9 / 0 / 12); the schedule
reuses S3.165's standing view (no re-valuation), and does not ride the dealer quote.
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 15 / 0 / 20 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a target position; a call with non-dealer participants.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-68 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.169 — Fixings of dealer markets

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.7 PROCESS *(part: the dealer markets' fixings; the curve read from them completes it at S3.170)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 6b); §7.11 (phx-market: K-86 fixings)
**Depends on**: S1.326 (fixings by (publisher, method); the day's prints a method names); S3.166 (client prints);
S3.168 (interdealer prints)
**Goal**: a pricing service fixes each dealer-market instrument that traded by its declared method — the
volume-weighted mean of the day's client and interdealer prices — which is the instrument's mark; with no trade there
is no fixing, and the last shows its age.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/fixing.rs` | the pricing service's declared method (volume-weighted mean over client and interdealer prints), applied by K-86 at 6b |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | the pricing service's publisher facet; the fixing record kind and horizon; the mark rule of dealer markets |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/fixing.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-69 |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | the service's method (POLICY of the service) |

**Design**:
- **Fixing** (MKT.12 done, MKT.20 core): the service — a firm with the publisher facet, named by S3.164 —
  fixes at 6b each instrument whose dealer market printed: `Σ price·qty ÷ Σ qty` over the day's client and interdealer
  prints (K-86's exact sums); with no print, no fixing (Law 3), and the last fixing shows its age (Law 8). The fixing
  is a K-86 fixing labelled as such, public from the next day.
- **Mark**: a dealer market's declared mark is its fixing (MKT.12); holders marking to it (ACC.2) read it.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no trade: no fixing (`fixing_absent_without_trade`). E6 — fixings are records, saved
(`fixing_round_trip`). E11 — day zero: the opening's latest fixings (`first_fixing_day_reads_snapshot`).

**Extension points**: fixing methods are declared data: S3.203 (benchmarks, another publisher and method), S4.106
(clearing houses' settlement prices), S5.163 (currency fixings).

**Unit tests**: `fixing_vwap_over_client_and_interdealer`; `fixing_absent_without_trade`; `fixing_round_trip`;
`first_fixing_day_reads_snapshot`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-69 — every fixing traces to the day's prints of its market; applicable from the first fixing.

**Budget**: ≈ 5000 fixings a business day at ≈ 200 phone-ns (K-86's mark).
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0 MB (fixings inside K-86's `marks.horizon` rows)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fixing without a trade; a valuation entering a fixing.

### S3.171 — Primary dealers' agreements and bids

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOV.5 DECISION *(part: the agreement and each primary dealer's own bid; the treasury's membership review completes it at S3.172)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a); §7.9 (phx-contract: K-53); §7.11 (phx-market: K-76)
**Depends on**: S3.121 (the treasury's auctions); S3.120 (bidding at auctions by kind); S3.163 (desks and limits);
S3.165 (the desk's value and width); S1.357 (the investor schedule, K-105); S1.257 (the agreement as a contract)
**Goal**: a primary-dealer agreement is a contract between the treasury and a desk — privileges declared as data in
exchange for an undertaking to submit a bid in every auction; each bid's size and price are the desk's own, bound by
its limits and inventory, so a desk at its limit bids small or low, or records a bid of zero size.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | the family `DLR.primary_dealer` (treasury, desk; privileges; undertaking) |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/pd_bid.rs` | SOV.5: the desk's bid |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/pd_bid.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-34 |

**Design**:
- **Agreement**: a K-53 row (treasury, desk) with the privileges its terms list (access to the treasury's buybacks and
  switches, S3.125) and the undertaking to bid.
- **Bid** (decider: the head of desk): at each auction the desk posts its investor schedule (K-105) at its own value of
  the line (S3.165's view), bound by its limits and inventory through the admission hook; a desk with no headroom
  records a bid of zero size — the undertaking met, nothing taken.
- The agreements are contracts from here: a bank is a primary dealer only under one.

**Edge cases**: E2 — every primary dealer at its limit: the auction clears on others' bids or fails, SOV.6
(`pd_bid_bounded_by_limits`). E10 — a desk ended: its agreement closes with it (`agreement_ends_with_desk`). E11 —
day zero: the opening's agreements are S3.173's (`agreements_read_at_day_zero`).

**Extension points**: `DLR.primary_dealer` is read by S3.172; the bid is converted by S8.190.

**Unit tests**: `pd_bid_bounded_by_limits`; `zero_headroom_zero_size_bid_recorded`; `agreement_ends_with_desk`;
`agreements_read_at_day_zero`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-34 — SOV.5: every primary dealer's bid is recorded in every auction, at size and price of its
own; a desk with no headroom records a bid of zero size; applicable from the first auction.

**Budget**: ≈ 2 auctions a business day × ≈ 20 primary dealers.

### S3.174 — Market makers on share books

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: EQY.6 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 5d, 6a); §7.11 (phx-market: K-78)
**Depends on**: S3.147 (share books); S3.165 (the quote form, declared here for the share class); S1.277 (covered
offer sides)
**Goal**: a desk covering listed shares posts its quote as two limit orders on each covered share's continuous book,
its offer side covered by units held or borrowed, so listed shares trade on books with market makers as well as
investors.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | the share class declared among quotable classes (risk unit: shares) |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/market_maker.rs` | logic-level tests |

- S3.165's quote for a share — view from S3.148's value rule at the desk's outlooks, reservation and width as there —
  is posted as a bid and an offer on the share's book, each the size its headroom allows; the offer side is
  `Covered<Qty>` of units held or borrowed (S3.175). Orders rest in price–time priority, and those unfilled at the close

### S3.175 — Securities lending

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.2 STATE; DLR.5 DECISION; EQY.9 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 2a, 5c, 5d, 6a, 7); §7.9 (phx-contract: K-53, K-55 event legs); §7.11 (phx-market: K-70
posted market); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-65, K-63)
**Depends on**: S1.257 (the loan family); S1.263 (fee accrual and event-waiting legs for manufactured payments);
S1.281 (instrument events paid to the holder of record, which the manufactured leg follows); S1.277 (liens on
collateral; `Covered<Qty>` from borrowed units); S1.296 (lendable units as posted offers); S3.103 (haircuts per
security and borrower); S3.149 (shorts covered only by borrowed units); S3.163 (desks, the first borrowers)
**Goal**: a securities loan passes title to the borrower against collateral worth more than the security, for a fee
that rises as the security's lendable supply is used up; the economics stay with the lender through manufactured
payments; lenders lend what they hold within their mandates, borrowers borrow to deliver a short or cover a fail, and a
short seller pays for its borrow.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | the family `DLR.sec_loan` (lender, borrower; security, units, collateral kind, haircut, fee, recall notice); reasons `DLR.lending_fee`, `DLR.manufactured`; the lending market per security |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/lend.rs` | DLR.5: availability and fee point |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/borrow.rs` | DLR.5: the borrower's choice among lenders in reach |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/points.rs` | decision points `DLR.lend`, `DLR.borrow` |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/lending.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | offers at 5d; the lending market at 6a; loans opened at 7 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-70 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the fee form (D'Avolio, 2002; Duffie, Gârleanu and Pedersen, 2002); the borrower's search (Stigler, 1961) |

**Design**:
- **Lenders** (decider: the lender's investment office): on their review (K-43), holders whose mandate or policy allows
  lending (banks; funds from S3.182; insurers from S4.137) post the free units they will lend (K-70 offers, a posted
  market per security, MKT.6) at a fee point `fee = f_0·(1 + u ÷ (1 − u))^η`, with `f_0` its reservation from its
  outlooks of the recall it may need and the spread on reinvested collateral, `u` its utilisation (lent ÷ lendable),
  η PREFERENCE of its management; the collateral it accepts and the haircut are its own (S3.103's rule).
- **Borrowers**: a desk or client that wants to sell beyond its free units (a short) or failed to deliver (SET.3)
  takes the cheapest lender in its reach (a declared count, TECHNOLOGY); capacity binds by lot on `DLR.borrow_lot`.
- **Loan** (DLR.2): at settlement the units move lender → borrower (title passes: the borrower holds them, free for its
  covered offers from the next day's 5d); collateral moves the other way — cash, or securities under a lien to the
  lender (K-63) at the haircut; the fee is read by day count (K-55) and paid on the loan's monthly dates; every
  coupon or dividend
  the lent units bear is owed to the lender as a manufactured payment on the event's payment day (an event leg of the
  loan, woken by K-65's event on the security).
- **Squeeze** (EQY.9): nothing caps the fee; as lendable supply is used up `u → 1` and the fee rises, and recalls
  (S3.176) force buy-ins — the squeeze is a consequence. With S3.149's covered sides, EQY.9 is complete.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no lendable units: no borrow, the short not posted (`no_lendable_no_borrow`). E6 — open loans,
liens and accruals live across a save (`sec_loan_round_trip`). E10 — the security's issuer ending while lent: its
cessation resolves the borrower's holding and the return obligation becomes the cessation's proceeds owed to the
lender, REG.12 (`lent_security_ceases`). E14 — a dividend on lent units: holder paid and the manufactured leg owed the
same day (`manufactured_payment_follows_event`).

**Extension points**: the lending market and `DLR.sec_loan` are read by S3.179 (brokers' borrowed securities), S3.191
(hedge funds' shorts), S4.117 (derivative hedges); `DLR.lend` is converted by S8.188 and `DLR.borrow` by S8.191.

**Unit tests**: `lending_fee_rises_with_utilisation`; `borrower_takes_cheapest_in_reach`;
`manufactured_payment_follows_event`; `no_lendable_no_borrow`; `lent_security_ceases`; `sec_loan_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-70 — every short position traces to a securities loan naming its lender; every lent security's
distributions were manufactured to its lender; applicable from the first loan.

### S3.176 — Recall and buy-in

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.9 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 2c, 5c, 9c); §7.7 (phx-agenda: K-45); §7.11 (phx-market: K-70, K-78, K-79)
**Depends on**: S3.175 (loans and their collateral); S1.237 (recall notices due the next business day); S3.147 and
S3.166 (the markets a buy-in buys in); S3.106 (repo, where reinvested cash collateral goes); S1.345 (a borrower's
shortfall as a claim)
**Goal**: a lender recalls when selling or voting the units is worth more to it than the fee still to earn; a borrower
that cannot return the security by the next business day is bought in at its cost while the lender keeps the
collateral; cash collateral the lender reinvests is its own position with its own risk.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/recall.rs` | the lender's recall decision |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/buyin.rs` | DLR.9: buy-in orders over the declared horizon |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/recall.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | recall notices at 9c (due next business day); returns at 2c; buy-in orders at 5d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-35 |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | recall notice, buy-in horizon and urgency (POLICY of each market) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the recall form (Aggarwal, Saffi and Sturgess, 2015) |

**Design**:
- **Recall** (decider: the lender's investment office), on its review and when woken by a vote's record day or its own
  sell decision: recall when `max(value of selling, value of voting) > fee still to earn` over the loan's expected
  remaining life; a recall is a K-45 notice issued at 9c, due at the next business day's 2c (TIME.7).
- **Return**: at 2c the borrower returns the units if it holds them free (units → lender, collateral → borrower, liens
  released); otherwise the loan is in default of return.
- **Buy-in** (DLR.9): from that day's 5c the lender posts buy orders for the units — limited at its outlook of the offer
  plus its declared urgency concession, each day's slice the remainder over the days left of the market's buy-in
  horizon — charged to the borrower from the collateral it keeps; a shortfall is a claim on the borrower (K-98 if it
  ends), an excess returned.
- **Reinvested cash collateral**: the lender's placement of cash collateral (repo, S3.106; money funds, S3.187) is its
  own position; a loss on it is the lender's, and the collateral is still owed back.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no offers: the buy-in stays offered each day, never taken at a valuation
(`buyin_remainder_offered_until_filled`). E6 — a recall issued before a save, due after it: a live K-45 message
(`recall_round_trip`). E10 — the borrower ended: collateral kept, the shortfall claimed on its estate
(`borrower_estate_claimed`). E14 — a recall and a manufactured payment the same day: both, the payment first by the
stage order (`recall_and_manufactured_same_day`).

**Extension points**: the recall is converted by S8.188.

**Unit tests**: `recall_when_sale_or_vote_worth_more_than_fee`; `recall_due_next_business_day`;
`buy_in_charged_to_borrower`; `buyin_remainder_offered_until_filled`; `reinvestment_loss_is_lenders`;
`recall_round_trip`; `borrower_estate_claimed`; `recall_and_manufactured_same_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-35 — DLR.9: every recall was returned or bought in, and every buy-in's cost landed on its
borrower; applicable from the first recall.

**Budget**: ≈ 300 recalls and ≈ 50 buy-ins a business day.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- adds 300 / 0 / 300 items to fin.book.order_ns (its share of fin.fixed.securities: 0.045 / 0 / 0.045 core-ms (B / NB / H) at 150 phone-ns an order)
- ledger: +0 B (recalls are K-45 messages)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a recall paid in the stage it is issued; a buy-in "at any price"; collateral released before the
units return or the buy-in settles.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-35 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.177 — Securities' depth in banks' liquid assets

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BFL.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9b); §7.11 (phx-market: K-86 market measures)
**Depends on**: S2.180 (the liquidity buffer and liquid assets: reserves, banknotes, bills, eligible assets, saleable
loans); S1.326 (each market's published depth and turnover, MKT.15); S3.147 and S3.166 (the markets securities trade
in); S3.103 (repo haircuts); S3.112 (the central bank's collateral haircuts)
**Goal**: a bank's liquid assets include every security it can sell or pledge, each counted at what its market's
published depth lets it sell within its horizon and at the haircut a lender or the central bank would apply to it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/liquid.rs` | BFL.3: a security's liquid value from its market's depth and its haircut |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/decl.rs` | securities classes added to the liquid-asset declaration |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/tests/liquid.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/bfl.rs` | LC-3-71 |

**Design**:
- For each security a bank holds (its K-65 holdings), liquid value = `max(sale value, pledge value)`: sale value =
  `min(units, depth_h) × mark`, `depth_h` the units its market's published depth and turnover (K-86, MKT.15) say it can
  sell over the bank's liquidity horizon (PREFERENCE of its management); pledge value = `units × mark × (1 − haircut)`
  at the best haircut it can reach (S3.103's repo haircuts, S3.112's central-bank schedule). Each figure carries its
  mark's age; an absent mark or depth gives no sale value.
- S2.180's buffer rule reads the sum as its liquid assets; nothing else changes.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a market with no depth published: pledge value only (`no_depth_pledge_only`). E12 — no mark:
neither value (`no_mark_no_liquidity`). E13 — a bank with no securities: S2.180's sum alone
(`no_securities_sum_unchanged`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `liquid_value_from_depth_and_haircut`; `no_depth_pledge_only`; `no_mark_no_liquidity`;
`no_securities_sum_unchanged`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-71 — every bank's liquid-asset figure names each security's depth, mark age and haircut it read;
applicable from the first bank review.

**Budget**: 35 banks × ≈ 200 security holdings on review days.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a liquidity weight table in place of depth and haircut; an absent mark read as zero or as par.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-71 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.178 — The central bank's asset purchases

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: CB.5 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a); §7.11 (phx-market: K-79, K-78); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-65)
**Depends on**: S3.111 (the committee's rate decision and its declared rule); S3.116 (the financing regime: whether the
own sovereign's debt is eligible); S3.166 (the dealer markets its orders go to); S3.147 (share books, for a programme
that declares shares); S1.357 (the investor schedule, K-105); S3.117 (the central bank's income, into which its
holdings' income flows); S1.281 (maturities of held bonds as events)
**Goal**: the central bank chooses asset purchases and sales — their size, the classes and whether to reinvest
maturities — for its policy reasons, and executes them by posting limit orders in secondary markets like any
participant.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/rules/purchases.rs` | CB.5: the programme decision and each day's orders |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/src/points.rs` | decision point `CB.purchase_programme` (the committee's office) |
| `crates/systems/sys-cb/tests/purchases.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/cb.rs` | the programme's daily slice posted to K-79 (and K-78) at 5d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/cb.rs` | LC-3-72 |
| `data/<country>/CB.toml` | the classes a programme may hold; its announcement rule (POLICY of the central bank) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the programme form (purchases when the rate is at the committee's declared floor and its outlook of inflation is below target; Bernanke and Reinhart, 2004) |

**Design**:
- **Programme** (decider: the committee's office, at its meetings): from its mandate and its own outlooks (inflation,
  activity, the curve's term premium as published), the committee's declared rule decides a programme — a size over a
  period, eligible classes, whether maturities are reinvested — or its unwinding; announced as a public event (OBS.3)
  and a dated POLICY record (VAL.6's announcement heuristic reads it).
- **Execution**: each business day of the programme the central bank posts the day's slice (remaining size over days
  left) as client requests in the dealer markets of eligible instruments (S3.166), each limited at its own value of the
  instrument (its outlook of the curve, through K-105) — never at market; unfilled slices carry to the next day; sales
  the same way.
- **Reinvestment**: when a held instrument matures (K-65), its proceeds are added to the programme's remaining size if
  the committee chose to reinvest. The holdings sit on its balance sheet (CB.1) and their income enters its lines
  (S3.117).

**Edge cases**: E2 — no dealer quotes: the slice is unfilled and carried, never forced (`unfilled_slice_carries`). E6 —
a programme across a save: size remaining and days left are saved columns (`programme_round_trip`). E11 — day zero:
the opening's holdings and any announced programme (`opening_programme_from_snapshot`). E13 — a central bank that
declares no programme classes posts nothing (`no_classes_no_orders`).

**Extension points**: `CB.purchase_programme` is converted by S8.174.

**Unit tests**: `slice_is_remainder_over_days_left`; `unfilled_slice_carries`; `reinvest_adds_maturities`;
`orders_limited_at_own_value`; `programme_round_trip`; `opening_programme_from_snapshot`; `no_classes_no_orders`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-72 — every central-bank purchase or sale traces to a programme decision and a limit of its own;
applicable from the first programme.

**Budget**: ≈ 50 requests a business day during a programme.
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +72 B resident (3 central banks × 24 B: size remaining, days left, reinvest flag)

**Guards**: none new (PC-150 holds its limits).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a purchase at market; a purchase sized by an auction's result (CB.13).

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-72 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.179 — Prime brokerage: accounts, margin and calls

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.3 STATE; DLR.6 DECISION; DLR.11 FORBID
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 9a, 9c, 9e, 2c); §7.14 (phx-risk: K-94 netting sets); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-63 liens);
§7.7 (phx-agenda: K-45 calls)
**Depends on**: S1.340 (netting sets per (broker, client), posted collateral as liens, calls as messages due the next
business day); S3.175 (borrowed securities); S1.257 (the cash loan line); S1.326 (market measures for the
concentration add-on); S3.163 (brokers are desks or their parents, with limits); S3.165 (the desk-side forbids this
completes)
**Goal**: a prime broker holds its client's assets under a lien, lends it cash and securities against them, sets a
margin requirement on the whole account from its own view of the portfolio, the market and the client, calls for more
when the requirement rises above the account's equity, and ends a relationship that no longer pays; margin is never
only a number and never nets across clients.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/decl.rs` | the PB agreement family; its netting set kind (per (broker, client)); reasons `DLR.pb_fee`, `DLR.margin` |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/margin.rs` | DLR.6: the requirement over the broker's scenarios |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/relationship.rs` | ending a relationship on the broker's review |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/margin.rs` | logic-level tests, the compile-fail one included |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | the 9c test-and-call handler (applied at 9e, due next business day's 2c) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-33 (margin part) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc54.rs` | PC-54: `MarginRequirement` built only from one (broker, client) account |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | brokers' scenarios and add-on (POLICY of each broker); PB review hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the margin form (Brunnermeier and Pedersen, 2009); the relationship form (Mitchell, Pedersen and Pulvino, 2007) |

**Design**:
- **Account** (DLR.3): a PB agreement (K-53) opens one K-94 netting set per (broker, client): the client's assets held
  under a lien to the broker (K-63), its cash loan (a loan line) and its borrowed securities (S3.175 loans with the
  broker as lender or intermediary).
- **Requirement** (DLR.6; decider: the broker's risk office), at 9c each business day: the largest loss of the
  account's positions over the broker's declared scenarios, each scenario's moves scaled by the broker's own outlook
  widths per class (so it changes as its view changes), plus a concentration add-on — position against the market's
  published turnover (MKT.15) — and the client's own record with the broker (calls met late widen it, declared).
- **Call**: test and call are one 9c handler: account equity at 9a's marks below the requirement issues a K-45 call for
  the difference, applied at 9e, due at the next business day's 2c (TIME.7); paid from the client's cash or failed
  (S3.180 closes out).
- **Relationship**: on its review the broker ends a relationship whose fees no longer cover its expected cost of risk
  (the requirement's shortfall probability at its outlook), with the declared notice.
- **Forbids** (DLR.11), with S3.163–S3.165: per-account construction (PC-54); every desk with its own equity, funding
  and limits (S3.163); quotes only from its state and headroom (S3.165); inventory at fair value, so its profit carries
  the inventory's gains and losses (S3.163's basis); shorts only on borrows (S3.149).
- Raising requirements as widths grow is how margin can spiral; nothing scripts it.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a crash day: every account's requirement rises, calls O(accounts) (`calls_linear_in_accounts`).
E5 — the crash day's margin work at `fin.valuation.margin_us` over every account (`margin_cost_per_account`). E6 — an
open call across a save: a live K-45 message (`margin_call_round_trip`). E10 — a client ended: its account closes into
its estate, the broker's claim ranking by its lien (`client_estate_claim_by_lien`). E13 — a client with no positions:
no requirement (`no_positions_no_requirement`).

**Extension points**: the netting-set kind is declared data read by S3.180 (close-out), S3.191 (hedge funds' leverage),
S4.123 (derivatives in PB accounts); `DLR.pb_margin` and the relationship review are converted by S8.189.

**Unit tests**: `margin_scenarios_scale_with_widths`; `margin_per_account_no_netting` (compile-fail);
`call_due_next_business_day`; `relationship_ends_when_fees_short`; `calls_linear_in_accounts`;
`margin_cost_per_account`; `margin_call_round_trip`; `client_estate_claim_by_lien`; `no_positions_no_requirement`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-33 (margin part) — DLR.11: no margin figure without its account's positions and scenarios; no
requirement over two clients; applicable from the first account.

**Budget**: ≈ 2000 PB accounts (of `valuation.margin_accounts` 10000) on business days at `fin.valuation.margin_us`;
calls ≈ 100 a day.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 6 / 0 / 6 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.crash_day (event): 1 core-ms (2000 calls issued at 500 phone-ns; requirements are the day's own
  line); joins H and B′
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.05 MB resident (2000 PB agreement rows × 24.6 B); netting sets in K-94's line (line 16)

**Guards**: PC-54 (above).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a margin that is only a number; netting across clients; a call paid in the stage it is issued.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests, the compile-fail one included; fast checks pass; PC-54 registered; the forms listed; the
  bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-33 complete (all four parts) registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.180 — Close-out of an unmet margin call

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: DLR.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 2c, 5c, 5d, 6a); §7.14 (phx-risk: K-94); §7.11 (phx-market: K-78, K-79); §7.15 (phx-end:
K-98)
**Depends on**: S3.179 (accounts, calls due at 2c); S3.147 and S3.166 (the markets positions are sold into); S3.176
(buying back shorts, the same slicing); S1.345 (a client's shortfall as a claim)
**Goal**: a client that cannot meet a margin call by the next business day is closed out: its broker sells its
positions and buys back its shorts into markets that must clear, a slice each day over its declared horizon at its own
limits, until everything is sold; the proceeds repay the broker and any shortfall is the broker's loss and its claim on
the client.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/closeout.rs` | DLR.8: the day's slice and its limits |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/closeout.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/dlr.rs` | a failed call at 2c opens the close-out; slices posted at 5d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/dlr.rs` | LC-3-08 |
| `data/<country>/DLR.toml` | close-out horizons and urgency concessions (POLICY of each broker) |

**Design**:
- **Trigger**: a call unpaid at 2c (S3.179) fails, visibly (SET.3); the account is in close-out from that day.
- **Slices** (decider: the broker's risk office): each day at 5c, for each position, the slice = remainder ÷ days left
  of the declared horizon; sells limited at its outlook of the bid less its urgency concession, short-cover buys at its
  outlook of the offer plus the concession; posted as `Continuous` orders on books or requests in dealer markets. Past
  the horizon the whole remainder is each day's slice at the same limits, until sold — positions are sold into markets,
  never taken at a valuation.
- **Proceeds**: each fill repays the client's cash loan and borrowed securities; on the last sale the account settles:
  an excess returns to the client, a shortfall is the broker's loss and its claim on the client — a K-98 claim if the
  client ends. This is L2's margin-call door: the sales' prints move marks, which widen other accounts' requirements.

**Edge cases**: E1 — many accounts closing out on one day: orders O(positions) (`closeout_orders_linear`). E2 — no
bids: the remainder stays offered each day (`closeout_remainder_offered_until_sold`). E6 — a close-out spanning a
save: remainder and days left saved (`closeout_round_trip`). E10 — the client ending mid close-out: its estate is the
counterparty, the broker's lien stands (`closeout_continues_against_estate`).

**Extension points**: the close-out slice is converted by S8.189.

**Unit tests**: `closeout_slices_over_horizon`; `closeout_remainder_offered_until_sold`; `shortfall_is_brokers_claim`;
`excess_returned_on_last_sale`; `closeout_orders_linear`; `closeout_round_trip`;
`closeout_continues_against_estate`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-08 — a margin call's chain (call, failure, close-out orders, sales, prints, others' requirements)
is traceable in events from the first call to the last sale; not applicable until the run has an unmet call.

**Budget**: ≈ 20 accounts in close-out on a stress day × ≈ 30 positions ≈ 600 orders.
- adds 600 / 0 / 600 items to fin.book.order_ns (its share of fin.fixed.securities: 0.09 / 0 / 0.09 core-ms (B / NB / H) at 150 phone-ns an order)
- on fin.calendar.crash_day (event): 0.1 core-ms (slices start at D+1 on each broker's schedule); joins H and B′
- ledger: +0 B (remainder and days left are K-94's netting-set columns)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a close-out order "at any price"; positions taken by the broker at a valuation; a shortfall
absorbed without a claim.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-08 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.182 — Fund kinds, mandates and managers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.1 STATE; FND.2 STATE; FND.13 PRIMITIVE; REG.7 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core: K-21 legal forms); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-64 fund-unit family); §7.14 (phx-risk: K-93
mandate limits); §7.9 (phx-contract: K-53 management contracts)
**Depends on**: S1.180 (legal forms and kinds as data); S1.279 (fund units as an instrument family); S1.280 (unit
holders by fund); S1.338 (mandate limits as declared limits); S1.332 (fair-value basis); S1.330 (the fund's own equity
and residue line); S1.257 (the management contract); S1.342 (fund estates)
**Goal**: a fund is a named party whose liabilities are its units, held by named investors; its assets are held at fair
value; its mandate — what it may hold, how much leverage, how it deals and redeems — is declared data; its manager is a
separate firm paid the fee its terms state; money, open-ended, exchange-traded, hedge, private-equity and private-credit
funds differ only in declared data.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the fund legal form; the family `FND.units` (K-64: redeemable or listed, dealing frequency, notice, settlement, gates, stable-price band, commitment and life); the family `FND.management`; mandate limits as K-93 limit kinds |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/fee.rs` | the management fee's accrual on the fund's value |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/kinds.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-73 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc151.rs` | PC-151: no `sys-fnd` rule matches on a fund kind's identity |
| `data/<country>/FND.toml` | fund kinds' mandates and redemption terms (FND.13: declared data); fund regulation (POLICY of the supervisor) |

**Design**:
- **Party** (FND.1): the fund legal form declares a separate party with limited liability that ends by L3's trigger
  (S3.193), a fair-value basis for every holding (ACC.2), offices (its portfolio managers — employees of the manager,
  PTY.16), and no deposits.
- **Units** (REG.7): an instrument family whose terms say whether units are redeemable at the fund (dealing
  frequency, notice, settlement, gates, a stable-price band where promised) or listed on a book, and for private-equity
  and private-credit funds the committed capital and the fund's life; holders are named investors (K-65).
- **Kinds** (FND.2, Law 10): money, open-ended, exchange-traded, hedge, private-equity, private-credit — each a set of
  declared mandate and unit terms; no mechanism reads the kind's name (PC-151).
- **Mandate** (FND.13): eligible classes (and, from S3.213, minimum ratings), concentration and leverage limits (K-93
  declared limits, the supervisor's regulation as POLICY), lending permitted (S3.175).
- **Manager**: a firm, the counterparty of an `FND.management` contract whose fee (a share of the fund's value a year,
  read by day count over the values since the last payment) is paid at quarter-ends; the fee point is the manager's,
  reviewed by S1.450's
  price review.

**Edge cases**: E3 — a fund with no holdings: its value is its cash, nothing divides by zero units, a fund with no
units ends (S3.193) (`empty_fund_value_is_cash`). E10 — a manager ending: the management contract passes to its estate
or a successor by the terms (`manager_end_passes_contract`). E12 — a fund kind missing a term is refused at assembly
(`missing_term_refused`). E13 — a country declaring no hedge funds has none (`undeclared_kind_absent`).

**Extension points**: fund kinds and `FND.units` terms are declared data read by S3.184–S3.202, S4.123 (derivative
mandates), S4.150 (members' DC funds).

**Unit tests**: `fund_kind_is_data_no_branch`; `fee_accrues_on_value`; `mandate_limit_binding_is_event`;
`empty_fund_value_is_cash`; `manager_end_passes_contract`; `missing_term_refused`; `undeclared_kind_absent`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-73 — every fund's units are held by named investors and every holding sits within its mandate or
its breach is an event; every manager's fee traces to its contract; applicable from day one.

**Budget**: 4500 funds' fees read by day count and paid at quarter-ends; mandate checks inside managers' orders.
- adds 0 / 0 / 4500 items to fin.dues.item_ns
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.3 MB resident (4500 funds × 64 B: mandate refs, manager contract ref, dealing
  terms ref, residue line)
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.11 MB resident (4500 `FND.management` rows × 24.6 B)

**Guards**: PC-151 (above); assembly refuses a fund form that may take deposits.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fund whose units have no named holder; a manager that is the fund; a kind branch.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; PC-151 registered; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-73 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.183 — The opening's funds, their holdings and their investors

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: funds by kind with managers, holdings and unit holders)*; GEN.5 STATE *(part: funds' latest published values)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed
**Depends on**: S3.182 (fund kinds and units); S3.146 (listed shares a fund holds); S3.142 (bond lines a fund holds);
S3.159 (households' direct holdings, beside which their fund units are drawn)
**Goal**: the opening's funds of each kind, their managers, their holdings and their unit holders come from the fund and
non-bank statistics in hand, each with its latest published value.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_fnd.py` | the derivation below |
| `data/profiles/*/profile.toml` | `FND.assets_to_gdp`, `FND.kind_shares`, `FND.investor_shares` |
| `data/<country>/gen/FND.toml` | funds by kind, managers (financial-services firms by size), holdings and unit holders |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `markets/GFDD.DI.07`, `markets/institutional_investors`, `markets/fsb_nbfi` → the primitives, this step (`GEN.dist.funds_pensions_insurance`'s fund part) |
| `data/sources/raw/manifest.json` | `for` gains S3.183 |

**Design**:
- **Size**: funds' assets to GDP (`markets/GFDD.DI.07`) split by kind (`markets/fsb_nbfi`: money, hedge, other
  investment funds; `markets/institutional_investors` for open-ended by class), spread over a count of funds per kind
  by Zipf's law in size (the declared procedure).
- **Holdings**: each fund's assets by its mandate's classes out of the listed shares' floats and the lines' unallocated
  shares (S3.146, S3.142), never beyond them.
- **Investors**: units held by households (by wealth and age, the surveys of S3.159) and institutions in the
  investor shares reported; the latest published value is assets over units (a present value, GEN.5).

**Edge cases**: E12 — a kind the sources do not report is not opened, and reported (`unreported_kind_not_opened`).
E13 — a country with no funds of a kind opens none (`no_funds_of_kind`). E11 — day one's dealing reads these values
(LC-3-09).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `fund_assets_to_gdp`, `holdings_within_floats`, `units_times_value_equals_assets`,
`unreported_kind_not_opened`, `no_funds_of_kind`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-09 at day one.

- ledger line 11 (holdings and lots): +0 B (inside S1.280's holdings, count 350000 fund unit holdings: 330000
  households', a tenth of households holding 1.5 funds each by the surveys of S3.159, and 20000 institutions')

### S3.184 — Net asset value

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.5 PROCESS; FND.9 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 9a, 9b, 9d); §7.2 (phx-exec: K-14 declared sweep); §7.5 (phx-pop: K-35 per-day value);
§7.7 (phx-agenda: K-46 party-position series); §7.17 (phx-audit: K-103)
**Depends on**: S3.182 (funds, units, fee accruals); S1.171 (the declared value sweep over funds' positions); S1.211
(the day's value per fund); S1.326 (marks); S1.335 (named valuers' labelled valuations); S1.336 (each fund's value as a
public series); S1.239 (party-position series watched by thresholds); S1.353 (the FND.9 audit family)
**Goal**: each fund's net asset value — assets at formed prices or at a named valuer's labelled valuation, less
liabilities, over units — is computed every business day after the day's marks, rounded by its unit price's convention
with the residue on the fund, and published; a stale print gives a stale value.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/nav.rs` | FND.5: the value per unit and its rounding |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/audit.rs` | the FND.9 family |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the value sweep; its record kind and public series; the fund's value as a party-position series (K-46) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/nav.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | the sweep at 9b; publication at 9d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-09 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc55.rs` | PC-55: the dealing price written only by the 9b rule |

**Design**:
- **Value** (FND.5): at 9b each business day, over the fund's holdings (K-65, a declared K-14 sweep partitioned by
  fund): assets at their marks (K-86) or, where a holding has none, a named valuer's valuation labelled with its
  prints' ages (MKT.20); liabilities: loans, accrued fees, redemptions payable; `NAV = (A − L) ÷ units`, rounded by the
  unit price's convention; the rounding residue is the fund's own line (Law 7). On a non-business day no price forms:
  the value read is the last business day's with the day's accruals.
- **Staleness**: every value carries the oldest mark age it used; dealing at a stale value moves value between
  investors (FND.5) — visible, never corrected.
- **Publication**: a K-37 record and a public series (K-92) per fund at 9d; the day's value cached (K-35) for dealing
  (S3.185) and fees; the value is written as the fund's party-position series (S1.239's `cross`), so thresholds on it
  (a stop, a mandate, a trigger) wake only when crossed.
- **FND.9 family** (K-103): units × value = assets − liabilities to the rounding its convention states, the residue on
  the fund; recounted from source rows, never from the cached value.

**Edge cases**: E2 — a holding with neither mark nor valuation: the value is not computed and dealing suspends by the
terms, never a zero (`unvalued_holding_suspends_nav`). E5 — quarter-ends: `valuation.positions` swept once
(`nav_sweep_linear_in_positions`). E6 — the cache is not saved, the published record is
(`nav_record_round_trip`). E7 — sweep by fund ranges, joined in fund order (`nav_independent_of_workers`). E11 — day
zero: the latest published value from the opening (LC-3-09 at day one).

**Extension points**: the value series is read by S3.185 (dealing), S3.186 (stable-price band), S3.192 (redemptions),
S3.194 (ETF gap), S3.198 (measures), S4.150 (DC pots), S4.123 (hedge funds' stops through the party-position series).

**Unit tests**: `nav_identity_with_rounding_on_fund`; `stale_mark_gives_labelled_stale_value`;
`unvalued_holding_suspends_nav`; `nb_day_value_is_last_plus_accruals`; `nav_sweep_linear_in_positions`;
`nav_record_round_trip`; `nav_independent_of_workers`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-09 — FND.9: every fund's units times its value equals assets minus liabilities to its price's
rounding, with the residue on the fund; applicable from day one.

**Budget**: `valuation.positions` 900000 fund positions at `fin.valuation.mark_ns` and 4500 funds' values; a
closed day's value is the last business day's with its accruals read by day count, no items.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 7 / 0 / 7 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-35): +0.05 MB resident (4500 funds × 12 B)

**Guards**: PC-55 (above).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day beyond
the declared sweep; an allocation per day; a constant value by construction; a valuation entering the value unlabelled;
a residue with no holder.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; PC-55 registered; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-09 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.185 — Dealing at the next value

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.6 PROCESS *(part: subscriptions and redemptions dealt at the next value, units issued and cancelled at settlement; investing and paying redemptions complete it at S3.192)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a, 7); §7.11 (phx-market: K-81 administered form); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-64 issued
amount)
**Depends on**: S1.319 (the administered form: a declared price with a quantity response); S3.184 (the next value);
S3.182 (dealing terms); S1.251 (dealings as commitments to their settle day)
**Goal**: an open-ended fund stands behind dealing in its units at its next value: an order taken in the decide stage
of one day deals at the next dealing day's meeting at the value computed after that order was taken, settles on the
terms' convention, and units are issued or cancelled at settlement.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/markets.rs` | each redeemable fund's dealing as an administered market (MKT.8): business days, the fund's dealing frequency, settlement |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/dealing.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | orders taken at 5c/5d of D; dealt at 6a of the next dealing day at D's value; commitments to settle |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-74 |

**Design**:
- **Dealing** (MKT.8, the one exception of MKT.16): orders posted on day D (subscriptions in money, redemptions in
  units, each its investor's own decision, S3.187–S3.190) deal at 6a of the next dealing day at the value computed at
  9b of D — a value no order in the fund's dealing formed, read after the order was taken (forward pricing).
- **Settlement**: subscriptions issue units and redemptions cancel them at settlement on the terms' convention (a K-50
  commitment; the issued amount moves, REG.3); a redemption's payment is the fund's obligation from the deal (S3.192
  says how it is met).
- **Suspension**: when S3.184 cannot compute a value or the fund's procedure is open (S3.192), dealing is suspended and
  orders stand to the next dealing day by the terms.

**Edge cases**: E6 — orders taken before a save deal after it: live offers and commitments
(`forward_order_round_trip`). E11 — orders taken on day zero deal at the first value computed after them, never the
snapshot's (`day_zero_order_deals_at_first_value`). E13 — a fund with no orders deals nothing
(`no_orders_no_dealing`). E14 — a subscription and a redemption of one investor the same day: both dealt, nets commute
(`subscription_and_redemption_same_day`).

**Extension points**: the dealing market is read by S3.186 (stable price), S3.192 (gates), S4.150 (DC pots dealt here).

**Unit tests**: `forward_pricing_deals_at_next_value`; `units_issued_and_cancelled_at_settlement`;
`suspended_dealing_orders_stand`; `forward_order_round_trip`; `day_zero_order_deals_at_first_value`;
`no_orders_no_dealing`; `subscription_and_redemption_same_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-74 — every dealing's value was computed after its order was taken; every unit issued or cancelled
traces to a dealing; applicable from the first dealing.

**Budget**: 30000 dealing orders a business day at 100 phone-ns and 4500 administered meetings at 1000 phone-ns.
- its share of fin.fixed.calls: 7.5 / 0 / 7.5 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 13 (liens and processes): +0 B (dealings inside K-50's line)

**Guards**: none new (PC-55 holds the price).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; dealing at a value computed before the order was taken; units issued before settlement.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-74 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.186 — Stable-price money funds

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.11 FORBID *(part: a stable unit price only as a term compared with the value, its break an event; the other forbids complete at S3.193)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 9b, 6a, 10a); §7.11 (phx-market: K-81); §7.6 (phx-record: K-36 events)
**Depends on**: S3.184 (the value per unit); S3.185 (dealing at the next value); S3.182 (the stable-price band as a
term); S1.213 (public events)
**Goal**: a money fund whose terms promise a stable unit price deals at that price while its value lies within the
terms' band; when the value leaves the band the break is a public event and dealing moves to the value, as the terms
state; nothing holds the value constant.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/stable.rs` | the dealing price: the stable price within the band, the value outside it |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the break's event kind (public) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/stable.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-75 |

**Design**:
- At 9b, after S3.184's value, the dealing price for the next dealing day is the terms' stable price if
  `|NAV − stable| ≤ band`, otherwise the value (the terms may also declare that a break suspends dealing for a period).
- A break is a public event (OBS.3) naming the fund, its value and the band — what depositors' and investors' safety
  outlooks observe (S3.187). Returning inside the band restores the stable price only if the terms say so.
- The value itself is always S3.184's; PC-55 refuses any declaration of a constant unit value.

**Edge cases**: E1 — many money funds breaking the same day on one issuer's default: one event each
(`break_event_per_fund`). E6 — the dealing price is a record of the day, saved (`dealing_price_round_trip`). E11 — day
zero: the band compared with the first computed value (`first_band_test_on_first_value`).

**Extension points**: the break event is read by S3.187 (safety outlooks) and S3.198 (measures).

**Unit tests**: `stable_price_within_band`; `stable_price_breaks_outside_band`; `break_is_public_event`;
`break_event_per_fund`; `dealing_price_round_trip`; `first_band_test_on_first_value`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-75 — every money-fund dealing at the stable price had its value within the band that day; every
break is an event; applicable from the first money-fund dealing.

**Budget**: 1000 money funds a business day, one comparison each.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.01 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new (PC-55).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a constant value by construction; a stable price kept outside its band.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-75 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.187 — Investors choose funds

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.3 DECISION *(part: a fund's expected return net of fee from the investor's own outlook; institutions' choice; households and firms complete it at S3.189)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5a, 5c, 5d); §7.13 (phx-val: K-92 fund value series, safety outlooks); §7.16 (phx-mind:
K-100)
**Depends on**: S3.184 (published values); S3.185 (dealing orders); S3.186 (money funds' breaks); S3.148 (institutions'
class choice); S1.336 (public series and methods)
**Goal**: investors subscribe and redeem from their own reasons — yield against alternatives, the performance they
observed, their own needs for cash: this step gives every investor a fund's expected return net of fee and a money
fund's safety outlook, and institutions choose funds within a class by them.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-securities/src/funds.rs` | the handles `fund_expected_return(investor, fund)` and `money_fund_safety(method, fund)` other systems read |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/choose.rs` | FND.3: expected return net of fee from the investor's outlook of the value series; institutions' choice within a class |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/safety.rs` | the public-series outlook of a money fund's safety per method (breaks, published holdings) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/choose.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | institutions' fund orders at 5d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-76 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | fund choice (Sirri and Tufano, 1998; Berk and Green, 2004) |

**Design**:
- **Expected return** (FND.3): the investor's method's outlook over the fund's published value series (K-92; adaptive
  or trend-following, so flows chase what investors saw) less its fee; width from the same series.
- **Money-fund safety**: a public-series outlook per method of the expected loss from a break of the stable price
  (break events, the fund's published holdings), like banks' safety outlooks (S2.195).
- **Institutions** (banks, and from S4.137 insurers and pensions; decider: the investment office): class weights by
  S3.148's rule; within a class, funds by expected return net of fee; orders to S3.185's dealing.
- What an investor observes is published — the value series and break events — never other investors' positions
  (Law 12).

**Edge cases**: E11 — a fund with no published history: its class's comparable funds' series, VAL.10
(`new_fund_valued_from_comparables`). E12 — no comparable: not a candidate (`no_comparable_not_candidate`). E1 — a
money-fund break raises every method's expected loss at once, orders follow each investor's review
(`break_raises_expected_loss`).

**Extension points**: the handles `fund_expected_return` and `money_fund_safety` are read by S3.188, S3.189 and
S3.190; converted with the investors' decisions by S8.185 (the choice of fund) and S8.168 (money funds among a
depositor's choices).

**Unit tests**: `expected_return_net_of_fee_from_own_outlook`; `flows_chase_observed_performance`;
`money_fund_safety_from_breaks`; `new_fund_valued_from_comparables`; `no_comparable_not_candidate`;
`break_raises_expected_loss`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-76 — every subscription and redemption names its investor's decision and the published series
it read; applicable from the first dealing.

**Budget**: institutions' fund comparisons inside S3.148's reviews (1000 a business day × 5 funds at 150 phone-ns).
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.8 / 0 / 0.8 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (core attribute)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an investor reading another's position or a fund's unpublished holdings; flows imposed by a rule on
performance rather than chosen.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-76 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.188 — Households hold funds

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: HH.7 DECISION *(part: money, bond and equity funds among savings choices)*; FND.3 DECISION *(part: households)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c)
**Depends on**: S3.158 (households' `choose_holdings`); S3.187 (the handles `fund_expected_return` and

**Goal**: fund kinds are classes and instruments in a household's holdings review: it subscribes and redeems funds by

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism

**Depends on**: S3.182 (mandates and their limits); S3.148 and S3.134 (share and debt value rules); S1.357 (the investor
schedule, K-105); S3.175 (borrowing securities for shorts); S3.179 (prime-brokerage accounts and calls); S3.106 (repo
leverage); S3.184 (the fund's value as a party-position series, on which its stop is a threshold)
**Goal**: a fund's manager invests its subscriptions and manages its portfolio within the mandate from its own views, by
schedules at its own values; a hedge fund takes long and short positions on its views with leverage only from named
lenders, and cuts positions when its broker calls margin or its losses reach its own stop.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |

| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-78 |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the fund's portfolio manager's office (PTY.16), on its declared review days and when woken by a flow
  beyond its outlook, a margin call (S3.179) or its value crossing its stop (a K-46 threshold on S3.184's series).
- **Active funds**: for each eligible instrument of the mandate's universe its own value (S3.148, S3.134 at the
  manager's outlooks); orders are its investor schedules (K-105) within the mandate's limits (K-93 through S1.298's

- **Hedge funds**: the same schedules on both sides — shorts only on units borrowed through its broker (S3.175,

  — each a real limit; when a call comes due or its loss since the last review exceeds its stop (PREFERENCE), its

- Trackers are S3.206's; derivatives S4.123's.

### S3.192 — Redemptions, buffers and gates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.6 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a, 7); §7.11 (phx-market: K-84 rationed queue); §7.8 (phx-ledger: K-49 failure)
**Depends on**: S3.185 (dealing and redemptions owed); S3.191 (the portfolio sold); S1.323 (queues carrying deferred
requests forward); S2.117 (credit lines drawn); S3.147 and S3.166 (the markets sales go to)
**Goal**: a redemption is paid from the fund's cash buffer or by selling into markets that must clear, by the fund's
declared liquidation order and its own limits; where its terms allow a gate, what lies beyond it is deferred to the next
dealing day as a claim, never dropped; a redemption the fund cannot pay on its date fails and opens its own procedure;
the cost of late sales falls on those who stay.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/liquidity.rs` | FND.6: buffer target, sales for redemptions, line draws, the gate |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/points.rs` | decision point `FND.manage_liquidity` |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/liquidity.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | the gate queue (K-84) and deferred claims; sales at 5d; the procedure opened on a failed payment at 7 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-38 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the buffer form (Chernenko and Sunderam, 2016) |

**Design**:
- **Buffer** (decider: the portfolio manager): a cash target `z_f × σ̂_flow`, its outlook width of daily net flows,
  `z_f` PREFERENCE; subscriptions beyond it invested (S3.191).
- **Redemptions**: dealt redemptions are paid from the buffer; beyond it the fund sells by its declared liquidation
  order (pro rata or most liquid first, PREFERENCE) with limit orders at its own limits, and draws a credit line
  where it
  has one (a real limit, S2.117).
- **Gate** (terms): on a dealing day whose redemptions exceed the gate share of units, the excess is deferred into a
  K-84
  queue per fund, pro rata with ties on `FND.gate_lot`, carried to the next dealing day as a claim on the fund, never
  dropped (FND.11).
- **Failure**: a redemption payment that fails at stage 7 (SET.3) opens the fund's own procedure as its terms and law
  declare: dealing suspends (S3.185), unpaid redemptions become claims ranking as the terms say, and the fund sells by
  its liquidation order; the ending is S3.193's.
- **Runs**: redeemers are paid at their dealing day's value, so later sales' costs fall on stayers — the first-mover
  advantage runs come from (L6); nothing scripts a run. With S3.185's dealing, FND.6 is complete.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a run day: redemptions far beyond the buffer, sales O(positions), the gate queue O(redeemers)
(`run_day_cost_linear`). E2 — no bids for the fund's holdings: the sales stay offered and the redemption fails on its
date if cash is short (`failed_redemption_opens_procedure`). E6 — the gate queue and deferred claims saved
(`gate_queue_round_trip`). E14 — a deferred redemption and a new one the same day: queue order, then lot
(`deferred_before_new_by_queue`).

**Extension points**: the procedure's state is read by S3.193; `FND.manage_liquidity` is converted by S8.183.

**Unit tests**: `redemption_beyond_buffer_sells_by_order`; `gate_defers_never_drops`; `late_sale_cost_on_stayers`;
`failed_redemption_opens_procedure`; `run_day_cost_linear`; `gate_queue_round_trip`; `deferred_before_new_by_queue`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-38 — FND.6: each fund's forced sales name the redemptions they met, and the cost borne by staying
investors is published per episode; applicable from the first forced sale.

**Budget**: liquidity reviews for funds with net redemptions, 1000 a business day at 300 phone-ns; forced sales' orders
on `securities`.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.fund_run (event): 5 core-ms (30000 sale orders at 150 phone-ns, gate queue operations); joins H and B′
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.04 MB resident (4500 funds × 8 B: the buffer target)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a redemption rationed by cash with the rest dropped; a sale "at any price"; a redemption paid at a
value other than its dealing day's.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-38 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.193 — A fund's ending and liquidation

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.14 PROCESS; FND.11 FORBID
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 2f, 9c); §7.15 (phx-end: K-96, K-97, K-98)
**Depends on**: S3.192 (the fund's procedure); S3.182 (life and mandate terms); S1.342, S1.343, S1.345 (estates, the
ending kernel, the waterfall); S2.133 (estates' administration: sales into markets); S2.132 (the insolvency law's
classes)
**Goal**: a fund ends when its manager closes it, when its life or mandate ends it, or when its assets fall below what
it owes its lenders or its units reach zero: its estate sells its assets into markets, pays its lenders first and then
its unitholders per unit; a shortfall to lenders is their loss. No fund is exempt.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/ending.rs` | FND.14: the triggers, tested at 9c |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the fund form's ending: its estate's classes (lenders, redemption claims by terms, unitholders per unit) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/audit.rs` | the FND.11 checks: every ended fund met a trigger; every leverage has a lender; every redemption paid, deferred or failed |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/ending.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-36 |

**Design**:
- **Triggers** (L3), tested at 9c: the manager's closure (S3.196); the fund's life ending or its mandate's end date;
  assets at 9a's marks below what it owes its lenders; units at zero. A trigger opens one estate the next day at 2f
  (K-97 moves its holdings, contracts and accounts; K-96).
- **Distribution**: the estate's administrator (S2.133) sells into markets; K-98 pays lenders (secured by their liens
  first), then redemption claims as the terms rank them, then unitholders per unit (apportioned by K-16, residue to a
  named party by the law); a shortfall to lenders is their loss; a household estate holding the fund's units is paid
  like any holder.
- **FND.11** is complete with S3.186 (stable price), S3.191 (leverage) and S3.192 (gates): the audit family and LC-3-36.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a wave of fund endings on a crash: estates opened in one turn (`fund_endings_linear`). E4 — an
estate whose assets never sell stays open, counted, its sales offered each day (`unsold_fund_estate_stays_open`). E10 —
unitholders ended: their estate receives (`ended_unitholder_estate_paid`). E13 — a fund with no lenders: unitholders
take all (`no_lenders_unitholders_take_all`).

**Extension points**: fund estates are read by S4.123 (hedge funds' derivative close-outs).

**Unit tests**: `fund_ends_on_each_trigger`; `lenders_paid_before_unitholders`; `unitholders_per_unit_with_residue`;
`no_fund_exempt_from_ending`; `fund_endings_linear`; `unsold_fund_estate_stays_open`; `ended_unitholder_estate_paid`;

### S3.194 — Exchange-traded funds and authorised dealers

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.7 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a, 7); §7.11 (phx-market: K-81 in-kind dealing, K-78 books); §7.9 (phx-contract:
K-53)
**Depends on**: S3.182 (ETF units: listed terms, the authorised-dealer agreements); S3.184 (the value); S3.147 (the
units' book); S3.174 (desks quoting on books); S3.163 (desks' limits and funding); S1.319 (administered dealing)
**Goal**: an exchange-traded fund's units trade on a book at a price that is not its value; an authorised dealer creates
units when their price is above the value by more than its all-in cost and redeems them when below, within its own
limits and balance sheet, and sells or buys the units on the book by its own quotes — which is how the gap narrows when
dealers have room, and why it widens when they do not.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the family `FND.ap_agreement` (fund, desk; basket rule; creation unit size); in-kind dealing reasons |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/etf.rs` | FND.7: the dealer's create-or-redeem decision |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/etf.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | creations and redemptions dealt in kind at the next value at 6a of the next business day |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-79 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the arbitrage form (Petajisto, 2017) |

**Design**:
- **Decision** (decider: the desk's head, under an agreement): at 5c, with `P` the units' last close and `NAV` the last
  value, create `k` creation units when `P − NAV > c` (its all-in cost: buying the basket at its outlook of the
  constituents' offers, funding at its line's rate, fees), redeem when `NAV − P > c`; `k` bound by its limits and
  funding headroom (K-93 through S1.298's admission hook).
- **Dealing**: in kind at the fund's next value (MKT.8): a creation delivers the basket (the fund's published holdings
  per creation unit) plus a cash balance and receives units; a redemption the reverse; dealt at 6a of the next business
  day, ties on `FND.creation_lot`; units issued or cancelled at settlement (S3.185).
- **Units**: created units are the desk's inventory, sold on the fund's book by its quotes (S3.174); units to redeem
  are bought there the same way. Price and value stay two numbers; the gap is an outcome (FND.7).

**Edge cases**: E2 — no authorised dealer with headroom: no creation, the gap stays
(`ap_creates_only_beyond_cost_within_limits`). E6 — a creation ordered before a save and dealt after it: a live
commitment (`creation_round_trip`). E11 — day zero: the opening's last close and value
(`first_ap_decision_reads_snapshot`).
E12 — no close yet: no decision (`no_close_no_ap_decision`).

**Extension points**: the create-or-redeem decision is converted by S8.184.

**Unit tests**: `ap_creates_only_beyond_cost_within_limits`; `redeems_when_below_value`; `in_kind_basket_per_unit`;
`creation_round_trip`; `first_ap_decision_reads_snapshot`; `no_close_no_ap_decision`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-79 — every creation and redemption names its desk's decision, the close and value it read and its
limits; applicable from the first creation.

### S3.195 — Private equity: commitments, capital calls and distributions

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 9c, 9e, 2c, 2e); §7.8 (phx-ledger: K-50 uncalled capital); §7.7 (phx-agenda: K-45 calls)
**Depends on**: S3.182 (private-equity and private-credit funds' terms: committed capital, life); S1.251 (uncalled
capital as commitments on both books); S1.237 (calls as messages due the next business day); S1.317 (stakes agreed by
bilateral negotiation); S1.281 (distributions to unitholders as events)
**Goal**: a private-equity fund's committed capital is a commitment on both books; when its investment decision needs
money it calls capital, due the next business day; an investor that cannot pay from its own liquidity defaults on the
call and forfeits its interest to the fund for the remaining investors; the fund distributes on exits by its terms.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/calls.rs` | FND.8: the call's size; default and forfeiture |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the commitment kind (uncalled capital), the call message kind, the distribution event on fund units |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/calls.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | calls issued at 9c, applied at 9e, due at the next business day's 2c; distributions at 2e |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-37 |

**Design**:
- **Commitment** (REG.10): each investor's commitment is a K-50 row (investor → fund, uncalled amount, the fund's
  life), recorded on both books.
- **Call** (decider: the fund's portfolio manager): when an investment decision needs money — a founding it backs
  (S3.197) or a stake agreed by bilateral negotiation (MKT.7, K-80) — the fund calls
  `need × commitment_i ÷ Σ commitments` from each investor (K-16's apportion, residue to the fund), issued at 9c, due at
  the next business day's 2c (TIME.7); the uncalled amount falls as called.
- **Default**: an unpaid call fails (SET.3); by the terms the defaulter's interest passes to the fund for the remaining
  investors (units cancelled, uncalled commitment ended), an event.
- **Distributions**: proceeds of an exit are distributed to unitholders by the terms as a unit event (S1.281) — never
  income from undistributed gains. Private-credit funds call capital the same way to lend (S3.201).

**Edge cases**: E3 — an investor with no liquidity defaults and forfeits (`capital_call_default_forfeits_to_fund`). E6 —
a call issued before a save, due after it: a live message (`capital_call_round_trip`). E10 — an investor ended: its
estate is called and pays or defaults (`estate_investor_called`). E14 — two calls on one investor the same day: summed
in one due (`two_calls_one_due`).
