### S3.196 — Launching and closing funds

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FND.12 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 3b); §7.5 (phx-pop: K-31 begin, K-32 columns); §7.10 (phx-hold: K-64 units issued)
**Depends on**: S3.182 (fund kinds and managers); S3.184 (published values and flows of comparable funds); S3.193 (a
closure's ending); S1.194 (a new party begun by a named event); S1.279 (the new fund's units issued); S1.450 (the
manager's fee point reviewed like any posted price)
**Goal**: a manager launches a fund of a kind when it expects the fees to pay, seeding it from its named accounts, and
closes one whose expected fees no longer cover its costs; fee changes are its own posted point.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/launch.rs` | FND.12: the launch and closure values |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/points.rs` | decision point `FND.launch_or_close` (the manager's chief executive) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/launch.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | a launch begun at 3b the next day (party, units, mandate, seed subscription) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-80 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the launch form (Khorana and Servaes, 1999; Zhao, 2005) |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the manager's chief executive's office, on its quarterly review (K-43).
- **Launch**: for each fund kind the manager may run, its value of the expected fees — its outlook of inflows from
  comparable funds' published flows and values (VAL.10), times its fee, over its horizon, net of running costs (staff
  hours, TECHNOLOGY) — against the launch cost (TECHNOLOGY hours and fees); it launches when the value exceeds it. The
  fund begins at 3b as a party (K-31, a founding event naming the manager), its units instrument issued (K-64), its
  mandate the kind's declared data, seeded by a subscription from the manager's named account.
- **Closure**: a fund whose expected fees no longer cover its costs is closed: S3.193's ending with the manager's
  closure as the trigger.
- **Fees**: a fee change is the manager's posted point, reviewed by S1.450 with flows against expectation as the
  pressure `sys-fnd` supplies.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no comparable funds: no launch of that kind (`no_comparable_no_launch`). E3 — a manager with no
cash to seed: no launch (`no_seed_no_launch`). E10 — the manager ending: its funds' management contracts pass by the
terms (S3.182; LC-3-73). E11 — day zero: the opening's funds only (`no_launch_on_day_zero`).

**Extension points**: `FND.launch_or_close` is converted by S8.182; S4.150's pension products use the same kinds.

**Unit tests**: `launch_value_against_cost`; `close_when_fees_short_of_costs`; `no_comparable_no_launch`;
`seed_from_named_account`; `no_seed_no_launch`; `no_launch_on_day_zero`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-80 — every fund launched names its manager's decision and its seed payment; every closure names
its decision and ends by S3.193; applicable from the first launch.

**Budget**: 500 managers reviewing quarterly (10 a business day) × 6 kinds.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.01 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger: +0 B (new funds are institution rows within their line)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fund begun without a seed from named accounts; a closure without the ending's sales.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-80 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.201 — Non-bank lenders lend through the banks' decisions

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: BNK.22 STATE; BNK.10 PROCESS *(part: non-bank lenders and private-credit funds buy loans through `quote_loans`; securitisation vehicles complete it at S4.161)*
**Architecture**: §7.3 (phx-core: K-21 lender facet as data); §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100); §6 (stage 5c)
**Depends on**: S1.425 (lending decisions: quote, decline, choose, standards, each lender's own assessment); S3.199
(funding sources); S3.200 (capital regimes); S2.107 (loan sales and `quote_loans`); S2.110 (bought bureau records read
by assessments); S2.108 (filed accounts); S3.182 (private-credit funds); S3.195 (their capital calls); S2.122
(insolvency tests); S3.193 (a fund's ending)
**Goal**: finance companies and private-credit funds write loans under the same contracts and decisions as banks,
without taking deposits, buy loans offered for sale, and fail when their funding does.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/src/decl.rs` | the lender facet as data: which kinds lend, and BNK.4–BNK.7's decision points declared for each |
| `crates/systems/sys-bnk/tests/nonbank.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/bnk.rs` | LC-3-11, LC-3-39 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc152.rs` | PC-152: no `sys-bnk` rule reads a lender's kind identity |
| `data/<country>/BNK.toml` | the finance-company and private-credit lender kinds |

**Design**:
- **Same decisions** (BNK.22, Law 10): S1.425's quote, decline, assessment and choice, and Stage 2's workout,
  provisions and enforcement, run for every party whose kind the data lists as a lender, each in its own loan office;
  each builds its assessment by the same rule from what it can observe — its own lines, records it bought from the
  bureau (S2.110), public filings (S2.108) — and reports to the bureau as its law requires. Borrowers shop among every
  lender they reach (BNK.6); a loan sale's asks (S2.107) reach them, answered by `quote_loans` (BNK.10 part).
- **Forms** (PTY.4): a finance company is a firm whose form may not take deposits; a private-credit fund is a fund kind
  (S3.182). A deposit contract whose issuer's form forbids deposits is refused at assembly and by the ledger (MON.1).
- **Cost and capital**: S2.179's marginal cost over S3.199's sources; S2.189's charge over S3.200's regime.
- **Failure**: a roll that fails and a line that is cut leave it short: its quotes decline on liquidity (BNK.5); a
  payment it cannot make is its default (S2.122) or its fund's ending (S3.193); its estate sells its loans (S2.107).
- Streams: none new (`BNK.lender_taste` covers borrowers' tastes over all lenders).

**Edge cases**: E1 — a paper market failing: several finance companies stop lending the same day, each by its own state
(`nonbanks_stop_by_own_state`). E3 — a finance company with no funding declines every ask
(`nonbank_declines_without_funding`). E10 — a lender ended: its loans move to its estate and are sold (LC-3-11). E12 —
a deposit contract for a non-deposit form refused (`deposit_contract_refused_for_nondeposit_form`).

**Extension points**: the lender facet is declared data read by S4.161 (securitisation vehicles buying loans); the
lending decisions are converted with banks' by S8.161.

**Unit tests**: `nonbank_quote_uses_its_own_marginal_cost`; `deposit_contract_refused_for_nondeposit_form`;
`nonbank_declines_without_funding`; `nonbanks_stop_by_own_state`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-11 — a non-bank lender whose funding fails stops lending and, if it cannot pay, fails, with its
estate selling its loans (not applicable until one does); LC-3-39 — BNK.22: no non-bank lender holds a deposit
liability, and every non-bank loan came from the same decision points as banks'.

**Budget**: 300 non-bank lenders' quotes inside S1.425's line (5 % of the day's loan quotes).
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) — their quotes are counted in S1.425's line
- ledger: +0 B (they are firm and fund rows)

**Guards**: PC-152 (above).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; lending code specific to a lender's kind; a non-bank taking deposits; a non-bank funded from nowhere
or unable to fail.

### S3.203 — Benchmark fixings from transactions

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: IDX.2 STATE
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 8, 9d); §7.11 (phx-market: K-86 fixings, the day's prints); §7.9 (phx-contract: K-55
fixings read as published)
**Depends on**: S3.101 (the money-market call: overnight matches printed per market); S3.105 (term bids and offers:
term matches); S1.326 (fixings by (publisher, method) over the day's individual prints); S1.263 (floating legs read a
fixing as published by day d, and the placeholder this retires); S1.215 (fixing records, public from the next day)
**Goal**: each country's floating-rate benchmark is fixed by a named administrator from the day's eligible unsecured
money-market transactions by its declared method; a day without them has no fixing, and a contract fixing that day uses
its own declared fallback; every floating contract fixes on it from here.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/src/benchmark.rs` | IDX.2: the trimmed volume-weighted mean over the day's eligible matches |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/src/decl.rs` | the administrator's publisher facet; benchmark series and their record kind |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/tests/benchmark.rs` | logic-level tests, the compile-fail one included |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/idx.rs` | the fixing at 9d from stage 8's prints |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/idx.rs` | LC-3-40 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc56.rs` | PC-56: `BenchmarkFixing`'s only constructor takes the day's match set |
| `data/<country>/IDX.toml` | each administrator's eligibility and trimming (POLICY of the administrator) |

**Design**:
- **Fixing** (IDX.2): at 9d of each business day, over the day's individual prints of the unsecured overnight market
  (S3.101's stage-8 matches, S1.326): eligible prints by the declared method (counterparty kinds, minimum size), the
  declared trim, then `Σ r·q ÷ Σ q` over the rest (ECB, 2019; IOSCO, 2013). Term benchmarks fix on term matches
  (S3.105); a compounded average is a read over past fixings.
- **Absence**: a day with no eligible match has no fixing (Law 3); a contract whose fixing day it is uses its terms'
  fallback (ISDA, 2020: the last fixing with its age, or a declared alternative series), never a rate the administrator
  posts; a policy rate is never a benchmark.
- **Record**: a K-86 fixing labelled as such, kept as a K-37 record public from the next day. Floating loans, interbank
  term loans, mortgages and notes read it on their fixing days (K-55, as published by day d): their reference was the
  series' one identity from origination, so S1.263's placeholder naming IDX (the series' last published value) ends
  with no contract's terms changed.
- One writer (Law 4): the administrator's 9d rule is the only writer of benchmark fixings; the pricing service's
  fixings (S3.169) are another fact with another writer.

**Edge cases**: E2 — no eligible match: no fixing (`benchmark_absent_without_transactions`). E6 — fixings are records,
saved (`benchmark_round_trip`). E11 — day zero: the opening's latest fixing
(`first_fixing_day_reads_snapshot_benchmark`).
E13 — a country whose money market has no unsecured segment has no benchmark; its contracts declare another reference
(`no_segment_no_benchmark`).

**Extension points**: benchmark series are read by S4.118 (swaps' floating legs) and S5.163 (currencies).

**Unit tests**: `benchmark_trimmed_volume_weighted_mean`; `benchmark_absent_without_transactions`;
`fallback_by_contract_terms`; `posted_benchmark_refused` (compile-fail); `benchmark_round_trip`;
`first_fixing_day_reads_snapshot_benchmark`; `no_segment_no_benchmark`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-40 — IDX.2: every benchmark fixing traces to the day's eligible matches; no fixing exists for a
day without them; every fallback used names its contract's terms; applicable from the first fixing.

**Budget**: 3 overnight and 10 term fixings a business day over 2000 prints each.
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.02 MB resident (13 fixings a day × 730 days × 2 B of record in K-37)

**Guards**: PC-56 (above).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a posted benchmark; a policy rate as a benchmark; a fixing where no transaction was.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests, the compile-fail one included; fast checks pass; PC-56 registered; the bench at the committed

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: IDX.1 STATE; IDX.5 INVARIANT; IDX.6 FORBID; IDX.7 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.11 (phx-market: K-86 last prints); §7.6 (phx-record: K-37 links); §7.13 (phx-val: K-92 public
series); §7.17 (phx-audit: K-103)
**Depends on**: S3.147 (closes); S3.169 (bond fixings); S3.162 (market capitalisation as a read); S3.145 (free float);
S1.215 (index definitions and links as the publisher's records); S1.336 (an index as a public series read through its
rule); S1.353 (the IDX.5 family); S3.203 (PC-56 for benchmarks)
**Goal**: a market index is its publisher's published rule over constituents and weights with a base; its level is
recomputed from the constituents' last prints whenever it is read, never stored as a number of its own; its return
equals the weighted return of its constituents; no index feeds its own constituents, none is empty and none wears two
names.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/src/market_index.rs` | IDX.1: the level as a read |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/src/decl.rs` | index definitions: publisher, rule, weights kind, base, divisor; the link record kind; the series declaration |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/src/audit.rs` | the IDX.5 family |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/tests/market_index.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/idx.rs` | LC-3-12 |
| `data/<country>/IDX.toml` | each index's rule, selection, weights and base (IDX.7: POLICY of its publisher) |

**Design**:
- **Definition** (IDX.7): publisher (a firm with the publisher facet), rule (selection from published data), weights
  (capitalisation from S3.162's read with S3.145's free float, amount outstanding for bonds, or equal), base, divisor;
  one identity per rule (assembly refuses two indices with one rule under two names). At the opening each publisher's
  rule selects its constituents from the opening's listed shares and lines by its own rule (no source mapping), with
  the base set at the snapshot's level and no link stored.
- **Level** (IDX.1): `L(d) = base × Π links × Σ wᵢ·pᵢ(d) ÷ divisor` over the constituents' last prints (closes,
  fixings), each with its age; the read returns the oldest age used. Never stored; the public series (K-92) forms
  outlooks from it through the read, at 5a on days a constituent printed.
- **IDX.5 family** (K-103): each business day the index's return equals `Σ wᵢ(d−1)·rᵢ(d)` of its constituents to the
  arithmetic allowance of its price convention (Law 7), computed from the constituents' prints.
- **Forbids** (IDX.6): the constituent rule refuses an instrument whose issuer tracks the index or whose price is set
  from it; an index without constituents is refused at assembly and at rebalance (S3.205); benchmarks only from match
  sets (PC-56).

**Edge cases**: E2 — a constituent never printed cannot be selected; one with an old print reads it with its age
(`unprinted_constituent_refused`). E10 — a constituent's issuer ending: its instrument ceases and the publisher's next
change removes it; until then its last print with age (`ceased_constituent_reads_last_print`). E11 — day zero: the
levels are reads of the opening's prints (`opening_level_is_a_read`). E13 — an index whose selection finds none is
refused (`empty_index_refused`).

**Extension points**: index definitions are declared data read by S3.205 (rebalances), S3.206 (trackers), S3.158
(households' class outlooks), S4.120 (index futures), S4.119 (CDS indices).

**Unit tests**: `index_level_is_a_read_of_prints_and_links`; `index_return_identity`;
`constituent_rule_refuses_own_tracker`; `empty_index_refused`; `one_rule_one_identity`;
`unprinted_constituent_refused`; `ceased_constituent_reads_last_print`; `opening_level_is_a_read`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-12 — IDX.5 and IDX.6: the family is clean for every market index; no index is an input to its own
constituents; applicable from day one.

**Budget**: 75 indices × 500 constituents (by their rules): levels read on demand (40000 reads a day at 5
phone-ns); the family's 40000 terms a business day fused.
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- its share of fin.fixed.recount: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.3 MB resident (37500 constituent entries × 8 B)

**Guards**: assembly refuses an index with no constituents or two names for one rule.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a stored market-index level; an index that is an input to its own constituents.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-12 registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.205 — Index changes, announced and chained

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: IDX.4 PROCESS *(part: constituent changes announced and chained; the trackers' trades complete it at S3.206)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9d); §7.6 (phx-record: K-37 links)
**Depends on**: S3.204 (index definitions and levels); S1.227 (rebalance dates)
**Goal**: on its rebalance dates a publisher's rule selects constituents from published data; the change is announced
before it takes effect, and its chain link is stored as the publisher's record, so the level does not jump.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/src/rebalance.rs` | IDX.4: selection on rebalance dates, announcement, the link at the effective day |
| `crates/systems/sys-idx/tests/rebalance.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/idx.rs` | announcements at 9d; links stored at the effective day's close |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/idx.rs` | LC-3-41 (link part) |
| `data/<country>/IDX.toml` | rebalance dates and notice (POLICY of the publisher) |

**Design**:
- **Change** (decider: the publisher's index office): on each rebalance date (K-43) the rule selects constituents from
  published data (capitalisation reads, free floats, turnover — MKT.15); the change is announced at 9d as a public
  record with an effective day at least the declared notice later.
- **Link**: at the effective day's close, `link = L_old(d) ÷ L_new(d)` is stored as the publisher's record (K-37), so
  `L` is continuous across the change; the divisor and weights change with it.

**Edge cases**: E6 — an announced change pending across a save: a record with its effective day
(`announced_change_round_trip`). E10 — a constituent's issuer ending before the effective day: the rule re-selects by
its declared fallback (`reselect_on_constituent_end`). E14 — two indices changing the same day: independent links
(`independent_links_same_day`).

**Extension points**: announcements are read by S3.206; the publisher's change is converted by S8.194.

**Unit tests**: `chain_link_no_jump`; `announcement_before_effective_day`; `announced_change_round_trip`;
`reselect_on_constituent_end`; `independent_links_same_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-41 (link part) — every constituent change stored its link; applicable from the first rebalance.

**Budget**: 5 changes a month.
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.01 MB resident (links and announcements, 120 records × 64 B)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an index jump at a constituent change; a change without notice.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-41's link part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.206 — Funds that track an index

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: IDX.4 PROCESS; EQY.3 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 6a); §7.11 (phx-market: K-78 closing call)
**Depends on**: S3.205 (announced changes); S3.191 (managers' investing, extended to trackers); S3.147 (the closing
call trackers trade in); S1.357 (the investor schedule, K-105); S3.182 (tracking tolerance as a mandate's term)
**Goal**: every fund tracking an index trades on a change's effective day at the close, each by its own decision within
its own tolerance, by limit orders, never at any price — so a tracked index change is a real, simultaneous trade by
every fund that tracks it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/track.rs` | EQY.3: a tracker's orders within its tolerance |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/track.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/fnd.rs` | trackers' `AtTheClose` orders at 5d of the effective day |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-41 (tracker part) |

**Design**:
- **Trackers** (decider: each tracking fund's portfolio manager): a tracker holds the index's constituents at its
  weights; on an announced change, and whenever its tracking difference exceeds its tolerance (PREFERENCE), it posts
  `AtTheClose` orders on the effective day (or its review day) for the difference, each limited at its outlook of the
  close ± its tolerance (K-105 for the size within the band). With S3.148's investors, EQY.3 is complete; with
  S3.205's links, IDX.4 is.

**Edge cases**: E5 — effective days crowd closing calls (`tracker_orders_at_close_linear`). E2 — a constituent with no
seller within the tolerance: unfilled, the tracking difference carried (`unfilled_tracker_carries_difference`). E6 —
a tracker's pending orders across a save: live K-70 rows (`tracker_orders_round_trip`).

**Extension points**: the tracker rule is converted by S8.181.

**Unit tests**: `tracker_orders_within_tolerance`; `tracker_orders_at_close_linear`;
`unfilled_tracker_carries_difference`; `tracker_orders_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-41 (tracker part) — every tracker's trades on an effective day are recorded with its limits;
applicable from the first rebalance.

**Budget**: tracker orders on effective days, 50000 on the rebalance day.
- on fin.calendar.index_rebalance (the publishers' declared effective days): 7.5 core-ms (50000 orders at 150
  phone-ns); joins H and B′
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0.001 MB resident (300 trackers × 4 B: tolerance ref)

**Guards**: none new (PC-150).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tracker ordering at any price.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-41 complete registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.207 — Rating agencies and their ratings

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: RAT.1 STATE; RAT.9 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 9d); §7.6 (phx-record: K-37 records); §7.7 (phx-agenda: K-43 reviews and wakes);
§7.15 (phx-end: K-98's step walker, which a structured method runs); §7.16 (phx-mind: K-100)
**Depends on**: S1.215 (ratings as records, public from the next day); S1.216 (filed accounts, what agencies read of
unlisted issuers); S2.108 (the filing decision and the fiscal year each firm chose); S1.265 (missed payments and
defaults as contract events that wake agencies); S1.165 (an index instance: the agencies rating an issuer); S1.450
(the agency's fee point); S1.345 (the step walker a structured method applies); S1.348 (the decision core)
**Goal**: agencies publish coarse, sticky, ordinal opinions of issuers and instruments on their declared scales,
formed from the issuer's published state and never from its price, by declared scorecards that move a notch only when
the score crosses a threshold by more than a band; agencies with different methods disagree.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-rat/src/scale.rs` | rating scales and notches, the vocabulary every referring rule reads |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/rules/rate.rs` | RAT.1: the scorecard over a `RatingView` |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/decl.rs` | the agency's publisher facet; method kinds per rated-object class (issuer, sovereign, instrument, structured); the rating record kind; the index instance issuer → agencies |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/points.rs` | decision point `RAT.rate` (the agency's rating committee office) |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/tests/rate.rs` | logic-level tests, the compile-fail one included |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/rat.rs` | reviews at 5c; ratings published at 9d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/rat.rs` | LC-3-42 (rating part) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc57.rs` | PC-57: `RatingView` and estimate views hold no print, mark or market-index field |
| `data/<country>/RAT.toml` | scales, methods, bands, windows (POLICY of each agency); reporting and filing deadlines (POLICY) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the scorecard form (Altman, 1968; Cantor and Mann, 2003) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `GEN.present.ratings`'s first read moved to S3.207 |

**Design**:
- **Coverage**: an issuer engages agencies when it first issues a listed share or a bond on a book (the number its
  exchange or book rules require, POLICY), paying each agency's fee on the fee point (S1.450); the engagement is a
  row of the issuer → agencies index instance (S1.165).
- **When** (decider: the agency's rating committee office): each rated issuer's annual review (K-43) and wakes — a
  report or a filing published (S3.209, S2.108), a missed payment or a default on one of its contracts (S1.265's
  events) — delivered to the agencies rating it through the index instance.
- **View** (PC-57): a `RatingView` of the issuer's published state — reported or filed ratios over the agency's
  window (leverage, coverage, size, earnings volatility); for a sovereign its published debt, deficit and output
  (STA) — and no price. A window shorter than the method asks is handled by the method's declared rule (POLICY of the
  agency); an absent ratio is Missing, never zero (VAL.10).
- **Method** (RAT.1, RAT.9): a scorecard — declared weights and thresholds map the score to a notch of the agency's
  scale; the notch moves only when the score crosses a threshold by more than the declared band, so ratings are
  coarse, sticky, lag what the data lag, and are sometimes wrong. Method kinds are declared per rated-object class
  (Law 10); a structured method runs K-98's step walker over a deal's declared waterfall under the agency's declared
  stresses.
- **Publication**: a K-37 record (agency, subject, notch, day), public from the next business day; the record's
  series is the subject's rating series, its tick grid the scale's notches.
- **Opening** (GEN.13): each agency rates every issuer it covers on day zero by its method, from the issuer's latest
  filed accounts (S1.486).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a mass default wakes the agencies of every defaulting issuer, one review each
(`one_review_per_woken_issuer`). E6 — ratings are records, saved and reloaded (`rating_record_round_trip`). E10 — an
issuer ended: its rating withdrawn with a record (`ended_issuer_rating_withdrawn`). E11 — a window of one report: the
declared short-window rule (`short_window_by_declared_rule`). E12 — a ratio absent: the method's declared treatment,
never zero (`absent_ratio_never_zero`). E13 — an issuer no agency rates has no rating record: unrated
(`unrated_issuer_has_no_record`).

**Extension points**: the agencies and their scorecards are S3.208's data; method kinds are data: S4.162 declares
the tranche method through `RAT.rate`'s method-kind
point; the scale is read by S3.212 and S3.213–S3.217; the rating decision is converted by S8.192.

**Unit tests**: `rating_view_has_no_price` (compile-fail); `scorecard_notch_with_hysteresis`;
`agencies_disagree_by_weights`; `one_review_per_woken_issuer`; `rating_record_round_trip`;
`ended_issuer_rating_withdrawn`; `short_window_by_declared_rule`; `absent_ratio_never_zero`;
`unrated_issuer_has_no_record`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-42 (rating part) — RAT.7's first forbid: no rating read a print or a price series (the
read-trace); applicable from the first rating.

**Budget**: 6000 rated issuers, 150 rating reviews a business day at 5 µs each; on a mass-default day 600 rated
issuers reviewed.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.75 / 0 / 0.75 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- its E1 share of fin.waterfall.mass_failure_core_ms: 3 core-ms (600 reviews × 5 µs)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.14 MB resident (18000 issuer → agency rows × 8 B)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.9 MB resident (37500 ratings a year × 24 B at the 365-day horizon)

**Guards**: PC-57 (above).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a rating derived from a price; an unrated issuer given a default grade.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests, the compile-fail one included; fast checks pass; PC-57 registered; the form listed; the
  bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-42's rating part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.208 — The opening's rating agencies and their scorecards

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: which of the opening's firms are rating agencies, and their methods)*
**Architecture**: §10.0a (the opening dataset) followed
**Depends on**: S3.207 (the publisher facet, scales and method kinds); S1.486 (the opening's firms and their latest
filed accounts); S3.146 (the exchange the opening names)
**Goal**: at the opening each country has its rating agencies, each with a declared scale and a scorecard taken from
a published model, so that agencies differ in method and can disagree from day zero.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/data/derive_rat.py` | the derivation below |
| `data/<country>/gen/RAT.toml` | the agencies (firms the opening names with the rating publisher facet) |
| `data/<country>/RAT.toml` | each agency's scale, weights, thresholds and band (POLICY of the agency) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the published models' coefficients (Altman, 1968; Ohlson, 1980; Zmijewski, 1984) |

**Design**:
- **Agencies**: in each country the three largest financial-services firms by equity at the opening (S1.486), after
  the exchange (S3.146) and apart from banks, insurers and funds, carry the rating publisher facet, three being the
  number of agencies that issue nearly all ratings (SEC, 2019, Annual Report on Nationally Recognized Statistical
  Rating Organizations, table of ratings outstanding).
- **Scorecards**: each agency's weights are one published model's coefficients (Altman, 1968; Ohlson, 1980;
  Zmijewski, 1984), one per agency, so agencies read the same filed ratios differently; the scale's notch
  thresholds are the model's implied default probabilities spaced evenly on a log scale between the bounds the paper
  reports (the declared procedure); the band is half a notch's width (Cantor and Mann, 2003, through-the-cycle
  rating), POLICY of the agency.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E12 — a country with fewer than three such firms has as many agencies as
it has firms (`fewer_firms_fewer_agencies`). E13 — a country with none has no agency and every issuer in it is
unrated (`no_agency_all_unrated`). E11 — day-zero ratings are the agencies' own reviews, never typed
(`unrated_issuer_has_no_record`, S3.207).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `tools/data` tests `agencies_largest_financial_services`, `thresholds_log_spaced_from_model`,
`fewer_firms_fewer_agencies`, `no_agency_all_unrated`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-42 (rating part) at day one.

**Budget**: opening only; the opening's span within its ratchet.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.001 MB resident (9 agencies' scorecards × 21 notches × 8 B)

**Guards**: `phx-check data`.

**Not allowed**: a value typed by hand; a rating typed at the opening; an agency without a declared method.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The derivation and tests; the data regenerated; fast checks; the opening's span within its ratchet (the bench
  at the committed resolution).
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.209 — Listed companies' reports and restatements

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: RAT.2 STATE
**Architecture**: §6 (stages 5c, 9c, 9d); §7.12 (phx-acct: K-90 statements and consolidation); §7.6 (phx-record: K-37
vintages)
**Depends on**: S2.108 (the filing decision's form and the fiscal year each firm chose); S1.333 (closed statements);
S1.334 (consolidation: a group's consolidated read); S3.157 (the group fact); S3.145 (the listed shares whose issuers
report); S1.215 (records with vintages, "as published by day d"); S1.227 (windows and review days on the agenda);
S1.348 (the decision core)
**Goal**: a listed company publishes, for each fiscal period, a statement that is a read of its books — its group's
consolidated statement where it is a parent — on a date it chooses within the legal window after the period's end, so
reports spread across the calendar; a correction to a published period restates it and both versions are kept.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/rules/report_date.rs` | RAT.2: the publication date by S2.108's filing-day form |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/rules/report.rs` | the report as a read of the closed statement; restatements |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/decl.rs` | the report record kind (vintages), its audience (public) and horizon; reporting periods and windows |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/points.rs` | decision point `RAT.report_date` (the chief executive's office) |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/tests/report.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/rat.rs` | the report read at 9c on its date; published at 9d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/rat.rs` | LC-3-43; LC-3-42 (report part) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the publication date form (Givoly and Palmon, 1982), shared with S2.108 |

**Design**:
- **Periods and window**: each listed company's reporting periods follow its fiscal year (S2.108) and the exchange's
  declared frequency; the window runs from the period's end to the legal deadline (RAT.9, `RAT.toml`).
- **Date** (decider: the chief executive's office): once its preparation hours (TECHNOLOGY, from its staff's
  capacity) are spent, at its first review when the period's result beats the last period's, and at its last review
  before the deadline otherwise; so good news comes early and dates spread (N8.9).
- **Report**: on its date at 9c, a read of the period's closed statement (K-90; for a parent, the consolidated read
  over the group S3.157 names), taken whole, published at 9d as a K-37 record, public from the next day.
- **Restatement**: an event recognised later but dated inside a published period (a provision, a loss found)
  produces a new vintage of that period's report at the next publication; both versions stay with their dates ("as
  published by day d", Law 12).
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E5 — the reporting season's busiest day, 300 reports, each a statement read
(`report_is_read_of_closed_statement`, timed by the bench's `reporting_peak` day). E6 — a report due across a save:
its date on the agenda, rebuilt (`report_date_round_trip`). E10 — a company ended before its date: no report
(`ended_company_no_report`). E11 — the first report after the opening compares with the snapshot's latest (GEN.5;
`first_report_against_snapshot`). E14 — a restatement and a new period published the same day: two records, two
vintages (`restatement_keeps_both_versions`).

**Extension points**: reports are read by S3.148 (values), S3.207 (ratings), S3.210 (listing), S3.211 (estimates),
S3.218 (surprises); the report date is converted by S8.193.

**Unit tests**: `report_date_good_early_bad_late_within_window`; `report_is_read_of_closed_statement`;
`group_reports_consolidated`; `restatement_keeps_both_versions`; `report_date_round_trip`; `ended_company_no_report`;
`first_report_against_snapshot`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-43 — RAT.2 and N8.9: report dates are spread across each window, and no report was read before
its date; LC-3-42 (report part) — every reported number is a read of its company's books; applicable from the first
report.

**Budget**: 2300 listed companies reporting four times a year: 37 reports a mean business day, 300 on the season's
busiest day, each a statement read of 2 µs.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.07 / 0 / 0.07 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- on fin.calendar.reporting_peak (the windows' busiest day, from the declared deadlines): 0.6 core-ms; joins B′ (a
  deadline on a closed day rolls to the next business day)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +3.2 MB resident (9200 reports a year × 352 B: a 32 B header and 40
  statement lines × 8 B, at the 365-day horizon)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a reported number the books do not produce; a report read before its date; a restatement that
overwrites.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the form listed; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-43 and LC-3-42's report part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.211 — Guidance and analysts' estimates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: RAT.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9d); §7.13 (phx-val: K-92 outlooks by method); §7.6 (phx-record: K-37)
**Depends on**: S3.209 (reports, with which guidance is published and after which estimates are revised); S1.336
(public series and methods: the earnings series of a covered firm and each method's outlook); S1.215 (records);
S3.207 (PC-57: estimate views hold no price); S3.163 (dealer banks, whose research units publish); S1.348 (the
decision core)
**Goal**: guidance is management's own outlook of the next period's earnings, published with the report; an estimate
is a named analyst unit's published outlook of a covered firm's earnings, formed by its own method from what it
observed — published reports, guidance and statistics — never from the share price, the model's forecast or its
parent's private state.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/rules/estimate.rs` | RAT.3: an analyst unit's estimate from its method's outlook |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/rules/guidance.rs` | RAT.3: management's guidance with the report |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/decl.rs` | guidance and estimate record kinds; analyst units' publisher facet and coverage lists; the covered firms' earnings series registered with each unit's method |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/tests/estimate.rs` | logic-level tests, the compile-fail one included |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/rat.rs` | guidance with the report at 9d; estimates revised at 9d of a report's day |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/rat.rs` | LC-3-50 (analyst part) |

**Design**:
- **Guidance** (decider: the chief executive's office): management's own outlook of next period's earnings (its own
  method over its books, VAL), published with the report as a record.
- **Estimates** (decider: the analyst unit's research office): each dealer bank (S3.163) keeps one analyst unit, a
  subsidiary with the publisher facet; its coverage is the listed companies its analysts' hours (TECHNOLOGY) reach,
  largest by capitalisation first. Its estimate of a covered firm's earnings is its method's outlook of that firm's
  published earnings series (K-92, the heuristic menu over reports, guidance and statistics, starting from the
  snapshot's latest reports, VAL.10), published at 9d of each day a covered firm reports, public from the next day. A
  consensus is a read (the mean of the latest estimates), never stored.
- **Reads** (Law 12, PC-57): only public records; never its parent's assessment or any private state of it; never a
  print, mark or index level.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E6 — estimates are records (`estimate_record_round_trip`). E10 — a covered firm ended: coverage drops
it (`coverage_drops_ended_firm`). E11 — a covered firm with one report: the method's declared rule for a short
history, never zero (`short_history_by_declared_rule`). E13 — a country with no analyst unit publishes no estimates
(`no_unit_no_estimates`).

**Extension points**: estimates are read by S3.148 (values) and S3.218 (surprises against estimates); guidance and
estimates are converted by S8.193.

**Unit tests**: `estimate_is_methods_outlook_of_reports`; `estimate_view_has_no_price` (compile-fail, PC-57);
`guidance_published_with_report`; `consensus_is_a_read`; `estimate_record_round_trip`; `coverage_drops_ended_firm`;
`short_history_by_declared_rule`; `no_unit_no_estimates`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-50 (analyst part) — no analyst read its parent's private state or a price (the read-trace);
applicable from the first estimate.

**Budget**: 37 reports a mean business day, each covered by 5 units: 185 estimates at 50 ns (a K-92 cell read and a
record write).
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0.01 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +0.88 MB resident (46000 estimates and 9200 guidance records a year × 16
  B, at the 365-day horizon)

**Guards**: none new (PC-57).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an estimate from the share price or the model's forecast; an analyst reading its parent's private
state.

### S3.212 — Rules refer to ratings: references, unrated rows and the binding wake

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: RAT.4 PROCESS *(part: the reference, its unrated row and the wake that binds every holder at once; the referring rules at S3.213–S3.217; insurers' mandates complete it at S4.138)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 9d); §7.7 (phx-agenda: K-46 thresholds, K-43 wakes)
**Depends on**: S3.207 (ratings, their scales and their series); S1.239 (thresholds on a watched series waking the
parties bound); S1.227 (the next business day's reviews)
**Goal**: a rule that refers to ratings declares the scale it reads, its boundaries, its cure period and what it does
with an unrated holding; a rating published across a boundary reaches every bound holder at its next business day's
decisions at once.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-rat/src/reference.rs` | `RatingReference`: (referring rule, scale, boundaries, unrated row, cure period), the declaration each referring system makes |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/refer.rs` | assembly of references; each rating series declared a K-46 watched series on the scale's notch grid; the crossing at 9d |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/tests/refer.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/rat.rs` | crossings after the day's ratings at 9d |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/rat.rs` | LC-3-81 (wake part) |

**Design**:
- **References** (RAT.4): a referring rule declares a `RatingReference` through its own system's declarations; its
  unrated row is a declared row of the rule, never a grade (Law 10). Assembly refuses a reference without an unrated
  row or with a boundary off its scale's notches.
- **Binding at once**: each rating series (S3.207's record per subject and agency) is a K-46 watched series whose tick
  grid is the scale's notches. A rating record crossing a registered boundary at 9d calls `cross`; K-46 wakes every
  registered party (K-43) for its next business day's decisions, once per decision kind. Who registers, and what the
  woken decision does, is the referring rule's: S3.213–S3.217.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a downgrade of a large issuer bound to thousands of holders wakes only the crossed thresholds,
O(log n + k) (`only_crossed_thresholds_wake`). E6 — thresholds rebuilt at load from the declared references and the
live positions (`thresholds_rebuilt_equal`). E13 — a reference without an unrated row is refused
(`reference_without_unrated_row_refused`). E14 — a holder crossed on two series the same day is woken once per
decision kind (`one_wake_per_decision_kind`).

**Extension points**: `RatingReference` is declared by S3.213 (funds' mandates), S3.214 (risk weights), S3.215
(the central bank's collateral), S3.216 (lenders' haircuts and limits), S3.217 (debt terms' triggers) and S4.138
(insurers' mandates).

**Unit tests**: `only_crossed_thresholds_wake`; `thresholds_rebuilt_equal`; `reference_without_unrated_row_refused`;
`boundary_off_scale_refused`; `one_wake_per_decision_kind`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-81 (wake part) — every rating crossing a registered boundary woke every registered party at the
next business day; applicable from the first crossing.

**Budget**: a few crossings a business day; a large downgrade wakes 10000 registered parties at 10 ns each (K-46's
`wake_entry_ns`).
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0.01 / 0 / 0.01 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (inside S1.239's thresholds: the referring rules' 500000 of its 600000
  entries × 8 B, stated by S3.213, S3.216 and S3.217)

**Guards**: assembly refusals as above.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an unrated holding read as a grade; a boundary crossing reaching holders at different days.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-81's wake part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.213 — Funds' mandates refer to ratings

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: RAT.4 PROCESS *(part: fund mandates)*
**Architecture**: §6 (stage 5c); §7.7 (phx-agenda: K-46 thresholds); §7.14 (phx-risk: K-93 mandate limits)
**Depends on**: S3.212 (the reference and the wake); S3.182 (funds' mandates as K-93 limit kinds); S3.191 (managers'
orders); S3.207 (ratings)
**Goal**: a fund's mandate names a minimum rating per holding class; a downgrade below it is a breach the fund cures
by its own sales within the mandate's cure period.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/mandate_rating.rs` | the breach review: sales within the cure period by S3.191's orders |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | each mandate's `RatingReference` (scale, minimum, unrated row, cure period) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/mandate_rating.rs` | logic-level tests |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/fnd.rs` | LC-3-81 (cure part) |

**Design**:
- **Registration**: a mandated fund registers a K-46 threshold at its mandate's minimum on each rated holding when it
  buys it, and releases it when it sells (5d apply phases).
- **Breach** (decider: the fund's portfolio manager): woken the next business day, the manager's review places the
  breached holding among its sales: S3.191's orders over the cure period, each limited at its own value (MKT.16);
  unsold at the period's end is a recorded breach (K-37, audience the fund's holders and supervisor). An unrated
  holding follows the mandate's declared row.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E6 — thresholds rebuilt at load (`mandate_thresholds_rebuilt_equal`). E10 — an issuer ended: its
holding ceases and the threshold is swept by K-46 (`ended_issuer_threshold_swept`). E13 — an unrated holding by the
mandate's declared row (`unrated_holding_by_mandate_row`). E14 — a fund crossed on two holdings the same day reviews
once (`one_breach_review_a_day`).

**Extension points**: the breach review is converted by S8.181.

**Unit tests**: `breach_sales_within_cure_period`; `unsold_at_period_end_recorded`; `mandate_thresholds_rebuilt_equal`;
`ended_issuer_threshold_swept`; `unrated_holding_by_mandate_row`; `one_breach_review_a_day`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-81 (cure part) — each mandated breach was cured within its period or recorded; applicable from
the first breach.

**Budget**: 5000 rated holdings bought or sold by mandated funds a business day, each a registration of 60 ns.

- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (inside S1.239's thresholds: 445000 of its 600000 entries × 8 B)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

(phx-hold: K-65 holder lists)
**Depends on**: S3.209 (reports); S3.211 (estimates and guidance: what each report is a surprise against); S1.336
(outlooks formed once per new release; surprises per method and party); S1.350 (a surprise raising attention); S1.280
(holders of the issuer's instruments); S3.148 (registered candidates and their value rule); S3.212, S3.213–S3.217
(the references every scale must have, and the downgrade loop's links)
**Goal**: a report settles every expectation standing against it: each holder's and candidate's surprise revises its
own outlook and wakes its review, so its value and its orders change and prices move because schedules moved; no
rating, report or surprise reaches a price otherwise; no scale exists that nothing refers to; the downgrade loop and
the price response to surprises are read and reported.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/rules/settle.rs` | RAT.5: the report as an observation of the earnings series; the wake set |
| `crates/systems/sys-rat/src/refer.rs` | RAT.7: assembly refuses an agency scale no `RatingReference` reads |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/route/rat.rs` | wakes at 9d for the next day's 5a outlooks and 5c reviews |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/rat.rs` | LC-3-13; LC-3-50 (response part); LC-3-42 (reference part) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc153.rs` | PC-153: no rule maps a rating, report or surprise straight into a price or an order limit |

**Design**:
- **Observation** (RAT.5): a report published at 9d is the next observation of the firm's earnings series (K-92); at
  the next day's 5a every method's outlook of it is formed once and its surprise (observed − expected, VAL.4)
  computed per method; each party's own deviation catches up when it reads.
- **Wake**: one walk of the firm's holder lists (K-65) and its registered candidates (S3.148's registration instance)
  raises the attention (REP.35) of those whose stake × surprise exceeds their review cost (REP.18); their reviews come
  due (K-43), their values (S3.148, S3.134) read the revised outlooks, and their orders change. Prices move because
  schedules moved.
- **Forbids** (RAT.7): no rating from a price (PC-57, S3.207); no rating nothing refers to — assembly refuses a scale
  that no `RatingReference` of S3.213–S3.217 or later reads; no estimate from the share price or the model's
  forecast (S3.211); no price-reaction rule (PC-153: a rating, report or surprise reaches a price only through a
  party's value and its order); no reported number the books do not produce (S3.209).
- **Measures** (RAT.6): the downgrade loop — a rating crossing a boundary, mandated sales, capital pressure, dearer
  funding, weaker published state, a further downgrade — searched in the run's events step by step (L7); price moves
  against the size of report surprises; the dispersion of estimates after volatile results. Reported, never enforced.
- Streams: none.

**Edge cases**: E1 — a report of a firm with many holders: one holder-list walk, only those over their review cost
woken (`surprise_wakes_only_over_review_cost`). E5 — the season's busiest day, 300 reports (timed by the bench's
`reporting_peak` day; LC-3-50). E11 — a firm's first report after the opening: surprise against the snapshot's outlook
(`first_surprise_against_snapshot`). E12 — no estimate or guidance standing: the surprise is against each party's own
outlook only (`surprise_against_own_outlook`). E13 — a scale nothing reads is refused (`unreferenced_scale_refused`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `report_is_observation_of_series`; `surprise_wakes_only_over_review_cost`;
`first_surprise_against_snapshot`; `surprise_against_own_outlook`; `unreferenced_scale_refused`;
`no_price_written_by_report`.

**Live checks**: LC-3-50 (response part) — after each report whose surprise woke holders and candidates, the orders
those parties posted changed with their revised values, and the price move is traceable to those orders in events;
LC-3-13 — RAT.6: the downgrade loop traceable step by step wherever it occurs; price moves against surprise size and
estimates' dispersion after volatile results reported; LC-3-42 (reference part) — every scale is read by a rule;
applicable from the first report (the loop: not until the run has one).

**Budget**: 37 reports a mean business day over 1000 holder rows each at `fin.holdings.holder_ns`, 5 in a hundred
rows woken; 300 reports on the season's busiest day.
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (B / NB / H)
- adds 1850 / 0 / 1850 items to fin.decide.attend_ns (the woken holders' and candidates' attention decisions)
- on fin.calendar.reporting_peak (the windows' busiest day, from the declared deadlines): 2.3 core-ms and 15000
  attention decisions; joins B′ (a deadline on a closed day rolls to the next business day)
- ledger: +0 B (wakes are K-43 agenda entries within S1.227's line)

**Guards**: PC-153 (above); assembly's refusal of an unreferenced scale.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a price-reaction rule; a surprise shared by all parties; a rating nothing refers to.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fast checks pass; PC-153 registered; the bench at the committed resolution within
  `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] LC-3-13, LC-3-50's response part and LC-3-42's reference part registered.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S3.219 — The Stage 3 gate

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: gate
**Clauses**: BNK.13 MEASURE; REP.18 PRIMITIVE *(part: Stage 3's RESOLUTION settings, taste distributions and review costs declared and measured)*
**Architecture**: §13 (the budget restated with the stage's measured lines), §14 (the bench's gate run).
**Depends on**: every step S3.100–S3.218; S3.100 (the macro reads it reads);
S2.216 (the Stage 2 gate, and BNK.13's other parts); S1.358 (the recorder, K-106: the run's macro series);
S1.494–S1.497 (the estimators, verdicts and chain relationships)
**Goal**: the Stage 3 exit and the budget are judged by §2.24's gate on the gate run: the policy rate reaches loan
rates, asset prices and investment through markets; a margin spiral and a fund run can happen.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/stage3.rs` | LC-3-14, LC-3-44, LC-3-45, LC-3-46, LC-3-47; LC-2-51 (pass-through part) |
| `perf/bench/<commit>-committed-gate.json` | the gate run's report, kept (`-k`) |
| `perf/reads/S3.219-*.json` | the macro reads from the run |
| data series | `markets/gz_ebp` (the excess bond premium, for the credit-spread read's relationship); `markets/CM.MKT.TRNR` (turnover, for the depth read) |

**Design**:
- **§2.24** governs the run, the pass criteria, a miss, Done when and Not allowed; this step adds only Stage 3's own.
- **Stage 3's heavy days**, each named and its time read from the run and composed on the calendar turn it can fall in:
  - the busiest record day, the dividend and meeting season's peak: the fused holder walk over 162000 holder rows
    (`fin.calendar.record_peak`);
  - the reporting season's busiest day (`fin.calendar.reporting_peak`);
  - an index rebalance's effective day, crowded closing calls (`fin.calendar.index_rebalance`);
  - auction days and the money market's month-end;
  - the event days, each composed on the worst turn it can join as §2.24 judges it: a crash day, every mark
    moving, requirements and calls over every account, close-outs, only crossed thresholds waking
    (`fin.calendar.crash_day`); a fund-run day, redemptions beyond buffers, gates and forced sales
    (`fin.calendar.fund_run`).
- **Stage 3's macro reads**: as S3.100 froze them in `data/observer/READS.toml`; this step reads them and never writes
  them.
- **BNK.13** (LC-2-51's pass-through part): on each of the committee's own rate changes in the run (S3.111), loan
  quotes' pass-through of it per bank — incomplete and lagged — read from the run's records; with S2.216's declines,
  standards and binding constraints, BNK.13 is complete.
- **L4** (the cost of capital): on each rate change the chain from the decision to overnight prints, banks' marginal
  cost of funds, loan quotes, the curve and investors' values, firms' marginal cost of money, investment, output and
  employment is traced with its lags (LC-3-14, LC-3-46).
- **L2** (the forced seller): the run's events are searched for forced sales by door — a margin call unmet, a
  redemption beyond a buffer, a funding line withdrawn or a repo defaulted, a mandate boundary crossed, a capital
  requirement met by shrinking, an estate's liquidation — each with its sale's prints and the holders its price
  reached (LC-3-44).
- **The exit** (LC-3-45): a margin spiral (calls, close-out sales, a price fall, wider requirements, further calls at
  other accounts) and a fund run (redemptions, forced sales, a fall in value, further redemptions) each appear as a
  traceable chain; until the run has one, each is listed as not yet seen with the run's length, its trigger and
  consequence shown by S3.179's, S3.180's and S3.192's unit tests; it never blocks (Appendix E 39) and nothing is
  tuned to produce it (N7). One whose conditions the run met without the chain forming is a finding against the
  mechanisms suspected (brokers' margin, funds' dealing terms, investors' flow responses).
- **The chains**: L2 and L4 are read here for their liveness; Part L's chains are not requirements and have no rows
  (their tests are N4's).
- **N2 and N8** are judged again on the gate run (the liveness counts of LC-3-47; the budget by §2.24).
- **Placeholders**: every placeholder Stage 3 retires is gone (the group tables of S3.100–S3.144 and of S3.145–S3.219);
  every remaining one names a later step.
- **Not applicable in Stage 3**: none of the stage's mechanisms; an event the run has not had is listed with the run's
  length.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1, E5: the heavy days above, measured and named in the report: `LC-3-47` and the gate's report.
- E6: a save and load mid-run restores every base, including T+n trades pending, open recalls and margin calls, gate
  queues and deferred redemptions, capital calls due, announced index changes, pending conversions and dividends
  between record and payment days, with every index rebuilt and the hash equal: §2.24's mid-run save, LC-0-35 and LC-0-36.
- E9: every store's growth over the two years within its declared capacity (SET.12–SET.16): the instruments register
  with paper rolled every few weeks (issues against retirements), ratings, reports, fixings and estimates within their
  horizons, fund estates open (E4) counted: `LC-3-47`.

**Extension points**: none.
**Unit tests**: none.
**Live checks**: `LC-3-14`: on each of the committee's rate changes in the run, the chain from the decision to
investment is traceable, with lags (not applicable until the run has a rate change); `LC-3-44`: L2 — every forced sale
names its door, its prints and the holders its price reached; `LC-3-45`: the exit — a margin spiral and a fund run
each exist as traceable chains, or are listed as not yet seen with the run's length; `LC-3-46`: L4's links are live,
as a trace — after each rate change every link's decision names the input it read from the link before (banks'
`fund_position` the corridor, their marginal cost of funds the overnight prints, loan quotes that cost, investors'
values the curve, firms' investment reviews their marginal cost of money; after a bank changes its dealers' limits,
the desks' quotes name the limits they read); `LC-3-47`: N2 over the run — the counts per year of auctions,
money-market matches, issues, trades per book, dealer requests, fund dealings, securities loans, margin calls, rating
changes and reports, a kind with none listed with the run's length and a finding only where its conditions occurred
without it; `LC-2-51` (pass-through part): BNK.13's pass-through of each rate change to loan quotes per bank, with
its lag.
**Budget**:
- this is the budget's gate: §2.24's day types and turns at the committed resolution and at the design point, with
  the heavy days above; ARCHITECTURE §13 restated with the stage's measured lines
**Guards**: none new.
**Not allowed**: as §2.24.
**Done when**:
- [ ] §2.24's Done when, with Stage 3's heavy days measured and LC-3-14, LC-3-44 to LC-3-47 and LC-2-51's
  pass-through part passing or listed as not yet applicable with the run's length; every placeholder this stage
  retires gone.

## 6b. Stage 8 — Minds (built after Stage 3)

Built after Stage 3 and before Stage 4 (spec Part O); numbered 8 because identifiers are permanent. Every decision
already runs through the decision core (K-100, S1.348; MND.20), each naming its decider; this stage gives every person
a mind (K-102, S1.352) and turns each decision built so far into its **option generator**: the rule states the
options its mechanism generates and each option's consequences on the concerns its decision touches, from the
decider's own outlooks and values (VAL.8), and the decider's mind weighs them (MND.7). No decision moves: each is
rewritten in place, in its own system, by the step that converts it. Offices of firms and banks are held by persons
from Stage 3 (S3.156); this stage appoints the offices below the board, lets boards remove chief executives, and turns
an institution's consequences into its holder's own through the holder's contracts. Offices the government fills
(a central bank's governor, supervisors' heads) stay empty until Stage 5 and decide at the founding preferences, now a
drawn character. The stages after this one write their decisions as option generators from the start.

**Order.** The macro reads frozen (S8.100); characters, the mind's hand-over, aspirations and the household as one
(S8.101–S8.106); households' and persons' decisions (S8.107–S8.120) and the life record's event entries (S8.121);
offices (S8.122–S8.127); the decisions taken in offices, one decision cluster a step — one crate, one decider, one
occasion (S8.128–S8.196); minds that change with life (S8.197, S8.198, S8.200) and the reason recorded with the
biography's hand-off (S8.199); the guard (S8.201); the gate (S8.202). The table below names every decision point
Stages 1–3 declare and the step that converts it; S8.201 refuses any left in rule form but the ones Stage 5 converts.

**Exit** (Part O): two persons in the same position decide differently, and a change of chief executive changes the
firm's decisions; the stages after it build their decisions on the mind.

**The API every step uses** (K-100 and K-102, ARCHITECTURE §7.16): concerns are `ConcernH` handles compiled from
`MND.concerns`; a decision kind is declared in `MND.decisions { name, taken_in, concerns, mode }` and compiled to a
`DecisionH`; its generator is `fn options(view: &<Decision>View, out: &mut OptionSet)`, pushing each option (key u32)
with its `Consequences` (one `Fixed` per declared concern) until the set, sized at the decider's attention, is full;
the core calls `choose` (`Mode::Best`, with the decider's tastes, REP.22) or `satisfice` (`Mode::Satisfice`, options
in arrival order) with the decider's `MindView`, and the `Choice` carries its `tipping: ConcernH`. A household's
choice is `choose_household` over its adults' views and weights. An office's consequences pass the mandate hook
(S8.122). A weighing costs, per option, concerns × `term_ns` 2 + `option_fixed_ns` 3 (`fin.decide.mind_ns`, S1.352).
No rule reads a mind; no mind reads another's private state.

### S8.101 — Character types by country from the preference survey

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: data

**Clauses**: MND.19 PRIMITIVE *(part: the character types' procedure and its inputs)*
**Architecture**: §10 (the opening's derived values), §7.16 (K-102's type table)

**Depends on**: S8.100 (the reads frozen first), S1.352 (K-102: the type table a mind's character indexes), S1.404
(the opening's persons and the country profile the household types already read), S1.179 (K-20: register handles)

**Goal**: the declared procedure that simulates each country's character types from its Global Preferences Survey
profile has every input in the register with its source: the country means, the within-country spread and the traits'
correlations, the map from traits to patience and risk aversion, and the concern weights' loadings.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | `MND.gps_within` (per trait: within-country variance), `MND.gps_correlation` (6 × 6), `MND.patience_map`, `MND.risk_map`, `MND.concern_loadings` (8 × 6), `MND.types_per_country` (RESOLUTION) — each with kind, unit, owner and source |
| `tools/data/derive_mnd.py` | the within-country variances from the country means; writes the derived rows with their sources |
| `data/inventory.toml` | rows `MND.gps_within`, `MND.gps_correlation`: derived, first read S8.102 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the procedure's form (a multivariate normal per country discretised into equal-share types) with its reason |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §10 | the procedure's inputs and where each comes from |

**Design**:
- **Inputs in hand**: `people/gps_country` — 76 economies' means of patience, risk taking, positive and negative
  reciprocity, altruism and trust, in standard deviations of the world's individual-level distribution. A country of
  the game reads its six means as the opening's profile gives them (the named country's row, or its level's derived
  values, as S1.404 reads `GEN.risk_aversion_location`).
- **Within-country variance** (derived): the survey's world individual distribution has unit variance per trait, so
  the within-country variance of trait t is `1 − Var_c(μ_{c,t})` over the 76 economies (unweighted, as the survey's
  world standardisation is). Written by `derive_mnd.py`, never typed.
- **Correlations**: the six traits' pairwise individual-level correlations, taken from the survey paper's table (Falk,
  Becker, Dohmen, Enke, Huffman and Sunde, QJE 2018); `MND.gps_correlation` with its table reference.
- **Traits to parameters** (PREFERENCE, sources in the entries): yearly patience `β = β̄ + s_β · z_patience` and
  relative risk aversion `ρ = ρ̄ · exp(−s_ρ · z_risk)`, with `β̄`, `ρ̄` the baselines already registered
  (`HH.patience` 0.96, `HH.risk_aversion` 2; Carroll 1997) placed at the world mean, and `s_β`, `s_ρ` the experimental
  measures' spread per standard deviation of the survey item from the module's validation (Falk et al., Management
  Science 2023). The other four traits are carried as their standardised values `z`, read by the concerns that declare
  them.
- **Concern weights**: `w_c = exp(Σ_t L[c, t] · z_t) / Σ_c' exp(Σ_t L[c', t] · z_t)` over MND.2's eight concerns; `L`
  holds a non-zero loading only where the survey paper's table of individual-level correlates reports one for a
  concern's outcome (patience with savings and education → wealth and legacy; risk taking with self-employment →
  −security; altruism and positive reciprocity with giving and helping → family, principle; trust with civic
  participation → principle); every other entry is 0 with the reason "no published correlate".
- **Number of types** `MND.types_per_country` is RESOLUTION (NUM.4), the valve's second setting (E 41).
- No draw is made here: the types are drawn at the opening by S8.102's rule.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a country whose profile has no GPS mean for a trait — refused at assembly with the country and trait; never a
  mean of 0 (`missing_trait_refused`).
- E8: `Var_c(μ)` ≥ 1 for a trait (within variance ≤ 0) — refused by `derive_mnd.py` and at assembly as a data defect
  (`within_variance_positive`).
- E13: a level with one economy — its means read directly; the within variance is the world's
  (`single_economy_level`).

**Extension points**: S8.102 reads every entry; S8.105 (aspiration speed), S8.197 (MND.14 age profiles) and S8.198
(goal menu) add their primitives beside these; migration (S5.183) reads the types of the country of birth.

**Unit tests**: `within_variance_from_means` (a three-economy table, exact); `within_variance_positive`;
`correlation_matrix_is_valid` (symmetric, unit diagonal, positive definite, refusal otherwise);
`concern_weights_sum_to_one`; `missing_trait_refused`; `single_economy_level`; `zero_loading_carries_reason`.

**Live checks**: none (LC-8-01 at S8.102).

**Budget**:
- none on the day: the derivation runs in `tools/data`, never in the world.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (the type table is S8.102's).

**Guards**: PC-90/PC-91 (every entry sourced; a derived row names its script).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a new fetch (the data are in hand); a loading chosen to make a result look right; a trait's spread
typed rather than derived

**Done when**:
- [ ] `derive_mnd.py`, the register entries, the inventory rows and the SHAPE entry written; unit tests pass; the fast
  checks pass.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §10 states the procedure's inputs.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S8.102 — Characters drawn at birth, arrival and the opening

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.1 STATE; MND.19 PRIMITIVE *(part: the types drawn)*
**Architecture**: §7.16 (K-102), §10 (the opening), §6 (stage 3b)

**Depends on**: S8.101 (the procedure's inputs), S1.352 (K-102: the character field and type table), S1.207 (K-33:
persons), S1.235 (K-44: births as hazard outcomes), S1.404 (the opening's persons), S1.176 (K-18: streams)

**Goal**: each country's character types are drawn once at the new game from its declared distribution, and every
person holds its own type, drawn once at its birth or arrival from its country's table — at the opening for the
opening's persons — independently of its parents'.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/lib.rs` | the `sys-mnd` system: declarations (streams, the type table's shape) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/rules/character.rs` | `draw_types(means, within, corr, maps, loadings, k, draws) -> TypeTable`; `draw_type(table, u) -> TypeIx` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/opening/minds.rs` | route: types per country at the new game, then a type per opening person |
| `crates/assembly/phx-world/src/day/population.rs` | route: a born person's type in 3b's outcome apply |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/lc_8_01.rs` | LC-8-01 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/mind_character.rs` | PC-160: `MND.character` read only in `sys-mnd` |

**Design**:
- **Types** (at the new game, once per country): K = `MND.types_per_country` draws `z_k ~ N(μ_c, Σ_w)` (Σ_w from the
  within variances and correlations; Cholesky in the pure rule) on the setup stream `MND.types` (subject: the
  country), each type's share `1/K`; each type row holds `β`, `ρ`, the four other traits' `z`, and the eight concern
  weights as `Fixed` (≈ 60 B a type; K × 3 countries). Written into K-102's type table; saved as state (SET.12).
- **A person's type**: one uniform from `MND.character` (subject: the person's identity, day of its birth or arrival)
  picks a type by the shares (cumulative search over K). Written into the person's character field (12 bits of K-102's
  mind, S1.352) by the outcome apply of stage 3b for births, and by the opening for every opening person. The draw
  names the person, never a parent, so it is independent of its parents' (MND.1).
- **Country**: a birth draws from the table of the country it is born in; an arrival (migration, Stage 5) keeps the
  type it holds — the migration step calls nothing here. An arrival new to the world (a first entry) draws from its
  country of origin's table, which S5.183's migration supplies through `draw_type`.
- **Children** hold a character from birth; the rest of their mind (traces, aspirations, goals, strategy records)
  starts at coming of age (S8.105, S8.197–S8.200).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe day's many deaths — nothing to do; the field is released with the slot (K-02)
  (`slot_reuse_rewrites_type`).
- E6: types and characters are state, saved; a load reads them, nothing is redrawn (`type_table_round_trip`).
- E7: a draw's address is (stream, person, day), so any worker count gives the same type
  (`draw_independent_of_order`).
- E8: K ≤ 2¹² types (the field's 12 bits); refused above at assembly (`type_count_refused_above_field`).
- E10: a slot reused after a death — the new person's type is written at its birth, never inherited from the slot
  (`slot_reuse_rewrites_type`).
- E11: day zero — every opening person holds a type before the first decision (LC-8-01).

**Extension points**: `draw_type` is S5.183's for first entries (migration); K-102's character field is read by S8.103's
`MindView`.

**Unit tests**: `type_shares_equal`; `draw_type_by_cumulative` (exact boundaries); `types_reproduce_moments` (a
fixture of 10⁵ draws of the pure rule: means and correlations within the draws' own sampling error, derived);
`draw_independent_of_parent` (the address holds no parent); `draw_independent_of_order`; `type_table_round_trip`;
`slot_reuse_rewrites_type`; `type_count_refused_above_field`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-8-01`: MND.1 — every living person holds a type of its country's table (its country of birth or its origin's);
  each country's shares of persons by type against `1/K`, within the sampling error of its persons' count; from day 0.

**Budget**:
- adds 50 phone-ns to `fin.hazards.hit_ns` at 330 / 330 / 330 items (births' type draws, stage 3b).
- the opening's 7.5 M draws ≈ 0.4 core-s, outside the turn.
- ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B (core attribute: the type's 12 bits of K-102's mind, S1.352).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.01 MB resident (K × 3 countries × 60 B type rows).

**Guards**: PC-160 — `phx-check` refuses a read of the stream `MND.character` outside `sys-mnd` and a write of the
character field outside 3b's outcome apply and the opening (one writer).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a type inherited from a parent; a type redrawn during a life; a common mind (MND.18)

**Done when**:
- [ ] `sys-mnd`, the rules, the routes and unit tests written; the fast checks pass.
- [ ] LC-8-01 registered and passing on the bench's 20-day run.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml` (the opening's span for minds
  reported).
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.16 (K-102's users) and §10 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
