### S8.124 — A board chooses, reviews and removes its chief executive by its members' minds

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PTY.17 PROCESS *(part: a chief executive by its board)*; MND.9 DECISION *(part: found out and removed)*
**Architecture**: §7.16 (offices), §7.6 (K-40 reads)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate for the board's members), S8.121 (the life-record entries candidates' records
hold), S8.117 (a candidate's own acceptance), S3.156 (boards and chief executives appointed, `FRM.appoint_executive`),
S2.108 (the published filing that wakes a review), S1.209 (K-34), S1.257 (K-53), S1.304 (K-72: the office's posted
vacancy), S1.321 (K-82: candidates meet it), S1.223 (K-40: `prefetch`), S1.224 (K-41: the board's tally)

**Goal**: a board reviews its chief executive when the firm's accounts are published, and when the office is vacant
chooses among the eligible persons it meets — interviewing those worth the hours and reading their records — by its
members' own minds and its constitution's majority, so a holder that favours itself against its mandate may be found
out and removed, and a new one changes what the firm does.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/appoint.rs` | generators: `interview` (interview or pass a met candidate), `appoint` (each interviewed candidate with pay on the trade's points, or leave vacant and search on), `review` (keep or remove) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.appoint_executive` moved to the option-generator path; `FRM.interview` and `FRM.review_executive` added |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/declare.rs` | the board's meeting interval per legal form, each board's meeting days counted from its firm's founding day |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | board meeting intervals (POLICY of company law); interview hours (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | `FRM.interview` (`mode = "satisfice"`), `FRM.appoint_executive`, `FRM.review_executive` (`mode = "best"`) with their concerns |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/live/mnd.rs` | LC-8-05, LC-8-06 |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | S3.156's selection form restated |

**Design**:
- **Review**: the firm's published filing (S2.108) wakes a review at the board's next meeting day (its constitution's
  interval from its founding day), so reviews spread as meeting days do. Options keep or remove; each member weighs
  the published results against its own expectation; the constitution's majority (K-41) decides.
- **Candidates** (PTY.17's eligible set): the persons its form admits who meet the posted vacancy (K-72, K-82) and
  those the members know (a shared employment or kin contract on either chain), in the order met, until the chair's
  attention is full (MND.7).
- **Interview** (satisfice, the chair's office): each met candidate is weighed on what its current state shows —
  skills, its employment history in its jobs' start dates, its current contracts and offices, its public reputation
  (K-37) — against the interview's hours at the chair's own value of an hour (Law 14); those interviewed have their
  life records prefetched (K-40 `prefetch(persons, into)` at the day's apply, read at the next 5c: an appointment
  takes time). The number interviewed is an outcome.
- **Appoint** (best, each member weighs, the majority decides): each interviewed candidate at the pay points it can
  offer against other institutions bidding, or leaving the office vacant and searching on; the offer is an appointment
  (K-80) the candidate answers with its own mind (S8.117).
- **Consequences** for the institution (then the chooser's own through S8.122):
    - `means`: expected results under the candidate (the results of what its record shows it led, K-37) less its pay;
    - `security`: the chance its record's losses recur;
    - `standing`: the institution's rank under it.
- **Removal** ends the appointment, paying what it owes, and vacates the office; the office is empty only while
  filling runs, its decisions meanwhile read the founding view (S8.104).
- **A declared alternative, not built**: a per-person career column (offices held, years in the occupation family; +2
  B × 5.5 M persons ≈ 11 MB on ledger line 2) would make the records' reads about 0; it is taken only if, at the
  core's close (S1.360), the time sum binds harder than memory.
- The Stage 3 selection form is deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no candidate — the office stays vacant and posted; the founding view decides; the vacancy's age is reported
  (`no_candidate_stays_posted`, LC-8-05).
- E10: a candidate or member who died — its application lapsed (K-45); the board votes with those seated
  (`board_votes_with_seated`).
- E14: a removal and a resignation the same day — one vacancy (`one_vacancy_same_day`).
- E5: the busiest filing day — its reviews fall on the boards' own meeting days after it
  (`review_on_next_meeting_day`).

**Extension points**: fund managers' offices (S8.181) and dealers' desks (S8.187) use the generators as declared
offices.

**Unit tests**: `candidates_include_known_and_met`; `interview_weighs_hours`; `records_read_only_for_interviewed`;
`removal_vacates`; `constitution_majority_counts`; `no_candidate_stays_posted`; `board_votes_with_seated`;
`one_vacancy_same_day`; `review_on_next_meeting_day`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-8-05`: PTY.16 (part), PTY.18 (part) — no office of a firm or bank vacant beyond its filling (a posted vacancy
  with meetings running); vacancies' ages published; from the first appointment.
- `LC-8-06`: MND.9, MND.17 (part) — after each change of chief executive, the firm's investment, leverage and payout
  over the next year against the year before, published per firm; from the first change.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.institutions`: 12 / 0 / 12 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 1.8 k board reviews a business day × ≈ 1
  000 phone-ns: ≈ 7 members × 2 options × (3 concerns × 2 + 3) and the results read; ≈ 260 appointments a business day
  × ≈ 6 candidates met, ≈ 3 interviewed × 7 members; ≈ 780 interviewed candidates' records prefetched a business day ×
  ≈ 10 µs expected decode, ≈ 10 frames — `prefetch_record_us` 85 is the worst — carried by the reader, S1.223).
- spread after `fin.calendar.filing_window_end` over 21 days: 3 core-ms a day on `fin.fixed.institutions` (≈ 50 k
  filings reviewed at each board's next meeting day, its constitution's interval).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (core attribute: K-53's appointment rows).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an appointment or removal drawn (PTY.18) or by a fixed rule on results; a declared shortlist size;
a chooser reading a candidate's private state beyond its record and reputation

**Done when**:
- [ ] The generators and their unit tests written; the rule forms they replace deleted; the fast checks (`fmt`,
  `clippy`, tests, `phx-check`) pass.
- [ ] LC-8-05 and LC-8-06 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml` (`tools/bench.sh`).
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

**Status**: planned

*(part: line heads, loan officers)*

### S8.127 — Owners vote on board seats and resolutions by their own minds

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: EQY.5's votes)*; PTY.17 PROCESS *(part: a board by its owners' votes)*
**Architecture**: §7.16 (offices), §7.10 (holdings)

**Depends on**: S8.126 (the nominees and the notice), S8.122 (the mandate, for an institution voting its holding),
S3.155 (owners' meetings and votes, the voting-cost comparison), S1.281 (the instrument events engine's one holder
walk), S1.280 (K-65: holders of record), S1.224 (K-41: tallies)

**Goal**: an owner's vote on each resolution — a seat's nominees, a distribution, an authority to issue or buy back —
is its own weighing of what each outcome is worth to its holding, taken by the holders whose stake makes voting worth
their hours, and the tally by holding decides, so who sits on a board and what it may do are outcomes of owners'
minds.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/rules/vote.rs` | `options(view: &VoteView, out)`: for, against, abstain; for a seat each nominee or abstain |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/points.rs` | the S3.155 vote moved to the option-generator path |
| `crates/systems/sys-eqy/src/decl.rs` | each resolution kind's value per (proposal, outlook method), computed once per meeting |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the vote form restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: the meeting's record day, in S1.281's one holder walk (the same walk as the dividend legs); 9d.
- **Turnout**: S3.155's comparison, a holder's stake × the change the resolution brings to its own value against its
  voting hours at its own value of an hour, is taken first on each row; only the holders past it weigh (≈ 5 % of
  rows).
- **Values**: each resolution's value per (proposal, outlook method) is computed once per meeting — for a seat, the
  firm's value under each nominee's published summary (S8.126); for a distribution, paid now against retained at the
  method's required return — and handed to every voter's view; no holder reads a record of its own.
- **Consequences**:
    - `wealth_and_legacy`: its holding × the value change under each outcome;
    - `means`: the dividends it expects;
    - `principle`: a nominee's declared stance, where its concern is declared.
- A person votes its own holding, a household by its adults (S8.106), an institution through its investment office
  (the mandate applies, S8.122), an estate through its administrator (S8.196). The tally (K-41) by holding decides by
  the constitution's majority; no outcome is drawn (PTY.18).
- The Stage 3 form is deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a holder with a tiny holding — its stake rarely clears its voting hours; when it does it votes like any other
  (`turnout_by_stake_and_hours`).
- E10: a holder ended before the record day — its estate votes through its administrator, or not at all as the law
  declares (`estate_votes_through_administrator`).
- E13: a resolution with no votes cast — fails by S3.155's rule (`no_votes_fails`).
- E5: the meeting season's record days — the voters' work rides the one walk (`votes_ride_holder_walk`).

**Extension points**: takeover votes (S4.174) reuse the generator's form.

**Unit tests**: `votes_by_holding`; `abstain_offered`; `turnout_by_stake_and_hours`; `values_once_per_method`;
`estate_votes_through_administrator`; `no_votes_fails`; `votes_ride_holder_walk`; `no_outcome_drawn` (compile: no
stream in the tally).

**Live checks**: none (LC-3-65 and LC-8-06 read the results).

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.holder_rows: 0 / 0 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H), inside S1.281's walk (≈ 75 k voters past the turnout comparison × 3 options × (3 concerns × 2 + 3) =
  27 phone-ns).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (core attribute: the values are K-03's day buffer).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a vote drawn or fixed by holding size alone; a separate pass over holder rows; the Stage 3 form kept

**Done when**:
- [ ] The generators and their unit tests written; the rule forms they replace deleted; the fast checks (`fmt`,
  `clippy`, tests, `phx-check`) pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml` (`tools/bench.sh`).

### S8.128 — A line head's prices by its own mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.day_zero_price, FRM.review_price, FRM.reprice)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stages 5b, 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate), S8.125 (line heads hold their offices), S1.450 (price reviews and moves),
S1.491 (day zero's opening decisions), S2.204 (retail energy tariffs posted through the price review), S2.205 (retail tariffs posted and repriced)

**Goal**: which price point a line posts, at day zero and at each review, is its head's weighing of each point's
consequences for the line through the mandate, so firms alike in costs but led by different minds price differently;
the rule's outlook arithmetic is unchanged.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/review.rs` | `review` and `reprice` become `options(view: &PriceView, out)`: price points from the current one outward, each with its expected profit, rank and stock risk |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/price.rs` | the pressure rule's expected sales per point kept as the consequence arithmetic |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.review_price`, `FRM.reprice`, `FRM.day_zero_price` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | the three decisions' concerns `[means, standing, security]`, `mode = "best"` |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: S1.450's review occasions (attention, REP.38; a surprise, REP.35), 5c; day zero's first posting (S1.491,
  GEN.13).
- **Options**: the trade's price points (REP.34) from the current point outward, as many as the head's attention
  allows (MND.7); keep is the current point.
- **Consequences** for the line (then the head's own through S8.122):
    - `means`: expected profit over the review horizon at each point from its own sales outlook, the day's unit cost
    (K-35) and stock;
    - `standing`: its rank by sales in its market;
    - `security`: the chance of unsold or perishing stock (GDS.8) or of stocking out, from its own outlook.
- The management type in `Prefs` no longer sets the point; the markup's update stays the rule's arithmetic. The Stage 1
  argmax is deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a market with no print — its own value from the closest observed (VAL.10); a point whose expected sales are
  `Missing` is not offered (`missing_sales_not_offered`).
- E5: a surprise day — each review within its unit; the reviews spread by attention (REP.35) (`review_within_unit`).
- E11: day zero — prices from the opening's snapshot and the head's first weighing (`day_zero_weighs_snapshot`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `points_from_current_outward`; `profit_at_point`; `rank_counts_on_standing`;
`missing_sales_not_offered`; `review_within_unit`; `day_zero_weighs_snapshot`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 45 phone-ns to `fin.decide.review_ns` at 338 k / 165 k / 338 k items (≈ 5 points considered × (3 concerns ×
  `term_ns` 2 + 3)), within the 100 S1.450 leaves for the minds' weighing.
- on `fin.calendar.opening` (day zero, outside the turn): 52 core-ms (≈ 1.15 M first postings × 45 phone-ns); joins
  neither.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a markup set by a management type; the Stage 1 argmax kept

- [ ] `tools/bench.sh -F decide`: `fin.decide.review_ns` within 550 with the weighing.

### S8.129 — A line head's stance and attention by its own mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.stance, FRM.attention)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §8 (outlooks), §6 (stages 5b, 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.128 (the price review the stance rides), S1.453 (a firm's outlooks and stances), S1.451 (firms'
attention, and reviews paid in hours), S1.350 (K-101: attention)

**Goal**: which outlook heuristic a line's head uses and how often it reviews its price are its own weighing — the
stance on the firm's own performance record, the interval on the loss a stale price costs against the review's hours —
so switching and review timing are outcomes.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/stance.rs` | `stance_in` becomes `options(view: &FirmStanceView, out)`: each heuristic in the declared set |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/attention.rs` | `review_chance` becomes `options(view: &AttendView, out)`: the review intervals on the kind's points |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.stance`, `FRM.attention` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **Stance** (VAL.7, inside the review's reconsideration): options are the declared heuristics; `means` is each
  heuristic's record of forecast errors on the line's own sales and prices (its own record, S1.453), priced at the
  line's margin; `security` the error's spread. The switching form is the adults' form in S8.108, on the firm's
  record.
- **Attention** (REP.38, K-101): options are the review intervals on the kind's declared points; `means` is minus the
  expected loss from a stale price over the interval (its outlook's drift and surprise, REP.35) less the review's
  hours at the staff's wage and the menu cost (S1.451).
- The Stage 1 forms are deleted; K-101 reads the chosen interval as before.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a line with no record yet — every heuristic's record is `Missing`; the current stance stands
  (`missing_record_keeps_stance`).
- E5: a surprise day — attention redraws ride K-43's reschedules (`surprise_redraw_reschedules`).
- E11: day zero — each firm's opening stance from the snapshot's distribution (S1.453)
  (`opening_stance_from_snapshot`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `stance_by_own_record`; `stale_loss_against_hours`; `missing_record_keeps_stance`;
`surprise_redraw_reschedules`; `opening_stance_from_snapshot`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 28 phone-ns to `fin.decide.review_ns` at 11 k / 5 k / 11 k items (the reconsiderations, one review in thirty: ≈
  4 heuristics × (2 concerns × 2 + 3)), within the 100 S1.450 leaves.
- adds 15 phone-ns to `fin.decide.attend_ns` at 246 k / 0 / 246 k items (≈ 3 intervals × (1 concern × 2 + 3)), in
  place of `review_chance`'s comparison within S1.451's 120.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a switching probability; a review chance declared as a rate; the Stage 1 forms kept

### S8.130 — A line head's production, inputs and way by its own mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.produce, FRM.inputs, FRM.way)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5b)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate), S8.125 (line heads), S1.443 (production on the firm's schedule; the visit
unit's itemisation), S1.444 (input orders), S1.441 (which way to run), S1.289 (K-68: standing rates), S1.211 (K-35:
the day's unit cost)

**Goal**: how much a line plans to produce, what it orders of each input and which way it runs are its head's weighing
of each option's margin and risks through the mandate, inside the firm visit's unit.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/produce.rs` | `target` becomes `options(view: &ProduceView, out)`: planned rates on the line's rate steps |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/inputs.rs` | `orders` becomes `options(view: &InputsView, out)`: order quantities per input on its lot sizes |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/way.rs` | `cheapest` becomes `options(view: &WayView, out)`: the ways the plant supports |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | the points moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: the firm's schedule visit (K-43), 5b; the chosen rate becomes the line's standing rate (K-68) and its
  orders intents (5d).
- **Production** (FRM.4): rates from the current one outward on the line's rate steps, within capacity (K-67) and
  labour, as many as its attention allows; `means` — expected margin over the plan's horizon at expected prices less
  the financing of work in progress and stock at its marginal cost of money; `security` — the chance of unsold or
  perishing stock (GDS.8) times its cost.
- **Inputs** (GDS.5): for each input due, quantities on its lot sizes up to its value in use (VAL.8); `means` — use
  value less price and carrying cost; `security` — the chance of running short (a stopped line) times the margin lost.
- **Way** (FRM.6): the ways the plant supports; `means` — margin at the input and labour prices it faces. A line with
  one way has no option to weigh.
- The Stage 1 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: an input with no seller in reach — no option for it; the plan reads the shortfall (MKT.10)
  (`no_seller_no_input_option`).
- E13: a line with one supported way — not weighed (`single_way_not_weighed`).
- E14: a sale and a production realised on one holding the same day — K-68 realises before the visit reads
  (`realised_before_visit`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `rates_within_capacity`; `order_up_to_use_value`; `shortage_risk_counts`;
`way_margin_at_faced_prices`; `no_seller_no_input_option`; `single_way_not_weighed`; `realised_before_visit`.

**Live checks**: none.

  step.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

allocation per day; a production or order rule's argmax kept beside the generator

### S8.131 — Extraction and stockists by their heads' minds

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: GDS.extract, GDS.stock)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5b)

**Depends on**: S8.130 (the visit's weighing), S8.122 (the mandate), S1.447 (extraction on its schedule), S1.472
(stockists and merchants), S1.191 (K-29: deposits)

**Goal**: how fast an extractor draws down its deposit and what a stockist buys, holds or sells are their heads'
weighing of today's margin against the value of waiting, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/rules/extract.rs` | `extract` becomes `options(view: &ExtractView, out)`: extraction rates |
| `crates/systems/sys-gds/src/rules/stockist.rs` | `carries` becomes `options(view: &StockView, out)`: buy, hold or sell quantities on lot sizes |

**Design**:

  value of the units left for later at its own price outlook (depletion makes waiting real); `wealth_and_legacy` — the
  deposit's remaining value (K-29); `security` — its outlook's price-fall risk on what it sells now.

  less purchase, storage, spoilage and the money tied up at its marginal cost of funds; `security` — its outlook's

- E2: no buyer in reach — hold is the one option besides selling at the meeting's price (`hold_is_always_offered`).

**Goal**: whether a line ships goods between places, on which route and room, or holds or sells locally — as seller or

**Status**: planned

**Goal**: whether a line posts a vacancy and at what wage, or lays off and whom, is its head's weighing of each

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |

**Status**: planned

(collective bargaining, unions and strikes)

**Goal**: the terms an employer offers at a contract's review date, and its offers and answers to a union, are its
head's weighing of the wage bill against how hard the job is to fill and a quit's cost, through the mandate (LAB.17).

**Files**:

### S8.138 — Investment by the chief executive's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: CAP.invest, staged projects)*; CAP.3 DECISION; CAP.13 PRIMITIVE; FRM.2 STATE;
FRM.8 DECISION
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate), S8.124 (chief executives hold their offices), S1.458 (investment on its
occasion), S1.460 (how an investment is funded), S1.483 (retires its placeholder `FRM.required_return`), S2.131
(investment at the cost of money, projects drawn in stages; retires its placeholder `CAP.hurdle`), S2.118 (the
marginal sources' costs)

**Goal**: whether and what a firm invests — a project's size, way and staging, or waiting — is its chief executive's
weighing of the project's own value against what the money costs at the margin now, through the mandate, so the hurdle
a project must clear is the holder's own and no declared number.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/rules/invest.rs` | `invest` becomes `options(view: &InvestView, out)`: waiting, and each project (size, way, staging) with its funding cost; `cost_of_funds`, `waiting_multiple`, `annuity` kept as the consequence arithmetic |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/points.rs` | `CAP.invest` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/FRM.toml` | `FRM.required_return` (drawn at founding, S1.483) and `CAP.hurdle` (S2.131), both `placeholder:MND`, deleted; the horizon kept (the generator reads it as the decision's horizon) |
| `tools/data/derive_frm.py` | the `state/typed_hurdle_rates` mapping deleted; the horizon's mapping kept |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: S1.458's occasions (attention on the stake, a need); 5c.
- **Options**: waiting; each project the rule generates — expanding a line at each size step, the ways it knows,
  staged or at once — as many as the chief executive's attention allows, each with its funding at the marginal
  sources' costs (S2.118).
- **Consequences** for the firm (then the holder's own through S8.122):
    - `means`: the project's own value (VAL.8: the output it expects to sell over the plant's life at the prices it
    expects, less running costs) less what the money costs at the margin now, over the decision's horizon;
    - `security`: the chance demand falls short, from its outlook's width (uncertainty is a reason to wait, CAP.3),
    times the loss;
    - `wealth_and_legacy`: the firm's value;
    - `standing`: its size's rank (empire building, where the holder's contracts allow it).
- The management's hurdle is gone: a project is taken when it weighs best for the holder, loss aversion and the
  mandate included. The declared hurdle has stood as placeholders naming MND — `FRM.required_return`, drawn per firm
  at founding (S1.483) and read by S1.458, and `CAP.hurdle` (S2.131); this step retires both and completes CAP.3,
  CAP.13 as they now read (the hurdle is the deciding holder's own weighing, MND.7, MND.9; the horizon
  distributions PREFERENCE, read as the investment decision's horizon), FRM.2 and FRM.8 (whether to invest, which S1.460 left waiting on the hurdle). Staged projects'
  undrawn budgets stay S2.131's K-50 commitments.
- The Stage 1 and 2 rule forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no project fundable — waiting is the one option (`unfundable_only_waits`).
- E12: a product with no print — its value from the closest observed (VAL.10) or the project not offered
  (`missing_print_not_offered`).
- E11: the opening's firms — their first occasion at their first attention date (`first_occasion_at_attention`).

**Extension points**: a line's entry and a spin-off are S8.144's, valued by the same consequence arithmetic.

**Unit tests**: `waiting_offered`; `project_value_against_marginal_cost`; `uncertainty_favours_waiting`;
`no_declared_hurdle` (compile: the view has no hurdle field); `unfundable_only_waits`; `missing_print_not_offered`;
`first_occasion_at_attention`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 66 phone-ns to `fin.decide.visit_ns` at 5 k / 0 / 5 k items (the investment occasions: ≈ 6 options × (4
  concerns × 2 + 3)).
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a declared hurdle beside the holder's weighing; the Stage 1 and 2 rule forms kept

### S8.140 — Funding by the chief executive's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.finance, FRM.fund, the cash placed)*; FRM.9 DECISION
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate), S8.138 (the investment a funding follows), S2.118 (a firm's funding decision;
retires its placeholder `FRM.leverage_tolerance`), S1.460 (how an investment is funded, `FRM.fund`), S3.153 (shares
among the sources), S3.108 (cash placed, the surplus branch of `FRM.finance`); S3.189 (money funds among firms' cash placements); S3.131 (bonds and paper among a firm's funding sources)

**Goal**: how a firm funds itself — retained cash, trade credit, a line, a loan, a bond, paper or new shares — and
where it places a surplus, are its chief executive's weighing of each source's cost now against how close it takes the
firm to distress, through the mandate, so the leverage a firm tolerates is its holder's and no declared number.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/finance.rs` | `plan` becomes `options(view: &FinanceView, out)`: each source it can draw now, and for a surplus each placement; `need` kept as the occasion's reading |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/funding.rs` | shares among the sources as options, their cost read as before |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/fund.rs` | `fund` becomes `options(view: &FundView, out)`: own cash, borrow each amount on the lending round's points, or not invest |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.finance`, `FRM.fund` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | `FRM.leverage_tolerance`'s distributions deleted; the cash buffer kept (it dates the shortfall occasion) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the pecking order's entry deleted; the form restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: the `finance` slot's occasions (the financing review, a shortfall within the horizon, S2.118) and an
  investment's funding (S1.460); 5c.
- **Options**: each source it can draw now at its cost — retained cash; a line's undrawn part (K-53); each loan quote
  it holds (K-80); trade credit on its suppliers' terms; bonds and paper at the costs S3.131's reads give; new shares
  at the cost S3.152's reads give (the issue itself is S8.158's) — and, for a surplus, each placement S3.108 lists
  (deposits, money funds, repo).
- **Consequences** for the firm (then the holder's own through S8.122):
    - `means`: the source's cost over the horizon, or the placement's return;
    - `security`: the change in its chance of distress at the new leverage, from its own cash-flow outlook;
    - `wealth_and_legacy`: owners' dilution for shares.
- The pecking order is no longer declared: an order emerges from each holder's weighing. The leverage tolerance,
  `FRM.leverage_tolerance`, has stood since S2.118 as a placeholder naming MND; this step retires it and completes
  FRM.9 as it now reads (the office holder deciding weighs the risk of distress, MND.7, MND.9).
- The Stage 1, 2 and 3 rule forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no source open (no line, no quote, no market access) — not funding, and the shortfall's distress occasion
  follows (`no_source_leads_to_distress`).
- E10: a quote lapsed since it was given — not offered (`lapsed_quote_not_offered`).
- E3: a firm with a surplus and no placement open — it holds cash (`surplus_held_without_placement`).

**Extension points**: S4.116's derivative positions ride the same view.

**Unit tests**: `source_cost_against_distress`; `no_declared_tolerance` (compile: the view has no tolerance field);

### S8.141 — A firm in distress and its answer to a lender by the chief executive's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.distress, the firm's answer to a restructuring)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §9 (procedures), §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.140 (funding), S8.122 (the mandate), S2.121 (a firm in distress), S2.125 (a firm's answer to a
lender's offer)

**Goal**: what a firm does in distress — cut costs and staff, sell assets, draw lines, raise expensive money, ask
suppliers for time, negotiate with lenders — and whether it accepts a lender's restructuring are its chief executive's
weighing, action by action, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/distress.rs` | `choose` becomes `options(view: &DistressView, out)`: each action open to it, and doing nothing more |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/answer.rs` | `accept` becomes `options(view: &AnswerView, out)`: accept or refuse |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.distress`, `answer_restructuring` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the ordering by cost deleted; the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: S2.121's occasions (a notice, a failed payment, a shortfall within the horizon) and a lender's offer
  (K-80); 5c.
- **Options**: each action FRM.12 declares open to it ("seek a buyer" from S4.179) and doing nothing more; the chosen
  action is applied to the view and the firm weighs again among the rest, until doing nothing more weighs best.
- **Consequences**:
    - `means`: the cash each action raises against the value it gives up;
    - `security`: the change in its chance of default by the grace's date times the loss to the holder (its office and
    holding, through S8.122);
    - `standing`: a cut's effect on its rank.
- **Answer**: accept or refuse; `means` is the going-concern value under the new terms against its best other route
  (S2.125's reading).
- The Stage 2 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day — each firm's occasion at its notice's first review date (`review_at_notice_date`).
- E3: a firm with nothing to sell and no lender quoting — only the actions open remain (`only_open_actions_offered`).
- E14: a notice and an offer the same day — the offer is weighed in the same view (`offer_in_distress_view`).

**Extension points**: "seek a buyer" (S4.179) adds an option as data.

**Unit tests**: `action_by_action_until_none`; `default_risk_counts`; `review_at_notice_date`;
`only_open_actions_offered`; `offer_in_distress_view`.

**Live checks**: none.

### S8.142 — Procedures and plans by the debtor's and creditors' minds

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.open_procedure, FRM.propose_plan, FRM.vote_on_plan by a creditor firm)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §9 (procedures), §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.141 (distress), S8.122 (the mandate), S2.123 (insolvency procedures), S2.124 (the plan, the
creditors' votes by class and confirmation)

**Goal**: whether a debtor opens a procedure, the plan it proposes and a creditor firm's vote on it are their chief
executives' weighing through the mandate; a lender's vote is its credit office's (S8.165).

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/procedure.rs` | the debtor's choice becomes `options(view: &OpenView, out)`: open each procedure its law admits, or not |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/plan.rs` | `plan` becomes `options(view: &PlanView, out)`: terms per class on the declared points within absolute priority; `vote` becomes `options(view: &VoteView, out)`: for or against |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | the three points moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **Open**: each procedure its law admits (liquidation, restructuring under a stay), or not; `means` — the holder's
  expected value under each; `security` — the chance of a creditor's petition if it waits.
- **Propose**: terms per class on the declared points (haircut, maturity, equity for debt) within absolute priority
  (the law's); `means` — the value left to owners; `security` — the chance the plan fails the classes' votes (its
  outlook of each class's recovery against liquidation).
- **Vote** (a creditor firm): for or against; `means` — its recovery under the plan against liquidation.
- The confirmation stays S2.124's rule (the law's). The Stage 2 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day — openings on each firm's own review date within the law's duty period
  (`opening_within_duty_period`).
- E13: a law with one procedure — open or not (`single_procedure_two_options`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `plan_within_priority`; `vote_by_recovery`; `opening_within_duty_period`;
`single_procedure_two_options`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.institutions`: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 500 openings × 27 phone-ns; ≈ 100 plans

### S8.143 — Payout and filing by the chief executive's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: FRM.payout, FRM.file_accounts)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.140 (funding), S8.122 (the mandate), S2.119 (a firm's payout), S3.151 (payouts with record dates,
and buybacks), S2.108 (filing decisions and the registry's filed accounts)

**Goal**: what a firm pays out — dividends and buybacks from cash after what is due — and when within the law's window
it files its accounts are its chief executive's weighing, read on the statement being ready, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/payout.rs` | `dividend` becomes `options(view: &PayoutView, out)`: none, dividends and buybacks on the payout points within the distributable reserves |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/file.rs` | `filing_day` becomes `options(view: &FilingView, out)`: file today or at a later review day within the window |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.payout`, `FRM.file_accounts` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/<country>/FRM.toml` | the adjustment speed's distributions deleted (the Lintner target is no longer a rule); the payout frequency kept (it dates the occasion) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | Lintner's and the filing-day forms deleted; the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: a statement ready (S2.119's dated entry); each filing review day until filed (S2.108); 5c.
- **Payout** (FRM.10): none, and dividends and buybacks on the payout points from cash after what is due, within the
  distributable reserves (the law's); `means` — the owners' cash now against its value retained at their required
  return (the holder's own holding, through S8.122); `security` — the firm's cash against its outlook's needs;
  `standing` — a cut's signal read by its rank.
- **Filing** (RAT.8): file today, or wait to a later review day within the window; `means` — the filing's cost and a
  late fine's chance; `standing` — what the record shows lenders and buyers now against later.
- The Stage 2 and 3 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no distributable reserves — none is the one payout option (`no_reserves_no_payout`).
- E5: the busiest filing day — each firm files on its own weighing within the window (`files_within_window`).
- E10: a firm ending before it files — no filing (`ended_firm_files_nothing`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `payout_within_reserves`; `retained_value_counts`; `no_reserves_no_payout`; `files_within_window`;
`ended_firm_files_nothing`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- adds 45 phone-ns to `fin.decide.attend_ns` at 3 k / 0 / 3 k items (≈ 5 payout options × (3 concerns × 2 + 3)).
- on `fin.calendar.year_end_statements` (the weeks after a year's close): 2.3 core-ms (≈ 50 k payout decisions × 45
  phone-ns); joins neither.
- adds 35 phone-ns to `fin.decide.attend_ns` at 1.8 k / 0 / 1.8 k items (≈ 5 days × (2 concerns × 2 + 3)).
- on `fin.calendar.filing_window_end` (the busiest filing day): 1.8 core-ms (≈ 50 k filings × 35 phone-ns); joins H.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a payout target by partial adjustment; the filing day by a fixed rule; the forms kept

### S8.144 — Which lines to be in: entry, spin-off and the voluntary close by the chief executive's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: FRM.11 DECISION; MND.7 DECISION *(part: a line's entry, a spin-off, FRM.close)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §9 (endings), §6 (stages 5c, 2f)

**Depends on**: S8.138 (the investment's consequence arithmetic), S8.122 (the mandate), S8.123 (owner-managers),
S8.120 (a person's founding), S1.461 (a firm enters a line by investing; retires its placeholder
`FRM.candidate_lines`), S1.490 (firm births: a spin-off), S1.428 (retires its placeholder `FRM.voluntary_close`),
S1.343 (K-97: the ending kernel), S2.130 (resale of plant), S2.133 (estate administration)

**Goal**: which lines a firm is in — entering a product by investing in plant and knowing a way, founding a spin-off,
closing a line it cannot make pay or winding itself down — is its chief executive's (or owner's) weighing from its own
paths, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/lines.rs` | `best_line` becomes `options(view: &LinesView, out)`: waiting, each candidate line, a spin-off, as many as the attention allows; `candidate_lines` fills to attention, not `FRM.candidate_lines`'s count |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/close.rs` | `options(view: &CloseView, out)`: continue; close each line; wind the firm down |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/endings.rs` | the spin-off's `venture` read as the option's consequences |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/points.rs` | `FRM.close` routed on the option-generator path; the placeholder `FRM.voluntary_close` deleted |
| `data/shared/FRM.toml` | `FRM.candidate_lines` and `FRM.voluntary_close` (both `placeholder:MND`) retired |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms, with their reason |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc166.rs` | PC-166 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/live/mnd.rs` | LC-8-07 |

**Design**:
- **When**: the investment occasion (S1.458) for entry and a spin-off; the chief executive's review of its lines
  (attention, K-101) and a line's sales falling short of its own expectation (REP.35) for a close; 5c. An
  owner-managed firm's owner decides (S8.123).
- **Entry and spin-off**: waiting; each product in its region's markets with a way it knows, and a spin-off venture
  (S1.490), each valued by S8.138's arithmetic with its funding (S8.140), as many as the attention allows.
- **Close**: continue; close each line whose inputs it can stop (sell its plant at the resale bids, lay off its staff
  paying what their contracts owe, withdraw its offers); wind the firm down (a voluntary dissolution: an estate that
  sells, pays every creditor and passes the residual to the owners, L3).
- **Consequences** for the firm (then the holder's own through S8.122), from its own paths — its price and sales
  outlook (VAL.23) and unit cost (K-35), never the market's mark:
    - `means`: the line's expected margin over the horizon against the proceeds of closing or the entry's cost;
    - `wealth_and_legacy`: going-concern value against liquidation value to owners;
    - `security`: the chance losses continue times their size;
    - `standing`: the office kept or lost.
- **Applied** at 5d as intents: a closed line's plant offered for resale, its staff laid off by notice (K-45), its
  offers withdrawn (K-70); a wound-down firm ends at 2f through K-97 with its estate (S8.196).
- The placeholders `FRM.voluntary_close` (S1.428) and `FRM.candidate_lines` (S1.461) are retired here, completing
  FRM.11.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe's damage — a struck line's review is its occasion (`damage_wakes_line_review`).
- E3: a single-line firm — closing its line is winding down (`single_line_close_is_wind_down`).
- E10: a line's plant with no bid — its proceeds read `Missing` and closing is not offered until a bid arrives
  (`no_bid_close_not_offered`).

**Extension points**: a strategy recorded (S8.200) is weighed by the same generator as declared data.

**Unit tests**: `entry_by_own_value`; `candidates_fill_to_attention`; `close_from_own_paths`;
`wind_down_opens_estate`; `damage_wakes_line_review`; `single_line_close_is_wind_down`; `no_bid_close_not_offered`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-8-07`: FRM.11 — every voluntary close names its decider and the choice's tipping concern; no firm is wound down
  while its own expected margin over the horizon exceeds its liquidation value to its owners unless the holder's own
  terms (S8.122) tipped it; each such case listed; from the first voluntary close.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.osearch`: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 5 k investment occasions × ≈ 6 options × (4
  concerns × 2 + 3) = 66 phone-ns), beside S1.461's 8.
- its share of `fin.fixed.institutions`: 0.4 / 0 / 0.4 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 10 k line reviews × ≈ 4 options × 11 =
  44 phone-ns); closings ≈ 300 a business day through K-97 at its per-ending cost.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: PC-166 — `phx-check` refuses any reference to `FRM.voluntary_close` or `FRM.candidate_lines` after this
step.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an exit rate; a declared count of candidate lines; a firm's close at the market's mark; the
placeholder kept

**Done when**:
- [ ] The generators and their unit tests written; the rule forms they replace deleted; the fast checks (`fmt`,
  `clippy`, tests, `phx-check`) pass.
- [ ] The placeholders `FRM.voluntary_close` and `FRM.candidate_lines` removed from the register; PC-166 written with
  its fixture; LC-8-07 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml` (`tools/bench.sh`).
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S8.146 — A seller's trade-credit terms and factoring by its head's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: TCR.grant_terms, TCR.factor)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate), S8.125 (line heads), S2.112 (a seller's terms per buyer), S2.115 (factoring
closed invoices)

**Goal**: the payment terms, early-payment discount and limit a seller grants each buyer, and whether it factors its
closed invoices and with whom, are its head's weighing of the sales each brings against the money tied up and the
buyer's default risk, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/terms.rs` | `grant` becomes `options(view: &TermsView, out)`: the grid's (term, discount, limit) points for a buyer, or cash only |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/rules/factor.rs` | `accept` becomes `options(view: &FactorView, out)`: each quote, or waiting |
| `crates/systems/sys-tcr/src/declare.rs` | `TCR.grant_terms`, `TCR.factor` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **Terms** (TCR.2; its review, a buyer's cash purchase with no pair): for each buyer pair it reviews, cash only or
  each point on the declared grid; `means` — the sales the terms keep (the buyer's record of purchases on the pair
  row) less the money tied up at its own cost of funds and the discount given; `security` — the buyer's chance of
  paying late or not (its record on the pair row and its filed accounts) times the exposure.
- **Factor** (TCR.3; its cash outlook short of its buffer): each bank's quote for its closed invoices, or waiting;
  `means` — the quote against the value of waiting for collections at its own cost of funds; `security` — the
  shortfall's distress risk if it waits.
- The Stage 2 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no bank quoting — waiting is the one option (`no_quote_waits`).
- E10: a buyer ended since the last review — its pair lapsed; not reviewed (`ended_buyer_not_reviewed`).
- E12: a buyer with no filed accounts — its record on the pair row only; `security` from the closest observed (VAL.10)
  (`no_filing_reads_record`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `terms_weigh_sales_against_tied_money`; `default_risk_counts`; `quote_against_waiting`;
`no_quote_waits`; `ended_buyer_not_reviewed`; `no_filing_reads_record`.

### S8.151 — Landlords' rents, lettings, repairs and investments by their own minds

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: HSG.7 — the rent review, the letting, HSG.landlord; the landlord's repair)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.106 (a household landlord weighs as one), S8.122 (the mandate for a firm landlord), S8.115
(repair's options), S2.153 (lettings and rents), S2.154 (landlords buy and sell), S2.159 (a landlord's repair)

**Goal**: what rent a landlord sets and whom it lets to, whether it repairs a unit, and whether it buys or sells
dwellings as investments are its own weighing (a household's adults, or a firm's chief executive through the mandate)
of rent against vacancy, costs and its outlook.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-hsg/src/rules/rent.rs` | `rent_point` becomes `options(view: &RentView, out)`: the rent on its points from the current outward |
| `crates/systems/sys-hsg/src/rules/landlord.rs` | `options(view: &LandlordView, out)`: keep, buy each listing in reach, sell each unit |
| `crates/systems/sys-hsg/src/rules/repair.rs` | the landlord's side: repair to each better class, or keep |
| `crates/systems/sys-hsg/src/declare.rs` | `HSG.landlord` and the rent review moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: the tenancy's anniversary rent review and a vacancy (S2.153); the landlord's investment review (a
  household's on its rent review, a firm's on S1.458's occasion, S2.154); 5c.
- **Rent**: points from the current outward, as many as its attention allows; `means` — the rent against the vacancy's
  chance and length at each point (the lettings market's published records); `security` — its outlook's vacancy risk;
  for a letting, each applicant or waiting.
- **Invest**: keep; buy each listing in reach (bids as S8.114's); sell each unit (asks as S8.114's); `means` —
  VAL.8's value from its rent outlook, vacancy, costs and price outlook against its marginal rate; `wealth_and_legacy`
  — the holding's value.
- **Repair**: as S8.115's, on the rent the better class earns.
- The Stage 2 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no applicant for a vacancy — the rent review weighs lowering (`vacancy_weighs_lowering`).
- E3: a landlord in arrears — `security` weighs a sale (`arrears_weighs_sale`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `rent_against_vacancy`; `invest_value_against_marginal_rate`; `repair_on_rent_earned`;
`vacancy_weighs_lowering`; `arrears_weighs_sale`.

  and S2.154's 3.5.
- ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (core attribute).

### S8.154 — An issuer's debt, paper and consents by the chief executive's mind

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: CRD.issue_debt, the paper roll with its route, CRD.offer_consent)*
**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stage 5c)

**Depends on**: S8.122 (the mandate), S8.140 (funding: a bond or paper among the sources), S3.130 (the issuer decides:
size, tenor, form, walk-away and refinancing), S3.136 (commercial paper rolled or not), S3.167 (the roll's route: placed directly or sold through
dealers), S3.138 (holders vote:
acceleration and waivers)

**Goal**: a bond's size, tenor, form and walk-away price, whether a paper programme rolls, and what an issuer offers
its holders for a waiver are its chief executive's weighing of the money's cost against its refinancing and default
risk, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/issue.rs` | `options(view: &IssueView, out)`: (size, tenor, form) on the declared points with a walk-away price, or not issuing |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/paper.rs` | `options(view: &PaperView, out)`: roll each amount on the points, placed directly or sold through dealers, or not |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/rules/holders.rs` | the issuer's side: `options(view: &ConsentView, out)`: a consent fee on the points, or none |
| `crates/systems/sys-crd/src/points.rs` | `issue_debt`, the roll and `offer_consent` moved to the option-generator path |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms restated |

**Design**:
- **When**: a funding decision choosing a bond or paper (S8.140); paper at maturity; a missed payment or breach's vote
  (S3.138); 5c.
- **Options**: issue at each (size, tenor, form) on the points with its walk-away, or not; roll each amount by each
  route (direct placement or through dealers, S3.167) or not, the route a term of the roll's option and not a fourth
  point; a consent fee on the points or none.
- **Consequences** for the issuer (then the holder's through S8.122):
    - `means`: the expected coupon cost over the tenor at its own rate outlook (for paper, the all-in cost by its
      route, the dealers' bid less their fees for a sale through them), or the fee;
    - `security`: refinancing risk at maturity and the chance of acceleration if the vote fails.
- The Stage 3 forms are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no investor's order at the walk-away — the issue fails (`walk_away_fails_issue`).
- E3: paper failing to roll — the shortfall wakes its distress occasion (S8.141) (`failed_roll_wakes_distress`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `tenor_against_refinancing_risk`; `walk_away_fails_issue`; `failed_roll_wakes_distress`;
`consent_fee_against_acceleration`; `roll_route_by_all_in_cost`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.institutions`: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 20 issues × ≈ 12 options × (2
  concerns × 2 + 3); ≈ 500 / 0 / 700 rolls × ≈ 4 options × 7).
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (core attribute).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161, PC-165.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; the Stage 3 forms kept

**Status**: planned

(banks classed as borrowers), S2.189 (the capital a loan consumes)

**Goal**: whether a bank quotes an applicant and on what terms is its loan officer's weighing of the loan's margin
against its own assessment of the loss and the capital it consumes, through the mandate; the lender's value (PC-40's
`LoanAssessment`) is the consequence arithmetic.

**Files**:

**Goal**: whether a borrower asks another bank and which quote it takes are its own weighing of each quote's cost

**Status**: planned

**Architecture**: §7.16, §6 (stages 5c, 8)

**Depends on**: S8.166 (the buffer), S8.122 (the mandate), S2.184 (a bank short of funding acts), S2.183 (the interbank ask and
its choice among the quotes), S2.185 (the facility request), S1.430 (a bank's request of the facilities, whose rule S2.185 moved into `sys-bfl`)

**Goal**: what a bank short of funding does — borrow from banks, pledge at the facility, sell loans, restrain lending
— which banks' term quotes it takes, and what it asks of the central bank's facilities are its chief executive's weighing of each action's cost against
failing for liquidity, through the mandate.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/shortfall.rs` | the least-cost order becomes `options(view: &ShortfallView, out)`: each action open to it, and nothing more, applied one at a time |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/facility.rs` | `options(view: &FacilityView, out)`: request each amount on the points against free eligible collateral, or none; the deposit facility for a surplus |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/rules/interbank.rs` | the choice becomes `options(view: &InterbankView, out)`: accept each quote received, or none |
| `crates/systems/sys-bfl/src/declare.rs` | `BFL.shortfall`, `BFL.facility`, `BFL.interbank` moved to the option-generator path |

**Design**:
- **When**: the shortfall review and wake (S2.184), 5c; the interbank choice at the 5c after its quotes are due
  (S2.183); the facility request at stage 8 (S2.185).
- **Options**: each action open to it and doing nothing more, weighed again after each is applied; accept each
  interbank quote received, or none; request each amount on the points or none.
- **Consequences**: `means` — each action's cost (a quote's interest over its tenor against the alternative
  source's, S2.179); `security` — the chance of failing for liquidity at stage 8's end
  times the loss to the holder; `standing` — the facility use's publication.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a run day — the review woken; actions until nothing more weighs best (`action_by_action_until_none`).
- E3: no free collateral — the facility request is not offered (`no_collateral_no_request`).

**Goal**: the policy rate and the collateral framework are the committee's weighing of its mandate's gap under each

answer.

### S8.197 — Experience accrues and character drifts with age

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.3 STATE; MND.12 PROCESS; MND.14 PROCESS; MND.19 PRIMITIVE *(part: the experience weights, the age
profiles)*
**Architecture**: §7.16 (K-102's traces; realise-before-read), §8 (the anchoring heuristic's reference)

**Depends on**: S8.105 (the mind's yearly step and its stamp), S8.103 (the `MindView` and the day's coefficient
cache), S1.352 (K-102: three traces), S1.207 (the person's named slot `experience`), S1.336 (K-92: published series'
yearly means in a ring), S1.213 (K-36: events naming the person), S1.454 (households' outlooks and the anchoring
heuristic)

**Goal**: each adult carries what it has lived through as three traces that fade — the inflation and the returns it
lived, and its own adversities — each weighted by how recent it is and how young the person was, and its patience,
risk aversion and concern weights drift with age along declared profiles, so the risk aversion its experience and age
shaped enters every choice it weighs.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/rules/experience.rs` | `accrue_published(trace, year_means, age) -> trace`; `accrue_event(trace, severity) -> trace`; `shaped(ρ, traces, age) -> ρ_eff` |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/rules/ageing.rs` | `drift(type_row, age) -> (β, ρ, weights)` from the declared profiles |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/rules/view.rs` | `mind_view` reads the person's stored experience factor and its (country, age) profile row beside the type row |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/declare.rs` | the experience factor as an i8 log-factor in the named slot `experience` (S1.207), its step derived from the traces' declared ranges and κ |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/declare.rs` | adversity events' severities; the post-event hooks on the declared events |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | `MND.experience_weights` (recency and age at the time), `MND.experience_effect` (on risk aversion), `MND.age_profiles` (patience, risk aversion, concern weights), `MND.adversity_severity` — PREFERENCE, each with its source |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc167.rs` | PC-167 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/live/mnd.rs` | LC-8-08 |

**Design**:
- **Traces** (MND.3; three i16 in K-102, S1.352): (a) inflation lived, (b) returns lived (crises carried by them), (c)
  own adversities — its unemployment spells, layoffs, a firm of its own failing, foreclosures, arrears, defaults,
  evictions, catastrophes that struck its own holdings.
- **Accrual** (MND.12): (a) and (b) from the published yearly means of its country's series it lived through (K-92's
  ring), weighted by recency and age at the time (Malmendier and Nagel 2011, 2016: the entries name the tables), at
  the mind's yearly step (S8.105's stamp) — one step per year missed, reading that year's mean, so the lazy
  realisation is exact; (c) written at the event by a post-event hook adding its declared severity, and faded at the
  yearly step. No trace reads an event the person did not live (REP.16).
- **Opening**: the opening's adults' traces are accrued over the country's history as K-92's ring holds it from the
  opening's profile; where it holds no history for a series, that trace starts at the opening (missing is missing,
  VAL.10). No new mapping: the series are the profile's.
- **What they shape** (MND.7): `ρ_eff = ρ_age · exp(κ_a·(a) + κ_b·(b) + κ_c·(c))`, κ the measured effects; a
  household's anchoring heuristic (VAL.6) reads its adults' trace (a), weighed as S8.106, as its long-window reference
  for prices, so expected inflation differs by age as lived inflation does (MND.17's measure).
- **Ageing** (MND.14): the declared profiles (patience and risk aversion across the life course: Dohmen et al. 2017,
  Falk et al. 2018's age gradients; concern weights' profiles only where a source gives one, else flat with the
  reason) applied on top of experience.
- **Where it is computed**: the shaped ρ depends on the person's own state — its traces and its age — not on the day,
  so it is filled at the person's own events, never daily: the factor `exp(κ·traces)` is recomputed at the yearly step
  and at an adversity write and stored as one i8 log-factor in the person's named slot `experience` (S1.207; the step
  derived from the traces' declared ranges, so every representable trace maps without a bound); the age profiles are
  functions of (country, age) alone, one row read at the view beside the type row.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe striking many holders — the adversity hook runs in the struck holders' `lose_batch` apply by
  holder range (K-60), no per-person pass (`adversity_in_event_apply`).
- E6: traces are state; the yearly ring's means are saved with K-92 (`traces_round_trip`).
- E11: day zero — every adult's traces from the opening's history (`opening_traces_from_history`).
- E12: a series with no published mean for a year — that year adds nothing to the trace, never 0 as a value; labelled
  (`missing_year_adds_nothing`).

**Extension points**: S8.200 reads the traces' effect on strategies' records; migration (S5.183) keeps a migrant's traces.

**Unit tests**: `recent_and_young_weigh_more`; `lazy_steps_equal_yearly_steps`; `event_adds_severity`;
`missing_year_adds_nothing`; `age_drift_from_profile`; `shaped_rho_exact`; `factor_recomputed_only_at_events`;
`factor_step_covers_trace_range`; `adversity_in_event_apply`; `traces_round_trip`; `opening_traces_from_history`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-8-08`: MND.3, MND.12 — risk-taking and expected inflation by age and lived experience published each year; a
  year holding a crisis with no difference by cohort in the following year is a finding; from the first year.

**Budget**:
- adds 1 phone-ns to `fin.decide.handler_mind_ns` at 1.6 M / 0.95 M / 1.6 M items (the stored factor and the (country,
  age) row read beside the type row); no per-day fill.
- adds 40 phone-ns to `fin.decide.handler_mind_ns` at 15 k / 15 k / 15 k items (the yearly steps, inside S8.105's
  realisation: the accrual 30 and the factor 10).
- its share of `fin.fixed.resolve`: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 10 k adversity writes a business day × 30
  phone-ns inside their events' applies: the severity 20 and the factor 10).
- on `fin.calendar.mass_default` (event): 4.5 core-ms (≈ 150 k adversity writes × 30 phone-ns inside the events'
  applies); joins H and B′.
- ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B (named slot `experience`, S1.207; K-102's three traces, S1.352).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.01 MB resident (3 countries × 100 ages × 10 profile values × 2 B).

**Guards**: PC-167 — `phx-check` refuses a write of a trace outside `sys-mnd::rules::experience` via the declared
hooks and the yearly realisation.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a trace written for an event the person did not live; an age profile chosen to make a measure look
right; a clamp on a trace

### S8.198 — Goals formed at life events, pursued, reached or given up

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.5 STATE; MND.10 DECISION; MND.19 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.16 (K-102's goal kind and the sparse goal rows)

**Depends on**: S8.105 (aspirations, against which a goal is given up), S8.197 (losses as adversity events), S8.124
(promotions as appointments), S1.352 (K-102: the goal kind and the sparse goal row), S1.235 (K-44: coming of age,
births as events), S1.213 (K-36: the events that reach a goal)

**Goal**: at a life event a person forms the goal its character and circumstances favour — a home, children, a firm,
an office, a degree, retiring by an age, a move — which raises the weight of the concerns it serves until it is
reached, or until the person's aspiration has fallen below it and it is given up.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/rules/goals.rs` | `options(view: &GoalView, out)`: each applicable goal and none; `pull(weights, goal) -> weights`; `reached(goal, state) -> bool`; `given_up(goal, aspirations) -> bool` |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/points.rs` | `MND.form_goal` (`taken_in = "person"`, `mode = "best"`) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/declare.rs` | the goal menu (kind, target type, served concerns, the aspiration that measures it, the events that reach it); formation hazards per life event; the post-event hooks |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | `MND.goals`, `MND.goal_formation`, `MND.goal_pull` (PREFERENCE, each with its source) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/live/mnd.rs` | LC-8-09 |

**Design**:
- **Menu** (MND.5; K-102's 4-bit goal kind): own a home, have children, found a firm, reach an office (its kind as the
  target), earn a degree or retrain (the occupation), retire by an age, move to a place (the zone). Each declares the
  concerns it serves and the aspiration that measures it.
- **Occasions** (MND.10): coming of age (K-44's event), partnering (S6.123), a child's birth, a promotion (an appointment,
  S8.124), a loss (an adversity event, S8.197); at each, the declared formation hazard for that event (MND.19) decides
  on `MND.goals` (subject: the person) whether the person considers forming a goal now (Law 15).
- **Choice**: the goals applicable to its circumstances and none; each option's consequences are the served concerns'
  expected gains from reaching the goal by its outlook; its own mind weighs them (best, with its taste). One goal is
  held at a time: the goal kind and one sparse row in S1.352's side table, laid out as S1.352 lays it — the target u16
  with its date folded in (4 B).
- **Pull**: while held, `mind_view` raises the served concerns' weights by the declared pull (re-normalised).
- **Reached**: a post-event hook on the events that reach it (a dwelling bought, a birth, a founding, an appointment,
  a degree, retirement, a move) clears the goal; **given up**: at the mind's yearly step (S8.105) a goal whose
  measuring aspiration has fallen below its level is dropped. Both are recorded (S8.199).
- A goal changes weights only; it forces no decision (no career or success drawn, MND.18).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a person with nothing — goals it cannot reach are still formable if applicable; weights move, outcomes do not
  (`unreachable_goal_moves_weights_only`).
- E8: the sparse rows' growth — ≈ half of adults hold a goal (≈ 3 M rows, S1.352's volume); a row released when its
  goal is reached or given up (`row_released_at_end`).
- E10: a person dying with a goal — its row released with its slot (`row_released_at_death`).
- E14: two life events the same day — one occasion; the first formed goal holds (`one_goal_at_a_time`).

**Extension points**: S6.120's and S6.118's events (household formation, schooling) and S5.142's (elections) declare
their occasions and
reaching events as data.

**Unit tests**: `applicable_goals_only`; `pull_raises_served_weights`; `reached_clears`; `given_up_below_aspiration`;
`one_goal_at_a_time`; `unreachable_goal_moves_weights_only`; `row_released_at_end`; `row_released_at_death`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-8-09`: MND.5, MND.10 — goals formed, reached and given up, by kind and age, published each year; a goal kind
  never formed over the run listed with the run's length (Appendix E 39).

**Budget**:
- adds 76 phone-ns to `fin.decide.mind_ns` at 12 k / 6 k / 12 k items (the occasions: the hazard's draw 50 and, for ≈
  30 % of them, ≈ 8 options × (4 concerns × 2 + 3) = 88).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB (the sparse goal rows are S1.352's 12 MB: ≈ 3 M × 4 B).

**Guards**: none beyond PC-161.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a goal that forces an outcome; a goal read from another person

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules, point, declarations, hooks, data and unit tests written; the fast checks (`fmt`, `clippy`, tests,
  `phx-check`) pass.
- [ ] LC-8-09 registered.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml` (`tools/bench.sh`).
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.16 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S8.199 — The reason recorded, goals' entries and the biography's hand-off

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: MND.15 PROCESS; OBS.10 PROCESS; OBS.11 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §7.6 (K-40 life records), §7.16 (the post-decision hook), §12 (observation)

**Depends on**: S8.121 (the entries written at their events), S8.106 (household choices' per-adult bits), S8.198
(goals formed, reached and given up), S1.223 (K-40: append, horizons, reads), S1.348 (K-100: the post-decision hook),
S1.213 (K-36: events naming a person)

**Goal**: every decision a person takes records the concern that tipped it in its life record, goals formed, reached
and given up are recorded, every entry kind is kept for its declared horizon, and any record can be read and handed
out, read-only, for a biography written outside the world.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/declare.rs` | the decision and goal entry kinds; each kind's horizon `OBS.life_horizon.<kind>` (RESOLUTION, SET.13) |
| `crates/systems/sys-mnd/src/record.rs` | `entry_of(choice) -> Entry` for the post-decision hook: one entry per decision occasion, packing its decisions' tipping concerns; a household's with its adults' `own_best_differs` bits |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/life.rs` | `life_of(person) -> RecordView` (read-only: the inspector's scope, and the participant's for its own persons); `biography_input(person) -> RecordText` |
| `data/shared/OBS.toml` | the horizons (RESOLUTION, E 41's valve) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc168.rs` | PC-168 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/live/mnd.rs` | LC-8-11 |

**Design**:
- **The reason recorded** (MND.15): K-100's post-decision hook appends one entry per decision occasion on the
  decider's record — a person's own; a household's once, on its record's first adult, with a bit per adult saying
  whether that adult's own best differed (`own_best_differs`); an office's on its holder's. The entry's 2-B payload
  packs each decision taken on that occasion with its tipping concern at 3 bits (a firm visit's plan, inputs, way,
  posting and services in one entry). A satisficing sequence (a search day, a viewing, the asks for quotes) records
  one entry for its day. An empty office's decision records nothing (no person took it).
- **Goals**: formed, reached and given up are entry kinds written by S8.198's hooks.
- **Horizons**: every kind for its declared horizon (SET.13; the owner's answer, §12), never shorter than a POLICY its
  keeper follows (none applies here); older entries released by K-40's merges.
- **Reading** (OBS.8): `life_of` reads a record through the inspector; a participant reads only its own household's
  persons' records (OBS.2). Looking changes nothing (Law 17).
- **The biography** (OBS.11): `biography_input` renders a record as text for a language model on the device; the model
  runs outside the world and nothing it writes is read by any world crate. Running it waits for the owner's call of
  the device run (§12); no world code depends on it.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a heavy day's decisions — the entries by source below, at K-40's append cost (`one_entry_per_occasion`).
- E6: records are state within their horizons, saved; K-40's segments shared by the snapshots (`records_round_trip`).
- E9: growth within the horizons — entries, bytes and growth a simulated year reported per kind (LC-8-10).
- E13: an empty office's decision — no entry (`empty_office_records_nothing`).

**Extension points**: S5.142's elections, S5.144's offices, S6.118's schooling and S6.123's partnering declare entry
kinds as data.

**Unit tests**: `tipping_packed_per_occasion`; `household_entry_carries_adult_bits`; `empty_office_records_nothing`;
`one_entry_per_occasion`; `horizon_prunes_by_kind`; `records_round_trip`; `biography_reads_only` (compile:
`biography_input` takes `&` and returns an owned text; no world type is writable from `phx-obs`).

**Live checks**:
- `LC-8-11`: MND.15 — the day's decision entries equal the decision core's count of decision occasions taken by
  persons (holders, households, persons) that day; from day 1.

**Budget**:
- entries by source at the design point, a business day / a non-business day: households' occasions 0.62 M / 0.49 M
  (spending 472 k every day, holdings, housing, borrowing, arrears, the child's decision); persons' 0.15 M / 0 (search
  days 90 k, work, pay answers, claims, founding, goals); offices' 0.68 M / 0.2 M (visits 246 k, price reviews 338 k,
  the rest); with S8.121's events, 1.5 M / 0.71 M, within S1.223's 1.6 M / 0.8 M.
- its share of `fin.fixed.observer`: 6.6 / 3.6 / 6.6 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the appends × `append_ns` 3.8 and the
  entry's packing 0.7).
- saved: ≈ 1.5 M × 250 + 0.71 M × 115 ≈ 457 M entries a simulated year, within `storage_mb_per_year` 250 (S1.223's
  figure at its 492 M).
- ledger line 18 (records): +0 B (core attribute: K-40's buffers, S1.223's 7 MB).

**Guards**: PC-168 — `phx-check` refuses any world crate depending on `phx-obs::life`, and any `&mut` from `phx-obs`
into the world.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an entry per decision beyond its occasion's packed one; an unbounded record; anything the
biography writes read by the world

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, the hook, the read views, data and unit tests written; the fast checks (`fmt`, `clippy`, tests,
  `phx-check`) pass.
- [ ] LC-8-11 registered and passing on the bench's 20-day run.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution for 20 days within `perf/budget.toml` (`tools/bench.sh`), records within
  K-40's ratchets.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §7.6, §7.16 and §12 updated; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.
