### S4.112 — A member's default: lots, auctions and porting

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRV.9 STATE; DRV.5 PROCESS *(part: an unmet margin call closes out a member's positions at a house)*
**Architecture**: §9.3 (a margin call unmet: its days and stages) writes lots, ports and appropriation on the core;
§7.11 (K-76's default-lot variant) follows; §7.9 (K-57 moves) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (reads frozen); S4.107 (the unpaid call); S4.111 (the waterfall); S4.105 (clients, backup
members); S4.110 (suspension); S4.106 (settlement prices); S1.312 (K-76: the default-lot variant); S1.265 (K-56: the
default); S1.267 (K-57: moves); S1.340 (K-94: sets ported); S1.277 (K-63: appropriation); S1.335 (K-91: labelled
valuation); S1.343 (K-97: the defaulter's side at its estate); S1.213, S1.215 (K-36, K-37: the public event, the lots);
S1.348, S1.352, S8.103, S8.122 (office holders' minds).

**Goal**: A member that fails an obligation to its house at settlement is in default: suspended, its house account
auctioned in lots against the house's reserve, its clients ported to members that accept them or closed out in the
lots, its collateral appropriated under the lien. The close-out is valued from the prints and runs down the waterfall.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-risk/src/closeout.rs` | record `DRV.default_lots`; decision points `default_bid`, `house_reserve`, `accept_port` |
| `crates/systems/sys-drv/src/default.rs` | 2d: default, suspension, lots; 7: moves and appropriation; 9a: close-out value |
| `crates/systems/sys-drv/src/rules/{default_bid,house_reserve,accept_port}.rs` | the option generators |
| `crates/systems/sys-drv/tests/default.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the three forms, with sources |

**Design**:
- **Completes**: DRV.9 — when a member defaults, its clients' positions move to another member or are closed out.
- **The trigger** (for a call issued at 9c of D): a failed obligation to the house recorded by K-56 at 2d of D+1 — an
  unpaid margin call (S4.107) or an unmet delivery or payment at its settlement (S4.120, S4.121). The default is a
  public event (K-36); the member is suspended (`admit` refuses it); `DRV.default_lots` is published (K-37, audience
  the members): its house account in lots per class by the rulebook's lot rule, each client account a port lot.
- **D+1, 5c**, each `fn options(&View, &mut OptionSet)` in the decider's office, concerns [means, security]:
  - `default_bid` (survivors): no bid, or a bid at each of the lot's price points within its funds; means = its own
    value of the lot (`claim_value`, VAL.8) − the price; security = the lot's loss at its outlook's width over the days
    it needs to hedge (TECHNOLOGY of the market);
  - `house_reserve` (the house): reserve points; means = the sale against its own value of holding to the next
    auction; security = its loss while holding. It sells only when a bid beats holding (MKT.17);
  - `accept_port` (members, the client's backup first): accept or decline; means = the client's expected fees − the
    capital and liquidity the positions consume at its funding cost; security = their loss at its outlook's width;
    only options `admit` passes.
- **6a**: each lot a K-76 call among the bids and the reserve (default-lot variant), ties by lot
  (`DRV.default_auction_lot`).
- **An unsold lot**: its rows stay between the house and the defaulter's estate (K-97 moved the side), called on no
  margin, re-offered at each next business day's 5c. The close-out values it at that day's settlement price (S4.106's
  labelled valuation), fixing the estate's claim; later changes, and the difference at its sale, are the house's own
  (named events on its equity, K-88).
- **7**: one instruction per lot — the defaulter's side moves to the winner (K-57 `move_end`), the price settling as
  premium; ported client sets move with their margin (K-94, K-57); liened collateral passes to the house under its lien
  (K-63) at a named valuer's labelled valuation, never a print. Unported clients' margin returns net of their losses.
- **9a**: close-out value = sold lots' prints and unsold lots' settlement prices against the rows' settled marks, plus
  collateral; **9c**: the waterfall (S4.111); **D+2, 2f**: losses land on named holders. The defaulter's own failure
  is its kind's (a bank's by S2.196's resolution; others' by their estates).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: two members defaulting on one day: separate lots, one waterfall run serving both (`two_defaulters_separate_lots`).
- E2: no bid on a lot: it stays between the house and the estate, valued at the settlement price, and is re-offered
  (`unsold_lot_valued_at_settlement_trued_up_at_sale`, `LC-4-10`).
- E6: lots, their re-offers and open calls are live state across a save (`save_round_trip_messages`, S1.237).
- E10: a bank member resolved the same day: its lots are the house's to sell; the bank's estate holds the claim
  (`bank_member_resolved_same_day`).
- E14: a client whose backup member also defaults: its port lot falls into the lots
  (`backup_also_defaulted_port_in_lots`).

**Extension points**: S4.114 (a house whose waterfall this exhausts); S4.120, S4.121 (failed deliveries and exercises as
defaults); S4.181 (supervisory tests of houses).

**Unit tests**: `lots_from_house_account`; `port_lot_per_client_account`; `backup_member_answers_first`;
`default_bid_consequences_signs`; `reserve_blocks_below_holding_value`;
`unsold_lot_valued_at_settlement_trued_up_at_sale`; `appropriation_at_labelled_valuation`; `closeout_value_from_prints`;
`failed_obligation_to_house_is_default`; `two_defaulters_separate_lots`; `bank_member_resolved_same_day`;
`backup_also_defaulted_port_in_lots`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-10` (DRV.5, DRV.9) — every default is traceable from the unpaid call to the lots, the auction
prints, the ports, the waterfall's layers and the losses on named holders, on §9.3's days; applicable from the first
member default (listed as not yet seen otherwise).

**Budget**:
- on `fin.calendar.member_default` (event: a member's default): 0.4 core-ms (10 k rows moved at 15 ns, 100 lot
  calls at 2 µs); joins H and B′.
- Counters: `phx_drv.defaults`, `phx_drv.lots_auctioned`, `phx_drv.lots_unsold`, `phx_drv.ports`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (lots move the defaulter's rows, O(1) a book, S1.267).

**Guards**: the three forms listed in `SHAPES.toml`.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a close-out at any price; a lot sold below the house's reserve; collateral appropriated at a print
or at a number no valuer published.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §9.3 restated for lots, ports, unsold lots and appropriation on the core.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.113 — Bilateral close-out

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRV.5 PROCESS *(part: an unmet call under a bilateral agreement closes out that agreement's contracts; the
close-out value a claim on the defaulter's estate)*
**Architecture**: §9.3 writes the bilateral close-out; §7.15 (K-98 claims on an estate) follows; §6.1 (2c, 9a, 7)
follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.107 (the unpaid call); S4.106 (the calculation agent's valuation);
S4.109 (the collateral held); S1.277 (K-63: liens appropriated); S1.345 (K-98: the close-out amount as a claim ranking
in the estate); S1.265 (K-56: the termination recorded); S1.343 (K-97: a counterparty's ending is a termination event
too); S1.213 (K-36: the termination recorded as an event).

**Goal**: When a bilateral call is unpaid at the next business day's 2c, or a counterparty ends, the survivor
terminates that agreement at its calculation agent's valuation, nets only that agreement's contracts, applies the
collateral it holds, and the net is a claim on the defaulter's estate or a payment to it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-drv/src/closeout.rs` | termination, netting within the agreement, collateral applied, the net |
| `crates/systems/sys-drv/tests/closeout.rs` | unit tests |

**Design**:
- **Trigger**: an unpaid `DRV.margin_call` under an agreement at 2c of D+1, or the ending of a party to it (K-97): the
  termination is recorded at 2d (K-56, K-36).
- **D+1, 9a**: the agreement's calculation agent values every row under it (S4.106's methods, labelled) at that day's
  marks; the net of the agreement's rows only (DRV.8: no netting across agreements).
- **Collateral**: cash rows set off; liened securities appropriated by the holder under its lien (K-63) at the agent's
  labelled valuation, or returned where the net is owed to the defaulter.
- **D+2, 7**: the net is a payment to the defaulter's estate, or a claim of the survivor on it (K-98, ranked by the
  estate's law); every row of the agreement closes (K-53).

**Edge cases**:
- E10: a counterparty ended by other causes: the same termination (`ending_terminates_agreement`).
- E1: two agreements of one survivor with one defaulter close out separately (`bilateral_closeout_nets_one_agreement`).
- E12: a row with no valuation that day: the agent's method's declared fallback horizon; if none, the termination waits
  a business day and records why (`termination_waits_without_valuation`).

**Extension points**: S4.123 (hedge funds' positions closed out by their dealers).

**Unit tests**: `bilateral_closeout_nets_one_agreement`; `collateral_set_off_then_claim`;
`net_owed_to_defaulter_paid_to_estate`; `ending_terminates_agreement`; `termination_waits_without_valuation`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-10` extended to bilateral close-outs; applicable from the first bilateral default.

**Budget**:
- on `fin.calendar.member_default` (event: a bilateral default or ending): 0.1 core-ms (1 k rows closed out at
  `fin.contracts.close_ns` with their valuations); joins H and B′.
- Counters: `phx_drv.closeouts_bilateral`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (the closed-out rows are S1.257's).

**Guards**: none.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; netting across agreements; a close-out value from a print no one formed or a valuation unlabelled.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §9.3 states the bilateral close-out.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.114 — A clearing house's recovery and resolution

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRV.5 PROCESS; DRV.8 FORBID; SUP.14 PROCESS *(part: a clearing house's recovery, service transfer or wind-down)*
**Architecture**: §9.2 (the resolution timetable) writes the houses' paragraph on the core; §7.15 (K-99 resolution
engine, K-98) follows; §6.1 (2b, 2c, 5c, 6a, 7, 9c) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.111 (`DRV.waterfall_exhausted`); S4.112 (lots the house could not
sell); S4.103 (the recovery tools declared); S1.347 (K-99: closed fact, pending legs, sealed bids, least-cost
selection, transfer, retry); S1.248 (K-49: a closed payer's legs pending); S1.267 (K-57: members' rows moved by book);
S1.345 (K-98: the wind-down's estate); S1.317 (K-80: sealed bids); S1.237 (K-45: recovery calls); S2.196, S2.197,
S2.199 (bank resolution on K-99: the closed fact, the first-price sealed bid, the least-cost rule, the transfer and its
retry); S1.348, S1.352, S8.103, S8.122 (bidding houses' office holders decide).

**Goal**: A house whose waterfall is exhausted is closed and recovers by its rulebook — haircutting the variation-margin
gains it owes that are still pending, and tearing up unmatched positions at their last settlement prices. Failing
that, other houses bid for its service and the authority selects by its least-cost rule; with no bid, the house is
wound down at the last settlement prices. Every position and margin balance lands on a named party.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/house_resolution.rs` | closing, recovery, the service transfer and wind-down on K-99 |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/rules/bid_for_service.rs` | the house kind's option generator |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/src/audit.rs` | SUP.7's family extended to houses (S4.183 completes SUP.7) |
| `crates/systems/sys-sup/tests/house_resolution.rs` | unit tests |

**Design**:
- **Completes**: DRV.5 — running past the waterfall's end is a real event; DRV.8 — no netting across counterparties, no exposure without margin or a stated reason, no clearing house that cannot run out.
On §9.2's days:
- **D, 9c**: `DRV.waterfall_exhausted`; at 9e the house is **closed** (K-99's fact, writer `sys-sup`); every leg it
  owes is pending (K-49's closed payer); legs owed to it settle.
- **Recovery** by the rulebook's tools in their declared order (SUP.14): at 9c of D, cash calls on survivors up to the
  declared multiple of each one's contribution (`DRV.margin_call`, reason `assessment`), due at D+1's 2c — an unpaid
  one is that member's default (S4.112); then, after D+1's 2c, the pending variation-margin gains the house owes are
  haircut pro rata to the loss still uncovered (ties `DRV.prorata_lot`) — only pending legs, so nothing settled is
  reversed (SET.5); unmatched positions (lots it still holds) are marked for tear-up at their last settlement prices.
  If recovery covers the loss the closed fact lifts at 2f and the haircut legs and tear-ups settle at that day's 7.
- **Otherwise, D+1 5c**: other houses decide `bid_for_service` (concerns [means, security]; options — no bid or a bid
  on the declared price points; means = the fees it would earn over its horizon against the capital, fund and
  liquidity the positions need at its funding cost; security = the positions' stressed loss against its capital);
  sealed bids through K-80. **6a**: the authority's least-cost rule (POLICY), its reserve the members' cost of a
  wind-down, ties by lot (`SUP.bid_lot`). **7**: members' positions and margin move to the winner by book (K-57) with
  their netting sets; the pending legs settle with it.
- **No bid**: wind-down at 7 — every row terminated at its last settlement price; net amounts are claims on the
  house's estate or payments to it; the estate distributes by its law (K-98).
- **A failed transfer** (a leg its payer cannot fund at 7b): nothing moves; at D+2's 2b the next bid at or above the
  reserve, or wind-down, settling at D+2's 7.
- SUP.7's family extended: what the acquirer took, what members lost to haircuts, assessments and tear-ups, and what
  the estate realised sum to the hole.
- **DRV.8 complete**: one side, underlyings (S4.101), netting only within a set (S4.102, S4.107), margin or a
  recorded reason (S4.109), a house that can run out (here).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a house failing on the day a large bank member is resolved: two resolutions on one K-99 timetable, each its own
  closed fact (`two_resolutions_one_timetable`).
- E6: a resolution between D and D+2 across a save: the closed fact, pending legs, bids and the reserve are live
  state (`resolution_roundtrip`, S1.347).
- E14: a haircut and a settled payment on one day: only pending legs are cut (`haircut_acts_on_pending_only`).

**Extension points**: S4.181 (supervision of houses; SUP.14's completion); S4.183 (SUP.7's identity over every
resolution kind).

**Unit tests**: `assessment_up_to_declared_multiple`; `haircut_acts_on_pending_only`;
`teardown_at_last_settlement_price`; `recovery_lifts_closed_fact`; `service_transfer_moves_margin_with_positions`;
`least_cost_selects_or_winds_down`; `failed_transfer_next_bid_or_wind_down`; `resolution_identity_house`;
`two_resolutions_one_timetable`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-09` (SUP.14 part, SUP.8) — every house past its waterfall recovered or was resolved: every
contract and margin balance landed on a surviving house, a member's named loss or the estate, on §9.2's days; a closed
house made no payment of its own; every haircut touched only pending legs; applicable from the first exhaustion.

**Budget**:
- on `fin.calendar.house_resolution` (event: a waterfall exhausted): 1.5 core-ms on its D+1 (100 k rows re-pointed at
  15 ns, O(1) a book); joins H and B′.
- Counters: `phx_drv.recoveries`, `phx_drv.assessments`, `phx_sup.house_resolutions`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (re-pointed rows are S1.257's; the house's estate is line 20's).

**Guards**: K-99's applies (only `sys-sup` writes the closed fact); no change.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a house that cannot run out; a loss past the waterfall that lands on nobody; a haircut of a settled
payment.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §9.2's houses paragraph restated on the core.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.115 — Derivative classes as declarations, legs from templates, series listing

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.8 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §3.4 (`if-risk`) writes `ClassDecl`; §7.10 (K-64: derivative series as instruments) follows; §7.9
(K-55 templates) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.101 (terms, the underlying check); S4.102 (clearing and
fungibility); S1.279 (K-64: series issued and retired, never reused); S1.340 (K-94: a series' positions as netting-set
position rows); S1.263 (K-55: shapes from templates); S1.180 (K-21: markets and their forms); S1.326 (K-86: the last
settlement price listing reads).

**Goal**: Every derivative class is declared data read by generic code (Law 10): its underlying kind, legs template,
market and form, risk unit, clearing rule, exercise, settlement, contract multiplier and price points. One
template function builds any class's terms. Listed series are instruments listed by each exchange's rule and retired
at expiry, so the register stays level over the run.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-risk/src/classes.rs` | `ClassDecl`, `RiskUnit`, `ClearingRule`, `ListingRule` |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/decl.rs` | the classes of this stage; their markets; streams |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/legs.rs` | `legs_from_template(class, series) -> DerivativeTerms` |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/listing.rs` | series listed and retired by each exchange's rule |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/classes.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/<country>/DRX.toml` | class specifications, listing rules, contract months, standard dates, the clearing obligation |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc170.rs` | PC-170 |

**Design**:
- `ClassDecl { underlying: SeriesKind | EventKind, legs: TermsTemplate, market: MarketH, risk_unit: RiskUnit, clearing:
  ClearingRule, exercise: Schedule, settlement: Cash | Delivery, multiplier: Qty, points: PricePoints }`; a class whose
  market is a book lists its series as K-64 instruments, so its cleared rows net per series (S4.102) as K-94 netting-set
  position rows (S1.340), never holdings. `RiskUnit` = PV01 per tenor bucket | CS01 per name | delta per underlying. No
  mechanism names a class.
- **This stage's classes** (declared here, activated by S4.118–S4.122): interest-rate swaps (fixed against a
  reference-rate fixing on the market's standard quarterly dates), CDS (single names and index baskets; running
  premium on the point grid, contingent leg on a credit event), futures (commodity grade at a delivery place; sovereign
  bond basket with conversion factors; equity index cash-settled), options (caps, floors, swaptions, on equities, on
  indices, on commodity futures; European or American by the exercise schedule), power contracts for difference (per
  region, block and delivery month). Currency classes are declared by S5.171 through the same declaration.
- **Clearing obligation** (POLICY of the supervisor): exchange contracts at the exchange's house; standard swaps and
  index CDS between financial parties at a house; the rest bilateral under an agreement.
- **Listing** (POLICY of each exchange): contract months; strikes at declared intervals around the last settlement
  price (K-86), listed at 9e for the next business day; each series a K-64 instrument; retired after its expiry's
  final settlement, its id never reused. OTC classes use standard dates, so trades share shapes (REP.3).
- Values are the exchanges' and the supervisor's published specifications, each primitive with its document cited.
- **Steady state** (E9): ≈ 60 futures underlyings × 4 contract months and ≈ 100 option underlyings × 4 expiries × 20
  strikes × 2 rights — ≈ 16 k listed series live at the design point, each retired at expiry; their marks kept for a
  declared horizon (RESOLUTION, `DRX.series_mark_days`, 20 business days, never shorter than the house's settlement
  cycle).
- **Kind**: `mechanism`, because the template function and the listing rule are code over DRX.8's declared data.

**Edge cases**:
- E9: listed series per underlying are its months × strikes, each retired at expiry: the register is level after a year
  (`listing_steady_state`).
- E13: a country with no exchange lists no listed class; its OTC classes trade bilaterally
  (`no_exchange_lists_no_listed_class`).
- E12: a class declaration missing a field is refused at assembly (`class_decl_complete`).

**Extension points**: S4.116–S4.124 (every class's users and markets); S5.171 (currency classes).

**Unit tests**: `legs_from_class_decl` (one template function builds a swap's, a future's and a CDS's legs);
`class_decl_complete`; `strikes_around_last_settlement`; `listing_steady_state`; `clearing_obligation_by_parties`;
`no_exchange_lists_no_listed_class`; `pc170_refuses_class_name_in_mechanism`.

**Live checks**: none (the classes' markets carry them).

**Budget**:
- ledger line 11 (K-64's instrument register): +0.7 MB resident (16 k listed series × 40 B; their positions are
  K-94's rows, S1.340), within the core's `[store] instruments` of 77 000 (S1.279); saved: +0.7 MB (the same
  register rows).
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (the series' marks at `DRX.series_mark_days` 20 are inside S1.326's marks).
- its share of `fin.fixed.calls`: 0.02 / 0 / 0.02 core-ms (100 series listed a business day at 200 ns, K-64 issue).
- Counters: `phx_drx.series_listed`, `phx_drx.series_retired`.

**Guards**: PC-170 (new, `phx-check`) — no mechanism of `sys-drx` compares a class's name (Law 10).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a class special-cased in a mechanism; a series never retired.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code, data with sources and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` (PC-170) pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §3.4 lists `ClassDecl` in `if-risk`.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.116 — Taking a position: the option generator, and firms' and banks' positions

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.9 DECISION
**Architecture**: §3.4 (`if-risk` decision point `take_position`) writes its user kinds; §7.16 (K-100, K-102) follows;
§6.1 (5c) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (classes, risk units); S4.108 (the margin a position needs);
S4.105 (a cleared class needs a clearer; the derivative review occasion); S1.341 (K-95: exposures per risk-unit bucket
read exactly from a party's own rows); S1.338 (K-93: mandates and position limits as declared limits); S1.357 (K-105: an
option's expected gain and its loss at the outlook's width); S1.336 (K-92 and own-outlook columns: the underlying's
outlook and width); S1.316, S1.315 (K-79, K-78: the quotes it can get); S1.348, S1.352, S8.103, S8.122 (the option set,
the office holder's mind); S1.350 (K-101: attention).

**Goal**: A user takes a position in a class from its own exposure, its own outlook of the underlying, the quotes it can
get, the margin it can fund and its declared limits. Its rule states target positions — among them the exact
minimum-variance hedge — with their consequences for its means and its security, and its decider's mind chooses; a
hedger and a speculator differ only in the exposure they hold. Firms and banks are the first users.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-risk/src/position.rs` | decision point `take_position`; `PositionView` |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/position.rs` | `position_options`, shared by every user kind |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/exposure/{firm,bank}.rs` | the firm and bank kinds' exposures |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/position.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | `DRX.take_position` (taken in the kind's declared office; concerns [means, security]; best) |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form of `position_options`, with its sources |

**Design**:
- **Inputs** (DRX.9): `E` — the exposure in the class's risk unit, read exactly from the party's own books: a firm's
  floating-rate debt and a bank's repricing gap as PV01 per tenor bucket from K-95's cells over its own rows; a
  lender's exposure to a reference entity as its exposure at default × the loss given default of its own assessment
  (K-53 cold columns); a producer's planned output or input from its plan. `δ` — one contract's sensitivity in the
  same unit, from its terms, so the hedge is one for one in risk units: no hedge ratio is estimated. The party's own
  outlook of the underlying (mean `m`, width `s`); the quotes in its reach for each size (dealers, K-79) or the book's
  best (K-78); its mandate and position limits (K-93); its free liquid resources against the house's margin per
  contract (S4.108); its clearer (S4.105) for a cleared class.
- **Options** (`fn position_options(&PositionView, &mut OptionSet)`): target positions on the class's lot grid — the
  current position (no trade), the minimum-variance hedge −E/δ in lots (Ederington, 1979), and the declared number of
  steps (RESOLUTION, `DRX.position_steps`) each side between them and the nearest bound: a declared limit, the margin
  it can fund, the size its quotes cover. Each option carries the price p(q) it would trade at.
- **Consequences** over the review horizon, by K-105's arithmetic: **means** = (q − q₀) × (m − p(q)) × multiplier −
  fees − the margin's funding cost at its own rate; **security** = the loss of the whole book (E + q·δ) at one width
  `s` of its own outlook. The mind's risk and loss aversion weigh them (MND.7); the speculative demand of a hedger
  with a view (Anderson and Danthine, 1981) emerges from that weighing, not from a parameter.
- **The order**: the chosen q* − q₀ as a request for quote taken if the quote still stands (K-79), or a limit order at
  p's price point standing into the book's closing call (K-78), through S1.298's admission.
- **Occasions**: the derivative review (S4.105's `position` kind for institutions, `FRM.finance`'s occasion for
  firms), woken also by a surprise in the underlying (REP.35) and a cut at admission (S4.110); the same occasion takes
  `choose_clearer` (S4.105) and `post_collateral` (S4.109) where they apply. Each review costs staff hours
  (TECHNOLOGY).
- **The first test** (S4.105), exact under three rules, per class: (1) the view is priced at the best one-lot
  executable price, the best K-79 quote in reach or the K-78 book's best, never the last print; (2) the exposure test
  is |E| ≤ half a lot (δ/2); (3) the round trip — both sides' fees, the spread at one lot and the margin's funding
  over the horizon — is costed at the smallest lot. With no position held, |E| ≤ δ/2 and |m − p₁| × multiplier not
  above that round trip, every option's means is at most zero and its security no better than holding, so holding is
  best and the review ends with no view gathered beyond the one-lot price. **Condition**: this holds only while
  `take_position` declares no per-option taste and quotes worsen with size (p(q) no better per lot as q grows); a
  change to either reopens the test.
- **Firms** (the firm kind's exposure): floating-rate debt, commodity inputs and outputs. **Banks**: the repricing gap
  by bucket; protection on loans they cannot sell. Other kinds register their exposure readers later: funds and
  dealers (S4.123, S4.117), generators and consumers (S4.122), insurers (S4.137), schemes (S4.155).
- **Representation** (N8.7, step 1): on a firm's `FRM.finance` occasion the rule reads the firm's exposure cells
  first — its K-95 PV01 buckets and its plan's commodity inputs and outputs, each O(1) — then the one-lot price and
  its view, by the first test above. Otherwise the firm's cost of
  funds and liquidity are read from S2.118's view gathered on the same occasion — one gather, not two.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: no exposure and no view beyond the quote: the no-trade option dominates, no order (`no_exposure_no_view_holds`);
  no position, |E| ≤ half a lot and a view that does not pay the one-lot round trip end the review at the first test
  (`first_test_exact_holds_best`); a view that pays it goes on to options (`view_paying_round_trip_passes_test`).
- E2: no quote in reach: only the current position is an option (`no_quote_only_hold`).
- E12: an absent outlook of the underlying (no print yet): its means are absent, the option set is hold only
  (`absent_outlook_hold_only`).
- E14: a margin call and a surprise the same day wake one review (K-43 lazy invalidation) (`one_review_for_two_wakes`).

**Extension points**: S4.117, S4.122, S4.123, S4.137, S4.155 (user kinds' exposure readers); S5.164 (currency
exposures).

**Unit tests**: `hedge_option_is_minus_e_over_delta`; `options_bounded_by_fundable_margin`;
`options_within_declared_limits`; `means_sign_follows_view`; `security_least_at_hedge`; `no_quote_only_hold`;
`exposure_read_from_own_rows`; `no_exposure_no_view_holds`; `absent_outlook_hold_only`; `one_review_for_two_wakes`;
`first_test_exact_holds_best`; `view_paying_round_trip_passes_test`; `first_test_prices_at_best_one_lot_not_last_print`;
`first_test_valid_only_without_taste_and_worsening_quotes`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-63` (DRX.9) — every derivative order has its decider's decision record naming its exposure, its
outlook and the tipping concern; applicable from the first derivative order.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.institutions`: 16 / 0 / 16 core-ms — the expected 5000 firms a business day whose exposure
  cells pass the O(1) read (of the 55 k `FRM.finance` occasions) and 3000 institutions' own occasions, each 9 options
  × K-105's 150 ns plus the view, 2 µs; no derivative review runs on a non-business day.
- Exposures are reads of maintained K-95 cells and K-54 sums (no pass); record +0 B (the occasion is S4.105's).
- Counters: `phx_drx.position_reviews`, `phx_drx.position_hold_only`, `phx_drx.position_orders`.

**Guards**: The form listed in `SHAPES.toml`; PC-61 applies (no change).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an exposure estimated where the books state it; a hedge ratio from a regression; a risk-aversion
parameter in the rule; an order "at market".

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken; the 5c span's position line
      read.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §3.4 lists `take_position` and its user kinds.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.117 — Dealers' derivative quotes and hedges

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DLR.4 DECISION
**Architecture**: §3.4 (`take_position`'s user kinds) writes the dealer kind; §7.11 (K-79 quotes) follows; §6.1 (5b, 5c)
follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (classes and their risk units); S4.116 (the position
generator a dealer's own hedge uses); S3.163, S3.165 (dealer desks and their quote form, declared per class with its
risk unit as data); S1.316 (K-79: quote tables per (dealer, instrument)); S1.338 (K-93: a dealer's limits).

**Goal**: Dealers quote every over-the-counter derivative class — swaps, CDS, rate options — from their own inventory in
the class's risk unit: long inventory lowers both sides, risk widens them, and a binding limit shrinks or stops the
quote. A dealer hedges its book in the underlying through the position generator, its exposure its derivative
inventory's sensitivity.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/src/rules/hedge.rs` | the dealer kind's exposure reader for `take_position` |
| `crates/systems/sys-dlr/tests/derivative_quotes.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/shared/DLR.toml` | the swap, CDS and rate-option classes declared to S3.165's quote form with their risk units |

**Design**:
- **Completes**: DLR.4 — a dealer's quote in each derivative class, skewed by its inventory in the class's risk unit.
- **Quotes** (DLR.4): S3.165's quote form is declared for each over-the-counter derivative class with its risk unit
  (PV01 per tenor bucket for swaps and rate options, CS01 per name for CDS): the dealer's inventory in that unit
  skews both sides, its own outlook's width widens them, and a binding limit (K-93) shrinks or stops them — the
  bid–offer is its output, never an input (MKT.19). Quotes post as K-79 quote rows at 5b.
- **Hedges**: a dealer's `E` for `take_position` (S4.116) is its derivative inventory's sensitivity in each
  underlying's class (K-95 over its rows), so it hedges on its own review occasion (S4.105's `position` kind).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a dealer at a binding limit quotes nothing in that class: a visible failed meeting for its clients
  (`binding_limit_stops_quote`).
- E3: a dealer with no inventory quotes symmetric around its own value (`flat_inventory_symmetric_quote`).
- E10: a dealer desk whose parent ends: its quotes lapse with its offers (K-70) (`ended_dealer_quotes_lapse`).

**Extension points**: S4.118 (swaps), S4.119 (CDS), S4.121 (rate options) meet on these quotes.

**Unit tests**: `dealer_quote_skew_in_risk_unit`; `binding_limit_stops_quote`; `flat_inventory_symmetric_quote`;
`dealer_hedge_exposure_from_inventory`; `ended_dealer_quotes_lapse`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-68` (DLR.4) — every dealer's derivative quote records its inventory in the class's risk unit, and
none is quoted at a binding limit; applicable from the first dealer quote in a derivative class.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.calls`: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (2 k derivative quotes reposted a business day at
  `fin.dealer.quote_ns` 150 phone-ns; a quote is standing state, reposted only when its inventory or mark changes).
- Dealers' hedging reviews are counted in S4.116's share.
- Counters: `phx_dlr.derivative_quotes`, `phx_dlr.derivative_quotes_stopped`.
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0 B (derivative quotes are among S1.316's 50 k dealer quotes).

**Guards**: none new; the quote form's own (a spread from a table refused) applies.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a spread applied to a mid; a quote that ignores inventory or a binding limit.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code, data and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §3.4 lists the dealer kind among `take_position`'s users and its derivative quotes.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.118 — Interest-rate swaps in the dealer market

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.1 STATE *(part: swaps, their market and the curve as the set of formed fixed rates; completed at S4.155
with schemes extending duration, its last named users)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-79 dealer market, K-76 interdealer call) follows; §8 writes the swap market and the curve's
read; §6.1 (5b, 6a, 6b, 7c) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (the swap class); S4.116 (users' positions); S4.117
(dealers' swap quotes); S4.102 (standard swaps between financial parties novate); S4.106 (swap fixings and the curve);
S1.316 (K-79: requests to dealers in reach, the best quote with size left); S3.168 (interdealer calls);
S3.203 (the reference-rate fixing the floating leg reads).

**Goal**: Interest-rate swaps — fixed against floating on a transacted reference rate, on the market's standard dates —
trade in the dealer market: clients ask the dealers in their reach, each dealer quotes both sides from its own
inventory in PV01 per tenor bucket, and the client takes the best quote with size left. The fixed rate is formed at
inception; the day's formed fixed rates across tenors, taken by the fixing publisher's method, are the swap curve.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/decl.rs` | the swap market (dealer form), its tenors, reach and search cost; the fixed-rate grid |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/swap_request.rs` | a user's chosen position → requests to dealers in reach |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/swaps.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/<country>/DRX.toml` | standard tenors and dates; search cost (TECHNOLOGY) |

**Design**:
- **Terms**: fixed against the reference-rate fixing (S3.203), on the market's standard quarterly effective and
  maturity dates, so trades of one tenor and fixed-rate point share a shape (REP.3); fixed rates on the class's point
  grid (REP.34).
- **Requests** (5b): a user whose `take_position` chose a swap position asks the dealers in its reach (the declared
  search cost in hours, TECHNOLOGY) for that size and side; each dealer answers from its quote (S4.117) over its
  inventory in the swap class's risk unit; the client
  takes the best with size left if it still beats holding (K-79), else walks away (MKT.10 records it).
- **Interdealer** (6a): dealers redistribute inventory in standard series through S3.168's call.
- **Settlement** (7c): a match between financial parties novates at the house (S4.102's clearing obligation); others
  open a bilateral row under the parties' agreement (S4.101). The fixed rate is the match's rate, never solved from a
  curve (DRX.7).
- **The curve as a read**: S4.106's swap fixings per tenor are the day's formed fixed rates by the publisher's method;
  the fitted curve labels what it interpolates. Users: firms switching their debt's rate and banks managing repricing
  gaps (S4.116), insurers (S4.137) and schemes (S4.155) extending duration, speculators with a view (any user),
  dealers (S4.117).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no dealer in reach or every dealer at a binding limit: the request fails visibly (`no_dealer_request_fails`).
- E11: the first days: no swap print yet; users' outlooks of swap rates start from the reference-rate snapshot
  (VAL.10); the curve has no swap point until a tenor trades (`no_swap_point_before_trade`).
- E7: requests are served in K-79's lot-drawn order, the same for any worker count (`requests_in_lot_order`).

**Extension points**: S4.124 (swap spread read); S4.137, S4.155 (duration demand).

**Unit tests**: `standard_dates_share_shapes`; `best_quote_with_size_left`; `fixed_rate_is_the_match_rate`;
`no_dealer_request_fails`; `clearing_obligation_routes_novation`; `no_swap_point_before_trade`; `requests_in_lot_order`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-03` (DRX.1, DRX.7, part) — swap fixed rates by tenor are published per country each business day,
each from its matches; per month the orders on each side carrying a view (means from `m ≠ p`) are counted; applicable
from the first swap trade.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.calls`: 3 / 0 / 3.6 core-ms (5 k requests a business day, 6 k on H, each reading its
  instance's run of 4 standing quotes once at `fin.dealer.quote_ns` 150 phone-ns).
- adds 10 k / 0 / 10 k items to `fin.contracts.open_ns` (swap rows opened).
- Counters: `phx_drx.swap_requests`, `phx_drx.trades_by_class`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (swap rows are S1.257's `DRV.contract` rows).

**Guards**: PC-61 applies (no change).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a swap rate solved from a curve; a spread applied to a mid; a market whose only participants are
hedgers.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §8 lists the swap market and the curve's read.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.119 — Credit default swaps and credit-event auctions

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.2 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-79, K-76's CDS-auction variant) follows; §7.9 (K-55 event legs) follows; §8 writes the
credit-event auction; §6.1 (5c, 6a, 7) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (the CDS class and index baskets); S4.116 (users' positions;
banks' protection on loans they cannot sell); S4.117 (dealers' CDS quotes); S3.137 (a reference entity's missed
payment or default as a public event); S3.204 (an index publisher's composition rule for baskets); S1.263 (K-55: the
contingent leg's amount); S1.171 (K-14: the declared sweep that finds the entity's contracts on an event day); S1.312
(K-76: the settlement auction); S1.277 (`Covered<Qty>`: debt offered only from free units); S4.102 (index CDS
cleared).

**Goal**: Credit default swaps give protection on a named reference entity's default for a running premium formed in the
dealer market, on single names and index baskets. On the credit event the premium stops and a settlement auction of
the defaulted debt sets the final price; every contract on the entity pays par minus that price. Recovery is what the
debt fetched; an auction that forms no price re-runs, its payouts pending.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/cds.rs` | the credit event on contracts; the auction's schedule and payouts |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/auction_bid.rs` | `cds_auction_bid`, the option generator of bidders and sellers |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/cds.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/<country>/DRX.toml` | the auction lag; index rolls |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form of `cds_auction_bid` |

**Design**:
- **Terms**: a running premium on the point grid, quarterly on standard dates, and a contingent leg on the credit event
  of the reference entity (an entity with public debt, CRD.6); index baskets declared by an index publisher's
  composition rule (the names most traded over its window, rolled on its dates; S3.204's machinery). Premiums form in
  the dealer market as swaps do (S4.118's path; dealers' CS01 quotes, S4.117).
- **The credit event**: on the day the entity's public default event (S3.137) is recorded, one declared K-14 sweep of
  the `DRV.contract` rows' shape column finds every row whose underlying is `Event { default, entity }` or an index
  basket holding the entity (≈ 0.7 M rows × 1 ns; event days only); on each, the premium leg stops, accrued to the
  event day, and the contingent leg waits on the auction; an index contract's basket drops the name with its weight
  settled like a single name.
- **The auction** (K-76's CDS variant) at 6a on the class's declared lag: of the defaulted debt, where protection
  buyers who hold it may offer it (`Covered<Qty>`: only free units) and dealers and distressed funds bid. Each
  participant's `cds_auction_bid` (concerns [means, security]; best): options — no order, or an order at each price
  point; means = its own value of the claim on the estate (its outlook of the recovery, VAL.8) − the price (or the
  reverse for a seller); security = the loss at its outlook's width. Ties by lot (`DRX.cds_auction_lot`).
- **Payout**: the final price is the auction's print; every contract on the entity pays notional × (1 − final
  price ÷ par) at 7 of the next business day. An auction that forms no print is a recorded market failure (MKT.10)
  and re-runs at the next business day's 6a, the payouts pending; there is no fallback recovery (DRX.7).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no crossing in the auction: re-run, payouts pending across days and saves (`cds_auction_without_print_reruns`).
- E1: a default wave: many entities' auctions on one day, each its own call, one sweep per event day
  (`default_wave_one_sweep_separate_auctions`).
- E10: a protection seller ended before the payout: its estate owes it (K-98 claim)
  (`ended_seller_owes_through_estate`).
- E14: the event and a premium due the same day: premium accrued to the event day only (`premium_leg_stops_at_event`).

**Extension points**: S4.124 (implied default probabilities and the credit basis as reads); S4.123 (distressed funds
bid).

**Unit tests**: `cds_payout_from_auction_price`; `premium_leg_stops_at_event`; `cds_auction_without_print_reruns`;
`offers_only_from_free_units`; `index_drops_defaulted_name`; `auction_bid_consequences_signs`;
`event_sweep_finds_entity_rows`; `default_wave_one_sweep_separate_auctions`; `ended_seller_owes_through_estate`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-15` (DRX.2) — every CDS payout equals notional × (1 − the auction's final price ÷ par), the
auction's prints are its match set, recoveries vary across events, an auction without a print re-ran with payouts
pending; applicable from the first credit event on an entity with contracts.

**Budget**:
- adds 5 k / 0 / 10 k items to `fin.dues.item_ns` (premium legs on their quarterly dates).
- on `fin.calendar.credit_event` (event: a reference entity's default, then the auction after the class's declared
  lag): 0.7 core-ms for the sweep on the event day; 12 core-ms on the auction day (100 k orders at 100 ns plus 2 µs,
  payouts at 25 ns); joins H and B′.
- Counters: `phx_drx.cds_auctions`, `phx_drx.cds_auction_reruns`, `phx_drx.cds_payouts`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (CDS rows are S1.257's `DRV.contract` rows; the auction's orders are day items).

**Guards**: the form listed in `SHAPES.toml`.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fixed recovery; a payout without an auction print; an implied default probability fed into a
premium.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §8 states the credit-event auction and its sweep.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.120 — Futures: storage carry and delivery

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.4 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-78 book and closing call) follows; §7.10 (K-60, K-63: deliverable holdings) follows; §8
writes the futures' expiry and delivery; §6.1 (5c, 6a, 7) follows.

**Depends on**:  S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (futures classes, delivery places, conversion factors);
S4.116 (users' positions); S1.196 (the firm record's layout: the `carry` slot); S1.227, S1.350 (K-43, K-101: `carry` as
its own lumpy kind in its named slot, its next review drawn from its stake; S1.350's rule for a kind with no slot);
S4.102, S4.107 (novated positions margined daily); S4.112 (a failed delivery is a default); S1.315 (K-78: books with a
closing call as the settlement price); S1.271, S1.277 (K-60, K-63: stocks and `Covered<Qty>` for delivery); S1.280
(K-65: a delivered bond moves to the long); S2.157 (commodities' grades at delivery places and their spot call); S3.118
(sovereign bond lines in the deliverable basket); S3.204 (index levels for cash settlement).

**Goal**: Futures on commodities (a grade at a delivery place), on sovereign bonds (a deliverable basket) and on equity
indices (cash-settled) trade on books, margined daily. Holders of stock arbitrage the future against spot within their
own storage and financing cost and their free storage capacity; within the delivery window a short delivers when it
beats closing out, choosing its cheapest deliverable by its own cost. Nothing forces convergence.

| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/futures.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms of `carry` and `deliver`, with sources |
| `data/shared/MND.toml` | `DRX.carry` (the holder's finance office; [means, security]; best); the lumpy kind `carry` and its stake read |

**Design**:
- **Books** (K-78), all business days, the closing call's print the settlement price (S4.106); positions novate and
  are margined daily (S4.102, S4.107).
- **The `carry` occasion**: its own lumpy kind (K-43, K-101) for holders of stock of a deliverable grade or bond. Its
  stake read is the value of that stock and of its free storage capacity × the width of its outlook of the basis
  (F − S); attention's cost-versus-stake draw sets its next review. A basis surprise (the basis moving beyond its
  outlook's width) raises the stake and redraws; a need (stock received, capacity freed) or a meeting (a margin call,
  an expiry's window opening) wakes it. It has no scheduled interval. The next review day is the firm's named slot
  `carry` (K-43); institutions declare the slot in their own layouts, and a holder of a kind with no slot files its
  occasion by S1.350's rule (the wake ring within seven days, a dated K-45 message beyond).
- **Occasions at the design point**: 20 k holders of deliverable stock; a review costs two staff hours at their
  firm's wage and the stake is its stock's value times the basis's daily width, which gives a daily chance of about 1
  in 10: 2 k `carry` occasions a business day. The gate's run reads the count (`phx_drx.carry_reviews`); a lower count
  is not assumed.
- **`carry`** (concerns [means, security]; best): options — nothing; sell k lots of the future against stock held;
  buy spot and sell the future (cash and carry) up to its free storage capacity (a declared limit from its held storage
  units, TECHNOLOGY); buy back the future, or sell spot and buy the future (reverse). Means = (F − S − its own storage
  and financing cost to expiry) × quantity; security = the basis's loss at its outlook's width. The theory of storage
  (Working, 1949; Brennan, 1958): contango within carry and backwardation when stocks are short follow from it.
- **`deliver`** (a short within the delivery window, 5c): options — close out, or give notice to deliver each of its
  deliverable holdings (grades, or bonds × conversion factor); means = what delivering it costs it, read exactly (the
  seller's quality option, Gay and Manaster, 1984). A notice pins the units (`Covered<Qty>`).
- **Assignment and settlement**: longs receiving are assigned by lot (`DRX.delivery_assignment`); delivery settles at
  7 as units against payment at the final settlement price (× conversion factor) in one link group (SET.4). A notice
  whose units or payment fail at 7 is the short's (or long's) failed obligation to the house, recorded by K-56 and
  handled as a default (S4.112). Index futures settle in cash on the index level at expiry.
- No order is placed to close a futures–spot gap: convergence is whatever carry and delivery produce (DRX.7).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a holder with no storage capacity has no cash-and-carry option (`capacity_binds_carry`).
- E5: a quarterly expiry on a heavy day: deliveries and cash settlements join 7's batches
  (`expiry_joins_settlement_batches`).
- E10: a short ended within the window: its estate delivers or closes out by the same rule
  (`ended_short_estate_delivers`).
- E2: no deliverable held and no counterparty to close: the short fails to deliver, a default
  (`failed_delivery_is_a_default`).
- E1: a basis surprise across many holders raises each one's stake; their reviews fall by attention's own draw over
  the following days (`basis_surprise_raises_stake_and_redraws`).

**Extension points**: S4.122 (power futures-like contracts settle in cash); S4.124 (curves against spot and storage).

**Unit tests**: `carry_threshold`; `capacity_binds_carry`; `cheapest_to_deliver_by_own_cost`;
`delivery_legs_at_final_price`; `assignment_by_lot`; `index_future_cash_settles`; `expiry_joins_settlement_batches`;
`ended_short_estate_delivers`; `failed_delivery_is_a_default`; `basis_surprise_raises_stake_and_redraws`;
`carry_occasion_in_slot_or_by_rule`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-14` (DRX.4, part) — every expiry's deliveries and cash settlements are against its final
settlement price; the futures–spot gap at expiry is reported, with no order placed to close it; applicable from the
first expiry.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.securities`: 8 / 0 / 10 core-ms (50 k book orders a business day, 60 k on H, at
  `fin.book.order_ns`).
- its share of `fin.fixed.institutions`: 4 / 0 / 4 core-ms (2 k `carry` occasions a business day, the count the
  attention rule yields at the design point, at 2 µs).
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot `carry`, taken from the firm reserve); institutions declare it in their own
  layouts, and other holders file by S1.350's rule for a kind with no slot.
- on `fin.calendar.quarterly_expiry` (the third Wednesday of March, June, September and December, the exchange's
  POLICY, rolled past a holiday): 12 core-ms (10 k deliveries and cash settlements at 25 ns, 40 k rows closed at
  `fin.contracts.close_ns`, S4.121's exercises); joins neither H (a third Wednesday is never a month's last business
  day) nor B′, unless a holiday closure rolls it onto B′.
- Counters: `phx_drx.deliveries`, `phx_drx.carry_reviews`, `phx_drx.delivery_fails`.

**Guards**: the forms listed in `SHAPES.toml`.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a future forced to converge; delivery of units not free; carry beyond declared capacity.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §8 states the futures' expiry and delivery.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.121 — Options: own value and exercise

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.5 STATE *(part: options on rates, equities, indices and commodity futures; options on currencies
complete it at S5.171)*
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-78, K-79) follows; §8 writes own option values and exercise; §6.1 (5c, 7) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (option classes, exercise schedules, notice deadlines); S4.116
(users' positions: an option's own value is the `m` of its consequences); S4.117 (dealers' rate-option quotes); S4.106
(settlement prices and the premium valuer); S1.315, S1.316 (books for listed options, dealers for rate options); S4.120
(options on futures deliver a future position); S4.102 (novation); S4.112 (a failed exercise settlement is a
default).

**Goal**: Options on rates, equities, indices and commodity futures trade for premiums formed on books or with dealers.
A party's own value of an option is its expected payoff under its own outlook of the underlying, discounted at its
required return; writers and buyers take positions through the same option generator. Exercise is the holder's
decision after each exercise date; writers are assigned by lot. Nothing exercises by default.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/option_value.rs` | own value from the outlook (log-normal with its mean and width) |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/rules/exercise.rs` | `exercise`, the holder's option generator |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/expiry.rs` | exercise assignment by lot; delivery or cash at 7 |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/options.rs` | unit tests |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the forms of `option_value` and `exercise`, with sources |

**Design**:
- **Own value** (VAL.8 arithmetic): the expected payoff under the party's own outlook of the underlying — log-normal
  with the outlook's mean and width — discounted at its required return (Sprenkle, 1961). A `Value`, never a price;
  it is the option's `m` in S4.116's consequences, so writers (selling for income) and buyers (protection) take
  positions through one generator. The premium is what the book or the dealers form.
- **`exercise`** (the holder; concerns [means]; best): the right is exercised as of an exercise date, at that date's
  settlement price. The class's specification declares the exercise-notice deadline (DRX.8), as exchanges set one
  after the close: 5c of the next business day. So the holder decides on that occasion, reading the exercise date's
  settlement price. Options: exercise, or hold on. Means = the exercise value net of its costs against its own value
  of holding on (none after the last date). Nothing exercises by default.
- **Assignment**: writers assigned by lot (`DRX.exercise_assignment`); delivery (units, or a future position novated
  at the house) or cash settles at 7 in one link group; a failed settlement is a default (S4.112).
- Implied volatility is a statistic of the formed premium (S4.124), never an input.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: an absent outlook of the underlying: no own value, the option set is hold only (`absent_outlook_hold_only`).
- E10: a holder ended before exercise: its estate decides by the same rule (`ended_holder_estate_exercises`).
- E14: exercise and expiry of the underlying future on one day: the future position opens, then settles by its own
  expiry rule in the declared order (`future_exercise_then_expiry_order`).

**Extension points**: S4.124 (implied volatility and its skew); S5.171 (currency options).

**Unit tests**: `option_value_rises_with_width`; `deep_in_the_money_value_near_forward_intrinsic`;
`exercise_only_when_exercise_beats_holding`; `no_exercise_by_default`; `assignment_by_lot`;
`exercise_at_exercise_dates_settlement_price`; `absent_outlook_hold_only`; `ended_holder_estate_exercises`;
`future_exercise_then_expiry_order`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-16` (DRX.5, part) — every exercise has its holder's decision record; unexercised in-the-money
options are counted and published; applicable from the first expiry.

**Budget**:
- adds 200 phone-ns to S4.116's review per option held (own value), counted in S4.116's share.
- on `fin.calendar.quarterly_expiry` (as S4.120's): 10 core-ms (10 k exercise decisions at 1 µs); joins neither H nor
  B′ unless rolled.
- Counters: `phx_drx.exercises`, `phx_drx.itm_unexercised`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (options are S1.257's `DRV.contract` rows).

**Guards**: The forms listed in `SHAPES.toml`; PC-61 applies (no change).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a premium from a pricing formula; automatic exercise.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §8 states own option values and exercise.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.122 — Power contracts for difference

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: ENE.5 DECISION; ENE.6 DECISION
**Architecture**: §7.11 (K-78, K-77's prints) follows; §8 writes the power contracts and their settlement; §6.1 (5b, 6a,
7) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.115 (the power class per region, block and delivery month, read,
not re-declared); S4.116 (positions); S2.209 (the wholesale coupled call's prints per region, day and block); S2.208
(generators' offers at avoidable cost; suppliers' and large consumers' bids); S2.204 (retail supply contracts at posted
tariffs); S1.315 (K-78: the exchange's book); S1.326 (K-86: the month's daily block prints read at payment); S4.102,
S4.107 (cleared and margined daily).

**Goal**: Contracts for difference on a region's day-ahead price per block and delivery month trade on the exchange's
book, cash-settled against the coupled call's prints. A generator sells forward its expected output, a retail supplier
buys its fixed-tariff customers' expected load, and a large consumer buys its own expected need, each through the
position generator; a generator's offers read its contracts, which change its revenue and its hedged margin, not its
marginal cost.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/exposure.rs` | the energy kinds' exposure readers for `take_position` |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/src/rules/offer.rs` | S2.208's offer generator: the contracts in its view and its means |
| `crates/systems/sys-ene/tests/cfd.rs` | unit tests |

**Design**:
- **Completes**: ENE.5 — a generator's offers read its contracts; ENE.6 — a supplier and a large consumer buy under a contract.
- **The class** (S4.115's declaration, read here): cash-settled on (region, block, delivery month). Its leg is read at
  payment: on the monthly payment date the leg's amount is the sum over the month's delivery days of (that day's
  regional block print − the strike) × the block's energy, read from K-86's history (K-55 indexed legs). Nothing
  accrues on any day, business or not; the position is margined daily at the house on business days.
- **Exposures** (for kinds that hold derivatives, E 33): a generator's planned output by block over the delivery month
  (its plan's available capacity at its own outlook of running); a retail supplier's fixed-tariff customers' expected
  load (its supply contracts, S2.204); a large consumer's own expected need. Each takes positions through S4.116.
- **Offers read the contracts** (ENE.5): S2.208's offer generator gains the generator's contract position in its view;
  each offer option's means include the contracts' settlement at its own outlook of the block price, which does not
  depend on whether it runs, so a price-taking generator's offers stay at avoidable cost, and its keep-or-retire
  consequences read the hedged margin over the contracts' horizon.
- **Buying under a contract** (ENE.6): a large consumer still bids its physical need into the call and settles the
  difference under its contract, so its price is fixed by the contract; a supplier bears the difference between
  wholesale and its tariffs net of its contracts.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a block with no print (a failed call, MKT.10): that day's term has no index value, recorded absent; the leg
  settles when the published fallback of the call's operator exists, else stays unpaid and visible
  (`absent_block_print_leaves_term_unpaid`).
- E5: negative block prices: the leg pays the other way; nothing floors the price (Law 6)
  (`negative_price_reverses_leg`).
- E13: a region with no generator holding contracts: the class lists but trades only with speculators' views
  (`class_trades_without_generators`).

**Extension points**: S4.124 (hedged against unhedged firms' shocks).

**Unit tests**: `cfd_leg_from_block_prints_at_payment`; `negative_price_reverses_leg`;
`offer_stays_at_avoidable_cost_with_contracts`; `generator_exposure_from_plan`;
`consumer_bids_physical_need_under_contract`; `absent_block_print_leaves_term_unpaid`;
`class_trades_without_generators`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-14` (ENE.5, ENE.6, part) — every power contract settled against its region's day-ahead print;
applicable from the first power contract's delivery day.

**Budget**:
- adds 5000 / 0 / 5000 items to `fin.dues.item_ns` on monthly payment dates (each reads its month's prints, 30 terms at
  2 ns); nothing on non-business days.
- Book orders are counted in S4.120's share of `fin.fixed.securities`; energy positions' reviews in S4.116's.
- Counters: `phx_ene.cfd_settlements`, `phx_ene.cfd_terms_absent`.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (contracts for difference are S1.257's `DRV.contract` rows).

**Guards**: none.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a generator's marginal cost changed by a financial contract; a household holding a power
contract.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §8 lists the power contracts and their settlement.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.123 — Funds' derivative positions

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: FND.4 DECISION
**Architecture**: §3.4 (`take_position`'s user kinds) writes the fund kind; §7.7 (K-46 triggers) follows; §6.1 (5c)
follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the stage's reads frozen); S4.116 (the position generator); S4.115 (risk units); S3.182 (fund
kinds and mandates); S3.191 (managers' investing, which reads derivative positions as part of the fund's book);
S3.184 (the fund's NAV, whose writer calls K-46's crossing); S3.179 (prime-brokerage margin calls); S1.239 (K-46: a
fund's stop as a threshold on its NAV series); S1.338 (K-93: mandates' permitted classes and limits).

**Goal**: Funds take derivative positions through the position generator within their mandates: a hedge fund on its
views alone, long or short; a bond or equity fund to hedge what its mandate says. A margin call from its lenders or its
losses reaching its own stop wake its review and bind, so it cuts.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/rules/position.rs` | the fund kind's exposure reader and mandate bounds for `take_position` |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/src/decl.rs` | the stop as a K-46 threshold on the fund's NAV series; the stop's declared limit |
| `crates/systems/sys-fnd/tests/position.rs` | unit tests |

**Design**:
- **Completes**: FND.4 — a hedge fund takes derivative positions on its views, including shorts, and cuts them when its lenders call margin or its losses reach its own stop.
- **Funds' exposure**: a hedge fund's `E` is zero in every class its mandate permits (its positions carry views only);
  a bond or equity fund's is its book's sensitivity in the class's risk unit where its mandate says to hedge it (K-95
  over its holdings). The mandate's permitted classes, gross and net limits and leverage are declared limits (K-93).
- **Cutting**: a margin call from its prime broker (S3.179) or a house (S4.107) wakes its position review, where the
  options are bounded by the margin it can fund, so a call it cannot meet leaves only smaller positions. Its **stop**
  (a term of its mandate, POLICY of its manager): a K-46 threshold on its NAV series (S3.184's writer calls the
  crossing) at the declared fall from its last high; the crossing wakes the review and binds the stop's declared limit,
  leaving only options that reduce risk (Law 6: a declared limit that binds is an event the fund sees).
- S3.191's `invest` reads the fund's derivative positions as part of its book.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a crash day crosses many funds' stops at once: each is woken once (K-46, E14) and cuts on its own review
  (`stop_binds_reduce_only`).
- E2: a fund whose lenders refuse further margin: only closing options remain; a failed close is S4.112's or S4.113's
  (`margin_call_bounds_options`).
- E10: a fund ended (liquidation, FND.14): its positions close out through its estate (`LC-4-10`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `hedge_fund_exposure_is_zero`; `mandate_hedge_exposure_from_book`; `stop_binds_reduce_only`;
`margin_call_bounds_options`; `stop_threshold_on_nav_series`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-64` (FND.4) — every fund's derivative order has a decision record and lies within its mandate;
every stop crossing is followed by a review whose chosen position reduces risk; applicable from the first fund
derivative order.

**Budget**:
- Funds' reviews are counted in S4.116's share of `fin.fixed.institutions`.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-46): +0.06 MB resident (5 k stop thresholds × 12 B).
- Counters: `phx_fnd.stops_crossed`, `phx_fnd.derivative_orders`.

**Guards**: none.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a stop as a clamp on a number rather than a declared limit that binds.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §3.4 lists the fund kind among `take_position`'s users.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.124 — Implied reads, and views on both sides of every class

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: DRX.7 FORBID; DRX.6 MEASURE *(part: every read but the currency ones, which complete it at S5.173)*
**Architecture**: §14.8 (the realism reads) writes the derivative reads; §7.6 (the measurement recorder) follows.

**Depends on**: S4.100 (the reads declared); S4.118–S4.122 (every class trading); S4.106 (the swap and sovereign
curves); S1.358 (K-106: the measurement recorder's series); S1.221 (K-39: accumulators keyed by a declared attribute);
S3.127 (the sovereign curve).

**Goal**: The derivative markets' statistics are reads of their prints, published as measures: the swap spread, the
credit basis and implied default probabilities, implied volatility with its skew, futures curves against spot and
storage cost, convergence at expiry, and the difference a hedge makes to a firm's shock. Every class is checked for
participants with views on both sides, and no price in any class comes from a parity, a curve, a formula or a fixed
recovery.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/measures.rs` | the reads' estimators and their recorder series |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/src/decl.rs` | accumulator: firms' interest cost change by hedged status |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/drx.rs` | `LC-4-03`'s both-sides count |
| `crates/systems/sys-drx/tests/measures.rs` | unit tests |

**Design**:
- **Reads** (at 10d into K-106 series; no world crate reads them):
  - swap spread: each tenor's swap fixing − the sovereign curve's rate at that tenor;
  - credit basis: a name's CDS premium − its bond's spread over the sovereign curve at the same maturity;
  - implied default probability: premium ÷ (1 − the mean recovery of this world's own past CDS auctions in that
    country) — absent until an auction has printed; never fed into a premium;
  - implied volatility by strike and expiry, inverted from each option print's premium (a statistic, Law 3), and its
    skew;
  - futures curves: each contract month against spot and against its carry (storage + financing to expiry);
    convergence: the futures–spot gap at expiry;
  - hedged against unhedged firms: the change in interest cost after a rate move, from K-39's accumulator keyed by the
    firm's hedged status (a declared attribute written when its position changes).
- **DRX.7**: the prohibitions hold by construction — PC-61 (no order, limit or print from a valuation, a curve or a
  formula), S4.119 (recovery only from the auction), S4.120 (no order closes a futures–spot gap); and the forbid on
  hedger-only markets is read by `LC-4-03`: per class, country and month, the orders on each side whose option carried
  a view (means from `m ≠ p`) are counted, and a class that traded with no view on one side is a finding. Currency
  classes (S5.171) inherit the same guard and check.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: reads absent until their inputs exist (no auction yet: no implied default probability)
  (`implied_pd_absent_without_auction`).
- E2: a month with no option print has no implied volatility, never a carried value (`no_print_no_implied_vol`).

**Extension points**: S5.172 (the cross-currency basis); S5.173 (the currency reads).

**Unit tests**: `swap_spread_from_fixings`; `implied_pd_absent_without_auction`; `implied_vol_from_premium`;
`carry_curve_read`; `view_count_by_side`; `no_print_no_implied_vol`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-03` (DRX.6 part, DRX.7) — the reads are published per class and country; every formed price has
its match; views on both sides counted, a one-sided class a finding; applicable from the first derivative print.

**Budget**:
- its share of `fin.fixed.stats`: 10 / 0 / 10 core-ms (10 k derivative prints read at 10d, 1 µs each; no derivative
  market meets on a non-business day).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool, K-39): +0.02 MB resident (1 k accumulator cells × 16 B).
- Counters: `phx_drx.reads_published`.

**Guards**: PC-61 (S4.106) covers every class; `LC-4-03` runs at every gate.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a read that any party's rule reads as an input; an implied statistic fed into a price.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; fmt, clippy, tests and `phx-check` pass.
- [ ] `tools/bench.sh` at the committed resolution: the budget read, no ratchet broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §14.8 lists the derivative reads.
- [ ] The two reviews are done and their findings fixed; status `done` and the section removed.
