### Pensions, securitisation, takeovers and private equity, supervision of insurers and clearing houses; the gate (S4.142–S4.185)

These steps come after 4A–4C (S4.100–S4.141) and activate the core's bases for four systems and the supervisor's last
duties:
- **PEN**: defined-benefit schemes and their rights, defined-contribution pots, trustees, sponsors, members, the
  guarantee fund.
- **SEC**: vehicles, pools of named loans, tranches and their waterfall.
- **MNA**: offers, acceptances, completions, private equity, seeking a buyer.
- **SUP**: tests of insurers and clearing houses, licensing, the resolution identity over every kind.

The stage ends at its gate, S4.185. Every decision here is an option generator: it states options with their
consequences on the concerns its kind declares (MND.2), and the decider's mind chooses through the decision core
(S1.348, S1.352).

**Exit** (spec Part O): every derivative class forms its price with views on both sides; hazard events become insurance
claims; pension liabilities move with rates, and hedged schemes' margin moves with them; DRV.7, INS.8, PEN.7, SEC.5,
MNA.6 and SUP.7 (every resolution kind) are clean; a clearing house or an insurer past its resources is resolved through
named parties when the run has one.

**Placeholders retired here**:

| Placeholder | Clauses | Introduced | Retired by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LAB.no_pension_terms`: a vacancy's terms carry no pension, naming PEN | LAB.1 (done at S1.08; the pension a job earns) | S1.413 | S4.145 |
| Seeking a buyer, the last act of distress, naming MNA | FRM.12 | S2.121 | S4.179 |

They introduce one:

| Placeholder | Clauses | Introduced | Retired by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tax relief on members' extra contributions, missing from their weighing, naming TAX | PEN.10, TAX.4 | S4.150 | S5.120 |

PEN.10 completes at S5.120, where the last placeholder standing in it is retired. LAB.1 stays done at S1.08; S4.145
retires its placeholder.

**Where the state lives** (bases only; nothing new):
- DB rights are rows of the **pension-rights** family (K-53, `Balance` layout; S1.257) between a scheme and a person.
  The row's own amount is the right in the scheme's accrued-pension unit (K-22; S1.183).
- DC pots are `pension-rights` rows between a trust and a person (K-53; S1.257), their own amount in the units of the
  fund they hold; the trust holds each fund's units in aggregate, one holding per fund (K-60; S1.280).
- A scheme's liability is an exact sum over its members' rows, valued by a declared sweep on the valuation weekday its
  queue reaches it (K-95's sweep representation; S1.341) against the funding curve (K-91; S1.335), and rolled forward
  between valuations as a party position series (S1.239).
- A member's two lumpy pension choices are its attention's review days (K-101, K-43; S1.350, S1.227).
- Pools are loan contracts whose lender side is the vehicle (K-57; S1.267), and tranches are instruments (K-64; S1.279).
- Takeover offers are public events on the event log (S1.213) that redraw each holder of record's `portfolio` occasion
  (K-101, K-43; S1.350, S1.227). Tenders are liens (K-63; S1.277).
- Tranche payments and write-downs are instrument events to holders of record (K-65; S1.281).
- Completions are link groups (K-48, K-49; S1.245, S1.248).

### S4.142 — Pension schemes, rights and the accrued-pension unit declared

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: PEN.2 STATE *(part: the scheme as a party, its benefit design as terms)*
**Architecture**: §3.4 (writes: the PEN declarations); §7.3, §7.9 (follows: the kind catalogue, units, families).
**Depends on**: S1.485 (the `pension_scheme` kind, with its sponsor link and account, and the DB pensions in payment it
pays); S1.180 (the kind catalogue compiles the declarations); S1.183 (special non-money units); S1.196 (typed kind
columns, sparse cold columns included); S1.209 (the trustee board as an office); S1.257 (families with declared
layouts); S1.263 (interned terms shapes).

**Goal**: the pension objects the later PEN steps hold are declared as data, and none is a new store: the scheme kind's
columns and office, the DC trust kind, the pension-rights, recovery-plan and compensation families, the design shape,
the reasons, and the accrued-pension unit with its compile-level guard. The tallies, the index instance and the
decision kinds follow at S4.143.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/declare.rs` | kind columns, families, the design shape, reasons and the unit kind declared to the kind catalogue (S1.180) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/units.rs` | `AccruedPension` (a typed quantity in index units), its two conversions and the PC-64 compile-level guard |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/declare.rs` | logic-level tests below |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/compile_fail/accrued_pension.rs` | PC-64's compile-fail test |

**Design**:
- **Kinds** (K-21, K-32 columns):
  - `pension_scheme` (the kind S1.485 declares with its sponsor and account): this step adds section count u8, design
    shape (terms id u32), revaluation index handle, year-end day u16, schedule-of-contributions rate (`Rate`, `Missing`
    until its first valuation), first valuation reference day u32 (its founding or opening day), last valuation day u32,
    funding state u8, and the office trustee board (K-34), whose holder decides `trustees` (S4.143).
  - `pension_trust`: a DC trust. Its fund menu is up to 8 fund instrument ids inline in a cold column, and beyond them a
    K-04 block list (the menu is the trust's own choice, never capped); its fee point; its sponsoring employers' count.
- **Unit** (K-22 special unit kind `accrued_pension`): one unit id per (scheme, revaluation index). A right's quantity
  is in **index units**: a slice accrued on day d adds `pay × accrual rate ÷ I(d)`, where I is the index as published by
  day d (K-37). Its money value on day t is `units × I(t)`, a read, rounded once by the scheme's convention (REP.9).
  Revaluation is exact, with no pass: the index moves and the rows do not.
- **Families** (K-53):
  - `pension_rights` (`Balance` layout, 24 B): side A the scheme, which keeps no side list (walks are rare: a valuation
    work day and a wind-up, each a declared sweep); side B the person, on its person chain. Own amount: units. Status
    active or deferred; the terms are the scheme's design shape. Due filing is from the terms and the person's birth
    date (pension age), with no own due. At an ending, a right goes to its survivor's destination, else it ends. A **DC
    pot** is a row of the same family: side A the trust, side B the member; its own amount is in the units of the one
    fund its terms name, which the trust holds in aggregate (one K-60 holding per (trust, fund), S1.280), so no member
    has a holding row of its own. It carries a sparse cold column of the member's two review days (u16 each, S4.150). At
    an ending, a pot goes to the member's estate.
  - `recovery_plan` (`Dated`, sponsor → scheme), paid on its schedule.
  - `compensation` (guarantee fund → person, `Balance`).
- **Design shape** (K-55 terms, interned): accrual rate, pension age, revaluation index (active and deferred),
  indexation in payment, survivor share, early-retirement reduction per month, pensionable-pay definition.
- **Reasons** (K-21), each with its lines and levy set: employee contribution, employer contribution, DC contribution,
  member's extra contribution, accrual follow-on (units), benefit, repair payment, guarantee levy, compensation.
- **Guard PC-64** (compile level, in `units.rs`): `AccruedPension` has exactly two conversions to money. The first is
  the actuary's valuation (K-95's sweep, S1.341). The second is the benefit due of a pension in payment, fixed at
  retirement. There is none to a money balance, so no promise is a cash balance (PEN.7).

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a country with no DB scheme declares the kinds and opens none, and every rule runs over an empty set. Test:
  `empty_country_declares_nothing`.
- E8: a trust's menu beyond 8 funds goes to its block list. Test: `menu_overflow_to_block_list`.
- E12: the schedule rate is `Missing` until the first valuation, never a default. Test:
  `schedule_rate_missing_until_valued`.

**Extension points**: S4.143 (the tallies and decision kinds on these kinds and families); S4.144 (the law's
handles); S4.145–S4.148, S4.152, S4.154 and S4.182 read these declarations; S5.126 reuses `pension_rights` and `accrued_pension` for the
earnings-related state right, with the social-insurance agency as side A; S6.128 reads rights and pots as a
household's pension saving.

**Unit tests**: `accrued_pension_converts_only_two_ways` (compile-fail); `index_units_value_exact` (units × I(t) rounded
once, equal to the sum of slices revalued); `empty_country_declares_nothing`; `menu_overflow_to_block_list`;
`schedule_rate_missing_until_valued`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Time: none on day paths (declarations compiled at assembly).
- Resident bytes:
  - ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (`pension_rights` 24 B a row × `[store.contracts] pension_rights`, S1.257's mix, DB
    rights and ≈ 2 M DC pots alike; status in the row's flags)
  - ledger line 11 (holdings and lots): +0 B (inside S1.280's holdings: one per (trust, fund), ≈ 5000)
  - ledger line 6 (institutions): +1 MB resident (≈ 5 k schemes × 26 B, ≈ 1 k trusts × 40 B, and S4.152's 160 B of
    sensitivities per scheme)

**Guards**: PC-64 registered (compile level, `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/units.rs`).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a kind branch on scheme type (DB and DC differ by declared data); a cap on a trust's menu.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations and `AccruedPension` with their tests; PC-64 registered.
- [ ] Fast checks (`fmt`, `clippy`, tests, `phx-check all`); the bench at the committed resolution with no ratchet
  broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §3.4 written (the PEN kinds, unit and families); two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.143 — Pension tallies, the pending pots' instance and the pension decision kinds declared

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §3.4 (writes: the PEN tallies and decision kinds); §7.9 (follows: tallies, the index instance).
**Depends on**: S4.142 (the kinds, families and reasons these key on); S1.254 (declared tallies); S1.165 (a declared
index instance); S1.196 (sparse cold columns); S1.348 (decision kinds with office, concerns and mode).

**Goal**: the pension tallies, the member's sparse entry, the index instance of pots pending and the six pension
decision kinds are declared as data through the bases' extension points, so the later PEN steps only fill and read
them.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/declare.rs` | tallies, the sparse person entry, the index instance and the decision kinds declared |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/declare.rs` | logic-level tests below |

**Design**:
- It serves PEN.2 and PEN.10's later steps (S4.145–S4.155), which complete them.
- **Tallies, columns and the index instance** (declarations through the extension points of K-52, K-32 and K-06):
  - pensionable pay this scheme year, per employment row of DB terms, saved: this step's own word, keyed by the row.
    Every DB member needs it, because the slice is fixed at I(d) of the year-end on the whole year's pay (E 32), and
    I(d) is not known until that day, so no pay can be accrued into the right as it is paid;
  - DC pending, per pot row (K-52, sparse: present only between a payday and its dealing), saved;
  - the member's chosen extra rate, a sparse cold person entry (rate point u16, keyed by person), present once the
    member has chosen, saved;
  - the instance "pots pending by (trust, fund)" (K-06), `#[saved(skip, rebuild)]`: a pot joins with its first
    contribution after a dealing and leaves at the allotment, so it holds members only from payday to dealing; rebuilt
    at load from the pending tallies, ≈ 60 ns a pot.
- **Decision kinds** (K-100), each declared `{ name, taken_in, concerns, mode }` with its concerns as `ConcernH` handles
  (MND.2) and its mode (MND.7):

  | Decision | Taken in | Concerns | Mode |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `offer_scheme` | the firm's chief executive | means, security | best |
  | `trustees` | the scheme's trustee board | means, security, principle | best |
  | `repair` | the sponsor's chief executive | means, security | best |
  | `pension_rate` | person (the member, PEN.10; its view reads its household's position) | means, security, wealth and legacy | best |
  | `pension_fund` | person (the member, PEN.10; its view reads its household's position) | means, security, wealth and legacy | best |
  | `at_retirement` | person (the member, PEN.10; its view reads its household's position) | means, security, wealth and legacy | best |

**Edge cases**:
- E6: the tallies and the sparse column are saved; the index instance is rebuilt from the pending tallies. Test:
  `pending_instance_rebuilds_equal`.
- E13: a scheme with no DB member keeps no pensionable-pay word. Test: `no_db_member_no_tally`.

**Extension points**: S4.145 (`offer_scheme`), S4.146 (the pensionable-pay tally), S4.148 (the pending tally and
instance), S4.150 (`pension_rate`, `pension_fund`, the sparse entry), S4.151 (`at_retirement`), S4.154 (`repair`),
S4.155 (`trustees`).

**Unit tests**: `pending_instance_rebuilds_equal`; `no_db_member_no_tally`; `decision_kinds_declared_with_concerns`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- Time: none on day paths (declarations compiled at assembly); the instance's rebuild at load, ≈ 60 ms at a payday-peak
  load (≈ 1 M pending pots × 60 ns), 0 otherwise.
- Resident bytes:
  - ledger line 18 (records): +16 MB resident (≈ 2 M DB employment rows × 8 B pensionable-pay tally, needed for every DB
    member: the year's pay awaits the year-end's index)
  - ledger line 2 (persons): +8 MB resident (≈ 1 M DC members who have decided × 8 B, sparse)
  - ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B standing; its own item, the DC pending window: +16 MB at the payday peak (≈
    1 M contributing pots × (8 B pending tally + 8 B instance membership)), held from payday to dealing
  - saved: +24 MB (the tallies and the sparse column; the instance is rebuilt)

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tally kept where a row's own amount serves.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations with their tests.
- [ ] Fast checks (`fmt`, `clippy`, tests, `phx-check all`); the bench at the committed resolution with no ratchet
  broken.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §3.4 extended (the PEN tallies and decision kinds); two reviews; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S4.144 — Pension law mapped for the three countries

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: data

**Clauses**: PEN.11 PRIMITIVE; SUP.13 STATE *(part: the pension guarantee fund's law)*
**Architecture**: §3.4 (follows).

**Depends on**: S4.142 (the scheme kind and the families the law governs); S1.179 (dated POLICY schedules with an
owner); S1.345 (a wind-up's order of rights as a declared class order).

**Goal**: each country's pension law is declared data, owned by its legislature, with a source for every value: the
funding rules, the deficit-repair schedule, the guarantee fund and its entry conditions, and the order of members'
rights on a wind-up.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/law.rs` | `PensionLaw` read from the register: a handle to each POLICY schedule |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/law.rs` | tests below |
| `data/<country>/PEN.toml` | pension law per country (POLICY, owner the legislature), each entry with its source |

**Design**:
- **Pension law** (PEN.11; each a `PolicySchedule` on K-20, owned by the legislature):
  - the valuation interval and the actuaries' turnaround (TECHNOLOGY of the actuarial firms, with its source);
  - the funding curve's publisher (swap or sovereign; both are traded curves, never a fixed rate);
  - the longest recovery period;
  - auto-enrolment minima;
  - the regulator's minimum collateral buffer, where the law declares one;
  - the guarantee fund's existence, entry conditions, cap per person and levy formula (SUP.13);
  - the order of members' rights on a wind-up, as a K-98 class order.
- **Sources**: the normal pension age from `oecd/pensions`; the laws' entries from the typed tables of each country's
  pension law named in the file, each with its reference. What no source gives is absent, and the rules that read it
  refuse or skip visibly (a country with no guarantee fund declares none, and nothing reads a zero cap).
- State-pension rules stay SOC's (S5.122).

**Edge cases**:
- E12: an absent entry is refused at assembly where a rule needs it, or is a named `Missing`. Test:
  `absent_guarantee_fund_is_missing`.
- E13: a country with no guarantee fund. Test: `no_fund_country_reads_none`.
- E6: the schedules are saved (K-20) with their dated changes. Test: `law_schedule_round_trip`.

**Extension points**: S4.145 (auto-enrolment), S4.152 and S4.153 (valuation interval, turnaround, funding curve,
recovery period), S4.156 (minimum buffer), S4.157 (the order of rights), S4.158 (the guarantee fund) read these handles.

**Unit tests**: `absent_guarantee_fund_is_missing`; `no_fund_country_reads_none`; `law_schedule_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- ledger line 1 (process): +0 B (≈ 300 dated schedules × 64 B within the register, S1.179).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a fixed discount rate or a default cap standing in for an absent law; a value without its source; a
fetch of new data.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `PensionLaw` and `data/<country>/PEN.toml` for the three countries, every value with its source; tests.
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.145 — Employers offer pensions; single-employer schemes established

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: SUP.9 PROCESS *(part: a single-employer scheme established by its sponsor under pension law)*
**Architecture**: §3.4, §6.1 (follows: slots 5c, 5d, 3b).

**Depends on**: S4.142 (kinds, shapes); S4.143 (the `offer_scheme` decision kind); S4.144 (the auto-enrolment minimum); S1.348 (option
generators through the decision core); S1.352 (the chief executive's mind chooses); S1.227 (wakes by need); S1.413
(vacancies carry terms; its placeholder); S1.490 (a new party created at 3b); S8.103, S8.122 (an office holder decides
with its own mind, the mandate entering through its contracts).

**Goal**: an employer decides, on its founding and when hiring proves hard, whether its jobs carry a pension, and of
which kind. A DB choice founds a scheme party that the employer sponsors. Vacancies posted from then on carry the chosen
terms, which retires S1.413's placeholder.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/rules/offer_scheme.rs` | the option generator and its consequences |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/rules/establish.rs` | the scheme's founding instruction |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/offer_scheme.rs` | tests below |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the form's source (equalising differences, Rosen 1986) |

**Design**:
- **When** (occasions by need only, so the firm's record carries no stake for this kind): on its founding, and when a
  vacancy stays unfilled past the firm's own patience (a surprise at its vacancy book, REP.35, woken through K-43).
  Decided at 5c.
- **Options** (a pure `options(view: &OfferSchemeView, out: &mut OptionSet)` over the firm's own state; each option's
  `Consequences` hold one `Fixed` per declared concern):
  - none;
  - DC at each contribution point of the law's minimum menu, through each multi-employer trust in its reach (its
    published fee) or a trust of its own;
  - DB with each design shape its country declares.
- **Consequences**, from the firm's own view:
  - **means**: the wage it would otherwise post to fill its vacancies within its patience, read from its own fill record
    on K-54 and the vacancy book; less the option's cost per worker (rates × its wage bill, K-54); less the
    administration hours at its own wage.
  - **security**: for DB, the width of its own outlook of the funding cost (VAL.8), at its outlook's rate.
  - The law's auto-enrolment minimum is a declared limit (K-93). An option below it is not generated, and the binding is
    an event the firm sees (Law 6).
- **Apply** (5d):
  - The chosen pension terms join the firm's employment terms (K-55 interned), and its vacancies re-post with them
    (K-70).
  - Existing jobs keep their contract terms until both parties agree otherwise, which is LAB's matter.
  - A DB choice writes a founding instruction: a `pension_scheme` party begins at the next day's 3b (K-31, K-32), with
    the firm as sponsor, its first contribution a flow from the firm's account, and its trustee office vacant. While the
    office is vacant, it reads the founding preferences (MND.16). The scheme's first valuation reference day is its
    founding day, so its first valuation (S4.152) sets the employer's rate; until then that rate is `Missing` and no
    employer contribution is levied (S4.146).
- **Cost**: the review costs the deciding office's hours (Law 14).
- **Streams**: none; the mind's choice draws on its own declared taste stream.
- **Placeholder retired**: S1.413's `LAB.no_pension_terms` (naming PEN), the placeholder in LAB.1 (done at S1.08); its
  primitive row and use are deleted.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a firm with no staff and no vacancies generates only the option "none". Test: `no_staff_only_none`.
- E10: a sponsor ending before the scheme's founding day means the instruction lapses. The founding reads the sponsor's
  liveness at 3b. Test: `founding_lapses_on_ended_sponsor`.
- E13: a country with no DC trust in reach generates no trust option. Test: `no_trust_in_reach`.
- E14: a founding and a review on one day read the stage's start state. Test: `founding_and_review_read_start_state`.
- E11: no scheme is founded on day zero (the opening's schemes stand). Test: `no_founding_on_day_zero`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**:
- `offer_scheme_equalising_difference`: over given fill histories and costs, the means consequence of an option equals
  the wage saved less its cost.
- `auto_enrolment_minimum_bounds_options`.
- `no_staff_only_none`.
- `founding_lapses_on_ended_sponsor`.
- `no_trust_in_reach`.
- `founding_and_review_read_start_state`.
- `no_founding_on_day_zero`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-80` registered (read at the gate): every job with pension terms names an employer whose
`offer_scheme` chose them. Every scheme names its sponsor, its founding day and its first contribution's flow.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 2 / 0 / 2 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 2 k occasions a business day (firms whose
  vacancy outlasted their patience, a share of `[store] vacancies`), each ≤ 8 options × 100 ns (K-102) + 30 ns handler.
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (occasions by need: no next-day slot).
- Counters: `phx_pen.offer_scheme_occasions`, `phx_pen.schemes_established`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a pension offered because of the firm's size or kind (a kind branch); a job's terms rewritten
without the contract's parties.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule and its tests; the placeholder's code and its `phx-check` count removed.
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; `LC-4-80` registered (read at the
  gate).
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.146 — Defined-benefit rights accrue as revalued career-average slices

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.2 STATE *(part: rights accrued as revalued slices)*; PEN.4 PROCESS *(part: DB contributions deducted at
payroll)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: slots 7a for levies; 4a for a job's end; the scheme's year-end on the agenda).

**Depends on**: S4.142 (family, unit, reasons); S1.253 (levy engine: contributions fused into the payroll
batch); S4.143's pensionable-pay tally; S1.227 (the scheme's year-end on the agenda); S1.215 (the revaluation index as
published); S1.270, S1.435 (wages paid with levies); S4.145 (DB terms on jobs); S1.343 (the ending kernel posts a dying
member's slice); S1.171 (the year-end walk as a declared sweep).

**Goal**: a DB job's wage pays its employee's and employer's contributions to the scheme at payroll. Each scheme year's
pensionable pay then adds a slice to the member's right, in index units, so the right is revalued exactly with no pass.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/levy.rs` | the contribution levy set of DB terms: employee rate from terms, employer rate from the scheme's schedule |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/accrual.rs` | `accrue_slice`, `accrued_schedule` (pure) and the year-end and job-end rules |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/accrual.rs` | tests below |

**Design**:
- **Contributions** (PEN.4) come from a levy set declared on the wage reason for DB terms (K-51), fused at emission,
  each rounded once:
  - the employee's rate (terms), deducted;
  - the employer's rate (the scheme's schedule-of-contributions column), added. Until the scheme's first valuation
    (S4.152) the rate is `Missing`: no employer item is levied, and each wage without one is counted
    (`phx_pen.employer_rate_missing`); nothing stands in for it.

  Both are paid to the scheme's account. The pensionable pay of the wage is added to the employment row's
  pensionable-pay tally (S4.142), in the same apply.
- **The slice** (PEN.2, E 32): `accrue_slice(pay, rate, I(d), convention) -> units = round(pay × rate ÷ I(d))`, a pure
  function, where d is the slice's day. It is posted:
  - on the **scheme year's end** (the scheme's agenda entry, K-43; the reason is business-only, since a scheme's
    administrator posts on business days, so a year-end on a closed day posts on the next business day, reading the
    closed year's tally by its period stamp, exactly): the rule walks the sponsor's employment side list (K-53) over
    rows with this scheme's terms, spread over the declared sweep's days (below). The walk is registered as a declared
    sweep with reason "scheme year-end" (`#[sweep(store = employment, cycle = reason)]`, K-14), cycled over 15 business
    days, all before the next month-end payday, so the sweep ledger counts its rows per day. Each slice is fixed at I(d)
    of the year-end day and the closed year's tally, so the day it is posted does not change it. For each row, it reads
    the tally, computes the slice, adds it to the member's active right, and resets the tally by its period stamp. The
    right is found on the person chain (k bounded by REP.31) and opened on the member's first slice;
  - on a **job's end** (4a), for that row alone, with the tally to date.
- **No aggregate is maintained**: the scheme's liability is valued by S4.152's sweep over the rows (K-95's sweep
  representation), so a slice writes only the right's own units.
- **`accrued_schedule(right, day)`** is a pure read of the member's annual pension in money at its pension age: units ×
  I (as published by that day), with the terms' indexation and survivor share. HH.7's valuation (S6.128) and retirement
  (S4.149) read it.
- A slice is posted into a right, never into money. The only conversions are PC-64's.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: the scheme year-ends of many schemes fall on one date (a calendar year-end). The walk costs the sponsors' DB rows
  only, on the pool by sponsor, on the first business day after it. Test: `closed_year_end_posts_next_business_day`.
- E12: a scheme not yet valued levies no employer item. Test: `no_employer_item_until_first_valuation`.
- E14: a job ending on the scheme's year-end. The 4a slice posts first, the row is closed and its tally reset, and the
  year-end walk skips it. Test: `year_end_and_leaving_same_day_once`.
- E12: an index with no publication yet reads its last publication with its age. An index never published is refused at
  assembly. Test: `slice_reads_index_as_published`.
- E10: a member dying before the year-end. The ending kernel (S1.343) posts the slice to date through the family's
  ending rule before the row's destination. Test: `death_posts_slice_to_date`.
- E6: tallies and rights are primary columns, saved. Test: `rights_round_trip`.
- E8: units in i64 at the index's fixed point; overflow stops. Test: `units_overflow_stops`.

**Extension points**: `accrue_slice` and `accrued_schedule` are read by S4.149, S4.152, S4.157, S4.147, S5.126 (the
earnings-related state right) and S6.128 (HH.7).

**Unit tests**:
- `db_accrual_slice_exact`: a slice for pay not divisible by the index, rounded once.
- `revaluation_by_index_equals_revalued_slices`: the value after index moves equals each slice revalued.
- `contributions_fused_at_payroll`: employee and employer items for a given wage and rates.
- `year_end_and_leaving_same_day_once`.
- `slice_reads_index_as_published`.
- `death_posts_slice_to_date`.
- `rights_round_trip`.
- `closed_year_end_posts_next_business_day`.
- `no_employer_item_until_first_valuation`.
- `units_overflow_stops`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-20` registered (read at the gate; PEN.7): every DB contribution levied at payroll landed in its
scheme's account the same day. Every scheme-year slice equals its tally × rate ÷ the index as published, on a named
member's right. Every scheme with a liability has members.

**Budget**:
- adds 2 phone-ns to fin.dues.item_ns at 0 / 0 / 2 M items (the levies are fused at emission at no added cost, S1.253;
  the work beyond them is the pensionable-pay tally add, once on each of ≈ 2 M DB wages; a non-quarter month-end payday
  carries the same)
- spread after fin.calendar.scheme_year_end over 15 days: 4 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.close_books (the year-end sweep
  cycled over 15 business days before the next payday: ≈ 2 M active members sharing one year-end, a slice being a tally
  read, a chain walk of ≤ 5 links and a row write, ≈ 30 ns; each slice at I(d) of the year-end day, so the spread is
  exact); joins H and B′ where its days fall on them
- ledger line 18 (records): +0 B (the pensionable-pay tally is counted at S4.142)
- Counters: `phx_pen.slices`, `phx_pen.db_contributions`.

**Guards**: PC-64 applies (no change).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a revaluation pass rewriting every right; a contribution computed on an aggregate payroll; a right
averaged across members.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules and tests; `LC-4-20` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.147 — The opening's pension rights and pots

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: data

**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §10.3 (follows: canonical drawing of a kind's opening); §10.0a (follows: the opening dataset).

**Depends on**: S1.485 (the opening's DB schemes, sponsors and pensions in payment, which this step's rights join; its
derived DB active share and DB asset allocation, read from its `data/<country>/gen/PEN.toml`); S4.142 (kinds, families,
unit); S4.146 (`accrue_slice`, used to express opening rights in index units); S1.123 (`#[opening]` rules); S3.182
(funds whose units the pots hold).

**Goal**: the opening world holds each DB scheme's active members' and deferred members' rights, and each DC member's
pot, drawn from the data in hand, with the schemes' assets balancing them.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/gen.rs` | `#[opening]` draws: active and deferred rights, pots, scheme assets |
| `data/<country>/gen/PEN.toml` | the deferred members' share and the DC participation and assets, with their sources, added beside S1.485's keys |
| `data/inventory.toml` | `markets/pension_main_2019` (5200 only), `markets/pension_structure` (DCA with DCP and DCU only), `markets/pension_participation` → the primitives, this step |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/gen.rs` | tests below |

**Design**:
- It serves GEN.4 (balanced opening balance sheets). The schemes, their sponsors and the DB pensions in payment are
  S1.485's (Part O's Stage 0); this step adds the rights still accruing and the pots. Only the columns S1.485 does not
  map are mapped here; its derived DB values are read, never derived again.
- **Rights**: active members from S1.485's DB active share of employment; deferred members from
  `markets/pension_main_2019` 5200, mapped here. Each active member's opening right is its career-average equivalent (E
  32), drawn by age and tenure from its job's start date and expressed in index units through `accrue_slice` at the
  opening's index. Deferred members are drawn among persons with a past job and no current DB job, by age (stream
  `PEN.open_right`).
- **Pots**: DC participation by plan type (`markets/pension_participation`) and DC assets (`markets/pension_structure`,
  measure DCA for definitions DCP and DCU), drawn as `pension_rights` rows of the trusts in the units of the opening's
  funds by the member's age (stream `PEN.open_pot`); each trust's holding of a fund is the sum of its pots in it.
- **Scheme assets**: the classes S1.485 reported as not opened (bonds, shares, fund units) are drawn as holdings by
  S1.485's derived DB asset allocation. A scheme's assets less its liability is its opening surplus or deficit: an
  outcome of the draws, never fitted (GEN.4).
- **Streams**: `PEN.open_right`, `PEN.open_pot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: day zero. Rights stand, and each scheme's first valuation reference day is the opening day. Test:
  `first_reference_day_is_opening`.
- E12: a country missing a series gets no draw from it; the step names the missing series and invents nothing. Test:
  `missing_series_refused_not_zero`.
- E13: a country with no occupational pensions in the data opens no right and no pot. Test:
  `no_occupational_opens_none`.
- E6: the opening's draws are state, saved like any other. Test: `opening_rights_round_trip`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `opening_right_in_index_units`; `balance_sheet_balances`; `first_reference_day_is_opening`;
`missing_series_refused_not_zero`; `no_occupational_opens_none`; `opening_rights_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-84` registered (read at the gate): every opening right and pot names its scheme or trust and its
person, and schemes' assets and liabilities balance their surplus.

**Budget**:
- Time: opening only (outside the turn): ≈ 4.5 M rights and ≈ 1 M pots at ≤ 200 ns a draw ≈ 1.1 core-s within the
  opening.
- Resident bytes: ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (rights counted at S4.142); ledger line 11 (holdings and lots): +0 B
  (one trust holding per (trust, fund), counted at S4.142).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; an opening funding ratio or deficit
imported as a target; a fetch of new data.

### S4.148 — Defined-contribution contributions dealt at the next value

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.3 STATE *(part: the pot fed by contributions)*; PEN.4 PROCESS *(part: DC contributions deducted at
payroll)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: slots 7a for levies; 6a for the dealing; 7d for units).

**Depends on**: S4.142 (reasons); S4.143 (the pending tally, the instance "pots pending by (trust, fund)"); S1.253 (levies fused
at emission in the pay item's dues legs); S1.254 (tallies); S1.165 (the declared index instance); S3.185 (forward-priced
dealing at the next NAV); S1.172 (apportionment with a named residue); S1.280 (the trust's holding of each fund's
units); S1.270, S1.435; S4.145 (DC terms on jobs).

**Goal**: a DC job's wage pays the employee's deduction, the employer's addition and the member's chosen extra to the
member's trust at payroll. Each member's amount waits as a recorded commitment until the trust's single subscription per
fund is dealt at the next value. Units then land in each member's pot, with the rounding residue on the fund.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/dc.rs` | DC levy set; the trust's daily subscription; the allotment |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/dc.rs` | tests below |

**Design**:
- **Levies** (K-51) on the wage reason for DC terms, fused at emission as dues legs of the pay item (S1.253), each
  rounded once:
  - the employee's rate (terms);
  - the employer's rate (terms, at least the law's minimum);
  - the member's extra rate (its sparse entry, written by S4.150; before its first decision, or when it chose none, no
    item is emitted, never an item of zero).

  They are paid to the trust's dealing account. The levy's follow-on adds each member's total to its pot's pending tally
  (K-52, keyed by the pot row). A pot (a `pension_rights` row, S4.142) opens on the member's first contribution with the
  trust's default fund. The first contribution after a dealing joins the pot to the instance "pots pending by (trust,
  fund)" (K-06); later ones before the dealing only add to the tally. The pending amount is a commitment on both books
  (REG.10): the member's subscription and the trust's order.
- **Order**: at the day's end, one subscription per (trust, fund) for the day's sum, placed in the fund's dealing
  (S3.185). It is taken with the next business day's orders and dealt at that day's NAV (MKT.16's one exception).
- **Allotment**: when the dealing settles, the instance's pots for that (trust, fund) are walked, and the units bought
  are apportioned over them by their pending amounts. This is K-16's largest remainder, with the residue to the fund
  (FND.9). The units bought land in the trust's one holding of that fund (one K-60 write), and each pot row's own amount
  is raised by its share: the member's claim, outside liquid wealth until pension age, and read so by HH. The pending
  tallies are cleared and the instance emptied for that (trust, fund).
- A pot is the member's `pension_rights` row counted in fund units; there is **no membership row** and no holding row
  per member.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a monthly payday puts every DC member's contribution into one dealing. The allotment costs one pass over that
  day's pending pots on the pool. Test: `payday_allotment_one_pass`.
- E1: a fund gated or suspended (FND.11, S3.192). The order carries forward by the fund's rule, and pending stays
  pending (counted). Test: `pending_persists_while_gated`.
- E10: a member dying with pending. The pending tally is part of its estate's claims on the trust, and the units are
  allotted to the pot row, which has passed to its estate. Test: `pending_passes_to_estate`.
- E14: two contributions to one pot before one dealing. The tally sums them. Test: `two_contributions_one_allotment`.
- E6: pending tallies are saved; the instance is `#[saved(skip, rebuild)]` from the pending tallies (≈ 60 ns a pot at
  load); the order is live across the save. Test: `pending_round_trip`.
- E12: an absent extra rate emits no item. Test: `absent_extra_rate_no_item`.

**Extension points**: S4.150 writes the extra rate and switches funds. S4.151 redeems pots.

**Unit tests**:
- `dc_units_at_next_nav_residue_on_fund`.
- `pending_allotment_until_dealing`.
- `two_contributions_one_allotment`.
- `pending_persists_while_gated`.
- `pending_passes_to_estate`.
- `pending_round_trip`.
- `payday_allotment_one_pass`.
- `absent_extra_rate_no_item`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-20` (extended) registered (read at the gate): every DC contribution levied at payroll is pending
on its pot until the dealing it was taken for, then units at that dealing. Pending sums equal the trust's open orders.

**Budget**:
- adds 10 phone-ns to fin.dues.item_ns at 0 / 0 / 1 M items (the levies ride the pay item's dues legs at no added cost,
  S1.253; the follow-on's pending-tally add, 2 ns, and the pot's instance join, 8 ns, once on each of ≈ 1 M DC wages
  expected at the design point; a non-quarter month-end payday carries the same)
- on fin.calendar.dc_dealing (the business day after a DC payday): 19 core-ms (≈ 1 M allotments × (15 ns apportion + 3.4
  ns row update)); joins B′ when the payday precedes four closed days, never H. It cannot spread over the pay window:
  units are dealt only at the value formed after the contribution (MKT.16)
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (the pending window's peak is counted at S4.142)
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (pots are `pension_rights` rows, counted at S4.142); ledger line 11 (holdings and
  lots): +0 B (one trust holding per (trust, fund), counted at S4.142)
- Counters: `phx_pen.allotments`, `phx_pen.pending_pots`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an order per member (one per trust and fund a day); units at a price not yet formed; a DC membership
row.

### S4.149 — Leaving and retiring: deferred rights, pensions in payment, deaths end them

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.4 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: slots 4a for jobs ending, 3b for deaths, 7a for benefits); §7.15 (follows: endings'
destinations).

**Depends on**: S4.146 (slices, `accrued_schedule`); S4.148 (pots); S1.343 (the ending kernel applies each family's
declared destination); S1.263 (indexed amounts in payment); S1.225 (the right filed at its pension age); S1.419 (the
person's retire decision ends its job); S1.485 (the pensions-in-payment family paid by schemes); S1.207 (the
household's partner role).

**Goal**: a member leaving a DB job keeps a deferred right, and one retiring, or reaching pension age while deferred,
gets a pension in payment fixed from its right. Benefits are paid monthly by the scheme to living members. A death ends
them and passes the survivor's share to a named survivor. A DC pot is unchanged by leaving, and S4.151 decides it at
retirement.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/status.rs` | leaving, retiring, pension age reached; the right's destinations at death |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/status.rs` | tests below |

**Design**:
- **Leaving** (the employment row closes at 4a): S4.146's slice to date posts. The right's status becomes deferred.
  Where the deferred revaluation index differs, the units convert once at `I_active(d) ÷ I_deferred(d)`, rounded by the
  scheme's convention.
- **Retiring**:
  - On the job's end by the member's retire decision (S1.419), or on the right's pension-age date (filed on the wheel
    from its terms and the member's birth date, K-42): the right closes, and a **pension in payment** opens (S1.485's
    family, payer the scheme).
  - Its amount is `accrued_schedule(right, d) × (1 − early reduction × months early)`, rounded once.
  - Its indexation in payment is by its terms (K-55 indexed amounts, read as published).
- **Benefits** are the pensions in payment's monthly dues, streamed at 7a (K-42 → K-55), paid by the scheme to the
  member's own account (E 48). A scheme short of cash fails the due visibly (SET.3), and it becomes the scheme's
  arrears, which S4.157 reads.
- **Deaths** (PEN.4, POP.3): the ending kernel (S1.343) applies the families' declared destinations.
  - A pension in payment or a right ends at the death.
  - Where the terms carry a survivor share and the member has a partner (its household's partner role at the death,
    K-33), a pension in payment opens to the partner. Its amount is the share of the right's value, rounded once.
  - Nothing is paid to the dead: the ending closes the row the same day, before stage 7's dues.
- **Retirement income**: a household's income moves from wages to the pensions its persons hold, read from their
  contracts (PEN's Done when).

**Edge cases**:
- E14: a death and a benefit due on one day. The ending (3b) closes the row, so the due is never raised, since the due
  is filed from the live row. Test: `death_before_due_pays_nothing`.
- E10: a scheme ending (wind-up) while rights point at it: the rights keep pointing at the scheme's estate until its
  wind-up (S4.157) moves them. Test: `rights_follow_scheme_to_estate`.
- E5: a month's pensions in payment on the H day (`[store.contracts] "SOC.pension"`, 2.25 M dues), streamed by the
  dues chain. Test: `benefits_stream_on_month_end`.
- E3: a member with no partner: the survivor share has no destination and the right ends. Test:
  `no_partner_no_survivor`.
- E12: no index publication since the right's last slice: the retirement amount reads the latest with its age. Test:
  `retirement_reads_latest_index`.
- E6: rights, pensions in payment and the wheel entries rebuilt from each row's terms. Test:
  `pension_age_filing_rebuilds`.

**Extension points**: S4.151 reads the retire event for DC pots; S4.157 moves every right at a wind-up.

**Unit tests**:
- `leaver_right_converts_once`: the index-to-index conversion is rounded once.
- `retirement_amount_with_early_reduction`.
- `survivor_share_to_partner`.
- `no_partner_no_survivor`.
- `death_before_due_pays_nothing`.
- `pension_age_filing_rebuilds`.
- `rights_follow_scheme_to_estate`.
- `benefits_stream_on_month_end`.
- `retirement_reads_latest_index`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-21` registered (read at the gate; PEN.4): members retiring move from wages to the pensions of the
kinds they hold, published by kind. Every benefit payment names a living member or a survivor. Deaths end benefits the
same day. Every deferred right reaching pension age became a pension in payment.

**Budget**:
- adds 1000 / 0 / 1000 items to fin.contracts.open_ns (leaving and retiring: a share of the ≈ 5.4 k job ends a day in DB
  terms, each a status write and ≤ one open or close).
- adds 0 / 0 / 0 items to fin.dues.item_ns (the DB pensions in payment are already in `[store.contracts]
  pensions_in_payment` and `[day.h] dues`).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (pensions in payment in S1.257's mix).
- Counters: `phx_pen.retirements`, `phx_pen.survivor_pensions`, `phx_pen.deferred`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; benefits paid to the dead; a pension amount averaged over members; a right that vanishes at a death
without its declared destination.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rules and tests; `LC-4-21` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.150 — Members choose extra contributions and funds

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.10 DECISION *(part: how much above the minimum, and into which funds)*; HH.7 DECISION *(part: pensions
among a household's savings)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: slots 5c for the occasions, 5d for the apply, 6a for a switch's dealing); §7.16
(follows: two lumpy kinds on attention).

**Depends on**: S4.143 (the `pension_rate` and `pension_fund` decision kinds, the member's sparse entry); S4.148 (pots,
the levy that reads the rate); S3.185 (a switch dealt at the next value); S3.184 (the funds' published values); S1.350
(attention: each kind's review days from its stake and cost, redrawn by surprises); S1.336 (each series' surprise
stamp); S1.227 (the household's agenda slot `pension`); S8.103 (the member decides with its own mind, its view reading
its household's position).

**Goal**: a DC member takes PEN.10's two choices as two lumpy decisions: the extra contribution above the minimum, and
the fund its pot holds. How often it reviews each is its own attention to what is at stake, raised by the surprises the
choice bears on. The options are weighed on the concerns each decision declares, from the member's own outlooks. The
chosen rate is read at the next payroll, and a switch is a redemption and a subscription at the next value.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/rules/member.rs` | the two kinds' attention declarations (review cost, variables borne on, stake read), options, consequences and apply |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/member.rs` | tests below |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the consequences' sources (buffer-stock saving, Carroll 1997; portfolio with human capital, Bodie, Merton and Samuelson 1992) |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the member (PEN.10; E 46: the pot is the member's), `taken_in = person` for both kinds. Its view reads
  its household's position (buffer target, income outlook) as `DEM.leave` and `POL.vote` do.
- **Two kinds**, each a lumpy kind on attention (K-101), weighed apart because a member's loss aversion makes the two
  choices' consequences not additive in one weighing:
  - `pension_rate`: the extra contribution. Its stake read is the contribution flow the rate governs (the wage times the
    admitted rate range, to pension age) and the variances of the fund's return and of the member's income.
  - `pension_fund`: the fund the pot holds. Its stake read is the pot's value and the variance of its fund's return
    against the menu's.
- **Review days**: each member keeps its own two next days, one per kind, in a sparse cold column on its pot's
  `pension_rights` row (two u16 day offsets, S4.142), each drawn on the member's own stream from its own stake (REP.38).
  The household's agenda slot `pension` (S1.227) holds only the earliest of its members' days across both kinds: on that
  occasion only the members whose own day is due decide, each redraws its own day, and the slot resets to the new
  minimum. This is exact, because the slot is only the agenda's key and sums no stake.
- **When** (occasions only, never a schedule of its own):
  - a need: the member's DC job starts (the hire's apply files both kinds), which is its first decision of each;
  - a review day drawn by attention from the kind's stake and its review cost (hours at the member's value of leisure,
    Law 14);
  - a surprise that raises a kind's stake redraws its review day (K-101): the fund's published value series surprise
    (S1.336, caught up at the member's next visit), and at their events a DC job's start or end, a change of the
    employer's rate (terms) and a change of the relief schedule (S5.120). Both kinds bear on the fund's series; the rate
    kind also bears on the job and the relief. So a fund's surprise wakes nobody at once; reviews follow over days as
    the members' visits and draws arrive.
- **Options**:
  - `pension_rate`: the extra-rate points the trust's terms admit, including none, at the pot's current fund;
  - `pension_fund`: the funds of the trust's menu, including keep.
- **Consequences** (one `Fixed` per declared concern, from the member's own outlooks, VAL.8):
  - **means**: the pot's value at pension age per unit contributed. It counts the employer's match (terms) and the
    fund's expected return (the member's own outlook of that fund's published value series, K-92), less what the same
    money in liquid saving would buy before pension age, at its own rate outlook.
  - **security**: the width of its outlook of the fund's return over the horizon, against its income outlook to pension
    age (its human capital); for `pension_rate`, the lock-up of the money until pension age against the household's
    buffer target.
  - **wealth and legacy**: the pot passes to the member's heirs at its death (E 46).
  - **Tax relief** is a consequence **absent** until TAX builds it. Placeholder, naming TAX: *pension contributions' tax
    relief missing from the member's weighing*. It is introduced here and retired by S5.120.
- **Apply** (5d):
  - `pension_rate`: the member's sparse entry records the chosen rate point (a chosen none is a recorded choice of no
    extra; the levy emits no item for it);
  - `pension_fund`: a new fund switches the pot. The trust places one linked instruction per (old fund, new fund) a day
    for the day's switching pots (K-48 link group): the pots' units redeemed from its holding of the old fund and the
    proceeds subscribed in the new, dealt at the next value (S3.185). The new units are apportioned to the pots by their
    redeemed values (K-16, the residue to the fund), and each pot row's terms name the new fund. A pot holds one fund,
    so no member holds units in more than one. New contributions are pending for the new fund from that day.
  - each occasion redraws its kind's next review (K-101).

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a member with no pot has no review days and no occasion. Test: `no_pot_no_occasion`.
- E14: two members of one household due on one occasion both decide; a member not yet due does not, and the slot resets
  to the earliest remaining day. Test: `household_slot_takes_only_due_members`.
- E12: an absent outlook of a fund with no published value yet: that option's means is `Missing`, and the mind weighs
  only what it has. Test: `unpriced_fund_consequence_missing`.
- E14: a switch and a contribution in one day: the contribution is pending on the old fund, dealt there, and then
  switched with the pot. Test: `switch_after_pending_order_free`.
- E10: a fund ending (FND.14) with pots in it: its ceasing resolves the holdings (REG.12), a need that files the
  `pension_fund` occasion. Test: `ended_fund_files_occasion`.
- E11: before its first decision a member has no entry, and no extra levy item is emitted. Test:
  `no_entry_no_extra_item`.
- E5: a surprise in a widely held fund raises the stake of every holder; each redraws at its own next visit, never on
  one day. Test: `fund_surprise_redraws_at_visits`.
- E7: the two kinds' draws are addressed by (member, kind, day) on the kind's stream. Test: `two_kinds_draw_apart`.

**Extension points**: S6.128 (HH.7) reads the pot and the member's entry as the household's pension saving; S5.120 adds
the relief consequence and its change as a surprise the rate kind bears on.

**Unit tests**: `rate_consequences_from_own_outlooks`; `fund_consequences_from_own_outlooks`; `stake_reads_declared`;
`job_start_files_both_kinds`; `no_pot_no_occasion`; `unpriced_fund_consequence_missing`;
`switch_after_pending_order_free`; `switch_is_one_linked_instruction`; `ended_fund_files_occasion`;
`no_entry_no_extra_item`; `fund_surprise_redraws_at_visits`; `two_kinds_draw_apart`;
`household_slot_takes_only_due_members`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-81` registered (read at the gate): every extra contribution levied names a rate its member chose,
every fund switch settled as one instruction at the next value, and each kind's review days follow its members' stakes.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.household_reviews: 21 / 0 / 21 core-ms (B / NB / H): the attention rule's occasions at the
  design point, ≈ 8000 `pension_rate` a business day (≈ 1 M contributing members, at a stake of their contribution flow
  against ≈ 2 hours' review cost, review about twice a year) at 0.9 µs (≤ 8 rate points × 100 ns and the handler), and ≈
  8000 `pension_fund` (≈ 2 M pots, at a stake of their value, review about once a year) at 1.7 µs (≤ 16 funds × 100 ns
  and the handler); the surprises' redraws ride K-101's redraw unit
- units: fin.decide.pension_rate_ns 900, fin.decide.pension_fund_ns 1700 (inside the share above)
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +8 MB resident (review days on ≈ 2 M pot rows × 4 B)
- ledger line 11 (holdings and lots): +0 B (inside S1.280's holdings, count 0: no member holds units in more than one
  fund)
- ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (named slot `pension`, S1.227, inside S1.196's 174 B)
- ledger line 2 (persons): +0 B (the member's sparse entry is counted at S4.142)
- saved: +12.4 MB (the pots' review days and the households' slot)
- Counters: `phx_pen.rate_decisions`, `phx_pen.fund_decisions`, `phx_pen.fund_switches`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a rule that computes the answer (a Merton share applied as the choice) in place of consequences the
mind weighs; tax relief read as zero; a switch dealt at a price not yet formed; a wake of every holder on a fund's
surprise; a list of triggers in place of attention; a review at a fixed interval; the two choices weighed in one
decision.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule and tests; the placeholder naming TAX registered in the placeholder count with S5.120 named; `LC-4-81`
  registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.151 — At retirement: an annuity or drawdown

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.3 STATE; PEN.10 DECISION *(part: at retirement, draw down or buy an annuity)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: 5c the occasion; 6a the dealing; 7a–7c the linked instruction).

**Depends on**: S4.149 (the retire event); S4.143 (the `at_retirement` decision kind); S4.148 (pots); S4.125 (annuity contracts); S4.129 (insurers' annuity points
posted on K-70); S3.185 (redemption at the next value); S1.245, S1.248 (a link group settles all or none); S8.103 (the
member decides with its own mind, its view reading its household's position).

**Goal**: when a member with a pot retires, it chooses between buying an annuity at a point an insurer in its reach
posts, and drawing the pot down as its own savings. An annuity purchase is one instruction: units redeemed, premium
paid, annuity contract opened, all or none.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/rules/at_retirement.rs` | the options and consequences; the purchase instruction |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/at_retirement.rs` | tests below |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the consequences' sources (Yaari 1965; Mitchell, Poterba, Warshawsky and Brown 1999) |

**Design**:
- **Decider**: the member (PEN.10), `taken_in = person`; its view reads its household's position.
- **When**: the retire event of a member holding a pot wakes its `at_retirement` decision (a need, K-43) on the next
  business day, at 5c.
- **Options**: drawdown; an annuity at each point the annuity cover kinds post in the member's reach (S4.129's standing
  offers on K-70: insurer, amount a month per unit of premium, indexation, survivor terms). No ask is sent.
- **Consequences**, from the member's own view:
  - **means**: each option's income stream valued under the member's own survival outlook. That outlook is its heuristic
    over the published period life table for its age and health (VAL.3, K-37). Drawdown's stream is the pot's value
    spent over the same outlook.
  - **security**: the chance, under that outlook and its outlook of the fund's return, that drawdown exhausts the pot
    while the member lives. An annuity carries the insurer's failure risk as the household sees it: the insurer's
    published solvency, and the protection scheme's cover as published (S4.139).
  - **wealth and legacy**: what drawdown leaves to heirs; an annuity leaves only its survivor terms.
- **Apply**:
  - **An annuity**: one link group (K-48). The pot's units are redeemed from the trust's holding at the next value
    (S3.185's commitment), the premium is paid from the proceeds to the insurer, and the annuity contract opens
    (S4.125's family, insurer → person). It is all or none (SET.4). A failed leg leaves the pot as it was, and the
    household's next occasion is woken.
  - **Drawdown**: the pot's units are delivered from the trust's holding to a holding of the member's own (one K-60
    move), the pot row ends, and the units are the household's savings for its holding decisions (HH.7, S3.158).
- **Streams**: none of its own (the mind's tastes, REP.22).

**Edge cases**:
- E2: no insurer posts an annuity point in reach. Drawdown is the only option. Test: `no_point_only_drawdown`.
- E10: a death between the retire event and the decision. The pot row passes to the estate, and the member's decision
  lapses with it. Test: `death_lapses_decision`.
- E1: the chosen insurer is resolved before the instruction settles. The link group fails as a whole, and the occasion
  is woken. Test: `insurer_failure_fails_whole_group`.
- E14: the redemption and the premium on one day are ordered by the link group, never by arrival. Test:
  `purchase_legs_ordered_by_group`.
- E6: the pending decision and redemption are live across a save (K-43, K-50). Test: `retirement_decision_round_trip`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `annuity_moneys_worth_consequence` (a given survival outlook and quote); `drawdown_exhaustion_chance`;
`no_point_only_drawdown`; `annuity_purchase_all_or_none`; `death_lapses_decision`; `insurer_failure_fails_whole_group`;
`purchase_legs_ordered_by_group`; `retirement_decision_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-21` (extended) registered (read at the gate): every retiring member's pot became an annuity
bought from a named insurer or a drawdown holding of the member's own. No annuity exists without its premium and its
redeemed units.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.household_reviews: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 100 retirements a business day with a
  pot (retirements are of the order of deaths, a share with pots), each ≤ 10 options at 100 ns + 30 ns handler, and one
  link group of three legs.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (annuities within S4.125's family).
- ledger line 11 (holdings and lots): +0 B (inside S1.280's holdings, count ≈ 25000 a year: the drawdown holdings of
  members' own, at most ≈ 100 retirements a business day)
- Counters: `phx_pen.annuities_bought`, `phx_pen.drawdowns`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an annuity without a named insurer's posted point; an annuity decided from a money's-worth threshold
in place of the mind's weighing; a partial purchase (a leg without its partners).

**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule and tests; `LC-4-21` (extended) registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.152 — The scheme actuary values each scheme's liabilities on its work day

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.2 STATE *(part: the liability is the schedule discounted at market rates)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: slot 9a valuations); §7.12 (follows: valuers); §7.14 (follows: linear aggregates valued
by a declared sweep).

**Depends on**: S4.142 (the scheme kind's valuation columns); S4.144 (the valuation interval, the actuaries' turnaround
and weekday, the funding curve); S4.146 (rights in index units); S4.149 (pensions in payment paid by schemes); S1.341
(K-95's `value(…, factor)` in its sweep representation); S1.171 (the declared sweep); S1.323 (the actuarial firm's
queue); S1.335 (valuers, curves, labelled extrapolation); S3.127 (the curve publisher's discount-factor tables); S1.215
(the published life table and index); S1.207 (the household's partner role, read for a survivor).

**Goal**: on each scheme's valuation work day, a named actuary values its liabilities as the exact sum over its members'
rights and pensions in payment, discounted at the curve the law names, extrapolated beyond the longest traded point and
labelled so. The valuation and its sensitivity per curve bucket are recorded for the funding test and every later read.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/valuers/actuary.rs` | the valuer's declaration and method: the per-row factor (pure over the life table, the DF table and the row's terms) and its bucket derivatives |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/valuation.rs` | work days, the queue, the sweep's registration and the recorded valuation |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/valuation.rs` | tests below |

**Design**:
- **Valuer** (K-91, MKT.20): the scheme actuary is a valuer held by a named actuarial firm (a firm of the professional
  services industry), paid its posted fee per valuation (Law 14). Its published method takes each row's factor from the
  row's own terms (pension age, indexation, survivor share), its member's birth day and sex, and its survivor's birth
  day (the member's partner, its household's partner role at the valuation, K-33), under the published period life table
  as of the valuation day; the funding curve's discount factors (S3.127; the publisher the law names); and points beyond
  the longest traded one extrapolated by the valuer's declared method, labelled extrapolated with the prints' ages
  shown.
- **Reference and work days**: each scheme's reference date is its own year-end at the law's valuation interval (and,
  for a new scheme, its founding or opening day), so schemes spread over the calendar (N8.9). The actuarial firm values
  after its declared turnaround, on its **declared valuation weekday** (TECHNOLOGY of the firm's work calendar,
  S4.144), at that day's curve, life table and membership. Members beyond the firm's weekly capacity (its staff hours
  per thousand members, TECHNOLOGY) wait in its queue (K-84, S1.323; FIFO, ties by lot) for the next weekday.
- **The sweep**: a declared K-14 sweep, `#[sweep(pension_rights.ends, reason = valuation_day)]` (S1.171), with the
  pensions-in-payment family's ends in the same registration. It makes one pass on each valuation weekday and serves
  every scheme the firms value that day (the scheme side keeps no list and no index instance). Per row: `units × I(t) ×
  factor(row)`, or money per year × factor for a pension in payment, summed per scheme by a keyed reduce (K-13), with
  each scheme's sensitivity per curve bucket (Σ rows × dfactor/dbucket) in the same pass. Exact, member by member (Law
  11); K-95 keeps no resident cells for this shape.
- **Record**: each valuation is a record (K-37, labelled a valuation, never a print), with its liability, its bucket
  sensitivities and its row count per status (read by S4.159's check), written to the scheme's columns and cold
  sensitivities.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a curve not yet published on a weekday is `Missing`; the valuation waits for the next weekday, and the wait is
  counted. Test: `valuation_waits_for_curve`.
- E5: a common year-end fills the firms' queues; each weekday values only what the firms' capacity lets through, and the
  rest wait. Test: `queue_releases_by_capacity`.
- E3: a member with no partner has no survivor term. Test: `no_partner_no_survivor_term`.
- E13: a closed scheme (no active members) is still valued. Test: `closed_scheme_valued`.

### S4.153 — The funding test, the recovery-plan demand, the schedule of contributions and the roll-forward

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.5 PROCESS *(part: a falling rate raises the liability and can open a deficit the sponsor must pay)*
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: slot 9a, 9c demands due next business day).

**Depends on**: S4.152 (the valuation and its sensitivities); S4.144 (the longest recovery period); S1.330 (the
scheme's maintained net assets); S1.332 (assets at their carrying values); S1.237 (a demand due next business day);
S1.239 (the "party position" series kind, written by its owning rule through `cross`); S3.127 (the day's discount-factor
tables).

**Goal**: each valuation is tested against the scheme's assets; a deficit demands a recovery plan from the sponsor, and
the valuation sets the employer's contribution rate for future accrual, which payroll reads. Between valuations the
actuary's published roll-forward moves each scheme's liability with the curve, labelled so, and is the value every other
reader takes.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/funding.rs` | the funding test; the recovery-plan demand; the schedule of contributions; the roll-forward and its position series |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/funding.rs` | tests below |

**Design**:
- **On the valuation's day** (9a):
  - funding ratio = assets at their carrying values (K-88, K-89) ÷ liability;
  - a deficit sends the sponsor a demand for a recovery plan (K-45, due next business day, TIME.7), which S4.154
    answers;
  - the **schedule of contributions**: the employer's rate for future accrual is the value of a year's accrual per unit
    of pensionable pay at the same method, less the employee's rate, written to the scheme's column, which S4.146's levy
    reads from the next payroll. Until a scheme's first valuation the column is `Missing` (S4.146 levies no employer
    item).
- **Roll-forward** (the actuary's published method, labelled a roll-forward with its base valuation's date): `L(t) =
  L(v) + Σ_b S_b × ΔDF_b(v → t)` over the recorded sensitivities, plus the recorded accrual and benefits since. At each
  publication of the funding curve (9a) the rolled-forward funding ratio of each scheme is written as a "party position"
  series (S1.239), whose writer calls `cross`, so the trustees' thresholds wake (S4.155). A falling rate raises it
  (PEN.5). Trustees, sponsors, the guarantee fund's levy and the measures read it.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a rate collapse moves every scheme's rolled-forward liability at once; only the crossed thresholds wake. Test:
  `collapse_wakes_only_crossed`.
- E11: before its first valuation a scheme has no funding ratio (absent, not zero). Test:
  `funding_ratio_absent_before_valuation`.
- E14: a valuation and a curve publication on one day: the roll-forward starts from the new valuation. Test:
  `roll_forward_restarts_at_valuation`.
- E6: the pending demand and the position series survive a save. Test: `demand_round_trip`.

**Extension points**: S4.154 (the demand), S4.155 (the funding ratio's series), S4.158 (the levy on underfunding),
S4.159 (funding ratios published) read these.

**Unit tests**: `deficit_demands_plan_next_business_day`; `schedule_of_contributions_rate`;
`roll_forward_first_order_labelled`; `collapse_wakes_only_crossed`; `funding_ratio_absent_before_valuation`;
`roll_forward_restarts_at_valuation`; `demand_round_trip`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-06` (part) registered (read at the gate): funding ratios against the curve are published per
scheme, and every roll-forward names its base valuation.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 5 k schemes × ≤ 20 buckets × 2 ns at each
  curve publication, plus the valued schemes' tests.
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B (columns counted at S4.142).
- Counters: `phx_pen.deficits`, `phx_pen.plans_demanded`.

**Guards**: PC-63 applies (no change).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a stored roll-forward replacing the valuation; a funding ratio fixed by anything but the valuation
and the assets' own values.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Funding test, demand, schedule and roll-forward with tests; `LC-4-06` (part) registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.

### S4.154 — Sponsors choose how fast to repair a deficit

**Status**: planned

**Kind**: mechanism

**Clauses**: PEN.9 DECISION
**Architecture**: §6.1 (follows: 5c answers to messages; 7a the plan's dues).

**Depends on**: S4.153 (the demand and the rolled-forward liability); S4.144 (the longest recovery period); S4.142
(the recovery-plan family); S4.143 (the `repair` decision kind); S2.179 (the sponsor's marginal cost of funds); S2.118 (its
funding options); S2.119 (its payout); S1.263 (a plan's schedule as shared terms); S8.103, S8.122 (the chief executive
decides with its own mind).

**Goal**: a sponsor pays what the schedule of contributions requires, and answers each deficit's demand by choosing a
repair period within the law. It weighs the deficit's cost against its own funding, investment and dividends. The plan
is a contract paid on its schedule.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/src/rules/repair.rs` | the options, consequences and the plan's contract |
| `crates/systems/sys-pen/tests/repair.rs` | tests below |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the consequences' source (the deficit as corporate debt: Treynor 1977; Bulow 1982) |

**Design**:
- **When** (by need, so the sponsor's record carries no next-day slot for this kind): the demand from S4.153, at 5c of
  the next business day; a missed instalment of its own plan (K-56).
- **Options**: repair periods from the shortest the sponsor can pay from its own cash outlook to the law's longest
  (PEN.11), at yearly points, with level instalments.
- **Consequences** (the firm's own view, handed to its chief executive's mind):
  - **means**: each plan's cost against the sponsor's marginal cost of funds (S2.179), and against the return of the
    investment and dividends it would displace. The guarantee fund's levy on underfunding (S4.158) is a cost of a slower
    plan.
  - **security**: the sponsor's own cash outlook's shortfall chance under each instalment, and the scheme's risk of a
    further deficit at the next valuation (its outlook's width).
- **Apply** (5d): a `recovery_plan` contract (sponsor → scheme) opens with the chosen schedule. Its dues are streamed at
  7a, and a missed instalment is an arrears event (K-56) that the scheme's trustees see.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a sponsor that cannot pay even the law's longest plan still chooses the longest. Its missed instalments are
  arrears, and a sponsor's end is S4.157's. Test: `unpayable_takes_longest`.
- E10: a sponsor ending with a plan open: the plan becomes a claim on its estate (S4.157). Test:
  `plan_becomes_estate_claim`.
- E14: a demand and an existing plan. The new plan replaces the old one's remaining schedule, one close and one open on
  the same apply. Test: `new_plan_replaces_remaining`.
- E5: plans' instalments fall on month-ends and stream with the H day's dues. Test: `instalments_stream_as_dues`.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `repair_consequences_by_cost_of_funds`; `plan_within_law`; `unpayable_takes_longest`;
`new_plan_replaces_remaining`; `plan_becomes_estate_claim`; `instalments_stream_as_dues`.

**Live checks**: `LC-4-06` (extended) registered (read at the gate; PEN.6): sponsors' contributions against their
investment are published. Every deficit has a plan within the law, or the sponsor's arrears or end.

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H): ≈ 300 demands a valuation cycle, each ≤ 30
  options × 100 ns.
- adds 0 / 0 / 5000 items to fin.dues.item_ns (plans' instalments on month-end paydays).
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (occasions by need); ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (≈ 3000 recovery-plan rows × 32 B,
  within the family's store).
- Counters: `phx_pen.recovery_plans`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a deficit nobody repairs; a repair pace as a parameter (it is the mind's choice over the
consequences).

**Done when**:
- [ ] The rule and tests; `LC-4-06` (extended) registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Two reviews; status `done` and the section removed.
