### S5.103 — Payroll contributions fused with withholding

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: payroll contributions, employee's and employer's)*; TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: withheld by
the employer at payroll, a liability of the collector until remitted)*
**Architecture**: §4.3 (follows: levies), §7.8 (follows: K-51 levy sets fused at emission; K-52 tallies), §7.9 (follows:
K-59 payables)
**Depends on**: S5.101 (`contributions` handle), S5.102 (the contribution schedules), S1.253 (K-51), S1.254 (K-52
per-contract year-to-date pay), S1.270 (collectors' payables per period), S1.435 (income-tax withholding at emission)
**Goal**: every wage due carries the employee's contribution deducted and the employer's added, fused with income-tax
withholding in the same emission, each rounded once by its own convention; the employer holds what it collected as
its liability to the treasury on its payable, by base, until remitted (S5.107).

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the `contributions` levy declarations on the payroll reasons (employee: deducted from the payee's leg; employer: an added item payer → collector), their collector role (the employer) and base (the per-contract pay) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/contributions.rs` | the levy's base: this due's pay against the contract's year-to-date pay and the schedule's ceiling |

**Design**:
- **Levy set** (K-51) on each payroll reason: withholding (existing), employee contribution, employer contribution —
  one declared set, evaluated at the due's emission (stage 7a stream, fused): each reads its base from the due's gross
  and the contract's year-to-date pay tally (K-52, S1.254), so a ceiling crossed inside the year charges only the part
  below it (`contributions`' ceiling in S5.101). Each levy is rounded once by its schedule's convention (REP.9).
- **Legs**: employee contribution reduces the payee's net item; employer contribution is an extra item from the
  employer; both accrue to the employer's payable per (collector, base, period) (K-59 `accrue`, S1.270), so each
  remittance names its base (TAX.5).
- **Follow-on**: the declared follow-on reason `SOC.earnings_rights` is added by S5.126 (the earnings-related state
  right); nothing is written for it here.
- The self-employed pay contributions on their return (S5.109) from `TAX.ssc_self_bands`, not at payroll.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a quarter-end payday streams 4.5 M wage dues with three levies each (withholding and the two contributions),
  evaluated in the due's one emission (`contributions_fused_exact_per_levy`; `LC-5-01`).
- E14: withholding plus contributions above the gross is a contract violation (`violation!(clause = "TAX.2")`), never
  skipped (`levies_above_gross_violate`).
- E11: the first due of a contract has year-to-date pay 0 because nothing was paid, not because it is missing
  (`first_due_ytd_is_zero_paid`).
- E13: a country with no employer contribution declares none (`empty_set_no_levy`).

**Extension points**: the payroll levy set gains S5.126's follow-on (earnings-related rights).

**Unit tests**:
- `contributions_fused_exact_per_levy`: the fused evaluation gives each levy what its own evaluation would, each
  rounded by its own convention.
- `ceiling_crossed_mid_year`: the year-to-date pay crossing the ceiling in this due charges only the part below it.
- `payable_accrues_per_base`; `levies_above_gross_violate`; `first_due_ytd_is_zero_paid`; `empty_set_no_levy`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-5-01` (from S5.103): TAX.2 — every contribution arose at a wage due (read-trace: reason and contract), accrued to
  its employer's payable under its base, and the payable's balance per base equals the contributions of its period.

**Budget**: two levies fused in each wage due's emission (K-51), their accruals in the same apply (K-59).
- adds 0 phone-ns to fin.dues.item_ns at 0.6 M / 0 / 4.5 M items (the levies ride the due's one emission).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (named slot: the employer's payable per base, S1.270's accruing family).
- Counters: `sys_tax.contribution_levies`, `sys_tax.contribution_bases_past_ceiling`.

**Guards**: none new (PC-70 covers the handle).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a contribution computed on a firm's wage bill; a levy evaluated apart from its wage's emission.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rules and unit tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] `LC-5-01` registered (read at the gate); the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S5.104 — Registration for value-added tax, compulsory and chosen

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: which sellers charge value-added tax: the law's registration threshold, and
registration below it where the law allows it)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.5 (follows: K-32 firm columns), §7.12 (follows: K-90 statements),
§7.16 (follows: K-100 decision core)
**Depends on**: S5.102 (`TAX.vat_registration_threshold`, `TAX.vat_lookback`, `TAX.vat_voluntary`,
`TAX.registration_review_hours`), S1.196 (K-32: a declared firm column), S1.333 (K-90: each firm's closed-period
statements on its own calendar), S1.348 (K-100 option generators), S8.103 (minds attached), S8.122 (the mandate
through the office holder's contracts)
**Goal**: where a country's consumption tax is a value-added tax, each firm is registered or not by the law's test —
its revenue over the law's look-back, read from its own closed statements, against the threshold — and, below the
threshold where the law allows it, by its office holder's choice: registering lets the firm reclaim the tax on its
inputs and obliges it to charge tax to every buyer. The test and the choice visit a firm only when its own period
closes.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/returns.rs` | decision kind `TAX.vat_registration` (`taken_in` the office the firm's legal form declares for its financing, concerns means and security, mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | firm column `vat_registered: bool` (K-32 declaration, cold); the test's slot at the firm's statement close (K-90's hook, stage 9b) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/registration.rs` | `compulsory(revenue_lookback, threshold) -> bool`; the option generator below the threshold |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/opening.rs` | each opening firm's registration from its opening statements (GEN.5): compulsory where the test says so, otherwise its first close's choice |

**Design**:
- **When**: at stage 9b of the day a firm's statement closes (K-90, due on its own calendar, N8.9), in the firm's own
  country where `TAX.consumption_form` is value-added; never a sweep of firms.
- **Compulsory**: revenue over the look-back (the closed statements' revenue line within it, a K-90 read) at or above
  the threshold in force (K-20) → registered from the next day; no decision is taken.
- **Chosen**, below the threshold where `TAX.vat_voluntary` holds, the decision point `TAX.vat_registration`:
  - **Options**: *registered*; *unregistered* (the firm's current state is one of them, so staying is an option).
  - **Consequences**, from the firm's own closed statement and outlooks: *means* — the input tax it would reclaim
    (`vat` over its purchases on the statement, by their classes) against the output tax it would charge to buyers
    who cannot reclaim it (its sales to unregistered buyers and households on the statement, whose share it would bear
    at its posted points by its own price outlook), and the return hours; *security* — the width of its sales
    outlook (a registration it may not keep past the look-back).
  - The holder's mind chooses (best); `TAX.registration_review_hours` of staff. Below the threshold for the whole
    look-back and not choosing to stay → deregistered.
  - **Dominance first**, fused in K-90's close pass (S1.328's hooks) in O(1): for an unregistered firm, register's
    *means* is the statement's reclaimable input tax less the output tax it would bear and the compliance hours at
    the firm's wage; its *security* is never better than staying's. Where that means is not above zero, staying
    dominates for every mind — the kind declares no taste term (REP.22) — so no option set is built and the firm
    stays. Only firms whose registration would pay (exporters and heavy buyers from registered sellers) and firms
    already registered by choice are weighed by the holder's mind.
- **Reads** of `vat_registered`: the sale's levy set (S5.105) — a registered seller charges output tax, a registered
  buyer reclaims input tax.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: a firm founded in the run has no closed statement: its look-back revenue is absent; it is unregistered until
  its first close, where it chooses (`no_statement_unregistered`).
- E13: a country with a retail sales tax declares no registration and the column is never read there
  (`rst_country_no_registration`); a law without voluntary registration offers no choice (`no_voluntary_no_point`).
- E10: a firm that ends carries its registration into its estate's final statements; nothing else reads it
  (`LC-5-02`).

**Extension points**: `vat_registered` is read by S5.105, S5.106, S5.107 and S5.178 (import tax as input tax).

**Unit tests**: `registered_at_threshold`, `deregistered_after_lookback_below`, `no_statement_unregistered`,
`rst_country_no_registration`, `no_voluntary_no_point`, `dominated_register_builds_no_options` (given a statement
whose reclaimable input tax does not exceed the tax borne and the hours' cost: no option set, the firm stays; a
positive one builds both options), `voluntary_options_consequences` (given statements: the
reclaimable input tax and the output tax borne on sales to unregistered buyers, each on its concern).

**Live checks**: `LC-5-02` (from S5.104): every registered seller's look-back revenue on its last statement date was
at or above the threshold then in force or its registration traces to its holder's recorded choice; every
unregistered one's revenue was below it.

**Budget**: the compulsory test and the dominance test are comparisons fused in K-90's close over the lines it has just
written, an expected 0.4 M firms below the threshold closing at a quarter end at ≈ 3 phone-ns; the choice is weighed
only where registration is not dominated, an expected 30 k firms at a quarter end (20 k whose registration would pay,
10 k registered by choice), ≈ 1 µs each with two options.
- its share of fin.fixed.close_books: 0 / 0 / 3.2 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the compulsory and dominance tests).
- adds 0 / 0 / 30 k items to fin.decide.attend_ns (the weighed choices, ≈ 30 core-ms on H at ≈ 1 µs).
- ledger line 5 (firms): +0 B (named slot `vat_registered`, one bit of the firm's cold flag word).
- Counters: `sys_tax.vat_registrations`, `sys_tax.vat_voluntary_registrations`, `sys_tax.vat_deregistrations`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; registration tested on any day but the firm's own statement date; a threshold read from an
aggregate; a registration below the threshold set by rule where the law lets the firm choose; a preference weight in
the generator.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declaration, decision point, generator, rule and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-02` registered (read at
  the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.105 — Value-added or retail sales tax at the sale, exports zero-rated

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: consumption tax in the form each country chooses — value-added tax at every sale
along the chain or retail sales tax on final sales only; imports at the border complete it at S5.178)*; TAX.2 PROCESS
*(part: charged by the seller at each sale)*
**Architecture**: §4.3 (follows: levies), §7.8 (follows: K-51), §7.11 (follows: K-74 seller-shard booking: tax rounded
once per sale)
**Depends on**: S5.101 (`vat`, `sales_tax` handles), S5.102 (rates, exempt products, form), S5.104 (registration),
S1.253 (K-51), S1.309 (K-74: a sale is its flow, tax rounded per sale in the seller's shard), S1.435
(retires its placeholder `TAX.consumption_at_till`)
**Goal**: every sale settled at once carries the consumption tax its country's law declares, charged by the seller:
under a value-added tax, the seller's output tax on every sale and a registered buyer's input tax reclaimable; under a
retail sales tax, tax on sales to the buyer classes the law declares final. The retail sales tax that stood in every
country as a placeholder is retired.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | levy sets on every sale reason (retail, service, between-firm, state purchase): `vat` or `sales_tax` by `TAX.consumption_form`; collector the seller; input-tax credit to a registered buyer as a declared follow-on on the buyer's payable |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/consumption.rs` | the base: the sale's net amount; the rate by the product's class (exempt products declared); zero rate when the buyer is sited in another country (read through the buyer's site) |
| `data/profiles/<level>/law.toml` | `TAX.consumption_at_till` removed; `TAX.consumption_form` in force |

**Design**:
- **Levy at the sale** (K-51 fused in K-74's seller-shard sweep): the sale's price is the seller's net point; the tax
  is `vat(net, schedule of the product class)` (or `sales_tax` where the buyer's class is declared final), rounded once
  per sale by the law's convention; the buyer pays net plus tax in the sale's one flow; the tax accrues to the
  seller's payable for its period (K-59). Retail posted points stay gross to final buyers as the law declares for
  each market kind (a posted point's display is the seller's, S5.116).
- **Input tax**: when the buyer is registered (S5.104), the tax it paid accrues as a credit (negative) on its own
  payable for the period — a declared follow-on of the sale reason read by K-51 at the same emission; an unregistered
  buyer's tax is a cost.
- **Exports**: a buyer sited in another country makes the sale zero-rated (`vat` over a zero schedule selected by the
  buyer's country, not a kind branch); imports are charged at the border (S5.178).
- **Sales on terms** are taxed at the invoice's statement (S5.106), not per sale.
- Retires `TAX.consumption_at_till` (placeholder:TAX).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a failed sale reverses its tax with the sale (K-74 reverses the flow; the accrual is posted only on settlement,
  K-49's apply) (`failed_sale_reverses_tax`).
- E13: a product class exempt in one country and taxed in another reads its own country's schedule
  (`exempt_class_zero`).
- E14: a registered firm buying and selling the same period nets output against input on one payable per period
  (`output_less_input_on_payable`).

**Extension points**: the payable's net per period is remitted by S5.107; S5.178 adds import tax as input tax.

**Unit tests**: `vat_per_sale_rounded_once`, `input_tax_credit_only_registered`, `export_zero_rated_by_buyer_site`,
`rst_only_on_declared_final_classes`, `exempt_class_zero`, `output_less_input_on_payable`, `failed_sale_reverses_tax`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-03` (from S5.105): TAX.2 — every consumption tax arose at a sale (reason and seller named), its
rate the one in force for the product's class in the seller's country, zero on exports; every input-tax credit
names a registered buyer.

**Budget**: one levy fused in each sale's apply (the tax is rounded per sale in the seller's shard already);
input-tax credits fused in the same apply.
- adds 0 phone-ns to fin.retail.all_in_ns at 6.75 M / 6.75 M / 6.75 M items.
- adds 0 phone-ns to fin.b2b.purchase_ns at 3.3 M / 0.3 M / 3.3 M items.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (named slot: the seller's and buyer's payables per period, S1.270's accruing family).
- Counters: `sys_tax.vat_levies`, `sys_tax.input_credits`, `sys_tax.zero_rated_sales`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tax leg written apart from its sale's flow; a rate chosen by the product's name in code; a
kind branch between the two forms of the tax (the form is declared data).

**Done when**:
- [ ] Levy declarations, rules and unit tests written; the placeholder's entry removed; fast checks pass.
- [ ] `LC-5-03` registered (read at the gate); the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] The two reviews done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S5.106 — Value-added tax on invoices at their statement

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: value-added tax on sales on terms charged per invoice at its statement)*
**Architecture**: §4.3 (follows: levies), §7.9 (follows: K-59 accruing statement contracts: the period's close)
**Depends on**: S5.105 (the tax on sales, its rates and input credit), S2.111 (invoices per (seller, buyer, statement
period) on K-59), S1.269 (K-59: `accrue`, the period's close on the wheel)
**Goal**: a sale on terms carries no tax leg of its own: at the close of the invoice's statement period the tax on the
period's net amount is added to the invoice once, due with it, accrued to the seller's payable as output tax and, for a
registered buyer, to its payable as input credit. One levy per invoice per period replaces one per sale.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the levy declared on the invoice family's period close (K-59's close hook), its collector the seller; the input credit a follow-on on the buyer's payable |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/consumption.rs` | the statement's base: the period's accrued net amounts by product class (the invoice's own per-class sums) |

**Design**:
- **When**: at the invoice's period close (K-59, due on the wheel at its statement date, stage 2a), in the seller's
  country's form: under a value-added tax, `vat` over each product class's net sum of the period, rounded once per
  class by the law's convention; zero-rated where the buyer is sited in another country; under a retail sales tax, no
  levy (a between-firm invoice is not a final sale unless the buyer's class is declared final).
- **Writes**: the tax added to the invoice's balance (the buyer owes it at the invoice's due date with the net, one
  item); output tax accrued to the seller's payable for the period in which the statement closes; the registered
  buyer's credit to its own payable (S5.104). Nothing is written per sale.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a month-end closes an expected ≈ 4.5 M invoices; the levy is fused into K-59's close (`LC-5-04`).
- E10: an invoice whose seller ended carries its tax to the estate's payable (K-97 moved the side)
  (`ended_seller_tax_to_estate_payable`).
- E14: a credit note in the period (a negative accrual) nets inside the class sum before the tax is computed
  (`credit_note_nets_before_tax`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `vat_on_invoice_row_at_statement`, `zero_rated_invoice_abroad`, `credit_note_nets_before_tax`,
`no_levy_per_sale_on_terms` (a sale on terms composes no levy item), `ended_seller_tax_to_estate_payable`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-04` (from S5.106): every invoice's tax equals its period's per-class net sums through `vat`
with the rates then in force; no sale on terms carries a tax item of its own.

**Budget**: one multiply-and-round per product class of an invoice at its close, fused in K-59's close over the sums it
already holds (≈ 3 phone-ns).
- adds 3 phone-ns to fin.contracts.close_ns at 0.3 M / 0 / 4.5 M items (≈ 1 / 0 / 13 core-ms).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (named slot: the invoice's per-class sums, S2.111's row).
- Counters: `sys_tax.invoice_levies`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tax leg per sale on terms; the tax on a period computed from anything but the invoice's own sums.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rule and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-04` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.107 — Collectors' payables by base, remitted net of input tax

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: remitted periodically on the law's calendar, net of tax paid on the collector's own
purchases under a value-added tax; between arising and remitting a liability of the collector to the treasury)*
**Architecture**: §7.9 (follows: K-59, K-53 declared cold columns), §7.8 (follows: K-48 dated items)
**Depends on**: S1.270 (collectors' payables: one per collector per period), S1.269 (K-59), S5.102
(`TAX.remittance_calendar`), S5.103, S5.105, S5.106 (the accruals by base)
**Goal**: each collector's payable holds its balance per base, so a remittance names each base's amount; on the law's
remittance date a positive balance is paid to the treasury and a negative one (input tax above output) refunded by it,
in the same stage 7 as the collector's other dues.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the payable family's declared cold columns: one `i64` per base the collector collects (withholding, each contribution, output tax, input credit); the remittance date from `TAX.remittance_calendar` |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/remit.rs` | the remittance's items from the row: one per base, net; the payer is the side the net sign names |

**Design**:
- **State**: the payable row (K-59, family `TAX.payable`, collector → treasury) accrues per base in its cold columns
  (K-51's accrual names the base); its balance is their sum. The row closes on its period's end and falls due at the
  law's remittance date (K-42).
- **At the due** (stage 7a stream): one dated item per base with a non-zero amount — a positive base paid by the
  collector to the treasury, the input credit netted inside the value-added base as the law states (output less
  input); a negative net value-added base is a refund item treasury → collector. Each item names the payer, the
  collector and the base (TAX.5, S1.270's family). The treasury's receipts are the items that settle.
- **Failed remittance**: an item that fails is an arrear by S5.115; the payable stays owed.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: remittance dates coinciding with a payday and a quarter-end add an expected ≈ 0.3 M items (`LC-5-05`).
- E3: a collector with no money fails its remittance, an arrear (S5.115), never a skipped leg
  (`failed_remittance_stays_owed`).
- E13: a collector that collected nothing in a period has a zero row that closes with no item (`zero_payable_no_item`).
- E14: output and input tax of one period net on the one row before remittance (`output_less_input_remitted`).

**Extension points**: the payable's bases gain the import tax customs collects (S5.178).

**Unit tests**: `payable_balance_per_base`, `output_less_input_remitted`, `negative_vat_base_refunded`,
`zero_payable_no_item`, `failed_remittance_stays_owed`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-05` (from S5.107): TAX.2, TAX.5 — every remittance equals its payable's per-base balances for
its period, paid on the calendar's date or in arrears; every refund names a collector whose input credit exceeded its
output tax.

**Budget**: remittance items in the dated stream.
- +0 items beyond `[day.h] dues` (the design point's H dues already hold tax 0.3 M); 20 k items a business day, to be
  checked against `[day.b] dues` before they are added.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (inside S1.257's table: `tax_payables`' further bases as run cells, 0.92 M × 8 B = 7.4 MB).
- Counters: `sys_tax.remittances`, `sys_tax.refunds`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a remittance that does not name its bases; a refund without a payable that owes it.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rule and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-05` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.108 — Capital income and realised gains per person

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: capital-gains tax on realised gains, on average cost for households' holdings, and
capital income, as each person's year-to-date positions)*
**Architecture**: §7.8 (follows: K-52 tallies keyed by person), §7.10 (follows: K-62 lots, average cost), §7.9 (follows:
K-58 participations)
**Depends on**: S1.254 (K-52 declared tallies keyed by person), S1.276 (K-62: the cost of the units a sale consumes),
S1.309 (K-74: the delivery batch), S1.281 (the instrument events engine: coupons and dividends to holders of record),
S1.268 (K-58: a joint holding's members and shares), S5.102 (`TAX.capital_income_attribution`, `TAX.gains_withheld`);
S1.276 also posts proceeds less cost to the K-52 tally a sale's reason declares
**Goal**: every person carries, for the tax year, its capital income received and its gains realised, written where
they arise: capital income in settlement's apply, a gain at the delivery of what was sold. Where the law withholds on
interest, dividends or gains, the paying party withholds as a levy of the paying reason.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the income reasons (interest, dividends, coupons, rents received) declared as feeding the person's existing taxable-income tally where the law includes them; a sparse tally `realised_gains` keyed (person, tax year) fed by the sale reasons of instruments and dwellings; withholding levies where `TAX.gains_withheld` or the law's interest withholding is present |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/attribution.rs` | a joint holding's income and gain split among its members by the law's attribution rule (apportion with the named residue) |

**Design**:
- **Capital income**: each flow of a declared income reason increments the payee person's taxable-income tally (the
  person's tax-year pair) in K-49's apply (K-52, fused), as the law includes that income; where the payee side is a
  joint holding (K-58), the amount is split among its members by `TAX.capital_income_attribution` (POLICY) through
  K-16's `apportion`, the residue to the member the rule names. Every person holds its own accounts (E 46), so a
  household is never the unit.
- **Realised gains**: at the delivery of a sale of instruments or dwellings (K-74 after settlement), the gain is the
  proceeds less the cost of the units consumed — the holding's average cost for a household's holding (TAX.1, REG.1),
  its lots' cost where the holder declared FIFO (K-62) — posted by the holdings apply into the seller person's
  `realised_gains` tally that the sale reason declares (S1.276). A loss is a negative gain. The tally is sparse: a row
  (person u32, gain i64, tax year u8) is opened at the person's first realisation of the year and released when its
  return is assessed (S5.109 folds it in), so it holds only the year's realising persons; exactness is unchanged —
  every realisation is posted to it and the return reads the whole sum.
- **Withholding** where the law has it: a levy on the paying reason (K-51), collector the paying bank, issuer or buyer
  as the law names, rounded once; it accrues to that collector's payable (S5.107) and to the person's withheld tally.
- The tallies reset by their period stamp at the tax year's start (no pass).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a quarter-end's dividend day (≈ 2.25 M holder rows) feeds ≈ 1.5 M persons' tallies, fused in the apply
  (`LC-5-06`).
- E10: a sale by an estate realises the gain in the estate's tally, not a living person's (`estate_gain_to_estate`).
- E11: the first tax year of the run starts from the opening's year-to-date positions (GEN.5); absent where the opening
  has none (`opening_ytd_absent_not_zero`).
- E14: two sales of one holding the same day consume lots in the declared order (`two_sales_same_day_lot_order`).

**Extension points**: the tallies are read by S5.109 (the return), S5.118 (a holder's sale timing), S5.121 (measures).

**Unit tests**: `gain_on_average_cost_not_divisible`, `joint_income_attributed_by_rule`, `withheld_only_where_declared`,
`estate_gain_to_estate`, `opening_ytd_absent_not_zero`, `two_sales_same_day_lot_order`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-06` (from S5.108): every person's `realised_gains` equals the proceeds less cost of its
deliveries in the year, and its taxable income includes the income flows the law includes, recounted from the flows
and deliveries of the year's touched persons.

**Budget**: tallies fused in settlement's apply and the delivery batch.
- adds 1.2 phone-ns to fin.stats.tally_ns at 0.9 M / 0 / 2.25 M items (≈ 1 / 0 / 3 core-ms).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool: realised gains): +6 MB resident (0.45 M expected realising persons a year × 13 B,
  the sparse `realised_gains` rows at their peak before the filing window); capital income joins the person's existing
  tax-year pair, +0 B.
- Counters: `sys_tax.gains_realised`, `sys_tax.capital_income_items`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a gain computed on a pooled or household aggregate; a year-end pass recomputing positions.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rules and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-06` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.109 — The personal return, filed on the person's chosen day

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: assessed on the annual return from the payer's own positions, filed on a day of
its choosing within the filing window)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.7 (follows: K-43 decision agenda), §7.16 (follows: K-100 decision
core, K-102 minds)
**Depends on**: S5.108 (capital income and gains), S5.103 (contributions), S1.435 (the Stage 1 filing decision
re-homed, TAX.7), S1.348 (K-100: option generators), S8.103 (minds attached), S1.227 (K-43 schedules and phases),
S5.101 (handles)
**Goal**: every person the law requires to file assesses its year from its own positions — taxable income, capital
income, realised gains, self-employed contributions — through the law's handles, less what was withheld, and pays or
is refunded at the next settlement. When to file within the window is the person's own decision, weighed by its mind.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/returns.rs` | decision kind `TAX.file` (`taken_in = person`, concerns means and leisure_and_health, mode satisfice); its view |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/points.rs` | the decision point: schedule within `TAX.filing_window` with phases drawn (TIME.5), carried in the household's `filing` slot on K-43; the window's last day a need occasion |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/file.rs` | the option generator and the assessment (pure) |

**Design**:
- **Who files**: a person whose positions the law's rule requires to be assessed (`TAX.return_required`, POLICY:
  income beyond final withholding, gains, self-employment); others' withholding is final and they have no occasion.
- **The assessment** (pure): `income_tax(taxable income, capital income included as the law includes it)` +
  `gains_tax(gains)` + self-employed contributions − withheld (the person's tallies), each through its handle with the
  schedule of the tax year, rounded once; positive → a dated item person → treasury at the next stage 7; negative → a
  refund item.
- **The decision** (`TAX.file`), option generator: options **file today** and **wait to the next occasion** — the latter
  only when the person's next scheduled occasion falls inside the window, so each person's last occasion before the
  deadline has one option and files. No day of the window carries a need occasion for everyone. Consequences: *means* —
  the refund or payment moved by the days until the next occasion, valued at the person's own rate on its deposits;
  *leisure_and_health* — `TAX.return_hours` at its value of leisure, paid once whichever day. Its mind satisfices
  (MND.7): refunds tend to be filed early and payments late, an outcome, not a rule.
- **Returns are day-local**: nothing is kept of a return beyond its item and, if it fails, its arrear (S5.115); the
  person's `realised_gains` row is released once folded into the assessment.
- **Streams**: phases of the filing schedule from the decision agenda's declared schedule stream (`TAX.file_phase`).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: the window's last review interval: of the persons the law requires to file (≈ 1 M a year expected), payers wait
  to their own last occasion inside the window; those occasions fall by each person's phase over the interval's
  business days (≈ 5), so ≈ 0.1 M returns a day at one option each, the window's last day no heavier than its other
  last-interval days (`last_occasion_in_window_one_option`; `LC-5-07`).
- E3: a person with no account files and its payment fails as an arrear (S5.115), never skipped
  (`unpaid_return_is_arrear`).
- E10: a person who died in the year files through its estate (the decision's decider is the estate's administrator
  rule, K-96), its assessment a claim in the waterfall (S5.114's ranking) (`estate_files_for_deceased`).
- E12: a position absent from the opening is not taxed as zero; the return reads only positions that exist
  (`absent_position_not_zero`).

**Extension points**: `TAX.file`'s refund is read by S6.129's household budget (HH.16).

**Unit tests**: `return_through_handles_less_withheld`, `last_occasion_in_window_one_option`,
`refund_early_payment_late_consequences` (the means consequence's sign by the assessment's sign),
`absent_position_not_zero`, `estate_files_for_deceased`, `unpaid_return_is_arrear`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-07` (from S5.109): every assessment equals the person's positions through the handles in force
for the year less its withheld tally; every required person filed within the window or is in arrears.

**Budget**: decision occasions spread over the window: an expected ≈ 1 M required returns a year, ≈ 10 k a day over a
≈ 90-day window at ≈ 300 phone-ns with a choice, and the last interval's payers at ≈ 60 phone-ns with one option.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 3 / 0 / 3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the window's ordinary days).
- on fin.calendar.filing_window_end (the last review interval before `TAX.filing_window`'s last day, the law's dates):
  6 core-ms; joins H (a law's deadline can fall in a quarter end's last days).
- ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (named slot `filing` on K-43: the earliest of its persons' chosen filing days, each
  person's own day re-derived at the take).
- Counters: `sys_tax.returns_filed`, `sys_tax.refunds_paid`, `sys_tax.last_day_returns`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a kept return beside the item it produced; a filing day drawn by chance or set by a rule outside
the person's decision; a preference weight inside the generator.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision point, generator, assessment and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-07` registered (read at the
  gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.110 — The corporate return and losses carried forward

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: corporate tax on reported profit with loss carry-forward and interest deductible as
the law states)*; TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: assessed from the payer's own statement)*
**Architecture**: §7.12 (follows: K-90 filed statements), §7.5 (follows: K-32 firm columns)
**Depends on**: S2.108 (the filing decision and the registry's filed accounts), S1.333 (K-90 statements), S5.101
(`corporate_tax`), S5.102 (`TAX.cit_*`, `TAX.loss_carry_cap`, `TAX.interest_deduction_limit`)
**Goal**: on the day a firm files its accounts, the tax office assesses its corporate tax from the filed statement:
reported profit adjusted as the law states, less losses carried forward to the law's cap; the tax, less instalments
paid, falls due on the law's date or is refunded; an unrelieved loss adds to the firm's losses carried forward.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the sparse tally `TAX.losses_carried_forward` keyed by firm (K-52, S1.254: a row only for a firm with losses unrelieved, its balance carried from year to year); the rule's slot at the registry's filing (S2.108's record written, stage 9d); the due family `TAX.corporate_due` (firm ↔ treasury, dated) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/corporate.rs` | taxable profit and the assessment (pure) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/opening.rs` | each opening firm's losses carried forward from its opening statements (GEN.5), a tally row where it has any |

**Design**:
- **When**: at the record of a firm's filed statement (S2.108), for the firm kinds whose legal form is taxed as a
  company (K-21 legal form data, Law 10); unincorporated owners' profits are their persons' income (S5.109).
- **Assessment** (pure): taxable = reported profit + interest expense above `TAX.interest_deduction_limit`; relief =
  the part of taxable profit the law's cap lets losses carried forward cover; tax = `corporate_tax(taxable − relief)`
  (the small-profits band a band of the schedule); due = tax − instalments paid for the year (the instalment family's
  settled sum, S5.111). A loss adds its amount to the firm's `losses_carried_forward` row (created at its first loss);
  relief subtracts, and a row relieved to zero is released.
- **Writes**: one dated row on `TAX.corporate_due` at the law's payment date (positive: firm → treasury; negative:
  refund), paid in stage 7; the tally's update.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a firm that ended before its due date has its due as a claim of the treasury in its estate (S5.114's ranking)
  (`ended_firm_due_is_estate_claim`).
- E5: fiscal year-ends cluster at calendar quarter-ends: an expected ≈ 0.46 M incorporated firms' filings a year,
  ≈ 0.15 M in a quarter-end's window, spread by each firm's own filing day (RAT.8) (`LC-5-08`).
- E11: a firm founded in the run with no loss history carries 0 losses because it has had none
  (`founded_firm_no_losses`); an opening firm's absent history is not 0 (`opening_losses_absent`).

**Extension points**: the `TAX.losses_carried_forward` tally is read by S5.111 (instalments) and S5.117 (after-tax
values).

**Unit tests**: `loss_carry_forward_cap`, `interest_deduction_limit`, `refund_when_instalments_exceed`,
`founded_firm_no_losses`, `opening_losses_absent`, `ended_firm_due_is_estate_claim`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-08` (from S5.110): every corporate assessment traces to a filed statement and the law in force
for its year; every firm's losses carried forward equal its filed losses less relief taken.

**Budget**: one rule call per filing, ≈ 1 µs: an expected ≈ 2 k a day, ≈ 20 k on a quarter end's heaviest filing day.
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 2 / 0 / 20 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the reports-due part of the line).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool: losses carried forward): +3.6 MB resident (0.3 M expected loss-making firms ×
  12 B, the sparse `TAX.losses_carried_forward` rows), new.
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (inside S1.257's `TAX.corporate_due` row: 0.46 M × 24 B = 11.0 MB).
- Counters: `sys_tax.corporate_assessments`, `sys_tax.losses_relieved`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an assessment from anything but the filed statement; a profit rate read as a parameter.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rule and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-08` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.111 — Corporate instalments on the basis the firm chooses

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.2 PROCESS *(part: the year's instalments on the law's dates, on the basis the payer chooses where
the law allows either)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-100 decision core), §7.9 (follows: K-53 dated
family)
**Depends on**: S5.110 (the corporate assessment and its instalment sum), S1.348 (K-100 option generators), S8.103
(minds attached), S8.122 (the mandate through the office holder's contracts), S1.257 (K-53), S5.102
(`TAX.instalment_days`, `TAX.underpayment_charge`, `TAX.instalment_review_hours`)
**Goal**: at its corporate assessment a firm sets the next year's instalments on the law's dates. Where the law allows
two bases — last year's assessed tax or the firm's own outlook of this year's — the choice is the office holder's,
weighed by its mind from the cost each basis is expected to carry.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/returns.rs` | decision kind `TAX.instalment_basis` (`taken_in` the office the firm's legal form declares for its financing, concerns means and security, mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/points.rs` | the point, woken by the corporate assessment (S5.110) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/instalments.rs` | the option generator; the instalment rows from the chosen basis |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the instalment schedule as dues on the `TAX.corporate_due` row's terms (S5.110's family), dated on `TAX.instalment_days` |

**Design**:
- **Options**: *last year's basis* — instalments summing to the assessment just made; *own outlook* — `corporate_tax`
  over the firm's own outlook of this year's taxable profit (its sales and cost outlooks, K-32 own-outlook columns),
  less its losses carried forward within the cap. Where the law allows one basis only, one option.
- **Consequences**: *means* — the expected underpayment charge (`TAX.underpayment_charge` over the outlook's shortfall)
  against the cost of paying early at the firm's own marginal cost of funds; *security* — the outlook's width (a basis
  on a wide outlook risks a larger charge). The holder's mind chooses (best); `TAX.instalment_review_hours` of staff.
- **Writes**: the instalments as dues on the schedule of the firm's `TAX.corporate_due` row (its terms), on the law's
  dates, paid in stage 7 as dated items.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a firm with no outlook yet (founded this year) has one option, last year's basis, which is absent — its
  instalments are none until its first assessment (`no_basis_no_instalments`).
- E10: a firm that ends stops its instalment dues at its ending; paid instalments count against its final
  assessment in its estate (`ended_firm_instalments_stop`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `instalment_options_consequences`, `single_basis_one_option`, `no_basis_no_instalments`,
`instalments_sum_to_basis`, `ended_firm_instalments_stop`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-09` (from S5.111): every instalment due traces to an assessment and the basis its decision
recorded; every underpayment charge to an assessment above the instalments paid.

**Budget**: one decision per corporate assessment (an expected ≈ 2 k a day, ≈ 20 k on a quarter end's heaviest filing
day, ≈ 1 µs with two options) and ≈ 0.46 M × 4 instalment items a year in the dated stream, on the law's dates.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 2 / 0 / 20 core-ms (B / NB / H).
- on fin.calendar.instalment_day (`TAX.instalment_days`, the law's dates): 0.46 M items to fin.dues.item_ns
  ≈ 6 core-ms; joins H (the law's instalment dates fall at quarter ends).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (the corporate-due row's terms); the decision is woken on K-43's dated wake ring
  (+0 B, core attribute).
- Counters: `sys_tax.instalment_decisions`, `sys_tax.instalments`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a basis fixed by rule where the law allows two; a preference weight in the generator.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision point, generator, family and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-09` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.112 — The property assessor, a named valuer

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: property tax's assessed values per (zone, class))*
**Architecture**: §7.12 (follows: K-91 valuations, valuer declarations), §7.11 (follows: K-86 prints)
**Depends on**: S1.335 (K-91: a valuer's declared method, labelled outputs, never entering a market), S1.326 (K-86:
dwelling and land markets' prints by (zone, class)), S1.323 (K-84: the assessment queue), S1.423 (the Stage 1 agencies,
the tax office among them, with their staff), S1.324 (K-85: staff hours as the day's capacity), S2.141 (the dwelling
appraiser's method, whose declared order the assessor may name), S5.102 (`TAX.assessment_days`, `TAX.property_classes`)
**Goal**: from each of the law's assessment dates the country's tax office values each taxed (zone, class) of dwellings
and land from the period's sales in it, labelled traded, interpolated or extrapolated with its inputs' ages (MKT.20),
at its assessors' capacity: the keys wait in the office's queue and are valued in order as its staff's hours allow; each
value applies from the next instalment after it is made and enters no market.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the valuer declaration `TAX.assessor` (publisher: the tax office; method; subjects: the taxed (zone, class) keys; days: `TAX.assessment_days`) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/assess.rs` | the method: the period's prints of the key; with none, the nearest key's by the method's declared order (zone distance within the class, then the class's neighbours), labelled |

**Design**:
- **When**: on an assessment date every taxed key of the country joins the tax office's assessment queue (K-84, in key
  order); each business day at stage 6c the office values keys from the queue within its assessors' hours (K-85) ÷
  `TAX.hours_per_assessment` (TECHNOLOGY); a key's value applies from the next instalment after its valuation, the
  previous value until then.
- **Value**: per (zone, class) the period's volume-weighted sale price per unit from K-86's daily sums (MKT.12's mark);
  absent prints → the declared nearest order, labelled `interpolated` with the input's age; nothing at all in the class
  → the key's value is absent and its holders owe nothing at that instalment (Law 8: never 0).
- **Writes**: K-91's valuation record per key (publisher, day, value, label, input ages); S5.113 reads it.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a (zone, class) with no sale in the period is valued from its nearest by the declared order, labelled
  (`assessed_nearest_labelled`); a class with none anywhere is absent (`assessed_absent_owes_nothing`).
- E11: the first assessment reads the opening's snapshot prints (GEN.5) as the period's
  (`first_assessment_reads_opening_prints`).
- E13: a country with no property tax declares no assessor (`no_property_tax_no_assessor`).

**Extension points**: the assessed values are read by S5.113 and by S5.157's local taxes.

**Unit tests**: `assessed_vwap_of_period`, `assessed_nearest_labelled`, `assessed_absent_owes_nothing`,
`valued_within_capacity_in_order`, `value_applies_from_next_instalment`, `first_assessment_reads_opening_prints`,
`no_property_tax_no_assessor`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-10` (from S5.112): every assessed value traces to prints of its period or names its nearest key
and label; no assessed value entered a market or an index (VAL.20).

**Budget**: an expected ≈ 40 k (zone, class) keys a round at ≈ 1 µs each, spread by the office's capacity (≈ 700 a day
over ≈ 60 business days at the design point's staff).
- its share of fin.fixed.valuation: 0.7 / 0 / 0.7 core-ms (B / NB / H).
- on fin.calendar.assessment_date (`TAX.assessment_days`, the law's dates): 2 core-ms (the keys queued, ≈ 50 ns each);
  joins B′ (a law's assessment date can be 1 January, taken on the first business day after it).
- ledger line 18 (records within horizons): +2 MB resident (40 k keys × 2 valuation records within the horizon × 24 B).
- Counters: `sys_tax.assessed_keys`, `sys_tax.assessed_interpolated`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an assessed value from a formula over incomes or rents; a value of 0 standing in for no sales.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The valuer declaration, method and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-10` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.113 — Property tax, a holding levy on the instalment dates

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: property tax on dwellings and land)*
**Architecture**: §4.3 (follows: levies: holding levies), §7.8 (follows: K-51), §7.1 (follows: K-06 holders by (zone,
class))
**Depends on**: S5.112 (assessed values), S1.253 (K-51: holding levies over index instances on a date), S1.165 (K-06:
holders by (zone, class)), S1.268 (K-58: a jointly held dwelling's members and shares), S5.102 (`TAX.property_rate`,
`TAX.property_classes`, `TAX.property_instalment_days`)
**Goal**: on each instalment date every holder of a taxed dwelling or parcel owes the law's rate on the assessed value
of what it holds, a levy computed per holder from the (zone, class) index of holders and paid to the treasury in that
day's settlement. No row is kept per owner.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the holding levy declaration over the owners' holders-by-(zone, class) index instance (S1.165, read for the taxed classes), date `TAX.property_instalment_days`, payee the treasury, handle `property_tax` |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/property.rs` | the holder's base: units held × assessed value per unit; a joint holding's split by its shares |

**Design**:
- **When**: stage 2a of each instalment day, K-51's holding-levy entry point over the owners' (zone, class) instance for
  the taxed classes, on the pool by key range.
- **Amount**: `property_tax(units × assessed value, schedule)` per holding, rounded once by the law's convention; a
  joint holding (K-58) is split among its members by K-16's apportion with the named residue; a holder is a person
  (E 46), a firm or an institution. The items join that day's dated stream (holder → treasury), paid at stage 7; one
  that fails is an arrear (S5.115).
- **Absent value**: a key whose assessed value is absent owes nothing that instalment (S5.112).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: an instalment day lists the taxed dwelling rows (an expected ≈ 1.6 M holder rows of dwellings; the 4.5 M unit
  rows include vehicles) and the taxed parcels; a law whose instalment falls on a quarter-end payday makes the
  composite day the gate reads (`LC-5-11`).
- E4: an estate holding a dwelling owes the tax as a claim of its administration (payer the estate)
  (`estate_pays_property_tax`).
- E10: a holder ended since the index was last written is not in it (K-06 removal at the ending, K-97)
  (`ended_holder_not_levied`).
- E3: a holder with no money fails its item: an arrear, never a skipped levy (`failed_levy_is_arrear`).
- E6: the holders' index is rebuilt at load, never saved (`index_rebuilt_equals_saved_holdings`).

**Extension points**: municipalities' local property taxes (S5.157) declare their own holding levy on the same index.

**Unit tests**: `property_levy_at_assessed_value`, `joint_holding_split_by_shares`, `absent_assessment_no_levy`,
`estate_pays_property_tax`, `ended_holder_not_levied`, `failed_levy_is_arrear`, `index_rebuilt_equals_saved_holdings`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-11` (from S5.113): every property levy traces to a holding in the index on an instalment date
and the assessed value then in force; every taxed holding on that date was levied or its key's value was absent.

**Budget**: instalment days only, stage 2a on the day's pool: ≈ 1.6 M levies at ≈ 5 ns and their items.
- on fin.calendar.property_instalment (`TAX.property_instalment_days`, the law's dates): 28 core-ms (1.6 M levies ×
  5 ns + 1.6 M items to fin.dues.item_ns); joins H (the law's instalment dates can be quarter-end paydays).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB (reuses the owners' holders-by-(zone, class) instance, S1.165), marked
  `#[saved(skip, rebuild)]`; its rebuild at load is K-06's over the unit rows already counted in S1.165's load cost:
  ≈ 1.6 M holdings × `fin.index.insert_ns` 15.4 VM ≈ 25 ms VM of the load's `load_ms`.
- Counters: `sys_tax.property_levies`, `sys_tax.property_levies_failed`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

### S5.114 — Inheritance tax, a claim ranked in the estate

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.1 STATE *(part: inheritance tax on estates)*
**Architecture**: §7.15 (follows: K-96 estates, K-98 claims and classes), §9.1 (follows: endings)
**Depends on**: S1.342 (K-96 estates' lifecycle), S1.345 (K-98: claims per class), S2.132 (the insolvency law's classes,
taxes among them), S2.133 (estate administration's inventory at its valuer's values), S2.135 (inheritance in kind),
S5.101 (`inheritance_tax`), S5.102 (`TAX.inheritance_*`)
**Goal**: when a person's estate has its inventory valued, the tax office computes the inheritance tax the law states —
on the estate or on each heir's share, as the law declares — as a claim of the treasury on the estate, ranked in the
class the law places taxes and paid in the estate's distribution before the heirs receive in kind.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the rule's slot at the estate's inventory (K-96 state change, stage 2f); the claim's family and class (K-98, the law's tax class) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/inheritance.rs` | the base (estate net of its debts, or each heir's share by the law of succession) and the tax (pure) |

**Design**:
- **When**: stage 2f of the day the estate's inventory is valued (S2.133), once per estate; again only if a later
  valuation of the administration changes the base (the claim is re-stated, not added).
- **Amount**: `inheritance_tax(base, schedule)` with the law's allowance; per heir where the law taxes shares (each
  heir's share from the law of succession S2.135 reads), summed into one claim of the treasury per estate, rounded once.
- **Writes**: a claim row (K-98) in the law's class; the estate's distribution pays it by the waterfall; an estate that
  cannot pay leaves the rest unpaid, a loss of the treasury recorded with the estate.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E4: an estate that never liquidates keeps the claim open with its others; nothing forces it
  (`claim_stays_open_with_estate`).
- E13: a country with no inheritance tax declares none (`no_tax_no_claim`).
- E1: a catastrophe's deaths open many estates the same day: one claim each (`LC-5-12`).

**Extension points**: heirs abroad: the estate's distribution to them is a capital-account transfer (S5.185).

**Unit tests**: `inheritance_tax_allowance`, `per_heir_by_succession_law`, `claim_restated_not_added`,
`no_tax_no_claim`, `claim_stays_open_with_estate`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-12` (from S5.114): every inheritance-tax claim traces to an estate's inventory and the law in
force at the death; each ranks in the law's class of its country's waterfall.

**Budget**: an expected ≈ 200 estates a day of persons at ≈ 1 µs.
- its share of fin.fixed.resolve: 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H).
- ledger line 20 (estates): +0 B (named slot: one K-98 claim row among the estate's claims).
- Counters: `sys_tax.inheritance_claims`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a tax taken from the heirs after distribution in place of a claim on the estate; a claim ranked
by its instrument rather than the law's class.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rule, declarations and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-12` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.115 — Tax arrears, their penalties and the tax office's enforcement

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.3 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.9 (follows: K-56 arrears, K-55 rate terms), §7.15 (follows: K-98
claims), §7.16 (follows: K-100 decision core)
**Depends on**: S1.265 (K-56: yesterday's fails become arrears at 2d; the arrears agenda), S1.263 (K-55: a rate term
accruing on its dates), S2.123 (the insolvency procedures a creditor's petition opens against a firm), S2.167 (a
creditor's petition against a person, an option of the creditor's workout), S2.132 (the tax class in the waterfall),
S1.348 (K-100 option generators), S8.103 (minds attached), S1.423 (the tax office among the Stage 1 agencies),
S5.102 (`TAX.arrear_penalty_rate`, `TAX.enforcement_after_days`, `TAX.enforcement_review_hours`)
**Goal**: an unpaid tax — a remittance, a return's payment, an instalment, a corporate due, a property levy or, from
S5.178, a customs demand — becomes an arrear of the payer to the treasury carrying the law's penalty. Persisting past
the day from which the law lets the tax office enforce, it is the office's to pursue: the office may petition under
the insolvency law, as any unpaid creditor may, or wait; in any estate the arrear ranks in the class the law places
taxes.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/returns.rs` | decision kind `TAX.enforce` (`taken_in` the tax office's collection office, concerns means and standing, mode best); its view |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | family `TAX.arrear` (payer → treasury, `Balance` layout) with the penalty as a rate term on its shape; every tax payment's reason mapped to it as its arrears family (K-56 declaration); the enforcement occasion at `TAX.enforcement_after_days` and each `TAX.enforcement_review_hours`-paced review after it (K-56's arrears agenda) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/rules/enforce.rs` | the option generator; the petition's content from the arrear (pure) |

**Design**:
- **Arrear**: at 2d, K-56 turns yesterday's failed tax items into rows of `TAX.arrear` (amount, since); the penalty
  accrues by the shape's rate term on its dates (K-55), so no rule posts it. Later payments reduce the row; paid in
  full it closes.
- **Enforcement** (`TAX.enforce`), woken by K-56's arrears agenda at `TAX.enforcement_after_days` (POLICY, the law's
  collection rule, S5.102) and, while the row is open, at the office's next review:
  - **Options**: *wait* (the penalty accrues; the next review is the office's); *petition* — through S2.123 (a firm)
    or S2.166 (a person), the same creditor's petition any unpaid creditor files, where the payer's law allows it.
  - **Consequences**, from the office's own view of the payer (its filed statements or its accounts' balances the
    office may read under the law): *means* — the recovery expected in the tax class of the payer's estate by the
    waterfall's order (S2.132) against the arrear with its penalty expected by waiting, and the staff hours of a
    petition (`TAX.enforcement_review_hours`); *standing* — the office's record of collection its holder is judged
    by under its mandate (MND.9).
  - The office holder's mind chooses (best); until the office is filled (S5.144) it decides at its founding view.
    The law enables the petition; nothing forces it.
- **In an estate**: the row is a claim in the law's tax class (S2.132), paid by the waterfall in every currency the
  payer held.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a mass-default day's failed tax items become arrears in K-56's mass marking (`LC-5-13`).
- E14: an arrear and a new payment of the same payer the same day: the payment reduces the row after the day's
  accrual (`payment_after_accrual_same_day`).
- E10: a payer that ended: the row names its estate (K-97) and is a claim, never petitioned
  (`ended_payer_arrear_is_claim`).
- E13: a law without a petition for tax debts offers the office one option, wait (`no_petition_law_one_option`).

**Extension points**: customs demands (S5.178) map their failure to `TAX.arrear`.

**Unit tests**: `arrear_penalty_accrues_exactly`, `enforce_occasion_at_law_day`, `enforce_options_consequences` (given
an arrear and a payer's statement: the expected recovery by the tax class against waiting, each on its concern),
`payment_after_accrual_same_day`, `arrear_ranks_in_tax_class`, `ended_payer_arrear_is_claim`,
`no_petition_law_one_option`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-13` (from S5.115): TAX.3 — every failed tax payment became an arrear with its penalty; every
petition by a tax office traces to an arrear past the law's day and its office's recorded choice; every tax claim in
an estate ranks where the law places it.

**Budget**: arrears at K-56's marking (≈ 20 ns) for failed tax items, an expected ≈ 2 k on a business day and ≈ 20 k on
a heavy day; enforcement decisions on the rows reaching the law's day and their reviews, an expected ≈ 1 k a business
day at ≈ 1 µs with two options.
- adds 2 k / 0 / 20 k items to fin.dues.item_ns (the marking).
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 1 / 0 / 1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the enforcement decisions).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (inside S1.257's `TAX.arrear` row: 0.2 M expected open rows × 28 B = 5.6 MB).
- Counters: `sys_tax.arrears`, `sys_tax.enforce_decisions`, `sys_tax.petitions`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a penalty posted by a handler; an arrear written off by the collector's choice; a petition filed
by rule after a number of days; a preference weight in the generator.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, decision point, generator and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-13` registered (read at the
  gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.116 — A consumption tax in the retail prices sellers post

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.4 PROCESS *(part: a consumption tax raises the retail price households see, through sellers' own
price reviews)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-101 attention: an announced change raises the
stake), §7.11 (follows: K-70 posted offers)
**Depends on**: S1.450 (the price review), S1.350 (K-101: a surprise or announcement raising the stake and redrawing the
review), S5.101 (`vat`, `sales_tax` handles), S5.105 (the tax at the sale), S1.179 (K-20: dated schedules with their
announced and effective days)
**Goal**: a seller's price review weighs its options at what it keeps after the consumption tax in force on the days
each price would stand — including a change announced but not yet effective — so a rate change reaches retail posted
points only through sellers' own reviews, woken by the announcement, and nothing else writes a posted point.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/rules/price_review.rs` | the review's consequences on *means* computed on the net of `vat`/`sales_tax` at the schedules in force over the price's expected life (announced changes read, VAL.6) |
| `crates/systems/sys-frm/src/lib.rs` | the announcement of a consumption-tax schedule change declared as a surprise source for the price-review attention of sellers of the taxed classes in that country (K-101 declaration) |

**Design**:
- **Reads**: the posted point is gross to final buyers where the law so declares (S5.105); the review's view carries
  the handles and the schedules in force on each day of its horizon (K-20: in force on d, announced changes included).
- **Consequences**: each candidate point's expected revenue is the gross point less the tax at each day's schedule,
  times the seller's own outlook of units at that gross point; the rest of the review is S1.450's unchanged.
- **Wake**: an announced change of a consumption-tax schedule raises the attention stake of the price reviews of the
  sellers of the taxed product classes in that country (K-101, O(1) per seller through the declared kind's stake), so
  they review before or on the effective day by their own attention.
- **Streams**: none new.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a rate change's announcement redraws the reviews of the sellers of the taxed classes (≈ 1.7 M posted points);
  K-101 draws each seller's next review from its raised rate, so the reviews spread by attention's own draw and the
  first business day carries the largest share (`announcement_spreads_by_attention_draw`; `LC-5-14`).
- E11: before any change, the review reads the opening's schedule; nothing differs from S1.450
  (`no_change_review_unchanged`).
- E13: a country whose consumption tax is a retail sales tax applies it only to its final classes' points
  (`rst_only_final_class_points`).

**Extension points**: none added; S5.135's writer makes the announcements this review then sees.

**Unit tests**: `review_net_of_tax_in_force`, `announced_change_enters_horizon`, `announcement_raises_stake`,
`announcement_spreads_by_attention_draw` (given raised rates, the share of redraws landing on each day is
1 − e^(−λ') then its decay, never all on one day), `no_change_review_unchanged`, `rst_only_final_class_points`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-14` (from S5.116; applicable once a parliament changes a consumption-tax rate in the run):
TAX.4 — after the change's effective day, retail posted points moved only through sellers' reviews, and every
review after the announcement read the new schedule.

**Budget**: no daily cost. The peak is the first business day after an announcement: 1.7 M × (1 − e^(−λ')) redraws
landing there, λ' the sellers' raised review rate; at the design point's raised mean interval of 10 days an expected
≈ 0.16 M reviews, then decaying day by day. A parliament announces on a business day (S5.135), and sellers review on
their own trading days, so no closed day's draws are carried to the next business day.
- on fin.calendar.tax_announcement (a consumption-tax change's announcement day, the parliament's): 0.16 M items to
  fin.decide.review_ns ≈ 88 core-ms on the first business day; joins H and B′ (an announcement on any sitting day
  can put its first business day on either).
- ledger line 14 (wheel and agenda): +0 B (core attribute: the redrawn day is K-43's column).
- Counters: `sys_frm.reviews_on_tax_change`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a posted point rewritten by the tax system; a price marked up by the tax rate by rule.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Rule change and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-14` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.117 — Corporate tax in a firm's values of projects

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.4 PROCESS *(part: corporate tax changes what a project is worth after tax)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.13 (follows: phx-val's value arithmetic)
**Depends on**: S1.458 (investment on the firm's own value of the project), S1.459 (project values), S5.101
(`corporate_tax`), S5.110 (losses carried forward), S2.131 (investment at the cost of money)
**Goal**: the investment decision's options carry their consequences after corporate tax: each project's added taxable
profit through `corporate_tax` at the firm's own position — the band it is in, its losses carried forward, interest
deductible to the law's limit — so a change of the corporate schedule changes what firms build.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-cap/src/rules/invest.rs` | the project's cash flows net of the tax its added profit bears at the firm's own position, year by year through the handle |

**Design**:
- **Tax on the project**: for each year of the project's horizon, `corporate_tax(profit with the project) −
  corporate_tax(profit without it)` at the firm's own outlook of profit and its losses carried forward within the
  cap, with the schedule in force on that year's filing (announced changes read); depreciation deducted as the
  law's schedule states (a declared part of the schedule, absent where the law has none).
- **Consequences**: *means* is the after-tax value; everything else is S1.458's.
- **Streams**: none.

- E13: an unincorporated firm's project is taxed at its owners' income tax (their persons' marginal rate), read
  through `income_tax` over the owner's own position — the legal form's data names which handle

**Extension points**: none.

`absent_losses_not_zero_in_project`.

### S5.118 — Gains tax in when a household sells

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TAX.4 PROCESS *(part: capital-gains tax changes when a holder sells)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points)
**Depends on**: S3.158 (households' `choose_holdings`), S5.108 (realised gains to date), S5.101 (`gains_tax`)
**Goal**: a household's sale options carry the gains tax each would bear at the seller person's own year-to-date
gains and the allowance left, so holders time sales against the allowance and the band.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/rules/portfolio.rs` | each sale option's *means* consequence net of `gains_tax(gains to date + this sale's gain) − gains_tax(gains to date)` for the selling person; the same at the next tax year's allowance for a sale deferred past the year's end |

**Design**:
- **Per option**: the gain the sale would realise is proceeds at the seller's expected price less the holding's average
  cost (K-60/K-62, S1.276's arithmetic); the tax is the handle's difference at the person's realised-gains tally
  (S5.108). A deferral option past the tax year's end reads next year's allowance (the schedule in force then).

- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a holding whose cost is absent (an opening holding with no cost basis in the snapshot) makes its gain absent,
  and the sale option carries no tax term rather than a gain on zero cost (`absent_cost_no_gain`).
- E14: two sales considered together in one review add their gains before the tax (`joint_sales_add_gains`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `sale_timed_against_allowance`, `deferral_reads_next_year`, `absent_cost_no_gain`,
`joint_sales_add_gains`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-16` (from S5.118): every household sale's decision recorded the gains-tax term at the seller's
own tally; the distribution of persons' realised gains around the allowance is published with TAX.6's reads.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/metrics.rs` | `TAX.receipts_by_base` (monthly, from the treasury's receipts tally by base), `TAX.effective_rates` (yearly, by decile of the sample's income and of its wealth), `TAX.receipts_elasticity` (receipts by base against the published output series, yearly) |
| `crates/systems/sys-tax/src/lib.rs` | the sample frame declaration (persons of the country, K-39 instance, stream `TAX.sample`), the records' kinds, audience public, lags |

**Design**:
- **Receipts by base**: the treasury's receipts tallied by (country, base) in settlement's apply (K-52), published
  monthly with the office's lag (K-37).
- **Effective rates**: at the tax year's close the office draws its sample of persons (K-39 frame, world stream
  `TAX.sample`) and copies each sampled person's closed-year tallies — tax paid (withheld + assessed) and income —
  into the frame, before the tallies' period stamp moves on (the person tax-year pair keeps no closed period). Over the
  office's lag it then reads the sample in daily slices: each sampled person's net worth (its accounts and holdings at
  their carrying values, labelled with the slice's day, as a survey's fieldwork reads it), accumulating the decile
  sums; the release ranks the sample and publishes the rate by decile. A sample, never a pass over every person.
- **Elasticity**: each base's receipts' log change against published output's over the years the run holds, with its
  interval; absent until two years exist.
- **Streams**: `TAX.sample`.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: in the run's first year the elasticity is absent (`elasticity_absent_first_year`).
- E13: a base a country does not tax publishes nothing, not 0 (`untaxed_base_publishes_nothing`).

**Extension points**: the reads are frozen in `READS.toml` (S5.100) and read at the gate (S5.187).

**Unit tests**: `deciles_from_sample`, `elasticity_absent_first_year`, `receipts_by_base_sum_to_receipts`,
`untaxed_base_publishes_nothing`, `sample_copied_before_reset` (the frame holds the closed year's tallies after the new
year's first posting), `slices_sum_to_whole_sample`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-17` (from S5.121): TAX.6 — receipts by base, effective rates by income and wealth decile and
receipts' elasticity to output are published on their calendars, and receipts by base sum to the treasury's tax
receipts.

**Budget**: the monthly publication reads the receipts tally (≈ 1 core-ms); the yearly sample of 50 k persons is
copied at the close (≈ 20 phone-ns a person) and read in slices over the office's lag (≈ 1 µs a person).
- its share of fin.fixed.stats: 0.05 / 0 / 0.05 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the monthly release, averaged).
- on fin.calendar.tax_year_close (the tax year's close, taken on the first business day after it): 1 core-ms (the copy
  into the frame); joins B′.
- spread after fin.calendar.tax_year_close over 10 days: 5 core-ms a day on fin.fixed.stats (5 k sampled persons a
  business day, each read once).
- on fin.calendar.effective_rates_release (the office's yearly release, a business day its lag after the close): 0.5
  core-ms (the ranking); joins H and B′.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool: the tax office's sample frame): +1 MB resident (50 k × 20 B: the member and its
  copied closed-year tallies).
- Counters: `sys_tax.sample_size`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a measure that sets anything; a decile computed over every person.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Metrics, sample declaration and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-17` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.
