### S5.139 — A platform's value to a household, through the law's own handles

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.4 DECISION *(part: applying each platform to its own household's position and outlooks)*; HH.12
DECISION *(part)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: rule handles), §7.13 (follows: phx-val: outlooks)
**Depends on**: S5.101 (tax handles), S5.123 (benefit rules as handles), S5.128 (published waits), S5.136 (platforms),
S1.336 (K-92 public series and methods: the household's outlooks)
**Goal**: the value of a platform to a household is the change in its disposable income over the term with the
platform's policy values in place of the law's, computed through the same rule handles the levies and benefits use —
income tax and contributions on each adult's own position, the consumption tax on its spending outlook, the benefits
it receives or would, and the change in the waits of the services its members use at the platform's appropriations.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/platform_value.rs` | `platform_value(view: &HouseholdPositionView, platform: &Platform, law: &Platform) -> PlatformValue` (pure), by term year |

**Design**:
- **Per year of the term** (its outlook's growth applied to each position): Σ adults `income_tax` and `contributions`
  on the adult's own taxable income and pay; `vat`/`sales_tax` on the household's spending outlook by class; the
  benefit rules' amounts for the benefits its members receive or are eligible for (the rule handles over their own
  positions); the published wait of each service its members use at the platform's appropriation for that function
  (the wait scaled by the capacity the appropriation funds at the agency's current costs), times the service's daily
  cost of going unserved (S5.128) — each under the platform's schedule, less the same under the law's.
- **Output**: `PlatformValue { by_year: [Money], redistribution: Fixed }` — the money change by year (the vote's
  *means*), and the platform's declared redistribution position (the vote's *principle*), read from its schedules'
  progressivity; no discounting here: the decision core hands the voter's patience to its mind (MND.20).
- A value is never computed at a mean across a band edge: every handle is called at each adult's own position (Law 11).
- **Only what differs is evaluated**: a platform's value is a difference from the law, so a schedule a platform holds
  equal to the law's contributes exactly zero and its handle is not called; the set of differing schedules is
  computed once per platform when the platform is adopted (a platform's own columns), not per household.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a benefit the household is not eligible for under either schedule contributes nothing; an absent position
  (a new adult's income outlook) makes that adult's term absent, never zero (`absent_position_absent_term`).
- E13: a platform identical to the law gives zero change (`law_against_itself_zero`).

**Extension points**: S5.177 adds tariffs' effect on the household's spending outlook when border policies enter
platforms; read by S5.140 and S5.152 (a founder's best platform).

**Unit tests**: `platform_value_through_the_laws_handles`, `law_against_itself_zero`,
`wait_change_valued_at_cost_of_going_unserved`, `absent_position_absent_term`, `each_adult_own_band`.

**Live checks**: none (S5.140's LC-5-31 reads the vote's consequences).

**Budget**: per household and platform, two handle calls (platform and law) per differing schedule per adult or
household base, ≈ 20 phone-ns each; with ≈ 6 platforms each differing from the law in ≈ 3 schedules, ≈ 0.7 µs a
household occasion, counted in S5.140's campaign day.
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B (named slot: each party's differing-schedule set among its platform columns).
- Counters: `sys_pol.platform_values`, `sys_pol.differing_schedules`.

**Guards**: PC-70 (the handles take the platform's schedule).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a platform valued at a group average; a second representation of the law beside its handles.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The function and its tests written; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.140 — The vote, each adult's own

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.4 DECISION; HH.12 DECISION; POL.10 FORBID
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-100 decision core, K-102 minds: `choose` with
tastes)
**Depends on**: S5.137 (intentions and occasions), S1.197 (the campaign window), S5.138 (published polls: closeness),
S5.139 (platform values),
S1.348 (K-100), S8.103 (minds attached), S8.106 (a household's adults deciding at one occasion), S1.336 (K-92: the
voter's outlooks of published unemployment and prices)
**Goal**: on its household's occasion each adult forms its intention: for the platform it expects to leave its
household best off — each platform applied to its household's position and outlooks, the incumbents' record read as its
own surprises in published statistics — or to abstain when voting is worth less to it than its cost; what a vote is
worth rises with the closeness of the race its vote counts in, as the latest published polls show it. Its tastes are
drawn on each occasion from one distribution for every platform, so alike voters spread across parties.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/elections.rs` | decision kind `POL.vote` (`taken_in = person`, concerns means, security, principle, leisure_and_health, mode best, taste stream `POL.vote_taste`); its view (the household's platform values, the voter's outlook surprises since the last election, the district's latest published poll, the voter's cost of voting) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/vote.rs` | the option generator |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/election_parameters.rs` | PC-190: no turnout, swing, loyalty or bloc primitive in POL's declarations |

**Design**:
- **Options**: each party standing in the voter's district, and abstain.
- **Consequences** of voting for a party: *means* — S5.139's value of its platform over the term; *principle* — its
  platform's redistribution position; *security* — for each governing party, the voter's own surprises of the
  published unemployment and price series since the last election (retrospective voting, Fiorina, 1981), entered in
  money a year (the change in its adults' expected time without work at their wages; the change in its real income).
  Each vote option's consequences are scaled by the race's closeness in the voter's district from the latest published
  poll; before the campaign's first poll closeness is absent and no scaling is applied (the calculus of voting's stakes
  term, Riker and Ordeshook, 1968; probabilistic voting, Lindbeck and Weibull, 1987 — listed in `SHAPES.toml`).
  *Abstain*: *leisure_and_health* — the cost of voting in hours at the voter's value of leisure saved (PREFERENCE:
  `POL.cost_of_voting`).
- **Choice**: the core's `choose` with the voter's tastes (REP.22) and mind; the intention is written into the column
  (S5.137); on election day the vote is the intention held at the day's close. Every adult has had an occasion inside
  the campaign (S5.137's schedule and need occasions), so an adult abstains only by its own weighing.
- **Forbids** (POL.10): the view carries no aggregate beyond published records and polls the voter can read; no
  turnout, swing, loyalty or bloc parameter exists in the register (`phx-check` refuses a `POL.*` primitive of those
  names' kind: PC-190); no election result is written by anything but the tally.
- **Streams**: `POL.vote_taste` (REP.22, through the decision core).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a campaign business day in the largest country carries its households ÷ P scheduled occasions, P the declared
  review interval in business days (`POL.vote_review_schedule`), and no poll-driven redraw (S5.137)
  (`phases_uniform_over_interval`, S5.137; `LC-5-31`).
- E11: before any poll, closeness is absent (`no_poll_no_closeness`).
- E12: an adult whose platform value is absent for every party (no position at all) holds only abstain's consequence
  and its tastes (`absent_values_abstain_by_cost`).
- E14: two adults of one household with different tastes may intend differently (`adults_differ_by_taste`).

**Extension points**: intentions are read by S5.138, S5.142; a founding adult's option set is extended by S5.152.

**Unit tests**: `vote_options_consequences`, `closeness_scales_vote_worth`, `no_poll_no_closeness`,
`abstain_saves_cost_of_voting`, `absent_values_abstain_by_cost`, `adults_differ_by_taste`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-31` (from S5.140): POL.4, POL.10 — every intention traces to a vote decision on an occasion with
its consequences recorded; no vote read a statistic but through the voter's own outlooks of published series, and none
read a poll but the published ones; turnout per election is published (a constant turnout across the elections the run
holds is a finding about the cost of voting or the value gaps).

**Budget**: households ÷ P occasions a campaign business day in the campaigning country, each ≈ 1.4 µs (platform
values ≈ 0.7 µs, after the representation that evaluates only schedules differing from the law, S5.139, and 1.9 adults
× 7 options × 50 ns): in the largest country 1.55 M households ÷ P = 20 is an expected 78 k occasions a day. Nothing
outside campaigns, nothing on non-business days (the vote is not among TIME.8's non-business decisions); new adults'
need occasions add an expected 300 a day.
- on fin.calendar.campaign_day (every business day of a campaign, the constitution's `POL.campaign_days` before the
  election): 110 core-ms; joins H and B′ (a campaign spans them when they fall inside it).
- ledger line 4 (households): +0 B (the occasion's day is S5.137's windowed group).
- Counters: `sys_pol.vote_decisions`, `sys_pol.abstain_intentions`.

**Guards**: PC-190 — no primitive of a turnout, swing, loyalty or bloc kind in POL's declarations (a declaration check).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a vote from an aggregate statistic in place of the voter's own position; a loyalty parameter; a
preference weight in the generator.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision point, generator and tests written; fast checks pass; PC-190 registered; `LC-5-31` registered (read at
  the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`, a campaign day measured; the two reviews done;
  status `done` and the section removed.

### S5.141 — Party finance: public funding, deposits, staff and polls bought

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.7 PROCESS *(part: a party stands by paying its registration deposit, and is paid per vote received
at the tally)*
**Architecture**: §7.9 (follows: K-53 dated families), §4.7 (follows: decision points)
**Depends on**: S5.134 (the funding and deposit entries), S5.136 (parties), S5.138 (polls for sale), S5.135 (the
constitution's nomination day), S1.413 (vacancy posting), S1.257 (K-53), S3.123 (the treasury's payment order)
**Goal**: parties pay their way: each party that stands pays the registration deposit on the nomination day and does
not stand if it cannot; at the tally each is paid per vote received by the treasury, and its deposit returned or
forfeited by the constitution's rule; parties employ staff and buy polls from pollsters when a fresher reading is
worth its price to them.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/lib.rs` | families `POL.public_funding` (treasury → party, dated at the constitution's payment date, in the treasury's order) and `POL.deposit` (party → treasury; return due back by the rule); the party kind's posting declaration (it employs); the declarations of `POL.funding_per_vote`, `POL.deposit`, `POL.deposit_return_rule` (their entries S5.134's) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/buy_poll.rs` | decision kind `POL.buy_poll` (`taken_in` the party's leader, concerns standing and means, mode best) |

**Design**:
- **Deposit** (stage 5c of the nomination day): each party with candidates pays `POL.deposit` per list or district as
  the constitution states; a failed payment means the party does not stand (a record).
- **Funding** (at the tally, S5.142): each party's entitlement `POL.funding_per_vote × votes`, exact in integers, a
  dated row paid at the constitution's date; the deposit returned or forfeited by `POL.deposit_return_rule`.
- **Staff**: a party posts vacancies through the posting rule and pays from its account.
- **`POL.buy_poll`** (the party's review days in a campaign): options buy each pollster's next poll at its price, or
  none; consequences *standing* — the votes the leader expects to gain by adapting on the fresher reading (its own
  outlook), *means* — the price (the value of sample information, Raiffa and Schlaifer, 1961, listed).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a party without money cannot stand (`deposit_failed_does_not_stand`).
- E10: a party dissolved after the tally has its funding paid to its estate (`dissolved_party_funding_to_estate`).
- E14: the deposit's return and the funding due of one party at one tally are two rows (`funding_and_return_two_rows`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `public_funding_per_vote_exact`, `deposit_returned_or_forfeited_by_rule`,
`deposit_failed_does_not_stand`, `buy_poll_value_against_price`, `dissolved_party_funding_to_estate`,
`funding_and_return_two_rows`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-32` (from S5.141): POL.7, POL.12 — every public-funding payment traces to its party's tally × the
rate and was paid on the declared date in the treasury's order; every standing party paid its deposit; every poll bought
names its buyer, pollster and price; parties spent only from their own accounts.

**Budget**: ≈ 30 parties: deposits on the nomination day, funding at the tally, poll purchases on their review days.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (≈ 30 decisions a campaign week).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0 B (≈ 60 rows an election).
- Counters: `sys_pol.funding_paid`, `sys_pol.deposits_forfeited`, `sys_pol.polls_bought`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a party or pollster paid but by named payments; funding by a share of an aggregate.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rules and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-32` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section

### S5.142 — Election day: the tally, the allotment and the seats

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.7 PROCESS *(part: an election held on its date; seats allotted, each to a person its party put up,
and a directly elected office to the candidate the constitution's rule elects)*
**Architecture**: §7.6 (follows: K-39 accumulators, K-37 records), §4.10 (follows: public events)
**Depends on**: S5.137 (intentions and their counts), S5.140 (votes), S5.141 (deposits and funding), S1.221 (K-39),
S1.215 (K-37),
S1.213 (K-36), S1.209 (K-34 offices), S1.257 (K-53 appointments)
**Goal**: on election day the adults vote their intentions as held at the day's close; the tally counts them by
(district, party) exactly; the constitution's rule allots the seats, each to the person its party's list puts up, and
a directly elected office to its candidate; the result is a public record at the close and a public event the next
day.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/lib.rs` | the tally's slot at stage 10a of the election day, reading S5.137's accumulator; the electorate's size from K-39's accumulator of adults by country; the result record kind; family `POL.appointment` (person ↔ parliament, the member's mandate and pay) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/allot.rs` | allotment rules: D'Hondt, largest remainder, plurality per district, the threshold; ties by lot |

**Design**:
- **Tally** (stage 10a): the counts of intentions by (district, party) held at the day's close (S5.137's accumulator,
  maintained exactly at each change), abstain and `none` apart, `none` published as undecided beside turnout; no
  ballot pass is made — the counts are the ballots' sums, recounted by the audit's rolling slice (LC-5-30).
- **Allotment**: the constitution's rule over the district tallies, ties by lot (`POL.seat_lot`); each seat to the
  next person on the party's list in that district (its candidacy rows); a directly elected office by its rule (with a
  run-off date where declared, a second tally on that date).
- **Writes**: appointment rows for the elected (the member's pay from the parliament's account); the result record
  (K-37, public at the close); the public event at the next 10a (K-36); funding and deposit rows (S5.141).
- **Streams**: `POL.seat_lot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: an election day (often a non-business day) reads 25 districts × 12 counts: no work proportional to the
  electorate on the day (`tally_reads_counts_only`).
- E2: a district where one party stands allots all its seats to it; a district where none stands is left empty and
  recorded (`no_candidates_seat_empty_recorded`).
- E10: an elected candidate who dies before taking the seat: the next on the list (the constitution's rule)
  (`dead_elected_next_on_list`).
- E7: the counts are order-free sums (`tally_integer_and_order_independent`).

**Extension points**: seats are read by S5.143 (coalitions), S5.153 (votes on bills), S5.144 (vacancies refilled).

**Unit tests**: `allotment_dhondt`, `allotment_largest_remainder`, `allotment_plurality`, `threshold_applies`,
`tally_integer_and_order_independent`, `no_candidates_seat_empty_recorded`, `tally_reads_counts_only`,
`dead_elected_next_on_list`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-33` (from S5.142): POL.10 — every seat traces to the tally of intentions and the allotment rule;
the result's undecided and turnout are published; platforms of the main parties at each election are recorded.

**Budget**: the election day reads counts and writes the seats' appointments (an expected 300 rows a country).
- on fin.calendar.election_day (the constitution's election date, often a closed day): 1 core-ms; joins H and B′
  (a closed day of either turn).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.03 MB resident (1 k `POL.appointment` rows × 25 B).
- Counters: `sys_pol.votes_cast`, `sys_pol.abstentions`, `sys_pol.undecided`, `sys_pol.seats_allotted`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a result written other than from the tally; a seat allotted by a vote share parameter.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, allotment rules and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-33` registered (read at the gate).

### S5.143 — Coalitions, the government and the new mandate

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.6 DECISION; POL.7 PROCESS; POL.3 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.11 (follows: K-80 bilateral protocol), §4.7 (follows: decision points), §4.6 (follows: the one
writer of a policy value)
**Depends on**: S5.142 (seats), S5.135 (the writer and the coalition procedure), S5.136 (platforms), S1.317 (K-80),
S1.348 (K-100), S8.122 (the mandate through the holder's contracts), S1.435 (retires its placeholder
`POL.values_standing`)
**Goal**: from the day after the result, coalitions form by the constitution's procedure — a formateur proposes a
coalition and its platform, the parties it needs accept or decline — and a majority's platform becomes the new
mandate, written with its announcement and the constitution's effective date; the head of government and the ministers
are persons the coalition names; with no majority after the procedure's rounds the standing mandate stays.
`POL.values_standing` is retired.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/polity.rs` | decision kinds `POL.form_coalition` (`taken_in` the formateur party's leader) and `POL.accept_coalition` (`taken_in` each invited party's leader), concerns principle and standing, mode best; message kinds `CoalitionProposal`, `CoalitionAnswer` (K-80) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/{coalition,accept}.rs` | the option generators |
| `data/profiles/<level>/law.toml` | `POL.values_standing` removed |

**Design**:
- **Procedure** (the constitution's, e.g. the largest party formateur, the next if it fails): one round a business day
  at 5c through K-80's protocol, answers by the next round's deadline; ties by lot (`POL.coalition_lot`).
- **`POL.form_coalition`**: options — sets of parties with a majority of seats and, for each, a coalition platform
  between their platforms (the seat-weighted positions and the formateur's own); consequences *principle* — the
  distance from its own platform; *standing* — office held (a formateur bargaining form, Baron and Ferejohn, 1989,
  listed).
- **`POL.accept_coalition`**: options accept or decline; *principle* — the proposal's distance from its platform
  against its expected distance at the next formateur's round; *standing* — ministries offered. Options beyond the
  party's ideology limit are not generated.
- **Government**: the formateur's leader heads the government (parliamentary form), or the elected president
  (presidential); ministers are persons the coalition names among its members (appointments; the choosing is S5.144's
  process). The mandate's values are written through S5.135's writer, announced now, effective on the constitution's
  date.
- Retires `POL.values_standing` (placeholder:POL), the last placeholder standing in POL.3, which completes here: the
  parliament's values now change only by a mandate or a passed bill.
- **Streams**: `POL.coalition_lot`.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a parliament where no majority forms keeps the standing mandate (`no_majority_standing_mandate`).
- E14: two proposals to one party the same round: it answers each by its options (`two_proposals_answered`).
- E6: a save between rounds keeps the open protocol's messages (K-45 saved) (`open_rounds_saved`).

**Extension points**: the mandate is read by S5.153 (the budget's platform) and S5.154.

**Unit tests**: `formateur_options_majority_only`, `accept_rule_against_next_round`, `no_majority_standing_mandate`,
`mandate_written_with_announcement`, `two_proposals_answered`, `open_rounds_saved`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-34` (from S5.143): POL.6, POL.7 — every mandate traces to a coalition accepted by a majority of
seats (or the standing one after the procedure's rounds); the head of government and the ministers are persons named by
it; its values' announcements preceded their effective date.

**Budget**: an expected 20 decisions a round, 3 rounds an election, ≈ 20 µs each.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (a round's day, ≈ 0.4 core-ms).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (the protocol's K-45 messages).
- Counters: `sys_pol.coalition_rounds`, `sys_pol.mandates`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a coalition by a rule on sizes; a mandate not written through the one writer.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision points, generators and tests written; the placeholder removed; fast checks pass; `LC-5-34` registered
  (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

**Status**: planned

offices unfilled), S3.119 (the debt office unfilled)
**Goal**: every public office is held by a named person under a contract that pays it: members of parliament and a
directly elected head by election, the head of government and ministers by the coalition, and the heads of agencies,
the central bank's governor and board, the supervisors' heads and the treasury's debt office by whom the law names.
The appointer chooses among the eligible persons by its own mind from their records; an office falls vacant by death,
resignation, removal or the end of its term and is filled again the same way. Offices of the state no longer wait at
founding preferences.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/lib.rs` | each public office's appointer and term as the law's data (POLICY): which office appoints it, eligibility (records a candidate must hold), term; the appointment families; the vacancy's wake (K-34 holder index on a death, K-42 at a term's end) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/appoint.rs` | the appointer's option generator (S8.124's form over the public office's data) |

**Design**:
- **Filling**: the appointer — a minister for an agency's head and the debt office, the government for the governor
  and the supervisors' heads (or as the law names) — posts the office (a vacancy with its eligibility on K-72, seen by
  persons whose goals include reaching such an office, MND.5) and adds the eligible persons it knows (its own
  contracts: colleagues, kin, fellow members); options are the applicants; consequences from their records (jobs and
  offices held, skills), public reputation, acquaintance, and the pay and terms against others' bids — its mind
  chooses (PTY.17, MND.7). The chosen accepts or declines by its own decision; accepted, an appointment row pays it
  and K-34 names it holder.
- **Vacancies**: a holder's death (K-34's holder index, at its ending), resignation (the holder's own decision on its
  reviews), removal (the appointer's decision), or the term's end (a due) opens a new filling; while it runs the
  office decides at founding preferences (MND.16) and the filling is an open record (PTY.18's only allowance).
- **Retires** the placeholders of S2.192 (`SUP.heads_unfilled`), S3.111 and S3.119: those offices are filled from
  this step. They were the
  last standing in PTY.16, PTY.17 and MND.9 (an office's decisions taken by its holder's own mind), which complete
  here; S8.201 carries MND.9 (part).
- **Streams**: none (ties in the appointer's choice go through the decision core's tastes).

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe killing several holders: each office's filling opens at the ending; they run independently
  (`vacancy_on_death_opens_filling`).
- E10: an appointer's own office empty: the filling waits in the appointer's founding preferences' decision, never a
  stand-in (PTY.18) (`empty_appointer_decides_at_founding_view`).
- E3: no applicant and no acquaintance eligible: the filling stays open, reported with its age (`LC-5-35`).

**Extension points**: municipalities' mayors and councils (S5.156) use the same appointment families.

**Unit tests**: `appointer_options_from_applicants_and_acquaintances`, `vacancy_on_death_opens_filling`,
`term_end_opens_filling`, `empty_only_while_filling`, `empty_appointer_decides_at_founding_view`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-35` (from S5.144): PTY.16, PTY.18 — every public office is held by a person under a paying
contract or has an open filling, with the filling's age; no decision in an office was taken by a stand-in.

**Budget**: ≈ 2 k public offices; fillings come at terms' ends, deaths and elections. Every eligible candidate is an
option (PTY.17: the applicants and the persons the appointer knows), each read from its person columns, mind, current
contract rows and its life record (K-40).
- **The formation's schedule** (the constitution's, POL.7): coalition rounds from the business day after the result
  (S5.143); once a coalition is accepted the ministries are filled over the interval to the new mandate's declared
  effective date (`POL.government_days`), each office's filling on its own day.
- **The records** are read before the result: the eligible set of each office is fixed by the law before the election
  (for ministries, the union over outcomes — every standing party's list candidates and its members whose goals
  include office), so from the campaign's first business day S1.223's `prefetch` reads them in daily slices (an
  expected 600 records over the campaign's 20 business days, 30 a day), decoded (1.5 KB each) and held in S1.223's
  prefetch buffer until the offices are filled; a person becoming eligible later is added on its day, and a record
  appended after its prefetch is refreshed in the buffer on the append.
- on fin.calendar.campaign_day (as S5.140's): 2 core-ms (the day's prefetch slice); joins H and B′.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.1 / 0 / 0.1 core-ms (B / NB / H) (fillings outside elections).
- ledger line 21 (day buffers): +1 MB resident (600 decoded records × 1.5 KB in S1.223's prefetch buffer, during a
  formation).
- ledger line 9 (contracts): +0.05 MB resident (2 k appointment rows × 25 B).
- Counters: `sys_pol.appointments`, `sys_pol.open_fillings`.

**Guards**: none new (S8.201's guard: no decision without its mind).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an appointment drawn; an office held by no one outside its filling; a career stated.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, the generator's registration and tests written; the three placeholders retired; fast checks pass;
  `LC-5-35` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.145 — The treasury's answer to a failed auction, the finance minister's options

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: TRS.3 DECISION; MND.7 DECISION *(part: the treasury's shortfall point converted to options)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-100, K-102)
**Depends on**: S3.122 (the answer to a failed auction: its arithmetic and the deferral placeholder), S3.123 (the
payment order), S5.144 (the finance minister's office filled), S5.127 (appropriation releases), S1.348 (K-100), S8.103
(minds), S8.122 (the mandate through the holder's contracts)
**Goal**: when an auction falls short, the treasury's answer is taken in the finance minister's office as options with
consequences, weighed by the minister's own mind: paying from the buffer, cutting or deferring outlays, returning at
another size or maturity, or central-bank financing where the country's financing regime allows it (TRS.3). The fixed
protocol order and its deferral placeholder are retired.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/points.rs` | `TRS.answer_shortfall` as a decision kind (`taken_in` the finance minister; concerns means, security, standing, principle; mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/shortfall.rs` | the option generator over S3.122's arithmetic |
| `data/profiles/<level>/law.toml` | the protocol's order entry removed |

**Design**:
- **Options**: pay from the buffer down to its minimum; defer discretionary outlays (appropriation releases of the
  functions the payment order ranks after debt service, and discretionary purchases) by one release date; an extra
  auction at another size or maturity; direct lending by the central bank where the regime allows (S3.116).
- **Consequences**, from the minister's own outlooks: *means* — the interest cost of each way of covering the gap at
  its outlook of auction prices; *security* — the chance and size of the account falling short again over the
  interval at its outlook's width; *standing* — the market's reading of a second auction or of central-bank financing
  (its outlook of the next auctions' cover); *principle* — the agencies' service lost by a deferral (their published
  waits, S5.128). The minister's mind chooses.
- Retires S3.122's placeholder (discretionary purchases deferred, naming SOC); TRS.3 completes here, S3.122 carrying
  its arithmetic.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a regime of "never" offers no central-bank option; a treasury with no discretionary outlay offers no deferral
  (`shortfall_options_by_regime`).
- E2: an extra auction failing again reruns the decision the next business day (`second_failure_reruns_next_day`).
- E14: a failed auction on a plan review day: the answer first, then the plan (the answer's wake precedes)
  (`answer_before_plan_same_day`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `shortfall_options_by_regime`, `shortfall_consequences_by_concern` (given a gap, a buffer and outlooks:
each option's cost, residual shortfall and service lost on its concern), `deferral_of_releases_by_order`,
`second_failure_reruns_next_day`, `answer_before_plan_same_day`.

**Live checks**: none new (LC-3-23 and LC-3-25 read the outcomes; LC-5-22 the releases).

**Budget**: failures are rare: an expected six decisions a year over the three treasuries, ≈ 10 µs each.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (a failed auction's day only, ≈ 0.01 core-ms).
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a fixed protocol order standing in for the minister's choice; a statutory payment cut outside the
declared priority; a preference weight in the generator.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision point, generator and tests written; the placeholder retired; fast checks pass.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

**Status**: planned

**Goal**: the treasury's forward funding plan — the buffer it keeps and the sizes and maturities of the auctions it
schedules — is taken in the finance minister's office as options with consequences, weighed by the minister's own
mind within the debt mandate.

### S5.147 — Making good a central bank's loss, the finance minister's options

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: the treasury's point on a central bank's loss converted to options)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-100, K-102)
**Depends on**: S3.126 (the treasury makes good a central bank's loss: the floor, the transfer's arithmetic), S5.144
(the finance minister's office filled), S5.146 (the plan whose review wakes it), S1.348 (K-100), S8.103 (minds)
**Goal**: when its central bank's published equity is below the floor its mandate names, whether and how far the
treasury restores it is the finance minister's choice among options, weighed by its mind, in place of S3.126's fixed
transfer of the whole gap.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/points.rs` | `TRS.make_good_cb_loss` as a decision kind (`taken_in` the finance minister; concerns means, security, principle; mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-trs/src/rules/cb_loss.rs` | the option generator over S3.126's arithmetic |

**Design**:
- CB.10 is complete at S3.126; this step makes its transfer the minister's choice (MND.7).
- **When**: the plan's review (S5.146) reading the central bank's latest published statement (K-37).
- **Options**: transfer the whole gap to the floor this period; transfer it over the plan's next periods in equal
  parts; defer to the next review. A floor declared absent offers none.
- **Consequences**: *means* — the outlay against the treasury's plan (the extra issuance each option needs at its
  outlook of auction prices); *security* — the central bank's equity below the floor while it waits (the chance its
  outlook gives of further losses); *principle* — the mandate's floor. The minister's mind chooses.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:

- E13: no floor declared: no options, the loss carried (`no_floor_no_options`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `cb_loss_options_consequences` (given a gap and outlooks: each option's outlay, time below the floor
and distance from the mandate on its concern), `no_statement_no_occasion`, `no_floor_no_options`.

**Live checks**: none new (S3.126's checks read the transfers).

**Budget**: an expected two occasions a year over the three treasuries, ≈ 10 µs each.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H).
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B.

**Status**: planned

**Goal**: after a default, the terms the treasury offers its holders are the finance minister's choice among options —

### S5.149 — Buybacks and switches, the finance minister's options

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: MND.7 DECISION *(part: the sovereign's operations point converted to options)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-100, K-102)
**Depends on**: S3.125 (buybacks and switches: the reverse call, the switch ratio, the monthly operations review),
S5.146 (the buffer target), S5.144 (the minister's office), S1.348 (K-100), S8.103 (minds)
**Goal**: the treasury's monthly curve operations — whether to buy back lines maturing soon, which, and whether to
offer holders a switch into a new line — are the finance minister's choice among options, weighed by its mind, in
place of S3.125's rule of buying back whenever cash exceeds the buffer.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sov/src/points.rs` | `SOV.operations` as a decision kind (`taken_in` the finance minister; concerns means, security, standing; mode best) |

- SOV.2 is complete at S3.125; this step makes its operations the minister's choice (MND.7).
- **Options**: no operation; a buyback of each line maturing within the declared smoothing horizon, sized by the cash
  above the buffer target in declared steps, its bid limited at the treasury's own value (S3.125); a switch offer from
  each such line into each open new line at the ratio of its own values.

  *security* — the redemptions left in the horizon (the rollover the plan must still fund); *standing* — the

  chooses.

- E6: an open switch offer is saved with its K-80 messages (`switch_offer_saved`).

### S5.150 — The primary-dealer review, the debt office's options

**Status**: planned

**Depends on**: S3.171 (primary dealers: the agreement and its criteria), S3.172 (the yearly review this converts), S5.144 (the debt office's
head filled), S5.129, S5.130, S5.145, S5.146, S5.147, S5.148, S5.149 (the other decision points converted after

**Goal**: the treasury's yearly primary-dealer review — which desks keep their agreement and which applicants are
admitted — is the debt office head's choice among options, weighed by its mind, in place of S3.171's cut at a declared
share. It is the last decision point left in rule form; with it every decision in the world is a choice among options
(MND.7), and PC-169 refuses a rule-form point everywhere.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |

### S5.151 — Parties adapt their platforms between elections

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.5 DECISION *(part: each party revises its platform toward positions it judges would have won it more
votes, from published results and polls, as far as its ideology preference allows)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points)
**Depends on**: S5.136 (platforms and ideology limits), S5.138 (polls), S5.142 (results), S1.348 (K-100), S8.103
(minds)
**Goal**: on its review days between elections each party's leader revises its platform from the published results
and the polls it can read, with their lags: toward the positions of parties that gained, by steps, never beyond the
party's ideology preference; a party that gained may keep its platform.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/polity.rs` | decision kind `POL.adapt_platform` (`taken_in` the party's leader; concerns standing, principle; mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/adapt.rs` | the option generator |

**Design**:
- **Options**: keep the platform; move each differing schedule a declared step toward the platform of the party that
  gained most since the last review (the predator move), or toward the platform of the party nearest the published
  undecided and abstainers' shares — each option within the ideology limit (a declared limit; options beyond are not
  generated). The adaptive rules of party competition (Laver, 2005; Laver and Sergenti, 2012), listed.
- **Consequences**: *standing* — the vote share the leader's outlook expects from published polls and results at each
  option; *principle* — the option's distance from the founding platform.
- **Writes**: the adopted platform (the party's columns) and its publication (K-37), read by each household at its next
  vote occasion during a campaign (S5.137).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: before the first result in the run, the opening's last election is the published result (GEN.5)
  (`first_review_reads_opening_result`).
- E13: a party alone in its country adapts toward nothing (keep is its one option) (`lone_party_keeps`).
- E14: a review and a new poll the same day: the review reads the poll only after its lag (`reads_polls_after_lag`).

**Extension points**: platforms are read by S5.139, S5.143, S5.152.

### S5.152 — Parties founded, split, merged and dissolved

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.5 DECISION
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.15 (follows: K-97 endings, K-96 estates), §7.5 (follows: K-31 a
party's beginning)
**Depends on**: S5.151 (adaptation), S5.141 (deposits and funding), S5.140 (vote occasions), S5.139 (a founder's best
platform), S1.194 (K-31), S1.343 (K-97), S1.342 (K-96), S1.348 (K-100)
**Goal**: a party that loses repeatedly can split, merge or disappear by its leader's own comparison of continuing
against each alternative; an adult far from every platform can found a party when standing is worth its cost to it. No
founding or dissolution is triggered by an aggregate threshold.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/polity.rs` | decision kinds `POL.continue_party` (`taken_in` the party's leader; concerns standing, principle, means) and `POL.found_party` (`taken_in = person`; concerns principle, standing, means, leisure_and_health) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/{continue_party,found}.rs` | the option generators |

**Design**:
- **`POL.continue_party`** (the party's review days): options continue; merge with the nearest party whose platform
  lies within both ideology limits; split (found a new party at the platform the predator move would reach beyond the
  limit, paying its deposit from the party's account); dissolve. Consequences: *standing* — expected seats from the
  polls it reads; *means* — funding per vote against staff costs and the next deposit; *principle* — distance from
  the founding platform (Laver and Sergenti, 2012, listed).
- **`POL.found_party`**: offered on a vote occasion (S5.140) to an adult whose goals include reaching parliament
  (MND.5); options found at its own best platform (S5.139's value) or not; consequences *principle*, *standing* — the
  votes it expects from published polls (the undecided and abstaining shares, the parties farthest from it) — and
  *means* — the deposit, founding hours and capital it subscribes (entry as the comparison of expected votes against
  the cost of standing, Cox, 1997, listed).
- **Writes**: a new party (K-31 begin, its account, its founder the leader); a merger's successor (K-97 moves the
  merged party's members, contracts and account to it); a dissolution into an estate (K-96).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E10: a dissolved party's funding due and deposit return go to its estate; its members' memberships end
  (`dissolution_moves_to_estate`).
- E13: a country whose last party dissolves has none until one is founded; its parliament keeps the standing mandate
  (`no_party_standing_mandate`).
- E1: several parties founded the same day are independent parties (`same_day_foundings_independent`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `continue_merge_split_dissolve_options`, `found_only_with_goal`, `split_pays_deposit`,
`dissolution_moves_to_estate`, `no_party_standing_mandate`, `same_day_foundings_independent`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-36` (from S5.152): every founding, split, merger and dissolution traces to its decision and its
consequences recorded; none to a threshold.

**Budget**: party reviews as S5.151's; founding options only for adults with the goal on their vote occasions (an
expected 1 % of occasions, 2 options, ≈ 0.7 µs).
- on fin.calendar.campaign_day (as S5.140's): 0.5 core-ms; joins H and B′.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.04 / 0 / 0.04 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the parties' reviews).
- ledger line 6 (institutions): +0 B (a founded party is an institution record among S5.136's).
- Counters: `sys_pol.parties_founded`, `sys_pol.parties_dissolved`, `sys_pol.parties_split`, `sys_pol.parties_merged`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a founding or dissolution by threshold; a split or founders drawn by chance.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision points, generators and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-36` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.153 — The annual budget, brought and voted

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: SOC.8 DECISION; POL.11 DECISION *(part: the governing coalition brings an annual budget on the fiscal
calendar — tax rates, benefit rules, appropriations, the borrowing plan — which the parliament passes or rejects by
vote)*
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.7 (follows: K-45 messages), §4.6 (follows: the one writer of a
policy value)
**Depends on**: S5.143 (the mandate and government), S5.132 (appropriation requests), S5.135 (the writer), S5.142
(seats), S1.237 (K-45), S1.172 (K-16 apportion), S1.348 (K-100), S1.423 (retires its placeholder
`SOC.appropriation`)
**Goal**: on the budget calendar the head of government brings the annual budget as a bill — the mandate platform's
tax schedules, benefit and service rules and border policies, each agency's appropriation from its request, the
borrowing plan's frame — and each party in parliament votes for or against it by its platform and its reading of its
voters; passed, its values are written with their effective day; rejected, the last budget stands. `SOC.appropriation`
is retired.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/legislation.rs` | message `Bill { kind: budget or emergency, values: [PolicyWrite], appropriations, effective }`; decision kinds `POL.bring_bill` (`taken_in` the head of government; concerns principle, standing) and `POL.vote_on_bill` (`taken_in` each party's leader; concerns principle, standing) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/{bill,vote_on_bill}.rs` | the option generators; appropriations by largest remainder |
| `data/profiles/<level>/law.toml` | `SOC.appropriation` removed |

**Design**:
- **`POL.bring_bill`**: options — the bill at the mandate platform's values, and variants moving some values toward
  the standing law (to gain votes); each carries the appropriations: the platform's spending per function apportioned
  over the function's agencies in proportion to their requests (K-16's apportion, residue to the named largest);
  consequences *principle* (distance from the head's party platform), *standing* (the passage its outlook expects from
  the parties' platforms and seats). An agency abolished by the bill names its successor (S5.127).
- **`POL.vote_on_bill`**: each party for or against: *principle* — whether the bill's values are nearer its platform
  than the standing policy (spatial voting on a bill against the status quo, Enelow and Hinich, 1984, listed);
  *standing* — its reading of its voters (its poll share's change since the election). Its members vote with it;
  passage by the constitution's majority of seats.
- **Writes**: a passed bill's values and appropriations through the writer (S5.135) with the bill's effective day; a
  rejected budget leaves the last one.
- Retires `SOC.appropriation` (placeholder:POL), the last placeholder standing in SOC.8, which completes here.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a budget's effective day re-resolves the changed handles' in-force values (K-20's per-day cache) and nothing
  else: no pass over parties (`effective_day_touches_handles_only`).
- E2: a parliament where no bill passes keeps the last budget (`rejected_budget_leaves_last`).
- E13: a function with no agency receives no appropriation (`function_without_agency_none`).

**Extension points**: emergency bills (S5.154) use the same message and votes.

**Unit tests**: `appropriation_scaled_by_largest_remainder`, `bill_vote_against_status_quo`,
`rejected_budget_leaves_last`, `effective_day_touches_handles_only`, `function_without_agency_none`,
`bring_bill_options_consequences` (given platforms and seats: each variant's distance and expected passage on its
concern).

**Live checks**: `LC-5-37` (from S5.153): POL.11 — every budget was brought on its calendar and voted; every rejected
budget left the last one; every appropriation traces to a passed budget or the standing one.

**Budget**: yearly: the bill's decisions (an expected 12 a country) on the budget calendar's day; the effective day
re-resolves K-20's cache; readers see the new values on their own occasions.
- on fin.calendar.budget_effective (the budget calendar's effective day, `POL.budget_calendar`, often 1 January or the
  first business day after it): 1 core-ms; joins B′.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B (the bill is a K-45 message).
- Counters: `sys_pol.bills`, `sys_pol.bills_passed`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a policy path; a budget written without a vote; appropriations set outside a passed bill.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Message, decision points, generators and tests written; the placeholder removed; fast checks pass; `LC-5-37`
  registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`, a budget's effective day measured; the two reviews
  done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S5.154 — Emergency measures between budgets

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.11 DECISION
**Architecture**: §4.7 (follows: decision points), §7.16 (follows: K-101: surprises and public events waking a
decision), §4.10 (follows: public events)
**Depends on**: S5.153 (bills and their votes), S1.350 (K-101), S1.213 (K-36 public events), S1.336 (K-92: the head's
outlooks), S1.348 (K-100)
**Goal**: between budgets the head of government brings emergency measures when its own outlook or a public event calls
for them — a supplementary appropriation to the responding function, or a change of a parliament-owned value — within
the mandate's platform position on emergency spending, voted like any bill.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/points.rs` | `POL.bring_bill`'s wakes: a surprise in the head's own outlooks of the published series its office reads (K-101's stake raised beyond its attention's draw), a public event of a declared kind (a catastrophe, a bank's or a peg's failure) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/bill.rs` | the emergency options (below) |

**Design**:
- **Options** on a wake: no measure; a supplementary appropriation to the function the event concerns (health,
  infrastructure, benefits administration) at the mandate platform's emergency position for it, or at declared steps
  below it; a change of a parliament-owned value the mandate platform holds (a benefit rule). Consequences as the
  budget's (*principle*, *standing*), and *security* — the outlook's shortfall the measure answers.
- A measure is a `Bill` of kind emergency, voted by S5.153's `POL.vote_on_bill`, written with its effective day.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E1: a catastrophe striking a region: one wake of the head, not one per party affected (`one_wake_per_event`).
- E14: two events the same day: one decision over both (K-43 dedupe) (`two_events_one_decision`).
- E2: a rejected emergency measure changes nothing (`rejected_measure_no_write`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `emergency_options_within_platform_position`, `event_kinds_wake_as_declared`, `one_wake_per_event`,
`two_events_one_decision`, `rejected_measure_no_write`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-38` (from S5.154; applicable once a measure is brought): every emergency measure names its
trigger (a surprise or a public event) and its vote.

**Budget**: an event's day only: one decision of the head (≈ 20 µs) and the parties' votes.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (an event's day, ≈ 0.2 core-ms).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 B.
- Counters: `sys_pol.emergency_bills`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a measure triggered by an aggregate threshold outside the head's own outlook; a measure written
without a vote.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Wakes, options and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-38` registered (read at the gate).

### S5.155 — Settlements incorporate as municipalities, merge or dissolve

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.14 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §7.5 (follows: K-31 a party's beginning and ending), §7.6 (follows: K-39 accumulators), §7.15
(follows: K-97 successors)
**Depends on**: S2.176 (settlements recognised by the statistics agency), S5.137 (counted intentions: the same
counting for a local vote), S5.134 (the municipal law's incorporation rule), S1.194 (K-31), S1.343 (K-97), S1.165
(K-06: the parties-by-(zone, kind) instance), S1.348 (K-100)
**Goal**: a settlement the statistics agency recognises incorporates as a municipality where its country's law provides
and its adult residents' vote carries — a dated event with its cause; a municipality whose settlement is no longer
recognised merges into its neighbour or dissolves by the same law. No number of municipalities is declared.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-state/src/polity.rs` | decision kind `POL.vote_incorporation` (`taken_in = person`; concerns means, place, principle; mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/lib.rs` | the municipal law's incorporation rule (POLICY: whether a recognised settlement may incorporate, the vote's majority and window); the local vote's counts on K-39 keyed (settlement, choice); the incorporation and dissolution events |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/incorporate.rs` | the option generator and the count's outcome |

**Design**:
- **Trigger**: a settlement's recognition (S2.176's record) opens a local vote window where the law provides; the
  settlement's households (the one parties-by-(zone, kind) instance, S1.165, read for its zones) have a need occasion
  within it, each on a day drawn over the window by its phase.
- **The vote**: each adult's options yes, no, abstain; consequences *means* — the local taxes the municipal law
  allows at their declared starting values on its own position, *place* — the local services the law assigns
  municipalities in its zones, *principle*. Counts move at each choice; at the window's close the count carries or not
  by the law's majority.
- **Incorporation**: a municipality begins (K-31) with its territory (the settlement's zones), its account at the
  central bank and its offices empty until its first local election (S5.156). **Dissolution**: when the settlement is
  no longer recognised, the law's rule merges it into the neighbouring municipality (K-97 successor) or dissolves it
  into an estate, its functions returning to the national agencies.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a country whose law provides no incorporation has none (`law_without_incorporation`).
- E10: a household moving out during the window leaves the settlement's count (`mover_leaves_local_count`).
- E1: several settlements recognised the same year run independent windows (`independent_windows`).

**Extension points**: municipalities are the parties S5.156 activates.

**Unit tests**: `incorporation_by_majority`, `law_without_incorporation`, `merge_names_successor`,
`mover_leaves_local_count`, `independent_windows`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-39` (from S5.155; applicable once a settlement is recognised): every municipality traces to a
recognised settlement and a carried vote; every dissolution to a recognition lost and the law's rule.

**Budget**: a settlement's window: its households' occasions spread over the window (an expected 5 k households a
recognised settlement, ≈ 1 µs each).
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0 / 0 / 0 core-ms (B / NB / H) (a window's days, ≈ 0.3 core-ms each).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB (reuses the parties-by-(zone, kind) instance, S1.165).
- Counters: `sys_pol.incorporations`, `sys_pol.municipal_dissolutions`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a municipality created by a size threshold; a number of municipalities declared.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations, rules and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-39` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.156 — Municipalities: their offices, elected

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.13 STATE *(part: a municipality is a public party of its settlement with offices held by persons — a
mayor and a council — elected by its adult residents)*
**Architecture**: §7.3 (follows: K-21 legal forms), §7.5 (follows: K-32 windowed groups), §4.6 (follows: policy values
and their owners)
**Depends on**: S5.155 (municipalities), S5.134 (the municipal law's entries), S5.137 (campaign windows and counts),
S5.140 (the vote), S5.142 (the tally and allotment), S5.144 (appointments)
**Goal**: a municipality has a mayor and a council, elected by its adult residents on the municipal law's calendar,
with the national election's machinery run over its territory: a local campaign's window, the residents' scheduled
occasions, the tally, the allotment and the appointments.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/lib.rs` | the municipality legal form (offices mayor and council; electoral unit its territory; declared a public owner and a provider of local schools and clinics for S5.131's and S5.128's registrations, which read the legal form's data); the declarations of the municipal law's entries (council seats, term, whether the mayor is elected directly); the local election calendar on K-42 |

**Design**:
- **Elections**: on the municipal law's calendar a local campaign opens S5.137's window over the municipality's
  residents, its counts keyed by the municipality; the residents' occasions follow S5.137's schedule (the same P) and
  S5.140's vote over the local parties' and candidates' platforms (a local platform holds the municipality's own

### S5.157 — Municipalities: local taxes and zoning by the council's bill

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POL.13 STATE
**Architecture**: §4.3 (follows: levies), §4.6 (follows: policy values and their owners), §7.8 (follows: K-51)
**Depends on**: S5.156 (municipal offices), S5.134 (the municipal law's tax and zoning powers), S5.113 (holding
levies), S5.153 (bills and their votes), S2.155, S2.170 (zoning as policy values)
**Goal**: a municipality levies the local taxes its country's law allows and zones its land within the national law,
both written by its council's passed local budget; its services and capital run through the registrations its legal
form declares (S5.156). Every one of these is a mechanism already built, activated for the municipality by
declaration.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/lib.rs` | the local levy declarations (a holding levy on its zones' taxed classes over the owners' (zone, class) instance; a surcharge on residents' income-tax assessment where the law allows) with the municipality as payee; the municipality as the owner of its zones' zoning values |
| `crates/systems/sys-pol/src/rules/local_budget.rs` | the council's local budget bill: local tax rates, zoning changes and local appropriations (S5.153's options and votes with the council as the voting body) |

**Design**:
- **Local taxes**: declared levies with the municipality as payee — a holding levy on the zones' taxed classes at the
  national assessor's values (S5.113's machinery), and a surcharge on residents' income tax where the law allows (a
  levy on the return's assessment) — rates written by the council's passed local budget.
- **Zoning**: the zoning values of its zones (S2.155, S2.170) are owned by the municipality within the national law's
  bounds (the national law's limit is a declared limit of the law); the council's bills write them.
- **Local budget**: once a year on the municipal law's calendar, the mayor brings the bill and the council's parties
  vote by S5.153's decision kinds; passed, its values are written through S5.135's writer with the municipality as
  owner.
- POL.12's municipal primitives are S5.134's; POL.13 completes here.
- **Streams**: none new.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: a new municipality has no revenue before its first levy date; it spends nothing it lacks
  (`new_municipality_no_revenue_before_levy`).
- E10: a merged municipality's successor takes its accounts, levies and zoning (K-97) (`merged_levies_to_successor`).
- E13: a country whose law gives municipalities no tax power declares none (`no_tax_power_no_levy`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `local_levy_payee_municipality`, `zoning_within_national_limit`, `council_budget_vote`,
`new_municipality_no_revenue_before_levy`, `merged_levies_to_successor`, `no_tax_power_no_levy`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-68` (from S5.157; applicable once a municipality exists): every local tax traces to a passed
local budget and the law's allowance; every zoning change to the council's bill.

**Budget**: local levies on instalment days, inside S5.113's pass over the same holdings (one more levy of the set);
the council's bills once a year.
- on fin.calendar.property_instalment (as S5.113's): +3 core-ms (the local levy at ≈ 2 ns on the 1.6 M holdings);
  joins H (as S5.113's).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0 MB (reuses the owners' (zone, class) instance, S1.165).
- Counters: `sys_pol.local_levies`, `sys_pol.zoning_writes`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a kind branch for municipalities (their data differ, not code); zoning outside the national limit.

**Goal**: per election, the incumbents' share against the published unemployment and growth; platform distances

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; an estimator chosen after reading the run.

### S5.159 — Foreign currency held at banks of its system, and nostros

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FX.1 STATE
**Architecture**: §7.8 (follows: K-47 accounts per (holder, issuer, currency); K-49 per-currency nets and
correspondents)
**Depends on**: S1.240 (K-47), S1.250 (K-49: currency-system membership as data, a non-member's legs routed through
its nostro at a declared correspondent, a missing nostro failing visibly), S2.195 (depositors' bank choice and its
alternatives), S1.180 (K-21: account kinds)
**Goal**: every currency is issued by its central bank; a party holds a foreign currency only as an account at a bank
of that currency's system, or at its own bank in that currency backed by the bank's nostro at a correspondent in that
system — a real position of the bank. Foreign-currency deposit kinds are among a depositor's alternatives.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fx/src/lib.rs` | each bank's currency-system memberships (data, K-49's declaration); the nostro relation (bank → correspondent, currency) as a K-47 account of the bank at the correspondent; foreign-currency deposit kinds (currency; whether receipts are converted on arrival at the bank's quote — a term the depositor chooses) declared for S2.195's alternatives |

**Design**:
- **Holding**: an account row (K-47) names its issuer bank and currency; a bank not a member of that currency's system
  holds its customers' deposits in it against its nostro at a member correspondent, and every leg of such a deposit
  routes through the nostro (S1.250), so the customer's row and the nostro move in one settlement.
- **Receipts**: a payment arrives in the currency paid (MON.13); on a deposit kind whose term converts on receipt, the
  bank's conversion commitment (S5.162) converts it as a trade with the bank.
- **Choice**: foreign-currency deposit kinds join the alternatives of the depositor's `bank_choice` (S2.195) by
  declaration; the choice is that rule's.
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a currency with no member bank in a country: its residents hold it only at foreign banks in reach or through a
  correspondent; none there means none held (`no_route_no_holding`).
- E1: a correspondent's failure: the nostros at it are claims in its resolution (K-99), and the customer deposits they
  back are the domestic bank's liabilities still (`failed_correspondent_nostro_is_claim`).
- E3: a party with no account in a currency cannot receive in it: the payment fails visibly (MON.5)
  (`no_account_in_currency_fails`).

**Extension points**: conversions (S5.162), translation (S5.165), reserves (S5.169).

**Unit tests**: `nostro_moves_with_customer_row`, `receipt_arrives_in_paid_currency`, `no_route_no_holding`,
`failed_correspondent_nostro_is_claim`, `no_account_in_currency_fails`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-42` (from S5.159): FX.1, MON.13 — every foreign-currency balance is an account at a member
bank or backed by a nostro at one; no payment arrived in a currency other than the one paid.

**Budget**: their legs are ordinary flows, routed through the nostro in the same settlement (S1.250).
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +3 MB resident (0.15 M expected foreign-currency accounts and nostros × 20 B).
- Counters: `sys_fx.foreign_accounts`, `sys_fx.nostro_legs`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a foreign balance with no bank of its system behind it; a conversion at the ledger.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Declarations and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-42` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.160 — The opening's positions in foreign currencies and abroad

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §10.0a (follows: the opening dataset), §10.2 (follows: drawn and derived sides)
**Depends on**: S5.159 (foreign-currency accounts and nostros), S1.279 (K-64 instruments), S1.280 (K-65 holdings of
instruments), S1.276 (K-62 lots), S1.257 (K-53 loans)
**Goal**: the opening world holds the positions in other currencies and abroad a present-day economy of its level
holds — central banks' reserves, banks' nostros and foreign-currency deposits, foreign-currency loans and sovereign
debt, institutions' and households' foreign holdings with their lots — each drawn once with its other side derived,
balanced (GEN.4) and carried on day one at the snapshot's fixings (GEN.5). Holders stay holders; closure limits only
search until S5.175.

| `data/profiles/<level>/economy.toml` | the positions' shares and distributions (ENDOWMENT) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fx/src/opening.rs` | the opening's contribution: pure functions over the base the opening hands them |

- This is the opening's Stage 5 contribution; GEN's clauses complete at S7.102–S7.105.

  `markets/imf_iip` and their currency composition from `markets/imf_iipcc`; portfolio holdings by counterpart and
  currency from `markets/cpis_bilateral_2019`, `markets/cpis_currency`, `markets/cpis_holders`; reserves from

- **Drawn and derived**: each position drawn once on its holder, its issuer's or debtor's side derived; nostros backing

### S5.161 — Two-currency trades settle both legs together on a joint value date

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FX.7 INVARIANT
**Architecture**: §7.8 (follows: K-48 link groups, K-49 per-currency passes and joint value dates), §7.17 (follows:
K-103 audit families)
**Depends on**: S1.250 (K-49: linked legs across currencies with joint value dates), S1.245 (K-48 link groups), S1.353
(K-103), S1.180 (K-21: the pair market's settlement convention)
**Goal**: every currency trade is one instruction with two money legs in two currencies, each landing in its own
currency, settling at the same stage 7 on its value date — the declared number of days that are business days in both
countries — or neither; the audit checks that every trade has its two legs and that dealer and client positions sum to
zero per currency.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-fx/src/lib.rs` | the currency-trade reason (two legs, one link group, value-date convention per pair from the market's declaration); audit families `FX.two_legs`, `FX.positions_sum` (K-103 declarations, pure checks) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fx/src/audit.rs` | the families' checks over handed values |

**Design**:
- **Settlement**: a trade's legs form one K-48 link group settled all-or-none in K-49's per-currency passes on the
  value date; a leg whose currency has no stage 7 that day waits pending until a day that is a business day in both
  (S1.250).
- **`FX.two_legs`**: every settled currency trade has exactly two legs in two currencies with opposite parties.
- **`FX.positions_sum`**: per currency, the dealers' and clients' traded positions sum to zero at each close
  (recounted over the day's trades, K-103's change set).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: a leg pending over closed days settles at the first joint business day with the day's other flows
  (`leg_pending_until_joint_business_day`).
- E14: two trades of one payer in one currency the same day: order by the declared payment order, ties by lot (K-49)
  (`same_payer_trades_in_declared_order`).
- E3: a payer short in either currency fails the whole trade (`fx_trade_two_legs_both_or_neither`).

**Extension points**: every currency trade of S5.162–S5.171 uses this reason.

**Unit tests**: `fx_trade_two_legs_both_or_neither`, `value_date_joint_business_days`,
`leg_pending_until_joint_business_day`, `positions_sum_zero_per_currency`, `same_payer_trades_in_declared_order`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-43` (from S5.161): FX.7 — the two families clean every close.

**Budget**: an expected 0.15 M two-currency groups a business day, ≈ 30 phone-ns each (S1.250's), the families fused
in K-103's daily pass.
- adds 0.15 M / 0 / 0.15 M items to fin.settle.flow_ns (≈ 5 / 0 / 5 core-ms).
- its share of fin.fixed.recount: 0.3 / 0 / 0.3 core-ms (B / NB / H) (the two families over the day's trades).
- ledger line 8 (accounts and side rows): +0 B (pending legs are S1.250's).
- Counters: `sys_fx.trades`, `sys_fx.pending_legs`.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; one leg settled without the other; a netting across currencies.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Reason, families and tests written; fast checks pass; `LC-5-43` registered (read at the
  gate); the families light under `phx inject`.
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.

### S5.162 — Banks' conversion quotes and the commitments behind them

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: FX.4 PROCESS *(part: banks convert their customers' payments as counterparties, from their own currency
books)*
**Architecture**: §7.8 (follows: K-50 dated commitments), §7.11 (follows: K-70 posted quotes), §4.7 (follows: decision
points)
**Depends on**: S5.159 (accounts and nostros), S5.161 (two-leg trades), S3.165 (the dealer quote form, declared per
instrument class with its risk unit), S1.251 (K-50), S1.296 (K-70 posted offers), S1.348 (K-100), S8.124 (a bank's line
heads)
**Goal**: each bank posts, per pair it serves, a conversion quote for its customers from its own currency book — its
nostros, reserves and customers' foreign-currency deposits — and stands behind it with a conversion commitment: a
customer paying in a currency it does not hold draws the commitment in the same instruction, the bank the counterparty
of both legs. Money never changes currency at the ledger.

**Files**:
| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/interfaces/if-open/src/currency.rs` | pairs; decision kind `FX.conversion_quote` (`taken_in` the bank's line head for currencies; concerns means, security; mode best) |
| `crates/systems/sys-fx/src/rules/conversion_quote.rs` | the option generator over S3.165's form with the bank's currency book as inventory |
| `crates/systems/sys-fx/src/lib.rs` | the conversion commitment kind (K-50) and its draw at stage 7a; the bank's declared cost per conversion (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc73.rs` | PC-73 |

**Design**:
- **Quote** (stage 5c, the bank's review days and wakes on a fixing surprise): options are quote pairs around its own
  outlook of the rate (S3.165's form: its inventory per currency, its outlook's width, its declared cost per
  conversion); consequences *means* — expected margin on its outlook of customers' flows; *security* — its currency
  book's open position at the outlook's width. The chosen quote is posted (K-70) with its commitment.
- **Draw** (stage 7a): a payment in a currency the payer does not hold is two legs — payer → bank in the payer's
  currency at the quote, bank → payee in the paid currency — one link group (S5.161); the bank's book moves; it squares
  in the interdealer call (S5.163).
- **Streams**: none.

**Edge cases**:
- E2: a bank quoting nothing in a pair (a bound limit): its customers' payments in that currency fail visibly
  (`no_quote_payment_fails`).
- E1: a bank's failure: its commitments lapse at its ending; the customers' payments fail until their deposits move
  (`failed_bank_commitments_lapse`).
- E14: several customer conversions of one bank the same day net in its book; each is its own two-leg group
  (`conversions_own_groups_net_in_book`).

**Extension points**: invoices and payments across borders (S5.176, S5.179) draw commitments.

**Unit tests**: `conversion_commitment_bank_is_counterparty`, `conversion_needs_a_counterparty` (compile-fail: no
`Money` of one currency built from another's but by a trade's leg builder), `quote_options_from_book`,
`no_quote_payment_fails`, `failed_bank_commitments_lapse`, `conversions_own_groups_net_in_book`.

**Live checks**: `LC-5-44` (from S5.162): FX.9, MON.13 — every conversion names its counterparty (a bank from its own
book, or a dealer); no leg landed in a currency other than its own.

**Budget**: ≈ 35 banks × 3 pairs, an expected 30 quote decisions a business day at ≈ 2 µs; conversions drawn are
S5.161's groups.
- its share of fin.fixed.institutions: 0.06 / 0 / 0.06 core-ms (B / NB / H).
- ledger line 17 (markets): +0.01 MB resident (105 posted quotes with commitments × 64 B).
- Counters: `sys_fx.conversions`, `sys_fx.conversion_commitments`.

**Guards**: PC-73 — `Money` in one currency is built from another currency's only by `phx-ledger`'s trade leg builder,
drawn on a match or a bank's conversion commitment; a fixing converts only into a reported figure, a labelled
translation or a labelled tax base; no decision view carries a reported figure (compile level).

**Not allowed**: a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an
allocation per day; a conversion without a counterparty; a quote from a formula over rates (FX.9).

**Done when**:
- [ ] Decision point, generator, commitment and tests written; fast checks pass; PC-73 registered; `LC-5-44`
  registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] The bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`; the two reviews done; status `done` and the section
  removed.
