### S6.126 — The population's measures published; no demographic rate stated

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: POP.13 MEASURE; POP.14 FORBID
**Architecture**: §7.6 phx-record, accumulators (follows); §14.8 the realism reads (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.221 (accumulators kept at events); S1.476 (vital statistics: the period life table, published on
the agency's calendar); S6.120, S6.121, S6.123, S6.124 (formations, leavings, separations as events); S1.402 (births
and deaths); S2.148, S5.182 (moves between regions and countries); S6.100 (POP.13's reads and the job-loss window).
**Goal**: age structure, fertility by age, the dependency ratio, household size, regional population and net migration
are published by each agency from counts kept at the events that change them, and their co-movement with incomes,
housing costs and employment is read over the run; no birth, migration, participation, formation, separation or
enrolment rate exists anywhere as a primitive or is read by a mechanism.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sta/src/vital.rs` | the series' declarations and their period close as a pure read of the accumulators |
| `crates/systems/sys-sta/src/lib.rs` | accumulators `STA.births_by_mother_age`, `STA.households_by_size`, `STA.persons_by_age_class` (country, region), `STA.moves` (origin region or country, destination) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/pop.rs` | `LC-6-14`, `LC-6-15` |

**Design**:
- Counts move at their events only: a birth by the mother's age class; a death, an age-class crossing on its date, a
  move; a household's size at each formation, leaving, separation, birth and death (one decrement and one increment).
  At the agency's period close the series are records published after its lag (STA.2); the dependency ratio and
  net migration are reads of those counts.
- The co-movements (births with house prices by tenure, with unemployment; moves with earnings gaps and housing costs)
  are observer reads over the run's published series, N3's fact 28 among them by its registered definition, as
  `READS.toml` holds them (S6.100) — reads, never enforced.
- **POP.14**: `LC-6-14` reads the register and the read-trace: no primitive whose id or unit is a birth, migration,
  participation, formation, separation or enrolment rate exists, and none is read by any mechanism; every birth,
  move, formation, separation and enrolment names its decision or hazard event.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a region with no births in a period publishes a count of zero births (a count), and a fertility rate over no
  women of the class is `Missing` (`fertility_missing_without_women`).
- E11: the first release follows the first period close; before it, the opening's latest values stand (GEN.5)
  (`first_release_after_first_close`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `household_size_moves_at_events`; `dependency_ratio_from_counts`; `fertility_missing_without_women`;
`first_release_after_first_close`.

**Live checks**:

### S6.127 — Schooling at the opening: education records, pupils and courses

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: data
**Clauses**: GEN.2 STATE *(part: education by age, region and occupation family as the law's stages record it,
and enrolments)*
**Architecture**: §10.2 drawn and derived sides (follows); §10.3 canonical drawing (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.404 (persons drawn with education and skills by occupation family, the draw this step's columns join
by declaration); S6.114 (the education law's stages and fields); S6.117 (the schooling family); S6.119 (the course
process kind); S5.128 (public schools' capacity and private schools at the opening).
**Goal**: every person opens with an education record in the law's stages and fields, every pupil with a schooling
row at a public or private school for its stage, and every adult on a course with its process, drawn once from
declared distributions with sources, so the first school-year date and the first retraining find the state they read.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-dem/src/opening.rs` | the contribution's added columns (education record) and rows (schooling, courses): pure functions over what the opening hands them |
| `tools/data/dem_opening.py` | attainment and enrolments mapped to the law's stages and fields |
| `data/profiles/<level>/people.toml` | attainment by age class, sex and region; enrolment by stage and public share (ENDOWMENT) |
| `data/inventory.toml` | rows per derived value |

**Design**:
- **Education records**: each adult's highest stage and field drawn from attainment by five-year age group and sex
  (`wcde/attainment`), the field from the occupation family S1.404 drew (the most schooled filling the most skilled
  work, GEN.2), mapped to the law's stages (S6.114).
- **Pupils**: each child in the law's compulsory ages holds a schooling row for the stage its birth date gives; beyond
  them, enrolment by stage from gross enrolment ratios (`wdi/SE.PRE.ENRR`, `SE.PRM.ENRR`, `SE.SEC.ENRR`,
  `SE.TER.ENRR`), public or private by the level's public share, at schools in reach with places (S5.128's capacities
  from pupil–teacher ratios); start days by the steady-path convention (the stage began on its school-year date),
  each row's own days `carried` the school days since then at the law's days a year, and `mark` zero on the group's
  count, which opens at zero.
- **Courses**: adults on a course at the snapshot, from the tertiary enrolment of adults above the typical age, each a
  process with its completion day.
- Drawn on the opening's streams by (party, purpose) (GEN.3); nothing balanced (a place is a contract whose fees
  follow the steady-path convention). The rows and processes are those S6.117 and S6.119 count in their ledger lines.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a level with no enrolment ratio for a stage refuses the assembly (no default enrolment)
  (`enrolment_ratio_refused_when_missing`).
- E13: a region with no private school: every pupil there holds a public row, or waits in the agency's queue
  (`no_private_school_public_rows`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `attainment_to_stages_arithmetic`; `pupils_by_birth_date_and_law`;
`enrolment_ratio_refused_when_missing`; `no_private_school_public_rows`.

**Live checks**: none new (`LC-6-09` at S6.118 covers the opening's rows at the first school-year date).

**Budget**:
- opening only, not in the turn: 1.6 M schooling rows × 60 ns and 7.5 M education words written ≈ 110 core-ms of the
  opening.
- ledger: `+0 B` beyond S6.117's and S6.119's lines (their counts include the opening's).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a person's schooling or skill drawn apart from the law's stages; a past series of enrolments.

### S6.128 — Holdings over the whole balance sheet

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: HH.7 DECISION
**Architecture**: §7.13 phx-val, public series and methods (follows); §7.14 phx-risk, declared limits (follows).
**Depends on**: S3.158 (`HH.choose_holdings`, its classes declared data); S3.187 (fund kinds among the classes);
S8.111 (the holdings decision as an option generator weighed by the household's mind); S4.146 (`accrued_schedule`,
a pure read of a member's DB right); S4.148, S4.150 (DC pots as fund-unit holdings; members' extra contributions);
S2.146 (dwellings chosen by where to live); S2.161 (the house-price series by zone and class); S1.245 (link groups
settling all or none); S1.476 (the period life table the survival outlook reads); S1.338 (declared limits whose
binding is an event); S1.336 (public series and their methods; K-92's series pairs).
**Goal**: households hold their savings across every class the world offers — deposits, banknotes, bills, funds,
shares and bonds, foreign classes, dwellings and pensions — by yield, risk, liquidity and what they trust, over their
whole balance sheet: dwelling equity, pension rights and the income they expect to earn enter the consequences of
every rebalancing, so the risky share moves over the life cycle as an outcome of the adults' minds.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/decl.rs` | banknotes added to `HH.holding_classes` as a tradable class whose order is a withdrawal or deposit at the member's bank (reason `HH.cash_withdrawal`, a link group of two legs); dwellings and pensions added as background classes (held, never traded by this decision); each class's liquidity cost; the public series pairs whose betas the methods form (each tradable class on the house-price series and on the income series) |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/rules/portfolio.rs` | the background values and exposures added to each rebalancing's consequences |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/limits.rs` | `HH.no_short` and `HH.tradable_within_wealth` as declared limits that remove options, with their binding events |
| `data/shared/SHAPES.toml` | the whole-balance-sheet consequences (Bodie, Merton and Samuelson, 1992; Cocco, Gomes and Maenhout, 2005; Flavin and Yamashita, 2002) with its standing assumption |
| `data/shared/HH.toml` | liquidity cost hours per class (TECHNOLOGY) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/hh.rs` | `LC-6-16` |

**Design**:
- **Background wealth**, each by the household's own model of value (VAL.8): dwelling equity — its outlook of its
  (zone, class)'s house-price series less the mortgage's balance; DB rights — its outlook of `accrued_schedule`'s
  payments discounted at its own required return and its survival outlook (the published life table); DC pots at the
  fund's published value (holdings); human wealth — its income outlook's present value to retirement at its patience,
  carried as a bond-like holding. The factors these need — each (zone, class)'s house-price outlook per method, the
  annuity factors by age, type and the published life table, the betas — are formed once per print or release per
  method or type (K-92) and read by each review, so a review adds a few reads, never a schedule's walk. A component
  it cannot form from its own outlooks is formed by VAL.10 from the closest published series; one that cannot be
  formed leaves the review undecided and its holdings as they are, recorded — never read as zero.
- **Consequences only**: S8.111's rebalancings are the options; this step adds background wealth to what each one's
  consequences read. **Means**: the mix's expected return over the horizon less each class's liquidity cost and
  switching costs. **Security**: the width of the household's total wealth after the move — the tradable classes'
  widths plus each background value's exposure through the class's betas on its series (the method's betas, formed
  once per (series pair, method) from the public series, never per household, VAL.23). **Wealth and legacy**: what
  is held for heirs. The adults' minds weigh them (MND.8); no rule computes a target or reads a preference. Standing
  assumption, named in `SHAPES.toml`: a household's simple model sees each class's width and these two betas and no
  other covariance.
- **Real limits** (Law 6): a rebalancing that would hold a class short (a household has no securities loan) or put
  tradable holdings above tradable wealth (it borrows only through HH.10) is not generated; each removal is the
  limit's binding event, which the household sees.
- **Banknotes** (MON.4): a class with no yield, its width from the household's inflation outlook, and no liquidity
  cost at a till; its order is a withdrawal or deposit at the member's bank — the member's deposit and the bank's
  banknotes (its account at the issuer) move in one linked instruction of two legs (K-48, SET.4), so the bank's
  liability falls as the person's banknotes rise, and a bank short of banknotes fails the withdrawal visibly (MON.5).
- **Background classes** are held as they are: dwellings are bought and sold only by where to live (S2.146), pension
  contributions only by the pension decisions (S4.150).

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a missing background value leaves the review undecided (`missing_background_leaves_review_undecided`).
- E3: a household with no tradable wealth beyond its buffer: no rebalancing generated; limits unbound
  (`no_tradable_wealth_keep_only`).
- E13: a country with no listed class of a kind: that class has no option (`absent_class_no_option`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**:
- `banknote_withdrawal_two_legs_linked`; `db_rights_valued_from_schedule`; `liquidity_cost_lowers_means`.
- `background_exposure_widens_security`: a class whose beta on the house-price series is high widens total wealth
  more for a homeowner.
- `human_wealth_narrows_total_width`: given widths, a larger bond-like human wealth narrows total wealth's width per
  unit of risky class.
- `limits_remove_short_and_over_wealth_options`: no option shorts a class or exceeds tradable wealth; each removal
  recorded.
- `missing_background_leaves_review_undecided`; `no_tradable_wealth_keep_only`; `absent_class_no_option`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-6-16`: HH.7 — LC-3-49 extended: every holding of every class traces to its members' decision or the opening;
  every limit's binding is an event; the risky share of financial wealth by age class and wealth decile is published;
  HH's Done when: when the gap between money funds' yields and deposit rates widens in the run, savers move from
  deposits to money funds, each move a decision traced to its fill (applicable when the run has such a widening).

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.household_reviews: 3.5 / 0 / 3.5 core-ms (B / NB / H) — S3.158's 35 k holdings reviews a
  business day (its attention rule's count at the design point) × 100 ns more (four background values from factors
  formed per print, two betas per option).
- its share of fin.fixed.outlooks: 0.2 / 0 / 0.2 core-ms (B / NB / H) — factors and betas formed on new prints and
  releases.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.3 MB resident (factors per (zone, class) and method, annuity factors by age
  and type, betas per series pair and method).
- household record: `+0 B (core attribute)` — background values are reads.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a target weight computed from a preference (risk aversion, patience) by a rule; a household as a residual holder
  (HH.19); a risky share declared or imposed;
- a background holding sold by this decision; a missing background value read as zero; a beta computed per household.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; the consequences in `SHAPES.toml`; `LC-6-16` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S6.129 — The propensity to consume by wealth and liquidity

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: HH.16 MEASURE
**Architecture**: §7.6 phx-record, accumulators and sample frames (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.448 (households' standing spending rate); S5.109 (the personal return: refunds as records naming
the person); S5.135 and S5.124 (benefit amounts changed on a budget's effective day by a dated schedule, and their
payment); S1.215 (records by subject); S1.179 (dated policy schedules); S1.221 (accumulators keyed by country and
bands; sample frames); S1.171 (a declared sweep of a frame by slot range); S2.114, S2.168 (defaults by household
type); S6.100 (HH.16's bands and benchmarks).
**Goal**: the marginal propensity to consume out of receipts tied to no income or household event is measured by band
of wealth and of liquid wealth, against non-recipients of the same band over the same dates, by the agency's
consumption survey, together with the saving rate, the wealth and income distributions, leverage, the debt-service
burden and defaults by household type — all reads, never imposed.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/metrics.rs` | `mpc(recipients, non_recipients, receipts) -> Missing<Rate>` per band (pure); the other reads |
| `crates/systems/sys-hh/src/lib.rs` | the untied receipts' sources declared (refund records of the return; benefit rows' amounts changed on a budget's effective day); the agency's consumption survey: its sample frame of households (size the agency's POLICY, STA.5), each sampled household's panel record (last interview day, its spending rate then), the interview's quarterly fieldwork window; accumulators `HH.spending_change` (country, wealth band, liquidity band, recipient or not) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/hh.rs` | `LC-6-17` |

**Design**:
- **The survey is its own event**: the frame (1 % of households, drawn on a world stream as STA.2's samples are) is
  ordered by each household's phase (TIME.5); on each business day of the agency's quarterly fieldwork window the
  day's slice of the frame is interviewed (a declared sweep of the frame, K-14). No spending occasion reads anything
  for the survey.
- **The interview** reads the household's standing spending rate now against its panel record's rate at the last
  interview, times the days between, and adds the change to its (country, bands, recipient or not) key, bands read
  from its wealth and liquid wealth over income now; a recipient also adds what it received.
- **Receipts are reads of their sources**, never a stored copy (Law 4): since the last interview, the refunds
  recorded for its persons (the return's records by subject) and the change in its persons' benefit rows' amounts
  effective in that interval (the dated schedule's old and new values times each row's terms). Benefit starts
  (S5.123) and inheritances (S2.135) come with a job lost, an illness, a birth or a death, each of which moves
  spending by itself: their responses are published beside the measure and never enter it.
- **The quarter's close**: per band, recipients' spending change per unit received less non-recipients' change over
  the same dates (Johnson, Parker and Souleles, 2006, who read a survey) — `Missing` for a band with no recipients.
  Published with the saving rate, wealth and income distributions (fixed-bin), leverage, the debt-service burden and
  defaults by household type (event counts).

**Edge cases**:
- E14: two untied receipts before one interview add; the interview reads both (`two_receipts_add`).
- E11: a household's first interview after the opening reads receipts since the snapshot day
  (`first_interview_from_snapshot`).
- E13: a quarter with no untied receipt in a country: the measure is `Missing` for it, never zero
  (`no_recipients_missing`).
- E10: a sampled household that ends leaves the frame; the frame is refreshed by the agency's draw
  (`ended_household_leaves_frame`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**:
- `mpc_metric_arithmetic`: over given rate changes, days and receipts.
- `tied_receipt_refused_from_mpc`: a benefit start or an inheritance does not enter.
- `benefit_change_from_schedule`; `no_recipients_missing`; `two_receipts_add`; `first_interview_from_snapshot`;
  `ended_household_leaves_frame`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-6-17`: HH.16 — the propensity by band is published each quarter with a budget's effective day or a filing
  window, by fact 14's registered definition (PC-90); equal propensities across bands are a finding about a mechanism,
  never a tuning (applicable after the first such quarter).

**Budget**:
- adds 0 phone-ns to fin.decide.spend_ns (the survey reads nothing on a spending occasion).
- on fin.calendar.consumption_survey (the agency's quarterly fieldwork window, ≈ 60 business days): 0.1 core-ms;
  joins H — 370 interviews a window's business day (22 k sampled a quarter) × 300 ns (the spending rate, the
  receipts' reads, bands, a fused increment).
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.35 MB resident (22 k panel records × 16 B).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a propensity to consume declared or imposed; bands chosen after seeing the run; a survey read on the spending
  occasion.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; `LC-6-17` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S6.130 — Income spread against defaults and spending

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: HH.17 MEASURE
**Architecture**: §14.8 the realism reads (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.358 (the recorder, K-106, writing declared series at each close); S1.495 (the estimators: OLS with
Newey–West intervals); S5.109 (the returns: each person's income for the year, the records the spread is read from);
S1.213 (defaults as events by region); S1.477 (spending by region in the national accounts); S1.221 (accumulators);
S6.100 (HH.17's file among the stage's reads).
**Goal**: how household defaults and aggregate spending relate to the spread of household incomes, their mean held as
a control, across the run's regions and years, is read with its interval from the world's own records — its statistic,
region-years and estimator fixed before it is first read.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/measure/HH17.toml` | the statistic (defaults per household and real spending per head on the income distribution's spread with its mean as control, region fixed effects), the region-years, the estimator and its version, `min_years`, benchmark and sign only where a cited source states one |
| `crates/systems/sys-sta/src/lib.rs` | the accumulator `STA.household_income_bins` (country, region, log bin) for the filing year, filled as the returns are filed |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/hh.rs` | `LC-6-18` |

**Design**:
- Each household's year's income, from its persons' filed returns (S5.109), adds one count to its (region, bin) key
  as the last return of the household is filed; at the filing year's close the spread (a declared quantile ratio) and
  the mean per region are handed to the recorder as that region-year's values and the bins restart. Defaults are the
  region's household default events; spending the region's household consumption published.
- The recorder (K-106) records the region-year series; the estimator (S1.495) reads them; the file is registered
  before any report that uses it (PC-90). The relationship is reported with its interval and the region-years read;
  a sign is expected only where the file's source states one.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: fewer region-years than `min_years`: not yet read, listed with the run's length (`fewer_years_not_read`).
- E13: a region with no default in a year: a count of zero defaults (a count) (`zero_defaults_counted`).
- E9: the bins hold one filing year; each year's values live in the recorder's series (`bins_restart_at_close`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `income_spread_from_bins`; `region_year_panel_from_records`; `fewer_years_not_read`;
`zero_defaults_counted`; `bins_restart_at_close`.

**Live checks**:

  registered file (PC-90 clean).

**Budget**:
- its share of fin.fixed.stats: 0.02 / 0 / 0.02 core-ms (B / NB / H) — 9 k households' last returns filed a business
  day (2.2 M a year over the filing window) × 2 ns fused increments; the reads run outside the turn.
- ledger line 16 (small-bases pool): +0.03 MB resident (25 regions × 64 bins × 16 B).

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per

- a statistic, window or benchmark chosen after a report that used it; a sign expected without a source.

### S6.131 — Two views: the participant's scope and the inspector's surface

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: OBS.2 STATE
**Architecture**: §12 observation and the player (writes the two builds); §4.9 records, audiences, scoped reads
(follows).
**Depends on**: S1.215 (records with audiences and publication days); S1.196 (a party's own columns, the scope's
reads); S1.348 (the player's party and its decisions); S1.176 (observer streams apart from the world's).
**Goal**: both views exist as two builds, each labelled on every screen: the participant's reads its own party and
public information after its lags and nothing else; the inspector's reads everything, for building and research, and
compiles only where the participant's build refuses it.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/scope.rs` | `ParticipantScope<'a>`: the player's party's own rows and columns, records whose audience includes it at or after their publication day, public events; no accessor of another party's private fact |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/Cargo.toml` | the `inspector` feature gating `Inspector` reads and the inspector's pages |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/label.rs` | `ViewLabel { Participant, Inspector }`, carried by every page |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc83.rs` | PC-83 |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc84.rs` | PC-84 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/obs.rs` | `LC-6-19` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §12: the two builds, the scope and the label |

**Design**:
- **Participant** (OBS.2, Law 12): `ParticipantScope` is the same scoped read a decision's view has — its party's own
  state, records after their lag, what it bought or was sent — so a participant sees what its party could know. Its
  constructor takes the player's party from the decision core and the day; every method returns a `Shown<T>`
  (S6.132).
- **Inspector**: the read-only `Inspector` surface of `phx-world`, behind the `inspector` feature; its pages may show
  any party, contract, finding and REP.15's report beside every distributional number.
- **Label**: every page carries its `ViewLabel`, and the renderer refuses a page without one.
- Nothing either view does writes (Law 17): both take `&World` through their surfaces only (PC-20).

**Edge cases**:
- E11: day zero: the participant sees the opening's public present values (GEN.5) and its own party
  (`day_zero_scope_reads_opening_public`).
- E10: the player's household ending (its last person dies): the scope reads its estate's public records only
  (`ended_player_scope_reads_estate_public`).

**Extension points**: S6.132–S6.137 and S6.134 build on the scope and the label.

**Unit tests**: `participant_scope_refuses_private` (compile-fail: no accessor of another party's columns);
`page_without_label_refused`; `day_zero_scope_reads_opening_public`; `ended_player_scope_reads_estate_public`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-6-19`: OBS.2 — the participant build contains no inspector page (its symbol list), every page carries its
  label, and the read-trace over the participant's page builds finds no read of another party's private fact.

**Budget**:
- no share of any turn line: pages build only when looked at, outside the turn's measured work.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world (a page is built into the observer's transient buffer).

**Guards**: PC-83 (a participant page takes `ParticipantScope` only, which has no accessor of a fact whose audience
excludes the player's party; compile level, with its rule file); PC-84 (the `inspector` feature refused in the
participant build: the build's feature check).

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a participant's view showing another party's private information; a view that writes.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; PC-83 and PC-84 registered; `LC-6-19` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §12 written (the two builds).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.

### S6.132 — Shown numbers: from a source, missing as missing, stale as stale

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: OBS.6 FORBID; OBS.7 FORBID
**Architecture**: §12 observation (writes shown numbers).
**Depends on**: S6.131 (the scope and the label); S1.326 (prints and marks with their day and market names); S1.215
(records with their publication day); S1.279 (an instrument's terms, its market name's source).
**Goal**: every number a page shows is a `Shown<T>` built only from a source — a record entry, a read of state at the
close, a published statistic, or a fixed-bin aggregate of such reads — with its date and age; a missing value shows as
missing, a price past its market's staleness horizon shows its age, a change only with its levels, and every
instrument by the name its market uses.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/shown.rs` | `Shown<T> { value: Missing<T>, source: Source, dated: u32, age_days: u32 }`; `Source` constructors (`Record`, `Close`, `Published`, `Aggregate`); `Change { from: Shown<T>, to: Shown<T> }` |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/names.rs` | `instrument_name(terms, market) -> String`: issuer, class or coupon and maturity as its market names it (Law 9) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc82.rs` | PC-82 |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/obs.rs` | `LC-6-20` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §12: shown numbers |

**Design**:
- `Shown<T>` has no public constructor but through a `Source`; a page's renderer accepts only `Shown<T>` and `Change`
  (no bare number). A `Change` is shown only with both levels (Law 8).
- **Staleness**: a print or mark older than its market's declared staleness horizon (MKT's) shows its age; a
  legitimate publication lag shows as the lag (a statistic's reference period and publication day), never as
  staleness.
- **Missing**: `Missing::Absent` renders as missing; zero renders as zero (a price of zero is a price).
- **Names**: an instrument is shown by `instrument_name`; an internal id is never a display name.

**Edge cases**:
- E12: an absent value is shown absent (`missing_shows_missing`).
- E2: a market with no print since the opening shows the opening's present value with its age (GEN.5)
  (`no_print_shows_opening_with_age`).

**Extension points**: every page of S6.133–S6.137 and the map, S6.134, displays through it.

**Unit tests**: `shown_only_from_sources` (compile-fail); `missing_shows_missing`; `stale_price_shows_age`;
`change_shown_with_levels`; `instrument_named_by_market`; `no_print_shows_opening_with_age`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-6-20`: OBS.6, OBS.7 — on the pages built at each gate's run's turn closes sampled on the observer's stream,
  every number traces to its record, read, statistic or aggregate and its date; missing values show missing; prices
  past their staleness horizon show their age; every instrument shows its market's name.

**Budget**:
- no share of any turn line: pages build only when looked at.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world.

**Guards**: PC-82 (`Shown<T>` is the only type a page may display, built only from `Source` constructors; compile
level, with its rule file).

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a number computed for display alone; a change without its levels; an internal id as a name.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; PC-82 registered; `LC-6-20` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §12 written (shown numbers).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S6.133 — Looking at a party

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: OBS.8 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §12 observation (writes the party page).
**Depends on**: S6.132 (shown numbers); S1.213 (the event log's observer read `naming(party, from, to)` over its
stored segments, outside the turn); S1.196, S1.207 (a party's columns, its persons); S1.257 (its contracts by side);
S1.271, S1.280 (its holdings: units, and instruments).
**Goal**: looking at a household or a firm shows the party itself — its attributes, persons, positions, contracts and
the recorded events that name it — and looking at one party or at a million leaves the world exactly as it was.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/pages/party.rs` | the party page generated from the kind's declared attribute schema (K-21): attributes, persons with their roles, positions, contracts by family, holdings, events naming it |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/pages/mod.rs` | pages generated from the view schemas the interface crates declare |

| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §12: the party page |

**Design**:
- The page reads through the participant's scope for the player's own party and public records of others, or through
  the inspector's surface in that build; each value a `Shown<T>`.
- Events naming the party are read by the event log's observer read `naming` within its horizon (SET.13), outside the
  turn; older ones are gone with their horizon, which the page says.
- Nothing is drawn to show a party (no observer draw is needed: every person is held, REP.26); the world's streams are
  never touched (REP.16).

**Live checks**:

  pages for a sample of parties (the observer's stream) leaves the next close's hash unchanged against the run's own.

**Budget**:

- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world.

file).

### S6.134 — The map

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: OBS.12 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §12 observation (writes the map); §7.4 phx-geo (follows: tiles, cells, parcels, the segment index).
**Depends on**: S6.131 (the two views and the participant's scope); S6.132 (shown numbers); S6.133 (the party page a
selection opens); S1.190 (K-28: cells, parcels, `crossing`, `cells_of`); S1.284 (K-66: named units by tile, a unit's
kind, owner and site, `in_building`); S1.187 (K-26: segments, the infrastructure's paths); S1.188 (a segment's use
today); S1.221 (K-39: population and employment by zone); S1.273 (K-61: units held by (zone, class)); S2.169
(buildings on cells).
**Goal**: the observer shows the world's map at any zoom — tiles and their terrain, the cells held, every building,
farm, forest and mine at its cell with its owner, occupants or users and value on selection, the land parcels and the
infrastructure along its paths with its use — aggregated by zone, region and country when zoomed out, built from what
the world holds and nothing else, and building it leaves the world exactly as it was.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/pages/map.rs` | the map page: its levels (cells and tiles, zones, regions, countries), the tiles in view, sites, parcels, paths with their use, a selection opening the party page; the zoomed-out sums per zone, region and country |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/pages/map_tests.rs` | unit tests over hand-built tiles, parcels, sites and segments |
| `data/shared/OBS.toml` | `OBS.map_detail_tiles` (SHAPE: the most tiles drawn cell by cell at once, the screen's legibility its reason) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/obs.rs` | `LC-6-28` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §12: the map |

**Design**:
- **Levels** (OBS.12): while the tiles in view are at most `OBS.map_detail_tiles`, each is drawn cell by cell; beyond
  it, the view is the sums of the zones, regions or countries it covers, the coarsest whose count in view is within the
  same setting.
- **Tiles and terrain**: each tile's surface, terrain, elevation and relief read from the map's tiles (K-25).
- **The cells held** (GEO.19): per tile in view, S1.284's named units by tile give every site's cell and kind — each
  building, farm, forest and mine at its cell, a building at its position within the cell (S2.169's column); S1.190's
  parcels give their rectangles; the tile's segment index and `cells_of` give the cells each path crosses. A cell none
  of them holds shows its tile's land.
- **Infrastructure** (GEO.4): each segment in view along its cells, with its mode, capacity, condition and closure, and
  its use today — S1.188's day-stamped load against its capacity, a stale stamp read as no trip that day, never as a
  default.
- **Selection**: a unit shows its owner (its K-66 owner, opening S6.133's page), its occupants or users (the holdings
  placed in it through `in_building` and their holders — a dwelling's household, a shop's firm; a segment's day's use)
  and its value (its cost for its owner's own books, the latest print or labelled valuation, MKT.20), each a `Shown<T>`
  (S6.132). In the participant's build every read goes through its scope (S6.131): the player's own units in full,
  others' as public records give them.
- **Zoomed out**: per zone, the population and employment (K-39), the units held by (zone, class) (K-61) and the named
  units by kind counted over the zone's tiles; regions and countries sum their zones. The counts are built from the
  close's state the first time they are asked and kept in the observer's buffer until the next close.
- **Only what the world holds** (OBS.6, Law 17): the map reads `&World` through the scope or the inspector's surface
  (PC-20, PC-85); it places nothing the world does not record — a unit held by (zone, class) in no building has no
  cell and appears only in its zone's sums, since drawing its tile is the world's own draw (REP.23) and the observer
  never calls it — and it opens no world stream.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a tile with nothing held shows its terrain only (`empty_tile_shows_terrain`).
- E12: a unit with no print or valuation shows its value missing, never zero (`unvalued_unit_shows_missing`).
- E10: a segment closed shows closed until its reopening day; a scrapped building is gone at the next close
  (`closed_segment_shown_closed`).
- E3: a unit counted by (zone, class) in no building is never placed on a cell (`counted_units_not_placed`).
- E2: a segment with no trip today shows no use (`no_trip_no_use`).
- OBS.2: the participant's map shows another party's unit only as public records give it (`participant_map_scope`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `site_placed_at_its_cell`; `parcel_drawn_as_rectangle`; `path_drawn_along_cells_of_segment`;
`level_by_tiles_in_view`; `zones_sum_to_regions_and_countries`. Edge cases: `empty_tile_shows_terrain`;
`unvalued_unit_shows_missing`; `closed_segment_shown_closed`; `counted_units_not_placed`; `no_trip_no_use`;
`participant_map_scope`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-6-28`: Law 17, OBS.6, OBS.12 — at closes of the gate's run sampled on the observer's stream, the world hash is
  taken before the map is built, the map is then built at every level over sampled tiles, zones and regions, and the
  hash taken again before the next day equals it; every site, parcel and path drawn names the world row it came from.

**Budget**:
- no share of any turn line: the map builds only when looked at, between turns, outside the turn's measured work.
- a detail view: per tile its named units, parcels and segments (≈ 35, 20 and 25 on average, a city's tile ≈ 2 k
  buildings) at ≤ 50 ns each and ≈ 100 cells a segment's `cells_of` at ≤ 5 ns → ≤ 20 ms for 400 tiles; the zoomed-out
  sums once a close, ≈ 1.6 M sites at ≤ 5 ns ≈ 8 ms, then reads.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world (the view in the observer's transient buffer, ≤ 4 MB, inside ledger line 1's
  process).

**Guards**: PC-85 holds (`phx-obs` imports no mutable accessor of the world); none new.

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a view that draws, writes or opens a world stream; a unit placed on a cell the world does not record; a use, value
  or count filled in where the world holds none; a cell grid kept for display.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code, the declared setting and unit tests; `LC-6-28` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §12 written (the map).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

**Depends on**: S1.213 (events with a develops-from link, public by the declared rule); S6.132 (shown numbers).
**Goal**: the public-event rule declares, per kind, which later events develop from it — a default, its estate's
distribution, the holders' losses; a failed auction, the next auction; a catastrophe, its claims — and the news shows
those chains; no news the state did not produce exists, and nothing written moves anything.

### S6.136 — The player acts through every decision point, its minds advising

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: OBS.4 PROCESS
**Architecture**: §12 observation and the player (writes the decision pages); §7.16 phx-mind (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.348 (the decision core: the player keeps a decision, intents queued and taken on the first day the
decision comes); S1.352 (minds: `explain`); S8.103 (every decider handed its own mind); S8.122 (offices held by the
player's persons at firms they own); S6.131, S6.132 (scope and shown numbers).
**Goal**: the player acts as its household, with its own means, through every decision point its household and
persons have — the offices its persons hold at the firms they own among them — and passes every check any party's
action does; its persons' minds advise, each saying what it would do and why, and the player decides or leaves the
decision to them.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/pages/decisions.rs` | a page per decision point the player's household and persons have, generated from the point's declared input view and option set: the options with their consequences by concern, the advice, a form for the intent |
| `crates/assembly/phx-obs/src/player.rs` | `advice(point, view) -> Advice` through `explain` on each deciding person's mind (read-only); `submit(intent)` into the decision core's queue for the player; the delegation setting per point |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/obs.rs` | `LC-6-23` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §12: the decision pages and delegation |

**Design**:
- **Pages**: for each decision point the player's household or its persons decide (and each office its persons hold),
  the page shows the view its rule reads, through the participant's scope, and the options its generator produces with
  their consequences; the advice is each deciding mind's `explain` (its best option and the tipping concern).
- **Acting**: `submit` queues the intent in the decision core; at 1b of the first day the point runs, it becomes the
  player's occasion and passes every check any party's does — admission hooks, funds, limits, the law; a refusal is an
  event the player sees. Where the player leaves a point to its minds (its delegation setting, defaulted from the
  setup, GEN.14), the decision is the minds' as any household's (Appendix E 50).
- The player's party is a household drawn at the opening on its own stream (the player's draw, CHN.3), counted in
  every family.

**Edge cases**:
- E3: the player's household with no money: its purchases fail as anyone's (MON.12) (`intent_passes_same_checks`).
- E10: the player's person dying: its offices and decisions pass as any person's; the pages follow the household
  (`pages_follow_household_after_death`).
- E14: an intent and a delegated decision on one point the same day: the intent is taken; one decision
  (`intent_before_delegation`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `intent_passes_same_checks` (a refused intent over given limits); `advice_reads_explain_only`;
`delegation_takes_minds_choice`; `pages_follow_household_after_death`; `intent_before_delegation`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-6-23`: OBS.4 — the player's party passes every family, each family counts it, and every action it submitted was
  decided or refused at its point by the same checks as any party's.

**Budget**:
- the player's decisions are one household's, counted in the household lines; advice 1 ms a page, outside the turn.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident (the delegation setting is one flag per point in the player's setup).

**Guards**: PC-85 applies (no change): `submit` goes through the decision core's queue, never a store.

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a privileged player; an action that bypasses a point's checks; advice that reads another party's private state.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Code and unit tests; `LC-6-23` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §12 written (the decision pages).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S6.138 — Every resolution setting, taste distribution and review cost registered and counted

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: tool
**Clauses**: REP.18 PRIMITIVE
**Architecture**: §7.3 phx-core, the register and the kind catalogue (follows); §13 budgets, the valve (follows); §6
the static checks (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.179 (the register); S1.180 (the kind catalogue); S1.348 (decisions counted by kind and standing);
every decision step of Stages 1–6 (their review costs and tastes declared).
**Goal**: the register holds every RESOLUTION setting — the representation's size, each kind's attribute classes,
zones, age classes, horizons, the audit's cycle, the draw scheme — each with its place in the owner's order of
refinement, and the map's grid and cell size marked as the owner fixed them (N8.5); every taste distribution per preference type; each kind's payment order; what reviewing
and changing each kind of decision costs; and each trade's price points; and every review cost is counted per decision
kind in the run.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/register_completeness.rs` | PC-192, a declaration check over the systems' declarations and the register's data: a decision kind with no review cost; a taste stream with no distribution for some type; a kind with a declared attribute but no classes; a trade with posted prices but no price points; a RESOLUTION entry with no place in the refinement order, but the grid and the cell size the owner fixed |
| `data/shared/REP.toml` | `refine_rank` per RESOLUTION entry by the owner's order (§12: persons, preference types, attribute classes and zones, horizons and snapshot intervals, age classes, the audit's cycle, the draw scheme); the map's grid and `GEO.cell_m` marked `owner_fixed` |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/rep.rs` | `LC-6-24` |

**Design**:
- The refusals are `phx-check`'s (PC-192), read from the declarations and the register's data before any build; they
  change no base and no kernel crate, and each names the declaration and the clause. A declaration they pass is then
  compiled by the core's own assembly refusals (S1.179, S1.180), unchanged.
- The review costs' hours are counted per decision kind by the decision core's tallies and reported in the run's
  report beside the decisions taken (REP.21, §2.21).
- Nothing in the world reads `refine_rank`: it is the valve's order for the owner and the bench's resolution
  change (§2.10), cited in a `Resolution-Change` trailer (PC-91).

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a missing entry is a refusal naming it, never a default (`review_cost_refused_when_missing`).
- E13: a kind with no lumpy decision declares no review cost and is not refused

**Status**: planned

earlier stage's opening contribution (its step).

derived sides and its sources — and a GEN report that lists every distribution with its source, every present value
with its source, every balancing change and every apportionment difference; no country copies a real one.

## 10. Stage 7 — Realism

**Exit** (spec Part O): the measurement of the world's run completed — every N3 stylised fact and N4 chain
relationship, and N7's calibration of primitives from data. What misses is recorded against the mechanism suspected;
the build continues by adding mechanisms, never by tuning. The gate (S7.106) judges it on the whole world's gate run.

**The run.** There is one: the world's run at the committed resolution with its one seed (Appendix E 36), settled for
the owner's length (GEN.6), measured by the bench's gate run (`tools/bench.sh -g`) until the owner calls the device
run. The recorder (K-106, S1.358) runs with it, its time and bytes inside the turns; the estimators, the verdict rule,
the fact reports and the chain relationships' computation are Stage 1's tools (S1.494–S1.497), used from the Stage 1
gate on for the facts and chains whose systems existed. A fact the run has not yet had time to produce is *not yet
credited*, reported with the years of play its file says it needs; no second run, seed, resolution or copy is made.

**What this stage adds.** After its reads (S7.100), nothing in the world: it completes the reads over the whole world
— slow distributions credited while held and moved (GEN.10), every fact (N3) and every chain (N4) read with its
verdict, every silent break mapped to what refuses it (PC-93), and the primitive register reported (N7). The old
"calibration" step is restated as that report: comparisons with real data are the facts' and chains' benchmarks
alone, and nothing is tuned (N7, GEN.11, PC-91).

**Conventions**, read by every Stage 7 step (a definition file may override one only in its first version):
- every report names the setup its run started from (GEN.11, GEN.14); each benchmark is the range real economies of
  the country's development level show, one range per level in its file (N3);
- each statistic is computed per country, with its estimator's interval from the run's own sample; the verdict per
  country is *reproduced* (the estimate in the range), *missed* (the interval wholly outside) or *inconclusive*;
- statistics use STA's published series where the fact is aggregate, else records and closes read through the
  `Inspector` (the inspector's view is for research, OBS.2); nothing is recomputed that a record already states.

**From a miss to a finding.** Every missed or inconclusive verdict, every chain relationship that misses, every chain
whose first link the run never had, and every silent break nothing refuses is written into the step that will fix it:
what was measured (statistic, estimate and interval, benchmark and source, years of the run) and the mechanisms its
definition's `suspects` list named before the report. A finding is closed only by a step that adds or corrects a
mechanism (a spec amendment first where the spec lacks it). Such a step is placed after the realism gate in **Stage 7
findings**, the range S7.107 onward in build order, its title naming its system; its Depends on names S7.106 and the
steps it changes. Never: a primitive, a rule's form or parameters, an opening distribution or a definition changed to
close a miss (N7, GEN.11; PC-90, PC-91). A reset of the play resolution is representation, set by measuring the budget
(N8.5), cited as such.

**Placeholders**: none introduced; none remain (S6.142).

**The stage's budget lines.** The wealth survey's fieldwork window (S7.101) is Stage 7's one line in the turn: about
11 core-ms on each of its business days, which can meet the quarter-end payday; the recorder's lines are S1.358's.
Every other step runs outside the turn.

### S7.101 — Slow distributions credited while the whole world holds and moves them

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: GEN.10 FORBID
**Architecture**: §14.8 the realism reads (writes the credit of slow distributions); §12 observation (follows).
**Depends on**: S7.100 (the reads); S1.496 (the credit rule for classes S and B, the verdicts; class S reported not
yet credited at Stage 1); S1.358 (the recorder, K-106); S1.171 (a declared sweep over a window); S6.128 (every class
a household holds); S6.130 (household incomes from the returns, binned); S1.261 (firms' headcount); S1.335 (valuers'
published methods: dwellings and pension rights at their valuations).
**Goal**: a stylised fact about a slow distribution — income, wealth, firm sizes — counts as reproduced only while the
whole world holds it and moves it: its statistic in its benchmark range at each year end of play, its distance from
the opening showing no drift away, and its members moving within it by the world's own flows; a fact about behaviour
counts only once the run has produced it after settling; nothing counts from the opening day alone.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/systems/sys-sta/src/distribution.rs` | the agency's household wealth survey over its fieldwork window (a census of households, each valued on its own interview day); firm sizes by employment bin; the published distributional series (fixed bins, top shares) |
| `crates/systems/sys-sta/src/lib.rs` | the survey's declared sweep (cycle: the fieldwork window, POLICY of the agency); accumulators `STA.net_worth_bins`, `STA.firm_size_bins`; the mobility sample (a fixed share of households and firms by identity, no draw) |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/realism.rs` | `LC-7-01` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §14.8: the credit of slow distributions |

**Design**:
- **Wealth** (fact 13's and GEN.8's reads): each household valued on its own interview day within the survey's
  fieldwork window (a declared sweep of households by slot range, one slice a business day): its members' accounts
  and holdings at that day's marks, dwellings and pension rights at the valuers' published methods (MKT.20, never a
  household's own opinion), less its members' debts; one count to its (country, net-worth bin) key and its top-share
  sums.
- **Income**: from the returns (S6.130's bins). **Firm sizes** (fact 8): each firm's (country, employment bin) key
  moved when its headcount crosses a bin edge (K-54's update), so the year-end distribution is read without a pass.
- **Credit** (GEN.10), by S1.496's rule on class S facts at each year end of play: the statistic in range; GEN.8's
  distance from the opening's distribution with no trend beyond its interval; the members moving within it — the share
  of the mobility sample whose bin changed between year ends, by the world's own flows. A class-S fact is credited
  only while all three hold; class B facts only over windows after settling.

**Edge cases**:
- E5: the survey's slices are spread over its fieldwork window, so no year-end heavy day carries a census; the window
  is the agency's declared survey design and avoids no calendar turn (`survey_slice_by_window_day`).
- E11: nothing credited from day zero or the settling period alone (`window_never_before_play`).
- E12: a household whose dwelling has no published valuation that day is surveyed with that holding `Missing` and
  counted apart, never at zero (`missing_valuation_counted_apart`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**:
- `held_only_while_in_range_every_year_end`; `drift_trend_on_given_distances`; `mobility_share_from_given_bins`.
- `window_never_before_play`; `firm_bin_moves_at_edge`; `survey_slice_by_window_day`;
  `missing_valuation_counted_apart`.

**Live checks**:

  play; nothing is credited from the opening alone.

**Guards**: PC-90 applies (no change) over the reads.

- a fact credited from the opening day, or over a window that begins before play; a census taken on one day.

needs; every fact file's series resolves to a series the world publishes or records.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/realism/coverage.rs` | `phx realism coverage`: every fact file's series, unit of observation and window resolved against the recorder's declarations; an unresolved one is listed with the file |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/realism.rs` | `LC-7-02` |

**Design**:
- N3 is complete here on the whole world; S1.496 built its reports and verdicts from Stage 1 on. All twenty-eight
  fact files are registered (`data/measure/N3/`); none is added here.
- **Coverage**: each file names its series (STA's published series by key, prints and fixings by market, event kinds,
  cross-sections); the tool resolves each against the recorder's declared series; one the world does not publish or
  record is a finding written into the step that will publish it — never a file edited to fit.
- **Reports**: S1.496's `phx realism compute` and `report` on the gate run's recorded series for all twenty-eight
  facts, per country; a later version of a definition reports beside the earlier (`Measure-Change` trailer).
- **Earlier reads** (LAB.14, FRM.19, CAP.10, EQY.10, XB.9, TEC.10, HH.16 and the gates' macro reads) are reads of the
  mechanism and credit nothing.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: a fact whose window the run has not reached is *not yet credited* with the run's length
  (`window_not_reached_not_yet_credited`).
- E13: a fact about a market a country lacks (a closed capital account) reports that country as not applicable, with
  the reason its file states (`absent_market_not_applicable`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `coverage_lists_unresolved_series`; `verdict_rule_reproduced_missed_inconclusive` (over given
estimates, intervals and ranges); `window_not_reached_not_yet_credited`; `absent_market_not_applicable`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-7-02`: N3 — every fact has a report per country with its verdict, or *not yet credited* with the run's length;
  every miss and inconclusive verdict names the step it is written into and its suspects.

**Budget**:
- no day work: the reads run over the recorded series after the run.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world.

**Guards**: PC-90 and PC-91 apply (no change).

**Not allowed**:
- a store, index, map or per-party pass outside the core bases; a pass over every party every day; an allocation per
  day;
- a statistic, filter, window, sample, suspect list or benchmark changed after a report that used it but as a new
  version beside the old; a country or a window dropped after seeing it; a second run or a copy of the world.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `phx realism coverage` lists no unresolved series, or each is written into the step that will publish it.
- [ ] Code and unit tests; `LC-7-02` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S7.103 — Every chain's relationships read on the whole world

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: mechanism
**Clauses**: N4; L1; L2; L3; L4; L5; L6; L7; L8; L9; L10; L11; L12
**Architecture**: §14.8 the realism reads (follows).
**Depends on**: S1.497 (the chains' relationships computed and reported); S7.102 (the facts L1 and L3 are held to:
17 and 11); every step whose events start a chain's first link.
**Goal**: what each chain of Part L implies for the relationships between macro variables — signs, leads and lags —
is read from the whole world's run around the run's own occurrences of its first link and compared with real
economies' benchmarks; a chain whose first link the run has not had is *not yet tested*, and one whose conditions the
run met without the chain acting is a finding.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/chains.rs` | `LC-7-03`, `LC-7-04`, `LC-7-05` |

**Design**:
- N4 and each chain complete here on the whole world, as one test over Part L (N4's text makes the chains one
  measure); S1.497 computed and reported them from Stage 1 on.
- For each chain (`data/measure/N4/L01.toml` … `L12.toml`, registered): its relationships read by S1.497 over every
  occurrence of its first link the recorder holds, with intervals and verdicts; L1 and L3 are held to the audit (N1)
  and to facts 17 and 11 (N4's text).
- **Traces** (LC-7-03): what no published work benchmarks is traced in the records over each occurrence — a default's
  arrears, workout, enforcement, collateral sale and losses on named holders in the order of claims (L1); a policy
  surprise's overnight prints, banks' marginal cost of funds, loan quotes, firms' marginal cost of money, investment
  orders and hiring in that order (L4); a discovery's diffusion (L12) — reported beside the relationships, no verdict.
- Part L's text is never edited by a result.

**Edge cases**:
- E11: a chain whose first link never occurred is *not yet tested*, listed with the run's length (Appendix E 39)
  (`LC-7-03`).
- E1: a mass default day is one occurrence of L1's and L6's first links, read with its subjects
  (`event_window_from_given_dates`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `event_window_from_given_dates`; `lead_lag_peak_on_given_series`;
`order_of_first_responses_from_given_series`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-7-03`: every chain has its report, read over every occurrence of its first link the recorder holds, its traces
  followed and reported with no verdict.
- `LC-7-04`: L6's weakness observed by name: every discretionary withdrawal, rollover refusal, limit cut and
  redemption around a bank's published losses read at least one record naming the institution it left (read-trace).
- `LC-7-05`: L5's standards: per bank and year of play, whether its published standards changed while its outlook of
  losses on its own book changed; a bank whose standards never moved while its outlook did is a finding.

**Budget**:
- no day work: the reads run over the recorded series after the run.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**:
- a chain claimed without its test, or a claim kept that its test missed; a trace reported as a relationship;
- a relationship, horizon or benchmark chosen after seeing the run; a knock-out or copy of the world to test a chain.

**Done when**:
- [ ] Every chain's relationships read and reported with verdicts, or *not yet tested* with the run's length; every
  miss written into the step that will fix it, against the chain's links.
- [ ] `LC-7-03`, `LC-7-04`, `LC-7-05` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S7.104 — Every silent break mapped to what refuses it

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: tool
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §16 drift guards (writes PC-93).
**Depends on**: S7.103 (the chains read); every step and `phx-check` rule a refusal names.
**Goal**: every "Silently broken by" item of Part L names what refuses it — a registered `phx-check` rule, a live
check not retired, an N1 family, or an assembly refusal — and PC-93 keeps the map complete and every refusal
resolvable; an item nothing refuses is a finding written into the step that will build its refusal.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `data/measure/N4/BREAKS.toml` | each item: its chain, its text, and its refusals by stable identifier (`PC-nn`, `LC-s-nn`, an N1 family, an assembly refusal's id) |
| `crates/apps/phx-check/src/rules/pc93.rs` | PC-93 |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §16: PC-93 and the breaks' map |

**Design**:
- The map keeps Part L's "silently broken by" items refused; it completes no clause of its own.
- Refusals are named by stable identifiers only — never by a step's Not-allowed text, since steps are removed when
  done: a Not-allowed line that is the only refusal of an item is made a `phx-check` rule, an assembly refusal or a
  live check in the step that owns it, and the map names that.
- PC-93 parses Part L's "Silently broken by" items from the spec, requires each in `BREAKS.toml`, and resolves each
  refusal: a registered PC rule, a registered live check not retired, one of N1's families, or a declared assembly
  refusal id.

**Edge cases**:
- E13: a chain with no break items needs no entry (`chain_without_breaks_needs_no_entry`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `every_item_mapped`; `unresolvable_refusal_refused`; `retired_check_not_a_refusal`;
`chain_without_breaks_needs_no_entry`.

**Live checks**: none.

**Budget**:
- no day work: a `phx-check` rule.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world.

**Guards**: PC-93 (every silent break mapped, every refusal resolvable).

**Not allowed**:
- a silent break marked refused by something that does not refuse it; a refusal named by text a step's removal
  deletes.

**Done when**:
- [ ] `BREAKS.toml` complete; PC-93 registered and clean, or each unrefused item written into the step that will build
  its refusal.
- [ ] ARCHITECTURE §16 written (PC-93).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S7.105 — The primitive register reported

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: tool
**Clauses**: N7
**Architecture**: §16.7 primitives' sources (follows).
**Depends on**: S6.138 (the register complete); S1.01 (PC-91: every change cites its source); S1.358 (the read-trace
of the run).
**Goal**: every primitive is traced to its source, or labelled estimated (with its estimation) or assumed (with its
reason), and the shares of assumed and estimated primitives are published by kind, system and country; outcomes are
compared with real data only through the facts' and chains' benchmarks, and nothing is tuned.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/register.rs` | `phx register-report` from the register's dump and `data/` |
| `crates/apps/phx-cli/src/checks/register.rs` | `LC-7-06` |

**Design**:
- N7 is complete here: every primitive traced to its source or labelled estimated or assumed, and the share of assumed
  primitives published.
- Per primitive: id, kind, unit, period, owner, `decided_by` for POLICY, source class (measured, estimated, assumed),
  `source_ref`, and where it is read (the run's read-trace).
- **Estimated** primitives name their estimation — a published estimate, or the method and the real data used; an
  estimation from the world's own run is tuning and is refused (a `source_ref` naming a run, a report or `perf/`).
- **Assumed** primitives state their reason; standing SHAPEs are listed with their reason and source (Law 2); the
  opening distributions (ENDOWMENT) per country are read from the register with their sources and listed. The
  report writes no primitive and no opening data.
- **Shares published** (N7): assumed and estimated over all, by kind, by system and by country.
- **Flagged for the reviewers**: a dimensionless share or ratio whose kind is not RESOLUTION or POLICY (a possible
  outcome imported, Law 2); countries whose opening parameters are identical (GEN.2 varies them); a primitive
  estimated from the same series a fact's benchmark reads (named with the fact). Each flag is resolved in review or
  written into the step that will fix it.
- Every primitive or opening change since S1.01 is listed with its trailer and source (PC-91).

**Edge cases**:
- E12: a primitive with no `source_ref` is refused by the report (and by the register)
  (`primitive_without_source_refused`).

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: `assumed_share_by_kind_system_and_country`; `estimation_from_world_run_refused`;
`flags_dimensionless_non_resolution_entries`; `primitive_without_source_refused`.

**Live checks**:
- `LC-7-06`: every declared primitive, stream and hazard was read at least once over the run (read-trace); an unread
  one is a finding (a mechanism that never runs), or its declaration is retired with its reason.

**Budget**:
- no day work: a report over the register and the run's trace.
- ledger: `+0 B` resident in the world.

**Guards**: PC-91 applies (no change).

**Not allowed**:
- a primitive changed to close a miss; an estimation drawn from the world's own outcomes; a source citing a realism
  report or a finding.

**Done when**:
- [ ] The register report committed with the shares; every flag resolved or written into the step that will fix it.
- [ ] Code and unit tests; `LC-7-06` registered (read at the gate).
- [ ] Fast checks pass; the bench at the committed resolution within `perf/budget.toml`.
- [ ] Both reviews are done; status `done` and the section removed.

### S7.106 — The realism gate

**Status**: planned
**Kind**: gate
**Clauses**: none
**Architecture**: §13 budgets (writes the final build's measured lines); §14.5 gates (follows).
**Depends on**: every step S7.100–S7.105; S6.142 (the whole world's gate).
**Goal**: the run of one build is measured — facts, chains, silent breaks and the register — every miss recorded
against a mechanism, and the final build within the budget with the recorder running.

**Files**:

| path | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `perf/bench/<commit>-committed-gate.json` | the gate run's report kept by the bench (`-k`), the recorder's time and bytes as their own lines |
| `perf/reads/S7.106-*.json` | Stage 7's macro reads from the run |
| `perf/realism/S7.106-report.json` | the realism report joining S7.101–S7.105's by reference, every part on the gate build |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | §13 with the final build's measured numbers |

**Design**:
- The run, the pass criteria, a miss and the Not allowed are §2.24's ("The gate"); this gate adds only the following.
- **Stage 7's heavy days**: the wealth survey's fieldwork days (S7.101), with the quarter-end payday they can meet;
  the recorder's year-end lines (S1.358). A heavy day the run has not had is listed with the run's length.
- **Stage 7's macro reads**: those S7.100 froze in `data/observer/READS.toml`, read against their benchmarks.
- **One build, one run**: every report joined names the gate build; a report computed on an earlier build is read
  again on this build's run before the gate is judged (a new build starts its run anew, Appendix E 36).
- **The stage's own checks**: every fact has a verdict per country or is *not yet credited* with the run's length and
  its `min_years` (LC-7-02); every chain its relationships read or *not yet tested* (LC-7-03); every silent break its
  refusal (PC-93); the register report committed (LC-7-06); PC-90 and PC-91 clean since S1.01; every miss,
  inconclusive verdict, untested chain and unread declaration written into the step that will fix it, naming its
  suspected mechanism (a findings step placed from S7.107 on).
- **What blocks**: realism misses do not block (Part O: the run has been measured and misses are recorded); the
  budget does (N8.8).

**Edge cases**:
- E5: the heavy days above — n/a: a gate reads its run; from the gate run's report.
- E6: a save and a load mid-run with the recorder's unexported series: LC-0-35 and LC-0-36 on the gate run.
- E9: every store and record within its horizon over the run — n/a: a gate reads its run; from the gate run's report.

**Extension points**: none.

**Unit tests**: none.

**Live checks**: every live check of every stage passes or is not yet applicable on the gate run.

**Budget**:
- the gate: §2.24's criteria at the committed resolution and at the design point, with the recorder running.

**Guards**: none new.

**Not allowed**:
- §2.24's; and a gate judged on reports of another build.

**Done when**:
- [ ] §2.24's Done when, with the recorder running, Stage 7's heavy days measured, the reads of S7.100 reported and
  the stage's own checks above holding; every miss written into the step that will fix it.
- [ ] The realism report committed, every part on the gate build.

## 12. Owner decisions

| Decision | Answer | Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bases first (N8.6, N8.7) | every base the whole project needs is designed and built first, in Stage 1's core steps, against the whole spec and the budget at the design point; later steps only activate bases and add behaviour | 2026-09-29 |
| Reviews (§0.1 rule 7) | independent agents review only major steps — each stage's gate, and steps the owner names; other steps are reviewed by the builder with the same two prompts | 2026-09-23 |
| Steps and gates | a step is done on its fast checks (format, lint, tests, `phx-check`) and the bench's read of the budget; the world's long run is at each stage's gate, `tools/bench.sh -g`: settled, two years, the audit and every live check, whose findings are fixed there; every gate is judged by §2.24 | 2026-09-26 |
| Size-rule allowances (§0.2) | a step retires the placeholder it replaces in that placeholder's own crate, as part of the step; under PC-40 a step may add the one lender's-value function it needs in `sys-bnk`, and no other `sys-bnk` rule | 2026-09-30 |
| Opening data mappings | each mapping of sources in hand into the opening's primitives is a `data` step of its own | 2026-09-30 |
| One bench (§2.10, §2.11) | `tools/bench.sh` is the one tool that runs and measures the world: its flags set the persons, days, seed, workers, checks, a time limit and a sampling profile; it writes the run's whole report, each stage of the day timed, and a summary; a step reads the budget on it at the committed resolution, a gate runs it with `-g`, and `-k` keeps the report a resolution change cites; no other tool runs or measures the world | 2026-09-29 |
| Finished-volume measure (N8.8) | a mode of the one bench, `tools/bench.sh -F`: each base filled with seeded random data at its size at the design point and run through its kernels at the design point's daily counts on an ordinary, a non-business and a heavy day; every base step's **Done when** includes its unit cost and bytes against `perf/budget.toml`; the device measure replaces it when the owner calls the device run | 2026-09-29 |

| Done steps (§0.4) | when a step is done its whole section is removed from the plan; whatever needs keeping about how it was built goes in the architecture | 2026-09-27 |
| Findings (§0.5) | a finding is solved at once, nothing postponed because it is long or complicated | 2026-09-27 |
| No findings table (§0.5) | a finding is solved in its step or written into the step that will settle it; every data point no source gives is closed by a derivation, a paper's table or a declared simulation, named in the step that reads it | 2026-09-28 |
| A step waiting on the owner (PC-09) | a step whose remaining **Done when** items are the owner's alone takes the status `awaiting owner`, which is not `building` | 2026-09-25 |
| A kernel's fixture in its tests | a kernel's hand-built fixture of a few parties, contracts and books, asserting its own arithmetic, is a logic-level test and not a world | 2026-09-25 |
| Memory budget (N8.4) | 4.5 GB resident | 2026-09-23 |
| Budget stance and the worst turn (N8, N8.2, spec Appendix E 41) | 1 s median and 2 s worst a business day, sustained, and 4.5 GB stand; a miss is met by changing how the world is represented and traversed, then by the play resolution, never by a mechanism or the population; where these cannot meet the worst turn, the owner decides on the gate's measured numbers, coarsening the spec in its own change before relaxing the budget | 2026-09-23 |
| Cost bounds (N8.6) | every operation a day performs costs at most O(log n) in the size of any store of the world — sublinear, never a walk over a world-sized collection to do one thing; a day's cost is the sum of its events', and a world-sized pass only a declared rolling slice | 2026-09-25 |
| Reading the budget | the budget is read at every step, never only at gates | 2026-09-28 |
| The budget's remainder (N8.7) | at the design point of 6.0 million persons the plan's steps fit with margin: the worst turn ≈ 1 688 ms (E1's next day on a campaign quarter-end payday with every dated day that can fall there; ≈ 1 617 ms without an event) against 1 800 and the owner's ≤ about 1 700; memory ≈ 3 946 MB against 4 349 and the owner's ≤ about 3 950; saves ≈ 3 160 MB against 3 866 (S1.360). A future miss is met strictly in N8.7's order — representation first, then E 41's valves in reverse order, each declared in `perf/design.toml` with its `forced_by` and what it frees — and what remains is recorded by the step that finds it as N8.7's finding with its exact numbers and put to the owner; no step moves the persons or an owner's setting on its own | 2026-09-30 |
| The design point at the finished plan (N8.7, spec Appendix E 51, N8.5, E 41) | 6.0 million persons, the steps' per-person figures (stated at 7.5 million persons' counts) × 0.8; the full audit's cycle 60 days; zones 1 000 (the valve to 500 withdrawn); the map's cells 100 m, fixed like the grid; within the margins — the worst turn ≤ about 1 700 ms and memory ≤ about 3 950 MB — E 41's valves restored in its order: two condition classes and every history horizon at 730 days or two years but the events', kept at 365 (730 would pass 3 950 MB) | 2026-09-30 |
| The core's close (S1.360) | a major step: independent reviews and `tools/bench.sh -g` | 2026-09-29 |

| The play resolution (REP.40, spec Appendix E 44) | the world holds a declared number of the setup's persons, `REP.persons`, every household and firm they form a party of its own; the input is the persons, not a divisor; it is set by measuring the day, 750 000 until a measure resets it; `tools/bench.sh -p` sets another for one run | 2026-09-27 |

| Save duration (N8.10) | a full save within 5 s on the phone, the world paused | 2026-09-23 |
| Load time (N8.10) | restoring a save within 5 s on the phone | 2026-09-29 |
| Save storage (N8.4) | the saves kept, with the one being written, within 4 GB | 2026-09-29 |
| Saves (SET.12, spec Appendix E 22) | every save full; no increments | 2026-09-23 |
| Save interval (SET.12) | every simulated quarter by default | 2026-09-23 |
| Determinism guards | none: the world is never run twice, not even to test the code; determinism is carried by construction | 2026-09-23 |
| Validating the world (PTY.12 and N6 retired, N3, N4, N8.5, spec Appendix E 36) | one run: the normal world run, on the phone; no reference run, no re-run at another resolution or seed, no copy for an experiment. | What the run has not produced (spec Appendix E 39) | never blocks a gate: listed as not yet seen with the run's length, its mechanism shown at logic level; only the budget blocks | 2026-09-23 |
| Measuring the representation (spec Appendix E 40) | only at the play resolution, in the one run; the valve's effect measured in the running world | 2026-09-23 |

| The map's cells (GEO.18, GEO.19, spec Appendix E 29, N8.5) | 100 m, fixed by the owner like the 10 km grid and no RESOLUTION valve: 10 000 cells a tile, a building, a parcel and a path placed to a city block; land held apart stored as parcels (rectangles of cells) and a path's cells computed from a per-tile segment index (S1.190) | 2026-09-30 |
| The map view (OBS.12) | the observer shows the world's map at any zoom — tiles and terrain, the cells held, what stands on each with its owner, occupants or users and value on selection, the parcels, the infrastructure along its paths with its use — aggregated by zone, region and country when zoomed out, from what the world holds only (S6.134) | 2026-09-30 |
| The world's shape and its latitude cycle (GEO.18) | a closed world of the same size (2,590 km each way), wrapping east to west and north to south, with no edge and no pole; a row's climate is read at a latitude that climbs evenly from 35°N at the first row to 58.3°N half the world away and falls evenly back: a temperate continent like Europe's | 2026-09-24 |
| Where local markets meet (REP.24, GEO.3, MKT.1) | a local market meets per region; within a region a buyer's choice weighs distance at zone resolution | 2026-09-29 |
