| Power lines in the wholesale auction (ENE.8) | a transport model: each line carries up to its capacity between the two regions it joins | 2026-09-29 |
| A posted-price market's mark (MKT.12) | the day's sales' mean weighted by units sold (revenue ÷ units) | 2026-09-29 |
| Grade in use (GDS.1, GDS.13, spec Appendix E 45) | each grade declares its content per unit; a way states a graded input in content; a richer grade yields more; the goods' base carries content per grade, and the ways' input reads are changed to content in Stage 1 | 2026-09-29 |

| Settling length (GEN.6) | one simulated year by default; adjustable | 2026-09-23 |
| Total population (GEN.14) | 300 million people, a world constant | 2026-09-23 |
| The setup (GEN.14, GEN.15, spec Appendix E 43) | world constants fixed for the simulation; a new game splits the population (each country 10–70%) and sets per country six three-level choices (development, public debt, private debt, risk appetite, inequality, openness) and a name; a real name labels institutions and currency and pre-fills the choices, never the data; the opening's numbers are derived from country-group profiles | 2026-09-23 |
| The default new game (GEN.14) | a population split of 50% developed, 30% emerging, 20% developing; every other choice at its middle level; generated names | 2026-09-23 |
| The opening (GEN.2, GEN.5, GEN.13, spec Appendix E 38) | a snapshot of the present: stocks, contracts and one latest value of everything observed (prints, fixings, rates, statistics, ratings, filed accounts, surveyed expectations); contracts' pasts by the steady-path convention; every party decides once on day zero; no series drawn, the settling year the only history | 2026-09-23 |
| Slow distributions (GEN.10, spec Appendix E 38) | held, not regrown: income, wealth and firm sizes credited while the world keeps them and moves their members; no decades runs | 2026-09-23 |
| The player's household (GEN.14, OBS.4) | the setup states the country the player lives in and whether the rule decides for it on a day it queued nothing, the default the first country and delegating; the household is drawn at the opening from that country's households, each equally likely | 2026-09-25 |
| Public events (OBS) | weather always public, a catastrophe when a struck tile loses at least a permille, a household's death, disability or birthday never (`OBS.public_events`, a standing SHAPE) | 2026-09-25 |
| One representation (spec Appendix E 14, 31, 33, 35, 44) | every contract between named parties, pairings recorded; no many-party lines, no individuals by rank, one kind of firm | 2026-09-28 |

## 13. The clause map

Every live clause of the spec is completed by exactly one step, listed here, one row per (system, completing step),
grouped by system in the spec's order: `| SYS | S<stage>.<nn> | numbers |` or `| SYS | S<stage>.<nnn> | numbers |`.
Steps before it may carry a clause in part, as their **Clauses** sections say (*(part)*). The rows of done steps
(S0.01–S0.28, S1.01–S1.14, S1.17–S1.23, S1.26) stay as they are; a retired step (§11) holds none. The chains of
spec Part L and the measurement items of Part N are rows of system `L` and `N`, a step completing one by listing it
bare (`N4`), its sub-items (`N8.8`) never.

`phx-check clauses` refuses:
- a clause missing from this map, or completed by two steps;
- a row naming a retired step;
- a step whose completed clauses — those in its **Clauses** section not marked *(part)* — differ from its rows here;
- a step marked done any of whose completed clauses nothing carries: no `#[clause(..)]` attribute, declaration's
  `clause` field, data file's `clause` key or `violation!(clause = ..)` names it (architecture §16.5).

A step this map names that the plan no longer holds is read as done, so a row never names a step not yet written,
and a step's rows are written, moved or removed in the same commit as its heading. `phx-check coverage --write`
regenerates architecture §19 from this map and the steps' statuses, taking the stages in §1's build order. The rows
of the laws (L) and of Part N close the table; they name the step that completes each and are held by review, not
by `phx-check`.

Retired clauses (REP.2, REP.4, REP.6, REP.8, REP.10, REP.11, REP.17, REP.19, REP.27, REP.28, REP.29, REP.30, REP.32, REP.33, REP.36,
REP.37, REP.39, SET.14, PTY.12, GEN.9, N6) keep their numbers and are not mapped.
